Other forks, made before or after from elsewhere, are untouched; forks made from it later inherit it through the lineage like any override. The same image attached twice to one version is one media id, so both copies go out or come back together. It doesn't change the slot's row version, so an open editor stays current. Path entries carry `excludedImages` (the shown version's media ids taken out in the entry's fork), and the API publishes the slot's event, which also has the next context read again.
  - `SetThinkingHidden` (thinkhide1, 2026-11-14): owner-scoped, hides one part of a live version's thinking from the model in a fork (`forkId`, else the fork through its message), or sends it again: `part` is `reasoning` (the provider's) or `sections` (the reply's own tagged sections, §12 "Reply sections"). One writer transaction: a `thinking_hide` override in that fork with target `<original version id>:<part>` and flag 1 or 0, written only when it changes there, through `writeOverride` as `SetImageExcluded` is (other forks untouched; forks made from it later inherit it). Nothing is deleted and the slot's row version doesn't change. Path reads add `hidden_thinking` (`thinkingHiddenSql` in `forkState.ts`, a bitmask: 1 reasoning, 2 sections) and path entries carry `hiddenThinking`. The RPC lives in its own group, `ThinkingApi` (`shared/thinkingApi.ts`, `server/api/thinking.ts`), because `AppCoreApi` is at TypeScript's instantiation depth; the handler publishes the slot's event.
  - `AmendVersion`: a finished user-written version as a fork shows it (`forkId`, else the fork through its message), `StaleWrite` when the fork shows another text in its place or the version was amended since. In place (the trigger keeps the earlier text) when no other fork shows it (`shownElsewhere` in `db/forks.ts`: a fork other than this one, in the bin or not, whose path holds the message and whose picker there shows that version, i.e. it doesn't replace it). Otherwise the fork gets a copy X′ (origin `edited`, `source_version_id` the message's own version X, `fork_id` the fork, its other columns X's but its generation, `version_history` and attachments copied, X's text added to its history) and a `replace` X → X′ in that fork, so the other forks keep X's text and history. A copy only this fork shows (no fork made from it since) is then amended in place. Not chatting in the fork (owner, 2026-10-27).
  - `SelectVersion`: in a fork (`forkId`, the current one if none is named), with `expectedVersionId`, the version the tab saw that fork show there, failing as `StaleWrite` when the fork shows another. Selecting what it shows writes nothing. Either id may be a fork's copy: it stands for its original, which is what the selection names.
  - `SetSlotHidden`: hides a live message from the model or shows it again in a fork (`forkId`, else the fork through it; ST's ghost toggle), as the user's doing: a `hide` override of that fork (§3.11, `writeOverride`), so another fork's context and stepped history are untouched. What the fork's context reads is its row, else the slot's own `context_excluded` (frozen; an ST import's hidden messages have it set and `hidden_by_user` unset) as a published staged LCM unhide's overlay shows it. A hide is a history reduction in that fork (`recordReduction`: `history_changes` row of the fork, which counts in it and in forks made from it later). Already so in that fork, it changes nothing. `StImportUnhide` writes `hide` rows of 0 in the fork through its slot. Publishing an LCM enable run writes one `hide_range` override with flag 0 and the run id. Visibility resolves individual hides and published ranges together in lineage and sequence order, so only that fork and forks made afterwards inherit the unhide; a later hide wins. The enable dialog captures the fork id as well as its leaf; offer, staging and publication use that fork even when another fork ends at the same message. Publication refuses if an unnamed run now resolves to a different fork, keeping visibility and settings in the same fork. `StImportUnhide` also accepts an explicit fork. Staging stays invisible and publication never writes a row per message. A range and individual hides keep their precedence in forks however deep: the one written nearest the fork wins (§3.8 "Fork labels").
  - `AddStateEvent`: a user's state change (origin `user`) at a live position, optionally attached to a version, scoped to `forkId` (else the fork through the position). `AddStateEvents` writes several in one transaction (the persona switch). Positions are checked against the fork, with a compatibility exception for positional writes on legacy imported paths. Legacy imported paths without fork rows retain `forkAt`'s current-fork fallback for positional writes (new ST imports have file-owned fork rows, §13), including writes addressed by the fallback ID the reader returned; a card swap still requires a position on its fork. Each event records immutable `fork_id` and the chat's next `state_seq` as `fork_seq`; rollout variable events record their rollout's fork too. Initial and imported events with null provenance remain shared base state. New initial user events, including `lcm.settings`, belong to the fork: summarization's switch and settings are per fork (owner, 2026-10-27). `ChangeLcmSettings`, `GetLcmSettings` and `SetLcmEnabled` accept the viewed fork, as do the cast, card-details and note-list reads and cast writes.
- **Reads:**
  - `GetChat`
  - `GetPath`: a window of a fork's path (the current fork's if none is named), or of the path to a named leaf; below.
  - `ListForks`: a chat's live forks, most recently current first, each with its name, pin, tip, the start of its tip's text, when it was made and last chatted in, and whether it's current.
    It reuses the shell summary's preview, split and activity time. Valid summaries require no message reads; a missing or stale summary computes only that fork (and its parent's path for the split), preserving the stored summaries of the other forks. The old preview lookup sorted every fork's full display path even when every summary was valid.
  - `ListVersions`: a message's own versions in a fork (`forkId`, else the fork through it): each as the fork shows it, a copy in its original's place and position, with the fork's flags. The count on a path entry is the same set.
  - `StateEventsAt`: the events that apply at a slot in a fork (`forkId`; none named, the fork through the slot, `forkAt`), in fold order, found by the chain and depth of their slots in the path's segments (`stateEventsOnPath` in `stateRead.ts`, `pathEvents` in `db/pathSegments.ts`, which the assembler's `events` shares), so the cost is the path's branch points and events, not its length. The segments drive the join (`CROSS JOIN`): left to itself, SQLite read every event of the chat. Version-attached events count only while the fork shows their version, and events on a deleted message only once it's restored (DESIGN §3.4, proposed). Events naming a library entity, ref or revision that was deleted for good, or scoped to a card that was, are left out (`played_by_me.set` clears a purged selected persona), so restoring a message can't bring a purged card back. In a fork that places insertions, the path is its display path through the slot (`stateEventsThrough`, `displayThrough` and `displayEvents` in `db/displayPath.ts`; spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §3.1, unit 4): the pieces through the slot's position drive the same join by chain and depth, an inserted slot being the only one at its chain and depth, and each event carries its slot's position. A fork that places none reads `stateEventsOnPath` as before, after one index probe per lineage entry. `AddStateEvent`, `ForkCardForChat` and the fork-notes preview check the slot with `onForkPath`, so an event can be put on an inserted message the fork shows and not on one it doesn't. What reads a fork as it stands (the fork-notes preview's "now", `RenameHistoryTargets`, the cast at a fork's tip) reads through its display end (`displayEndOf`), an inserted message after the tip included. The note binding a chat note's editor resolves (`noteAt`) is the nearest before the slot in display order. The composer’s cast, card and note reads request `StateEventsAt.displayEnd`: when the named slot is the fork’s structural tip (null included), it reads through the display end. Plain `StateEventsAt` remains a precise read through its named slot. Composer cast changes set the same flag on `AddStateEvent`/`AddStateEvents`; the writer resolves the display end inside the transaction so a new change follows events on a trailing insertion. The live-slot check applies to the slot written to, after that resolution: a deleted tip that retains a shown insertion (§3.11) resolves to the live inserted message after it, where the change folds before the next turn, while an explicit position at a deleted message is refused, since its events don't fold. Version-attached events and chat-wide LCM settings keep their explicit positions. This also covers an insertion above the first message in a fork with no structural tip.
- **Fork-scoped events and swaps** (`stateRead.ts`, `forkState.ts`, `@rp/shared/state.ts`; fork independence unit 6, card forks unit 2). Events with provenance apply only within the fork's bounded lineage, like overrides; a `suppress_event` override with flag 1 removes an event in that fork, flag 0 restores it. The writer's overlay helper supports null positions for these rows, and database triggers check that they name an event of the same chat. Changeset undo uses this storage support; its history UI is documented in §3.13.
  - Positional events fold in path depth and per-position sequence order; in a fork with insertions, in display position order (`eventOrder(e, position)`), so an inserted message's events fold after its anchor's and before the next message's. Branch-owned keys (`branchOwned`, currently `card.swap`) are written at slot null without a version or scope and fold last, in `fork_seq` order, including when reading before the first message. `StateEventsAt(leafSlotId)` chooses the viewed fork when reading an earlier position; an explicit `forkId` distinguishes forks sharing a tip. The assembler, chat groups, cast and notes use the same visibility and suppression rules. Frozen assembly rebuilds retain their originally pinned event IDs.
  - `card.swap { entity, replaces }`, exposed by `ChangeCast`'s `Swap`, substitutes a live card in the same family, with ownership checked for both IDs (`replaces` may be binned). A missing cast member is a no-op. Cast order, absence, played-by-me and the card's lorebook binding and embedded-lore switch follow the replacement; the original's card binding stays dormant and comes back on swapping back. Later positional cast and lore-switch writes resolve the displayed card to its pre-swap cast identity before storage, so the final swap fold preserves those changes. Purging an original or intermediate card keeps only its routing IDs and cast flags where a live replacement needs them; its definitions and dormant bindings stay purged. As before, a swap whose incoming card was purged is omitted, unless that card is only an intermediate on the way to a live replacement. New swipes and continuations resolve their writing card through the swaps, and the assembler does the same for a request at an earlier message. Existing message authors stay unchanged. A swap configures the next version; historical card chat-membership indexes, lists and usage counts include the replacement only after an authored version records it.
  - Later forks inherit branch-owned events from any fork point through the lineage bound; existing forks do not. Deleting or restoring a message cannot remove a swap. Neither branching nor deleting copies an event, positional or not: each carries its fork's label when written (`state_events.fork_label`) and is visible in the forks whose points lie from that label to the end of its writer's range (`eventVisibleSql`, two comparisons; "Fork labels" below), so assembly pins and suppression targets always name the one event.
  - `forkStateEvents.test.ts` covers shared-tip and initial events, per-fork settings, branch-owned state at earlier positions and in assembly, later/earlier/empty forks, delete/restore, selected-version effects, family and user refusals, suppression, and a 70-deep chain of forks. Shared fold tests cover card position and flags, lore keys and dormant bindings; `stateKeys.test.ts` includes both swap IDs; schema tests cover provenance and fixed fork labels. The review regressions additionally cover cast changes after swaps, purged originals and swap chains, the viewed fork's next-context note preview, changed-fork enable publication, and client LCM/cache responses at shared tips. The LCM graph oracle tracks per-fork settings and amended-version replacements, and addresses rendered chunks in the same fork as its context assertions.
- **Human note inheritance on fork** (`db/forkNotes.ts`, `ForkNotesDialog.tsx`; U21, owner 2026-10-28). `PreviewForkNotes` compares the source fork at the chosen message and its current tip, using the same event visibility, suppression and note-switch defaults as assembly. It lists live chat notes with human binding/switch changes after the point and card notes with changed chat activation, including cards in the cast or played-by-me set at either endpoint. A card removed after the fork point still gets its note choices. Version-attached effects after the point stay causal and are excluded from the carry-back choice. Card text remains library-owned. Chat-note revisions carry their complete document, including placement and shared-note links; linked text retains shared notes' global semantics.
  - The registered `message.branch` action opens a fork dialog: every changed note defaults to **As it was then**, with **As it is now** alongside it. **Set all notes** changes every row, and individual overrides show a mixed state. Accordion rows expand to the existing CodeMirror merge view, forced side by side at both desktop and phone widths, with explicit then/now headings and on/off labels. Development builds alone expose the button-to-diff comparison variant. Cancel writes nothing; with no changed notes the action creates the fork immediately after the preview.
  - `CreateFork.notes` carries the reviewed comparison and per-note selections. In one writer transaction it recomputes and compares a canonical JSON projection, refuses stale or invalid selections with `ForkNotesChanged`, creates the fork, and writes only the chat-note revision bindings and note switches that a now choice changes from then at its base. Then choices use positional inheritance without new events; unchanged bindings and switches retain their version attachments and default-on behavior. Missing choices default to then. Source and existing sibling forks are untouched; later forks inherit those choices through the normal bounded lineage. Calls without selections retain positional inheritance. No schema change is needed.
  - **Unsaved text is the latest state** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §4.1). The preview's `ForkNote.unsaved` is a chat note's unsaved text at the source's latest message when it differs from now (not for card notes, whose text is the card's on every branch, nor linked text, which is shared). The dialog flushes open editors before the preview (`flushOpenEditors`), marks such a row "Unsaved changes", compares then against that text, and says in each choice's explanation where the text goes: **As it is now** takes it to the new branch, **As it was then** leaves it on the source, still unsaved. The writer moves it after the choices' events (§3.10, Unsaved note text goes with a fork), keeping it for each row chosen then. After the fork, open editors read again (`refreshOpenEditors`).
  - `forkNotes.test.ts` covers mixed/all-now/default choices, API round trips, card activation defaults, stale/unknown selections with rollback, version-attached effects, membership and later inheritance, including removed/played cards and version-attached bindings/switches after swiping an inherited message. Isolation probes cover the preview at both RPC and worker boundaries. `e2e/forkNotes.spec.ts` exercises defaults, set-all, mixed overrides, CodeMirror diffs and persisted text at 1440/390 in light/dark; `FORK_NOTES_DEV=1` runs both variants through Vite, and `SCREENSHOT_DIR` writes screenshots outside the repository.
- **Ownership.** Every operation takes the acting user and touches only that user's rows. Anything else is `NotFound`, so another user's data isn't even confirmed to exist. That includes:
  - someone else's card as a speaker or participant
  - every entity, ref, revision, connection and model a state event's value names (`db/stateRefs.ts`), with the kind each key expects (a note for `note.activate`). Note keys also reject a note owned by another chat of the same user, as declared by `chatOwned`; card-owned notes remain usable across chats. The stricter `chatOwned: "required"` declaration on `author_note.set` accepts only notes whose upstream document names this chat as owner; card and shared notes are refused without changing the previous choice. Each key declares its id fields, with their table, kind and links (`stateKeyIds` in `@rp/shared/state.ts`), and the checker reads only the declarations. A new key doesn't compile until it's declared. Every id schema (`EntityId`, `RefId`, `ConnectionId`, …) is made by `idSchema` (`@rp/shared/id.ts`), which annotates its table (`ID_TABLE`); ESLint forbids `Schema.brand` anywhere else in `src`. `packages/shared/test/state.test.ts` walks each key's value schema, record keys included: an id the declaration doesn't name, an id below a top-level field, an id inside a template literal or a suspended schema, or a declared field that isn't an id schema fails it. An id typed as a plain string isn't seen, so state values use the id schemas. `test/stateKeys.test.ts` checks every key's ids through the writer against an oracle written apart from the declarations: another user's id, an id of another kind, one that doesn't belong to the value's other ids, and things in the bin (allowed only for `removes` keys) are each `NotFound`. Keys that add something need it live; keys that remove something (`removes`: `participant.leave`, `presence.set`, `note.deactivate`, `lorebook.detach`) check ownership only, so a deleted or purged card can still be taken out of a chat.
  - another user's version as an edit's source
- An event's `scope` is a role (`narrator`, `summarizer`) or a participant, which must be a live card of the user's, checked like a value's ids (`scopeIds`). Lane and `agent:<entity>` scopes (DATA-MODEL §5.1) aren't accepted until something uses them.
- `var.set`'s `value` is free-form and not checked: whatever later reads an id from it must check ownership itself.
- **Registered state keys** (`@rp/shared/state.ts`, shared/server `test/pluginState.test.ts`). `StateEventData` preserves the typed built-in keys and their default fold. Every built-in registers its value schema, id declaration, positional/branch scope and projection through `registerStateKey`, the same API used by plugins. `stateKeys` supports scoped overrides, disablement and restoration; declarations and branch ownership resolve through its active entries. New keys use `<plugin>/<key>` and registration validates names and declarations with `stateKeyProblems`, failing with `StateKeyRegistrationError`. Plugin values normally fold into `ChatState.plugin[id]` (`reduce(current, value, scope)`, else last value); `apply(state, value, scope)` can wrap or replace a projection into chat state. Removed entries and stored values incompatible with an overridden schema are skipped without deleting events. `WritableStateEvent` checks current availability and value validity. The private worker wire uses `StoredStateEventData`, allowing registration to be installed before validation; the writer then refuses unavailable keys and invalid values and checks every declared id against the acting user inside its transaction. Positional events follow the path and selected version; branch-owned events have no slot, version or scope and fold after positional events in chat sequence order, using the same frozen fork lineage as `card.swap`.
- **State modules in workers** (`db/stateModules.ts`). `Database.layer` exposes `StateModules` alongside `Writer` and `Reader`. Register a trusted module reference (`id`, absolute `module` URL, `exportName`) in a scope; its `InstallStateModule` export receives `stateKeys` and installs entries through that registry. Registration installs on the server, and each private worker request carries the complete active module stack, overwriting inherited headers. Each worker installs it in a request scope before entering the database transaction and removes it afterward. This preserves overrides, disablement, scope cleanup and worker respawns, for source and bundled workers. The bridge compiles plugin schema predicates with the installed Effect interpreter that dynamic modules import: bundled Effect has private refinement parser results incompatible with another copy. Schema predicates execute synchronously in the writer; imports execute outside transactions. Already admitted requests retain their snapshot; future requests after scope exit see restored registrations. ESM caches module code, so changed code needs a new URL. This is trusted module execution, not installation/consent UI. Shared tests cover declarations, built-ins, reduction, disablement and schema changes; worker tests cover save/fork/reload, positional versus branch ownership, fold order, ownership refusal, scope cleanup and built-in overrides in both worker modes.
- **Paths are read by chain segment** (spec/FORK-INDEPENDENCE-DELTA.md §2.1, unit 1). Each slot has a chain (migration 0052): a slot inserted as the first child of its parent continues the parent's chain; a later child or a root starts one, whose id is its own. The database assigns it (`slots_chain_assigned`), so every insert gets one whatever wrote it. A chain is a run of slots at consecutive depths, so the path from the root to a slot is a few segments `(chain, depths lo to hi)`, one per branch point it passes. `pathSegments` (`db/pathSegments.ts`) finds them newest first: a chain id is its head's id, so the next segment up is two lookups by id (the head's parent, and that parent's chain head). Each step must go strictly up, so a corrupted parent link can't make it loop. A slot is on the path iff a segment has its chain and covers its depth.
- **Display paths** (spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §2.3, unit 1; `db/displayPath.ts`, shared by readers and the writer). A message can be inserted between two others: it's an ordinary slot below the message it was inserted below (its anchor; a root above the first message), marked `inserted`, and an `insert` override with flag 1 places it in the fork it was inserted in, which forks made from that fork later inherit through the lineage. What a fork shows is its display path: the structural path (root to tip by parent links, by chain segment as below) with the fork's placed insertions spliced in. `pathPieces(sql, chat, fork, tip)` returns it as pieces in order, each a structural run `(chain, lo, hi)` or one inserted slot, with its start position: the tip's segments, then the fork's effective `insert` rows with flag 1 (`placedInsertions`: one range scan of `fork_overrides_point` on `(fork_id, kind)` per lineage entry, so the fork's insertions, not the chat's length), then `splice`. The gap of a slot P is the inserted slots anchored at P, newest first by id, each followed by its own gap, then P's structural successor; the gap of null comes before the root. So inserting below P always puts the new message directly below P. An insertion whose anchor isn't shown isn't reached; one that is on the structural path itself (a fork made at or below it) is where the path has it. `positionOf(pieces, slot)` and `onDisplayPath(pieces, slot)` take the slot's id, chain and depth: a run holds a slot by chain and depth, an inserted piece by id. Whether a fork shows a slot is `onForkPath` (`db/forks.ts`): for a slot that wasn't inserted it's `onPath`, at its cost, so chats without insertions read exactly as before; `forkThrough` (and so `forkAt`), `shownElsewhere`, `forksShowing`, `CreateFork` and a branch's choice of fork use it, and their candidate forks include those whose tip is above an inserted slot. `displayEnd` is the last piece's slot: the tip, or an inserted slot when everything structural after its anchor is gone from the fork's view. `hiddenAtFork(parent, at, child)` lists what a fork made at `at` mustn't place so that it shows exactly its parent's display path up to `at`: every inserted slot the new fork's own pieces would show that the parent doesn't show at or before `at`, which includes a slot the parent has structurally below `at` while inheriting its `insert` row. Pieces include messages deleted in the fork; whether one is shown is for the caller, as on the structural path. `depth` stays structural. Path windows read by position (below, "By position"), and so do state events (`StateEventsAt` above) and context assembly (§15 "Inserted messages"); the bin's handling of inserted slots is in §3.11, and LCM's in §16 "Inserted messages". `test/displayPath.test.ts` compares `pathPieces` with an oracle that keeps each fork as a list (append at its end, insert directly below the anchor, a fork made at P starts as its parent's list up to P) over random sequences of appends, insertions, forks at any shown message or before the first, and deletions, and over a 70-deep chain of forks, which copies nothing: order, positions, membership of every slot of the chat, the display end and the deletions.
  - **Moves** (schemafinal, 2026-11-16). After insertions are spliced in, a fork's effective `move` rows with flag 1 (`placedMoves`, one range scan per lineage entry, as `placedInsertions`) are applied (`applyMoves`): a move applies when its anchor is null, shown where the path or the fork's insertions have it, or a moved slot that is shown (where its own move puts it, or at its own place when that move doesn't apply), whether or not the moved slot is on the structural path; a cycle of anchors applies none of its moves, and a move that doesn't apply leaves its slot at its own place, if the path has one. Each applied slot leaves its place (a run is split there; the left part's `endId` is the slot before it), a left-out slot (a row naming itself) leaves it and isn't shown, and shows as a `moved` piece directly after its anchor; several after one anchor go newest first by seq, each followed by those moved after it. What was inserted or is structurally below a moved slot stays where it was. The cost is the moves, not the path: runs split only at the moved slots and anchors. `rearranges` (insertions or moves) replaces `placedInsertions(...).length > 0` wherever a reader keeps its structural code for a plain fork; `displayEnd` and `lastShown` end at a cut run's `endId`. A fork made later inherits the rows through its lineage; a fork made before or beside keeps its order. **A new fork follows its parent's order where it was made** (finalwipe1, 2026-11-16; `db/forkOrder.ts` `placeAsShown`, called by CreateFork, a send below a message that isn't the tip, SwitchBranch, starting threads, a Resume that branches and a restore that comes back as a branch). Without moves it writes `hiddenAtFork`'s rows, as before. With moves it lists both display paths (`displayIds`) and writes rows of its own until the fork shows exactly the parent's display path through that message, then its own line below it: what it would show that the parent didn't by then is left out (an inserted piece unplaced); the slots that keep their structural order stay at their own place (a row of 0 when they were moved); every other one follows the slot before it. So a fork made above a message its parent moved down doesn't show it, and one made below a message its parent moved up (or at a message moved down) shows what came before it there, off its own structural line. A later move on either fork never changes the other. Readers that ask whether a fork shows a slot (`onForkPath`, and the candidate filter of `forkThrough`, `forksShowing` and `shownElsewhere`) check the slot's effective move first, one probe of `fork_steps`. A deleted message that something is moved after stays the fork's tip (`liveGaps`), so the moved message keeps its place. Only a chat with moves pays the listing: at 5,000 messages it's a few listings of the path per new fork (`test/messageMoveScale.test.ts`).
- **Forks** (spec/FORK-INDEPENDENCE-DELTA.md §2.1, unit 2; `db/baseline.ts`, `db/forks.ts`). A fork is what the user sees as one chat line, from the first message to its tip. It's a row (`forks`), because a leaf can't be its identity: a tip moves with every message, moves up when its last message is deleted (`relocateLeaf`, per fork), and can be a message another fork shares (one made at a message before anything is sent in it, ST's checkpoint). Its history is its path: the slots from the root to its tip, read by chain segment as below. A slot is on a fork's path iff a segment of its tip holds it (`onPath`), which costs the path's branch points. Forks share the slots, versions and every other row of their common history. Which version a message shows, amends of a user's message another fork shows, and stars and picker flags are per fork (below); swipes belong to the message, so a swipe made in any fork is in every fork's picker there (CHATS.md "Forks", owner 2026-10-26). Deletion and hiding are per fork too (below, §3.11). The rest of what belongs to a fork (summaries and history edits) is later units of the delta; events are fork-scoped (§3.8), including new ST imports (§13). Each fork has its own composer (§3.10).
  - **The current fork** is the one the chat opens on: the one last chatted in or made by forking, whichever is more recent (UX-REWORK §3, owner). "Chatted in" is adding a message or a version there (owner 2026-10-27): a send, a reply, a queued message when it's sent, a swipe, a continue, an edit or a written version (`AddSelectedVersion`, `AddVersion`). Selecting an existing version isn't. `chats.current_fork_id` is set in the same transaction as `CreateFork` (`created_at`, and `last_chatted_at` the same time: making a branch is the user's activity in it, which the shell's Recent counts) and as those writes (`last_chatted_at`). When it goes to the bin (§3.11), the live fork with the latest of the two takes over; a chat's last fork doesn't go (below). `chats.active_leaf_slot_id` stays as the current fork's tip (§3.7), for what still reads the chat's leaf: the assembler, LCM, the cast, chat lists.
  - **Per-fork selection** (spec/FORK-INDEPENDENCE-DELTA.md §2.2 and §2.3, unit 3; `db/baseline.ts`, `db/forkState.ts`). What a fork changes is a row of its own in `fork_overrides`, never a change to a shared one. Each per-fork write takes the next `chats.state_seq` as its `seq`, in its transaction. A fork G sees its own rows, its parent's up to when G was made (`branched_at`, the chat's state seq then), its grandparent's up to when the parent was made, and so on up: its lineage. The effective value of a key is the nearest lineage entry with a row for it, the newest there, else the base column. Fork labels index that as a step function, so `effectiveOverrideSql` is one index probe whatever G's depth or the chat's number of forks. So a choice in F never shows in G, made before or after; a fork made later inherits it, from any point of F's path, since a selection is keyed by slot, not position; and nothing a fork does later reaches a fork made from it.
    - `SelectVersion`, `AddSelectedVersion` and `AddVersion` with `select` write a `select` row in their fork (`writeSelect`). A new slot's first selection is its own column, set at insert (`StartChat`'s greetings insert their versions first). A fork's own row is updated in place, taking the new seq, while no fork was made from it since (no child with `branched_at` ≥ its seq: a grandchild reads it through its parent's bound, which is earlier), so swiping back and forth at a tip nobody forked from leaves one row.
    - **Fork labels** (spec/FORK-COST.md, forkbuild; `db/forkLabels.ts`, its schema in `db/baseline.ts`). Each fork has a base and an epoch (how many forks were made from it so far) in `fork_labels`: its point is base·enc(epoch), its range everything from base·enc(0) to base·ff (`enc`: one byte e + 1 below 224, f0 and two bytes below 65,760, else f1 and eight bytes; order-preserving, prefix-free, never starting with ff; labels are BLOBs). Making G from F gives G F's point as its base and moves F's epoch on, so the ranges nest like the fork tree, and what F writes afterwards sorts after all of G's range. `fork_steps(kind, target_id, label, override_id)` (`WITHOUT ROWID`) holds, for each override row written in F, a step at F's point naming it and, the first time F writes that key, a step at F's end naming what was in force there before (null: the base column); the effective row of a key in any fork is the step with the greatest label at or below its point: `SEARCH fx_s USING PRIMARY KEY (kind=? AND target_id=? AND label<?)`. A `hide` is two such probes, the slot's own and those of the published LCM ranges holding it (`hide_range`); the one whose writer has the longer base (the deeper in the lineage) wins, the newest of one writer's. Rows that are added rather than keyed carry their writer's point (`state_events.fork_label`, `history_changes.label`) and are visible where label ≤ point < the writer's end (`labelVisibleSql`). Triggers keep all of it: `fork_labels_made` (forks), `fork_overrides_steps` (every insert into `fork_overrides`, from whichever file writes it), `state_events_fork_label`, `history_changes_label`; an in-place update keeps its step, which names the same row. The event-label trigger fills only missing labels: the legacy interrupted-import suffix copy retains each event's original label and sequence, even after the writer has children. Labels, a fork's parent and its moment, and an event's label never change, and an override goes only with its chat, whose cascade takes its keys' steps (`fork_overrides_go_with_chat`). Bulk loads pause the triggers with a row in `fork_label_pause` and call `rebuildForkLabels`, which recomputes a chat's labels and steps from seqs (children ordered by `(branched_at, id)`; a row of seq s at the epoch counting its fork's children with `branched_at` < s, which reproduces seq ≤ `branched_at`, ties included). Making a fork (`insertFork`) is its `forks` row, its label and its parent's epoch: three row writes whatever the history, swipes, overrides or genealogy, and nothing is copied. A per-fork write adds at most two steps. Three reads list rows rather than look a key up (`placedInsertions`, `shellPlainForksQuery`, the ST re-import's local-choice check): they walk the lineage by parent (`lineageCte`, a recursive CTE of `(fork_id, bound)`), one range probe of `fork_overrides_point` per entry, once per statement. Labels grow by the parent epoch's encoded length per level of genealogy (one byte below 224); steps cost about 125 bytes each, at most two per fork and key. `test/forkLabels.test.ts` builds random fork trees (ties, in-place updates, deletes and restores, events, history reductions), a chain of 300 and a fan-out of 600 through the real helpers (all override kinds, published hide ranges, suppression and 20 swipes per slot) and compares every lookup, event and reduction in every fork with the lineage rule computed in the test from the rows, before and after `rebuildForkLabels`, including a paused bulk load and subsequent live writes; checks the SQL and rebuild encoding past 65,759 children; and checks that making a fork 200 deep writes one label and nothing else.
    - **Parallel threads, stored shape** (spec/THREADS.md §4, TH1; `db/baseline.ts`, `db/threads.ts`, `db/threadReads.ts`). A thread is a fork; a split (`thread_splits`) records that forks run alongside each other from a message S of the fork F they were started in: its S, F, F's point when it was made (`fork_label`, read before the new threads' forks, so they sort inside it) and the chat's seq then (`seq`, from which `rebuildForkLabels` recomputes the label as `pointAt(F, seq)`), its origin (registered kinds `user`, `rollout`, `import`), the bin item of its Undo while that's in the bin, and a reserved reply. Its threads (`thread_members`, keyed by split and ordinal) are F continuing (ordinal 0, `starts` 0, always present) and forks made from F at S (`starts` 1, each starting one thread at most), with a name the user can set (`name_user`), extras (`meta_json`) and a row version. Triggers keep a split's message, branch and reply in its chat, a split frozen (its label moves only under `fork_label_pause`), and a member its split, place and branch; everything goes with the chat. `insertSplit`/`insertThreadMember` (writer, in the caller's transaction) take the next seq and F's point, then the caller makes the threads' forks (`insertFork` from F at S), whose `branched_at` is then ≥ the split's seq. Which thread a fork G is in is derived, never stored per message: a split is in G when its label ≤ G's point < F's end (rows added in F are visible the same way) and S is on G's display path; G is in the member whose fork's range holds its point (that fork or one made from it), else in F's thread. `threadCandidates` reads the label half for a chat's forks in one statement; the shell's fork summaries keep each fork's places, innermost first (`fork_summaries.threads_json`, format 9; `placesOf` with the walk's path), and a new split touches only F's summary (the `shell_touch_thread_split` trigger) and bumps the chat's stamp. A split shows only while two of its threads have a live fork (`shownSplits`); `ListForks` gives each fork its shown places (`Fork.threads`), and `ThreadsOf` a fork's sets: S and its position on the fork's display path, each thread's name, how many live forks it has and the one a link opens (of its live forks, the one current most recently). Also stored for later units: `thread_sends` (the messages of one send to several threads), `queued_messages.send_group`, `chat_merges.timelines` (`together`, `separate`) and `split_id`, `chat_merge_messages.source_version_id` and `media_json`, a bin kind `threads`, and the `presence_away` override kind (a branch's correction of who was there for one message, keyed `<slot id>:<card id>`, flag 1 away, checked by a trigger; §16.2 [D] 2026-11-12). `test/threadsSchema.test.ts` checks the triggers and kinds on a bare database, and which thread every fork is in against the lineage rule over random fork trees with nested splits (splits in threads and in their branches, branches made before and after a split), before and after a rebuild, under a paused bulk load and with live writes after it.
    - **Starting threads** (spec/THREADS.md §5.2, TH2; `db/threadWrites.ts`, `api/threads.ts`, `@rp/shared/threadsApi.ts`). The registered command `thread.start` calls `StartThreads` (writer, one transaction) with the branch F the tab is in, a message S on F's display path, the row version the tab saw (the slot's plus F's selection there, else `StaleWrite`) and two or more threads, each a cast (cast characters and the user's own cards; `ThreadsRefused` when someone isn't in the cast at S, or a thread has no character and the chat no narrator), an optional name and an optional card to write as. It records the split (F continuing as thread 0), makes a fork from F at S per other thread (shown at S as F shows it: its swipe there), then marks in each thread at S, as `away.set` events with origin `user` and the split as their ref, the cast characters of the others away and its own back if they were; narrators are in every thread. Each new thread gets an empty composer with F's reply choices, writing as its card (F's composer too, when its card is given). At an earlier message (§5.2 step 5, [D] 2026-11-12) the messages F shows after S, deleted ones included, stay F's thread: every cast character assigned out of F's thread is counted not there for each of them by a `presence_away` override of F (`insertCorrections`, value a JSON object mapping contributing split ids to whether each applies), written after the threads' forks so only F and branches made from it later see it. The user stays in F. Readers apply the override through `correctedAwaySql`: `knowsSql` and `readKnowers` (assembly's knowers, `knewThrough`, LCM audiences, paths and the summary panel's view checks, History search and the agent's `KnowersOf`, all now given the fork) leave a corrected card out of a message's knowers unless it's the speaker, an explicit branch absence also applies when no cast was recorded, and a merge's join is hidden whole from a corrected card (`away` on the knowers result, checked before the join's per-viewer projection; the agent's history tools count it missed). The correction is projected in the existing knowledge query, with an indexed slot lookup and no extra statements for a chat without overrides. `RenameThread` (row-versioned; an empty name clears it) names a thread in all its branches. `UndoThreads` puts the split's new threads' forks in the bin as one item of kind `threads` (forks made from them stay, as when deleting a branch) and suppresses the split's away marks and F's correction (`setSplitApplied`: event overrides and only this split's contribution to each correction flipped, in place unless a fork was made from F since); restoring brings the forks back and reapplies both; purging empties their unshared messages and keeps fork tombstones. `ThreadsOf` and the shell's `ListForks` read the result (TH1). `test/threads.test.ts` runs both starts through the real server: a branch made before S merged in after it, swipes chosen on S and after it, a sibling at the tip made before; each thread's marks and composer; Wren's context in F and in the sibling; rename; Undo and restore; refusals and another user's probes. `test/threadsScale.test.ts` (slow; 3,000 messages with 20–50 versions each, 300 branches, ten splits, one at message 1,000 correcting about 2,000 messages) measured on the dev host: StartThreads 86 ms, ListForks 32 ms and ThreadsOf 6 ms from stored fork summaries (272 ms for the ThreadsOf that recomputes the ten touched summaries; an unsettled ListForks at this shape costs about 1.1 s with or without threads), the first thread's next reply 474 ms for Wren (corrected) and 546 ms for Mira, Undo 181 ms and restore 108 ms.
    - **Threads review** (review-threads1, 2026-11-12; TH1/TH2 only). Corrections cover all characters assigned out of the continuing thread, including ones already away at S, and their earlier card identities. Their override `value_id` keeps each contributing split's applied flag as a JSON object, retaining false entries so an in-place Undo can be restored; overlapping splits undo independently, and forked copies keep their prior object. The database checks that object shape. Explicit absences also protect cast-less messages; a speaker keeps its own words through replacement-card identities. Merge previews and writes freeze the source fork's corrected knowers for messages and summary intersections, so an ordinary merge today cannot reintroduce its absent stretch; for a cast-less source row with explicit absences, the frozen finite audience is the source cast less those absences. Knowledge windows use one query, with `fork_overrides_presence(slot_id, target_id)` for the absence projection; no extra read statement is added to unthreaded chats. Split ordering uses display positions, including inserted S, and fork-summary format 9 invalidates the former ordering. Start input is capped at 32 threads and names at 200 characters (start and rename, public and worker schemas); fewer than two still gets `ThreadsRefused`. The model-content purge guard authorizes `threads` bin items under the same owner and slot checks as branches. Tests added in `threads`, `threadsSchema`, shared `threads`, and `viewSummaries` cover these failures, nested inserted splits, CorrectPresence/Undo, summary freshness in the affected branch and audience only, and played thread messages surviving Undo/restore and a descendant branch surviving purge. **BASELINE CHANGED**, fresh deploy; no migrations. These implementation details supersede the earlier TH2 deltas in the retained proposal; TH4–TH8 remain unbuilt.
    - **Threads in the client** (spec/THREADS.md §5.1, §13, TH3; `features/threads/`, registered as a plugin would). **Reads**: `threadSets.ts` reads a fork's sets with `ThreadsOf` once per fork and version (the chat's row version, which a split, a rename and an Undo bump here or in another tab, and `forksChanged`'s count, `useForksVersion`), however many surfaces ask, keeping the last answer while a newer read is on its way; a loader in `chatOverlays` reads the shown fork's, and the parts that read the store synchronously hear of each answer (`timelineInputsChanged`, which `ChatPage` adds to its rows' inputs, and `branchPartsChanged`). `ThreadInfo.cast` is each thread's characters at S (not away there, narrators and the user's own cards left out), what an unnamed thread is called by (`threadName`: "Mira and Tobin", else "Thread 2"). **Start**: the `message.threads` action ("Start parallel threads here…", place group) and the ⋯ `chat.threads` command ("Start parallel threads…", at the newest message, read with `ReadPath` when the window shown doesn't reach it) open `StartThreadsDialog.tsx`, "Threads from #N": the cast at the message (`GetCast`), rows This branch (everyone) and New thread (nobody), Add a thread, each with a name (placeholder: its characters' names), the cast as toggle chips (the user's cards marked, narrators listed once as in every thread) and Writes as (This branch: "As now", the composer as it is; a new thread: one of the user's cards in it, else a narrator, else its first character); Start stays disabled with the reason (`startProblem`); at an earlier message a line says what happens to the messages after it, naming who leaves ("#4–#6 become this branch’s thread. Wren counts as not there for them, in this branch only.", `playedLine`). It sends the slot's row version as the tab saw it. The user stays put; the toast offers Open “…” and Undo. **The branch control's extension points** (`features/chat/branchParts.ts`, `branchControlParts`): a part may name the trigger (`trigger`: kind, label, icon, hint), leave forks out of the Branches list (`listed`) and add a section above it (`Section`); the threads part makes the trigger "Thread: Mira and Tobin ▾" with the threads icon (truncating as the branch trigger does), leaves out every fork that is in a set the shown fork isn't in as the same thread (`listedAsBranch`: another thread's forks, of a set the shown fork is in or one it's outside), and adds the Threads section (`ThreadsSection.tsx`): per set, "Threads from #N" with its Undo, then one row per thread, the branch row's box, title line with an inline rename (`RenameThread`) and "this one", the open fork's last message and time with "since #N", its characters' faces; a set the shown fork is outside is read from one of its forks. Under a section the Branches list is always headed. **The timeline**: `timeline.threads` (order 30, after the summaries) puts a divider row after S, "Parallel threads from here: Mira and Tobin (this one) · Docks", the others links (`?fork=`, the panel kept; a middle-click opens a new tab), with Undo. **Undo** (`useUndoThreads`): `UndoThreads`, the bin's toast with its Undo (restore), and a tab showing a removed thread follows to the branch they were started in; another tab showing one gets the server's Reload and the deleted-branch fallback. **The left panel**: the shell's new `threads` section lists the forks of shown sets (`ShellFork.threads`) by last message; `pinnedBranches`, `peers` and `other` leave them out, and a chat's "⑂ N" (`ShellFork.branches`) doesn't count a new thread's forks. Its rows carry `ShellFork.thread` (the innermost shown thread's name and characters, read by `threadLabels` for the returned rows only), so the panel's foot and the chat-scoped list show a "Threads" group before the branches, rows named as the header names them ("Open thread Docks"), without the branch rename or "Make this branch its own chat". **Notes**: on the chat's own notes in a thread, `chatNoteActions`' "Also change it in “Docks”" copies the note as this thread has it saved to the other thread's newest message on (`CopyNoteToBranch`, writer `db/noteCopyWrites.ts`: the note's revision binding inserted at the target fork's tip; false when it's the same there; NotFound for another chat's fork or the same one). Tests: `test/threads.test.ts` (client: names, which forks are branches, the dialog's rows, defaults, refusals and line, one read per fork and version, the transform's row and the trigger), the server's `test/threads.test.ts` (each thread's cast, the shell's Threads list, labels and ⑂ count, the note copy), `e2e/threads.spec.ts` (1440 and 390, light and dark: starting at the newest and at an earlier message, the header, popover or sheet, timeline row and left panel with layout audits, rename, switching by link with bounded reads, a middle-click to a new tab, a second tab on a thread that's undone, Undo and restore, a chat with a branch beside the threads, the note copy).
    - **Threads client review** (review-threads3, 2026-11-12). Thread reads discard answers superseded by a newer request, so an older in-flight read cannot restore an undone set or evict the newer cache entry. Start validation includes cast members played by the user (personas outside the cast still need a cast character), and its earlier-message explanation names every cast member assigned out, preserves pre-existing absences, and states that speakers retain their own messages. Undo's explanations state that the continuing branch keeps its messages, new threads and their messages go to the bin, and descendant branches stay. The Threads section scrolls within half the viewport height so ten sets remain reachable on phone sheets. Its open links and the left panel's rows use the existing app context menu actions; left-panel thread links also support middle-click. `branchControlParts.tabTitle` extends browser and workbench titles without another fork read; the threads feature supplies “Thread: <name>”. Shell thread labels accompany a returned fork in every section (including ordinary chat lists), keeping the row identical wherever `WatchShellForks`' fork-id reducer sees it. Their characters are included once in `people` even after leaving the latest cast, and the client resolves those historical names separately from the latest cast. Labels read each distinct member once, independent of the number of its returned fork rows; the query-count regression compares one and 300 rows. **Note copying** still copies saved content, explicitly explained on the action. It checks the destination's replacing-note claim within the same writer transaction and refuses with `EditRefused` on conflict. A changed copy creates a saved revision with the destination's previous revision as first parent and the copied revision as second parent, then binds that revision at the destination's latest message. This preserves the destination's History and its existing Restore action; identical document hashes are a no-op. It does not copy or discard either branch's drafts. No baseline change. Regressions cover out-of-order reads, user-played cast members, copy/restore and replacement conflicts, shell snapshots and incremental rename/Undo/restore/purge, explicit scope probes, and shell reads at 3,000 messages / 300 branches / ten splits with a bounded page across 31 chats. Browser tests add lifecycle request limits in sibling tabs, a deliberately reintroduced read-loop failure, ten-set reachability, titles, stale purged URLs, app context menus and middle-clicks, with 1440/390 light/dark audits on the changed surfaces. This entry supersedes the earlier TH3 descriptions of section-only shell labels, direct revision rebinding and Undo wording; `spec/` remains the retained proposal and is unchanged by this review.
    - **Sending to several threads** (spec/THREADS.md §6, TH4). **Write**: `SendToThreads` (command `thread.send`, writer `db/chatSetupWrites.ts`), one transaction for 2–32 targets, the thread the user is in first. Each target names a fork the user owns, distinct, and every pair must be different threads of a set they share (`separateThreads` in `db/threads.ts`: on each fork's path, a split where they have different ordinals), else `ThreadsRefused` and nothing is written. Each copy is exactly an append there through `sendOrQueue` (the body of `SendOrQueue`, extracted): the first target's under the tip the tab read (`LeafMoved` otherwise), the others' under their tip now; posted at once, or queued behind a reply still generating with `queued_messages.send_group`, which `postQueued` turns into the `thread_sends` row when it posts. A posted copy gets its `thread_sends` row (`group_id`, a uuidv7, shared by all) and its reply (its speaker, round and Auto flag as that thread's Next planned it; none for No one). The other targets are written first and the first one last, so the chat's current fork stays the one the user is in; the composer's draft is committed once, with the first copy. The API (`api/threads.ts` `send`) refuses up front with `GenerationUnavailable` when a reply is wanted and no model is set, rewrites each copy's text as a send there would, starts each reply's generation after the commit (generations in different forks run in parallel, each assembled from its own fork's path only), and publishes each posted entry, the chat and the queue. A copy carries `PathEntry.copies` (the other copies' slot and fork, `sendCopies` over `thread_sends` with live slots and forks), so a deleted copy drops out of the others' links. **Client** (`features/threads/sendTargets.ts`, `SendToThreadsChip.tsx`, `copies.tsx`): the strip's `composer.threads` chip (order 35), only in a thread, "To this thread ▾"; its popover "Send to threads" lists the other threads of every set the shown fork is in, innermost first, each once, with a live fork (`offeredThreads`), a tick, its characters' faces and, ticked, "Writes as" ("As there": that thread's composer speaker, or any of the user's cards and the cast). Ticks are kept per tab and fork shown until unticked, so a run of messages to both needs them once; ticked, the chip reads "To 2 threads" and Send's hover adds "here and in “At the docks”". A send then goes through the composer's **send-route registry** (`composerSendRoutes` in `composerControls.tsx`: `takes`, `hint`, `send`, `subscribe`; `useSendRoute` reads the route's id and hint as the store's snapshot), which plans each other thread as its own composer would (`GetCast`, `ReadPath`, `OpenComposer`, `GetComposerChoice`, `planReply`), consumes a one-reply pick there, and calls `session.sendToThreads`. **Afterwards**: the header's `message.also-in` detail, "Also in At the docks", links each copy (`?fork=…&slot=…`; a middle-click opens a new tab); the editor's **save-option registry** (`messageSaveOptions` in `editorHistory.tsx`) adds "Save in both" (or "Save in all 3") beside a Save then labelled "Save here", for an edit of a user-written copy: it saves here, then amends each other copy in its own fork (`AmendVersion`, or `EditVersion` when the copy's shown version is no longer the user's own), with a toast naming any copy that changed or went; the delete toast's **offer registry** (`messageDeleteOffers` in `messageActions.tsx`, `useDeletedToast`'s extra actions) adds "Delete the copy in “At the docks” too" for a message deleted whole. Tests: server `test/threadSends.test.ts` (two replies generating at once, each request built from its own thread only; the links; the current fork stays; a swipe stays in its thread; delete drops the link; a copy queued behind a running reply posts with its group; No one; Stop in one and a failure in the other independent; refusals write nothing), `test/isolation.test.ts` (another user's forks), client `test/threads.test.ts` (offered threads, ticks), `e2e/threadSends.spec.ts` (the chip and popover with layout audits at 390 light and 1440 dark; ticking, Writes as, Send's hover, two replies, the link both ways, Save in both, deleting the other copy).
    - **Joining threads** (spec/THREADS.md §7, TH5). A join is a merge (§12 "Merging another chat into this one") whose source is another thread of this branch: `mergePlan` (`db/merges.ts`) recognises it by `joinSplit` (`db/threads.ts`: of the splits both forks see, the innermost where they're different threads, with the source's thread there) and then calls it by its thread's name (`threadTitle`: its name, else its characters at S, else "Thread 2"), names only that thread's present characters in the templates, refuses "Nothing new in “At the docks” since it was last joined." and "“At the docks” has nothing since the threads parted.", and adds to the preview `thread`, `back` (the thread's characters away here at J, who are back from J on), `timelines` (in a chat with one shared context the request's choice, together by default, with `choosesTimelines`; `separate` with separate contexts, the Context setting, `contextPerSpeaker`) and, when separate, `views`: per cast member (narrators and the user's own cards left out) the section it reads through `viewedJoin` and whether it reads any (`readable`). The digest covers the position too. **Write**: `JoinThreads` (command `thread.join` in `api/merges.ts`; the writer's own `JoinThreads`, which shares `MergeChat`'s body, `merged` in `db/merges.ts`, and answers each join's `MergeResult` in order): one transaction, a J per thread, each planned at the position previewed and written below the previous (consecutive); a fork twice is refused ("Each thread can be joined once at a time."), and so is a source that isn't another thread of this branch. `writeMerge` writes each J as a merge does (the J slot, the cast union, `participant.join`, `chat_merges` with `timelines` (the join's own choice: `separate` only when chosen in a shared-context chat, so a chat switched to one shared context later reads its other joins whole) and `split_id`, the frozen `chat_merge_messages` with `source_version_id` and `media_json`, the image ids of the version copied) plus `away.set { away: false }` at J for `back`. Deleting a J restores the away marks with it (they're its slot's events). **Reads**: `ThreadsOf` gives each other thread `joined` when a join of it is on the asked fork's display path (not deleted): the latest join's slot, its number there and `upToDate` (the thread's fork still ends where that join's `source_tip_slot_id` pinned it). The timeline row (`MergedChatRow.tsx`) reads "Joined “At the docks” · 2 messages" with the threads icon when `MergeInfo.thread` is set. **Client**: `MergeChatDialog.tsx` takes a source picker (`threads`, `MergeSourcePickerProps`) for its thread mode, "Join threads", so `features/chat` doesn't import the threads feature: several sources at once, previewed together (each "What comes in" block, the cast's union, "How the characters see it" (in a chat with one shared context a choice, "Everyone reads both threads" or "Each character reads only its own thread", sent as `timelines`; with separate contexts a line), "What the model reads" with a **For** select over `views` when separate; one source keeps the title and framing fields, several come in under their names with the preset's line), **Join** calls `JoinThreads` and the toast says "Joined “At the docks”" or "Joined 2 threads". `features/threads/JoinThreadsDialog.tsx` is the picker ("Threads to join": the other threads of the shown fork's sets, innermost first, `otherThreads`, each with its faces and what joining brings from its own `PreviewChatMerge`, "2 messages since #3" or "3 new messages since the last join", else the refusal and disabled; the only joinable one is ticked already) and registers `message.join-thread` ("Join a thread here…", place group) and ⋯ `chat.join-threads` ("Join threads…"), both offered while another thread has something not joined here (`joinOffered`). The Threads section's row adds "Joined at #5", and the send chip leaves out a thread joined with nothing new since (`offeredThreads`). The threads' RPCs and commands (`StartThreads`, `ThreadsOf`, `RenameThread`, `UndoThreads`, `CopyNoteToBranch`, `SendToThreads`, `JoinThreads`; `thread.start`, `thread.send`, `thread.join`) are classified in `agent/exposures/exclusions.ts` as not exposed to the workshop agent in W6 (writes without an approved undo adapter, `ThreadsOf` a read outside its first exposures). With the default empty join prompt her assembled request is unchanged at the join. A character that knows any projected joined row keeps private addresses. Private numeric arguments name exact current known view coordinates; a missing coordinate never skips to a later row. Source offsets (`joined_from`) are unavailable in private views. Missed, nonexistent, out-of-range and stale opaque addresses/queries all answer `No earlier messages match.` without a title, source position, ids, timestamps, last-message number or list of available ranges.

      Opaque addresses in new runs remain stable across replies, re-joins and missed insertions when the known prefix does not change, including an own source line joining another thread that was already private (source version ids supply its original identities). A known insertion, selected version or knowledge change invalidates affected later addresses; removed addresses cannot resolve to a missed row. View numbers are labels rather than address suffixes; allowed own-storyline gaps can change them while the opaque address stays stable. Legacy numeric coordinates can move after an edit; opaque addresses are preferred. The registered tools share a `snapshot` hook (`RolloutTool.snapshot`, `prepareToolSnapshots`), so overriding/disabling them also replaces their projection.

      **Constant snapshot and cold preflight** (threads6, 2026-11-13; no baseline change). Before `StartRollout`, reader `HistoryProjectionNeeded` checks just the chat's join slots against the causal display path's structural runs and placed insertions, their effective deletion/hide/selection, and frozen-row knowledge including away corrections and stretch views. It reads metadata, never the path's message prose or swipes. Unaffected paths and viewers skip full projection; their tool reads stay lazy. The probe retains the same speaker exception as row projection after earlier-split away corrections, including a join whose selected swipe/regeneration is authored by the viewer. A negative probe, or a positive probe whose subsequent projection is ordinary (for example a join hidden between the two reads), saves a 17-byte `{ "ordinary": true }` marker: reads stay lazy, but an edit racing the first tool call cannot introduce unfrozen private coordinates. Such a newly private map answers no match in that run and on Resume; ordinary maps keep all existing behavior. Hidden separate joins still define the stretch for visible together joins, so they participate in preflight stretch detection even though their own rows are not sent. An affected run prepares its path once in a reader, hands it to the session in memory (`Generation.agentToolState`), and never rereads it in the run. No projection, hash computation or history allocation is inside a writer transaction.

      The immutable snapshot stores only `{ "digest": "<64 hex digits>" }` under `agentToolState["history.private"]`: **77 bytes per private reply**, independent of view length, id length and prose. It commits with full SHA-256 to the seed and ordered `(immutable identity, view number)` address map; an unverifiable view keeps only its refusal flag. Ordinary preflights keep only the constant 17-byte marker above; it costs no history read on Resume either. This replaces review-threads5's O(known rows) identity list (93,735 bytes for 2,402 known rows with realistic 36-byte ids in `threadSummariesScale`). It adds no table, column, reference or cleanup resource: the digest belongs to the existing rollout snapshot and follows its retention/deletion and chat-purge lifecycle, including the existing retained rollout evidence for binned/purged individual versions and branches.

      **Causal tool stretches** (review-threads6). `KnowersOf` accepts the tool's frozen `leafSlotId`; it, indexed `SearchChat` and `HistoryProjectionNeeded` bound stretch discovery to that leaf. A later separate join on the same fork cannot retroactively filter an earlier shared-context passage or invalidate its frozen digest. Both ordinary frozen searches and private thawed reads have regressions for this case. Summary planning retains its full planning-fork scope when no causal bound is supplied, preserving private continuity before a join.

      Resume, a step edit and `RebuildContext` replay recompute at the snapshot's original causal leaf. An identical map reads identical addresses/numbers with current known text, as ordinary tools do. A changed map conservatively invalidates **all** old message reads/searches to `No earlier messages match.`, including numeric 1; it never adds a newly known row or redirects a stale coordinate. For example, Wren's frozen shared beginning plus two docks lines reads as before after a later join beyond the frozen leaf. A known insertion before either line changes the map, so even an earlier unchanged address now answers no match; restoring the original map makes the original address usable again. This trades partial availability after edits for fixed storage and fails closed across deletion, swipe, insertion, knowledge correction and Undo. It does not alter the already recorded transcript. No provider request includes the digest; assembler version stays **67**, with unchanged definitions and initial request bytes. The changed tool results subsequently enter requests normally. `threadSummariesScale` records before/after snapshot bytes, cold/cached/thawed reads, unaffected preflight costs, Generate-to-first-text latency against an immediate loopback provider with paired eager-preparation controls, and actual `StartRollout` transaction hold time in a helper worker at 300 branches, two 3,000-message threads and 20–50 swipes.

Message search/read retain the same refusal when a readable frozen row is a nested joined transcript or its source provenance cannot be verified; recursively addressing that transcript is not built. Readable frozen messages condensed by a source summary can instead be searched/read without exposing the summary's range. The stored `stretch_before_slot_id` and the shared stretch resolver are unchanged. Definitions, including numeric/string address schemas, are byte-identical across views.     - **Threads TH8 review** (historical; its uniform message refusal is superseded by threads5 above; review-threads4, 2026-11-13; assembler version **66**, **BASELINE CHANGED**, fresh deploy). There is one stretch-membership mechanism: `db/threadStretches.ts` resolves the viewed fork's effective live joins into display-path chain intervals, bounded by the causal leaf for replies.     - A slot's row version as a fork shows it is the slot's plus the newest seq of the fork's selection, replacement, deletion and visibility overrides (`slotInFork`, `selectionIn`): it moves with the fork's choice, amend, hide or restore and never with another's, so a tab of G isn't refused for something done in F. Every per-fork write takes a newer seq, so it only grows. `AddSelectedVersion` checks the same value that path entries carry, along with `shownForkId`, the fork whose choices they show. Image-version regression tests cover writing after hide, unhide and restore, rejecting older editors and keeping sibling forks unchanged.
    - Deleting a swipe is the deleting fork's (§3.11); only when no live fork shows it does it also select a neighbour in the forks in the bin that showed it (the bin writer), and so does deleting one for good in every fork that showed it. An ST re-import writes its file's fork only, with origin `import`; effective local choices in that fork stop it (§13).
    - **Copies and flags** (unit 4; `db/baseline.ts`). A fork's copy of a version (`versions.fork_id`) is shown only where a fork's effective `replace` names it, in its original's place: in the path, the picker (`ListVersions`), the assembler (where it counts as its original: a swipe's number and count, `{{currentSwipeId}}` and `{{lastSwipeId}}`, are the message's own versions'), LCM's paths and freshness, notes, a fork's tip text, the alternates' first words, chat summaries and bin excerpts (`shownInSql`, `shownJoin` in `db/forkState.ts`: the selection, then the replacement of what it selects, each one probe). Replacements are keyed by the message's own version, not by position, so a fork made later inherits an amend from any point of the parent's path (§2.3 of the delta). A state event attached to a version applies where the fork selects it or shows it as its copy (`attachedApplies`). Stars and picker flags are `star` and `picker_hide` overrides on the message's own version, read through the lineage like a selection; the version's own columns are the base. Deleting a copy deletes the swipe it stands in for (the message's own version, with every fork's copies of it), and deleting that for good empties the copies too (§3.11). New ST re-imports keep the shared suffix and write only the file fork's selection override. The legacy suffix-copy helper (`stImportFork.ts`) is retained only to resume old interrupted records that already started copying (§13). `test/forkVersions.test.ts`, `test/forkVersionsReimport.test.ts`.
    - Readers take the fork they're in: the one named, else, for a read at a slot or leaf (`GetSlot`, `ListBranches`, `StateEventsAt`, the assembler, LCM's operations), the fork through it (`forkAt`: the current fork if its path holds it, else the most recently current one whose does), provided once per operation as `ForkView` (`atLeaf`; `AssembleContext` also takes a `forkId`). What reads the chat's current line (groups, chat summaries, bin excerpts, a fork's tip text) reads the current fork's or that fork's own.
  - **Generations and queued messages** record their fork: a generation the fork it was started in (`GenerationRequest.forkId`: a send's, a swipe's or continue's, a queued reply's), which its context is read in, its summaries are planned in before and after it (the Summarizer's position carries it to `PlanSummaries` and the enqueue writes), and its rollout records, so the user chatting in another fork meanwhile changes nothing in it; without one, the current fork when its path holds the reply's leaf, else the most recent fork through it. A queued message records the fork it was sent in, where it posts later (§12).
- **Paths are read in windows.** `GetPath` reads the last `limit` depths of the path (at most 1000): only the segments reaching into them, then a range of `slots_chain` per segment, so its cost depends on the window and the branch points inside it, not the chat's length. Deleted messages count toward the limit but aren't returned, so a window can be short or empty; `olderLeafSlotId` is where the next older window ends, null at the root.
  - Measured on a 2,001-slot chat: a 200-slot window takes about 22 ms end to end (before chains, walking up parents; the window's rows are the same). `test/graph.test.ts` checks that paging back reconstructs the whole path without gaps, and `test/pathScale.test.ts` does it for a 100,000-slot path with 200 branch points, in windows of 1,000 and, through the branch points, of 7. The bound is checked without a clock, since a 40 ms budget failed at load averages of 40 to 60. Cycles are planted among slots older than a window (with the schema's trigger dropped): a parent link, and a chain head's parent pointing below its own chain. A walk past its limit would never end, so a window must still come back, read in a child process (`test/support/windowProbe.ts`) that is killed if it stalls, since nothing else stops SQLite mid-statement. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` of GetPath's query (`pathWindow` in `reads.ts`) must show every table reached by index, the slots by a range of `slots_chain`.
  - A window is read as its fork shows it: each slot's selection, the replacement of what it selects and that version's two flags are one probe of `fork_steps` each, so it costs the window, not the chat's length, the fork's depth, its forks or its overrides. `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows each step found by `fork_steps`' primary key.
  - Rows visited are counted (`test/pathScale.test.ts`: temporary views shadow `slots`, `versions`, `state_events`, `forks`, `fork_overrides`, `fork_labels` and `fork_steps` and count each row read, which keeps their indexes usable) on fixtures of 2,000 and 100,000 slots that differ only in length, each with 200 forks, lineages 40 deep, 20,000 selection overrides, 10,000 stars and the chat's first fork's copies of its last ten messages, which forks made from it inherit, plus a chain of 160 forks below the deepest. A 200-slot window visits 1,222 rows at the tip and 1,262 through 40 branch points as the slots' own selections show it; in the fork 40 deep, 1,249 and 1,665 (with the lineage, 2,432 and 2,684), and 1,249 at the tip 200 forks deep, the same in both fixtures.
  - Reading all 2,001 slots in one call took 113 ms, of which the SQL was 13 ms; at 20,000 slots the SQL alone is about 180 ms. Hence the windows.
  - **By position** (spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §2.3, unit 3). A window is the last `limit` positions of the fork's display path (`PathEntry.position`, from 0; `depth` stays structural), so a fork that places insertions is read through its pieces: `GetPath` and `ReadPath` (`readDisplay` in `reads.ts`) take the pieces up to the display end for a null leaf, up to a named leaf (the tip included) where the fork shows it, or along the path to a leaf it doesn't show, then read the positions in the window with `displayWindow`: the overlapping pieces as JSON driving one range of `slots_chain` per structural stretch and one lookup by id per inserted slot. The cursors (`olderLeafSlotId`, `older`, `newer`) are the slots at the positions next to the window, which may be inserted ones; `Around` a slot outside the requested path opens a fork that shows it (`forkThrough`), as before; a target past an explicitly named leaf is outside that path even when it is on the same fork's full display path. `test/forkInsert.test.ts` covers that boundary with and without insertions in the initially viewed fork. A fork that places none (`placedInsertions` is empty: one range probe per lineage entry, walked by parent) is read exactly as before (`pathWindow`), its positions its depths, so chats without insertions read the same rows. The cost with insertions is the branch points, the fork's insertions on the path and the window: every read reads all of them, because positions count from the root. `walkTowards` and its only-child check ignore inserted children. `ListForks` and the writes that return a fork (`forkOut`) take each fork's tip text from the last message it shows (`lastShown` and `withDisplayEnd` in `db/forks.ts`): an inserted slot after the tip when everything structural after its anchor is gone from the fork's view, skipping inserted ones deleted there; the tip itself stays structural. `test/forkInsert.test.ts` pages `GetPath` (windows of 1 to 100) and `ReadPath` (`Bottom` then `Older`, `Around` then `Newer` and `Older`) through a fork with insertions above the first message, nested, mid-path, deleted and after the tip, checking every entry's position, and checks a fork without insertions numbers by depth and the forks' tip texts. `test/pathScale.test.ts` adds a fork with 1,000 insertions (every tenth below the one before) to the 2,000- and 100,000-slot fixtures: paging back by 1,000 at the tip and by 7 through the branch points reconstructs the display path built from first principles; the rows visited are the same in both fixtures: 602 for the segments (201 branch points), 3,003 for the insertion lookup (each insertion's row, slot and anchor, and the fork's lineage walked by parent), and 1,267 and 1,312 for 200-position windows at the tip and around depth 1,100; and `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` of the insertion lookup shows `fork_overrides_point` on `(fork_id, kind)` and no table scan.
- **Append cost.** About 2.6 ms per message end to end, including the RPC hop and a commit with a full flush (`synchronous = FULL`, ZFS).

**Summaries belong to the viewed fork's state** (fork independence unit 7; `db/lcmFork.ts`, §16). Summary material and revisions remain shared immutable records. `summary_revision` and `summary_choice` overrides select text and replacements through the same bounded lineage as messages; the shared selected revision is frozen by a database trigger. Summary reads and UI actions accept `forkId`, including coverage at a shared tip. A summary's optimistic row version includes its effective revision and choice sequences, so another fork's edit doesn't invalidate the tab's base. A fork created later inherits the choice, however deep. Queue rows and their rollouts record the planning fork; assembly, completion, failure, startup recovery and completion planning retain it. Queue overlap and serial ordering, reply maintenance pins, scheduling coalescence and backfill approval/pause/spending are per fork.

**Known limits:**
- **Operations addressed only by a leaf choose their fork** (`forkAt`): the current fork when its path holds the leaf, else the most recently current one through it. Two forks at the same tip need an explicit fork to disambiguate. Summary UI calls provide it; a background summary job uses its stored fork. Legacy synthetic jobs with null provenance retain the current-fork fallback.

- **`StateEventsAt` reads every event on the path,** because state can come from any ancestor. Since chains it no longer walks to the root (that was linear in chat length, roughly 180 ms of SQL at 20,000 slots): at the tip of the scale fixtures, with 200 branch points and 56 events applying, it visits 715 rows at 2,000 and at 100,000 slots, where the walk visited 2,310 and 100,310. A chat with events on most messages still costs their number; DATA-MODEL §5.2's checkpoints of folded state would bound that.
- **Results cost about 0.1 ms per path entry** to encode and decode as Schema classes across the worker boundary, and the decode side runs on the main thread. If large windows show up in the event-loop budget, the transfer types should become plain structs.

### 3.9 Library operations

Versioned documents (DESIGN §4, DATA-MODEL §3) for cards, presets, lorebooks, notes and preset overlays. Every kind forks the same way: a fork is an entity of its own (spec/LIBRARY-FORKS.md). Contracts are in `db/ops.ts`, writes in `db/libraryWrites.ts`, reads in `db/reads.ts`, and the logic both share in `db/library.ts`. Domain types are in `@rp/shared/library.ts`; the merge is in `@rp/shared/merge.ts`.

**The model.**
- **Revisions** are immutable snapshots with parents, like git commits.
