- **Refs** are movable pointers. Every entity has exactly one (`entity_refs.entity_id` is `UNIQUE`, and never moves): its head, its label and subtitle, its import source and the revision it last merged (`merge_base_revision_id`).
- **A fork is an entity of its own** (libfork, 2026-11-06; spec/LIBRARY-FORKS.md), for every kind: its lineage is on its entity row (`entities.forked_from_entity_id`, `forked_from_revision_id`, `forked_at`, `forked_in_chat_id`, 0056), and it has its own ref, revisions, tags, archive and bin state. `LibraryRef.parentEntityId` is that parent ("variant" on screen for presets and lorebooks). Nothing flows between a fork and its parent except an explicit merge.
- **What a ref merges from** (its source, `parent_ref_id` in `refSelect`): its own import line when it has one; otherwise its live parent's ref. Its merge base is `merge_base_revision_id`, or before its first merge the revision it was forked from.
- **An entry follows its imports.** Imports form their own line of revisions, each one's parent the previous import. The entry merges the latest import, and its merge base is the import it last merged. So a re-import merges with edits made on the entry itself, as a fork's merge does.
- **"Update available"** is derived, not stored: the source's head differs from the merge base. A card fork shows it only for its own imports (its parent's new versions are in the card's Merge panel); presets, lorebooks and notes show it for their parent too.
- Documents are any JSON object for now. Per-kind schemas arrive with the importers (PLAN phase 1).
- A content hash over canonical JSON (sorted keys) means identical edits and repeated imports add no document revision. Accepting a new parent revision writes a merge revision and record even if its content stays the same; an unchanged merge source is `up_to_date`.

**Operations.**
- **Writes:**
  - `CreateEntity`
  - `EditRef`: a new revision on the head, with `expectedRowVersion`. It commits its draft even when it changes nothing.
  - `ForkRef`: a non-card fork from the ref's head (`forkEntity` in `db/libraryWrites.ts`, the step every kind's fork shares): a new entity of the same kind with one revision, `parents: []`, origin `user`, `origin_ref` `{"forked": <source revision>}`, the message `Forked from <label · subtitle>`; the lineage above; the source's tags; no copied revisions (its History runs on through the source's, `RefHistory` below), import source, archive state or `last_used_at`. Cards are refused (`RefOperationRefused`): they fork with their names (`ForkCard`). `ForkWithDrafts` (the editor's Make a variant) is this, then moves the ref's unsaved fields to the fork.
  - `ForkCard`, `SetCardParent`: card forks, below
  - `ImportFile` (§11.1): a new import revision, merged into the entry; it returns the entry's outcome; forks stay unchanged. The HTTP import route refuses a new file version for a preset or lorebook fork (409: it takes new versions by merging from its original); a card fork can take a new version of a card file wholesale ("Import a new version…", §11), its note with it, which starts its own import line.
  - `MergeFollowed` and `PreviewMerge`: legacy update paths share the explicit merger's refusal of manually linked parents without a known merge base.
  - `ResolveMerge`: commit a hand-resolved merge, refused if the followed ref moved again since the preview or a manually linked parent has no known merge base.
  - `SetEntityTags`: folders; `persona` is the persona folder
  - `SetEntityArchived`
  - `SetRefArchived`: archives or restores the ref's entity, so a fork alone, returning the ref; archiving again keeps the first time (`coalesce`). One writer transaction; the client's `SetRefArchived` (editorApi) is this, as the user.
- **Reads:**
  - `ListLibrary`: by kind, tag and archive state, forks included
  - `GetRef`
  - `RefHistory`: the ref's line, a git branch's log (owner, DESIGN §4 [D] 2026-11-06): the first-parent chain, and from a fork's first revision (`parents: []`, `origin_ref` `{"forked": <rev>}` equal to its entity's `forked_from_revision_id`) on into the revision it was forked from and that entity's line, through every fork back to the first original (`previousRevisionSql` in `db/revisionNumbers.ts`, one recursive query). The original's later revisions aren't on it. An inherited revision carries `entry` (its entity, ref, label and subtitle; no ref when that entry is in the bin or gone), and a fork's first revision `forkedFrom` (the revision and entry it was forked from). The `before` cursor and inherited Restore revisions must be reachable on this actual line; belonging to an ancestor entity alone is insufficient. `revisionNumber` counts the same line, so numbers run on across fork points.
  - `PreviewMerge`: the resolver's view
  - `CardFamily`, `LibraryGenealogy`: the family, below
- No chat-scoped copies: a chat uses library entries as they are (DESIGN §6.1), and a chat's own notes are §3.10's.
- **Ownership** is enforced as in §3.8. Binned entities and chats are `NotFound`.

**Archive, last modified and last used** (the preset pickers', §12; the owner, 2026-11-01). Every `LibraryRef` carries `updatedAt` (`entity_refs.updated_at`: the head moved, by an edit, an import or a merge, or a rename), `archivedAt` (`entities.archived_at`, per entity, so per user: an entity has one owner) and `lastUsedAt` (`entity_refs.last_used_at`). All three columns were in the baseline, so no schema changed. `ListLibrary` returns the archived or the other entries; archiving changes neither `updatedAt` nor `rowVersion`, and an archived preset in use stays in use: assembly never reads `archived_at`. **Last used** is recorded by `StartRollout`, in its transaction: the preset ref its context snapshot names (`$.inputs.preset.ref`, read back from the row just written, so the snapshot isn't bound again), when the ref is the user's. Before that nothing recorded which preset a generation used, apart from its snapshot, and nothing fills the column in for generations made before: the database starts fresh from the baseline (§3.7). A model's last use needs no column: `ListModelUse` (reader) groups the user's `generation` requests in `llm_requests` by connection and model through the `llm_requests_owner` index. `test/presetPicker.test.ts`: archive and unarchive as the owner and not as another user, the first archive time kept, a variant archived alone, the preset in use still the account's and the next request's, `updatedAt` moving with a rename and not with archiving, last used after a reply, the model's last use.

**Card archive and bulk review** (cardarchive, 2026-11-06; DESIGN §2.1). Cards reuse `entities.archived_at` and `SetRefArchived`. **BASELINE CHANGED** (review-cardarchive, 2026-11-07): the covering `entity_revisions_activity` index keeps revision origin, parent and date reads off document overflow pages; no columns or tables changed, and no migration is supplied (§3.7). Stars are retained independently of archive state. `ShellCards` keeps archived cards (personas included) in a separate `archived` array; normal `cards`/`personas`, `ListCards`, `ListCardUsage` and live `ListLibrary` exclude them. Existing chat casts retain archived definitions. `ListArchiveCandidates` runs `db/cardArchive.ts` in a reader worker: card summaries, indexed version participation with human messages/nonempty replies (excluding greetings, including unselected retained versions), user-authored card revisions, draft timestamps and fork timestamps determine last use, without loading message text or card documents. Card field edits (including persisted drafts) and forking count; creation alone does not. Before a fork relationship is unlinked or changed, its timestamp is retained in both cards’ `entity_refs.last_used_at`, so changing lineage cannot make either card never used or move its last use backwards. Imported initial model messages count as greetings; binned chat history counts until purged. Added uses the same arrival date as the shell. Favourites and archived/binned cards are excluded. The shared `cardArchiveCriteria` registry supplies criterion labels, defaults and predicates (never used after N days; previously used but inactive N calendar months); criteria combine with OR. Calendar-month subtraction clamps to the last day of a shorter target month, preserving the UTC time of day; it never rolls the cutoff into the next month (`shared/test/cardArchive.test.ts`). `ArchiveUnusedCards` re-runs eligibility in one writer transaction, then archives selected eligible ids with one timestamp. Its receipt contains only changed ids and that timestamp; `UndoCardArchive` restores only owned live cards still carrying it, so repeated Undo and a later rearchive are safe. No content, revisions, labels or stars change. Contracts live in editorApi and db/ops; foreign ids never change another owner’s cards. `test/cardArchive.test.ts` covers discovery reads, existing cast, stars, ownership, eligibility races, 5,000-card preview and conditional batch Undo.

**Explicit library merges** (forkmerge, 2026-11-02; `db/forkMerge.ts`, `db/forkMergeWrites.ts`, `@rp/shared/forkMerge.ts`). Parent edits, imports, saves, restores and merges never change child heads. Every kind's parent is its entity's `forked_from_entity_id`, and its original revision `forked_from_revision_id` (libfork, 2026-11-06: presets, lorebooks and notes used to keep both on the ref, as `follows_ref_id` and `entity_refs.forked_from_revision_id`); `merge_base_revision_id` advances only on an explicit merge. Until an entry has its own import line, its parent's head is its merge source; an own import line then takes precedence. A parent linked manually without a known fork revision (`SetCardParent`) refuses merging; relinking clears a previous parent merge base (retaining an own import base) and advances the ref row version. A merge record's parent revision (`library_merges.theirs_revision_id`) is cleared when the parent is purged, so a fork's merge history survives it. No migration is supplied: the database starts fresh from the baseline.

- Reader operations and authenticated RPCs: `ForkMergeStatus` returns parent, base, the new parent versions newest first along its first-parent line and merge records; `PreviewForkMerge` takes an optional `theirsRevisionId`, defaults to the latest, and returns base/ours/theirs, the clean merged document, changed units and conflicts. Only versions since the current base are allowed, never arbitrary revisions supplied by a caller. Both run in reader workers. `LibraryGenealogy` returns the same full family from any member, with stable node identities, parent identities, ref links, states, fork revision/date and latest non-undone merge time. Every kind reads it from `libraryFamily` (below), retaining purged members with no ref.
- `CommitForkMerge` rechecks the preview's child row version, base and selected parent revision inside one writer transaction. The selection has `excluded` unit paths (keep ours) and `resolutions` for each included conflict (omitted value deletes). Units are changed scalar fields, keyed elements such as prompts/entries, and `$order` paths. Array-order conflicts resolve ordering separately from element content. Documents must validate, protected fields must come from a side, named resources must belong to the user, and merges never grant regex approval or agent edit permissions. The `library.merge` policy is registered through the shared registry in both workers; disabling it refuses the new merge operations.
- Active field drafts refuse previews and commits, including legacy explicit update application, with Save/Discard instructions. After saving, the refreshed preview compares saved revisions. Exclusion advances the base with everything else: excluded changes are accepted as deliberately omitted and are not offered again unchanged on the next merge.
- Accepted explicit merges write a normal revision with `[oldHead, selectedParentRevision]` and a `library_merges` record: child ref, old head, prior base, selected parent revision/source ref, choices, time and undo revision. The next base is the selected parent revision. Legacy clean `MergeFollowed`/re-import and hand-resolved `ResolveMerge` also record merges; their selection is empty because the legacy resolver submits a complete document. Identical repeated imports do not create another import revision. No outcome flows to children; legacy follower result arrays are empty.
- `UndoForkMerge` requires the recorded merge at the current head, the current row version and no active drafts. It writes a compensating revision holding the pre-merge document (permissions stay restricted), marks the record undone and restores its prior base, including null. After later edits it refuses; ordinary history restore remains available for content without rewinding merge ancestry. History is never deleted.
- Tests: shared `forkMerge.test.ts` covers units, inclusion/exclusion, deletion, separate order resolutions, clean word merges, invalid choices and prototype-key data. Server `forkMerge.test.ts` covers historical versions, base advancement, records, undo, stale/foreign revisions, connected genealogy, drafts and staged creator updates on cards. The library/editor tests now explicitly merge each child; isolation probes include every new RPC.

The non-card Family dialog caps indentation after six levels while retaining nested folding, so deep descendants fit on phones and desktops (`e2e/libraryForkFamily.spec.ts`, with scoped layout audits). `test/libraryForkScale.test.ts` checks listings, genealogy, History paging and inherited Restore with 2,200 entries, including a 200-deep family; it runs in `server-slow`.

**Schema versions (interim, until per-kind migrations exist).** Every revision of an entity has the schema version it was created with. A re-import (`ImportFile`) refuses a document of another `schemaVersion` before writing anything, so no merge ever spans versions.

**Card names are revision content.** `name` is the display name, `nickname || name` is the model's name (CCv3), and `character_version` is the subtitle. For cards only, `entity_refs.label` and `subtitle` are derived query caches: database triggers refresh them on insertion, head movement and attempted metadata updates. Other entity kinds retain ordinary library labels. Existing label/subtitle RPC arguments remain compatible: card forks and `RenameRef` write standard fields in a new revision; card creation reads the document's names. The card editor edits all three through normal drafts and explicit Save, rather than a separate library rename. Fork names take precedence over unsaved name/version drafts; those drafts remain on the source, while other selected drafts move to the fork. Card forks are independent entities; they have no followers.

Cards' `label` and `subtitle` on `entity_refs` are caches of the head revision's standard fields (`name`, `character_version`); the `card_names_insert` and `card_names_update` triggers keep them in step, so a display-name change or a new head never leaves them stale. A display-name change preserves the former model name as `nickname` if there was none.

**Card summaries** (decisions1, 2026-11-02). What the card lists read of a card revision is in `card_summaries` (`db/baseline.ts`), one row per card revision, written by the `card_summaries_insert` trigger in the revision's own insert (and removed with it by `card_summaries_delete`), so no write path can leave one out: `fields`, the JSON array of `name`, `nickname`, `character_version`, `avatar_media_id`, `character_book.name`, `avatar_crop` and `extensions.talkativeness` as the document has them, `book` (it embeds a lorebook) and `book_entries`. Revisions are immutable, so a summary never goes stale. It's a table of its own rather than columns of `entity_revisions`, because SQLite reaches a column after `doc_json` only through that document's overflow pages, which is the read it saves. `cardSummary` in `db/cards.ts` reads a row as `parse` reads a document (anything malformed is empty); the shell's cards (`ShellCards`, `ShellForks`, `ShellLibrary`), `ListCards` and `CastCards` (`loadCastCards`), `ListCardUsage`, `ListChatGroups`, `castCardAt` and the chat list's card-name search read only these, never the documents. `loadCards`, which needs greetings and fields, still parses. Measured with `test/shellCardsScale.test.ts` (opt-in `SHELL_CARDS_SCALE=1`; 437 cards, one in eleven with an embedded lorebook; each read after a write so it computes again; medians of 15 at load 30–46 on 48 cores), master → this: at 4.3 MB of card documents GetShellCards 43 → 34 ms, `ListCards` 30 → 20 ms, `ListCardUsage` 26 → 23 ms; with 1,000-entry lorebooks (26.8 MB) GetShellCards 86 → 39 ms (its reader part 55 → 23 ms), `ListCards` 124 → 23 ms, `ListCardUsage` 52 → 22 ms, the same as with small cards. The synthetic ST scale folder (night/uiaudit/fixtures) is no longer on the dev host, so the test builds its own library of that size.

The client checks display-name/version pairs against live and archived library card refs for New card, Fork, a name/version edit and the card History browser’s Restore. Each submission reads those refs directly again before writing; same-origin browser tabs broadcast library invalidations and a focused tab refreshes its name check. It excludes the current ref and permits an imported collision when that pair is unchanged. The disabled action has a nearby explanation until either field differs. The client's check prevents sequential stale-tab submissions, without making simultaneous check/write pairs atomic. Imports and storage allow duplicates; `ForkCard` alone also checks on the server, in its transaction (above). Group members include the selected card version; Groups tiles on home show the member count, with the members' labels and versions in its tooltip. Chat sidebar summaries subscribe to library changes as well as chat changes. Chat search and summaries share `chatCast`: both resolve active-path bindings before reading display name, version and model name. Search filters before pagination, preserving literal substring matching and ASCII case folding. An SQL prefilter first narrows the chats to a superset of the matches (the title, the head of any ref of a participating card, or a revision a `card.binding` in the chat pins), so `chatCast` resolves only those; a search that matches nothing reads no casts.

History collision repair (nostartchat, 2026-11-04): selecting a library revision reads its saved document and checks card display name/version against live and archived cards. A collision is shown as a status in that revision’s comparison and disables its Restore action; submission still rechecks names against the server. Comparison controls are labelled “Revision comparison mode”, distinct from the “Revision changes” content.

**Card forks** (spec/CARD-FORKS-DELTA.md §2, unit 1; `db/cardForkWrites.ts`). A fork is a card of its own, as every kind's fork is (above): its own entity, ref, revisions, chats, tags, notes and bin state, tied to its parent only by the relationship on its entity row (0056), outside its content, so nothing flows between them: the fork takes no automatic updates, exposes parent versions through the explicit merge operations above, and edits to either never reach the other. What cards add is names: a card forks with a display name, model name and version (`ForkCard`), not a label, and `ForkRef` refuses cards.
- **`ForkCard`**, one writer transaction, from a card ref's head. Its display name (nonempty), in-character name and version accept the same unrestricted string lengths as the card document and `ForkCardForChat`; the dialog does not truncate them:
  - `forkEntity`'s steps (above): one revision in the new entity, `parents: []`, origin `user`, `origin_ref` `{"forked": <source revision>}`, the message `Forked from <name · version>`: the head's document with the three names given (`name`, `nickname`, `character_version`). Media ids, the embedded lorebook, `extensions.world`, modules and agent flags are in the document, so they come along; media rows are per user, not per entity, so nothing else is copied;
  - `forked_from_entity_id` and `forked_from_revision_id` (the source), `forked_at`;
  - the parent's tags, the persona folder included;
  - each of the parent's own notes (a note whose `owner.card` is the parent, not in the bin) as a fork of that note (`forkEntity`, so the copy can merge the original note's later changes): one revision from its head with `owner.card` the fork and the parent among its condition's cards changed to the fork (so a note on the card's own turn is on the fork's; the other cards stay), `origin_ref` naming it, its label and tags (DESIGN §4, owner's Q2: notes are forked with the card);
  - always (owner, 2026-11-02; no `moveDrafts` any more), the ref's unsaved fields but its three name fields, which the dialog decides and which stay on the parent, moved as §3.10's Unsaved note text goes with a fork: the parent goes back to its head, the text in each field's edit history. A draft that started from the revision copied starts from the fork's first revision, the same content; an older base stays the parent's revision. A draft's base is read from the ref's entity or any card in its parent chain, by `CommitEditorDrafts`, `SaveEditorDraft` and `GetRevision` alike (`draftBase` in `db/library.ts`), so typing on and the save dialog's comparison work on the fork, and a field the parent changed since the draft started still conflicts there.
  - It copies no revisions (its History runs on through the parent's, `RefHistory` above), no `source_path`/`source_hash` (a re-import never reaches it), no archive state, chats or `last_used_at`.
  - It's refused (`RefOperationRefused`, `EditRefused` over RPC) for a display name and version another of the user's cards has, live or archived and not in the bin, checked in the same transaction as the write: the same rule the client checks (below), so a fork made through the RPC can't skip it. Other kinds are refused: cards only, as the owner decided (Q3).
- **`ForkCardForChat`** (`db/cardForkWrites.ts`, `ChatSetupApi`): one writer transaction resolves the selected fork's state at the supplied slot, filters purged references with the same routing rules as `GetCast`, requires the source card in its cast, and copies the revision that `cardInChat` reads (including a pinned revision). It shares `ForkCard`'s copy steps and name/version clash check; the new entity records `forked_in_chat_id`. A fork-owned `card.swap` at slot null replaces the card through the existing lineage rules (§3.8). `note.activate`/`note.deactivate` events for copied notes are replayed onto the copies at their original slots and version attachments, owned by the selected fork, including switches on unselected versions or deleted slots so swiping or restoring retains them. Queued message speakers and reply speakers, and the composer's speaker and next-reply choice, move to the new card **only in that fork**; sibling forks' queues and composers remain theirs. Queue row versions advance so an old queue editor cannot silently undo the swap. Already-written message versions keep their speakers. `GetCast.cards` also retains earlier cards named by the line’s swaps when an authored version records them, so messages still show their original card’s name and avatar after a reload; `participants` and `playedByMe` define the active cast, card tabs and note groups. The API publishes `State`, the changed composer choices and the queue, and refreshes cache estimates; the client invalidates library, chat-card and note queries. A failure at any write rolls back the card, notes, swap, queue and composer updates together.
- **`SetCardParent`** ("Mark as a fork of…", or with null "Unlink"): sets or clears the relationship of a live card, `forked_from_revision_id` null since nothing was copied. Neither card's content changes. Refused: the parent not the user's live card (`NotFound`: another user's, another kind, in the bin), the card itself, or a parent that is already its descendant (a recursive walk up from the parent). Marking a card with the parent it has changes nothing. Both return the family.
- **The family** (`libraryFamily` in `db/library.ts`, read `CardFamily` for cards and `LibraryGenealogy` for every kind, and the editor's variants list for presets and lorebooks): every entity of the kind connected by `forked_from_entity_id`, one recursive query from a live entity of the user's: up its parents to the root (the member with none), then down from the root to every fork of a fork, so the tree is the same from any member. `UNION` keeps even a cycle the writer should have refused from looping. Each member has its parent, the ref it opens in, its display name and version, its state (`live`, `archived`, `binned`, `purged`), what it was forked from (revision, chat, when), and the user's live chats with recorded version participation and the last message among them (as `CardUsage`). Binned and purged members stay in the tree: a purged one has no ref or names left, and its forks keep it as their parent, without the revision they copied. A card in the bin can't be asked for (`NotFound`), as anything else in it.

**Three-way merge** (`merge3`, shared so the server's merge and the resolver's preview always agree):
- Objects merge per key. Only own keys count, so `__proto__` or `constructor` are plain data.
- **Arrays merge per element when every element has a unique `id`, `identifier` or `uid`.** That covers preset prompts and order, older cards' modules and lorebook entries, so additions on either side survive and deletions apply unless the other side edited the element (then it's a conflict). **Order** follows the side that reordered the elements all three share, or ours if neither did, with the other side's new elements placed after their predecessor there. Both reordering differently is a conflict at the array, and ours' order is kept.
- Other arrays are atomic.
- **Text changed on both sides merges word by word** with diff3 (`node-diff3`), keeping whitespace. Edits to different sentences of the same prompt combine; overlapping edits conflict. A conflict keeps ours in the merged value and is reported with its path, e.g. `["prompts", "identifier=main", "content"]`, and each side's value; a side with no value there (added or deleted) has none.
- `test/library.test.ts` and `packages/shared/test/merge.test.ts` run the owner's case from DESIGN §4 end to end: a softened impersonation rule and an added `{{summary}}` prompt survive an upstream re-import that rewrote another sentence of the same prompt, changed a sampler and added a prompt.

**Known limits:**
- Arrays without element identities, like a card's `alternate_greetings` or `tags`, are atomic: changing them on both sides is a conflict.
- `ListLibrary` filters by kind, tag and archive state; card discovery/search is in §12, and full-text history search in §3.13. The Library page has no general full-document search control or server-side library-text search RPC. Importing and exporting files is §11; editing, and "used by N chats", §14.

### 3.10 Drafts

Drafts with server-persisted undo history, for every text field (DESIGN §6.2). The patch model and history policy are in `@rp/shared/drafts.ts`, storage in `db/drafts.ts` (shared by the writer and readers), and the history table in migration `0003_draft_history`, which replaced the `drafts.undo_log` blob.

**Invariants.** DESIGN's "input boxes can be trusted with your life" is these five, which every change to drafts, the composer (§12) or the editors (§14.6) keeps:
1. **Nothing typed is lost.** Every text typed into a composer or an editor field is, at every moment, reachable from the UI: in the field, in its draft's history, in the recovered texts, or in the message, queued entry or revision it was committed into. Until it reaches the server, this browser's copy of it counts, since opening the field brings it back. Only the user removing it from a field that showed it (typing over it, picking an earlier state) or deleting its target for good takes it away.
2. **A commit names exactly what it commits.** A send (posted or queued) names the draft its text came from by id and the session it was typed in; the writer derives the commit text from the message content or Generate direction actually stored, and binds the draft to that chat's composer; an editor commit names each field's draft by id and the row version this tab saved, which changes with every change of its text. Only that draft, holding exactly that, is committed; no other draft or text changes.
3. **A save names the draft it was typed into**: its id, row version and session, never only a key or a tip. Another draft there now (the one named moved to a variant, and a new one started) is a conflict: the save goes on top, the other text one step back.
4. **A browser copy goes only once acknowledged.** A copy in IndexedDB is deleted only when the server acknowledged exactly that copy (by its id), or when a newer copy of the same draft (a composer's draft, an editor's field, a summary's edit), typed from its text, replaces it; never on a failure, a `NotFound`, navigation, expiry, capacity pressure, logout, another account signing in, or a newer copy of another draft. The user can inspect, copy out, retry or explicitly delete a copy in Browser recovery. Authored settings and pending first messages also have server drafts (below). Legacy browser-only copies remain until their editor transfers them, they are sent or saved, or the user deletes them; Browser recovery links pending-message copies to their page. After a pending first send succeeds, additional unsent text is atomically re-filed as a browser copy addressed to the saved chat before navigation; opening its composer atomically replaces that handoff with a draft-addressed copy, retained until its exact save is acknowledged. Legacy browser-only copies and first-send handoffs don't hold up logout, which keeps the session only while a copy that has a server draft to go to can't be saved; they wait for the user's next login in this browser.
5. **Lost text is found where it was lost.** Text a save went over is one step back in that field's history. Every draft save, restore and discard returns recovery metadata (`Draft.recovered`); composer saves also return their recovery boolean (agreeing with `Draft.recovered > 0`), and keepalive returns `x-drafts-recovered`. A write that sends text to the recovered texts says so (`recovered`), and the composer or editor shows it, with a link to the bin. A replay that displaces text saved elsewhere returns `Draft.displaced` (the other text and its save time, otherwise null). The client keeps the conflict beside that composer or field until acknowledged or switched; typing and refresh do not dismiss it.

One client rule carries 1 and 3: **a field's base** (the draft id, row version and session its saves name) **changes only together with the text it shows, or when the server answers a save with exactly the text sent.** Text typed on a base the server has moved past is saved on top of the newer text, never as typing on it, except that a deliberate deletion remains in place and older submitted text is recovered; so a stale answer (a replayed save's, a refresh's) can't make a tab's save coalesce over text it never showed. A copy that replaces another names that copy's base; once the server confirms the text a newer copy was typed from, the copy is made again on the confirmed version. Message-editor replay and live saves use the same acknowledgement rule: an exact active text/images response advances only a copy with explicit ancestry from the sent copy and the same original tuple. A later descendant is durably refiled before replay completes, including when its ancestor was empty; rejected responses and unrelated copies do not grant a new base.

**The model test** (`test/protocol/drafts.model.test.ts`) runs two tabs, two chat destinations and two browser-copy owners with the real `ComposerDraft` and `EditorStore`, in-memory IndexedDB, and a real server with database workers and sockets. Random operations cover typing, timers, refreshes during unsaved/in-flight edits, account-scoped recovery/logout flushes, keepalive, reloads, offline periods, reordered/lost/duplicated requests, sends and queued directions, branches and appends, undo/revert/revisions/conflicts/variants, bin restore, chat and branch purge, and real server restarts. The oracle compares complete text against reachable fields, their histories, recovered texts, stored message/direction and revision values; an obsolete composer's row is not a UI endpoint. It checks commit session, destination chat and text, browser-copy owner partitioning, both composer recovery surfaces, each copy's complete draft/version/session/revision base against its ancestry and exact acknowledged text, including identical pending and in-flight payloads, every draft-writing response's recovery metadata, receipt persistence and exactly-once replay, and explicit copy ancestry with historical acknowledgements even after a successor copy is removed. A shared test clock advances the writer's history clock without main-thread SQLite writes. Directed cases exercise whitespace through keepalive/reload, stale identical-text sessions, receipt replay across restart, background movement, both queue purge paths and retention beyond 1000 states. They also send with another chat's identity, flush copies under two owners, refresh a field before holding its save and typing further, and deliver a `next` save after two completed queued sends. Directed replay cases require the client conflict to remain through more typing until acknowledged or switched; switching similar texts must have a separate undo step. `e2e/offlineDrafts.spec.ts` stops the real server by PID, types into composers and editor fields, closes persistent browser contexts, and restarts the same data directory and port. Six scenarios reopen the original profile with ordinary recovery, another profile's conflicting draft, or a message/revision committed elsewhere: they check server persistence, both conflict times, preview, switch and undo, the sent message and recovered offline text, and the editor revision conflict picker. The browser suite exercises real account changes, expired sessions, recovery retries and logout notices. They hold an older save while Send clears the box, replace copies through overlapping completion callbacks, reject unrelated-field ancestry, and remove an acknowledged successor before its failed predecessor. `npm run check` runs these plus 4 seeds of 150 steps; `DRAFT_MODEL_SEEDS`, `DRAFT_MODEL_STEPS`, and `DRAFT_MODEL_SEED` select longer runs or one seed. Failures shrink to a short trace (`DRAFT_MODEL_DEBUG` adds drafts and copies, `DRAFT_MODEL_SHRINK=0` skips shrinking).

**Keys.** A draft is keyed by user and target:
- `composer` (a chat, with the fork in `field`; `composerKey()` builds it)
- `version_edit` (a version)
- `scratchpad` (a slot)
- `snippet` (a note ref, with the viewed fork in `field` for a chat-scoped snippet)
- `entity_field` (a ref plus a JSON path in `field`)
- `summary_edit` (a summary)
- `user_field` (a private user workspace key plus a field; settings and text before its target exists)
- `queue_edit` (a chat, with the queued item id in `field`; kept after posting or withdrawal)
- `insert` (a chat, with the fork and the anchor in `field` as `fork:anchor`, the anchor empty above the first message; `insertDraftKey`): the text of a message being inserted (spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §3.1). Its owner is the user's chat with a live fork of it and an anchor of the chat; it's listed with the chat's message editors and removed with the chat. `InsertMessage` commits it

The first save checks that the target belongs to the user. Independently supplied draft ids are checked even when the enclosing chat/ref belongs to the caller: an existing foreign id is `NotFound` before version comparisons, for saves, restores, discards, editor revision commits and keepalive, with no mutation or recovery. `copyFrom` must name an owned composer in the same chat. Editor revision bases must belong to the ref's own entity. The legitimate late-save exception is an absent draft id after movement/purge: a composer save to a still-owned chat recovers its submitted text; an editor save can recreate an owned field while retaining its original base. No foreign row is treated as absent. Drafts are never visible to other users.

**Saving.**
- The client saves debounced while the user types (`SaveDraft`). Each save supplies the draft id, row version and session as last seen, with nulls before a field has a draft. Composer saves always name an existing identity and a durable operation id.
- **The writer decides a conflict in the save's transaction** (`drafts.ts` `saveOnto`), one rule for every kind of draft, live or from a closing page; no client reads and retries:
  - Typed on the draft as it is: saved, coalescing with typing as below.
  - A deliberate deletion advanced `cleared_version` past the supplied base: keep the deletion, recovering submitted text instead of reopening it. The watermark survives subsequent edits, so it also blocks older text after the field is used again. `deletions_json` retains its origin draft id and row version independently of movable history. Moving message history leaves a resting barrier at the source key; a source copy is checked against that retained origin, not the new row's counter. Compound `user_field` forms record each cleared text input by its JSON path. Array paths use stable item identities (`id`, `identifier` or `uid`), with separate whole-item removal barriers; reconciliation and marker-value refresh both resolve the identity. Arrays without unique identities retain a conflicting array as a whole, and legacy numeric array markers reject automatic replay rather than being projected onto different items. Stale snapshots preserve the latest protected values and save unaffected inputs, recovering the original snapshot; ordinary commits retain these values even when draft storage is emptied. Form initialization snapshots carry `seed` through browser recovery, RPC and keepalive: they establish a history baseline, never a new deletion, and cannot overwrite protected inputs. The subsequent typed snapshot remains a separate durable copy. `editingFrom` travels with each authored copy, RPC and keepalive: it records the text actually edited and retains evidence of local clears across failed acknowledgements. For generic/legacy anonymous arrays, authored clear events also carry explicit array-path evidence in `editingFrom` until acknowledged: later reuse of the same text in another input/item cannot cancel a clear through equal final string counts. Whole-field clears carry an opaque `clearId` through later text, replacement copies, synchronous pending-message backup and closing saves. The writer records that event even if only a final nonempty copy survives, the final text equals current storage, or the first seed never reached the server. The same event can continue after a lost acknowledgement without advancing its barrier; a different later clear still blocks it. Queued transitions preserve their original event ids when replayed onto an earlier exact acknowledgement, and only acknowledged intent is retired. Root events protect the whole field without manufacturing later per-input clears. Event ids are compared only for equality; server versions retain deletion ordering. The string-only provenance format remains readable. First-party editable object lists already provide stable identities; anonymous snapshots remain supported at the generic API boundary without inventing item identities. Only proved removals create per-input barriers; exact current-base legacy saves can derive that intent from their base, while older unversioned/initialization snapshots conservatively preserve nonempty untouched inputs. Retrying an already empty input does not advance its deletion barrier. Each queued input change keeps its own edit version and provenance; exact acknowledgements replay only later actual input transitions onto the acknowledged baseline, so an older response cannot erase a later clear or reuse an acknowledged clear over fresh remote typing.
  - Another tab changed the text since (`drafts.text_version`, the row version the text last changed at, past the one named): saved as its own entry, marked `displaced`, so the other tab's text is one step back, and goes to the recovered texts when the session ends or the entry is dropped, however short it is.
  - The session it was typed in has ended since (`drafts.session` counts them; each commit or discard ends one): a field's text starts the next session with the revision it was typed against, so committing it meets the edit conflict on that base; a composer's goes to the recovered texts (below).
  So a stale tab never overwrites newer text unseen, and nothing it goes over is lost.
- The server diffs the new text against the stored text into one reversible patch (`start`, `removed`, `inserted`) and records it in `draft_history`. Patch boundaries never split a surrogate pair, so stored text stays valid UTF-8.
- History is a row per entry, not a blob, so a save never rewrites the whole history.
- Text is capped at 1,000,000 characters (`DraftTooLarge`).

**History.**
- **Typing coalesces.** A save within 5 s of the last entry extends it, until the entry spans 60 s, so continuous typing is one entry per minute rather than one per save.
- **A destructive change always gets its own entry,** so the text before it is one step back. Destructive means removing more than 200 characters or more than half the text, e.g. select-all plus a stray key.
- `DraftHistory` lists the restorable states newest first, with lengths and short excerpts. `GetDraftState` returns one state's full text, built by undoing newer entries from the current text.
- Walking history back needs only lengths, since destructiveness depends only on them. Earlier text is rebuilt only as far back as needed, as slices of the current text, so no step copies the whole text.
- `RestoreDraftState` moves the draft back to that state, and records the restore as its own entry, so it can be undone too.
- At most 1000 entries and 1,000,000 changed characters are kept per draft, oldest dropped first. The text from before a dropped destructive or displaced entry goes to the recovered-text section first.
- **A library field (`entity_field`), a message's edit (`version_edit`) and a summary's edit (`summary_edit`) keep whichever is more: their last 200 states or their last 30 days** (`DraftHistoryPolicy.fieldStates`, `fieldDays`; owner, 2026-11-01, and 2026-11-02 for messages and summaries), with no size limit of its own past the 1,000,000-character text cap; an entry goes only when it's beyond the newest 200 and older than 30 days. A settings value (`=` field) or the held structural changes (`HELD_FIELD`, §14.6) never go to the bin as JSON, dropped, committed or discarded (`toBin`). `DraftHistory` takes `before` (a seq) to page on to older states.

**Committing.** `AppendMessage`, `SendOrQueue` (posted or queued), `AddVersion` and `EditRef` take an optional `commitDraft`: the draft's id and session (`drafts.ts` `commit`). The storage boundary derives the commit text from the stored version content/direction, queued content/direction or revision field, and checks the draft's target against that destination. Insertion commits also match the exact fork and anchor field; appends and queued sends accept an insert draft only below their named tip, and composer drafts only in their source fork. An unrelated draft is neither ended nor returned as the send's draft, even when its chat, text and session match. `insertDraftReview.test.ts` covers posted and queued Write/Generate paths and mismatches within a chat. The draft is committed **in the same transaction** only if it holds exactly that text in that session, so a reload never shows already-sent text in the composer, and a send never ends text it didn't take: another tab's text typed on since, a replacement draft at the same tip, a session sent already. Otherwise it stays as it is, and the write returns it as it left it, with how many texts committing sent to the recovered texts (`recovered`). `ClearDraft` and `RestoreDraftState` name the draft's id as well as its row version.

**History only lives while a draft is being written** (owner, 2026-10-10). Once committed, the text is preserved in a version or revision, so a commit or discard deletes the draft's history and empties its text. The row stays, so other tabs' row versions keep working. What a commit or discard would otherwise lose goes to the recycle bin's **recovered-text section** (§3.11):
- the text from just before **each** destructive change in the session (hours of typing in a card field wiped, then saved)
- the text another tab's save went over (a displaced entry)
- a discarded draft's text

This applies to every kind of draft but the three that keep their history (`keepsHistory`: library fields, message edits, summary edits, below): what a bad save loses is the editing session, and the previous version being intact doesn't change that. The next save after a commit starts a fresh session. `ListActiveDrafts` lists drafts with unsent text.

**A library field's edit history outlives its revisions** (owner, 2026-11-01; `keepsHistory` in `drafts.ts`). For an `entity_field` draft, a commit (a Save, or a reply's checkpoint, §14.2a) ends the session (`status = 'committed'`, `session + 1`) but keeps its text and every history entry, records the revision now holding its text (`drafts.committed_revision`), and sends nothing to the bin: every state stays reachable from the field's edit history (§14.6). The text version doesn't change, so a tab that saw exactly that text and types on in the ended session goes on from `committed_revision` as its base, without a conflict; one that hadn't seen it keeps its own base and meets the edit conflict at Save, as before. Three more rules keep the history running through what the box showed:
- A field's first save, typed on a revision, first records the revision's text as the draft's starting state (`revisionContent`), so the text from before the first edit is a state too.
- A resting draft typed on a revision whose text it doesn't hold (one restored or merged in since) first moves to that text, as an entry of kind `revision` (`DraftState.kind`), then takes the typing.
- A discard still ends the session the old way (history deleted, text to the bin), except that the revision text the history started from, which that revision keeps, isn't sent to the bin.

**Note editors resolve the current display end** (`noteHere` in `db/noteAt.ts`), including an inserted message after the structural tip. The returned edit position is used by Save, revision restore and shared-note link writes; a stale caller naming a deleted message of the same chat still edits the branch's current state. Precise historical reads retain `noteAt`. Draft carry resolves the source at that same display end, so taking a note **As it is now** carries typing on a binding at a trailing insertion too. `test/chatNoteBranches.test.ts` and `test/forkDrafts.test.ts` cover these cases.

**Unsaved note text goes with a fork** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §4.1; `db/carryDrafts.ts`), as git carries uncommitted changes onto a new branch. In the writer transaction that makes the fork, each live field draft (held structural changes aside) is saved onto the same field at the new target, still unsaved and typed on the same revision (its first state that revision's text, so the new branch can go back too), and the source draft settles on its revision's text (`settleOn`): its session ends, its edit history keeps the moved text one step back, so the edit history's preselected state puts it back in one pick. No dialog and no extra step.
- `carryChatNoteDrafts` runs wherever a chat fork is made by forking: `CreateFork` (Branch from here, after the note choices' events), `AppendMessage` and `SendOrQueue` with `branch` at a message other than the fork's tip, and a branch queued onto a reply being written (`chatSetupWrites.ts`). It moves the drafts at `<ref>/<source fork>` of each chat note whose version at the new branch's tip is the one at the source's tip; so a note unchanged since the point moves, one taken **As it was then** (or positionally, by a call without choices) after a saved change stays. Opening a line no fork follows (`SwitchBranch`) and a bin restore make fork rows without the user branching, and carry nothing.
- `carryFieldDrafts` also runs for a card's fork (`copyCard`: Fork, Fork for this chat): each of the card's notes' unsaved fields moves to its copy, and the card's own but its names to the fork (owner, 2026-11-02; §3.9), each original going back to its head with the text in its history. Neither dialog asks. Both dialogs flush open editors first and refresh them after.
- Copied card notes record their source note and revision in the existing entity fork columns. Drafts typed on the copied head use the copy's first revision; older bases retain their source revision, including through repeated copies, so Save and the save comparison still detect concurrent changes. `test/cardForks.test.ts` covers older bases on both cards and copied notes through a second fork, including a conflicting field and typing on the moved draft.
- `test/forkDrafts.test.ts` covers a branch at the tip (moved, source reverted, restored from its history), a branch send from an earlier message, then/now/no choice after a saved change, text typed through an earlier message's position going with the branch, and a card fork's fields and notes (names staying); `e2e/editor.spec.ts` covers Fork card with no checkbox and the original's edit history putting the text back; `e2e/forkNotes.spec.ts` covers the dialog's unsaved rows and choices and the Notes tab across a branch at the latest message, with the source's edit history putting the text back, at 1440/390 in light/dark.

**A message's or a summary's edit history outlives its saves** (owner, 2026-11-02: the library field's rule, with its retention). A `version_edit` or `summary_edit` draft is committed as above (`end`): its text and history stay, nothing goes to the bin, and `EditSummary` records the revision it wrote as `committed_revision`. The text an edit starts from (`startText`) is the version's content for a message edit and the named summary revision's (one of that summary's own) for a summary edit; with it the rules above hold for them too:
- The first save records that text as the draft's first state, so the text from before the edit can be put back. Message edit states snapshot the complete image set too, including inherited images in text-only edits; reopening and Cancel record the version's saved set, so an amendment cannot change what an older state restores (`editImages.test.ts`).
- A resting draft typed on text it doesn't hold (a version amended or an amendment restored elsewhere, another summary revision picked, a regex rewrite of the saved text) first moves to it as a `revision` state, preserving the old initial state even when the earlier saved session made no changes. A reopened message editor names no draft (`base` null) before it has read one, so this applies to it too.
- **Saving a model reply's edit makes a new version, and the draft moves to it** (`commit`'s `moveTo`: `AddSelectedVersion`, `AddVersion`; `AmendVersion` moves it to the copy a branch gets), so editing the message again goes on with the same history. It moves only while resting, and never over a draft the new target has.
- **Cancel (`DiscardMessageDraft`, `DiscardSummaryDraft`) keeps the history too**: the draft goes back to the text it started from as a `revision` state, the cancelled text one step back, and its session ends; nothing goes to the bin, since nothing is lost.
- A resting summary draft put back from its history is typed on its `committed_revision`; the client takes a draft's base revision only from an active draft (`summaryDraft.ts` `baseOf`), so typing after a save names the revision shown.
- A reopened editor reads its resting draft for "History of this edit" (`GetMessageDraft`, `NotFound` when there's none, as for its history; `GetSummaryDraft`), so the list shows the states from before the last save, and picking one makes it the newest state (`RestoreMessageDraft`, append-only). Versions (swipes), "Saved amendment history" and summary Revisions are unchanged.

**The composer belongs to a fork** (DESIGN §6.2, owner; spec/FORK-INDEPENDENCE-DELTA.md unit 2):
- Its key is the chat plus the fork (`composerKey`; migration 0053 moved each from the tip it was keyed by to the fork ending there). A recovered text whose fork isn't known has the field empty.
- Each chat and each fork has its own composer, and a half-typed message waits where it was left. Two forks at the same message have two.
- Appending, deleting and restoring move a fork's tip, never its composer, so nothing has to move or merge: a model reply leaves text typed meanwhile where it is, and a send's recovery text stays with its fork.
- `OpenComposer` (by fork, the current one if null) with `copyFrom` copies the text into a new fork's composer when one is started, never overwriting text already there. A new composer also inherits its source composer's speaker, reply pick, No one (`drafts.no_replies`) and Guidance switch; an existing one keeps its own choices, including a reset to turn order or Guidance off. The baseline's `drafts.guidance` gives new composers a default of off; Guidance is no longer an account preference. `GetComposerChoice`/`SetComposerChoice` read, change and publish Guidance with the other choices. Every composer `Draft` response includes `guidance`, including fork copies and the first-send handoff, so text and mode appear together without a separate mode read or visibility gate. The speaker/reply read retains its existing send guard while typing and Guidance remain available. A pending composer inherits Guidance through the new-chat link from its source composer, otherwise starts off; `StartChat.guidance` keeps the pending value on the saved composer in the creation transaction.
- Switching between existing forks carries nothing.

**Saving composer text names the draft it was typed into**, not the fork (`SaveComposer`, `drafts.ts` `saveComposer`, by the rule above):
- `OpenComposer` makes an empty draft for a fork that has none, so every text has a draft to name. A fork that has one is read in a reader; only a new one takes the writer.
- A save carries the draft's id, and the row version and session the client had. The text goes onto that draft.
- A save from a session that has ended (its text was sent, or queued, from another tab), or onto a draft that is gone, isn't taken as the start of the next session: its text goes to the recovered texts, and the reply says so (`recovered`) with the draft as it is now.
- `next` marks text typed after a send of that session that may not have arrived (a page closed while it was out): it starts the session the send ended, or, if the send never arrived, goes on top of the text it would have taken, which is then displaced. Pending saves carry `operationId`; the writer records its receipt in the save transaction (`composer_save_receipts`, migration `0015`). Replaying it returns the current draft without applying or recovering the text again, even after that text was sent. Its original displacement metadata is reconstructed from history while that session and entry remain, so a retry still explains the conflict; receipts keep only the session, history position and time. The enclosing recovery boolean repeats the receipt's original recovery flag; when a draft remains, `Draft.recovered` repeats that flag as 0 or 1. A fresh save reports the actual recovered count. Draft reads and writes that displace no text return `displaced: null`. The displaced text's time comes from the previous history entry (the initial draft's creation time before its first change), rather than a client comparison. Receipts live until the chat is deleted. Opening a composer replays each eligible durable composer copy with its original operation id even when its base predates a known deletion: the writer acknowledges an already-applied clear by receipt or recovers stale text without reopening the deleted field. A failed replay retains the browser copy, and a known deletion blocks fallback display of that copy. `client/test/draftDeletionReview.test.ts` covers successful and failed replay; `server/test/protocol/composerDeletionReplay.test.ts` exercises a lost clear acknowledgement and stale-text recovery against the real writer. All composer saves require `operationId` and `next`; there is no identity-less replay path. A next save can reopen only the immediately following session.
- `SendMessage` and `Generate` name the draft as `composer` (id, session) and return it as the send left it (`draft`): committed, or still active with another tab's newer text.

**Cleanup.** Draft targets aren't foreign keys, since one column points into several tables. Triggers delete a draft when its target (chat, slot, version, summary, ref) is deleted (`test/schema.test.ts`).

**Authored settings and pending text (backlog U02/U05).** `EditorApi` exposes `GetUserDraft`, `SaveUserDraft`, `UserDraftHistory`, `RestoreUserDraft` and `EndUserDraft`. They reuse the named worker operations above; the key is `user_field`, scoped by the authenticated user. Target strings name private workspaces, not references granting access to a connection, model or chat. Requests also name the account that typed them; RPC and closing-page writes refuse a different logged-in account, even on the first save before a draft id exists. Foreign draft identities are still refused. The baseline and frozen equivalence fixture include this kind. These workspaces survive removal of their named target, preserving unsaved text.

`features/editor/userDraft.tsx` shares a subscribed store across each editor's lifetime. It saves changes in order, first recording the starting text so destructive edits have an initial undo state. Each typed change has an IndexedDB `userDraft` copy, including the observed draft id, row version and session. Closing sends its pending copy through `POST /library/drafts`; Browser recovery and logout retry that same payload. Opening reads the server draft and replays copies without refreshing their bases; a device with no browser copies reads the active server text. Old account-instruction `setting` copies transfer when that editor opens. The displayed text keeps its own draft base through refused replays and typing during undo/restore; an unseen server response cannot advance that base. Each save acknowledgement immediately re-files later typing on the acknowledged base, even if another queued operation delays its save. Existing editors use one small ↶ icon button (`UserDraftUndo`, tooltip and name **Undo / history**), in the form's header where it has one (`CardHeader inline`, so it stays beside the title on phones; the connection Settings form, the summarization instruction's Save row); its popover holds **Undo field change** and the field's history (the **Field undo history** list, read when it opens), each entry restoring its version. Both use server history and leave refused local text in place until it reaches the server. `UserDraftNotices` shows only what needs saying (a failed save, recovered texts, another device's edit); `UserDraftStatus` combines both only when the editor opts into history, otherwise it shows notices alone. Displaced text has a persistent notice with preview, switch and acknowledgement actions; recovery results link to recovered texts in the bin. Open private draft editors also receive saves, restores, endings and closing-page saves from other sessions through `UserDraftChanged` on the account-scoped `SubscribeNotices` stream. The editor registers `editor.user-drafts` in `userNoticeReceivers`, independently of optional reply-alert channels. Clean editors take newer text and its observed base; an editor with queued or refused local writes retains its text and shows a preview with Load the other device’s text and Keep my text. Loading first saves the local text into field history; keeping writes on the original observed base, preserving the displaced remote text through the normal draft rules. An ending event contains empty storage, not the saved setting or JSON form. It leaves the displayed text intact and offers Keep my text or Reload saved value. Reload first persists the displayed text, discards that exact draft version into recovered texts, and reloads the page to read the actual saved resource; a refusal or typing during the choice prevents the reload. It never feeds an ended row’s empty content into a form. Events at or below the observed row version are ignored. `UserDraftSync` on subscription/reconnect and backlog overflow refreshes open workspaces; account isolation applies to text events too. `client/test/userDraft.test.ts`, `server/test/notices.test.ts` and `e2e/privateDraftSync.spec.ts` cover live refresh, out-of-order events, reconnect reads, unsaved conflicts and both choices, including fresh browser contexts at 1440 and 390 pixels.

The account and per-fork summarization instructions retain their explicit Save buttons; the chat instruction's workspace names both the chat and viewed fork. Saving flushes the submitted text, writes the setting, and ends only that draft version. These are separate writer transactions: if ending fails after the setting saves, the draft remains available. Text typed during Save stays in its browser copy and queued draft; failed setting saves leave the active draft untouched. “Use account default” discards the instruction draft only after the reset succeeds, recovering its text.

The account summarization instruction stays disabled until both generation defaults and its private draft have loaded. This prevents a late initial draft read from replacing the native selection while the user starts typing; `e2e/privateDraftSync.spec.ts` holds that read, verifies the disabled field, then replaces the loaded text and checks its persisted value.

**Creation and naming controls (newcarddialog, 2026-11-02).** `UserDraftStatus` shows notices alone by default; existing model settings, pricing, global regex and chat-instruction editors opt into its history button with `history`. New card, library fork/variant, chat card fork, chat/group rename, new chat, add model, save key and rename key forms have no detached history control. New connection likewise omits its header history action. Their draft saving and recovery notices remain intact. New preset already has no history control; new notes are created inline, and there is no standalone new-lorebook dialog. New card has no standing title explanation, and its **Version** label has the tooltip "Shown as the card's subtitle."

**Creation/naming copy (newcarddialog follow-up).** Standing title descriptions are omitted from New preset, New user, library card/variant forks, chat card forks, Save a key, Add a model, Enter a new key, Branch from here, Mark as a fork of, entry copy/move and Import a new version. Choice-relevant facts live in field help: fork names explain draft transfer, variant names explain inherited updates, model ids name the provider id, handles explain sign-in, key fields name the destination, parent and target-lorebook fields explain their effects, and the card-file choice explains replacement scope. Chat/group rename guidance appears beside Name as question-mark help. The chat-fork form also omits its standing original-use count. New note and snippet actions create inline; persona creation uses New card. No shared dialog behavior changes.

The same mechanism protects connection settings (including name and base URL), the model's entire custom-settings form (including incomplete numbers and invalid JSON), new connection and model forms, card creation/fork/rename names (in the library and chat), the empty-chat title, chat/group/branch naming, and credential names and allowed-address text. Multi-field settings and small name forms keep a JSON snapshot as their undoable field, so restoring brings back the complete form, including the connection/model/ref row version it was edited from. For these snapshots, coalescing stays within the same changed JSON field paths. Destructiveness is also measured against each string field, so erasing a short name cannot disappear in a patch coalesced against a much larger settings form; its prior snapshot is marked for recovery and retained on commit. Parsing this extra form structure is bounded to shallow, small trees; raw instruction/prose drafts retain the ordinary string policy. Connection and model forms advance later snapshots' settings row version only after their own Save succeeds, including queued typing and browser copies, so the next edit remains saveable after a reload. A model editor kept open in the chat panel also advances its committed snapshot after its own Save. “Load the latest” on a stale model draft recovers that draft and reads the current model instead of reopening the same stale base. Secret inputs are excluded. Existing connection sections and account/chat setting contributions remain registered through their existing slots. Search/filter text stays transient.

Before a chat exists, `StartChatPage` uses its card or group pending-copy key as the private workspace, with field `First message`. A reload or another device finds that prose without creating a chat. The existing browser copy and first-send carry protocol stay in place: after a successful first send, extra text is addressed to the created chat before the pending server draft ends. No provider call is started by draft storage.

`client/test/userDraft.test.ts` covers refused replay bases, typing during undo, immediate copy rebasing, persistent displacement and form versions after Save. `server/test/userDrafts.test.ts` covers persisted history, destructive recovery, scopes and version-fenced ending; the isolation matrix probes all five RPCs in both directions. `e2e/userDrafts.spec.ts` covers server reads after panel close/reload and from fresh browser contexts, both instruction editors' refused and delayed saves, model JSON still being typed, connection edits typed during Save across reload, fork-dialog retry after a refused draft write, persistent conflict preview/switch and recovery links, and the desktop/phone light/dark layouts.

The streaming above covers private `user_field` workspaces (authored settings, names and pending first messages). Library fields, message edits, summaries and existing-chat composers keep their own refresh/recovery lifecycles; they do not subscribe to private-workspace text events.

Copy audit (2026-11-04): shared confirmation, history, navigation and disclosure controls use existing Button hints and Tooltip explanations on hover and focus. Segmented choices retain their descriptions and fall back to the selection action; disclosures without custom help explain the next expand or collapse action.

Preset and lorebook copy audit (2026-11-04): editor controls and entry menus have hover/focus explanations; preset help names the cache prefix and cache breakpoints directly. Utility-prompt and lorebook-settings disclosures explain their contents. Labels and actions are unchanged.

Library copy audit (2026-11-04): creation, transfer, search, history, update, shared-note and import controls use existing explanations. Redundant archived-preset guidance is removed; controls keep their labels and actions.

Chat copy audit (2026-11-04): message, summary, queue, history, branch, image and panel actions use the existing explanations. Action hints omit promises about retained text; redundant names-in-prompts, branch-name and summary-request introductions are removed. Lorebook hints name the book and its scope; toggle hints name the next click. Labels and actions are unchanged.

Settings copy audit (2026-11-04): connection, model, key, account, network, pricing, global-regex and bin controls explain their actions. Pricing and global-regex introductions live in heading question-mark help; explanations keep technical terms and omit recovery instructions.

Character and navigation copy audit (2026-11-04): card tiles, chat lists, sorting, persona actions, setup links and shell navigation use existing hover/focus explanations. Sort-menu descriptions use the shared menu explanation rather than permanent text under each label; redundant empty-chat guidance is removed. No labels changed. The focused `LAYOUT_AUDIT_COPY_ONLY=1` entry in `e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts` audits surfaces whose copy changed size across the standard width/theme profiles. `e2e/explanations.spec.ts` checks revised menu/switch descriptions and Cancel hover help; `e2e/presetMarkers.spec.ts` checks the concise cache-breakpoint explanation.

### 3.11 Recycle bin

Delete explanations use “Moves this <thing> to the bin, from which it can be restored later.” without additional text. Delete toasts say “<Thing> moved to the bin.” and retain the Undo and Open the bin actions. Cancel and Discard explanations name the action without recovery instructions.

**Insertion boundaries and previews.** A deleted tip that retains a shown insertion remains a valid parent for `SendOrQueue`, as for `AppendMessage`. Sending or generating proceeds immediately past a deleted anchor, even when its selected version is still generating: the queue never waits on a deleted reply. State reads accept a deleted insertion anchor (its replies still need the state at that boundary), and next-context reads accept an explicitly named deleted tip of a live fork. `lastShown` in `db/forks.ts` supplies the display-end text for `ChatSummaries`, fork bin items and affected-fork warnings, as for the fork list; `ChatSummaries` message counts use display positions when the fork places insertions. The sidebar's `ShellLibrary` walks those same pieces, consuming structural runs once and reading the single inserted pieces with the fork's selections and deletions; its preview, visible-message count, navigation endpoint and activity include inserted messages. Chats without insertion rows retain the structural walk. `forksShowing` and `shownElsewhere` exclude purged forks explicitly: clearing a purged fork's tip alone does not remove an inherited insertion above the first message from its pieces. `test/bin.test.ts` covers sends and Generate at deleted complete/generating tips, preview text, purge retention and amend copies, exact fork counts and byte sizes, row-version bumps and restore/fork deletion/purge/eviction interleaved through a 70-deep chain of forks. `test/deletedTip.test.ts` exercises cast, next context, regenerate and send through RPC with a synthetic provider, and a cast join and a macro binding made at the deleted tip reaching the next turn's request after the insertion. `e2e/insertedBin.spec.ts` covers deleted-tip sends and swipes, the bin warning and restore at 1440 and 390 pixels in both themes.

Deleting is deliberate and fundamentally non-destructive (DESIGN §6.2): deletes go to a per-user bin, from which they can be restored or deleted for good. Schema in migrations `0004_recycle_bin` and `0009_bin_index`, logic in `db/bin.ts` (migration `0014_deleted_subtree_roots` retains subtree barriers after purge), handlers in `db/binWrites.ts`, types in `@rp/shared/bin.ts`. The writer builds one bin, with the draft store it recovers text for, and shares it across its handler groups.

**Deleting marks, it doesn't remove.**
- A delete creates one `bin_items` row. A chat or entity is marked with `deleted_at` and the item's id. A message, swipe or fork is deleted in a fork (below, since unit 5); branches deleted before that carry the marks of their whole subtree and restore as they did.
- Every read skips marked rows, and what a fork deleted in its own view (`slotDeletedIn`, `versionDeletedIn`, `shownVersionDeletedIn` in `db/forkState.ts`). Paths walk through deleted messages without showing them, so their replies stay where they were. Writes treat deleted things as `NotFound`.
- Restoring clears the marks, so things come back exactly where they were, with their versions and attached state.
- **Deleting is per fork** (spec/FORK-INDEPENDENCE-DELTA.md §2.4, unit 5; `db/bin.ts`). A message or swipe deleted in a fork is a `delete_slot` or `delete_version` override of that fork with `flag = 1` and the bin item, whose origin names the fork (`forkId`, `forkName`); restoring writes the row with `flag = 0`. Another fork that shows it keeps it, in its path, picker and context. Only when no unpurged fork shows it, including a fork in the bin (`forksShowing` in `db/forks.ts`) is the slot or swipe also marked (`deleted_at`, `bin_item_id`) under the item, which changes nothing another restorable fork shows and keeps the walks that read marks as they were (alternates in the switcher, tips following a restore). The marks are frozen otherwise (triggers in `db/baseline.ts`: `slots_deletion_per_fork`, `versions_deletion_per_fork`, `slots_hide_frozen`). Deleting a fork's tip message moves that fork's tip up to the nearest message it still shows (`relocateLeaf`, per fork's view), and only that fork's. It stops at a deleted message whose gap still holds an inserted message the fork shows and hasn't deleted (`liveGaps` in `db/bin.ts`: each such slot and its anchors up to a structural one), so that message stays on the display path; the tip stays on the deleted message, and an append in the fork goes below it, after its gap (`AppendMessage` accepts a deleted parent only when it's the fork's own tip, which happens only then; spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §2.4). Without insertions it's the walk it always was. **Inserted messages** (spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §3.1, unit 5) are deleted, restored and purged as any message: `forksShowing` and `shownElsewhere` read display paths, so a fork that shows one by inheriting its `insert` row counts for the mark and in `BinItemForks`. Restoring one in its fork puts it back in its gap, without moving the tip or making a fork, since whether the restored message is still on the fork's path is `onForkPath`. Making room keeps an item whose message a fork other than the deleting one still shows on its display path. `test/bin.test.ts` ("the bin with inserted messages") covers these, deleting a fork that inserted a message or was made at one, an anchor deleted mid-path and at the tip, and a random oracle through the writer (each fork a list; appends at its end, insertions below a shown message or above the first, forks at a shown message, deletions of any shown message, tips included) checking every fork's view after every step.
- **Restoring a message** deleted in a fork clears its row and any mark under fork items. The fork's tip that went up from it comes back down onto that message, also when the tip had gone up past messages the fork deleted before (it sits on the message the fork shows nearest above, `shownAbove`, the walk `relocateLeaf` makes), so a multi-delete's Undo over an older deletion brings the tip back to the end instead of making a fork per message; if the fork went on since, the message isn't on its path any more, so it comes back as a fork of its own (`insertFork`: parent the fork, base the message's parent, tip the restored message), which doesn't become current. A swipe's restore writes `flag = 0` and normally leaves the selection. If a global purge removed this fork's last available swipe, its automatic `delete_slot` override records that purged selection in `value_id`; restoring a swipe clears that automatic deletion, selects the restored swipe, and brings its message back. Restoring a mark that a slot's own column holds, as it was: every live fork whose tip has nothing below it follows what came back, on the newest reply at each step (`followRestored`), and a branch brings back its forks as they were. `test/forkDeletion.test.ts`, `test/binApi.test.ts`.

**Deletes need no confirmation:** each returns the bin item for the "deleted, open the bin" toast. The behaviors:
- **Swipes:** `DeleteVersion` deletes one swipe in a fork (`forkId`, else the fork through its message), the normal delete (owner). If the fork showed it, the previous swipe shows, as in ST, or the next one if it was the first. Deleting the only version the fork has left deletes the message in that fork. A fork's copy (§3.8) is deleted as the swipe it stands in for; the bin item names that swipe, its size counts the copies, and a restore brings each fork's copy back in its place. Deleting it for good empties the copies and their histories too (owner, 2026-10-27: delete for good erases the text everywhere).
- **Messages and forks:** `DeleteMessage` deletes one message in a fork, and its replies stay. `DeleteFork` deletes one fork (owner, 2026-10-27: only that fork goes; forks made from it keep their shared history): the fork is marked (`forks.deleted_at`, `bin_item_id`) under an item of kind `branch` whose origin names it, and the messages of its path that no other unpurged fork has (`sharedDepth` in `db/forks.ts`: below the deepest slot another restorable fork's path shares, including forks in the bin) are marked under the item, the first of them also `branch_deleted` (the barrier a deleted branch's root always was). Inserted messages count by display path (`insertedUnseen`): one the fork shows by its `insert` row is marked too when no other unpurged fork shows it, and one on its structural path past the shared part (it was made at or below it) is left unmarked when another fork shows it by its own row. The item's message count and size follow. Restoring the fork clears the marks other forks' items put on the inserted messages it shows, as on its structural path. A chat's last live fork isn't deleted (`CannotDeleteLastFork`). If it was the current fork, the live fork most recently current takes over (§3.8). Its composer and any save in flight stay its own, so Undo restores it with its draft. `UndoThreads` deletes a split's new threads the same way, each fork in turn under one item of kind `threads` (§3.8 "Starting threads").
- **Several messages at once** (job msgactions1; ST-COMPARISON item 24; moving messages, owner Q4, is not built). `DeleteMessages` (`@rp/shared/messageSelectionApi.ts`, a group of its own merged into `AppApi` like the split chats, so the core group stays under TypeScript's instantiation limit; handlers `api/messageSelection.ts`) takes a fork and 1–1,000 distinct slot ids (`DeletedSlots`, `MULTI_DELETE_LIMIT` in `@rp/shared/bin.ts`) and deletes each exactly as `DeleteMessage` would, in one writer transaction (`deleteMessages` in `db/bin.ts`, writer `DeleteMessages` in `db/binWrites.ts`): one bin item per message, in display order (the client sends them top down), each origin carrying `group` (a uuidv7 shared by the call) and `groupSize`; the fork's tip is relocated once and the chat's row version bumps once; eviction spares every item the call made (`evictDeleted` takes a list). It is all or nothing: a slot not live in that fork, or not the user's, fails the whole call with `NotFound` and writes nothing. Structural-message retention is checked for the whole set; inserted messages use `forksShowing` with `first` to stop at the first other fork found.
