On start, after an RPC socket opens (including reconnect), on focus/online/visibility, every 30 seconds, and whenever a lazy chunk fails to load, a no-cache `/healthz` request compares the server's `x-client-build` with this tab's `VITE_BUILD_ID`. A mismatch latches one small banner, “The app was updated. Reload to continue.”, with a Reload button (explained on hover/focus) that flushes open editors (1.5 s cap) and reloads; synchronous browser draft backups remain the recovery guarantee (§3.10). Chunk failures are seen through Vite's `vite:preloadError` (installed in `register`) and through the boundaries that catch lazy imports: `lazyPanel` (`panels.tsx`), the router's `defaultErrorComponent` (`routes.tsx`), the message renderer boundary and plugin entry boundaries. Once the build is confirmed changed, a failed panel or route shows “This part needs a reload.” with the same Reload button (`StalePart`); a failed import while the build is unchanged still reads as the server being unreachable, with Try again. A confirmed chunk failure reloads the tab by itself once per server build (sessionStorage guard) only when nothing is typed: no editor reports unsaved changes and no text box, contenteditable or changed text input holds text. The proactive checks never reload by themselves. `e2e/staleBuild.spec.ts` swaps the served build (new build id, old lazy chunks removed) under an open chat at 390/1440 with the layout audit, covers the once-only auto reload and the focus check; `e2e/macroHighlight.spec.ts` covers reconnect and draft recovery.
**Size formatting** (binunits): `@rp/shared/byteSize.ts` supplies binary units and one-decimal grouped read-only sizes (B/KB/MB/GB); `ui/byteSize.ts` converts editable capacities. Library file rows and maximum-file messages, new-file revisions, folder-import selected totals, and the settings-preset JSON file-limit message all use it. Import parser reports and HTTP upload/export limit errors use the same shared formatter, so server-originated size errors also show readable units. The folder browser has an 8 px inner gutter. Existing portrait upload hints already say “16 MB”; no other UI storage-byte totals or editors exist.

`packages/client`:
- **Dismissible windows** (dialogclose, 2026-11-02): `ui/Dialog`, `ui/Sheet` and `ui/Popover` provide a top-right X by default through `WindowClose`. It uses the shared close icon, a 32 px hit target (44 px with a coarse pointer), the accessible name and hover/focus tooltip “Close”. Titles reserve space for it and wrap without crossing it. The X calls the same open-change handler as dismissal, so cancellation and draft protection stay with the caller; Escape and outside dismissal remain available. `ConfirmDialog` uses the alert-dialog primitive, has no X, and disallows outside dismissal; its action buttons resolve it. Footer buttons that only closed a dismissible window are removed. The mobile navigation drawer uses the same X. The nonmodal column editor retains its explicit return control and disabled pointer dismissal. Portrait/picture surfaces and the side image viewer retain their own controls pending portraitview.
- **Menu bounds** (`ui/Menu.tsx`): menus, submenus and action menus keep an 8 px viewport margin and remain inside it when their trigger shifts or scrolls out of view (Base UI’s `sticky` positioning). Popup height is capped to the available space and the contents scroll; a newly mounted lorebook-row menu can therefore still reach Delete near the window’s bottom.
- **Build and routing:** React 19 with React Compiler 1.0 (Babel plugin), Vite 8, and TanStack Router (code-based routes, built from the route registry below).
- **Server state:** comes through one `AtomRpc` client (`rpc.ts`) over the same WebSocket protocol, with reconnect on transient errors. Components read it with `@effect/atom-react`.
  - **Queries** render through `AsyncView` (`actions.tsx`): loading, an error with a retry, or the value. **A loading state always ends** in the content or in something the user can act on: `Loading` (`ui/Spinner.tsx`) given `onRetry` says after 15 s that it is taking longer than it should, with Try again. `AsyncView`, the group page, the new-chat pages (whose load failure also offers Try again), the chat view, the editor and the session check pass one; a lazily loaded page's fallback retries by loading the page again. **A read lost with the connection isn't a dead server** (`FailureView`): the socket drops when the server's answers are slow to arrive (a missed ping) and reconnects, so on an `RpcClientError` the view asks `/healthz`; while the server answers, it shows `still` ("Still loading your chats…" in the left panel) with a spinner and asks again by itself a second later, at most five times a minute; "Can't reach the server" shows only when the server doesn't answer, or the connection keeps dropping. Each query names reactivity keys (`connections`, `credentials`, `models`, `network`, `users`). `allOf` combines queries a page needs into one atom, so they're requested together rather than one after another.
  - **Shared read lifetimes** (tabperf3, 2026-11-02). `features/library/queries.ts` gives every live/archived entity-kind list one atom, shared by the library, pickers, card-name checks, notes and lorebook editors under the existing `library` invalidation key. These lists, account defaults, model-use lists and global regex retain their results for 400 ms after their last subscriber, so speculative React renders that suspend do not repeatedly start the same read; lorebooks retain their existing five-minute lifetime. Reactivity invalidations still refresh retained queries after writes. `useAtomRevalidated` refreshes once when the first reader returns, rather than again for each editor joining an already mounted reader. The first local chat-context snapshot is identified separately from server change notifications: `useRefreshOnContext` skips a query already waiting or completed since that session began, but refreshes an older result. Every actual server Cache notification still refreshes it. Display regex starts once the initial context is known. Both card prompt-use explanations share one `GetCardPromptUse` query under `settings`/`library`, so a preset change refreshes their guidance. `e2e/chatReadCounts.spec.ts` counts real WebSocket requests for chat navigation, panel tabs and large editors; its chat-open and shared-card budgets accompany preset-rename and snippet-scope write regressions. `READ_COUNTS_WORK` selects a persistent synthetic scale dataset and five measurement runs.
  - **Paired chat-open timing** (`perf/chatOpen.perf.ts`, opt-in). `CHAT_OPEN_DATA`, `CHAT_OPEN_CHAT`, `CHAT_OPEN_REFERENCE` and `CHAT_OPEN_WORK` select an existing synthetic database/chat, archived reference client and work directory; `CHAT_OPEN_CURRENT` optionally selects the candidate build. One server and database serve both builds through an atomic static-root symlink swap. Each build has its own browser context with identical panel state and two discarded warmups, followed by 15 samples per build (`CHAT_OPEN_RUNS` overrides), with AB/BA pair order alternating. In-page click/DOM/animation-frame timestamps record editable, painted and attachment-ready milestones; RPC start/end times, long tasks and host load are saved outside the checkout. A process check before and after each sample rejects interference from another build/test job. Controller-side polling time is retained separately, so it does not define the in-page latency.
  - **Writes** run through `useAction`, which tracks the pending state and the error, and invalidates the keys the write changes, after a success and after a `StaleWrite`, so the user sees the latest version. It calls the client directly rather than through `AtomRpc.mutation`: that atom is shared per RPC, so a second call would interrupt the first.
  - **Errors** keep their tags (`errors.ts`) and are shown in a sentence each. The server's own messages, such as the last-admin or own-password-first rejections, are shown as given: the client doesn't repeat the server's rules.
- **Sessions** (`session.ts`, §4). The app shell reads `GetSession`. `Unauthorized`, from it or from any later call, sends the user to `/login?next=…` (a path on this site only). Login and logout are `fetch` calls to the HTTP endpoints, followed by a full page load (a failed logout says so and loads nothing), so the WebSocket reopens with the new cookie and nothing cached for the previous user survives.
- **Registries** (spec/PLUGINS.md §8; `registry.ts`, `routes.tsx`, `slots.tsx`). The same rules as the server's (§6): entries by id, a registration overrides the same id, `disable` hides one, and each returns a function that undoes it, in any order.
  - **Routes:** each screen registers an id, a parent (a layout entry, or `root`), a path relative to it and a component, and optionally a navigation label and order. The router is built from the registry at startup. A layout's navigation lists its children, admin-only entries for admins (the server still decides).
  - **Settings navigation** (`features/settings/index.tsx`, `groups.ts`): the `settings` route's children are its pages, each at its own URL (`/settings/chats`, so a link lands on the page it means). `settingsGroups` registers the headings they sit under: **Models** (Connections, Keys, Network, Costs), **Chatting** (Chats, Interface, Regex scripts, Notifications), **Account** (Account, Users), **Admin** (Server status). A group lists the core pages it holds (`pages`, by route id) so the default layout is in one place; a page that names `nav.group` itself sits there instead, and a page in no group this user sees goes under **More**. A group can be `adminOnly`: others don't see it, and a page it claims sits for them in the next group that claims it too. Admin is admin-only and Account also claims Server status, so a user who isn't an admin finds it under Account and never sees an Admin heading. A plugin adds a group, joins one with `nav.group`, or overrides or disables a group by id. From 768 px the groups are a column beside the open page and `/settings` opens the first page; below it `/settings` is the grouped list and each page opens alone under a back link to it and its name. A page inside a page (a connection, a new connection) gets a back link to that page instead, without a heading; a connection's own back link shows only from 768 px, beside the column. The layout sets the document title only at the list, since its effect runs after the page's own `useTitle`. Each page's `nav.description` (a field of the route entry) says what it's for: under its name in the phone's list, and from 768 px the link's tooltip, with a hidden copy outside the link as its accessible description so the link's text stays its name (`e2e/settingsNav.spec.ts`).
  - **Slots:** a named place in a screen that renders its registered entries in order. The first is `connection.sections`: every section of a connection's page is an entry.
  - **Chat panels** (`features/chat/panels.tsx`): descriptors register stable IDs, labels, order, icons, a placement (`tools`, the default, or `cast`), availability, components and optional preloading. The chat feature installs This chat, Model, Prompt preset, Notes, Lorebooks, Summaries and History edits as tools and Cast in the cast strip through this API; the character feature installs the `card:<entityId>` tab family in the cast strip through a matcher and a tab-list function whose entries carry a portrait and, on the persona, the word "you", in the chat's join order with the persona last. A card tab exists only for a card of the viewed chat (a participant, the persona, or one that left on this branch; any card while the cast is still loading). `panelHere` resolves a requested tab against the viewed chat: a family's tab this chat doesn't offer, such as another chat's character carried by a sidebar link's `?panel=` or this browser's remembered tab, opens the panel's default tab (This chat) instead, as a pick in the sidebar does, and the URL is rewritten to it (`e2e/chatPanelSwitch.spec.ts`). URL and remembered-tab validation resolve against the registry, and the same descriptors supply header buttons, tab labels and bodies. Exact IDs can override or disable one tab of a family; an explicit disable blocks family fallback. Validation with a viewed chat requires a tab actually offered by that descriptor, including command targets and panel navigation. Composer settings buttons and a character tab’s Notes link disappear while their target panel is unavailable. `lazyPanel` supplies a per-mounted-panel loading/error boundary and retry with a fresh lazy import, and a static `preload`: once the panel is open and the browser idle, it loads every registered tab's code (`preloadPanel`, beside a descriptor's own `preload`), and a tab whose code is loaded mounts its content at once instead of through `React.lazy`, whose fallback React holds on screen for at least 300 ms (night/tabperf: a first visit took 370–800 ms in the 100,000-message chat whatever the data's speed, now 125–340 ms with its data on a host at load 40). Visited bodies remain mounted while switching tabs, retaining drafts. Disabling or making a descriptor unavailable removes its tabs and prevents its body from opening.
  - **Chat commands** (`features/chat/commands.tsx`): registered IDs, labels, order, icons, availability and handlers receive the viewed session and fork, history navigation and message navigation. The history feature contributes `history.search-replace` and `history.edits`, both opening the existing history workspace. The search-and-replace command declares Mod+H; menu and keyboard invocation resolve the same effective registration, including overrides and disabling. Commands can declare a target panel; both history commands do, so hiding or making History unavailable also hides the menu entries and disables Mod+H.
  - **Editing/version shortcuts** (`replyCommands.ts`): ArrowUp in an empty composer edits the last loaded message; Ctrl/Cmd+ArrowUp edits the last message on your side, from the empty composer or outside inputs. At the tip, it searches older path windows if needed and opens the target; a changed fork, tip, path or cast cancels the read. Both resolve `message.edit`, including its availability, override and disablement. Message rows and commands share `cast.ts`'s side classification: a played card is on your side even when the model wrote it, and another cast card is a reply even when you wrote it. ArrowLeft/ArrowRight outside inputs step versions of the last finished reply through the effective `messageVersions` registration; hidden versions are skipped and Right past the last generates another. Buttons and gestures share `stepVersion`, which rechecks the viewed fork and selection after a list read. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter in a message editor and its Save button invoke registered `message.save`. Commands ignore typing in other inputs, shadow editors, composition, repeats, extra modifiers and dialogs. Each shortcut is in its control's explanation (Edit's, the version arrows', Continue's, Save's, Search and replace's in the ⋯ menu) and in the ⋯ menu's Keyboard shortcuts dialog; the composer has no shortcuts popover of its own (owner, 2026-11-02, DESIGN §10.1).
  - **Composer controls** (`features/chat/composerControls.tsx`): entries declare an ID, placement, order, availability and component, with an optional invocation handler. Placements, top to bottom (composer2, owner 2026-11-01): `queue` (full-width rows directly above the box, only while something is queued), `banner` (rows at the top of the box, inside its border, only while they have something: what says how the box stands), then the text on its own row, then the box's control row: `speaker` at its start, `tools` (icon buttons) after it and `actions` at its right end, then `strip` (the next-reply strip of chips) under the box. A placement may be a function of the context, so a control can move with the width instead of vanishing (`compact`). The chat feature registers the model, preset, cache and Next chips and the keyboard shortcuts `?` (strip), the speaker and recent speakers (speaker), earlier text (tools), and Guidance, Generate and Send (actions) through this API; `guidanceEdit.tsx` registers the guidance-edit bar in the `banner` placement, the box's first line. The composer supplies the viewed session and fork, speaker/persona/reply choices, presentation state and callbacks (`replyNow`, `history`); Stop stays on the version being written (DESIGN §3.1 [D]), never in the composer. draft submission, recovery and fork checks stay in its host. Buttons and Enter both resolve the current handler by ID, so replacing or disabling Send/Generate also changes keyboard invocation. Empty Enter and the empty Send button share `replyNow`: with no text or attachments they request a reply without posting a human message. The button does so with guidance on too (there's no guidance to lose; Enter is then Generate), never while a reply's guidance is edited (`editingGuidance`). There is no separate Reply now control: the ▶ chip (ST's force talk) was removed as redundant with the empty Send (owner, 2026-11-17; replynow1), which names who replies, the whole round ("Mira replies", "Mira and Wren reply", "Get a reply" while the decision model chooses; before replynow1 a round read "Mira reply"). The strip wraps on wide screens and scrolls sideways on phones, and the box's control row is a wrapping flex row, so an added control takes its place without breaking the layout or ever narrowing the text.
  - **Continue shortcut** (`replyCommands.ts`, `ContinueAction.tsx`): Alt+Enter resolves the effective `message.continue` handler for the latest finished model reply with text. The button and shortcut share availability and next-model capability checks; disabling or replacing that action affects both. If the next model has not arrived yet, Continue awaits the session’s in-flight context read (or starts one), then rechecks the fork, leaf and selected version before acting. A failed or unresolved capability still reports its reason. Alt is excluded from both composers’ send predicate. Keyboard continuation leaves composer text untouched and sends none of it as guidance; the visible Continue button retains its guidance behavior and names the shortcut in its tooltip. Commands ignore composition, dialogs and repeat events.
  - **Message actions** (`features/chat/messageActions.tsx`; msgactions, owner 2026-11-01): an entry has an id, `order`, `group`, `available`, an optional keyboard `run`, a default `pinned`, a `describe` component and an optional dialog. `describe` calls `show` with the action's view on the message (`MessageActionView`: a short `label`, a `hint` explaining it in full, a distinct `icon`, `tone`, a `disabled` reason or `dimmed`, and `onSelect` or a `link` element); it's a component so a view can follow state (Continue's model check), and `viewOf` makes one from a plain function. The host renders each view twice from the one description: as a row of More actions and, when pinned, as an icon button on the message, so pinning is the registry's, not any action's. The chat feature registers, in menu order: Edit, Continue, Write your own version, New version with guidance… (`guidanceEdit.tsx`), Saved amendment history (`editorHistory.tsx`), Generate a version (human-written turns only), Branch from here, Insert message above/below and Duplicate (`insertMessage/`), Hide from the model, Request it was generated from, Show the original text (`rewrites.tsx`), Copy text, Copy link, Delete version (Delete message with one version) and Delete message (all versions, on a message with several). `message.context` owns both inspector offers. Dialogs mount outside the menu popup, are tied to the effective registration, and close when it is removed, replaced or becomes unavailable. Hosts receive the viewed entry, session/fork, generation/visibility flags and error/undo reporting. `chatBranchControls` registers the header branch picker and its naming/deletion dialogs as `chat.branches`; `messagePreviews` registers the inline history replacement preview as `history.message-preview`; `summaryPreviews` registers the opened summary's replacement preview as `history.summary-preview`. Both preview bodies read the preview provider and the effective History panel, so disabling History removes its inline preview too.
  - **Request action composition** (realuse, 2026-11-05): `message.context` supplies a bare router link; the message-action host owns its menu label, pinned icon and explanations. A tooltip wrapped around the supplied link consumed the host's children, leaving an unnamed menu row and pinned control. `e2e/requestAction.spec.ts` covers navigation from stopped replies and pinned completed replies at 1440/390 px with a fake provider.
  - **Message details** (`features/chat/messageDetails.tsx`, `modelMarks.tsx`, `versionMetrics.tsx`; msgmeta, owner 2026-11-01, after ST's message header and the column under its portrait). An entry of the `messageDetails` registry has an id, a `place` (`header`, after the name, or `portrait`, the column under the portrait, as wide as it, in 11 px muted type), an `order`, the `label` and `description` its Interface switch shows, and a component that renders nothing where the message has none. The chat feature registers, in the header: **Date and time** (`message.time`: "14:32" today, "Mar 4, 14:32" this year, "Mar 4, 2025, 14:32" before, in the browser's locale and its 12- or 24-hour clock, since accounts have no setting for either; the full date and time with seconds in its tooltip), **Cost** (`message.cost`, order 15, from `versionMetrics.tsx`: the §15 cost, "$0.012"), **Model icon** (`message.model-icon`) and **Model name** (`message.model`: `Version.model`, "connection · model" or an import's "API · model", the connection part giving way first); under the portrait: **Message number** (`message.number`, "#3", counted from #1 as the app numbers messages; ST's display counts from #0), **Generation time** (`message.timer`) and **Token count** (`message.tokens`), the figures of §15 "Generation time and tokens". They follow the version shown, so stepping through versions changes them. Every one has a tooltip (hover or focus). The Interface settings' **Message details** fieldset (`MessageDetailSettings`) lists a switch per registered detail, on by default, each with its description and a hint; the choices are the account's `DisplayPrefs.messageDetails` (false hides one), merged by id on the server as the message toolbar's are (`db/displayPrefs.ts`), so a plugin's detail gets its own switch. On a phone the column stays under the (at least 48 px) portrait, where the text beside it leaves room; the header keeps the name and time on their own line. Model labels (modellabel, 2026-11-05): the registered `message.model` detail uses the header's available width up to the toolbar, without a fixed cap. `ModelLabel` measures an invisible intrinsic-size copy and its container with ResizeObserver; the visible connection and separator appear only when the full connection/model text fits. Otherwise the model alone truncates as needed. The measuring copy keeps sizing stable while streaming or resizing; the tooltip retains the full historical text. `e2e/messageDetails.spec.ts` covers the exact Custom/deepseek import at 1440, 390 and 320 px, both themes, with optional scoped layout measurements and header crops. The cost (msgcost1, 2026-11-16) is a `shrink-0` header item like the time where the header doesn't wrap. Where it wraps (below 640 px, or a chat column under 30 rem), neither the cost nor the model label starts a line of its own (`headerGives`: no flex basis, growing up to its content, the cost first): the label takes what the time's line leaves and truncates, so the cost never adds a line, and a long model name no longer takes a third line of its own (review-msgcost1: with a 26-character connection name the cost had pushed the label down between about 328 and 368 px). `e2e/messageCost.spec.ts` compares every message's height and its header's with the cost shown and hidden at 1440 and 390, and for a long connection name at every 8 px from 320 to 640 in both spacing modes, the cost unclipped on the time's line.

**Lab marks** (`modelMarks` registry): an entry has an id, the lab's `label`, an `order`, a `models` pattern tested against the model's key and the `providers` (connection kinds or ST API ids) that are the lab's own; `markFor` takes the first match by key, then by provider, so "anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet" through OpenRouter shows Anthropic's mark and the tooltip says "Anthropic's model anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet through OpenRouter", and OpenRouter's own mark shows only for a key naming no lab. Built in: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Meta, xAI, Qwen, Cohere, Moonshot AI and OpenRouter; anything else gets the app's model icon. The marks are the labs' logos from Simple Icons 16.35.0 (https://simpleicons.org, CC0 1.0; labicons, owner 2026-11-01), each one's path vendored into `modelMarks.tsx` (no runtime dependency) and filled in the text colour, at 14 px: Anthropic, Google (Gemini's sparkle), DeepSeek, Mistral AI, Meta, Qwen, Moonshot AI and OpenRouter. OpenAI, xAI and Cohere aren't in that set, so theirs are LobeHub Icons 1.101.0's mono logos (the `@lobehub/icons-static-svg` package, MIT, its notice beside the vendored paths; owner approved, importreport 2026-11-02), filled even-odd in the text colour as the set draws them. The svg says which (`data-mark-source`: `simple-icons` or `lobehub`). ST's icons are AGPL-3.0 and this app isn't, so none of those is copied; a plugin can replace any mark by id. The accessible name is "<lab> model" and the tooltip names the lab. `Version.modelRef` (`{ provider, model }`) feeds it: the model's connection kind and key for a reply generated here, ST's `extra.api` and `extra.model` for an import (§13). Tests: client `test/messageDetails.test.ts` (registrations, hiding by id, time formats, lab matching, which marks are Simple Icons and which LobeHub logos and that every mark paints only in `currentColor`, a plugin's mark ahead of the built-ins), `e2e/messageDetails.spec.ts` (an imported chat whose last reply has swipes by two labs: the mark, model, time and "#3 8.0s 214t" change as the versions are stepped through, the tooltips, a version generated here with its connection, the generic mark and its ledger figures, the switches hiding each detail; each mark's source, accessible name and paint in the header's text colour, the Anthropic logo and the OpenAI drawing at 1440 and 390 px in both themes, without sideways scrolling).
  - **Inserting messages** (`features/chat/insertMessage/`, registered in `features/index.ts`; spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §4, unit 9). Three registered message actions in "More actions" (group `place`, after Branch from here): **Insert message below** (`message.insert-below`, order 71) on every message, **Insert message above** (`message.insert-above`) only on the first message of the path shown (the window starts at the root), and **Duplicate** (`message.duplicate`), which inserts a copy of the version shown directly below at once and is disabled, with the reason under it, for a version still being written or failed. The insertion editor fills the `chat.message-stream` slot (`presentation.tsx`; `ChatPage` renders it below each message and above the first), inline under its anchor, a sheet below 640 px. It holds the speaker (`SpeakerSwitcher`, defaulting by the registered `insertSpeakerDefaults`: below a character's message, the composer's speaker; below the user's own, the character who spoke last before it), the composer's text box with its `insert` draft (`MessageDraftTarget.Insert`, the session's message editors, so the text is saved, restored on reload and committed as every editor's is), **Generate as ⟨speaker⟩** (the text, if any, is the direction), **Insert** and one **Cancel** (fcomposer, 2026-10-31: it closes the editor, and text typed goes to the recovered texts, as every message editor's Cancel does; with nothing typed it just closes; the sheet's close on phones is the same Cancel). What the next reply re-reads and the cache warmth ("The model will re-read N messages on the next reply (the cache is cold)", `cacheLine`) is no longer one of its lines: while the editor is open it publishes it to the chat's `cacheNotes` (`CacheIndicator.tsx`), so the strip's cache chip shows "↻ re-reads N messages" and the sentence in its popover. Above the buttons, the registered `insertEstimates` lines: "Before the model's history start: the next reply won't see it." (before the stepped start and below nothing a summary covers), and "Inside summarized history: the summary is rewritten on the next reply." when a summary in use covers the anchor. Below the last message at the fork's tip, Insert and Generate are the composer's `SendOrQueue` and Generate X (a reply being written queues them), and that send commits the insert draft (the composer commit takes `composer` or `insert` drafts). Elsewhere they're `ChatSession.insertMessage` (the `InsertMessage` RPC). The new message shows in place, highlighted for 2.5 s (`ChatView.highlight`), with a toast "Message inserted" or "Message duplicated" and **Undo** (`undoInsert`: a running generation stopped, then `DeleteMessage` to the bin). While an inserted message is being generated, a note under it says the next reply won't include it until it's finished. Nothing marks the messages after an inserted or edited one (DESIGN §3.1 "No mark").
  - **Moving messages** (`features/chat/moveMessage.tsx`, registered in `features/index.ts`). **Move up** and **Move down** in "More actions" (group `place`, after Duplicate), each with its hover explanation, disabled with the reason on the first or last message of the branch (and while generating); the session's `moveMessage` reloads the fork's order and highlights the moved message; the toast has Undo (`undoMove`).
    Undo retains the inserting fork when the toast is created, including if the viewer switches to a fork inheriting the insertion before clicking it (`insertUndo.test.ts`). The browser insertion suite covers saved drafts over reload, directed and undirected generation, and appends after a duplicated display end whose structural tip was deleted, at both widths and themes.
    Slot events can arrive out of commit order. The session reads the authoritative window when an anchor is outside it, a newer sibling is already shown, or an unknown inserted slot has no position; inserted slots never enter the append path or become the structural tip. `insertMessage.test.ts` covers reversed sibling events, a child arriving before its anchor, repeated off-window events and a positionless inserted root. Ordinary append events also follow above-first insertions when the structural tip is null.
  - **Numbering by position** (spec §2.3). The header’s paged branch scan is scoped to the viewed fork and refreshed on path revisions, so insertions also renumber branch points outside the loaded window (`e2e/insertMessage.spec.ts`). The client numbers messages, and compares them with the server's positions (the history start, the summarized-through point, the LCM cursor, `cursorPosition`, and summaries' and coverage ranges, the image ranges, the branch header's and picker's numbers), by `positionOf(entry)` (`features/chat/position.ts`: `position`, or the depth in a window without insertions) and `lcmCursor`. An inserted slot's `Slot` event (`PathEntry.inserted` with its `position`) is placed by the session directly below its anchor, the messages after it renumbered; above the window only the numbers move, another fork's is ignored, and later events of a slot keep the position the window gave it. An inserted message is never the leaf: an append (here or from another tab) goes below the fork's tip (`leafSlotId`, the window's structural tip), including after an inserted message shown last. The branch header keys fork points by slot, since an inserted message shares the next message's depth. `test/insertMessage.test.ts` covers the actions' availability, the estimate lines, the speaker default and the placement; `e2e/insertMessage.spec.ts` covers the flow at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark.
  - Client registries expose a subscription and stable immutable snapshots of effective entries and explicit disablements. Panel, command, composer-control and message-action hosts derive their rendered output from those snapshots, so React Compiler retains registration, disabling and disposal as render dependencies. An empty chat-command menu removes its trigger. Routes are still assembled at startup; generic slot outlets also subscribe to captured snapshots. `chatContributions.test.ts` and `actionContributions.test.ts` register synthetic panels, commands, controls and message actions in Effect scopes, exercise replacement/addition/disabling through their hosts and invocation paths, and verify built-in restoration. `e2e/chatContributions.spec.ts` loads a synthetic plugin into the mounted app through Vite, closes its Effect scopes, and checks live panel/control/command/dialog removal, built-in restoration, dependent links and dynamic-family URL validation. The fixture is absent from production builds.
  - **Remaining chat presentation contributions** (`features/chat/presentation.tsx`, `registerPresentation.tsx`): the chat feature registers `card.edit`, `card.fork-for-chat` and `card.choose-version` in `chatCardActions`; both Cast rows and character panels render this outlet. Each action owns its dialog, so removing an action removes an open dialog. Library/editor/card-page actions, badges, provenance and family sections retain the `cardContributions` registry from card forks. A root card's comparison dialog is titled “Compare with family”; descendants use “Compare with parent”.
  - **Timeline rows** (`timelineContributions.tsx`): `timelineTransforms` applies ordered, reversible transformations to message rows. `timeline.history-budget` inserts the history notice; `timeline.lcm` inserts the LCM boundary and substitutes selected summaries. Built-in dividers locate their boundaries from the current rows’ depth ranges, so earlier plugin insertions, entry copies and range projections do not shift them onto another message. Rows have open keys, estimated heights, inclusive depth ranges, optional last-slot identity and a render function; the virtualizer consumes these rather than a closed feature-row union. The host retains paging, measurements, scroll anchoring and link positioning. Boundary, summary and rail bodies render `timelineBoundaries`, `timelineSummaries` and `timelineRails` outlets. Removing all summary bodies restores the originals; removing all boundaries omits their rows; removing all rails also removes reserved width and coverage reads. Recursive summary expansion remains implementation inside the registered summary body.
  - **Settings and message versions** (`presentation.tsx`): `chatSettingSections` registers This chat's sections in order: the chat's name and persona (`settings.chat`), summaries on or off (`settings.summaries`), then, collapsed, names in prompts (`settings.macro-bindings`) and message roles (`settings.roles`), and the pointer to Settings → Chats (`settings.account`); `summaryPanelSections` adds sections to the Summaries tab after the summaries (`summaries.settings`, the chat's summary settings, collapsed); `accountSettingSections` registers the account's summary defaults; `summarySettingFields` supplies the shared LCM fields for both scopes. `messageVersions` supplies version arrows/picker and the optional step handler used by both its buttons and touch swipes. Disabling/replacing that registration affects both paths; a replacement without a step handler declines touch navigation. Draft recovery, version selection, regeneration and error reporting retain their existing session operations.
  - **Chat composition** (`presentation.tsx`): `chatSurfaceProviders` composes ordered wrappers for history preview, preset workspace and portraits, passing the viewed session, view, resolved cast and panel navigation. `chatColumns` holds columns left of the messages (the portrait column, §14.5a; the chat page marks its messages column `data-chat-main` for a column's measurements); `chatOverlays` installs the preset overlay; `chatComposer` installs the composer. Preset consumers tolerate a missing workspace. Built-ins register through `registerPresentation` from the chat feature; lazily loaded bodies keep their implementation in their feature modules. All these outlets subscribe to registry snapshots and support additions, replacement, disablement and disposal. `presentationContributions.test.ts` exercises scoped alternatives through every outlet and row projection, provider ordering and shared gesture resolution; `e2e/presentationContributions.spec.ts` exercises the mounted compiled hosts with a synthetic plugin.
  - The core features register through them (`features/index.ts`), as plugins will.
- **Secrets in forms** (`SecretInput`, `PasswordInput` in `ui/Field.tsx`). Keys, header values, proxy URLs and passwords are uncontrolled inputs read from the form on submit, so React never mirrors them into the DOM's `value` attribute, and dialogs that take them mount only while open, so Cancel forgets them.
  - **Keys aren't password fields.** Browsers' password managers offer to save any `type="password"` field whatever its `autocomplete`, and a saved key would later be offered on the login form. Key fields are plain text masked with `-webkit-text-security` (a browser without it gets a password field instead, so a key never shows in clear), with `autocomplete="off"` and the opt-outs of 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden and Dashlane (`data-1p-ignore`, `data-lpignore`, `data-bwignore`, `data-form-type="other"`). Account passwords stay password fields.
- **Screens** (`features/`), on stock components (CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §8):
  - **Login:** wrong password, `429` with a countdown from `Retry-After`, proxy mode, and "no login needed" when the server signs the caller in without one. A disabled account fails like a wrong password, as the server intends.
  - **Connections:** list, create, and a page per connection: settings (with the row version, so a change made elsewhere is a `StaleWrite` with "load the latest"), key, check, models, custom headers, network route, delete.
  - **Keys:** keys go in and never come out; only the hint shows. A connection whose address its key doesn't allow says so, and allowing it takes the key typed again. Replacing a key lists the origins of the connections using it, then those it allowed before, none ticked, and flags each that the old key didn't allow (§3.12).
  - **Models:** the merged list per connection, each field marked as the user's, the provider's or unknown. Refresh, hide, edit overrides, add by id.
  - **Network** (admins): the proxy as the server returns it, the bypass list, `forceProxy`, and `InvalidNetworkSettings` as a list of problems.
  - **Account** for everyone (password, log out, how you're signed in), and **Users** for admins (create, set passwords, disable).
  - **Import** (`features/library/`, §11): pick or drop files (`FileDrop` in `ui/`: a label around a hidden file input, so it's a picker by click or keyboard too). They upload one at a time, each with its state (waiting, importing, imported, not imported, failed) and its report rendered as plain text, so file text that looks like HTML or Markdown shows as typed. A failure gives its reason, an ended session included. The picker is disabled until a batch is done, so a second batch can't interleave with it. A file over the 64 MB cap is refused before it's sent. With `?into=<ref>` it updates that entry from its new version and says what happened to each variant.
  - **Library** (`/library`, `features/library/list.tsx`): a place to find and open cards at a heavy user's scale (hundreds of cards, long names, personas, forks). Tabs for Cards, Lorebooks, Presets and Notes, each with its count. Cards have a search (display name, version, in-chat name) beside **Show** All / Characters / Personas, then a line with the count ("438 cards", "2 of 438 cards") on the left and a sort (Last used: the card's own last turn, `CardUsage.lastMessageAt` from the shell read; Name; Most chats; Recently changed: `LibraryRef.updatedAt`; Added: `ShellCard.addedAt`; each explained in its option; name breaks ties, and a card with nothing to sort by comes last either way) with the character surfaces' direction button beside it (`SortDirection` in `characters/cardBrowse.tsx`: newest or oldest first, most or fewest, A to Z or Z to A; `e2e/librarySort.spec.ts`), and a **List** / **Grid** view on the right; the tab, show, sort, its direction and the view are remembered per account in the browser (`rp.library.<userId>`). Lorebooks and presets have a search by name. Presets also have the preset pickers' views (§12 "Preset and model pickers": Name, Modified, Used, Archived, the sort shared with the pickers through `DisplayPrefs.presetSort`), each row's line saying when it was edited (or used, or archived), and an archive button beside Edit (`library.archive`, below); archived presets are left out except in Archived (`libraryAtom.archivedPresets`). There are no folders or user tags in the data model yet (the `persona` tag is the only one the client shows) and no bulk actions. A list row is one line of layout that never wraps: a 40×60 picture, then the name, which is the item's link (a character's or persona's details/chats page; a lorebook's or preset's editor at `/library/$refId`; the picture repeats it for a pointer only), clamped to two lines and shown in full on hover, then one line with the Persona / variant / "update available" badges, the `badge` card contributions (the fork count) and "version · N chats · last chatted …" (usage from the shell read, as on the home grid; a persona also shows its usage beside its Persona badge), truncated; then the item's actions. A grid tile is the home grid's tile with the same lines and actions. Rows and tiles use `content-visibility: auto`, and an item mounts its `badge` contributions (which read the card's family) only once it comes within 400 px of the viewport.
    - **Item actions** (`features/library/itemActions.tsx`, the `libraryItemActions` registry). Each entry has `available(context)` and any of `direct` (always shown beside the item), `menu` (its entry in the item's overflow menu, "More actions for <name · version>") and `dialog` (mounted by the host outside the menu, so it survives the menu closing, and unmounted when its action is removed or disabled). `registerItemActions.tsx` registers `library.chat` (direct, cards: **Chat**), `library.edit` (direct, every kind: **Edit**, a link to the entry's editor at `/library/$refId`, so it can be linked and Back returns to the library), `library.archive` (direct, presets that aren't a chat's copy: the archive or, archived, unarchive icon button, a toast if it fails), `library.persona` (a ticked **Persona** item, cards), `library.update` (**Update from file…**, upstream entries but cards, which merges the file) and `library.export` (an **Export as** group, one item per registered export format of the kind, downloaded through a blob link; a failure is a toast). For a card the menu then lists, after a separator, every `actions` card contribution that has a `menu` entry (§14, card contribution seam). **Import a new version…** (`features/cardImport/`, its own feature, §11.1) registers `card-import.new-version` three times: in `libraryItemActions` (cards' upstreams, a menu item and its dialog, in place of `library.update`), in `cardContributions` (`placement: "actions"`, `overflow`: the editor's More menu, inline on the card page) and in `chatCardActions` (a chat's character tab). Each is a button or menu item with its explanation that opens `NewVersionDialog`: pick the file (`FileDrop`), the preview (`mode=preview`) as the changed fields (`changedFields` against `replacementDoc`, text diffs and `ReadableDiff`), the card's picture and the file's side by side when they differ, what's kept and what isn't applied, how many chats follow the card or keep a fixed revision, and "History → restore revision N undoes it"; then **Replace**, which flushes open editors first, invalidates `library` and calls `refreshOpenEditors` so open editors show the new text. `ImportNewVersion({refId?, entityId, label})` is the exported button; without `refId` it finds the card's ref through `CardFamily`. `e2e/cardImport.spec.ts` runs it from the editor at 1440 and 390 px in both themes. `test/libraryItemActions.test.ts` covers availability per kind and the host's direct actions, menu and disabling; `e2e/chatContributions.spec.ts` checks plugin card and library actions appearing and going live in an open menu and a dialog unmounting with its action; `e2e/libraryPage.spec.ts` (seed in `e2e/support/librarySeed.ts`) imports the realistic synthetic ST folder with its pictures repainted as portraits, plus 420 synthetic cards (pictures, long and unbroken names, long versions, forks), and checks the page at 1440 and 390 px in both themes, and that cards, lorebooks and presets open at their own addresses and a stale address says so.
  - **Characters** (`/`, the home screen; `features/characters/`, DESIGN §2.1): the user's character cards as a grid (two to five columns by Home's own width, a container query, so a split frame keeps tiles at their size), personas left out, from one read (`ListCardUsage`, §12), with the user's groups among them as ST shows its group tiles (`ListChatGroups`, §12; both requested at once). Each character's tile has the avatar, the library label and subtitle, and "N chats · <time ago>" or "Never used"; a group's has its members' faces as one picture (`GroupFaces.tsx`: two side by side, three as two above one centred, the same size with no empty slot, four or more in a 2×2 with "+N"), "Group · N" over it, its wrapping name and full wrapping member list (readable on touch screens) and "N chats · <time ago>". Search (a card's label, subtitle and in-chat name; a group's name and its members' names and labels), All / Groups / Never used, and sort by last message (never by last opened; on a tie a group before its members; never used last) or name, restored from the home URL (§12). A click continues the card's latest chat, or opens its pending chat (`/cards/$entityId/chat`) when it has none, so nothing is made. Each character's tile also has **New chat** and **Inspect**, shown on hover or focus with a mouse and always on a touch screen; a group's tile continues its latest chat on a click and has **New chat** (the group's pending chat, below) and **All N chats** (a one-chat group's **Group page**), which opens the group's page; on a narrow tile the second goes under the first (`e2e/homeGroups.spec.ts`, with the bin's readable names).
  - **A group's page** (`/groups/$chatId`, `GroupPage.tsx`, named by any of its chats; `ListGroupChats`, §12): its faces, name and use, **Continue the latest chat**, **New chat** (`/groups/$chatId/new`), its chats (`ChatList` given the group's chats, latest message first, each deletable with the toast; deleting the chat the page is named by moves the page to another of the group's chats), and its characters, each linking to the card's page. A chat that's in no group (gone to the bin, or down to one character) says so, with a link home.
  - **A card's page** (`/cards/$entityId`): avatar, label, subtitle, the in-chat name when it differs, **Continue** (its latest chat), **New chat**, **Edit card** (`/library/$refId`), every chat it joined as peers (`ListChats` by card, the list as below, those with a message first so the first is the one Continue opens), and its definition read from the ref's head (`GetRevision`), each field folded to four lines with Show more, measured again when its width changes (a `ResizeObserver`), keeping what the user opened. A card that isn't a character (a persona, or in the bin) says so and links to the library.
  - **Chats** (`/chats`, the sidebar's list as a page for phones, plus a chat without characters) and a chat (`/chats/$chatId`): §12. Phones have Characters and Chats in the top bar.
  - **The chat list** (`features/chat/ChatList.tsx`; the sidebar, `/chats` and a card's page): pages of 50 (`ListChats`), Load more after the last, and each page's cast, length and last message from `ListChatSummaries`. A row has the readable name and the time of its last message, then on a line of its own when it started (ST's file-name date, else its creation) and its message count, the other characters on a line that may be cut short, and the last message; a name or cast cut short shows in full on hover. A refreshed first page is right down to its last chat, so once later pages are loaded, their chats above its end are dropped (gone, or moved up into it) and the page after it is read again, so a chat pushed off it isn't skipped. Find a chat asks the server (`search`), so it finds chats not loaded yet, and pages its results the same way.
  - **Server status** (`/settings/status`): the server's health. Everyone sees whether it runs normally or is busy (event-loop p99 over 50 ms), its version and how long it has been up; the numbers behind that (event-loop p99 and max, database readers) are an **Admin diagnostics** card shown to admins only.
  - **Bin** (`/bin`, from the header): §3.11. **Notifications** (`/settings/notifications`): §12.
  - **The card and preset editors** (`/library/$refId`): §14.6.
- **Styling** (CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §8):
  - **Tile toggles** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1). On a fine pointer with hover, off favourite stars on character tiles (home, sidebar and character pick grids) and library grid tiles appear only on tile hover or focus anywhere within the tile; on stars always show. Group-tile and chat-list tile pins, and message-image context toggles, share the rule. `tile-toggle-surface` and `tile-toggle` in `styles.css` change opacity and pointer events only: no layout shift, no removal from the tab order or accessibility tree, and existing hover/focus explanations remain; a hidden toggle takes no clicks, so a click there reaches the tile (archivebtn, 2026-11-06: an invisible archive button had covered tile centres in narrow frames). Star and pin overlay backgrounds belong to the button so hiding it leaves no empty patch. Coarse-pointer or no-hover devices keep off toggles visible because tapping the tile already opens it. Chat-list Delete stays in the upper corner on touch, clear of the pin below it. Stars and pins beside names in ordinary rows and editor headers keep their existing visibility. Portrait favourite stars retain their `bg-surface/85` contrast chip during direct hover and while their tooltip is open; the generic icon-button hover wash must not replace it (starhover, 2026-11-02). Library grid footers and their registered action groups wrap within the tile, keeping the favourite and every action inside the clipped tile even at its minimum width; the footer starts with an 8 px inset. Picture links document their intentional edge-to-edge hit target for the layout audit. **Archive toggle** (archivebtn, 2026-11-06; DESIGN §2.1 [D]): a character tile's star keeps the top left corner and its archive toggle (`CardArchive.tsx` `ArchiveControl`, the registered `archive-toggle` card placement) the top right, each in an overlay of its own, so a hidden one moves nothing. Both take `PICTURE_TOGGLE` (`ui/Tooltip.tsx`: `tile-toggle` plus `OVER_PICTURE`, the one backing, on the button; the card placement passes it as `className`) and `aria-pressed` (archived is on), show their new state at once, and follow the rule above. Pickers have none (their top right is the membership mark). Headers, the card page and the side panel's card tab show star and archive side by side, always, as one group (`CardFavourite`), so a wrapping toolbar moves them together (the switchers audit had the archive alone crossing the panel's scroll area at 1024). Card ⋯ menus have no Archive entry; a tile's right-click menu has one. `e2e/tileToggles.spec.ts` checks rest, hover, focus and Tab order on an ordinary, a favourite, an archived and an archived favourite card at 1440/390 in both themes, corner insets, size and backing, the hovers' text, and touch. `e2e/starHover.spec.ts` checks computed opacity, centre/corner hit targets, the retained chip and clicks without navigation across home/sidebar/library grids, library rows and Cast picks, in both themes with synthetic portraits, blank avatars, fork badges and state marks. `e2e/hoverToggles.spec.ts` covers both themes at 1440/390, hover, focus within, sequential tabbing, stable geometry, persistent on states, library/sidebar grids, group pins and touch; `e2e/chatImages.spec.ts` covers image-context toggles.
  - **Semantic tokens only.** `styles.css` defines colors by role (`canvas`, `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `accent`, `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `overlay`, …), for light and dark, with `data-theme` overrides.
  - **The default Tailwind palette is removed** (`--color-*: initial`), so a class like `bg-zinc-800` doesn't exist. Only token utilities (`bg-surface`, `text-muted`) can be written. A redesign changes token values, not components.
  - **Cursors, hover and scrollbars** (`styles.css`, its base layer, so a utility class still wins): every enabled control (buttons, the button-like ARIA roles, summaries, selects, checkboxes and the labels holding them) shows the pointer, a disabled one the arrow, a busy one `progress`; text fields keep the text cursor and drag handles their own. Icon buttons, the version counter and reasoning actions hover with the see-through `hover` token, so they look the same on the user's raised messages as on replies. Every scrollbar is thin, a muted `scrollbar` thumb on no track, `scrollbar-hover` while the pointer is over what scrolls; a scrolling list of cards keeps a stable gutter and a gap before the bar (the sidebar). `e2e/cursorsAndBars.spec.ts` checks the computed cursors, equal hover styles on both sides in both themes, and the sidebar's gap.
  - **One import path for UI components.** Feature code imports from `src/ui/`, never from Base UI directly; ESLint enforces it. Base UI carries behavior and accessibility (labels, focus traps, keyboard), and `src/ui/` carries the look: buttons, fields, select, checkbox, switch, radio group, dialogs, cards, badges, alerts, menus, tooltips and icon buttons, and line icons (`Icon.tsx`).
  - **Plain HTTP works** (uuidfix, 2026-11-07). The app is also opened over plain HTTP on LAN addresses, which aren't secure contexts, so `crypto.randomUUID` is missing there. Client ids come from `uuid()` (`src/uuid.ts`, a v4 UUID from `crypto.getRandomValues`); ESLint forbids `.randomUUID` in `packages/client/src`. `e2e/insecureContext.spec.ts` removes `crypto.randomUUID` before the page loads, then attaches an image and adds a cost formula.
  - **Portaled menus** (`ui/Menu.tsx`) use fixed viewport coordinates for both ordinary and action-menu positioners. A menu opened in a scrolled fixed phone sheet stays clickable instead of making the document scroll repeatedly under it. The explanations spec exercises portaled menu descriptions at 1440 and 390 px in both themes.
  - **Submenus** (`ui/Menu.tsx`, exportsubmenu, 2026-11-02). `MenuSubmenu` wraps Base UI's submenu root and trigger with the menu's semantic styling, fixed positioning, collision padding and item explanations. Hover, click, Enter and → open it; ← and Escape return to its parent. Hover opens immediately and allows 200 ms to cross into the submenu; clicks explicitly open it, including without hover. Its trigger's side explanation is suppressed while the submenu is open so the explanation cannot cover the choices; the accessible description remains. `Menu` supplies an action context: `MenuAction` renders the same registered action as a menu item there and a button elsewhere. The Cast member menus (saved and pending chats) use `Menu` with `keepMounted`, keeping registered actions' dialogs alive after selection closes the menu. There is no blanket click-capture dismissal. Export uses this submenu in Cast and the library; standalone editor controls use the same format items in a root menu. `e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts` offers `LAYOUT_AUDIT_EXPORT_MENUS_ONLY=1` for these menus (including pending Cast); the detector's optional `scope` limits findings to the selected surface without hiding its boundary checks.
  - **Explanations beside controls** (owner, 2026-11-01): action buttons, menu items and choices say what they do in a short sentence beside them, so their labels stay short and plain. Feature code passes `description` and `ui/` shows it:
    - **Menu items and select options** (`MenuItem`, `MenuLinkItem`, `MenuCheckboxItem`, `ActionMenu` items, `SelectItem`; `ui/Explanation.tsx`). With a mouse it's a tooltip-styled box beside the highlighted item, hovered or reached with the arrow keys: one `HighlightExplanation` per popup, rendered in the positioner (so the list's scrolling doesn't clip it), follows `data-highlighted` on the items carrying `data-explain` through a `MutationObserver`, on the right of the list or the left when the right has no room, level with the row and kept inside the window, so it never covers the rows below. The first shows after 350 ms, the rest at once while the list is open. On a touch screen or under 640 px (`pointer-coarse`, `max-sm`), where nothing hovers and there's no room beside, the box is hidden and the text shows under each label in muted type instead. The same element is the item's `aria-describedby`, `aria-hidden` so it stays out of the name: `getByRole` names are unchanged, while an item's text content includes it. `NativeSelect` can't draw beside the browser's list: a description is the option's `title`.
    - **Segmented choices**: an option's `description` is its tooltip and its description; on touch and narrow screens the chosen option's shows under the row. `RadioGroup` options, `Checkbox` and `Switch` keep theirs inline under the label; a `Checkbox`'s or `Switch`'s `hint` says what turning it on or off does, as a tooltip over the row on hover and focus, under the label on touch and narrow screens, and as its description (the Lorebooks tab's switches, whose effect differs by where the book comes from: a card's own, added to this chat, or global, which the hint spells out).
    - **Buttons**: `Button`'s `hint` is a tooltip on hover and focus and the button's description; `IconButton`, `SquareIconButton` and `Popover` take `hint` in place of the label as the tooltip. A chat panel registration's `description` (`PanelDescriptor`) is its tool tab's tooltip and its explanation under More. Registries whose entries become menu items (library item actions, chat commands) carry an optional `description` the host passes on, so a replacement brings its own.
    - **Wording** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1): an explanation says what the control does or what the user gets, with no field names or mechanism, and names SillyTavern only on interop surfaces. `test/stWording.test.ts` parses every client `.ts`/`.tsx` file with the TypeScript compiler and fails on "SillyTavern" or the word "ST" in any string literal, template part or JSX text (comments aren't read) outside its allowlist: whole files for the ST import (`stImport`, `stJobs`, `import`, `FolderBrowser`), connection import from an ST preset (`StSettingsImport`, `connections/list`) and chat export (`chatExport`), and single strings for the export menu item and the Import from SillyTavern entry points. The server's import reports and format diagnostics are interop text and aren't checked.
    - **Headings explain nothing standing** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1): `CardHeader` and `Fieldset` take `description` only for a line of state (a count, progress, who's signed in) and `about` for an explanation the user needs, shown by `ui/AboutHint.tsx`: a quiet "?" (accessible name "About <heading>", its text also the button's description) beside the heading, whose tooltip-styled popup opens on hover, focus or tap. Most former heading descriptions were dropped; Group greetings, the summary sizes, the preset's prompt order and a few others use `about`. The same applies to `Field`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `Slider`, and the editor's field wrappers: help for choosing a value uses `about` beside the label, while `description` keeps live state visible (missing setup, key destinations, active proxies, defaults, progress and errors). Field and choice help remains the control's accessible description. A choice's help button sits outside its clickable label so opening help never changes the value. Card text-field hints use the same "?". Dialogs skip an initial help button when choosing their opening focus, keeping the first control focused; explicit focus and autofocus keep their existing behavior. `e2e/presetTextSwitches.spec.ts` checks help by click and keyboard focus at desktop/phone widths in both themes, including an unchanged switch; `e2e/models.spec.ts` checks field help and accessible descriptions alongside visible reported limits.
    - `e2e/explanations.spec.ts` checks a note's Position select and the Add note menu at 1440 (beside the list, never over it, level with its row, moved by the arrow keys, gone when the pointer leaves) and at 390 with touch (under each label, no box, nothing sideways), in both themes; and spot checks of a panel tab, the Lorebooks tab's choice, a book's switch and its "Remove from this chat", the chat menu and a button.
  - Inputs use 16 px text on touch screens, so iOS doesn't zoom into them. A submit the client refuses focuses the first invalid field, whose description carries the error.
- **Row actions and scrolling edges** (owner, 2026-11-02). `ui/rowSpacing.ts` shares trailing content padding (`rowActionInsetClass`, 8 px by default, overridable with `--row-action-inset`). It belongs inside the row, before any scrollbar, and does not depend on whether the list overflows. `PickerList` reserves 32 px after a secondary action, matching the preset name's inset including its check column; model rows currently have no secondary action. `BlockHeader` gives prompts, notes and snippets 4 px above and below their header row (so a highlighted action button doesn't touch the block's edge; owner, 2026-11-02) and 8 px after their actions, matching the leading content padding (switches, handles and portraits are accessories, not empty edge padding). Sidebar `ForkRow` instances (chat lists, pinned chats, branch lists and character pages), start-chat choices, the chat's lorebook rows and branch/version picker action groups use the same helper. Lorebook entry headers use 16 px (their outer 8 px, the layout audit's, plus the title field's 8 px); the legacy chat list's Delete and pin sit 10 px from the row edge, matching its link's padding. Library rows/tiles and Cast retain their existing surrounding gutters. Shared tooltip and popover positioners use Base UI's collision placement with 8 px viewport clearance; tooltip width is capped to the viewport less that clearance. `e2e/rowEdges.spec.ts` uses synthetic overflowing lists at 1440/390 in both themes, classic scrollbars, reduced motion for stable geometry, actual `clientWidth` measurements excluding the scrollbar, row-edge measurements, a filtered preset list without a scrollbar, preset checks at 320/480/768/1024 px, hover and keyboard-focus tooltip bounds, and optional screenshots/geometry via `SCREENSHOT_DIR`. `ROW_EDGES_BEFORE=1` records the same scenes against an unchanged build without enforcing the new inset assertions.
- **Message text** is Markdown through `ui/Markdown.tsx` (§12).
- **Tests:**
  - `test/` (Vitest): the registries.
  - `e2e/` (Playwright, `npm run test:browser` for Chromium, `npm run test:browser:all` for Chromium/Firefox/WebKit, outside `npm run check`): both commands first build the client and database worker bundles (including for specs that explicitly use bundled workers), then run the built client against the real server and its database workers (bundled; `E2E_DB_WORKERS=source` runs them from source), with a worker per three of the host's free cores, at most 12 but at least a sixth of the cores (`PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS` overrides it), each file with its own servers on random ports and fresh data directories, and a fake OpenAI-style provider on loopback. One flow per screen (the import screen's in `e2e/library.spec.ts`), a cross-user check through the UI (another user never sees someone's connections or keys, in a separate tab or after logout in the same one), every screen at phone and desktop width in light and dark with no sideways scrolling, and dialogs from the keyboard. `SCREENSHOT_DIR` saves screenshots. `e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts` (the layout audit over a large synthetic library) is opt-in: it runs only with `LAYOUT_AUDIT=1`. The library export test checks the exact blob handed to a native download, its filename, and saved bytes. If Chromium reports `canceled`, file saving is quarantined only when a separate plain synthetic download also cancels; the blob assertions still run, and the report is annotated. An unwritable browser download directory reproduces this even without the app or CSP; the original environment's cause was not established. The browsers come from `~/.cache/ms-playwright`; CI installs Chromium's headless shell. Other engines are opt-in, installed for the pinned Playwright version with `npx playwright install firefox webkit`. The queue conflict flow has its own server with a synthetic reply longer than the test deadline (`queue.spec.ts`), so the queue cannot drain between edits on a loaded host. The Firefox suite includes key-field CSS masking and password fallback checks (`secrets.spec.ts`). Firefox has an intermittent reload timeout in `chatSetup.spec.ts` (the second reload after changing chat settings), reproduced in repeated runs; its cause is unresolved. On this host WebKit cannot launch: its system libraries are missing, so its suite and masking remain unverified.
- **Stable unavailable controls** (stablebuttons, owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1). A control between other elements stays visible, disabled and greyed with a hover/focus reason when temporarily unavailable. Only a trailing control whose appearance moves nothing else may come and go; constant item-kind applicability remains distinct. `FieldEditHistory` always renders `EditHistory`, disabled with "No edit history yet." before the first state. Revert stays disabled in the shared save cluster while clean or saving. Key actions, model-limit pencils, queued Edit, Continue round, message actions, version arrows/counter, the header's branch trigger, saved and pending composer Send, composer history/cache/next-reply choices and summary edit/catch-up controls keep their places. Shared buttons and popover triggers support focusable disabled controls with tooltips and faded styling. `MessageAction.available` describes applicability; `disabled` returns a temporary reason and also guards keyboard invocation. Whole-text editor actions remain mounted, using `TextAction.applies` for applicability and `unavailable` for an unavailable reason; empty Send text to snippet stays disabled. The selection action retains its existing leading position in the end-aligned strip and moves no other control. Responsive overflow menus still adapt to the room available, and item lists and navigation still reflect their contents. `e2e/stableButtons.spec.ts` measures both one-line and multiline field history, text-action/save strips, connection keys/model limits, queue/message/version/composer controls and summary headers at 1440/390; `replyRounds.spec.ts` and `lcmEnable.spec.ts` measure round and catch-up transitions.
- **Layout audit** (`e2e/support/layoutAudit.ts`, `e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts`). Browser geometry checks with a 1 px tolerance: controls inset by the shared 8 px content spacing from enclosing borders, padded edges and scrollports; text width/height clipping without ellipsis or line clamp, including text fragments past container edges; a control's short label (16 characters or fewer) cut by an ellipsis, which is for names only (replynow1, 2026-11-17; `layoutAuditRules.spec.ts`; a user-given name, the chat's title or a branch's, is marked `data-layout-name` and may be cut); unequal gaps and CSS-declared row alignment; painted sibling/content intersections, including across wrappers. SVG icons are atomic drawing surfaces; rows include transparent hover actions and the children of `display:contents`, and respect grid row spans and flexible spacers. Invisible hanging whitespace in pre-wrapped text is excluded from clipping findings. It walks open shadow roots (code editors), clips overlap measurements to ancestor scrollports, and excludes hidden/closed content and screen-reader text. Native field values can scroll. Single divider borders do not establish a surrounding box. `data-layout-audit-ignore="rule: reason"` opts out only that rule in a component's subtree; missing reasons are failures. `data-layout-overlay="reason"` allows overlap with the underlying page, while still checking the overlay's own contents. Shared portals, portrait actions and row actions declare these intentions at their source. Joined segments, edge tabs, full-width disclosures and editor surfaces explain their inset exceptions; header portrait stacks explain their overlap exception. Each finding has a selector, measured discrepancy, related container and screenshot crop, attached before a soft assertion so the sweep continues. The spec imports synthetic scale data into a fresh database (or reuses an explicitly supplied `LAYOUT_AUDIT_WORK` outside the checkout), then visits home filters, sidebar views, chat panel tools and card sub-tabs, editors, settings, import, bin, inspector and dialogs at 1440/1024/390 px in light/dark, including a panel widened by dragging. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_ST_FOLDER` accepts a synthetic ST fixture; otherwise the checked-in scale generator supplies hundreds of cards and thousands of chats, supplemented by the realistic synthetic fixture. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_SURFACES` and `LAYOUT_AUDIT_SMALL=1` restrict iteration only; `LAYOUT_AUDIT_SHOTS` (a surface pattern) keeps a whole-window screenshot of each matching surface under `shots/` in the work folder, for before-and-after evidence. Run the full spec before UI approval. Controls over a picture (carrying or inside a `data-layout-overlay` whose positioned container holds an image or `[data-portrait]` it covers) get a sixth rule, `overlay` (archivebtn, 2026-11-06: the archive toggle passed with its backing on a wrapper, under a hidden star's kept place, shown on every tile, because overlays were exempt and the audit only saw the Archived view): one backing, on the control itself; no space kept by a hidden sibling before any shown control, including between visible controls; in a grid of tiles the first shown control of each overlay at the inset most tiles use; where a pointer can hover, a control shown on a tile at rest must be a pressed toggle; and a hidden control takes no pointer events. `expectLayout(..., { hovered: true })` audits with the pointer left on a hovered tile. A seventh rule, `fill` (composerbottom1): a `[data-chat-main]` column ends at the bottom of its frame (the page's `main` or a workbench pane's `[data-frame-body]`), and its last in-flow block (the composer) at the column's bottom. Broken geometry fixtures verify the detector's eight rules, reasoned exceptions, overlay contents and shadow-root traversal. A row of tabs (`ui/Tabs.tsx`, not the panel's `PanelTabs`) wraps onto further rows rather than run out of its column, beside its `end` controls too (the card editor's tabs on a phone); `wrap` now only makes the tabs tighter for a narrow column. A toolbar's separator takes the toolbar's gap with no margin of its own, so its gaps stay even. `Segmented`'s inline explanation (touch and narrow screens) is `w-0 min-w-full`: it wraps at the choices' width rather than set the column's. A preset prompt header's chips, count and actions group (`PromptDocument.tsx`) may shrink (`min-w-0 max-w-full`) and wraps inside the header at 390 px.
- **Note and block insets** (layoutlint, 2026-11-02). `Switch.labelHidden` removes the hidden label from its flex row, avoiding a phantom gap that pushed a centred switch outside its leading accessory slot; notes, prompt switches, lorebooks and regex switches use it. `BlockHeader` keeps 8 px above/below and before its controls, with 12 px after its actions (matching the name control's additional 4 px content inset). Notes grid sections have `min-w-0`, so column text can shrink and wrap. Sidebar headers/rows, tile actions, picker/chat scrollports, summary dividers, import banners keep their surrounding insets. The composer's rows and the next-reply strip keep 8 px too. The portrait's corner toolbar, the card editor's sticky tabs (`Tabs` `rowOverlay`), framed field text and the new-tag chip declare their overlay or inset intent; a multi-line field's bottom strip (`ui/FieldFrame.tsx`) is padded 8 px. Message footers no longer use a negative bottom margin that reduced version controls’ clearance to 6 px. Sticky save/tool bars, field expand actions and group collage count badges declare their intended overlay behavior; compact tag remove actions and full-row outline drag handles explain their inset exceptions. Menu and select popups keep the same 8 px surrounding inset, including non-native menu items and options. Branch rows and their scroller have the same inset. Ordinary `Tabs` leave scrolling to the enclosing view; only height-filling tabs create their own padded scrollport, avoiding flush controls against a redundant nested scroll box. Slider thumbs declare their intentional overlap with the track. The borderless next-reply strip explains that its inset belongs to the surrounding composer and its horizontal scrollbar is hidden. These changes repair existing layouts without introducing surfaces.
- **Picture overlay scope** (fix-layoutaudit-popover, 2026-11-07). The picture-control rule applies to local overlays: it skips layers positioned against `document.body` and layers portalled through a Base UI portal inside their positioned host. Popup contents still receive the other geometry checks, and local picture controls inside a popup retain the picture-control checks. Regressions cover the branch menu over message portraits in a 1024 px half-width frame and the composer's speaker picker over portraits, in both themes; the speaker picker no longer waives overlay findings. `starHover.spec.ts` also audits picture controls at rest and hovered.
- **Development:** `npm run dev:server` (the development entry point, `src/dev/main.ts`, §12) and `npm run dev:client`. Vite proxies `/rpc` and `/auth` to the server.

### The chat panel's tool order (tabdrag1, 2026-11-17; DESIGN §10.1 "Tab order")

- **One list.** `DisplayPrefs.panelTabOrder` (the account's `display` setting, written whole by `SetDisplayPrefs`; at most 200 values of at most 200 characters) holds the tools' tab values in the user's order; empty is the registry's order. `ui/tabOrder.ts`: `inOrder` puts the tools it names first, in its order, and the rest (new or plugin tools) after in theirs; `storedOrder` writes a rearranged chat's tools back with each stored tool this chat doesn't offer (Summaries in a workshop, a disabled plugin) kept after the one it followed. `ChatPanels.tsx` applies it, and Reset writes `[]`. No schema change: the `display` row decodes over the defaults.
- **The fit** (`fitTools`): everything when it all fits; otherwise the longest prefix beside More. When the open tool is past that prefix it's a **guest**: its width and the divider's are reserved first and the prefix counted again, so the result is a pure function of the measured widths and the row's width, and showing the guest never changes the count it was computed with (no flipping at boundary widths). The guest renders after a `bg-border` divider (`data-tab-guest-divider`), in the tab list, as the selected tab (`data-tab-guest`, described "Its place is under More"); its entry in More stays at its place with a "Shown above" check (`data-shown-above`, hidden from its accessible name).
- **Dragging** (`ui/ToolTabs.tsx`, pointer events on window): a mouse or pen drags past 5 px; a finger after a 500 ms rest (Base UI's long press opens the tool's context menu at the same moment; moving then closes it and drags, and `touchmove` is cancelled while armed so the sheet doesn't scroll). Targets: before a row tool (by its middle), the row's end, More (the end of the order; held 600 ms, More opens), or before a More entry. The row's end and More's start are one place in the order, so a drop is then stepped on (dropped in More) or back (dropped in the row) until the tool lands on the side it was dropped on. The drop mark is an accent bar; the dragged tool fades and a copy follows the pointer (portal, `data-layout-overlay`); the release's click is swallowed, so a drop never opens a tool; Escape cancels. More stays open (controlled) during a drag and while an entry's context menu is open; a drop in the row closes it. Tools that change place slide there (Web Animations FLIP, 180 ms; none with reduced motion).
- **Without a drag**: every row tool, the guest and every More entry is a `ContextMenu` trigger with Move left/right (up/down in More), Move to start, Move to More / Move to end / Move out of More (the last place in the row where it shows as a tool), Arrange tabs… and Reset tab order (disabled at the usual order). More ends with Arrange tabs…, a `Dialog` over the shared `SortableList` with Move up/down buttons per row and an "In More" badge for those past the current fit. `MenuItem` takes a `className` for the drop mark.
- **Tests**: `client/test/tabOrder.test.ts` (ordering, kept absent tools, moves, a fit that is stable and monotonic over every width); `e2e/panelTabOrder.spec.ts` (drag within the row, context-menu moves and Reset, onto More / inside More / up from More / held on More, the guest's place, marker and removal, dragging the guest, a 120-pixel resize sweep with no tab-list mutations after each step, reload persistence, Arrange tabs…, touch long-press drag and menu, layout audit of the guest row, More, the tool menu and Arrange tabs at 1440 and 390 in light and dark).

### The workbench: frames and tabs (workbench, 2026-11-05; DESIGN §10.1)

The center column is the workbench (`features/workbench/`), registered as the shell's `shell.center` slot (`centerColumn` in `shell.tsx`; with nothing registered the shell shows the routed page as before, through the same `CenterPage`).

- **Model** (`model.ts`, pure, `client/test/workbenchModel.test.ts`): a tree of splits (`row`: side by side, `column`: above each other, with shares summing to 1) over frames, each with its tabs and the one shown; the focused frame; the tabs most recently focused first. A tab is an id, its view's URL and a preview flag.
