After the connection's `idleTimeoutS` of silence (`ProviderSettings`, Int ≥ 1, default `DEFAULT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` 300 in `@rp/shared/providers.ts`; stored in `provider_settings_json`; the connection form's Advanced "Wait for a response (seconds)") the request aborts and fails as `providerError("no_response", "The provider sent nothing for N s.")`, not retried
  - our `fetch` (§2, outgoing requests)
  - `onResponse` for the status and `Retry-After`
  - `onProviderStreamEvent` for raw usage
- **The result:** provider configuration comes only from the connection, resolved model and explicit request options. Environment keys, custom headers, organization/project, cloud modes, cache retention and logging do not override them. The effective model/catalog headers join the request inventory before any capture or HTTP; connection headers retain their normal override precedence.
- **The pi model** is built per request from the merged description (`resolveModel`). When pi's catalog entry is for the same wire API, it's the base, so its request settings carry over. For example, DeepSeek's `max_tokens` field and reasoning replay come from the catalog (`test/providerStream.test.ts` checks the request body).
- **Catalogs** (`catalog.ts`) belong to their kind and load on first use. pi-ai's per-provider catalogs serve the built-ins; an exact match there fills the fields the list didn't report and records them in `upstream.catalog`. A model added by id gets the same (price, reasoning, vision, thinking levels; liveapi F1): `refreshModels` and `catalogUpstream` share `describeModels` (kind catalog, then catalogs by id, then shims).
- **Claude thinking per family** (thinkhide1; reviewed 2026-11-14; `claudeThinking.ts`). On Anthropic Messages, family defaults fill models without catalog compatibility data; catalog-listed models and saved overrides retain their original request shapes. Direct, Bedrock, Vertex, dated and proxy-prefixed Claude ids are recognized. The 4.6 Opus/Sonnet families prefer adaptive thinking, map xhigh to high and support max; 4.5 and earlier retain budgets. Claude 4.7 and later use adaptive thinking without a budget; an unknown Claude family defaults to that newest shape. Mythos Preview uses adaptive thinking with no xhigh. With no effort selected, Opus 4.7/4.8 and Sonnet 5 can send disabled (thinking is otherwise off on Opus 4.x); families that reject disabled omit the field and use their model default. Explicit adaptive requests include summarized display and effort, with the requested output cap unchanged. Interleaved thinking is automatic with adaptive thinking; legacy manual-mode headers and budget adjustment remain pi-ai's. The family parser does not affect other wire APIs. Sources: [thinking configurations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking-troubleshooting), [effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort). `claudeThinking.test.ts` checks actual request bytes, boundaries, output caps, missing effort, explicit overrides and cloud ids.
- **List fields** (liveapi F2; `modelLists.ts` `fromOpenAi`): besides OpenRouter's and vLLM's, the OpenAI-style list reader takes `context_window` (documented in the models-list responses of Groq and Requesty), `max_output_tokens` (Requesty) and `input_modalities` (xAI's `/v1/language-models`), which fill context, output limit and vision. Fields no public provider documents are not read.
- **Compatibility shims** (`shims.ts`, registry `shims`; owner, 2026-11-07: "specific models on specific providers can have their own compatibility shims"): each names its providers (providerchoice: the connection's provider, not its kind), optionally its APIs, the models it's for in the user's terms, and a model pattern, and can set capabilities, fix some against user edits, and rewrite the final payload. Registered and replaceable by id like any entry, never global. Capabilities and the shims' names go into `upstream` at refresh and add (`shimmedUpstream`; `upstream.shims` and `upstream.fixed`); `resolveModel` ignores a user edit of a fixed field; the model page lists their labels under "Provider rules" (with a "?" explaining them; the UI never says "shim") and disables a fixed Prefill, whose "?" says why. Payload rewrites run in `onPayload` after the registered transforms (`applyShims`). Built-ins:
  - `claude-haiku-5-no-top-p` (anthropic, anthropic-bedrock, anthropic-vertex, openrouter): drops `top_p` ("`top_p` is deprecated for this model", F7).
  - `bedrock-openai-chat-automatic-cache` (openai-bedrock, Chat Completions) and `bedrock-openai-before-5.6-automatic-cache` (openai-bedrock, Responses, GPT-5.5 and earlier and GPT OSS): strip `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, which AWS documents only for GPT-5.6 and later on Responses.
  - `openai-responses-gpt-5.1-5.4-reasoning` (openai and openai-compatible, Responses): with an effort other than none, drops `top_p` and `temperature` and requests `reasoning.summary: "auto"` (F9).
  - `openai-chat-gpt-5.4-tools-no-effort` (openai and openai-compatible, Chat Completions): a Chat Completions request with tools sends `reasoning_effort: "none"`, as OpenAI's error says to; reasoning with tools needs a Responses connection (F10).
  - `openrouter-gemini-4-argon-reasoning-on`: `thinkingLevels.off = null`, so pi-ai sends no effort "none" (F11). Its payload rewrite also removes explicit "none" efforts from model settings or user-edited thinking levels, retaining other reasoning options.
  - `openrouter-gemini-no-prefill`: prefill `none`, fixed; Continue uses its nudge (F13).
  - **Route rules** (liveapi2, DESIGN): a shim that names `upstreams` (OpenRouter provider slugs and names) and `fails` is stored in `upstream.routes` and applies only when the model's routing pins one upstream (`pinnedRoute` in `@rp/shared/providers.ts`: `only` with one entry, or `order` with one and fallbacks off, less `ignore`; a variant such as `deepinfra/fp8` counts as its provider). `routedUpstream` applies the pinned upstream's rules over the listed capabilities, and `resolveModel` calls it, so the assembly applies them at send and the model page shows them for the routing as edited; a payload rewrite applies when the request's own routing pins one. Routing is a model setting, so changing it changes which rules apply with no refresh. Built-ins, measured live: `openrouter-deepseek-together-no-prefill` (reply came back as reasoning with empty text), `openrouter-mimo-streamlake-no-prefill` (reply started over), `openrouter-mimo-xiaomi-no-prefill` (unreliable: went on in some runs, restarted in others); each sets prefill `none`, fixed, so Continue uses its nudge, and the prefill-dropped message names the rule. Not pinned, no rule applies and the page's Provider rules lists a note per failure for the upstreams the routing may reach ("Prefill fails on StreamLake; pin a provider to be sure."). The rules' "?" says some apply only when routing picks one provider. Pinned pricing is built: the route's own price from OpenRouter's endpoint list ("Pinned pricing" below).
  - `test/providerShims.test.ts` covers each, the prefix and catalog paths, route rules (pinning, unpinned notes, assembly) and F12 below.
  - `e2e/providerRules.spec.ts`: the model page's rules and locked Prefill (help, no internal words), and a pinned and an unpinned DeepSeek/MiMo model's route rules, with scoped layout audits at 1440/390 px in light and dark.
- **Catalogs by id** (`contextCatalog.ts`, registry `catalogs`): for a window neither the list nor the kind's catalog reports (OpenAI-compatible `/models`, a proxy in front of Claude, GPT or Gemini, DeepSeek's list, a model added by id). Ids are compared without router or resource prefixes (`anthropic/`, `models/`, `~`), Bedrock regions and vendors, variant tags (`:free`, `:batch`), Vertex versions (`@…`) and Bedrock's `-v1`, with `4.5` read as `4-5`; then without date and snapshot tags (`-20250514`, `-2024-08-06`, `-0613`, `-latest`), then without trailing segments down to two. Built-ins, asked newest registration first: `pi-ai` (pi-ai's first-party catalogs, then OpenRouter's) and below it `families`, a maintained table of current families by prefix with each family's smallest current window (Claude 200,000; GPT-5 400,000, its chat models 128,000; GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, o-series, gpt-oss; Gemini 1,048,576; DeepSeek 128,000; Grok, Mistral, Llama 3.1+, Kimi K2). A plugin's catalog goes before both. Matches give the window and, when also missing, the output limit; never prices. `refreshModels` and `AddUserModel` apply them, so a model refreshed before this landed shows its window as assumed until the next refresh. `test/contextWindow.test.ts` covers each kind's list, dated and routed ids, the family table and a plugin catalog.
- **Context-length errors** (`contextLimits.ts`, registry `contextLimits`): a failed request whose reason is `context_overflow`, `bad_request` or `unknown` and whose text one of the registered wordings recognizes (OpenAI/DeepSeek/OpenRouter/vLLM "maximum context length is N tokens", OpenAI's "configured limit of N tokens", Anthropic's "> N maximum" and "+ … > N", Gemini's "maximum number of tokens allowed (N)", llama.cpp, LiteLLM, xAI, Together, Mistral, and a generic "context window of N") becomes `context_overflow` with `contextLimit: N`. The reply's failed version records it with the model (`VersionError.contextLimit`), and the version's error offers **Save N as its context size** (a registered `message.failure-actions` slot entry), which calls `SaveLearnedContext`. It is never applied without that click.

**Audited environment defaults** (`providerEnvironment.ts`; pi-ai 1.0.3, openai 7.19.0, Anthropic 0.129.0, genai 2.21.0). Matching is case-insensitive, by whole family prefix so new SDK variables are covered:
- `OPENAI_`, `ANTHROPIC_`, `AZURE_OPENAI_`, `AWS_`, `GOOGLE_`, `GEMINI_`, `GCLOUD_`, `CLOUDSDK_`, `PI_`. These cover keys, organization/project, base URLs, cloud modes, profiles/credential files, headers, logging and cache retention, including `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` and lowercase Google auth aliases.
- pi-ai's other credential/OAuth families: `ANT_LING_`, `QWEN_`, `NVIDIA_`, `DEEPSEEK_`, `GROQ_`, `CEREBRAS_`, `XAI_`, `TYPESAFE_`, `RADIUS_`, `OPENROUTER_`, `AI_GATEWAY_`, `ZAI_`, `MISTRAL_`, `MINIMAX_`, `MOONSHOT_`, `HF_`, `FIREWORKS_`, `TOGETHER_`, `BASETEN_`, `OPENCODE_`, `KIMI_`, `META_`, `CLOUDFLARE_`, `XIAOMI_`, `COPILOT_`.
- Exact names, also lowercase: `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY`. Node can initialize its environment proxy before JavaScript runs (including `--use-env-proxy`); provider requests still use explicitly routed undici dispatchers, never that global dispatcher.

Explicit request keys and disabled credential discovery keep Anthropic out of ambient profile/config-file chains. Google is the key-authenticated Gemini REST backend, with no cloud credential chain. `providerInventory.test.ts` poisons every audited name, scrubs it, and compares real HTTP requests, captured mappings, stored captures and Version events against a clean baseline. It also checks future prefix members, server-setting overlaps, and Google in a fresh Node process with authenticated ambient/configured proxies. `startup.test.ts` checks both real entry points.

**Connections** (`Providers`):
- `createCredential`, `replaceCredentialKey` and `allowCredentialOrigin` (which checks the retyped key) handle credentials, and `setHeaders` and `setProxy` encrypt the other secrets (§2) before calling storage (§3.12).
- `createConnection` and `setKey` accept a key typed for a connection: it becomes a credential named after the connection, bound to its origin.
- **Before a request or a model-list fetch,** the connection's origin is checked against its credential, before the key is even decrypted. An origin the credential doesn't allow is `unusable`: "enter the key again to allow it", and nothing is sent.
- `refreshModels` fetches the upstream's list (`modelLists.ts`; OpenAI-style, Anthropic and Google formats, decoded with Schema) and merges each model over pi's catalog. What the list reports wins: OpenRouter's context length, pricing, modalities and parameters, vLLM's `max_model_len`.
- `testConnection` fetches the list and reports the route the request took.

**Streaming** (`stream`): a `Stream` of events:
- `attempt`
- `route`, e.g. "direct: no proxy configured"
- `text` and `thinking` deltas
- `retrying`
- `done`, with pi's final message, the counts and the cost

It fails with a typed `ProviderError`.

- **Error classes** (`errors.ts`):
  - `unusable`: no key, an unreadable secret, a route the API can't take
  - `auth`, `rate_limited`, `overloaded`, `context_overflow`, `refused`, `bad_request`, `network`, `aborted`, `unknown`

  They're classified from pi's final message, the HTTP status (or the status the SDK left at the start of the message), and pi's overflow and retry checks. A refusal carries Anthropic's category when given.
- **Retries happen only before the first token:** `rate_limited`, `overloaded` and `network`, with `Retry-After` honored or exponential backoff. After output, a failure is never retried; it ends the stream with `afterTokens`.
- **Rate limits:**
  - The status and `Retry-After` are read in our own `fetch` wrapper, because pi-ai's `onResponse` only fires for successful responses (the SDKs throw first).
  - A `Retry-After` pauses the whole connection. A request waiting on it emits a `paused` event, and the pause is checked after taking a concurrency permit, so queued requests honor it too.
  - A pause longer than the retry policy's maximum (60 s by default) fails fast as `rate_limited` instead of stalling silently.
- **Overflow:** a completed generation is never turned into a failure afterwards. An error counts as `context_overflow` only against a context window that some source reported, never against the default used for unknown models.
- **The stream always ends.** Typed failures go through its queue, and a defect becomes a `ProviderError` (`unknown`) instead of leaving the stream open. An invalid base URL is an `unusable` error.
- **A per-connection cap** (`max_concurrent`) queues requests.
- **Every attempt is a ledger row** (§3.12), opened and closed with `acquireUseRelease`, so it closes on every exit:
  - a stopped stream aborts the HTTP request and closes the row as `aborted`, wherever the interruption lands
  - a call that throws instead of reporting, and a defect, close it as `failed`
- **Secrets never appear in errors.** Provider errors, including ordinary response errors published as `Version` events and model-list response bodies, use the same request inventory as context capture and ledger metadata. It covers keys, effective connection/catalog headers, bare Bearer tokens, Basic base64/decoded credentials and their username/password components, both proxies, and endpoint URLs with userinfo and encoded/decoded path/query values. Routes have no sensitivity annotations, so all their nonempty path segments and query values are treated conservatively as secrets [P]. This can redact ordinary matching text; cache comparison still uses the unredacted digest. Redaction replaces matches once, longest first, so short secrets cannot rewrite a redaction marker. Metadata is then capped.
- **Google:** the REST adapter requires the controlled fetch. Direct, instance/custom proxy routing, forced-proxy policy, redirects, status observation and aborts use the same `Network` transport as the other providers. Neither startup `--use-env-proxy`/`NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` nor ambient proxy variables select its route.
- **A kind's wire API is fixed per connection.** If a plugin overrides a kind with another `api`, existing connections become `unusable` rather than silently speaking another API.
- **Forcing the proxy** (owner, 2026-10-11): with `forceProxy` in the network settings (admin), non-admins' connections ignore `direct` and custom proxies and use the instance proxy, and setting either is refused. The bypass list still applies; the admin sets it. Forcing needs a proxy (`setInstance` refuses it without one), and without a usable one, non-admins' requests are `unusable` rather than direct.

**Caller fields:** `options.payload` is set over the body pi-ai built, before the registered transforms run, for what the caller decides that pi-ai doesn't model: the context assembler's exact Chat Completions messages and per-provider samplers (§15). Objects merge key by key (Google's `config`); anything else replaces.

**Explicit cache breakpoints** (`providers/breakpoints.ts`, PROVIDERS §8), enabled only by the model’s `cacheBreakpoints: "explicit"` (and suppressed when request cache retention is `none`):
- **The caller names positions:** `options.breakpoints` lists indices into the request's `context.messages`, most important first.
- **The `onPayload` step finds their wire messages by alignment, not by index.** It walks the transcript and the payload in order and matches by role and text. pi-ai drops empty user messages, merges consecutive tool results and may append mid-conversation system messages, so positions shift.
- **The marker** goes on each message's last cacheable block (never a thinking block). It reuses pi-ai's own `cache_control` value, so TTLs match.
- **Limits:** on Messages nothing is added when pi placed no marker (caching off), and SDK/tool markers count against the four-marker ceiling. `cacheLayout.maxMarkers` can lower the ceiling.
- **pi-ai's own Messages markers stay:** the system prompt, the last tool, the last message.
- **Bedrock OpenAI-compatible APIs:** `cacheLayout.marker: "prompt_cache_breakpoint"` opts into a registered transform that adds `prompt_cache_breakpoint: {mode: "explicit"}` to `input_text` blocks on Responses (three explicit slots beside its automatic final checkpoint), or `text` parts on Chat Completions (the configured budget, conservatively four by default, reserving an explicit final checkpoint). Chat payloads retain assembly order; Responses aligns the converted transcript. String content becomes a one-part text array, and empty or non-text targets are skipped. The cumulative text estimate must reach `cacheLayout.minTokens` (default 1,024); tools/images can make this conservative. The request-level cache mode is preserved. Both the explicit gate and the encoding capability are required; API compatibility alone does not enable this wire extension. Direct OpenAI models normally stay `auto`. Responses remains capped at four total writes; an explicit-only Chat profile can declare a larger verified budget.
- **Scheduling identity:** `cacheIdentity.ts` recognizes both marker spellings, strips controls from prefix content hashing, and hashes the applicable control at the checkpoint. This keeps a moving later marker from invalidating an earlier prefix key.

**Default cache markers** (livefix, 2026-11-07; the live suite's F3, F4, F5, F8). With the model's breakpoints `auto` (the default), `providerRequest` still names the assembly's reusable endpoint, its last breakpoint (reference-harness's (c)), as `stable: { message, end }` (`end` is how many messages the assembly built; a tool loop's messages follow it). Callers pass it as `options.stable`, and registered transforms get it with the request's `cacheRetention` and `sessionId`; `RequestTarget` now carries the model key. `cacheRetention: "none"` drops it.
- **`anthropic-stable-endpoint`** (Messages, `auto` only): pi-ai marks the last message, which is the end-of-request instruction or a prefill, so the next request never read the history. The transform removes markers from the assembled messages after the endpoint and puts pi-ai's marker (and TTL) on the endpoint, within the four markers. A tool loop's last message keeps pi-ai's marker, since the loop's next request repeats it. The next turn reads what this one wrote, less the instruction.
- **`openrouter-cache-control`** (OpenRouter Chat Completions, `anthropic/claude*` and `google/gemini*`; `breakpoints.ts` `applyRouterCacheControl`): the assembler's messages replace pi-ai's, markers included, so this places OpenRouter's `cache_control` (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/prompt-caching) on text parts. Claude: the system message, then the explicit breakpoints or the endpoint (and a tool loop's last message), within four markers, `ttl: "1h"` for long retention. Gemini uses only the last marker: one `{type: "ephemeral"}` on the deepest target, in both layouts. A payload with a top-level `cache_control` (OpenRouter's automatic placement, from the model's payload fields) gets none. A plugin that places its own markers later replaces this transform by id.
- **`openai-prompt-cache-key`** (Chat Completions and Responses requests whose connection's provider settings have `promptCacheKey` on: the `openai` provider by default, `openai-compatible` only when the user turns it on, since a custom server may refuse the field): `prompt_cache_key` is the chat's id (clamped to 64 characters) whenever the payload has none; pi-ai sets it only for `api.openai.com`, and OpenAI routes cache reads by it.
- `test/providerCacheLayout.test.ts` checks each placement through the real SDK conversion and a mock provider.

**Usage and cost** (`usage.ts`):
- **Counts:** pi-ai's normalized usage (uncached input, cache reads, cache writes with Anthropic's 1-hour subset, output, reasoning) when the provider reported usage. The documented raw hit fields also normalize reads, including DeepSeek/Together fields that the compatible adapter can omit, Bedrock metadata, Google/Vertex usage and Fireworks' dedicated cached-token header. A reported header count survives tool-only, interrupted and failed output even when other counts remain unknown. Discounts alone never verify a hit.
  - The provider's raw usage object is kept with it. OpenRouter's reported cost and routed upstream are read from it.
  - Where the reported read and write together exceed the prompt (OpenRouter's Gemini explicit cache writes the prefix and reads it in the same request, and bills both), the uncached input is the prompt less the larger of the two, never negative.
  - Usage is estimated from the context and the output when the provider produced output without reporting usage, and unknown when nothing came back.
  - A stopped or failed request records as output at least the tokens of the text that arrived, marked `estimated` when that's more than reported. Anthropic's `message_start` reports only a placeholder output of 1.
- **Cost:** from the cost-formula registry (above). With the built-ins only: the provider's reported cost when there is one, otherwise the price table.
  - The formula uses per-million rates from the model's price (catalog or list), with the context-size tier on total input.
  - Long cache writes are priced at twice the input rate.
  - **Pinned pricing** (pinnedpricing; DESIGN liveapi2). When an OpenRouter model's routing pins one provider (`pinnedRoute`), its cost uses that provider's own price, not the model's headline price. The source is OpenRouter's public per-model endpoint list, `GET {base}/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints` (https://openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference), fetched with the models list's authentication and transport (`fetchEndpoints` in `providers/modelLists.ts`); `refreshEndpoints` gives up after 10 s (`ProvidersOptions.endpointsTimeoutMs`) and stores that as a failure. `data.endpoints[]` gives each endpoint's `tag` (the routing slug, `deepinfra/fp8`), `provider_name`, `context_length` and `pricing` as USD-per-token decimal strings (`prompt`, `completion`, `input_cache_read`, `input_cache_write`, a fractional `discount`, and `overrides`). It is stored as `ModelUpstream.endpoints` (`{ fetchedAt, error?, list }`, each endpoint's price per million tokens): the discount is applied, an override that depends only on the prompt length (`min_prompt_tokens`) becomes a `Price` tier and one that depends on the time of day is left out, and a price of -1 ("varies") is none. A model id with a variant (`:free`) has no list; the 1-hour cache-write price isn't kept. `SyncFetchedModels` keeps `endpoints` across a models refresh (`json_set` in the same transaction), and `SetModelEndpoints` (writer) replaces it.
  - **Fetching and the fallback.** The `RefreshModelEndpoints` RPC (`ProviderListApi`, a group of its own for the TS2589 limit; `Providers.refreshEndpoints`) fetches and stores the list for OpenRouter models, and returns other kinds' models unchanged. A failed or timed-out fetch is stored as `error`, keeping the list fetched before (empty if none), so the page says why and a route priced before keeps its price. The client (`useEndpointsFetch`, `features/connections/models.tsx`) asks once the routing, as saved or as being edited, pins one provider and the list is missing or stale (`endpointsStale`: a day, ten minutes after a failure; asked at most once per ten minutes per model in a session). Without the page: saving a model's routing (`EditModel`) starts the fetch in a detached fiber (`Providers.ensureEndpoints`, which fetches only for a pinned OpenRouter model whose list is missing or stale and not already being fetched, and never fails), and so does each OpenRouter stream when it starts, alongside the reply and outside any storage transaction. The reply's close prices with that fetch's list if it has arrived, else with the stored one (a stale list, or the general price when there is none); it never waits for the fetch, so the fetch can't delay or fail a reply. A pinned model never opened is thus costed at its provider's price from its first reply whenever the list arrives before the reply ends. A failed or timed-out fetch keeps the general price (or the earlier list's), with the page's note.
  - **Matching and use.** `matchEndpoints` (`@rp/shared/providers.ts`) takes the endpoints whose `tag` equals the pinned routing entry or lies beneath it (`deepinfra` matches `deepinfra/fp8` and `deepinfra/turbo`, `deepinfra/fp8` only that one), case-insensitively; else those whose tag's provider or `provider_name` matches once written as a slug (`Google Vertex` and `google-vertex`). Several matches are priced at the dearest, and the page says so. `routedPrice` returns the price and a `PriceSource` (`pinned`, or `fallback` for a failed or unlisted route, with the general price); `resolveModel` sets `EffectiveModel.price` and `priceSource` from it, so `buildPiModel` and every `costOf` call (`modelPrice(model)` in `Providers.ts`) use it, and a routing edit changes the price with no refresh. A cost the provider reports (`reported`) still wins. The backfill estimate's cache-write rate (`lcmEnableReads.ts`) still reads the headline price.
  - **On the model page**, no new layout: the model's row shows the pinned provider's price with its name in brackets, and the Provider rules section lists a note ("Priced as Together." or "Fireworks's own price couldn't be fetched, so the model's usual price applies."), each with a short hover explanation.
  - **Tests:** `test/pinnedPricing.test.ts` (matching by slug case, base and full slugs, names; dearest of several; fallbacks; staleness; the documented response parsed with a mock server, authentication, discount, tiers, "varies"; a failed fetch stored; variant ids and other kinds not asked; a refresh keeping the list) and `providerStream.test.ts` (a pinned model's reply costed at its provider's price with no page opened, and at the general price after a failed fetch), `e2e/pinnedPricing.spec.ts` (the row and the notes, the hovers, the layout audit at 1440 and 390 px in light and dark, against a fake provider serving the documented shape). The isolation matrix probes `RefreshModelEndpoints`.
  - **User formulas (U12, 2026-10-28):** `@rp/shared/costFormulas.ts`, `providers/userCosts.ts`. The registered `user-pricing` contribution reads an owner-scoped snapshot supplied to each stream (shared across retries) and estimate. It is replaceable/disableable through the existing cost registry. User-scoped `settings`, key `cost`, stores each user's revision and rules; `GetCostSettings` and `SetCostSettings` run in reader/writer workers. Writes compare the expected revision, check connection ownership, and replace the rules in one transaction; foreign connections are `NotFound`. Each cost records `user:<rule-id>:<settings-revision>`; later changes or removal leave historical ledger costs untouched.
  - A rule names an exact model, optional provider kind, connection and exact reported upstream, a display-only currency label, and five non-negative per-million rates (uncached input, cache read, short cache write, long cache write and output including reasoning). Context tiers replace all rates for the whole request above their threshold, based on total input including cache reads and writes. A connection condition wins over kind/upstream-only conditions, then upstream, then kind, with the last rule breaking ties. Unmatched requests keep reported/catalog pricing. Unknown counts remain unknown. Validation limits rules to 100, tiers to 16 distinct non-negative integer thresholds, identifiers/names to 160 characters, labels to 16 and finite rates to 1e9. These declarative weighted sums never evaluate code.
  - **Known prices and their order (prices1, 2026-11-16; spec/PRICES.md §3, §4, §5.1, §6).**
    - **Sources.** `providers/priceSources.ts` gives every formula a request's `PriceSources` (`registry.ts`): `endpoint` (the model's `upstream.priceFeed`, only while the connection's `priceEndpoint` setting is on; a rate the server leaves unknown comes from the next source), `list` (the model list's price when `upstream.priceFrom` is `list`, or a pinned OpenRouter route's endpoint-list price) and `builtin`. `price` is still passed as the first known of them, and a caller passing no `sources` gets the old single `builtin` formula over `price`.
    - **The order** (owner, DESIGN §9), newest registration first: a user rule naming this connection; the reported charge; the price endpoint; the list; an account-wide or per-type user rule (it never overrides a connection's own fetched prices); the built-in table. `user-pricing` and `user-pricing-general` are the same rule matcher over the two scopes. Admission bounds follow the same order (`reported` excluded as before).
    - **Ledger ids:** `builtin:pi-ai@<version>+<supplement hash>` (`BUILTIN_PRICE_VERSION`), `list:<model list fetched at>` or `list:endpoints:<endpoint list fetched at>`, `endpoint:<price list fetched at>`, and unchanged `reported` and `user:<rule>:<revision>`. The reply's cost details name the source in user terms. No column was added.
    - **The built-in table** (`providers/prices/`): pi-ai's catalog plus our supplement, one data file per provider (`anthropic`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `openai`, `google`, `deepseek`), each entry naming its official pricing page and the date it was checked. A supplement entry replaces pi-ai's price for its (pi provider, model) whole. Entries may carry announced dated changes and DeepSeek's off-peak hours (weekday 01–04 and 06–10 UTC are peak; Chinese holidays aren't modelled). Bedrock IDs are priced by inference profile (`global.` as listed, geo profiles and bare IDs at the in-region 1.1x, `us-gov.` not priced); Vertex at 1.1x when the connection's `region` isn't `global`. The supplement is applied both at refresh (`withCatalog`, which records `priceFrom`) and at cost time, so a corrected table prices the next request without a refresh. Models stored before `priceFrom` count as built-in.
    - **`Price`** gained `cacheWriteLong` (absent: 2x input, as before), `perRequest` and `currency`; tiers gained `cacheWriteLong`. `CostRule` gained an optional `perRequest`.
    - **The price endpoint client** (`providers/priceEndpoint.ts`): on Refresh models for a connection whose `providerSettings.priceEndpoint` is true, `GET {base}/v1/prices` (a trailing `/v1` dropped from the base) with the model list's credentials and the connection's headers through `Network.fetchFor`. A valid body stores each listed model's feed (`SetModelPriceFeeds`, writer; null removes a model the list no longer names); 404/405/501, 401/403, timeouts and invalid bodies are logged and leave the last feeds. `SyncFetchedModels` keeps `priceFeed` (and `endpoints`) across refreshes. The parser accepts the base fields alone, reads the extension fields (`currency`, `valid_until`, `cache_read`, `cache_write` as a number or by TTL, `per_request`, `tiers`), and treats absent, null, negative, non-finite or above-1e9 rates as unknown, never zero. Not built: the hourly timer, `ETag`/`304`, the in-memory probe state, route pricing, and the connection-form opt-in and model-page source line (the setting exists in the schema only).
    - **Tests:** `prices.test.ts` (the main-models coverage list per provider, Bedrock profiles and GovCloud, Vertex regions, dated changes, off-peak hours, prototype ids, long writes, tiers and per-request charges, the full precedence order and ledger ids, sources of stored models, refresh marking) and `priceEndpoint.test.ts` (the parser; no request to `/v1/prices` without the opt-in; one request per refresh with it, priced as `endpoint:<t>`).
  - **Admission:** registry entries can claim a reservation even without a point estimate (`reserves`); upstream-only overrides therefore cannot fall through to cheaper catalog bounds. The user contribution's upper bound covers every possible route before dispatch, every reachable tier (including decreasing rates), every cache partition and maximum output. Without a generic override it also covers catalog fallback. Unknown fallback prices or mixed currency labels return no bound, holding money-capped backfill before dispatch. Estimates without an upstream use the generic matching rule when no route can override it; otherwise the registered estimator quotes the conservative route bound, or unknown when currencies differ or fallback prices are missing. They do not guess a routed upstream.
  - **Editor:** the registered Settings → Costs route (`features/costs.tsx`, registered from `features/index.ts`) adds/removes formulas and tiers, edits all conditions/rates and labels, and saves explicitly. Non-secret edits use the existing server user-draft store and browser recovery copies, with field undo and recovered texts. Stale settings refuse the save and offer an explicit choice to carry the draft onto the saved revision; discard returns to saved pricing. Formula names wrap within the editor, with the remove action on its own row on phones, so even a maximum-length unbroken name keeps controls reachable. No past-row recompute action is implemented.
  - **Tests:** `userCosts.test.ts` exercises weights, exact matches, specificity, tier boundaries, unknown counts, validation, and conservative bounds; `providerStream.test.ts` checks worker persistence, an in-flight rule change, estimates and immutable historical costs through the real adapter; `userCostBackfill.test.ts` checks custom-currency estimates and model/upstream admission holds before the provider sees a request. The isolation matrix probes both new RPCs in both directions, including a foreign connection. `e2e/costs.spec.ts` covers explicit save, reload, drafts, tier editing and removal at 1440/390 in light/dark, including viewport bounds for the remove action beside a maximum-length unbroken name. Screenshots honor `SCREENSHOT_DIR`.

**Tested** (`test/providerStream.test.ts`) against a scripted provider speaking the real wire formats (`test/support/mockProvider.ts`):
- OpenRouter streaming with reported cost and upstream, and the built-in cost
- a 429 retried with each attempt recorded
- a mid-stream failure kept and not retried, a 401 not retried
- stopping, a missing key, Google through the configured proxy (including a failed proxy)
- Anthropic's cache split and catalog pricing
- explicit breakpoints through pi-ai's real Anthropic conversion
- DeepSeek's dialect
- a keyless local server

**Client RPCs** (`api/providers.ts`, contract in `@rp/shared/api.ts`):
- **Connections:** `ListConnections`, `CreateConnection` (with an existing credential or a typed key), `UpdateConnection`, `SetConnectionKey`, `SetConnectionCredential`, `SetConnectionHeaders`, `SetConnectionProxy`, `DeleteConnection`, `TestConnection`.
- **Credentials:** `ListCredentials`, `CreateCredential`, `RenameCredential`, `ReplaceCredentialKey`, `AllowCredentialHost` (the key typed again), `DeleteCredential`.
- **Models:** `RefreshModels`, `ListModels`, `AddUserModel`, `EditModel`, `SaveLearnedContext` (null forgets it), `SetModelHidden`.
- **A new connection's models** (`features/connections/defaultModel.tsx`, the `default-model` entry of `connection.sections`, first on the page): the New connection form marks the created connection fresh (`freshConnections`), and its page then runs `RefreshModels` once; when the account has no default model, the first listed model becomes it (`ChangeGenerationDefaults`). The entry says "Found N models." and, whenever the account's default model is on this connection, "Using <model> for new chats · Change" (Change: Settings → Chats); a failed fetch shows the provider's error there. The model list shows a model's id only where it differs from its display name. The form's name is optional: left empty, the connection is named after the typed Base URL's host, else the provider kind, as its placeholder shows. The form's key step is one **API key** field (for kinds with `keyOptional` its description says it may be left empty, which sends none), with **Use a saved key instead** when saved keys exist; there is no No key option. `e2e/firstRun.spec.ts`, `e2e/models.spec.ts`.
- **Network and usage:** `GetNetworkSettings`/`SetNetworkSettings` (admins only, otherwise `Forbidden`), and `ListLlmRequests`.
- **Errors keep their tags** (`NotFound`, `StaleWrite`, `ModelKeyTaken`, `ProviderError`, `Forbidden`, from `@rp/shared/errors.ts`). Storage and worker failures are logged on the server and reach the client only as `ServerError`, including from the provider operations and network settings.
- `test/rpc.test.ts` checks over a real WebSocket that a key never comes back out. Cross-user access is checked by the isolation matrix (§4).
- **At startup,** requests a previous process left `running` are marked `interrupted`.

**Signed thinking** (thinkhide1; reviewed 2026-11-14; `providers/thinkingBinding.ts`). The final provider hook checks the serialized request after transforms, shims, loading and image limits. Each successful signed assistant response records SHA-256 prefix digests, connection/model identity and a digest of transport identity (address, credentials, headers and provider settings). The record and the block occupy the same transcript JSON, saved together by `SaveRolloutTranscript`; no separate write can publish an unbound block. Unknown/legacy unrecorded blocks are dropped. Checking hashes the request prefix once and copies the running hash for each block. Intra-message checks additionally examine the blocks preceding that signature; no history text is retained solely for the guard. Anthropic checks system, ordered tools and prior non-thinking messages, plus text/tool blocks preceding a signed block inside its own assistant message. JSON data ordering, string-versus-block shape, text whitespace and array order stay significant. Only actual API cache-marker positions are ignored: identically named tool-argument/schema fields still count. Thinking alone is not part of a later block's prefix (the live measurements take precedence over older generic preservation guidance). At the first mismatch that block and later blocks are removed; earlier ones, text, calls and results stay. Empty thinking-only messages are removed. Unchanged requests retain their original payload object and wire bytes.

The replaceable `thinkingBindings` registry covers Anthropic Messages (including cloud transports/proxies), Claude reasoning details on Chat Completions (OpenRouter and proxies) and Responses encrypted reasoning items. Responses includes instructions, ordered tools, reasoning configuration and output format in its head, and records per-item offsets using pi-ai's Responses serializer. Google function-call thought signatures have a separate required positional contract and are preserved; they are not treated as Anthropic prefix-bound blocks. Sources: [Anthropic preserved thinking](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking), [OpenAI preserved reasoning](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/preserved-reasoning), [Google signatures](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/generate-content/thought-signatures).

Only the measured pre-output HTTP 400 containing both the invalid-thinking-signature sentence and the different-conversation sentence permits one retry without signed reasoning. Other signature errors, status codes and post-output errors do not. The retry remains inside one provider request stream: no new reply version or tool execution is started; each HTTP attempt has its own ledger row. A short `RequestNotice` reaches the chat's existing notice callback, and the request inspector records why thinking was omitted. There is no retry that restores rejected blocks. A manual-thinking request whose blocks must be dropped disables thinking before dispatch, following the documented graceful handling of an edited tool turn. Hiding reasoning for a still-open manual-thinking tool turn is deferred until it ends; adaptive turns can omit it immediately on Resume.

The Anthropic binding registers `finalRequest: { tool_choice: { type: "none" } }`: at the cap the loop keeps its declarations and deferred-tool load points unchanged and forbids calls. The measured `live-thinking2.md` confirms acceptance, text answers and full cache reuse. The same replaceable binding owns family defaults and manual-turn hiding deferral. The core session consumes this registered policy; other providers retain their existing tool-removal cap behavior (Responses consequently drops bound reasoning when declarations change). Native loading, dispatcher and every-tool offers remain frozen throughout ordinary runs. Tests cover prefix edits, signed and redacted blocks, intra-message edits, model/transport changes, compaction projections, loading, real agent/Resume paths, cap bytes and fallback accounting. No live provider calls are made by these tests.

## 7. Deployment

**Client build identity** (macrohighlight, 2026-11-02): Vite embeds a new UUID for each production build as `import.meta.env.VITE_BUILD_ID` and emits the same identity in `dist/build-id.json`. `/healthz` retains its `ok` body and adds `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Client-Build`, read from the configured client directory on each request so a replaced bundle is visible without restarting the server. A missing stamp leaves liveness usable without the header. Vite development uses `development` and proxies `/healthz`; its notice checks are disabled. This stamp identifies the client bundle independently of the database worker source hash (§3.6).

`Dockerfile`: a multi-stage build on `node:24.22.1-trixie-slim`.
- The client and database workers are built in one stage. The final image holds only what runs: production dependencies, the root `package.json` and lockfile (the bundles' stamp includes it), the shared and server packages' `package.json` and `src`, the client build, worker bundles, and client source for authenticated editable copies (§17). No tests or scripts.
- `.dockerignore` keeps data directories, databases (`*.db*`, `*.sqlite*`), `secret.key`, `instance.lock` and `.env` files out of the build context at any depth (`**/`). Verified with throwaway builds: files planted in `packages/server/data/` (including `.sqlite`), `packages/shared/` (`.db-wal`, `.sqlite3`) and `packages/server/.env` didn't reach the image.
- It runs as the `node` user with `DATA_DIR=/data` as a volume, `HOST=0.0.0.0`, and a health check on `/healthz`.
- **It doesn't start without exposure settings** (§4), since `HOST=0.0.0.0` is beyond loopback; CI checks this. Connections from the host arrive from the bridge gateway (e.g. `172.17.0.1`).
  - Behind a reverse proxy: `AUTH_MODE=proxy`, `TRUSTED_PROXIES` set to the proxy container's name on the shared network, not its address, which changes when the container restarts, and `PUBLIC_ORIGINS` set to the public URL.
  - Built-in login: set `ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE` (a Docker secret). The server then starts with the admin protected, and no browser needs to reach loopback.
  - Single user without a password: publish on loopback only (`-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`) and set `ALLOWED_IPS` to the gateway.
  - Publishing beyond loopback (`-p 8080:8080`) makes the gateway allowlist unsafe: where Docker doesn't pass the client's address through (rootless Docker's default port driver, `docker-proxy` for IPv6 clients), outside clients also appear to come from it.
  - **The health check** fetches `127.0.0.1` on `PORT` inside the container. In proxy mode with `TRUSTED_PROXIES` set, add `127.0.0.1` to the list, or the container reports unhealthy. Inside a container, loopback is only the container's own processes, which can read `/data` and the server secret anyway.
- The P5 image is 605,307,296 bytes unpacked (577.27 MiB), 4,331,524 bytes larger than P4 (600,975,772 bytes); its shipped client source directory is 4,256,419 bytes. It installs every workspace's production dependencies. Memory at idle is about 188 MB.

### ST differential harness

`npm run test:st` (`packages/server/test/st/`) checks the compatibility contract (DESIGN §1.2) against a stock SillyTavern. It's opt-in, outside `npm run check` and CI: it needs Docker, and a run takes about 4 minutes on the loaded host.
- **ST** is the official image at 1.19.0, pinned by digest (`container.ts`). It runs on the host network, listening on 127.0.0.1 at a random port, in whitelist mode with loopback only, as the calling user. Its config and data directories are fresh, under a temporary directory (`ST_DIFF_TMPDIR`, kept with `ST_DIFF_KEEP=1`). It never sees an existing ST install.
- **Cleanup:** the container and the directory go on any exit, signals included. The container's removal is registered before `docker run`. A run killed outright (`SIGKILL`) leaves both behind. The next run removes such a container only if it matches all of: a name starting `rp-st-diff-` and our label (`docker ps -a --filter name=^rp-st-diff- --filter label=rp-harness.st-diff.owner`, checked again in code), a label value naming this PID namespace, and an owner process that's gone. The directory stays until removed by hand. Nothing else is ever removed.
- **The mock endpoint** (`mock.ts`) is an OpenAI-compatible server on loopback. It records every request and answers with a fixed reply, streamed or not, so ST completes the turn.
- **Fixtures** (`fixtures.ts`) are synthetic. The card goes through our card importer and PNG exporter, and the lorebook through our World Info importer and exporter, so ST parsing them checks those too. The presets are the parser tests' fixtures, and `rewrite` (regex scripts with each flag, for the rewrite comparison). They're loaded through ST's HTTP API from a page, as its UI imports files. `settings.json` is written directly: ST's fresh-install settings with the custom source pointed at the mock, auto-connect, the fixture persona, and the presets' regex allowed. `bind_preset_to_connection` is off, so a preset can't switch the connection (connection data is out of scope).
- **ST builds prompts in the browser**, so the harness drives its UI with Playwright (`st.ts`). A capture opens a fresh page, selects the preset through ST's preset manager, opens the character's chat, and sends a message from the composer. It returns the body the mock received. Capture pages answer ST's write endpoints themselves, so every capture starts from the same files.
- **Macros run in ST's own engine** through `SillyTavern.getContext().substituteParams(text, { name1Override, name2Override })`, the entry point its prompt building uses. With an options object it runs the new `MacroEngine` when `experimental_macro_engine` is on, as it is in a fresh 1.19 install. The chat is open, the clock is fixed, the page runs in UTC, the variables are set per vector, and `Math.random` is reseeded per vector for `{{roll}}`. `{{random}}` can't be compared: ST draws it from an entropy-seeded generator.
- **Comparisons** (`comparisons.ts`), each a section of the report, with every difference as a JSON path and both values:
  - **The exported card, lorebook and chat:** with the baseline settings, ST's request carries their text, macros expanded.
  - **Macros:** each vector (`macroVectors.ts`) through ST and through our engine (`ourMacros.ts`, §10), comparing the output and the variables after it. Ours gets the context ST's page has: the vector's names and variables, the fixture card and chat, ST's model and token settings, the clock. The vectors are the engine's own tests (`packages/shared/test/macros/`) where ST can evaluate them, plus a few of the harness's. Left out: `{{random}}` (entropy) and `{{pick}}` (seeded differently, §10), and anything about origins, freezing or limits. A vector whose difference §10 documents names the line, and its differences are listed apart without failing the run.
  - **Preset round trips:** each preset file, and its import and export through our format, loaded into ST for the same chat. The two requests must be identical.
    - ST applies only the settings a preset has, so a dropped setting would pass whenever the file's value is ST's default. So the file is loaded over the baseline (a fresh install's settings), and the round trip over a poison preset. In the poison preset, every setting ST applies differs from the baseline, taken from ST's own list (`settingsToUpdate`). Our importer fills a missing field with ST's default, as a fresh ST does, so the requests match only if the round trip carries every setting.
    - The file is captured twice, so an unstable capture isn't mistaken for a lossy round trip.
    - A preset whose request equals the baseline's is flagged as not applied.
  - **The context assembler** (`assembly.ts`, §15): for each of two gate cards, each preset and each generation type, the request ST sends against the one we build for the settings ST had in force (read from the page, through our preset importer), compared as JSON. ST's other generation types are started through `getContext().generate`, and its post-processing, a connection setting, is set on the page before sending.
  - **Regex scripts on text as it's written** (`rewrites.ts`, §12 "Rewrites"): synthetic replies, messages, edits and reasoning through the `rewrite` fixture preset's scripts (a chain-of-thought strip on replies, ellipses in the user's messages on edits too, a prompt-only one that mustn't touch stored text, a reasoning one with a macro), allowed. ST's side is `getRegexedString` from `extensions/regex/engine.js` in a page with the preset selected and the chat open (`evaluateRegex`), which is what ST stores; ours is the assembler's `rewrite`. First result (2026-10-31): all eight the same; with our edit flag dropped on purpose, the edit case is reported.
- `ST_DIFF_ONLY=assembly` (comma-separated: `fixtures`, `macros`, `presets`, `rewrites`, `assembly`) runs only those comparisons.
- **First results (2026-10-12):** the exported card, lorebook and chat all reach ST's request. The three preset fixtures (`default`, `full`, `legacy`) round-trip with identical requests, over the poison preset too. Checked against deliberate breakage, all reported: a card bound to a missing lorebook, a round trip with one sampler changed and a space added to one prompt, and a round trip without `temperature`, which only the poison preset reveals for `default`. All 318 macro vectors without a documented deviation match ST. The exit status is 1 when a difference isn't expected.

## 8. Import formats: cards and lorebooks

**Documents** (`@rp/shared/docs/`, Effect Schema). Each has a `schema_version`.
- **Card names:** standard `name` is the display name; `nickname` is the name sent to the model, falling back to `name` when absent or empty; `character_version` is the subtitle. All three travel with revisions and exported files.
- **Cards** (`card.ts`): the union of Character Card V2 and V3, in the specs' field names. Card modules are card notes (DESIGN §5.0): `modules[]` stays optional in the schema so older revisions decode, and only the 0049 migration reads it (§14.4).
  - `extensions` is the card's `data.extensions`, verbatim, so `extensions.<plugin-id>` survives (PLUGINS §3.3), except `regex_scripts`: ST's scoped regex scripts become the card's `regex[]`, as data, through the preset importer's `readRegex` (same shape, ids and depth rules as §9). The export writes them back to `extensions.regex_scripts` (`regexToSt`). `regex_approved` is the user's allowance, as on a preset: the importer never sets it, a file's own field is never read, export never writes it, and only `SetRegexApproval` changes it (§14.3).
  - Keys the specs don't define are kept verbatim too: `unknown_fields` for those in `data`, `unknown_root_fields` for the top level. They can't go in `extensions`: an export would then write them to a different place, or a plugin's namespace could collide with them.
- **Lorebooks** (`lorebook.ts`): ST's World Info entry fields in snake_case, the same document for standalone lorebooks and a card's `character_book`. ST's numeric enums are named (`position: "at_depth"`, `role: "system"`, `selective_logic: "and_any"`). Each entry has a unique safe-integer `uid`, so the three-way merge (§3.9) matches entries by it. On import, usable ids are kept (the first wins), and every other entry, missing, invalid or duplicate, gets a number after the largest, so renumbering never takes an id another entry has. A card book id that isn't a whole number is kept in `unknown_fields` and written back on export. Our own fields are `decision_hint` and `placement_override`.

**Parsers** (`packages/server/src/formats/`) are pure functions over bytes: no database, no files. Each returns an `Effect` that fails with `FormatError` when the file can't be imported at all. Everything recoverable becomes an issue in the `ImportReport` (`@rp/shared/importReport.ts`) instead, so one bad field never costs the whole file.
- **Lenient fields** (`fields.ts`). A missing or null field takes its default quietly, as in ST. A field of the wrong type takes its default too, and the report names its path. Whole numbers must be safe integers (up to 2^53), as `Schema.Int` requires; file values are only converted to text when they are text or numbers, since an object's `toString` can throw.
- **Bounded reports** (`ReportBuilder`, `@rp/shared/importReport.ts`). At most 200 issues per file, then one `report.truncated` issue with the count. Paths keep 16 segments; file text quoted in a message or path is cut to 40 characters (`shownText`), and lists of file-supplied names to the first 10 plus a count (`shownList`). The preset importer (§9) uses the same builder.

**Card import** (`importCard`, `cardImport.ts`, `card.ts`). The format comes from the bytes, never the file name.
- **JSON:** detection follows ST: any `spec` with a `data` object is V2 or V3 (an unknown spec is read as V3, with a warning), otherwise a `name` means V1. V1 is mapped as ST maps it (its placeholder creator note dropped, comma-separated tags split).
- **ST's top-level copies** of V1 fields and its local state (`chat`, `create_date`, `fav`, `avatar`) aren't kept; other top-level keys are.
- **The embedded `character_book`** is mapped as ST's `convertCharacterBook` does: ST's World Info fields come out of each entry's `extensions` into the entry, with its defaults; whatever else is in `extensions` stays. One deliberate difference: the spec's own `case_sensitive` is the fallback when the extension has none (ST ignores it). An entry without `enabled` is disabled, as in ST, with a warning.
- **Card notes** an export carried stay in `extensions.rp_harness` for the card importer (`importers.ts` `exportedNotes`), which makes each of `notes` (and an older export's `modules`) a card note, keeping its id as `module_id` so a re-import finds it. An invalid entry is dropped and reported; an invalid placement becomes "with the definitions"; `agent_editable` is never read.
- **PNG** (`png.ts`): the card is base64 JSON in a `tEXt` chunk. As in ST (`src/character-card-parser.js`), `ccv3` wins over `chara`, keywords match in any case, and a bad CRC or a missing IEND rejects the file. The avatar returned is the PNG without its card chunks. V3's `chara-ext-asset_` chunks are skipped with a note (the spec discourages them; ST ignores them).
- **CHARX** (`zip.ts`, our own reader of the central directory; stored and deflated entries only): `card.json` at the root, or else, as in ST, the first entry whose name ends in `card.json`. It must be V2 or V3. Assets come from `embeded://`, `embedded://` and `__asset:` URIs, normalized as ST normalizes them. The avatar is the main icon, as ST picks it. Only ST's image formats are extracted; other assets (audio, Risu modules and scripts) and unreferenced files are reported and skipped. Each returned file keeps the URI the card's `assets` use for it.

**Card export** (`cardExport.ts`) flattens a card document to a standard card.
- **V2 and V3 carry the same `data`,** V3's fields included, as ST's two PNG chunks do. V2 also has the V1 fields at the top level, for V1 readers. Fields the specs don't define go back where they came from, written first, so they never override a defined field.
- **The embedded lorebook** is written as ST's `convertWorldInfoToCharacterBook` writes it, our own entry fields in `extensions.rp_harness`. One difference: `use_regex` is false unless the entry says otherwise. ST writes true, but its keys are plain text, which a V3 reader would take as patterns. An imported `true` is kept, though it's usually ST's boilerplate: ST never reads the field. The keyword matcher ignores `use_regex` and recognizes ST slash syntax (DESIGN §1.3).
- **Card notes** (`importer/exporters.ts` `withNotes`): ST's Character's Note to `depth_prompt` as before (the first note when it is exportable, in chat and on in every chat; one that is not goes with the others, so an import does not switch it on everywhere), and every other exportable card note into `extensions.rp_harness.notes` (id, title, content, placement, `scan_lore`, `on_by_default`; a linked one as its shared note's text, which `ExportSource` puts in it). Private notes never leave. Conditions naming library ids stay behind; the self-referring `own_turn` condition, self card-field replacements (including `own_position`) and the portable `move_group` travel in the extension. A conditioned or replacing note never becomes ST’s `depth_prompt`: ST receives the original card fields.
- **PNG:** existing card chunks are removed, then `chara` (V2) and `ccv3` (V3) go in before IEND, as ST writes them. The image must be a valid PNG.
- **CHARX:** `card.json` (V3), the avatar as the main icon (at its own path if it came from a CHARX, otherwise `assets/icon/images/main.<ext>`), and each embedded asset whose file is given. An embedded asset without a file, with a path outside the archive's folder, or with a name already taken (`card.json`, the avatar's, another asset's) is left out of the card, so our own import takes every export back.
- **Round trips are lossless:** an exported card imports back to the same document, in every format, and keeps every field of the file it came from (`test/formats/cardExport.test.ts`). The exceptions are ST's top-level copies and local state, and private modules.

**Lorebooks** (`worldInfo.ts`, `lorebook.ts`).
- **ST World Info files** import with `importLorebook` and export with `exportLorebook`. A file must have `entries` (an object keyed by uid, or a list), as ST's import requires. Missing fields take the defaults of ST's `newWorldInfoEntryDefinition`. Entry `extensions` are kept verbatim, as ST keeps them. The book is named after the file unless it names itself. ST's `originalData`, a copy of the card book a World Info file was made from that goes stale with every edit, is dropped with a note.
- **A card's `character_book` and World Info** convert through the same document, following ST's two conversions (`convertCharacterBook`, `convertWorldInfoToCharacterBook`). What one format has no place for is lost going to the other, as in ST: a card book's settings (description, scan depth, token budget, recursive scanning) and its entries' `name`, `priority` and `use_regex` don't go into World Info, and World Info's character filter has no standard card-book field; resolved filters round-trip in our extension namespace.
- **Our own entry fields** (`decision_hint`, `placement_override`) are written to `extensions.rp_harness` in both formats and read back from there.
- Round trips are lossless within each format: an export keeps every field of the file it came from (except `originalData`) and imports back to the same document.
- Not supported: other lorebook formats ST converts (NovelAI, Agnai, RisuAI), and V3's standalone `lorebook_v3`.

**Hardening** (`safety.ts`). These parse untrusted files, so every input is capped (`defaultLimits`), and each cap has a test with a crafted file that fails when the check is removed.

| Cap | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| File size | 64 MiB | Bounds memory and work for everything below |
| Card JSON | 8 MiB | About 2M tokens of text, more than any model's context holds: a bigger card couldn't be used. Applies to a JSON file, a PNG's card chunk once decoded, and a CHARX's `card.json` |
| World Info JSON | 32 MiB | Lorebooks are scanned, not sent whole, so they can outgrow a context: a full lorebook with 2 KB of content per entry fits. The value cap, not this one, bounds the parse work |
| JSON nesting | 64 levels | Real cards nest about 8 deep. Counted in the bytes before parsing, which also bounds the recursive walk after it |
| JSON objects and lists | 250,000 | Counted before parsing: 10M empty objects in 32 MB cost `JSON.parse` 1.1 GB. A full lorebook has about 60,000 |
| JSON values and keys | 1,200,000 | Counted before parsing (every comma and colon): parsing costs about 1 µs each, and a 30 MiB list of zeros took 4 s and 1.1 GB without it. ST writes about 110 per entry, so a full lorebook has 1.1M |
| Prototype keys | 100 | Each is dropped with a warning; more make the file hostile |
| Lorebook entries | 10,000 | An assumption to revisit with real files: a lorebook of a few thousand entries is already exceptional. 20,000 full ST entries would need 2.2M values, about 2 s of parsing |
| PNG chunks | 16,384 | Bounds the chunk walk |
| PNG chunk size | 32 MiB | Checked against the declared length before anything is read |
| Zip entries | 1,024 | Bounds the directory walk |
| Zip entry, uncompressed | 64 MiB | Checked against the declared size before inflating |
| Zip total, uncompressed | 128 MiB | Over every entry extracted from one archive |
| Compression ratio | 100 | For entries over 1 MiB; a zip bomb's is in the thousands |

- **Inflating stops at the declared size** (`maxOutputLength`), so a header that understates an entry can't make the parser allocate more than the caps allow (`zip.bomb`). Sizes and CRCs are checked after.
- **Zip paths** must stay inside the archive: no `..` segment, leading `/`, backslash, drive letter or NUL. One bad path, duplicate name or encrypted entry rejects the whole archive, so an importer that later writes files by these names can't be pointed elsewhere.
- **Prototype keys** (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) are dropped right after `JSON.parse`, with a warning. `JSON.parse` makes them plain own keys, but a later assignment, `Object.assign` or merge can turn one into a prototype change.
- **Nothing in a file is executed or rendered.** Scripts in a card (RisuAI's modules, Lua assets) are skipped, never stored.

**Known limits:**
- **The importer must run the parsers off the main thread.** They're synchronous: measured on this host under load (2026-10-11, load average 25), the worst file within the caps (one object of 595,000 keys) took 850 ms and 80 MB of heap, a list of 1.19M short strings 460 ms, and a full lorebook (10,000 entries with every ST field and 2 KB of content, 29 MiB) 480 ms. The walk after parsing steps through lists by index and skips scalars, and unknown fields and extensions are kept by deleting the known keys from the parsed objects instead of copying them. On the main thread that would stall every live stream (§3.1).
- The registered card and lorebook importers store documents, avatars/assets and reports through the format workers and import workflow (§11; PLUGINS §8).

---

## 9. Import formats: presets

ST chat-completion presets (DESIGN §1.2). Pure functions with no database access; the importer that writes into the library comes later.

**The document** (`@rp/shared/docs/preset.ts`, `PresetDoc`, `schema_version` 1) is the prompt portion of ST's chat-completion preset, normalized:
- `prompts[]`, keyed by `identifier`, with ST's per-prompt fields: role, content, `system_prompt`, `marker`, in-chat injection (`injection_position` `absolute`, at `injection_depth`, by `injection_order`), `injection_trigger` and `forbid_overrides`.
- `order[]`: one prompt order with enabled flags (DATA-MODEL §16.3). Every entry names a prompt; the end-of-request texts are never in it (below). Import appends prompts outside the ST order, off, and reports their names; the markers ST still sends when its order leaves them out (world info before and after, description, personality, scenario, persona description) are appended on instead, in ST's order, so the request is unchanged. `presetOrder.ts` presents older revisions the same way without rewriting them. The `newestMessage` marker defaults to immediately after `chatHistory`; export preserves its position for reimport.
- `utility_prompts{}`: text used in specific situations. Model settings are separate (below).
- `reply_sections`: tagged sections at the start of a reply (§15 "Reply sections"): `{ enabled, pairs: [{ open, close, case_sensitive?, regex? }], send_back }`, tags literal text unless `regex` (owner, 2026-11-02). Absent means `DEFAULT_REPLY_SECTIONS` (on, literal `<think>` / `</think>` and `<thinking>` / `</thinking>`, case-insensitive, send_back 0), so new and built-in presets parse. ST keeps its reasoning formatting in `power_user.reasoning`, outside presets: a folder import copies it into each imported preset beside the switches below (auto_parse → enabled; prefix/suffix → one literal, case-sensitive pair, as written (never `regex`: ST has none there); add_to_prompts → send_back = max_additions, else 0). Preset files neither import nor export it. The registered editor section `preset.reply-sections` (`features/editor/ReplySectionsSettings.tsx`, after End of request) edits it as one value field.
- `pin_examples`, `strip_examples`, `collapse_newlines`: optional prompt-content switches (U20, 2026-10-28), absent means false for older revisions. ST stores these globally in `power_user`, outside its chat-completion presets; our importer/exporter carries explicit top-level values as a portable extension. A folder import copies the source `settings.json` power-user values into each imported preset and includes them in its reimport hash, so changing only those settings updates the preset. They stay on the prompt preset, never on model settings. The registered preset editor exposes them under Text and context using the existing server drafts and revisions.
- `prefill{assistant, impersonation, continue, continue_postfix}` keeps the text and continuation behavior. Wire formatting lives on the model.
- `regex[]`, keyed by `id`: ST's regex scripts as data (`@rp/shared/docs/regexScript.ts`, shared with cards and the global list). `prompt_only` scripts apply to the assembled prompt (§15), `markdown_only` ones are display rules (§10), a script with both flags runs in both, as in ST, and scripts with neither flag rewrite text as it's written (§12, "Rewrites").
- `regex_approved`: whether the user allowed this preset's scripts to run, as ST asks once per preset. **The assembler and the display must run none of them, prompt or display, until it's true.** An import always sets it `false` and drops a `regex_approved` field in the file, and export never writes it (DESIGN §11: an imported file never grants itself capabilities).
- `extensions{}`: the preset's other ST extension data. `unsupported{}`: top-level ST fields the document doesn't model. Both are kept for export.
- The schema refuses duplicate identifiers and order entries that name no prompt, since the library merge (§3.9) matches array elements by identity.

**Legacy parsing** (`packages/server/src/formats/preset.ts`, `importStPreset`): a file's bytes or text to the document plus an `ImportReport` (`@rp/shared/importReport.ts`). Report messages are plain text that quotes the file: clients render them as text, never as Markdown or HTML. The import follows ST's own loading (`openai.js`, `PromptManager.js`):
- **What it accepts.** A file with any field only chat-completion presets have. Instruct, context, system prompt and reasoning templates, text-completion and NovelAI presets, and Advanced Formatting exports are recognized by ST's own tests and reported as unsupported, with no document (DESIGN §1.2). Anything else is an error.
- **ST's migrations:** `names_in_completion`, `custom_prompt_post_processing: "claude"`, the old inlining and system-prompt flags, and `main_prompt`/`nsfw_prompt`/`jailbreak_prompt` into the prompt list.
- **Missing fields get ST's defaults** (`default_settings`), and the report lists them. ST itself keeps the previously loaded preset's value for a missing field; a fresh ST has the defaults.
- **Prompts are sanitized as ST does:** the built-in prompts are added when missing, a prompt without an identifier gets one that nothing in the file uses (ST's random one means it's never sent), and of duplicate identifiers only the first counts. A prompt without `system_prompt` is `true`, because ST sends a relative prompt from the order only when the flag is exactly `false`.
- **One prompt order:** ST uses only the global one (`character_id` 100001), or its default order when there's none. Other orders are dropped and named in the report. A global order without a list of entries is empty in ST, so ST would send none of the preset's prompts; the import uses the default order instead and says so. Entries naming no prompt are dropped, as in ST. A prompt listed more than once is kept once. An in-chat prompt is enabled if any entry is, and since ST injects it once per enabled entry, a repeat is a warning. A relative prompt keeps its first entry, which is the one ST checks.
- **Prompts ST never sends are imported disabled**, with a warning: an in-chat prompt with a depth that isn't an integer from 0 to 10000, or with no valid role (the markers ST fills, like `charDescription`, default to `system`), and any prompt whose non-empty list of generation types has no valid entry.
- **Values go through ST's conversions:** numbers through `Number()`, checkboxes by truthiness, text as strings. An unusable value gets the default and a warning, including text fields of prompts and regex scripts that hold something else.
- **Regex depths as ST reads them:** a minimum below -1 or a maximum below 0 is no bound. An infinite maximum is no bound; an infinite minimum, which excludes every message depth, becomes `Number.MAX_VALUE`. Both are reported.
- **Connection and model fields are dropped** and listed in one info entry (DESIGN §1.2). They include proxy URLs and passwords, which are never stored. `custom_prompt_post_processing` is a connection field in ST but is kept, as `postprocess`.
- **What's kept for export:** other fields go to `unsupported{}`. A known ST field set to a non-default value is a warning; an unknown field is info. A prompt's or regex script's unknown fields go to its own `unsupported{}`. Other `extensions` entries are kept and reported.
- **Regex scripts** come from `extensions.regex_scripts`, as data. Ids are kept; a missing or repeated one gets an id nothing in the file uses.

**Legacy export** (`exportStPreset`, used by the differential fixtures): the document as an ST chat-completion preset, with the `unsupported{}` fields and `extensions` back in place and the regex scripts in `extensions.regex_scripts`. The one order is written as the global order, which is the only one ST reads. No connection or model data is written, so ST keeps its current connection when it loads the file. Modelled fields win over an `unsupported{}` entry of the same name.
- Tested on the fixtures: every field ST reads comes back with the value ST would use, and importing the export gives the same document, with nothing dropped or defaulted the second time.
- **Differences from the source file** that ST treats the same: missing fields are written with ST's defaults, prompts get all their fields explicitly, numbers written as strings become numbers, and regex depths ST ignores become `null`.

**Hardening** (the file is untrusted, review tier A). `importStPreset` never throws on a file's content; every problem goes in the report.
- **Parsing goes through the shared `parseJson`** (`formats/safety.ts`, §8), with a preset cap of 2 MB (`MAX_PRESET_BYTES`, in bytes) and the shared limits on depth, containers, values and prototype keys, all checked before `JSON.parse`. ST's bundled default preset is 8 KB, so 2 MB is 250 times it. A 2 MB import takes about half a second of CPU on the shared host; 8 MB took 3.4 s. The parser's `FormatError` becomes the report's one error.
- **Prototype keys** (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`) are dropped at any depth with a warning each. An own `constructor` key can't reach a prototype by assignment, but a deep merge walking `target.constructor.prototype` can, and the library merges documents (§3.9).
- **Conversions:** `String()` and `Number()` only ever see primitives. An object whose `toString` and `valueOf` aren't functions would make them throw.
- **Nothing is executed.** Regex scripts are stored as strings and never compiled. **Compiling one later needs a ReDoS guard**: a pattern like `(a+)+$` takes exponential time on some inputs, and a script runs on every message.
- **The report is bounded** by the shared `ReportBuilder` (§8): 200 issues, then one `report.truncated`, with file text, lists and paths shortened, so an issue is about 1.5 KB at most.
- **Every output matches the schema:** a seeded fuzz test mutates the fixtures with hostile values (infinities, wrong types, unconvertible objects) and decodes every document the importer returns against `PresetDoc`.
- **Linear time:** lookups go through maps and sets, including the renaming of repeated regex ids, which was quadratic at first (30,000 repeats took 46 s).
- Each limit's test was checked against its bug: with the check disabled, the test fails.

---

**Conditioned prompts and the end-of-request texts** (`@rp/shared/presetConditions.ts`, `@rp/shared/endOfRequest.ts`; DESIGN §2.2, owner 2026-10-27 and 2026-10-29). Who the model writes as and the one-turn direction reach the model through the preset:
- Every prompt of the order has a `condition`: `always`, `as_character` (the model writes as any card the user doesn't play), `as_user` (it writes as a card in the played-by-me set) or `with_direction` (the generation has a non-blank direction). Absent means `always`.
- **ST's triggers stay a filter of their own beside the condition** (owner 2026-10-28): `injection_trigger` lists the generation types a prompt is sent for, as ST's `shouldTrigger` (none: every type), and both it and the condition must allow the prompt (`triggersFor`, `collectionOf`). The types are ST's: `normal` (a first reply), `swipe` (a new version of a reply, which also matches `regenerate`: there's no regenerate that deletes the reply), `impersonate` (the speaker is a card the user plays), `continue` and `quiet` (a summary request). The import keeps a prompt's triggers as they are and maps none onto a condition, so a `normal`-only prompt isn't sent on swipes, as in ST. The preset editor shows them as **Generation types** checkboxes on every prompt (Normal, Continue, Impersonate, Swipe, Regenerate, Quiet; none ticked: every type), with a badge in the prompt's header when any is ticked.
- **The end-of-request texts** are four prompts of the preset with fixed identifiers, so layering, the library merge (§3.9), revisions and drafts treat them as any prompt: `groupNudge` ("When a character speaks"), `impersonationPrompt` ("When your card speaks"), `continueNudge` ("When you continue a reply", owner 2026-10-31) and `directionPrompt` ("When you give guidance"). They're never in the order, have no condition and ignore ST's triggers; the assembler sends them as the request's last message (§15 "Who writes, and the direction"). Defaults: `[Write {{speaker}}'s next message. Write only for {{speaker}}.]` for both turn texts, ST 1.19's `[Continue your last message without repeating its original content.]` for the continue nudge, and `[What happens next: {{direction}}]` for the direction, each closing its own bracket. The built-in preset and newly created prompt presets use these defaults; ST imports retain their own nudge and impersonation wording.
- **`withEndOfRequest`** gives a preset its four texts: ST's `group_nudge_prompt` becomes `groupNudge` with `{{char}}` as `{{speaker}}`, ST's `impersonation_prompt` becomes `impersonationPrompt` with `{{user}}` as `{{speaker}}` (each reported), ST's `continue_nudge_prompt` becomes `continueNudge` as it is (it speaks to the model), any text still missing gets its default (an empty ST field keeps ours), and none of them stays in the order. Their `utility_prompts` fields are emptied as they move, so the move happens once; export writes them back (below). The assembler never reads those three fields. It's pure and idempotent. The import runs it (so ST's built-in default preset, read through the same import, has the texts too), and so does every read of a stored preset: the assembler's preset source, the editors' `OpenEditor` and `CommitEditorDrafts` (`editedDoc`, also for a draft's base revision), the impersonation notice and export. No revision is written until the user saves; the first save writes the converted document. `presetOrder` never lists the four, even in an order that names them. There's no data migration: deploys start from an empty database.
- **Agent instructions** (sendmsg1, 2026-11-17; DESIGN §7.2 [D]). `agentInstructionsPrompt` (`@rp/shared/presetOrder.ts`, identifier `agentInstructions`, a system prompt, not a marker) is a prompt of the order like Main: held, edited, moved and switched on and off like any. It's sent only when the reply uses tools (`AgentAssembly` present) and never in a workshop, whose own text stays the `workshopTurn` override. `agentInstructionsPlace(prompts, order)` decides where: a preset without the prompt (every ST import, older presets) is `end`, the fallback; with it, last among the order's entries that are on is `end` too; off is `off`; anywhere else `order`. `end` joins the end-of-request message after the turn and direction texts, as the default always did; `order` makes `collectionOf` collect it and `compose` place it (`relative("agentInstructions")`) as its own message with its role.
