Its text (`agentInstructionsText` in `stages.ts`) is the preset's own, macros expanded and subject to its condition and triggers, or, when empty or missing, the app's default (`agentInstructions` in `@rp/shared/agentInstructions.ts`, from the tools offered and the contract), as the `agent:instructions` "Agent instructions" piece. `builtinPreset` (`db/assemblySources.ts`) holds it last and empty, so a chat on the built-in preset, and every preset made from it, sends byte for byte what it sent before. The preset editor labels it (`promptKinds.tsx`: "Agent instructions", with a hover explanation of when and where it's sent), shows the default under its text while empty, and, for a story preset without it, a placeholder row at the end of the list, "Add to preset", which adds it there, empty. Tests: `agentInstructionsPrompt.test.ts` (the fallback; held empty and last is byte-identical to the fallback, and the built-in preset's requests are those without it; edited text with macros replaces the default; moved above the chat history it's its own system message there; off, nothing; a plain reply never sends it).
- **Export**: `groupNudge` and `impersonationPrompt` go back into `group_nudge_prompt` and `impersonation_prompt` with `{{char}}`/`{{user}}` restored, and the three are left out of `prompts` and the order. **`directionPrompt` isn't exported**: ST has no field for it, so a reimport has the default direction text. A prompt's triggers go out as they are, and a condition becomes the types it allows (`as_user`: `impersonate`; `as_character`: `normal`, `swipe`, `regenerate`, `continue`), narrowed to the prompt's own triggers when it has any (`triggersWithCondition`); a condition that isn't `always` is also written as a `condition` field, which ST ignores and our import reads back; a `with_direction` prompt is written off in the order, since ST would send it every turn, with a `sent_with_direction` field, so an export reimports to the same document. **A prompt whose condition and generation types never meet** (`gatesNeverMeet`: none of its triggers is a type its condition can hold for here, as the assembler decides it: `as_user` holds for `impersonate` and `continue`, `as_character` for `normal`, `swipe`, `regenerate` and `continue`, `with_direction` for all but `quiet`, which only `always` prompts are sent for) is never sent here, so it goes out **off** in the order, its triggers as they are (ST would otherwise send it on them: "when writing as your card" with only Normal would run on every normal turn there), with an `enabled_here` field holding its switch here; the import turns it back on when that's true and its gates still never meet, so the export reimports to the same document. Turned off here, it stays off.

**The three import surfaces** (`formats/presetSettings.ts`). Normal file and folder library imports use `importPromptPreset`: prompts, order, roles, injection positions, utility prompts, prefill text and regex data. Samplers, budgets, wire formatting and model/provider options are excluded, with an explicit report. The legacy parser remains for format compatibility and the ST differential oracle; it is not the library import surface. Normal exports use `exportPromptPreset`, so they carry no samplers or wire settings. The exporter hydrates legacy-only fields from a recognized chat-completion default before validation, allowing prompt-only revisions to export without restoring model settings to the file. Known secret fields are discarded rather than retained in the unsupported round-trip bag.

`PreviewStSettings` parses a supplied file in the format worker and returns a bounded report and only the requested settings portion. The shared model editor advances its write version from each successful save, including when kept open in the composer panel. On a model's settings screen, the model import loads samplers, context/reply budget, wire formatting, stop strings, logit bias, streaming and supported routing settings into the form; Save applies it through `EditModel`. Connections offers a separate import taking API type, URL and model id, creating a keyless connection and optional user model through the existing operations. URL credentials are refused; keys, passwords and unrelated content are ignored and never echoed. Each surface reports ignored fields. These settings imports do not run during folder import. The folder allowlist still excludes `secrets.json` and connection settings; ST's selected prompt preset is adopted under §13's existing rules.

---

**Own-turn notes marker** (ownturn1): built-in and imported presets include `ownTurnNotes` after `chatHistory` and its adjacent `newestMessage`. It is an ordinary movable/removable marker in the editor; its notes, fallback and cache boundary are described in §15. Empty, it changes no request bytes.

## 10. Macros

**Prompt syntax highlighting** (macrohighlight, 2026-11-02): each `MacroSpec` requires `kind: "value" | "directive"`, inherited by its aliases. Character, chat/time and prompt-template macros are values; utility values are input, token limits, roll/random/pick and outlet. Directives are space/newline/noop/trim/if/else/reverse, comments and banned, plus all local/global variable writers (set/add/inc/dec/delete/set-key); variable get/has/get-key are values. `macros/highlight.ts` uses `parse.ts` and the engine's exported `pairScopes` to produce nested spans, including `::` arguments and case-insensitive block pairing. Known scoped openers/closers are directives; comments and the comment alias dim their whole argument or paired block, suppressing inner marks. Unknown names remain unmarked while their known children can highlight. Variable shorthand reads/writes follow the equivalent registered getter/setter kind. No handlers execute during highlighting. The client display and editor use one `macroRegistry` (`client/src/macros.ts`). Tests cover every builtin/alias classification, nested spans, scoped blocks, comments containing macros, unknowns, shorthand, parser recovery and incremental equivalence.

`{{user}}` follows the single selected persona (its in-chat model name), or the pinned `macro.binding` text, including an explicitly empty pin; without a selected persona it is `User`. It never joins persona names. Other persona cards in the cast are ordinary characters until selected.

**Opt-in display transformations** (U10, 2026-10-28; `client/src/features/chat/displayPipeline.ts`, `registerDisplay.tsx`). Human and model message text stays verbatim by default, while template greetings retain their existing expansion. The registered **Interface** chat panel has two independent account choices, `outputMacros` off and `displayRegex` on by default [P] (fregex, 2026-10-31: the scripts' approval is ST's consent, so a second default-off switch would surprise), merged by the existing worker-owned `SetDisplayPrefs` transaction. Output macro expansion uses the position's names and speaker fields with the shared display-only macro flag; it drops variable effects. The transforms run on streaming text too, as ST formats a message on every update (`useDisplayed.ts`, fregexs): one run at a time per text, each on the newest text, the last answer kept on screen meanwhile; a reply that just finished keeps its streamed display until the final one is ready, and a streaming text a display script applies to shows nothing before the first answer. The viewer's choices never enter assembly: editing, copying, storage and later requests use the original version text.

The reversible `displayTransforms` registry runs up to 20 ordered transformations; built-ins are `display.macros` then `display.regex`. The preset reader and panel are registered through `chatSurfaceProviders` and `chatPanels`. Display regex runs the scripts of the registered lists (`displayScriptLists` in `displayScripts.ts`, by `order`; built-ins `display-regex.global`, `display-regex.preset`, `display-regex.character`, registered in `registerDisplay.tsx`, each replaceable or disableable by id): the account's global scripts, then the current preset's (only when it is `regex_approved`), then the message's character's (only when that card is approved; `GetCardForChat.regex` carries them), and requires the viewer switch. A model-side message's character is its speaker. A user-side message, or a reply without a recorded speaker, uses the chat's only character the user doesn't play, when there is exactly one (`displayScripts.ts`). Global scripts, the preset document and card scripts refresh on library signals (including `globalRegex` saves), window focus and server context notifications, so a script edit or approval change from another tab or device reaches an open chat even when the preset id and assembled prompt stay unchanged. A card refresh keeps the scripts it already has until the new read arrives. Scripts that rewrite saved messages, rather than only the display, run on the server (§12, "Rewrites"), not here. Only enabled `markdown_only` scripts run (with `prompt_only` as well, in both places, as ST's `getRegexedString` runs them), with user/assistant-side placement (as in prompt assembly, independent of who wrote the version) and message depth relative to the viewed fork's tip. An off-window tip is read with a one-message `ReadPath`; bounded-depth scripts wait with an explanation until that read succeeds. Both reasoning panels (the provider's reasoning and "Thinking in the reply") display through the same transforms with placement 6 (reasoning), the message's character's scripts as a reply's (fregexs). Unsaved drafts, prompt-only and storage rewrite scripts never enter this display runner. `run_on_edit` does not gate ordinary rendering; it belongs to edit-time rewriting. Capture replacements and trim strings use the same pure `@rp/shared/regexReplace.ts` runner as prompt regex. Replacement/trim macros and raw or escaped pattern macros use the bounded macro engine; escaped scoped block macros are skipped with an explanation.

Imported regex executes in a separate browser worker, with one queued worker active at a time, at most 128 pending jobs, and a 500 ms deadline per job, counted from when the worker says it has loaded ("ready"; loading may take 10 s on a busy machine before the job falls back), so a slow start never shows text a display script would hide. A worker that answered is kept for the next job; one that ran out of time is terminated. The script editors' "Try it" runs its one script through the same queue (`runRegexJob`). While a display script that applies to a text hasn't answered for it yet (`useDisplayed.ts`), a finished text keeps its place invisibly (`pending`, `aria-hidden`) and a streaming one shows nothing. Before the lists themselves are read (the viewer's choices, the chat's preset, the global list, the speaking card's scripts) a text still shows without them for a moment as the chat opens; waiting for them too was tried and left out (fregexr report). `CardScripts` keeps a member's first read even when a refresh restarted it. An overflowing queue keeps the original text with an explanation. The worker that answered takes the next job (a streaming reply doesn't start one per frame); one that times out or fails is terminated and the next job starts a new one. Limits per message: 200,000 input/result characters, 100 scripts, 2,000 pattern characters, 100 trim strings and 1,000,000 produced characters across replacements. Invalid or oversized scripts keep their input with a plain-text explanation. A macro limit in a pattern, replacement or trim string skips that script with an explanation too, preserving its input rather than using an unresolved macro as regex data. Timeout discards the job's partial work and shows its original input with an explanation. The normal Markdown sanitizer handles transformed output. `displayScripts.test.ts` covers scope order, per-scope approval, the character rule and the card cache; `e2e/regexScripts.spec.ts` covers a stored rewrite with its original text and restore, the global editor, and card approval at 1440/390 in light/dark. `displayPipeline.test.ts` covers opt-in, human/assembly preservation, registry override/disable/restore, script filtering, depths, captures, trimming and limits. `e2e/displayTransforms.spec.ts` covers approval (including revocation and reapproval from another editor tab and a separate RPC session), saved viewer choices, rendered Markdown, original editor/storage text and the next provider request at 1440/390 in light/dark under the production CSP.

`packages/shared/src/macros/` (DESIGN §5.6): a pure engine, for the server's context assembler and for the client when it renders text. It follows SillyTavern's current macro engine (`public/scripts/macros/`, ST's default), read at ST commit `06bde939`.

**Expanding text** (`expand.ts`): `expand({ text, origin, purpose, displayRule?, registry, context, frozen?, random, limits? })` returns `Expanded` or `LimitExceeded`. It's the module's only way in, so the origin check can't be skipped.
- **`origin` and `purpose` are required** and decide whether anything expands:
  - card and preset text always does (lorebook entries and notes count as card text)
  - a chat message does when its stored macro mode is `template`, whoever wrote it (DATA-MODEL §15, invariant 7). The defaults stay as DESIGN §5.6 says: greetings are `template`, typed and generated text `verbatim`.
  - for `purpose: "display"`, the opt-in display rule (`displayRule: true`) expands verbatim messages too
  - display never changes state: its variable writes are dropped
- **`context` is the state at the text's position** (`context.ts`): names, the card's fields as stored (unexpanded), the messages before it, the clock and time zone, and whatever else ST's macros read. Card text expanded against it follows the state, so `{{user}}` in a greeting follows a persona change until the message is sent.
- **The caller's side of the contract:**
  - `messages[].text` is resolved text, as shown: a macro's output is never expanded again, so a template message passed raw would make `{{lastMessage}}` say `{{user}} said hi`.
  - Re-rendering or re-assembling a message passes the state from before that message's own `var.set` events, with its frozen values. Otherwise `{{incvar}}` in a greeting would count twice.
- **Freezing.** Random, roll, pick and the time macros are `volatile`. Each value drawn is keyed by its text (a card field's name, or none), offset, macro, its source as written (not its expanded arguments, so a name inside them doesn't move it), and repeat count. The result returns them as `frozen`, and passing them back makes a re-expansion identical, whatever the clock or random source. The time macros (`volatile: "clock"`) freeze the time they read, as epoch milliseconds, and work their value out from it again, so a date format naming `{{char}}` keeps its date and follows the name. Random, pick and roll freeze their value, and a frozen value the macro couldn't produce with its arguments now (not one of the choices, outside the dice's range; a clock outside 1900 to 2200) is drawn again (`accepts`), so moved text, changed arguments and forged values all draw again. Stored entries that aren't strings are ignored.
- **Variables are effects** (`variables.ts`). `context.variables` holds the chat's variables (`local`: the chat state's `vars`) and the global ones. Macros work on an overlay, and every write comes back, in order, in `effects` as `{ scope, name, value }`, with `value: null` for a deletion. `variables` is the state after the text, to pass to the next text expanded at the same position. The caller records local effects as `var.set` events. Global variables come back as effects too, but nothing persists them yet (DATA-MODEL §16).
- ST's variable rules are kept: values are stored as given, numeric text reads as a number (`007` → `7`), addvar adds, appends to a JSON array or concatenates, and the shorthands (`{{.name}}`, `{{$name}}`, `=`, `+=`, `-=`, `++`, `--`, `||`, `??`, `||=`, `??=`, comparisons) only expand their value when it's needed. Names are own keys only, so unlike ST `{{hasvar::constructor}}` is false.
- **Variable values are bounded.** A write that would produce a value over 1 MB is refused (ST has no cap): the macro produces nothing, no effect is recorded, and the result lists it in `refusedWrites`, so the caller can show it. Reading a value costs its length once per write, since the read and the JSON parse are cached; a shorthand comparison or test costs the value's length each time, and so does each message the last-message macros and `{{idle_duration}}` look at.

**The registry** (`registry.ts`, `builtins.ts`). Macros register by name and aliases, matched case-insensitively, through the generic registry (`@rp/shared/registry.ts`). The built-ins register through it like a plugin. A definition declares positional arguments (optional ones last, some whole numbers only), an optional list tail, delayed argument resolution (for `{{if}}`), and `volatile`. Arguments are strict, ST's default: a call with the wrong number of arguments, or a non-number where a whole number is expected, stays as written.

**The parser** (`parse.ts`) is a hand-written scanner in place of ST's Chevrotain grammar: no regex that can backtrack, each macro start parsed once, nested macros parsed with an explicit stack instead of recursion. A macro that's never closed stays text however deep it goes, as in ST.

**Hardening.** Imported card text is untrusted, so one expansion is bounded (`MacroLimits`, overridable per call):
- **Depth:** 32 macros evaluated inside one another (arguments, blocks, `{{if}}` branches, card fields), so deep nesting can't overflow the stack.
- **Expansions:** 10,000 macros evaluated.
- **Length:** 256K characters (262,144) in any one text, refused before parsing. That's about 60K tokens, far above any real card field, lorebook entry or preset prompt. The cap applies to each piece separately, since each is expanded on its own: a preset prompt, a card field, a greeting, a note, an `{{if}}` branch. It keeps the worst input to a fraction of a second on the server's shared event loop.
- **Work:** 4,000,000 units, about one per character produced by a macro, read from or written to a variable, or looked at by the parser, and one per die rolled. Pairing blocks costs 40 per macro, measured against parsing (the maps and sets it builds), plus one per entry its search looks at. This bounds the output and the time taken, and stops values that double. Each level pairs its block's content again (as ST does), and that's counted too, so deeply nested blocks can't cost depth × size for free.
- **The parser charges as it goes**, every 64K steps, so a budget that runs out stops it partway. The reviews' worst inputs at full size under the cap are tests: each stops within the default limits. Measured best of five on this host at load 46–60, each took 38–173 ms.
- Handlers count large output before building it (`{{space::N}}`, `{{newline::N}}`, dice, and `{{datetimeformat}}` at 13 characters per format character, its most).
- **Reaching a limit fails the whole text** with `LimitExceeded`: nothing partial comes back. It says which limit, and where: `scope` is `""` for the text itself or the card field it happened in (`card.description`), and `offset` is the innermost macro being evaluated. The caller fails that one piece (a preset prompt, a greeting) with a visible error saying where, not the whole turn.
- **Linear time:** no regex that backtracks (ST's `{{trim}}` regex, quadratic on runs of newlines, is a scan here); recovery after a name uses a precomputed table; pairing blocks searches square-root blocks of running sums, so many unclosed openers cost about n√n. The parser and the pairing count their steps as work, so the tests assert linear time as a work bound rather than a time.
- **No code evaluation:** nothing calls `eval`, `Function` or a dynamic import, and a test scans the sources for them.
- **Untrusted names** are looked up as own keys or in `Map`s: variables, frozen values, outlets, macro names.
- **Nothing throws out of an expansion** for bad input: a macro whose handler fails stays as written, as in ST, and so does a variable shorthand whose operation fails (deeply nested JSON, say), where ST gives up on the whole text.
- Each guard's test was checked against its bug: with the check disabled, the test fails or times out.

**ST's behavior reproduced** (vectors in `packages/shared/test/macros/`, most from ST's `tests/frontend/MacroEngine.e2e.js`):
- arguments as `{{a::b::c}}`, `{{a:b}}` or `{{a b}}`, trimmed; after a single colon or a space the rest is one argument
- nested macros evaluated inside-out, left to right; an unknown or wrongly called macro stays as written, its nested macros expanded
- scoped blocks `{{name}}…{{/name}}` as the last argument, trimmed and dedented unless the opener has `#`
- `{{if}}`/`{{else}}` with only the chosen branch expanded; `{{trim}}`; `\{` escapes; the legacy `<USER>`, `<BOT>`, `<CHAR>`, `<GROUP>`, `<CHARIFNOTGROUP>` and `{{time_UTC+2}}` forms
- card fields expanded once per expansion, on their own, with card-field macros inside them empty
- moment's `en` formats and humanize thresholds for the time macros
- quirks, each with a test: `{{char's}}` resolves like `{{char}}` (Chevrotain drops what can't follow a name); an unknown macro with a block comes back as `{{foo}}bar}}`; a comment's argument is still evaluated; `{{if}}` matches `if` and `else` case-sensitively when splitting

**Deliberately different from ST:**
- Text completion is out of scope (DESIGN §1.2), so the instruct, system-prompt and context-template macros resolve as in ST with instruct mode off, instead of reaching the model as text (`builtins/prompts.ts`): instruct sequences are empty, `{{systemPrompt}}` is the card's own system prompt, or empty without one, where ST's default returns its default system prompt ("Write {{char}}'s next reply in a fictional chat between {{char}} and {{user}}."), a text-completion prompt that doesn't exist here, `{{defaultSystemPrompt}}` is empty, and `{{chatStart}}` and `{{exampleSeparator}}` are ST's default `***`.
- `{{pick}}` is seeded like ST's but without seedrandom, so it picks differently for the same seed.
- Where ST's parser recovers from a malformed macro (a bad nested macro, a stray operator), the macro stays literal here and scanning resumes after its `{{`. ST's recovery depends on the input and can swallow text after it.
- `{{hasExtension}}` is always false: ST extensions don't exist here.
- Names inside a card field's macros resolve against the same bindings as the text around them. ST resolves them from the page's persona and character and ignores the call's name overrides. That's the rebinding DESIGN §5.3 moves away from: a card field nested in a prompt follows that prompt's bindings.

---

Card name bindings use `nickname || name` throughout assembly: card blocks, greetings, example messages, transcript speaker names, group nudges, notes, lorebook keys and postprocessing. Browser greeting/template expansion uses the same effective name. UI cast metadata carries the revision's display name, model name and subtitle; pinned and chat-local card bindings resolve all of them from the selected revision, together with its avatar.

## 11. Importing

Files into the library and back out (DATA-MODEL §3, §11, §14; PLUGINS §8). The parsers of §8 and §9 do the reading; this section is what stores their output.

### 11.1 Storage

Card re-imports update only the ref named by `into` or matched by the ST folder’s `source_path`. The card’s own edits are three-way merged against its previous import, with conflicts kept pending for the normal update resolver. Card edits, imports and resolved updates return no follower outcomes; forks carry no source path/hash and keep their content and notes. The folder importer already routes through `ImportFile`; it creates no card variants or overrides. Non-card refs retain following and merge propagation.

One write operation, `ImportFile` (`db/libraryWrites.ts`), stores a parsed file in one transaction:
- **A new file** becomes an entity, an `upstream` ref and a revision with `origin = import`. The ref records the file's name (`source_path`) and the SHA-256 of its bytes (`source_hash`), and the revision's `origin_ref` both, as JSON.
- **A re-import** names the upstream ref (`intoRefId`). As §3.9 describes: a new revision on the import line, merged into the upstream; its children keep their heads until an explicit merge. The result lists non-card follower outcomes with their labels; cards return none. Only the user's own upstream of the same kind takes it: another user's ref is `NotFound`, a variant or another kind `RefOperationRefused`.
- **Documents cross as JSON text.** The parsed document reaches the main thread from a format worker and goes on to the writer as a string, so the main thread copies it but never walks or decodes it.
- **The writer only stores.** Every user's writes wait on the one writer (§3.1), so the format worker works out the document's content hash and search text too, from the JSON as stored, and the writer inserts them as given. Only a card with media, or one that keeps its avatar, is parsed in the writer, to name its files; it's also hashed and given its search text there. That's left as is: cards are capped at 8 MiB, and a 7.7 MiB card took 187–244 ms of writer time on the shared host. A test checks that the worker's hash is the writer's own: an edit that changes nothing makes no revision.
- **Known limit:** a large import still holds the writer while its revision and its full-text index entry go in, and a re-import while it merges. A reviewer measured a 19.6 MiB, 10,000-entry lorebook within the caps holding it for seconds on the loaded shared host (about 440 ms of that was the index insert, unloaded). Lorebook entries as rows of their own, or a lower lorebook cap, would bound it.
- **Merge staging** (`mode=merge&into=<cardRef>` on `/library/import`): parse and store file/media, add or reuse its import revision, and return `stagedRevisionId` without changing the card head or card-owned note entities. `PreviewForkMerge` compares it with the last merged import and local head; `CommitForkMerge` saves the reviewed result. Embedded lorebook fields merge with the document. Exported card-note sidecars keep their independent histories and are not updated here. The client: Import a new version… → **Merge…** (`features/cardImport/upload.ts` `stageVersion`), then the merge review (§14.6 "Merging into forks") on the returned revision.
- **Media** (`media_assets`, `media_refs`, already in `0002`; no migration was needed). A card's avatar and embedded assets are files under `DATA_DIR/media/<2 hex>/<sha256>`, written before the transaction. The transaction records each file once for everyone (`ON CONFLICT (sha256) DO NOTHING`) and gives the user a reference to it. The card document then names them: `avatar_media_id`, and `asset_media_ids` by each asset's URI (built with `Object.fromEntries`, since a URI comes from the file and could be `__proto__`). A file written for an import whose transaction then fails, or before the server stopped, stays on disk with no row naming it. The sweep (`sweepMedia`, at startup and every hour) deletes those once they're an hour old, and leftover temporary files with them. It reads the recorded hashes in a reader worker (`ListMediaHashes`) and works through the files with libuv's file I/O, which doesn't block the main thread. Files aren't deleted when an import fails: another user's import of the same bytes may have recorded them meanwhile.
  - **An import in progress keeps its files.** Imports hold the hashes they've written in an in-process set until they commit or give up, and the sweep skips those. A file an import reuses has its time refreshed, so an old orphan's bytes uploaded again count as new. A candidate is checked again just before it goes (`IsMediaRecorded`, and the set), so a commit that lands after the listing is respected. It's then moved aside, checked once more, and deleted, or moved back if an import took it meanwhile; an import that found it gone writes its own copy. The age alone doesn't decide, so a forward clock jump can't take a file an import is about to record. A file moved aside by a sweep the server stopped in the middle of (`<hash>.<id>.swept`) is put back by the next sweep, the one at startup included, if its hash is recorded or held and its file isn't back already; any other is deleted. `test/importMedia.test.ts` covers each case: a commit landing after the checks and after the move, through a hook at each step, and a crash between the move and the delete.
  - **Links are never followed.** Every entry is read with `lstat`: only plain folders and files under the media folder, itself not a link, are looked at, and every path deleted must resolve inside it. A linked folder, a linked file and a linked media folder each leave the file they point at alone.
- **ST's Character's Note** (`data.extensions.depth_prompt`) becomes the card's first note (DESIGN §4.1a): a note entity whose document (`@rp/shared/docs/note.ts`) has the depth, the role, `owner: {card}` and `on_by_default: true` (ST always sends it), and `scan_lore` when the folder import's settings have ST's `allowWIScan` (`characterNoteScan`). A re-import of the card updates that note the same way, merged with the user's edits to it. "The card's first note" is the oldest live note whose upstream head names the card and isn't a note made from a module or a Character Author's Note (`cardNote` in `db/library.ts`). The card's other notes an export carried (`notesDocJson`) are made, or merged into the one with the same `module_id` (`cardNoteFrom`), in the same transaction.
- **The embedded lorebook** stays in the card document (§8).
- **A new version without the card's files keeps them.** A JSON card holds none, so re-importing one into a card imported as a PNG or CHARX would otherwise drop its avatar and embedded assets as the new version's change, and a PNG export would fall back to the placeholder. The import carries the upstream's current `avatar_media_id` forward when the file has no avatar, and each `asset_media_ids` entry whose URI the new document's `assets` still name but the file doesn't hold. It returns `keptAvatar` and `keptAssets`, and the route adds an info line for each to the report.
- **Replace: "Import a new version…" of a card** (owner, 2026-11-01; DESIGN §4). `ImportFile` with `replace: {expectedHeadRevisionId}` (`replaceCard` in `db/libraryWrites.ts`, the same transaction, after the media and kept-avatar steps above): refused (`RefOperationRefused`, `409`) unless the card's head is still the one the preview showed and the schema version matches; the file goes on the import line as a re-import's does (no new import revision when it's the last import's content); then the card's next revision is the file's content wholesale, `replacementDoc` (`@rp/shared/cardReplace.ts`, which the client's preview also uses) keeping from the card only what a file can't carry: the cutout while the picture is the same one, regex approval only when the scripts are identical (DESIGN §11), module agent permissions off where they were off. It has two parents (the head, the import), origin `merge`, the message "Replaced with a new version from <file>", and the merge base moves to that import, so a later re-import of the same file is `up_to_date` and a newer one merges against it. Fields typed since the last revision take the new text by `drafts.settleOn`, as `RestoreRevision` does (§14.2). The card's notes (a differing Character's Note in the file isn't applied), its favourite (the file's `fav` isn't read) and its chats are untouched: chats that follow the card read the new head from then on, chats bound to a fixed revision keep theirs. A card without an import line (a fork, a card made here) takes it, the file starting its line. History's Restore of the previous revision undoes it. The preview reads the card through `CardReplaceSource` (reader, `db/importReads.ts`): head and its number, document, picture hash, first note's text, favourite, whether it has an import line, and the chats that follow it or are bound to a fixed revision where each stands (`chatStateAt`, `db/cards.ts`, at the chat's active leaf). `test/cardReplace.test.ts` covers a preview storing nothing, Replace's one revision with the kept fields, the stale-head refusal, a later re-import being up to date, a pinned chat keeping its revision, another user's card, and a card made here.

`ExportSource` (`db/importReads.ts`) reads what an export takes: the ref's head document, the card's first note, its other notes (a linked one with its shared note's head text; one whose shared note is in the bin is left out), and the stored files the document names. **Only files the user holds a reference to come back.** A document is data, and an edit could put any media id in it; another user's file is left out as if it weren't there (`test/importStorage.test.ts`).

### 11.2 Importers and detection

**The importer registry** (`importer/importers.ts`, PLUGINS §8) is a registry of §6's kind: entries by id, overridden or disabled for the length of a scope. An importer has a format id, a `detect` test and a `parse` from bytes to a document, its report and the files that came with it. The built-ins register in order: `card` (PNG, CHARX, or JSON with a `spec`), `st-world-info` (JSON with `entries`), `st-preset` (any field only ST's preset and template files have, `isStPresetFile` in `formats/preset.ts`, so instruct and context templates reach the preset importer and are reported as unsupported), and `card-v1` (JSON with a `name`, asked last since the key is common). Parsing runs in a format worker (§11.3), so the registry lives there: a plugin's importer will be a module that worker loads.

**Detection reads the bytes, never the name** (`importer/detect.ts`). PNG and zip by their magic bytes; for JSON, the top-level keys, read in one pass without parsing: strings are skipped by their quotes and nesting is a counter, so a hostile file costs a linear scan and can't overflow a stack. The importer that's chosen parses the file properly, under its own caps (§8). A file no importer recognizes, and a file its importer rejects (`FormatError`), become a report with one error and nothing to store.

**Every document an importer returns is checked against its kind's schema** (`validateDoc`, in the format worker): one that doesn't pass is an importer bug, logged, and the file's report says it can't be imported (`file.invalid_document`), with nothing stored. The preset importer once kept a regex placement of `1e20`, a whole number but not a safe one, which its schema refuses.

**What a parse returns** (`parseFile`): the report, the SHA-256 of the file, the document and its label as JSON text, and each file that came with it, with its SHA-256, size and image type from its magic bytes (and a PNG's size from its header).
- **Labels:** a card's name, a lorebook's name, a preset's file name (ST names presets by file), falling back to the file name; control characters removed, at most 200 characters.
- **ST's Character's Note** leaves the card's `extensions` and becomes the note document, so it lives in one place. ST's defaults apply: depth 4, role `system`. An empty one, which ST writes into every card, stays in the extensions untouched.
- **Files are copied to buffers of their own** before they cross to the main thread. An extracted asset can be a view into the upload or into Node's shared buffer pool, and transferring that buffer would detach the pool under the worker.

### 11.3 Format workers

The parsers are synchronous and take up to about a second on a hostile file (§8), so they run in worker threads (`importer/worker.ts`), never on the main thread. `Formats` (`importer/Formats.ts`) is the main thread's side.
- **The pool is the database readers'** (`db/readerPool.ts`, §3.1), with workers of its own. A worker is busy until it answers, so the pool's size is how many files are parsed at once, and the rest queue in order. A worker that dies (a crash, or its heap limit) fails only the file it had, with `FormatWorkerFailed`, which is logged, and is respawned a second later. The files queued behind it wait for the new worker, and fail only if it dies before it's ready too. A file whose send fails (§3.1) also fails alone, even first in line on a new worker. Unlike a database read, the file isn't retried: a file that stopped one worker would stop the next, and its bytes were transferred to the first. `test/formatWorkers.test.ts` checks this with a test worker that dies on request: one stop, the file fails, and the files behind it parse, also behind a file that can't be sent. A CHARX whose assets share one file exports (`test/libraryImport.test.ts`): the export reads the file once, so its buffer is in the request twice.
- **The interactive lane** (`ThumbnailLane` in `Formats.ts`, `thumbnailSize`, one worker by default): the same worker code in a pool of its own for what the browser waits for, thumbnails (§14.5b) and token counts (`CountTokens`, §6 "Text tokens"), so neither queues behind an import's files, and an encoding's ranks are in memory once.
- **The heap limit,** 512 MB (`resourceLimits.maxOldGenerationSizeMb`), bounds what one file can cost the server: the worst file within the caps took 80 MB, and a worker from source needs about 85 MB for its modules.
- **The upload is transferred, not copied,** when its bytes have a buffer of their own. A view into a larger buffer is copied first: small Node Buffers share a pool, which can't be transferred, and transferring the buffer under other views would empty them.
- **Measured** in the test: an 11 MB lorebook parsed on the main thread blocks it for hundreds of milliseconds. Through a worker, the main thread's longest stall stays under a quarter of that and under 250 ms; measured alone, 130 ms against 1,224 ms under a load average near 90. The bounds are loose because the host is shared.
- **Bundled** like the database workers (§3.6): `formats.mjs`, stamped with them, and refused when missing or stale.

- **A job has 30 s** (`jobDeadline` in the pool, format workers only). A parse or export still running then, such as a parser bug that never returns, gets its thread terminated (`Formats` keeps the newest thread of each worker id for that). The pool then treats it as a crash: only that request fails, and the worker is respawned for the files queued behind it. The worst file within the caps parses in about a second unloaded. The test stops a looping worker at a 2 s deadline, and fails when stopping it does nothing. The database readers have no deadline and behave as before.

### 11.4 Upload and export

**Plain HTTP, not RPC** (`importer/routes.ts`). RPC messages are JSON, so a file would cross as base64: a third larger, one WebSocket message held whole, and decoded on the main thread before the format worker could have it. Over HTTP the body arrives as bytes, is capped as it streams, and goes to the worker as it is.

**`POST /library/import?name=<file name>[&into=<upstream ref>]`**, the file as the body:
- **Who:** the same resolution as an RPC (`Accounts.resolve` on the request's headers: the session cookie, proxy identity or local admin, §4); `401` without one. The cross-site guard of §4 runs first, as for every request.
- **Only `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`** (`415` otherwise): a cross-site form can't send it, and a cross-site `fetch` with it needs a preflight the server never answers. That's on top of the `Origin` check.
- **Size:** at most 64 MiB, the parsers' own file cap (§8). A larger `Content-Length` is `413` before anything is read. Without one, or when it lies, reading stops as the body passes the cap, and the `413` closes the connection.
- **Reading the body** (`importer/body.ts`, from Node's request directly). First the upload waits for its first bytes, then takes a memory permit (two per format worker), then reads the rest. So the server holds at most that many bodies, and an upload that sends nothing holds no permit; the rest wait in their sockets, where TCP holds the sender back.
- **Stalls and trickles are dropped,** each with a `408` sent before the connection closes:
  - a pause of 10 s between chunks, or before the first
  - while it holds a permit, less than 32 KiB/s averaged over each 10 s, the first 10 s being its allowance; so a trickle of a byte every few seconds, which never pauses for 10 s, holds a permit for about 10 s
  - a body still arriving after 15 minutes
  
  The numbers are for a slow phone. A 1 Mbit/s uplink, about 120 KiB/s, sends a 30 MB card in about four minutes: the minimum rate leaves it a margin of almost four times (a 0.5 Mbit/s one still passes), and the deadline gives a full 64 MiB file 15 minutes, about 73 KiB/s. The cost is that an upload that does keep up 32 KiB/s, from a user willing to spend that, holds its permit for up to the deadline.
- **Exports have permits of their own,** taken before they read their files, so stalled uploads never hold them up.
- **One transfer per user at a time:** a user's second upload or export waits for the first, for up to the 15 minutes an upload may take (`503` after that). So no user holds more than one permit, and an export started during one's own upload just waits. `test/transfers.test.ts` covers the `408`, exports and silent uploads going through while two other users stall, an upload going through while two others trickle, and the wait; each test fails against the previous design.
- **The name** is used as the label fallback and the source path, without folders or control characters, at most 255 characters. The format never comes from it (§11.2).
- **`into` is checked first,** before the body is read (`GetLibraryRef`): another user's ref, or none, is `404`, and a variant `409`. After the parse, a file of another kind is `409` before its media are written. So a refused import stores nothing (`test/importMedia.test.ts`).
- **Then:** the format worker parses the file (§11.3), its media are written to disk, and `ImportFile` stores it (§11.1).
- **`mode=preview|replace`** ("Import a new version…", §11.1) needs `into` naming a card's upstream (`400` without, `409` for another kind), checked before the body is read. `preview` parses the file in the format worker and answers `CardReplacePreview` (`@rp/shared/cardReplace.ts`): the report, the document and Character's Note as the worker encoded them, how many other notes and embedded files it holds, its picture's type and bytes as base64 (at most 16 MiB, a browser image type; otherwise none), which the dialog shows through a `blob:` URL, and `CardReplaceSource`. It writes no media and stores nothing. `replace` also needs `head`, the head the preview showed, and stores as `ImportFile` with `replace`. Both take the same auth, content type, size caps, permits and one-transfer-per-user rule as any import. With any of the three modes (merge too), `link` (at most 2,048 characters; `400` otherwise or without a mode) names the card's page on the card source the file came from: a parsed card gets it in its `source` list unless it's there (`withSourceLink`, `importer/sourceLink.ts`, which adoption uses too), in the preview and in what's stored, so a source's newer file, which doesn't name its own page, never reads as removing the card's link back (§11.5 Updates).
- **The answer** is `ImportResult` (`@rp/shared/libraryImport.ts`) as JSON: the report, and what the file became, or `library: null` with the report saying why. `into` naming another user's ref, or none, is `404`; a variant or another kind `409`; a format worker that failed while it had the file (a crash, its deadline, a failed start) `500` with "The import failed on the server; try again." That wording never blames the file: a file the parsers can't read is a report, not a failure.

**The exporter registry** (`importer/exporters.ts`) uses §6's scoped registry inside each format worker, like importers. Each entry owns its format id, entity kind, client label, MIME type, extension, media requirement (`none`, `avatar`, `all`) and writer. Built-ins register in preference order; registering the same id overrides it, `disable` hides it, and closing the scope restores the previous entry. Worker bootstraps install registrations before serving requests; every worker in a pool must install the same registrations, including replacements after a crash. `workerHandlers.ts` supplies the shared export and parser handlers (including per-job trusted ST parser resolution), while `worker.ts` supplies the built-in bootstrap. Direct `exportFile` callers honor an explicitly passed registry or the current `Exporters` service, building scoped defaults only when neither is supplied.

`Formats.listExports` reads data-only metadata through the worker's `ListExportFormats` operation. The authenticated `ListExportFormats` client RPC exposes that catalog; the library uses its kinds, ids, labels and order for export choices, with no separate format map. The HTTP export route validates against the same worker catalog, reads only the media its entry requests and uses its MIME type and extension. It sends this metadata with the export; the executing worker refuses a changed id, kind, MIME type, extension or media requirement before writing, so a scope closing or inconsistent workers cannot silently label bytes with another exporter's headers. New formats need only a worker registration. Documents remain data and downloads remain attachments. `test/exporters.test.ts` installs a synthetic format and an override in a real worker: the client RPC lists them, HTTP uses their bytes and metadata, a disabled format is refused, and closing the plugin scope removes the addition and restores built-in choices and output. It also checks stale metadata and registrations/restoration on two workers and their respawns. `exporterRegistry.test.ts` checks dispatch through a supplied service. The existing import/export tests retain their fixtures and assertions.

**`POST /library/export`**, JSON `{refId, format}` (at most 4 KiB, `application/json` only): the ref's head as a file.
- **Built-in formats** (`importer/exporters.ts`): a card as `card-png`, `card-v2-json`, `card-v3-json` or `card-charx`; a lorebook as `st-world-info`; a preset as `st-preset`. An unknown, disabled or another kind's format is `400`, another user's ref `404`.
- **Written in a format worker** like a parse, since a large lorebook takes as long to write (`importer/exporters.ts`). The document is decoded against its kind's schema first; one that no longer matches (an edit made it invalid) is `422` with a sentence.
- **The card's note goes back** as ST's `depth_prompt`, unless the note is private.
- **Files:** the avatar and assets the user holds (§11.1), read from disk by the paths `mediaPath` makes and no other. Only the files the format holds are read: the avatar for a PNG, every file for a CHARX, none for JSON. Each file is read once, however many times the document names it. Their total is capped at 128 MiB, the CHARX reader's own (§8), before anything is read (`422` past it): a document can name the same file any number of times, and the archive holds a copy for each.
- **A PNG needs a PNG avatar.** A card with none goes into a 1×1 placeholder PNG. A card whose avatar is another image type is refused (`422`), suggesting CHARX, which keeps the image, or JSON, rather than having its avatar silently replaced.
- **The response** has the file's type, `Content-Disposition: attachment` with the label as the name (an ASCII fallback, and the real name percent-encoded), `nosniff` and `no-store`.

**Export with unsaved changes** (owner, 2026-11-02; `features/cardExport/`). The file is always the ref's head, a saved revision, so every way to export asks first when the entry has fields not in it. The entry points: the full editor's **Export…** (`card-export.editor` in `cardContributions` `actions`), the character and persona tabs' **Export…** (`card-export.chat` in `chatCardActions`), each a menu of `ListExportFormats`' card formats (PNG, V2 JSON, V3 JSON, CHARX), the saved and pending Cast member menus' **Export…**, and the library's item submenu **Export…** (`library.export`, every kind's formats: cards and personas, presets, lorebooks). All share `ExportMenu` (`CardExport.tsx`), with the hover/focus explanation “Exports this card as a file.” for cards. Each calls `requestExport` (`exportRequests.ts`: the ref, the format and its name, the entry's label), answered by one host registered in `appTools` (`card-export.check`, the dialog `ExportCheck.tsx` loaded lazily), so a menu that closes doesn't take the question with it. It uses the editor open on that ref on the page if there is one (`openEditorStore`, the plain stores `useLeaveGuard` tracks in `openEditors.ts`), else a store of its own opened on the server's drafts (`OpenEditor`), flushes pending typing, and names the unsaved fields (`unsaved.ts`: `fieldLabel`, each once; a preset's held changes as one line). With none it downloads at once, as before. Otherwise a dialog, "<label> has unsaved changes", lists them and offers **Save and export** (`EditorStore.commit`, a revision with no message, then the download of that head; a failed save says so and exports nothing), **Export the last revision** (the head without them; they stay unsaved) and **Cancel**. The download is `POST /library/export` (`downloadExport` in `features/library/files.ts`). A card's exportable notes are refs of their own and go in the file too (`exportDrafts.ts`, `ListCardNotes`): both a linked slot's own fields and its shared text (`ListSharedNotes`) are checked, including a note whose draft makes it exportable. Shared refs are checked and saved once even if several slots link to them. Each note's unsaved fields are named "Note “<title>”: <field>"; **Save and export** commits the card, then each note with changes (a revision each), and stops at the first failure; **Export the last revision** takes every last revision. Held-only preset changes also trigger the question. If any editor or note read fails, the export stops with an error toast instead of skipping the check. `test/exportDrafts.test.ts` covers these inputs, shared-ref reuse and failed reads. `e2e/editors2.spec.ts` covers Cast hover, click, keyboard submenu navigation and PNG downloads, unsaved drafts by hover and keyboard, and the full editor (both choices, Cancel, and no dialog with nothing unsaved; at 1440 and 390, both themes), the library menu on the server's drafts, a card's note with unsaved typing (named, left out by the last revision, saved by Save and export), and the character tab; `test/exportUnsaved.test.ts` the names.
### 11.5 Card sources: browsing a third-party archive (cardsrc1, 2026-11-07; spec/CARD-SOURCES.md phases 1 to 4)

The server browses card archives run by others, through their public APIs only, and the browser only ever talks to the server. cardex is the first: a public archive run by a third party, read through its public API v1. Production registers the cardex adapter; the development instance, previews and every test register the same adapter pointed at the fake archive instead, so they never contact cardex.zip and show only our own synthetic cards.

- **The registry** (`sources/CardSources.ts`, the `CardSources` service): adapters by id, overridden or disabled for a scope like every registry (`makeRegistry`). `CardSources.layerWith({adapters})` builds it; `serverWith`'s fifth argument takes it (the default registers none). An adapter (`sources/adapter.ts`) declares its id, name, `hosts`, scheme, key need (`none` / `optional` / `required`) and rate, and implements `capabilities`, `search` (an opaque cursor in; `next`, `total` and `totalEstimated` out), `tags` (a prefix → tags with counts), `card` (the file's bytes and its summary), `image` (one of its own refs) and `versions` (a batch of ids → version, `updatedAt`, `supersededBy`). It never sees the network directly: each call gets a `SourceHttp` made for that adapter.
- **Not an open proxy** (`sources/guard.ts`, DESIGN §11). The client names a source id and a query, card id or image key, never a URL. A request must use the adapter's scheme and one of its `hosts`. A host that resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address (the default bypass ranges and unspecified addresses, IPv4-mapped too) is refused unless the admin listed that host by name in Settings → Network's bypass list (a `local` adapter, the fake's, is exempt). Requests go through `Network` with the instance's proxy. The source guard validates each redirect hop and gives `Network` the checked IP addresses; it connects to a checked literal directly or through HTTP/SOCKS proxies, preserving the original HTTP Host and TLS hostname, with separate pools for each pinned origin and TLS identity. Redirects stay within the origin. Requests carry a fixed `User-Agent` naming the app, its version and that it browses on its user's request, no cookies and no referrer; 15 s to the first byte, 60 s in all, and capped streaming reads (JSON 2 MiB, cards 64 MiB, images 16 MiB). Failures are one `SourceFailed` with a `reason`: 429 `rate_limited` (with `retryAfterMs`), 401/403 `unauthorized`, 404 `not_found`, 5xx and network errors `unreachable`, other statuses and over-cap bodies `bad_response`, and `disabled` when the source is off for the user.
- **Image keys.** Results carry `thumb` and `image` as keys this server issued: the adapter's ref in base64url plus an HMAC (`Secrets.sign`, purpose `card-source-image`) over user, source and ref, so nothing is stored per key. `GET /sources/:sourceId/image?k=<key>&w=` (`api/cardSources.ts`; the key is in the query, being longer than a path segment may be) checks the session (401), the MAC (404 for another user's or a made-up key) and `w` (400), and answers with an `ETag`, `private, max-age=86400` and `nosniff`. A width makes a WebP through the thumbnail lane (§14.5b), stored beside the cached file.
- **Consent** (spec §5.1). `ListCardSources`, the switches, the key, the rating, the recently viewed list and Clear never contact a source. Only `SourceCapabilities`, `SourceSearch`, `SourceTags`, `SourceCard` and the image route do, only while the source is on for that user, and the client calls them only while the source's option is open. `test/cardSources.test.ts` asserts that nothing reaches the fake archive before then.
- **Self limits** (`sources/limiter.ts`). A token bucket per source for the instance (the adapter's rate, else 2/s with a burst of 8); a request waits at most 5 s for a token, else fails `rate_limited` with the wait. A 429 blocks the source for its `Retry-After` or a backoff doubling from 1 s to 5 minutes, reset by the next success. Identical concurrent requests (same user, source and request) share one upstream request (`makeCoalescer`); when every waiter is interrupted (a superseded search), so is it.
- **The cache** (`sources/cache.ts`) is files on disk, not rows: `DATA_DIR/cache/sources/entries/<sha256 of the key>.json` and content-addressed blobs under `blobs/<2 hex>/<sha256>`, with an in-memory index rebuilt by a scan at startup that removes orphans and temporary files. Keys are per user, so one user's cache is never another's. Result pages live 10 minutes, capabilities and tags 24 hours from when they were fetched, cards and pictures 7 days from last use. A sweep every 10 minutes drops what's expired, then evicts the least recently used past the instance cap (1 GiB by default), skipping pinned entries. A blob shared by several entries goes with the last of them, its thumbnails with it. Active card and image requests retain their fetched bytes, so a response larger than the configured cache cap can still be opened or adopted even when admission immediately evicts its blob.
- **Settings** (`db/settings.ts`). The user key `sources` (`SourcePrefs`: each source on or off, its key's credential id, the last rating, the recently viewed list, at most 50) changes through `ChangeSourcePrefs`, `RecordRecentRemote` and `ClearRecentRemote` (`db/sourcePrefs.ts`, writer). The app key `sources.admin` holds the sources turned off for everyone and the cap. A source's API key is a `credentials` row named "<source> API key", bound to the source's origins and write-only like provider keys. A source starts on for every user (spec D1), and nothing is sent until its option is opened.
- **RPCs** (`@rp/shared/cardSources.ts`, `CardSourcesApi`): `ListCardSources` (admins also get the cache's cap and use), `SetCardSourceEnabled`, `SetCardSourceAdminDisabled` and `SetSourceCacheCap` (admins), `SetCardSourceKey`, `SetCardSourceRating`, `ClearSourceCache` (the user's entries and recent list), the four source calls, `ListRecentRemote` and `ClearRecentRemote`.
- **Settings → Card sources** (`features/cardSources/SourcesSettings.tsx`, in a "Cards" group): per source, **Show <name>** (disabled with the reason while an admin has it off), the admin's **Allow <name> on this server**, the API key when the source takes one, and **Clear cached cards**; for admins, the cache's use and its size limit.
- **Browsing** (phase 2; `features/cardSources/browse.tsx`). Each source the user has on is the last option of **Show** on home and in the sidebar's Characters view, after a divider (`separatorBefore` on `Select` and `Segmented` options), with `show=src.<id>` (`sideShow` in the sidebar). While it's shown, its results replace the user's cards: the local grid, pins, New card and the archived actions are not rendered, so nothing local mixes in, and Include personas stays in place, disabled with a reason. The query has URL keys of its own, `sq`, `stags`, `sxtags`, `sf` (filter values by id), `ssort` and `sreverse` (`side…` in the sidebar), so switching back finds the local search untouched. `useSourceBrowse` reads the source's capabilities once per session, applies the remembered rating, debounces typing by 300 ms, abandons a superseded search (which interrupts its upstream request), retries once after a rate limit's wait and appends pages as the sentinel nears the scrolling area. The search box searches the source; the source's sorts and its reversible direction replace the local ones; a **Filters** button (pressed while open, with the count of active filters) opens an inline panel generated from the capabilities (tags with suggestions from `SourceTags`, choices, ranges, toggles, text), and chips below show each active filter with its own × and Clear filters. Tiles reuse the card grid's face and size with the picture from the image route, a rating badge, and a context menu (Open, Inspect, Add to my cards, Open in a new browser tab, Open on <name>, Search <name> for cards by its creator); a click (and Open) opens the card's draft chat, Inspect its card page. Failures say what happened (can't reach, a rate-limit countdown, key or source off with a link to Settings, a bad answer), with Retry, also for a page that failed while scrolling. A folded **Recently viewed on <name>** row above the results lists the cards opened, with Clear. The phone's menu (`PhoneBar`) compares the page's own URL keys sorted, so a side-panel write that reorders them (choosing Characters after Back from a card page) no longer closes it.
- **The card page** (`RemoteCardPage.tsx`, route `/sources/$sourceId/cards/$remoteId`, tab kind `remote-card`): the cached card's picture, name, creator, tags, description and other fields folded, greeting and lorebook counts, and Open on <name>, saying whether it's in the user's cards, with **Start a chat** (the draft chat) and **Add to my cards** or, once theirs, **Open your card**. Opening it records it in the recently viewed list.
- **Adding a card** (phase 3, first part; spec §4.5 trigger 3). `AdoptRemoteCard` (`CardSourcesApi`; `CardSources.adopt`) takes the cached file (fetched again if it was evicted; the user asked), parses it in a format worker, appends the card's page on the source (else `<source>:<remoteId>`) to its CCv3 `source` unless it's there, writes its media under the media holds as an upload does, and calls the writer's `AdoptRemoteCard` (`db/cardOrigins.ts`): one transaction that runs `ImportFile`'s write for a new card (entity, upstream ref with the file name as `source_path` and the SHA-256 of the source's bytes as `source_hash`, revision 1 `origin = import`, the document, avatar and assets with their `media_refs`, the Character's Note as the card's first note) and inserts the `card_origins` row (`adopted`, the source's version and the file's hash). A card the user already has from there, live or archived, is answered with `existing` instead, so a second add from another tab or device makes no duplicate; an origin whose card went to the bin or was purged is dropped and the card is added again. The avatar's thumbnails are made after the commit. The client's `useAdoptRemote` shows "Added <name> to your cards." with Show it (the card's page), or "You have <name> already.", and reloads the library's queries. Tiles offer it in their context menu and flash once as the card becomes the user's.
- **Draft chats** (phase 3, second part; spec §4.2, §4.4, §4.5 trigger 1). `/sources/$sourceId/cards/$remoteId/chat` (`RemoteStartChatPage`, in `StartChatPage.tsx`; tab kind `chat.start`) is the pending chat as for any card, with the card `SourceCardForChat` reads from the source's cache (recorded as recently viewed): a `CardForChat` under the placeholder id `src:<sourceId>:<remoteId>` (`remoteEntityId`, `remoteOf` in `@rp/shared/cardSources.ts`; `cardTextOfDoc` in `db/cards.ts` reads the document as `loadCards` reads a revision, never offering its regex scripts), its picture the media id `srcimg:<sourceId>:<imageKey>`, which `mediaUrl` turns into the source's image route, so every avatar of the cast shows it. A card the user has from there already opens their own card's pending chat instead. The header has a badge naming the source beside "new"; Send's and Generate's hovers say they add the card (`PendingComposerContext.adds`); the character tab is the card editor (below), with "From <name> · not in your cards" and Add to my cards at the top of its header. On the first turn, `StartChat` (`api/chatSetup.ts`) reads each placeholder's card from the cache for its greetings, prepares its adoption (`CardSources.prepareAdoption`, as Add to my cards does), writes the media under the holds (`storingAdoptions`) and calls the writer's `AdoptAndStartChat` (`db/cardOrigins.ts`): one transaction with each card's `AdoptRemoteCard` write (or the user's card from there) and then `StartChat`'s, the placeholders replaced by the cards' ids, so the card and its chat both exist or neither does. A failure keeps the typed text, with "The card couldn't be added, so the message wasn't sent." The answer's `adopted` names each card; the client asks for the reply with the card's own id, shows "Added <name> to your cards." with Show it, and opens the saved chat in place, its panel on the card's tab.
- **Editing a source's card** (phase 3, third part; spec §4.3, §4.5 trigger 2). The draft chat's character tab is the same `CardPanel` as any card's, on an `EditorStore` whose ref id is the placeholder. `makeEditorHandlers` (`api/editor.ts`) is wrapped by `remoteAware`: a call whose `refId` (or `cardRefId`) is a placeholder goes to the user's card when they have it from there (`HeldRemoteCards`), so an editor left open on the placeholder carries on with their card; otherwise to `remoteHandlers`: `OpenEditor` answers the cached document (`CardSources.card`) as a ref at revision 0 that nothing references, with the user's drafts of it; the draft calls keep drafts under target kind `remote_card`, id `<sourceId>:<remoteId>`, with no base revision (`RemoteCardDrafts` lists them; Revert is `RevertRemoteDrafts`); history and notes are empty; and `CommitEditorDrafts` prepares the adoption as Add to my cards does and calls the writer's `AdoptAndCommitDrafts`: one transaction that adds the card (or takes the user's card from there) and commits the fields as its revision 2. Every adoption (Add to my cards, the first send, Save) moves the card's `remote_card` drafts to the new card's fields on its head revision (`moveDrafts`), so nothing typed is lost; the keepalive leaving-drafts route maps a placeholder the same way. Calls that need a saved card (pictures, gallery, forks) are not found. In the tab the portrait is a plain avatar, the card's actions are a disabled Export… ("Add <name> to your cards to export it."), Save's hovers say it adds the card (`SaveControls.adds`), the full-editor link and the lorebook's large editor aren't offered, and the merge notice waits for a revision (`MergeNotice` skips revision 0). The card tab family's `matches` takes a placeholder too. When the card becomes the user's, the tab swaps it in place (`PendingChat.swap`: their card as saved replaces the greeter, its greeting pick and macro draws kept) and the panel's URL follows (`card:<entityId>`).
- **Held cards** (spec §3.7). `HeldRemoteCards` (reader, `db/cardOrigins.ts`) takes a page's ids and version ids and answers the user's live cards among them, archived ones included, by `card_origins` (`UNIQUE (owner_user_id, source_id, remote_id)`), else by the version id against `entity_refs.source_hash` (`entity_refs_source_hash`) when it's a SHA-256: the same file imported from disk. `SourceSearch` and `SourceCard` mark each such summary with `held` (`entityId`, `refId`, `archived`, and `update`: below). Results are cached per page; `held` is worked out on every answer, so it's never stale. A held tile has a check badge over its portrait ("You have this card", "…, archived"), and a click opens the user's card as a click at home does (its latest chat, else its pending chat); its menu has Open your card and Show on <name>.
- **Updates** (phase 5; spec §3.8). `card_origins.remote_version` is the source's version the user has (the one added, or one taken since) and `seen_version` the newest the source reported, null until it reports another (baseline). They're recorded only from what the source just sent: a results page or a card's file fetched now (not one read from the cache, so an older page can't undo a newer version) goes through the writer's `NoteRemoteVersions` for the user's tracked cards among it (`HeldRemoteCards.tracked`: found by origin row, not by hash), and **Check for a newer version** (`CheckRemoteVersion`) asks the adapter's `versions` (cardex: the batch lookup) for one card. Nothing is checked in the background (D4). `held.update` and the library's `updateAvailable` (`source_update` in `refSelect`, one primary-key probe per card) say a newer version waits; a result tile shows "update available" over its portrait. `CardOrigin` (local; null when the source is off or unknown) feeds the card editor: `card-sources.update` in `editorNotices` (order 5, before the merge notice) shows **A newer version is on cardex** with **Review and merge** and **More choices…**, and Metadata → Sources has Check for a newer version (hover "Asks cardex whether <name> has changed since you added it."), saying what it found. Opening the update fetches the newer file through `GET /sources/held/<entityId>/file` (owner-scoped; the version in `x-remote-version`, the card's link back to its page in `x-source-link`, which the client sends as the import route's `link` for the preview, the staging and Replace; the cached file is used when it's that version, else fetched again), and it then goes where a newer file from disk goes: Review and merge stages it on the card's import line (`mode=merge`) and opens the merge review, after which the merge notice offers it until merged; More choices… opens the new-version dialog with the file already read (`NewVersionDialog`'s `source`: no file picker or Choose another file; titled "The newer <name> on cardex"), where Replace and Merge… work as for a file and **Add as a separate card** (`AddRemoteVersionAsCard`) adds the newer file as a card of its own in one writer transaction (`AdoptRemoteVersionAsCard`: `ImportFile`'s write with no origin row, the first card keeping it). Each of the three records the version as taken (`TakeRemoteVersion`), which ends the notice. `test/cardSources.test.ts` covers Check, the file route, staging, taking, the link back kept through preview, staging and Replace, Add as a separate card, cached and fresh pages and another user's refusals; `e2e/cardSourceUpdates.spec.ts` the notice, the dialog, Review and merge, Replace, Add as a separate card and the tile at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, with the layout audit. The fake archive's `publish(slug)` (`/__fake/publish?slug=`) makes a newer version under the same slug.
- **Source tracking** (schemafinal, owner 2026-11-16; **BASELINE CHANGED**, fresh deploy). `card_origins.recognized_by` is `adopted`, `recognized` or `linked`: a card linked to its archive entry (by the user, or an import's link hints) is a `linked` origin, which may have no version (`remote_version` may be empty only then), and is recognized as that entry; a later byte match of the card's file upgrades it to `recognized` with the version. `card_origins_remote` is no longer unique: after **Add as a separate card** (`AdoptRemoteVersionAsCard`) the new copy gets its own `adopted` origin at the version it was made from, and the original records that version as taken, so both cards track the source. `ignore_updates` (0/1) is set by `SetRemoteUpdatesIgnored` (writer and API, owner-scoped, returning the `CardOrigin`): while set, the card's `CardOrigin.newerVersion` is null, `HeldRemoteCards` reports no seen version and the library's `source_update` filter skips it. The client offers **Ignore future updates** on the update notice and as a checkbox under Metadata → Sources (`features/cardSources/updates.tsx`), each with its explanation. A linked card with no known version shows an update as soon as the source reports any version.
- **Only tried** (phase 6; spec §9 D3). The third criterion of Archive unused cards… (`tried` in `cardArchiveCriteria`, `@rp/shared/cardArchive.ts`, beside Never used and Not used in the last): a card added from a card source (its `card_origins` row) with at most N of the user's own messages in all the chats it was in (N = 1 by default, off by default). Criteria now see a card's facts (`ArchiveCardFacts`: added, last used, the source it came from, the user's messages) rather than two dates. `archiveCandidatesSql` stays one reader query: it joins the card's origin by its key and, only for a card that has one, counts the distinct slots of `writer = 'human'` versions among the versions the card took part in (`version_participants` by the card, then `versions`, `slots` and `chats` for the owner), unpurged; the writer's `ArchiveUnusedCards` checks again with the same query. A matching card's row in the dialog adds "N messages of yours". The criterion carries `forCardSources`: the dialog offers it only while a card source is on, labelled with their names ("Only tried: added from cardex, with at most"), with its own count beside it ("12 cards", one more query of the same kind). `test/cardArchive.test.ts` adds origins to half of its 5,000 cards and messages to three, checks the counts, the writer's recheck and another user's refusal, and the query plan's index searches; `e2e/cardSourceTried.spec.ts` covers the criterion's count, the archive and its absence with cardex off at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, with the layout audit.
- **The cardex adapter** (phase 4; `sources/cardex.ts`, `cardexAdapter({origin})`, https://cardex.zip by default): anonymous (`key: "none"`), 10 requests/s with a burst of 60 as cardex asks. `capabilitiesOf` maps v1's `/api/v1/capabilities` (filters by name, type, allowed values and optional labels) to the existing generic Filters panel, only offering criteria cardex still lists: Rating (`nsfw`: Safe, Everything, Mature only; cardex's default `include` is the rating default), Match (`mode`: Words for `fts`, Meaning for `semantic`), Tokens (`min_tokens`/`max_tokens`), Leave out forks, Site (`source`, several; `CARDEX_SITE_LABELS` in `@rp/shared/cardSources.ts`) Creator (`author`, `site/handle`), Search in (`fields`), Kind (Characters and lorebooks, Characters, Characters with a lorebook, Lorebooks; below, "Standalone lorebooks"), excluded sites, alternative-tag groups (`|` between alternatives, commas between required groups), included/excluded creator lists (comma-separated identities, backslash escapes), picture SHA-256, added/created date bounds, cover presence, deletion flags and Chub verified/recommended marks. Chub marks declare a generic toggle dependency on Site being Chub alone; the panel disables them with a reason otherwise and clears incompatible marks when the site selection changes. Tokens help reads the live minimum default (300 at verification). Sorts are Popular, Newest (reversed: `oldest`), Created (`created_desc`/`created_asc`), Name (`name`/`name_desc`), Tokens (`tokens_desc`/`tokens_asc`) and Best match (`relevance`, `popular` without words); with none chosen cardex's own default applies. `searchParams` sends only what was chosen, `kind=both` unless Kind says otherwise, at most 20 tags each way, and 48 a page; text mode pages by cardex's `next_cursor` (token `c:<cursor>`, or `s:<encoded sort/cursor>` after a temporary order substitution), semantic mode by number (`p:<n>`, no sort and no cursor, 240 results at most). A cursor cardex refuses (400 `invalid_cursor`: expired, or another query's) restarts the search from page 1 and sets the optional `SourcePage.reset`, so the client replaces its earlier pages instead of appending the restart; other misuse (400 `bad_request`) is an error. The guard (`sources/guard.ts`) reads up to 4 KiB of a 4xx refusal's body and passes its error code on as `SourceFailed.code`; a 401/403 from a source with no key is `refused` ("<source> doesn't allow downloading this card.", not a key problem). Summaries' paths (`/t/<sha256>.512.webp?v=1`, `/i/<sha256>.<ext>`, `/c/<slug>`) are resolved against the origin and anything off it is dropped; the creator's `site/handle` comes back as `creatorQuery`, which "Search for cards by its creator" uses. A card is the batch lookup for its slug (summary and `file_sha256`) and then `/api/v1/download/<sha256>?mode=mirrored`, the card PNG with its portrait; a CHARX original, whose mirrored and self-contained files answer 404, falls back to `mode=json`, which every card has (V2/V3 JSON with the `extensions.cardex` block, no portrait). A summary's `download_modes` (the modes that answer 200, in the order mirrored, self-contained, json, original; a CHARX card's are json and original) picks the best of mirrored and json with no 404 first (`downloadModeOf`); an empty list is a plain refusal (`refused`) and nothing is tried; a list with neither is a bad response. Responses cardex cached from before it listed them (up to 30 minutes) lack the field, so the 404 fallback stays; the file name comes from `Content-Disposition`. Batches (`batchUrl`) are sorted, without duplicates, joined by `%2C` (cardex's canonical form, else a 308) and chunked by 100. `cardSourceSetup` decides what `main.ts` registers from `FAKE_CARD_SOURCE` alone, since the development instance runs a production build: unset, cardex (production's units); `off`, none; any other value, the fake. Server tests that spawn `main.ts` and the browser tests' `main.ts` runs set `off`. `test/cardex.test.ts` checks the mappings and the adapter against the fake; no test contacts cardex.
- **Archive token estimates (review-cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** Opening a card also reads its v1 detail envelope for `card.token_counts`, preserving valid nonnegative per-field and greeting counts with their tokenizer name. Inspect annotates its existing definition headings with these archive estimates. The same envelope’s `earlier_origins[].listing` supplies earlier-listing links beside the existing archive link, retaining only URLs on the archive origin. The imported document still comes from the bounded PNG/JSON file, not the envelope’s definition text.
- **Filter suggestions (review-cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** The existing tag field and capability-declared creator text fields share inline suggestion buttons, counts, More and Retry. `SourceSuggestions` carries an opaque cursor through the registry adapter, using `/tags` and `/search/authors`; expired cursors replace the suggestions, and changing text discards pending and previous results. Creator-list fields escape comma-containing identities. Suggestions stay behind source consent, the per-user cache and the same network guards. Older adapters retain first-page tag suggestions through `tags`.
- **Conditional reads (review-cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** `sources/httpCache.ts` wraps the guarded HTTP interface with ETag validation. Responses with validators retain their capped bodies and headers in the same per-user, source-scoped, size-limited disk cache for up to 30 days since use, so expired parsed pages, cards and pictures can send `If-None-Match` and reuse bytes on 304. Normal parsed-cache lifetimes still apply, and explicit version/file refreshes validate immediately. Keys separate response kinds, credentials and request headers. Clearing the source cache clears validators too; a changed validator replaces its body and a non-cacheable reply removes the old response. Validation owns the retained bytes before starting the network request, so eviction or an explicit cache clear during a 304 cannot leave the caller with a missing blob. All validation still passes the host guard, rate limiter and request coalescer.
- **Result counts (review-cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** The first text-search page (and a cursor restart) also reads `/search/count` with the same filters. Counts are exact until the archive caps or times out its count; the existing Show count appends `+` for that lower bound (for example `100,000+`). Later pages retain that count. Meaning search retains its bounded result count.
- **Regional files (review-cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** HTTP 451 is `region_unavailable`, shown as “This card is not available in your region.” with the existing Retry action. It remains distinct from an unreadable response or a refused download.
- **Live verification (cardexlive, 2026-11-12).** Manual, anonymous checks used only v1, inspecting keys/types/lengths/hashes, never card definitions. Search summaries, batch version lookup, files, pictures and invalid-cursor errors match the adapter. The earlier verification found the advertised docs URL unavailable and upstream errors in name-with-text and ascending-token sorting. The follow-up removes unconditional workarounds: every first page tries the requested order. Only a 500/502/503/504 from a nondefault sort can trigger one substitute request, using the ordinary direction for a reversed sort or best match/popularity otherwise. A temporary notice says which order was used. A 429 or a 503 with Retry-After uses the source limiter and one delayed retry of the requested order first; a second 503 still waits its delay before a substitute, while a second 429 remains rate limited. Network errors, invalid queries, default-order failures and later-page failures never change order. Substitute cursors retain their actual sort through paging and expiry; pages carrying a substitute notice bypass the parsed-page cache so reload tries the requested sort again.
