Pending content is drawn with quiet bars where text isn't known, and the branch name when it has one; `LoadingProgress` ("Loading branches… 120 of 600", a polite status) sits on the breadcrumbs' line, or the open chat's branches' header, so nothing moves when it goes; the chat lists render before the cards (`WatchShellCards` still waits for the full snapshot). Tests: `test/shellProgress.test.ts` (pending rows and exact endpoints against a full read, current first, name-only search, complete-chat readiness, thread membership/counts, account isolation and mutations between parts), `e2e/branchProgress.spec.ts` (a chat made cold as an import leaves it: server stopped, its stored summaries removed, started again; mid-pass and complete at 1440/390 in both themes with layout audits and unmoved rows; a pending branch opened, two-tab mutations, restart and chat deletion). The nested Start/Undo browser regression waits for the undone row to disappear before measuring its existing one-second quiet window; request-count limits are unchanged.

Invalidation (which stored summaries a write leaves stale, unchanged from importperf except where marked): a reply or append reaches only the fork whose tip moved (another tip move also the children whose split it moves); a swipe, selection, edit or hide of a slot the forks whose shown path holds it; a fork's override or event the forks whose lineage holds that fork up to its sequence; a fork's creation, deletion or restore that fork and its children; an insertion, moved slot, chat-wide event or event changed in place every fork of the chat; card bin/purge/archive every summary of the owner (`shell_user_stamps`); a write on another connection every fork of the chat at the next noted write (new: before, until a read recomputed them); a format change every summary. `test/summaryValidity.test.ts` covers storing after another fork's write, settlement moving only reached forks' stamps, and an unnoted move staling the chat, besides the earlier rules.

The left panel's place comes from the URL alone (owner, 2026-10-31: "tied to the path"): search params `character` (a card's chats), `forks` (one chat's forks) and `side=characters` (the thumbnail grid), listed in `features/characters/sidebarSearch.ts` and read by `useShellNavigation` (`shellData.tsx`); nothing is kept in memory or storage. With neither scope the panel shows no crumbs (home, settings, a chat opened from All chats); otherwise All chats › display name, or › chat name (the branch shown is marked in the list below instead). Crumbs and the Chats/Characters switch navigate to the same path with new params (the switch replaces the history entry), so back/forward, reload and links agree and the chat and right panel stay. Routes can declare `retainSearch` in the route registry (`routes.tsx`), installed as TanStack's `retainSearchParams` middleware; the chat, request-inspector and start-chat screens retain the sidebar params, so moving around a chat keeps the panel. Routes also declare `fill` (TanStack `staticData`): `CenterPage` renders a screen whose matched route says so to fill the height and scroll inside itself (the chat, the card, card-source and group start-chat screens, the picture viewer), so the composer stays at the bottom however short the chat; it replaced a path list that left out the card-source start-chat page (composerbottom1, `e2e/composerAnchor.spec.ts`), and navigation that changes the scope sets the keys to `undefined` (`sidebarCleared`) explicitly. Picks in the panel carry its scope; the phone sheet closes on picks (a counter) and on other navigation, not on the sidebar params. Rows are fork rows only. **A chat's branches** (owner, 2026-11-01): a chat row (title, its current fork's last message, its date) ends in "⑂ 12" when it has more than one branch (`BranchesButton`), which scopes the panel to the chat without opening anything, as a Groups tile and the branch menu's "Show in the left panel" do; the crumbs go back. Scoped to a chat, the panel lists its branches, named and pinned ones first (`peers`), then the rest (`other`), each by its last message, newest first (the server's `sectionRows`); each row is the branch's label (`forkLabel`), "opens here" beside the one the chat opens on, its last message's date and time, and its preview; the one shown is marked; a pick opens it and the panel stays. **The open chat's branches** sit at the panel's foot below whatever it lists (`OpenChatBranches`, registered in the `sidebar.foot` slot by the characters feature) while the chat has two or more and the panel isn't already its list: the same rows, a pick opening the branch without changing the list or the crumbs, collapsed or expanded per device (`localStorage` `rp.openChatBranches.<user>`), its header's ⤢ making them the panel's list. On a phone it's the same inside the sheet, which a pick closes (`e2e/branchList.spec.ts` at 1440 and 390). Character tiles select all three parts and open the character's last-speaking line at its speaking slot; an unused character opens an unsaved greeting with its definitions. Cast names offer the same character navigation. Header cast chips select that character's right-panel tab in the current chat. Ordinary chat rows change the middle, retaining the right tab when applicable and falling back to This chat for an unrelated character tab (implementation proposal). Groups tiles also scope the left panel to the selected chat's forks, clearing any previous character scope and grid mode. Home and grid tiles fill their grid row with their last line at the bottom, so a row's tiles match whatever lines they have. The row of the fork open in the middle is marked (`aria-current`, accent border), so a chat opened from All chats, which has no crumbs, still shows where it is. The sidebar's header row holds the app name and the image toggle, an eye icon (struck through while images are blurred or hidden) beside its settings popover. The header has no Start a chat control or picker (nostartchat, 2026-11-04). On a phone, picking a character closes the left navigation drawer through the selection counter; a new chat still opens its character card sheet. That modal sheet is portalled within the main content landmark, retaining the landmark while hiding the covered chat content from assistive technology; focus trapping and the sheet’s Close control remain in place. New chats remain available through Characters (also in the phone navigation drawer): unused cards open their pending chat, used cards open their chats; the character tab's New chat and library chat action also open the pending chat. Card grids, lists and pickers omit bare character versions, including their accessible names; labelled version fields in editors and the card definition retain them. Without accounts the footer's account link reads Account rather than the single user's handle, `local`; Browser recovery's button reads **Unsaved text**. Tests: `e2e/shellNavigation.spec.ts` (no row links, switch width, tile rows, URL-tied crumbs through back/forward/reload/links and the branch-menu entry). Ordinary rows resolve both URL and account-remembered right tabs before checking the destination cast, including navigation from home. Explicit card-detail pages retain search over every associated fork and show 50 rows at a time, with Load more; row metadata includes the original start date, cast, message count and excerpt.

The shell uses `chat_pins` for account-wide chat pins and user-scoped `settings` key `shell.pinsCollapsed` for the pins fold. `chats.current_fork_id` determines the shell's current row; its tip is mirrored by `active_leaf_slot_id`. Opening a fork is the client's view alone. Chatting in a fork (a send, swipe, continue, or import advancing its leaf) makes it current.

**Stable shell fork identities (U01, 2026-10-28).** The shell enumerates every live owned `forks` record, including interior checkpoints, empty forks and several forks at the same tip. Rows and React keys use the actual fork id. The slot query materializes the live fork views once and enumerates their chain segments with indexed depth ranges. An indexed check for overrides per view lets untouched chats read base selections and deletion flags directly; chats with overrides resolve selections, replacements and deletion in each fork's bounded lineage. Event visibility uses the same lineage helpers. State folds positional events on that path and registered branch-owned state last. Deleted messages contribute neither excerpts, counts nor speaking activity; a surviving endpoint supplies the bounded excerpt. Names, creation dates, pins and current status come from the fork record. Character activity is rebuilt from that fork's selected, surviving messages, and keeps the fork's own cast and departure classifications. Work scales with the visible fork paths and applicable event metadata, in reader workers.

`SetChatPin` pins the owned live chat in `chat_pins` (one row per user/chat), independently of branch pins; legacy `leaf`/`forkId` payload fields are ignored. `SetForkPinned` (`PinFork` publicly) only changes the live owned branch's `forks.pinned_at`. Shell rows expose `chatPinned` separately from branch `pinned`. Global Pinned uses ordinary chat rows with current-branch portraits/title and opens that branch; branch pins never enter it. The chat's branch lists order pinned, unpinned named, then other branches, each newest last message first (`pinnedBranches`, `peers`, `other`). Pin tooltips explain the local or global action. The baseline defines the independent chat-pin key directly; no existing pins are migrated. Writes run in writer-worker transactions. Tests cover independent pin/unpin semantics, current-branch global rows and ordering. Home pins, Groups tiles, character clicks and left-list rows navigate with an explicit `fork` URL parameter, alongside any message/leaf location; same-tip peers therefore retain their own state and drafts when opened. The character feature and shell remain registered through `features/index.ts`. `SetHomePinsCollapsed` keeps its account-owned writer transaction. Tests: `shellForkIdentity.test.ts` covers checkpoints, peers, empty paths, selection-specific excerpts, cast/departures, deletion and branch pin isolation; existing shell navigation, edge and scale tests remain. It also covers user-played turns across chained card swaps: activity checks the played identities before and through the swaps, since existing messages keep their original speakers, and a later change to model-written turns resumes activity only at that position. `e2e/shellForkIdentity.spec.ts` covers exact fork URLs through pins, Groups and character navigation at desktop and phone sizes in both themes.

The right panel retains Cast, This chat, Lorebooks, Notes, Summaries, plus character-card tabs (`panel=card:<entity id>`) with definition, Edit card and the existing variant refs. No origin or lines-and-forks section is added. On phones the panels are independent sheets; the left sheet keeps its breadcrumbs above the scrolling rows. Character selection closes the left sheet even when the middle chat id stays the same.

**RPCs.** Every one acts as the caller, and another user's ids are `NotFound` (each has a cross-user probe in the isolation matrix, §4).
- **Chats:** `ListChats` (most recent first, by last message, else creation; paged by `(time, id)`; with `entityId`, only chats with recorded version participation for the card, those with a message first, paged by `(has a message, time, id)` with the cursor's `empty`, and `NotFound` unless the card is the user's; with `search`, only the chats whose title, or a card in which by label or in-chat name, has the text, matched with `LIKE` with its wildcards escaped, through the cards that match and `card_chat_membership`), `CreateChat` (a title only, for now), `GetChat`, `RenameChat`, `DeleteChat`. `RenameChat` is an owner-scoped `RenameChats` writer transaction: whitespace is normalized, a blank name restores the cast-based title, and an imported ST timestamp is retained. It marks `title_source = user` so re-import does not replace the choice, advances the chat row version, and publishes `Chat` to open tabs. The header title opens the rename dialog; bin entries and deletion toasts read the new title.
- **Groups:** `ListChatGroups` (`ChatGroups` in the readers, `db/chatSetupReads.ts`, `groupsOf`). There's no group entity: a group (`ChatGroup` in `@rp/shared/chatSetupApi.ts`) is the chats with the same readable name (`chatName` in `@rp/shared/chatName.ts`, which the client's `chatTitle.ts` uses too: an ST group chat's "<group>: <date>" title gives the group's name, a chat made here its title, by default its characters' names joined with " & ", or one character's name and the day it started, the persona left out as the header leaves it out: `titleFor` in `db/chatSetupWrites.ts`) and the same set of characters the user doesn't play (the cast folded at each chat's active leaf: joins and leaves on that path, less the latest applicable `played_by_me.set`; the persona tag alone does not say who the user plays), two or more; chats in the bin don't count. Each has its members (in the latest chat's join order, with in-chat name, label and avatar), its count, its last message and its latest chat (the one with the latest message, else the newest), the groups by that. One owner-scoped reader operation loads each active path's cast events (indexed by chat), card metadata and purged references, then uses the shared `foldState` and `withoutPurged` rules before grouping. Superseded events, deleted slots and unselected-version events are excluded as in `StateEventsAt`; message text is never loaded. `test/chatGroups.test.ts` covers replacements, leaves, sibling branches, the realistic ST folder's three groups and a 2-second budget at 5,000 chats with ten-message active paths. `ListGroupChats` is the group a chat is in with its chats, latest message first (`Chat` rows; NotFound when it's in none). `RenameGroup` reads that group then renames its chats in one writer transaction, publishing `Chat` for each. Chats renamed independently between the read and write keep their new titles. The grouping key stays the readable name plus current cast: renaming a single chat separates it into its own group tile (or joins an existing matching tile); the header dialog explains the effect and offers to rename the whole group. The group page has a Rename group action. These grouping semantics are a proposal, avoiding a separate group identity and migration.
- **Characters:** `ListCardUsage` (`CardUsage` in the readers, `db/chatSetupReads.ts`): every live card that isn't a persona, with its metadata, and its distinct live chats with recorded version participation (group chats included): their count, last message and latest chat. Empty cast configuration establishes no use. One query seeks `version_participants` by card through `card_chat_membership`, then looks up the chats; `CROSS JOIN` preserves that order. The 1,000-card/5,000-chat synthetic regression covers cold and warm reads. The shell's own `CardUsage` projection counts fork paths and uses the card's last speaking turn, as described above.
- **Reading:** `ReadPath`, below, and `ListVersions` for the version picker.
- **Writing:**
  - `SendMessage` and `Generate` add a message under a fork's tip (`forkId`; the current fork if none is named), which makes that fork current: the user's text, or a model reply that streams. Without `branch` the parent must be the fork's tip (`LeafMoved` otherwise); with it, any slot, which starts a fork there (DESIGN §3.2; `AppendMessage`, §3.8). `SendMessage` takes the speaker (Send as X); `Generate` the speaker (Generate X) and a one-turn `direction`, stored on that reply (DESIGN §2.2). Onto a message whose selected version is still generating, both are queued instead (the send queue, below), and return `Queued` rather than `Posted`. Both take an optional `composer`, the draft the text was taken from (its id and session): it's committed in the send's transaction, posted or queued, only if it still holds exactly that text (§3.10), and both return that draft as the send left it, with `recovered`.
  - `SwitchBranch` finds the fork through another of the alternates at a message, by index, for the client to open (below). `CreateFork` is "Branch from here"; `NameFork`, `PinFork` and `ListForks` are §3.8's operations.
  - `Regenerate` accepts any message, including a human-written or impersonated turn. It is a swipe: a new model version of a slot, selected and streamed, with the speaker and the `direction` of the version it replaces (DESIGN §2.2, guidance on swipes), unless a `direction` is given with it (the guidance editor's box, §12), an empty one meaning none; later turns never see a direction. A speakerless old version uses another version's speaker or the slot's first speaker; on the user side it falls back to the first card played at that position. An optional model choice is ownership-checked and stored on the new version in the same transaction; normal generation already records its model during assembly. `Version.model` resolves the stored model id to “connection · model” for headers and picker previews, or null for older/imported versions without a recorded model. `EditVersion` saves an edit as a new version "edited from" its source, and `WriteVersion` is "write your own". Both record the message's speaker on the new version, as a swipe does: an edit its source's, a written version the shown version's, so a message keeps its speaker whichever of its versions is live. All three take the fork they're done in (`forkId`, the current one if none is named), select the new version there only and make it current, and check the slot's row version as that fork shows it (`StaleWrite`), through the writer's `AddSelectedVersion`. A path entry carries the message's `side` as the context reads it when its speaker isn't one of the cast: its first version's (a human's is the user's, unless a greeting), deleted or not, so which versions are live never changes it. It also carries that first version's speaker (`firstSpeakerEntityId`), whom the message shows as when no live version names one.
  - **Message editors' drafts.** The text typed into an edit (`version_edit`, keyed by the version edited) or into "write your own version" (`scratchpad`, keyed by the slot) is a server draft like a summary's: `SaveMessageDraft` (thin over `SaveDraft`), `DiscardMessageDraft` (over `ClearDraft`; an edit's goes back to the saved text as a state of its history, which outlives saves, §3.10; a written version's text goes to the recovered texts), `GetMessageDraft` (a reopened edit's resting draft, for its history), and `MessageDrafts`, a chat's drafts with text (`ListMessageDrafts` in the reader). `EditVersion`, `WriteVersion` and `AmendVersion` take the `draft` the text came from (id and session) and commit it in the same transaction, only if it holds exactly that text (`drafts.ts` `commit`); `EditVersion` and `AmendVersion` take the thinking field's `reasoningDraft` the same way (§12 "Thinking in a message's edit").
  - **Message history** (`messageHistory.test.ts`). `VersionAmendments` reads all earlier saved texts of an owned, live, unpurged human-written version from `version_history`, newest first. `RestoreVersionAmendment` resolves an amendment belonging to that version and calls the existing `AmendVersion` with the viewed fork and expected version row count; it preserves the current text in history, copies when another fork shares the version, and publishes the updated slot. Generated-source edits still use `EditVersion`, creating a new version. `MessageDraftHistory` and `RestoreMessageDraft` use the common owner-checked draft store for version edits, scratchpads and queue edits. The shared message controller uses these APIs for all three targets; text typed during a history restore stays in the box and its next save and browser copy use the returned draft row version. Message and summary history controls read up to 1,001 states (the 1,000 retained patches plus their starting text), and show an empty history before the first draft save. A restore is another undoable history step, with the draft's id and row version checked; commit/discard still ends that session's history.
  - `SelectVersion` (in a fork, against the version the tab saw it show, §3.8), and `AmendVersion` for a finished user-written version (`NotAmendable` otherwise; DESIGN §3.1), in the fork named (`forkId`): in place, or when another fork shows it, as a copy in this fork only (§3.8), which the tab then reads again. `ListVersions` and `SetVersionFlags` take the fork too. A version's `rowVersion` is one more than the number of times it was amended, counted from `version_history`, since `versions` has no `row_version` column.
  - `StopGeneration` stops one generation and returns the version as saved. A Stop that loses the race with the natural finish, or comes twice, gets the finished version too; NotFound means it isn't the user's or is in the bin.
  - `DeleteMessage` and `DeleteVersion` (in a fork, `forkId`, else the fork through them) and `DeleteFork`: to the bin (§3.11). Generations under what was deleted are stopped. `DeleteMessages` deletes several messages of one fork as one change, and `RestoreBinItems` is its Undo (§3.11 "Several messages at once").
- **`SubscribeChat`:** a stream of event batches, below.

**Windows of a path** (`ReadPath`, `db/reads.ts`). The client never loads a whole chat: it reads windows of up to 500 slots and pages from cursors.
- `Bottom` and `Older` read the window ending at a slot by chain segment, as `GetPath` does (§3.8): the cost is the window.
- `Newer` walks down from a slot the client already has, towards the leaf. A run of only children needs no check; at the first branch, the rest of the window is the leaf's ancestors, found in one walk up from the leaf, which costs its distance from the leaf once per page. Walking up once per branch instead cost 7 s for a page of 60 branch points 99,000 messages from the leaf (5 s at 70,000, 0.7 s at 10,000); one walk costs 150, 110 and 30 ms, and a page without a branch about 10 ms (the 100,000-message fixture, bundled workers, a loaded host). `pathWalks` counts the walks up, and a test checks that a page through 20 branches takes one. The slot isn't checked against the path (that would cost its distance from the leaf on every page): a slot of the chat that isn't on it walks down its own branch.
- A read names a fork (`forkId`; the current fork when null), whose tip is the path's leaf, or a leaf of its own (`leafSlotId`, as `useForks` scans a path). The window says which fork it read (`forkId`, null for a read by leaf).
- `Around` opens at a slot (deep links, DESIGN §10.1), about half the window above it. It checks that the slot is on the path, a walk from the leaf to it, once per open. A slot on another path opens the fork through it that was current most recently instead (`forkThrough`), or with none, the path through it following the newest reply at each step (through a message deleted on its own, never into a deleted branch); `forkId` and `leafSlotId` say which.
- Deleted messages are walked through but not returned; the cursors (`older`, `newer`) still move on.

**Branches** (DESIGN §3.2). Each path entry carries an optional `branchName` (read from the fork that starts at that alternate), plus `branchCount` and `branchIndex`: its slot and the siblings in its chat that a path can reach (live, or deleted on its own with replies left in place, what `Around` follows), and its place among them by creation. Reachability walks arbitrary chains of individually deleted placeholders by the parent index, stopping at a live descendant or a deleted subtree root. The subtree marker survives purge, so restoring a separately deleted descendant cannot expose that subtree. Live siblings need no descendant walk. Two counts per entry, by the parent's index (first messages by chat and depth), so a window costs the number of siblings more, not the chat's length. The indexes are named (`INDEXED BY`): before schemaclean, without statistics SQLite took the now-removed lane index, scanning every slot per entry, which made a 60-slot window of the 100,000-message perf fixture take 5 s instead of 0.3 ms; `test/graph.test.ts` checks the plan. `SwitchBranch`, in the writer, takes the sibling at the index asked for and the fork through it (§3.8): the one current most recently, so the alternate's own line opens, at its tip. It moves nothing and makes nothing current; the client opens the fork it names. The composer stays with each fork: switching carries no text (DESIGN §6.2). `test/branches.test.ts`. A slot's `branchName` is the name the user gave (or took off) the fork it starts (`PathEntry.startsForkId`: the slot that fork appended first, at the message it was made at), else its own label (an ST import's, or a continuation's name from before forks), else that fork's name; `PathEntry.forkId` is the fork that appended it. `NameFork` names a fork (blank clears it), advances its first message's row version and publishes that `Slot`; a message that starts no fork (one that continues its parent's line) can't be named in unit 2. `ListBranches` lists reachable siblings with names and message previews in the same order as `SwitchBranch`. All are owner-scoped. The header's branch control (below) lists every fork by these names and renames and deletes them with the existing bin/Undo flow. Deletion switches to the preceding surviving sibling (the next for the first), fences older window reads, and clears the deleted slot/leaf from the URL while keeping its panel. If no sibling remains it follows the writer's surviving active path. This also works from a window in the middle of a long chat. `test/naming.test.ts`, the isolation matrix and `e2e/naming.spec.ts` cover naming, grouping, branch deletion and restoration at both widths.
- Which branch to land on below the sibling is the newest reply at each step, as for a deep link; `slots.last_visited_at` isn't kept, so a sub-branch visited last isn't remembered [P].
- A message deleted on its own at a fork counts as a branch while its replies stay; on its own path, its replies show without the switcher for that fork.

**Live updates** (`chat/ChatHub.ts`). Every committed change is published to the chat's subscribers, from any tab of the user:
- `Slot` (a message added, or its selection or versions changed, as one fork shows it: `shownForkId`; a tab showing another fork reads the slot again as its own fork shows it), `Version` (a generation ended, an amend, or a star or picker flag; with `forkId` when it's as one fork shows it, which tabs on another fork leave; an amend that gave the fork a copy also publishes that fork's `Slot`), `Chat` (the leaf or last message moved), `Reload` (something in the chat was deleted or restored), `Deleted` (the chat went to the bin; it comes after the `Version` events of the generations that stopped, and the subscription ends with it), `Cache` (the cache-warmth estimate, §15). The chat is checked once the subscriber is registered, so a chat deleted in between refuses the subscription rather than leaving it open. A client showing a deleted chat goes back to the chat list.
- Streamed text comes as `Delta { versionId, offset, text, replace? }`, reasoning as `Reasoning` and reply-section panel text as `Section` (below, "Reply sections") with the same fields, and an agent reply's steps as `Steps { versionId, steps }` ("Agent rollouts"), never as whole messages (CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §5). `replace`: regex scripts rewrote the text so far, and the text from `offset` on is `text` (§12, "Live rewrites"). Their separate offsets let a client tell a repeat from a gap; batching coalesces each kind separately.
- Each subscriber gets a chat's events in batches at most every 16 ms. Consecutive deltas of a version are merged, and any other event is a barrier, so order holds.
- **No events are lost between loading and subscribing.** Each subscription starts with `Hello`, which carries the text and reasoning so far of every version generating in the chat, taken in the same synchronous step that registers the subscriber. A client subscribes first, then reads its windows, and applies events idempotently (by id, row version and offset). A second `Hello` means the socket reconnected: the client reads its windows again. This replaces the per-chat sequence number EFFECT.md §5 proposed: nothing needs replaying, since state comes from reads and live text from `Hello`.
- Publishing never blocks: events are queued per chat, and one timer sends the batches. Each subscriber may fall 512 batches behind (about eight seconds of a busy chat; a stalled socket or a throttled tab), then it starts over: its backlog is dropped and it gets a fresh `Hello`, which makes the client read its windows again, as after a reconnect.

**Generation** (`chat/Generations.ts`). One fiber per generating version, in the service's scope, any number at once and several under one slot.
- The **generator** (`chat/Generator.ts`) is an interface: given a chat position, a stream of text strings and separate reasoning chunks. The server's is the context assembler in front of the provider layer (`chat/ContextGenerator.ts`, §15). A server built without one (only tests) refuses `Generate` and `Regenerate` with `GenerationUnavailable` before anything is written.
- Text and reasoning accumulate separately on the main thread and are published as deltas. Every 2 seconds both are saved (`SaveGeneration`, status still `generating`), so a crash keeps most of it. A 500 ms tick merged into the stream (`SAVE_TICK`, resume1) saves text left unsaved when the deltas stall, so the 2 s holds when the provider pauses too.
- **How a generation ends:** complete; `stopped` by the user, with its text; `interrupted` when the server stops (the scope closes and the fiber's exit handler saves it); `failed` with the generator's error class and message, and the text so far (DESIGN §3.1). Continue creates a new version with the old text and streams onto its end (DESIGN §7.5); the original stays in the picker.
- **Length cutoffs** (DESIGN §3.1; backlog U08): a provider `length` stop on a reply request is `ProviderError(length_cutoff)`, so the request, rollout and retained version fail with an explicit output-limit cause. Text and reasoning already received remain on that version, including when display streaming is off (the reply strategy flushes its buffer before propagating the failure). Failed versions stay out of ordinary context, including while selected. Continue uses their partial text through the existing prefill flow and creates a new version; the failed original remains. Other request purposes retain their existing length handling, including the summarizer’s truncated-output marker. The soft judge’s mark-only behavior is unchanged. `test/continueReasoning.test.ts` covers both streaming modes, exclusion at the mock provider and Continue; `e2e/backlogBindingsCutoff.spec.ts` covers the failure cause and Continue at 1440 and 390 in both themes.
- At startup, versions a crashed process left `generating` become `interrupted` (`InterruptGenerations`).
- **Nothing blocks the event loop.** Text arrives in chunks, publishing is a queue push, and saving is a message to the writer worker. `test/chats.test.ts` runs six streams at 300 tokens a second and checks the event-loop monitor's maximum stays under 100 ms on this shared host.

**Chats from cards, speakers and settings** (`@rp/shared/chatSetupApi.ts`, `api/chatSetup.ts`, `db/chatSetupWrites.ts`, `db/chatSetupReads.ts`, `db/cards.ts`; DESIGN §2.1, §2.2, §3.5).
- **Cards as chats see them.** A card is read from its upstream ref, or its oldest variant without one: the in-chat name and greetings from the document, the library label, and the persona folder (the `persona` tag). A chat's own `card.binding` isn't applied here; the context assembler resolves that. `ListCards` lists the live ones, `SetPersona` moves one in or out of the persona folder, and `GetCardForChat` returns its ordinary greetings (`first_mes`, then the alternates, empty ones left out), group-only greetings separately, and the fields its macros read.
- **Chats are made on the first turn, never before** (DESIGN §2.1, PLAN phase 2). Opening a card shows its greeting with nothing written (`/cards/$entityId/chat`), so greeting-only chats can't pile up, and `chats.status = 'pending'` isn't used. `StartChat` writes, in one transaction: the chat; `participant.join` for each card and the persona at the start, and `played_by_me.set` for the persona; each card's chosen greeting as its own message in card order, with every alternate greeting as a version of that message (origin `greeting`, `macro_mode = template`, `greeting_ref` with the card and its index), the one picked selected; then the first turn, the user's message (the client then asks for the reply, as after any send) or a reply with its direction. The title is the one asked for (a group's new chat), else the cast's names, or one name and the date, never just the first character's name.
- **A new chat of a group** (`/groups/$chatId/new`, `StartGroupChatPage` in `StartChatPage.tsx`, named by any of the group's chats) is the same pending chat with the group's characters (`ListGroupChats`): each member greets in order, with its card's greetings to pick from independently. Like ST (`getGroupChat` and `getFirstCharacterMessage` in `group-chats.js`), each starts at a random nonempty greeting and cards without greetings are skipped. The pending list scrolls while the composer remains visible. `StartChat.greeters` keeps each preview's selected index and frozen macros; without that payload, the server still greets with every card in order (random choices for a group unless its first greeting was explicitly requested, the requested greeting for a single card). **Playing as** (the Cast tab's You play) picks the persona as for a card; **Reply from** (in the Cast tab, with two characters or more) picks who answers a human-written first message (the first character by default); Generate writes the selected **Writing as** speaker. The first send is `StartChat` with the pending cast (initially every member) and the group's full name as the title (the same unrestricted string as `CreateChat`), so the chat is one of the group's (`ChatGroup`: the same readable name and characters) and the tile and page count it (`e2e/chatSetup.spec.ts`).
- **The pending chat is the chat page** (pendingchat, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §2.1, owner: it looks and works like any other chat). Its state is a `PendingChat` (`chat/pendingChat.ts`: greeters, greeting picks, persona, who replies first, the fallback note), a subscribable store whose `view()` is a `ChatView` with no chat and the pending cast (persona and characters as participants, as `StartChat` will write them). `StartChatPage.tsx` renders the saved chat's parts around it: the `chatColumns` slot, the header's frame (`PendingChatHeader` in `ChatHeader.tsx`: the cast's faces, the name the chat is saved under, `pendingTitle` mirroring the server's `titleFor`, a "new" badge with its tooltip, and the `pendingChatHeaderActions` slot, where the chat feature registers the panel button; no pin, branches or ⋯), the message list's column (padding and gap) with each greeting as a message row, its alternates stepped at its end as a message's versions, the composer's column, and `ChatSidePanel` itself, resizable, its tab in the URL and remembered as in a saved chat (`usePanel`, now in `ChatPanels.tsx`). The panel takes either a session's content or `{ pending, view }` (`SidePanelContent`); a descriptor's optional `pending` component is its body before the first send (`PendingPanelProps`), and a tab without one stays in its place and says it's available once the chat is saved, its tooltip too. Pending bodies: Cast (`PendingCastTab`: You play with the pending persona switch, the characters with ⋯ Edit the card here, the card's actions with no session, Remove from chat for all but the last, then `pendingCastSections`: Reply from with two or more characters and the saved chat's Add characters grid, `CastAdd` over a `CastAddTarget` that joins the pending chat), the character family (`PendingCharacterTab`: the card editor and actions, the entry from the library lists, `pendingCardInfo.ts`; Fork for this chat and Use another version need the saved chat and are left out, `ChatCardActionProps.session` is null), Model (its picker, the account's), Prompt preset (its picker and the account's preset in the same editor column as a saved chat's, `PendingPresetTab` in `PresetTab.tsx`, which brings its own `PresetWorkspace` since the pending page has no chat providers; presetempty1, 2026-11-17: picker-only looked broken), Interface and Snippets (the same). The phone bar gives way to the header on pending routes too. The first send replaces the URL with the saved chat's, keeping the panel's tab, and opens it in place: after `StartChat` (and the reply's `Generate`) the same action reads the path's bottom window and the cast at its leaf and seeds them (`seedChat` in `session.ts`, with the chat `StartChat` returned), so the new `ChatSession` starts on them, `loading` false, and its first read replaces them with no skeleton or placeholder title in between; a failed read only leaves the seed out. The pending page also loads the chat page's code ahead (`chatPageLoader.ts`), and the `/chats/$chatId` route renders it directly once loaded, so the route's `ChatSkeleton` fallback doesn't show either. Tests: `e2e/pendingChatPanel.spec.ts` (resizing, the same tabs before and after the first send, a tab that waits, no skeleton or placeholder title added during the first send (a MutationObserver), adding a character before the first send).
- **The first request of a chat not sent yet** (cardex3, 2026-11-12; DESIGN §2.1, owner: "Make sure this doesn't cause anything to be sent to inference providers"). `PreviewChat` (`DraftPreviewApi` in `inspectorApi.ts`, its own handler layer `makeDraftPreviewHandlers` in `api/chatSetup.ts`) takes what `StartChat` takes (`StartChatInput`, `@rp/shared/chatStart.ts`) and `replier`, who answers a sent message. It draws the greetings as `StartChat` does (`drawGreeters`, shared by both: the preview's frozen values kept, the rest drawn), only each greeter's picked greeting, the one a request reads (a card with a thousand greetings costs a preview one), checks that every card it names is the caller's, reads a source's card with `preparePreview` (the page's cached file only, using a non-mutating cache peek; a missing file refuses and asks to reopen the card; no portrait fetching or cache timestamp writes), and asks the reader for `AssembleDraftChat`. Without a model it builds nothing (the send would refuse first); otherwise it builds the request with the assembler over `db/draftSources.ts`: the database sources for everything the library holds (cards, notes, lorebooks, the preset, the model, the global scripts), with the chat's own parts stood in for under the id `draft`: `StartChat`'s events (summarization settings, the joins, the persona), each greeting as picked, the typed message and owner-checked image facts (Send), the target after them (Send: the replier; Generate: the speaker, with guidance as its direction), and a source's card's document and notes under its placeholder id. Its estimate is the next context's (`estimateOf`, shared with `CacheWarmth`), its request is the inspector's (`inspectWire`, `contextMessages`), counted with the local tokenizers (`textDisplay`); message sources link nowhere. Nothing is written, no generation starts, and no provider is asked anything, not even a token count with counting set to the provider: the path has no provider call, and the reader worker has no network. `test/draftPreview.test.ts` checks that a preview sends nothing to a recording provider, makes no chat, and equals the messages the same chat's first reply then sends (Send and Generate); `cardSources.test.ts` does the same for a source's card, with the archive asked nothing more. Client: `features/chat/draftRequest.tsx`. `useDraftPreview` keeps one request out at a time (a change while one is out is asked for when it returns, so a slow build never piles reads ahead of the send) and asks again, never while the first send is on its way, 400 ms after the input (the greeters with their drawn values, persona, speaker, replier, text, guidance) or the account's selections/settings or library revision signal changes (`defaultsAtom`, shared with the model/preset chips); Send's request with text in the box, Generate's with an empty box or with guidance on. The next-reply strip's `pending.context` control (`DraftContextChip`) shows "~1.2k tokens", its popover the size, the model's window and reply reserve, the tokenizer note, a plain warning that random choices, the clock and automatic decisions can change the request, and **View request**, which opens `DraftRequestDialog` (`request=first` in the URL) with `DraftRequestView` from `ContextPage.tsx` (the inspector's message list and not-sent list; no usage or continuity). `e2e/draftRequest.spec.ts` covers the chip, popover, dialog, URL and zero provider requests at 1440 and 390 in light and dark, with the layout audit.
- **Group-only greetings** (2026-10-30). The pending chat has Add characters and Remove from chat in its Cast tab before the first send, including re-adding an original group member. Cast, persona and greeting picks update together against the latest state, so a delayed Add character read cannot restore an older selection. Adding a second card also exposes the group header and Reply from picker. `GetCardForChat` returns ordinary greetings and CCv3 `groupGreetings` separately, with empty entries omitted. The shared scoped `greetingSources` registry (`@rp/shared/greetings.ts`) registers `greetings.ordinary` and `greetings.group-only`; plugins can replace or disable either source. The preview and API macro freezing use `offeredGreetings`; the API passes the resolved option text, card indexes and frozen macros over the private writer RPC, so scoped source additions, overrides and disablement survive source and bundled worker boundaries without re-evaluating a separate registry. The worker-owned `StartChat` transaction checks ownership and stores that snapshot. Ordinary greetings stay available, and group-only greetings join them only with more than one distinct character card, excluding the selected persona. Each selected group-only greeting says “group greeting”. Removing a second character (or changing persona so only one character remains) resets an unavailable selection to the card's first available ordinary greeting and shows a visible note. The chosen greeting is stored as a normal template greeting version, with its frozen macros and original card index; all offered greetings become versions. Group-only greetings are never stored as available versions in a one-character new chat. ST group-chat import is unchanged. Unit/server tests cover availability, fallback, persona exclusion, duplicate ids, and source override/disable/restoration through both source and bundled workers; `e2e/groupGreetings.spec.ts` exercises adding/removing a character, a delayed card read, choosing the first reply speaker and storing a chosen group greeting at 1440 and 390 pixels in light and dark, plus re-adding an original group member.
- **Macros in display** (`features/chat/macros.ts`) go through `expand()` (§10), which decides from the stored macro mode. A greeting resolves against the cast at its own position (`GetCast` after its parent): `{{user}}` follows the persona picked until the first send, and a later change of who the user plays doesn't rewrite it. Its speaker card's fields (`{{description}}` and the like) come from the card as the preview had them. Its random and time macros are frozen as the preview drew them: `StartChat` stores each greeting's drawn values in `frozen_macros`, and display passes them back. The server freezes every greeting itself (`chat/macros.ts`), with the names the preview used: it keeps what the preview drew for the picked greeting where the macros could have drawn it, and draws everything else, so no greeting is left volatile and a card's greeting count is no limit. The bounds are one expansion's (at most 10,000 values and 16,000,000 characters, above what its work limit lets it draw), so whatever a preview drew is accepted, so a greeting reads the same tomorrow (DESIGN §5.6).
- **Single persona selection** (DESIGN §2.2, owner 2026-10-29). The `played_by_me.set.entities` and `playedByMe` arrays retain their public types, but the graph and ST-import writers persist only the last ID after ownership validation. The state fold also takes only the last ID, including in supplied initial state; cast assembly and prompt-name reads independently select one. `PlayedByMe` accepts an empty array to clear the selection. New-chat creation and the `Persona` control write zero or one ID; fork reads use the same fold, so selection stays independent by path and fork. Historical message speakers stay unchanged. No migration is needed for empty databases.

- **The cast** (`GetCast`) folds participants, presence, played-by-me, card bindings, role projection, the attached lorebooks (`lorebooks`, those on; `listedLorebooks`, every book attached and not removed, on or off, in the order first attached), the card books the chat turned off and its lorebook placement setting at the viewed position. Cards resolve as assembly does, including in-chat names. Model and preset normally follow account settings. `Cast.model`, `Cast.preset` and `Cast.presetLocked` expose per-chat locks; `ChangeCast` writes binding or unbind events at the displayed leaf and publishes `State` (§15).
- **Text typed while the first send makes the chat** goes along to the new chat's composer (`composerCarry.ts`).
- **Message headers on phones** (`Message.tsx`) put the full wrapping speaker name on its own row, with time, number and streaming status below. Desktop headers retain their compact row.
- **Text typed in a chat not made yet** (`StartChatPage.tsx`) has a private `user_field` server draft (`userDraft.tsx`), under `pending-chat:<card>` per user or `pending-group-chat:<characters>:<name>` per group. Each keystroke also writes its complete draft-addressed browser copy synchronously to `localStorage` (`typedBackup.ts`, `rp.pendingTyped:<user>:<key>`) and asynchronously to IndexedDB, so reloading immediately after a keystroke cannot race both saves. The draft store reconciles both before showing the composer, replays the original bases, removes only acknowledged copies, and rebases later typing on each acknowledgement. Legacy `pendingChat` copies and timestamp-only localStorage text remain readable; `newerText` compares their times with the server's, including ended drafts' `updatedAt`. Modern copies use server versions, with no cross-clock comparison. **Deletion wins** (owner, 2026-11-02): clearing retains an empty server draft with its update time; discard/commit retains the ended row. `drafts.cleared_version` / `Draft.clearedVersion` records the last deletion's row version, retained even through subsequent typing. Copies based before that deletion (or legacy copies without a base) cannot automatically reopen the text. New typing after an explicit reopen or the editor's own Cancel carries `observedDeletion` (the observed draft id and row version) beside its original text base; the writer checks it against the current deletion watermark. It never changes the copy's original drafting base before that text is acknowledged. A later deletion, or an observation of another draft, still wins. Opening an editor or pending composer checks `deletedSince`; a freshly opened blank message/insertion editor matches its displayed starting text against the resting draft before its first save, recording that deletion separately from its text base (offline replay keeps its original base and observation); stale browser copies remain available for explicit inspection in Browser recovery. The writer's `saveOnto` also enforces the barrier for all draft kinds, including keepalive and Retry saving: stale submitted text goes to recovered texts and the deletion stays in place. A keystroke typed from an observed deletion's version wins over that older tombstone, even with a slow browser clock. Text not yet observed on another device cannot overrule its deletion by wall-clock time. Moving drafts to a fork keeps the original field's deletion watermark unchanged too, so late typing still lands on the original. A normal commit keeps its deletion watermark unchanged (a form save or a posted message is not a deliberate deletion): its session still protects the submitted text, and separately typed `next` text keeps its existing handoff semantics; text typed during an editor's own Cancel keeps its original base and is re-filed with that separately observed cancellation before saving anew; `next` cannot bypass a later manual deletion. `test/userDraft.test.ts`, `test/userDrafts.test.ts` and `e2e/pendingDeletion.spec.ts` cover old copies, ended/empty rows, later keystrokes, synchronous-only reload recovery and independent browser contexts with a clock a year ahead. While the first send is out, the pending draft holds the submitted text and what's typed since, as a failed send leaves them. A successful first send acknowledges only its submitted text; any further text is atomically re-filed as a `pendingChat` handoff carrying the saved `chatId` (`composerCarry.ts`) before navigation. Browser recovery links it to that chat. `StartChat` returns the destination composer's base from its creation transaction; the handoff retains that base rather than adopting a later read. An unversioned legacy handoff cannot automatically cross a known deletion. Opening its composer atomically replaces an eligible handoff with a normal draft-addressed `composer` copy; refusal or reload keeps a recoverable copy. Message (including insertion), summary and composer recovery check known barriers before replay or fallback display, so a failed write after a successful read cannot redisplay deleted text. Fresh message/write/queue/insertion editors read their resting draft before enabling input, with a retry when opening fails. Their very first durable copy therefore already carries the post-Cancel base, without depending on the save debounce or page-exit read. Recovery reads resting drafts omitted by the active-only list and shows a copy that passes the deletion precheck before its replay write finishes, keeping its original base; an acknowledgement replaces that text only if no later typing changed it. Compound-form fallback reconciles cleared inputs without discarding other pending keystrokes, retaining the raw copy for explicit recovery. Both card and group flows use this handoff; chat creation remains lazy.
- **Pending composers** (`StartChatPage.tsx`) use the same compact input row as the saved chat: **Generate** and a Send icon (`ui/Tooltip.tsx` `SquareIconButton`), with the accessible names **Generate X**, **Send as X** (or **Send** without a persona) and the send tooltip. Both share `ui/AutoGrowTextarea.tsx` and `composerKeys.ts`: the input grows with its text and width changes; The account’s Enter sends choice controls plain Enter; Shift+Enter inserts a newline and Ctrl/Cmd+Enter always submits. Generate takes the text as the first turn's direction only with guidance on (below); otherwise it leaves the text in the box. With guidance on, Send gives way to **Generate X** as the primary action, Enter submits it, and the text leaves the box as a sent message does (a failure puts it back); only text typed meanwhile goes along to the new chat's composer. Its label truncates to the available width for long speaker names, retaining the full accessible name. Since composer2 (2026-11-01) it's the chat composer's box (`ComposerBox`): the input on its own row, and under it the speaker chip (a portrait alone on phones) at the start and the **Guidance** icon toggle, Write (the saved composer's: a spark and the word, ghost, primary with guidance on; an icon on phones, `PendingComposerContext.compact`) and Send at the end. Since pendingchat (2026-11-02) the draft's Undo / history sits after the speaker chip, where the saved composer has its earlier text, its notices in the box's header; the `notes` placement renders above the composer as the saved chat's composer notes do (the no-model note in the same `chat-column` wrapper); and a `strip` placement under the box holds the next-reply strip's model and preset chips (`pending.model`, `pending.preset`: `ModelChip` and `PresetChip` with no session). The speaker chip always shows the selected speaker and opens the same cast-only picker: the selected persona plus this card or the group's cards. **Playing as** independently picks `{{user}}` from the library. Both Send and Generate write the chip's speaker; guidance changes only the writer. `StartChat` stores that speaker in the fork's composer choice in its creation transaction, so the saved composer keeps it. First-turn creation and browser-copy handoff remain lazy. The speaker, guidance and action contributions are registered through `pendingComposerControls` from the chat feature (a fourth placement, `notes`, is a row above the composer, for what to know before sending), with keyboard invocation resolving the same registration as the buttons. `e2e/pendingChatHandoff.spec.ts` covers both widths and both pending routes, keyboard/touch submission, growth, tooltip and browser restoration.
- **The composer** (`Composer.tsx`; fcomposer 2026-10-31, redesigned in composer2 2026-11-01 after the owner found a 230 px input on a 4K screen, squeezed by the controls on its row, and the guidance-edit bar cut off from the box by the strip). Top to bottom, in the chat column (below): queued messages (`queue`; each one's Edit and Withdraw at the end of one row, not stretched across the column), directly above **the box** (`ComposerBox`, shared with the pending composer). The box is one border holding, in order, its header (`banner`, the replay/restored/recovered notices; hidden while empty), the growing input **on a row of its own, the box's whole width** (at least 85% of the column at 1440 and wider; in practice all of it less 10 px of padding), what's attached, and one **control row**: at its start the speaker chip (portrait and name; the portrait alone in the compact layout) and up to three recent-speaker avatars (only where the composer is at least 760 px wide; the speaker picker lists them first anyway), earlier text (History) and attach; at its right end the **Guidance** switch (an icon toggle with `role="switch"`, its explanation in its tooltip and in the input's `aria-describedby`), **Generate** and Send. Generate shows a spark and one word, "Generate" ("New version" while a reply's guidance is edited; the spark alone in the compact layout), ghost, or primary with guidance on; its accessible name stays **Generate <name>** and its tooltip says whose turn the model writes, since the name is on the speaker chip at the row's start. The row wraps rather than narrowing the text. Under the box, after any notice or error, the **next-reply strip** (`nextReplyStrip.tsx`, a group named "Next reply"): small chips for the model, the prompt preset, the cache and, in groups, **Next**, and `?` (keyboard shortcuts, an icon drawn centred in its round chip) at its end. The order follows time: the messages, what's queued to post after them, the box and what describes it, then the reply that comes after what's typed (who writes it, with which model and preset). Each chip opens a popover of full-width rows that wrap rather than truncate, the same at every width (the strip scrolls sideways on phones). On a phone a chip keeps its whole text (wider, past 20 rem, it's cut with an ellipsis, its whole text in its name and tooltip), and the row fades at an edge with more chips past it (`StripRow`, `data-more-before`/`data-more-after`). While the chat, the account's selections or the cast load, the model and preset chips are a disabled "…", the speaker chip says "…" and Generate says "Generate …", so no placeholder ("Choose a model", "Default (built-in)", "You", "Reply") shows before the real value. The model chip waits only for the model list to be read (`useModelChoiceList`): a model missing from it is looked for once more (one added in another tab), then the chip says "Model not found" and still opens to choose one. Generate has a tooltip explaining that the model writes the selected speaker's turn, including a persona's. Send with text sends as that speaker, then asks the character **Next** names; with no text it asks for that character's reply alone (the accessible name and tooltip say “<name> replies”); with no one to reply (every character muted) Send posts the message and asks for nothing. Its cached history follows the session's path revision: Slot and Version events, Reload and reconnects invalidate it even when the tip stays unchanged or the changed turn is outside the loaded window. Providers without a limiter refuse bounded calls before sending. Reported usage consumes the budget; missing or estimated output exhausts it, and bounded failures never retry automatically. `GetVersionMetrics` must have all counts reported before another bounded reply can start. Starting a reply reserves its reply allowance before any asynchronous hook or RPC, so a lost acknowledgement cannot replenish it; a failed acknowledgement also prevents continuing a token-bounded run.
