The tab's own checks can't see a change it hasn't been told of yet, so the server decides. An Auto turn's `Generate` carries `auto: { token }`: null for the turn the user's own click starts (Start, Continue), else the token the run's last turn handed back in its `Posted` result (`auto.token`). A turn that may not start fails with `AutoRefused { reason }` and nothing is sent: `changed` (the branch), `settings` (the configuration), `replayed` (not the token last handed back: a lost acknowledgement asked again, a duplicate), `expired` (the server knows no such run: it restarted). The row says why in plain words (`stopText`: "the chat changed", "a setting, preset, model or library entry changed", "the server restarted"); Continue starts a new run. A `Generate` without `auto` is exactly what it was: no token asked for, none returned.
    - **What the token is.** `<run id>.<nonce>`: a handle, with no state in it. The state is the run's row in `auto_guards`, a TEMP table on the writer's connection (nothing in the database file, no baseline change): user, chat, branch, the current token, the reply its last turn wrote (slot, version), and `broken` with the operation that broke it. The token says which run and which turn; the row says whether anything changed. A writer restart drops every run.
    - **How a change is seen.** TEMP triggers on the writer's connection, as `db/summaryValidity.ts` has, note each row write in `auto_touches`, and only while the chat has a live run. `transaction` (`db/tx.ts`) settles the notes at the end of every write transaction, inside it: each live run the notes reach, and whose own turn didn't write them, is marked broken for good. What reaches a branch: an override, an event or a `forks` row the branch wrote itself, and a message or reply queued in it (it posts later inside the reply's own transaction) (rows a parent writes later are invisible to it, DESIGN §3.2); a message on its path, in the version the branch shows there (the path is walked from the tip down to the shallowest touched message, once, and only for a foreign write); an inserted message anywhere; and everything the notes can't place (an event without a branch, one changed in place, a deleted message row, threads, a summary changed outside a summary job), which reaches every branch of the chat. A chat with threads is `wide`: its branches read each other, so every touch of the chat reaches its runs. Stars and picker-hides never count. The configuration is user-wide: `settings` of the app and the user (not a device's), a connection's or model's sent columns, a library entry made, deleted or moved to another revision, a revision rewritten, and text being typed into an entry (`entity_field` drafts, which a request reads). Any of them breaks every live run, with `settings`.
    - **Own effects (review-orchestr2).** Ownership requires a known internal reply operation as well as the current reply or its rollout ancestry. Merely naming a version, rollout or job is insufficient: user edits, thinking visibility, swipes, Resume and workshop operations are external. `FinishGeneration` is own only on successful completion. Own output, presence, notes, send-message posts and decisions retain authorization; settings, credentials and plugin-data writes always break it, including in the same transaction. A summary job exempts only summary rows and summary overrides, through `CompleteSummary`; a user rewrite is external. Image-token samples carry the transient run token internally so the run's own calibration survives; outside calibration ends it because it can change context fitting.
    - **Coverage.** In addition to the graph, overrides, state events, threads, queue and library heads, TEMP triggers watch attachments, amendment history and new alternatives (macro amendment/swipe counts), merge joins and copied messages, summary inputs/parents/choices/revisions, entity visibility, ref source names, credentials, plugin data, image-token facts and sent user fields. App/user settings include decision, tool, plugin, regex, model and account configuration. Chat titles are watched conservatively for extensions. Cache-prefix warmth, usage/cost ledgers, drafts for unsent messages and ordinary last-used timestamps remain bookkeeping. Plugin activation is observed through its settings transaction; private plugin storage is watched because registered parts can read it.
    - **Registered request parts (review-orchestr2).** Plugin activation and restoration happen before their pin transactions. Every core registry now exposes a monotonic mutation revision, including disablement and scope restoration; state-module stacks do too. The plugin host watches its request registries, all provider/execution registries and the assembly/state-module declarations. `chat/autoConfiguration.ts` hashes only these revisions and watched-scope identity; local per-request registries are excluded. The main thread supplies that digest internally at admission; the writer freezes it in the TEMP run row. Admission and final dispatch compare the current digest. A new, replaced, disabled or restored part therefore ends the old authorization before a pin write, including an activation that is later rolled back. A mutable custom request registry without a revision fails closed for Auto. Ordinary sends do not inspect the digest. Dispatch checks both sides of the writer RPC and again synchronously before controlled fetch; no new part can slip into that asynchronous gap. No public payload, persisted schema or model-facing bytes change.
    - **Dispatch boundary.** `SendOrQueue` checks and rotates the handle in the placeholder transaction. `StartRollout` and `StartDecisionRollout` reject an already broken turn before its request record. The transient `GenerationRequest.autoGuard` is provided to the reply fiber through `AutoRequestGuard`, inherited by decision calls and every tool round. `AuthorizeAutoRequest` runs on the writer after provider preparation, before invoking the provider adapter, and again immediately before controlled fetch after cache waits. No live storage read contributes new request data after that check. A missing handle, including after a writer restart or replacement Start, refuses; ordinary sends have no handle and do not call this operation. Summary jobs retain their independent scheduling authorization.
    - **Cost and lifetime.** Every write transaction settles once at its end; attribution adds no separate probe or autocommit writes. An idle transaction pays one empty-touch-table probe. A partial index on live chat ids avoids scanning unrelated runs in per-row triggers. An indexed expiry sweep runs inside settlement at most once a minute when writes occur; checks also enforce the 24-hour inactivity limit directly. No persisted schema object changes. TEMP writes cannot recursively fire the main-table capture triggers or summary-validity triggers.
    - **Conservative stops.** Configuration/library changes currently invalidate all live runs, including unrelated entries and accounts. A chat with threads invalidates every run in that chat on a watched chat write: the guard does not attempt to prove which parallel stretch each speaker could read. Ordinary sibling message, edit and hide activity remains independent outside threaded chats. Import publication conservatively ends every run in its chat, including new imported paths beside a retained local continuation; the TEMP imported-slot/version triggers cover versions inserted before slots. `st_import_stage` changes are bookkeeping and leave runs valid. All supported mutations run on the single writer; approved full-trust code that bypasses the storage/provider contracts remains outside this guarantee.
    - **The other stamps.** `chats.shell_stamp` (fork summaries), `job/planperf2`'s `chats.lcm_stamp` and `job/reimport2`'s import stamp each answer "did anything a cached result read change?" per chat, in the database file, with baseline triggers. This guard answers "did anything change that this run didn't cause?" per branch and per writer, which needs who wrote it; a stamp can't say. It depends on none of them. What could be shared later is the noting: one set of TEMP touch triggers feeding both `settleSummaries` and `settleAutoRuns` (they watch nearly the same tables), and the two per-chat stamps could become one with a column mask. The attribution stays the guard's own.
    - **Tests.** `server/test/autoGuard.test.ts` plays a tab with delayed notifications: older edits, last-reply thinking visibility, token chaining/replay, sibling isolation, merge, Undo, queued input, a real writer restart and a change after the request record but before dispatch. `autoGuardStorage.test.ts` checks the source-table matrix, immutable/fork-scoped summary edits, own-operation boundaries, settings in an own transaction, expiry, token confinement and bookkeeping. `sendPresence.test.ts` keeps an Auto run through its own presence-tool round and send-message declarations. `autoGuardParity.test.ts` emits the ordinary request catalogue for comparison with master; `autoGuardCost.test.ts` is the separate slow writer measurement. Client `autoRun` tests retain token propagation and the stop texts; the browser Auto/decision/presence gates retain their width/theme layout checks.
  - **Repeated Continue round.** A Continue with nothing held returns the current chat queue, so a second tab keeps seeing the running round and its controls; the writer still starts the next reply at most once.
  - **Round replacement events.** A send or single reply that removes a round returns the changed queue from `SendOrQueue`, including an empty one. The API publishes it to every tab even when the new turn has no round of its own.
  - **Withdrawing a queued action.** Its following round entries are cancelled in the same transaction, up to the next user action in that fork’s queue. A later queued action and its own round remain intact. No reply from the withdrawn action can start when the current generation finishes.
  - **Stopping an older reply.** Only the active round is held. A queued replacement action and the round following it post normally when that older reply stops or fails; its own reply can then hold its own remaining round.
  - **Persisted choices** (`speaker.ts`, `@rp/shared/composerApi.ts`): migration `0036_composer_choice` adds nullable speaker and reply-from card ids to the draft row, with owner triggers, foreign keys and purge cleanup; the baseline's `no_replies` (0/1) holds Next's No one. `GetComposerChoice` reads by draft id; `SetComposerChoice` updates only named fields in the writer transaction without changing the text's row version/history. The API publishes `ChatEvent.ComposerChoice` to all tabs. Choices travel with a moving draft; branch copies and reopening restore them. The client rereads on reconnect, serializes rapid picks and rereads after writes to catch a newer tab's event. Send is disabled until the current draft's choices and turn order are loaded and its choice is saved; typing depends only on the text draft being ready, so a slow choice read never blocks writing. With no saved choice, the speaker defaults to the first played card.
  - **Speaker search** (`SpeakerSwitcher.tsx`, `ui/Popover.tsx`, `ui/Tabs.tsx`): at the composer, the speaker chip opens one popover with two sections and one search field over both: **Speak as**, the chat's cast only, the persona and the cards in the chat (owner 2026-10-28), the current speaker ticked, and **Your persona**, the persona folder (`ListCards` cards marked persona), the current persona ticked. Picking a persona is the Cast tab's `ChangeCast` `Persona` change; if the speaker was the old persona, it becomes the new one. A pending chat's composer (`StartChatPage.tsx`) has the same two sections: it opens on the account default persona, and picking one sets only that pending chat's persona (`PendingChat.setPersona`). A search that matches no one in the chat says “No one in this chat is called ‘Zara’ · Add to chat”, the button opening the Cast tab (adding a card stays explicit there, PHASE1 §2). The recent-speaker avatars beside the chip are the cast's too. Search is focused on open, filters by name or library label without case/accent sensitivity, and puts recent speakers then the cast first for an empty query. Up/Down, Home/End and Enter move through both sections as one list and pick; Escape closes. Without the persona section (the insertion editor's speaker) it's the cast alone, and TanStack Virtual renders only visible rows plus the active option, so hundreds of cards remain reachable with keyboard and scrolling. The search (and the persona control's tabs) stay above the scrolling list on phones. Picking a speaker never changes the cast or the played set. With `persona`, the same switcher is the Cast tab's persona control, from the library: Members / Personas / All cards, opening on Personas every time; a non-persona card not in the chat says "adds to this chat" (it joins), while a persona-folder card says nothing, since it takes the place of the persona played until then. In-chat names and avatars take precedence over library values. Pointer activation of any tab, including the remembered active tab, returns focus to search through the stock Tabs callback; keyboard navigation retains focus on the tabs.
  - **Tests:** `e2e/composerSpeaker.spec.ts` covers Auto's pick (cards with talkativeness 1 and 0, a name in the box or the tip, the last speaker not answering itself), its refresh when the tip is deleted and restored, a saved one-reply pick, empty Send, writing a persona's turn, reload and live cross-tab speaker sharing, search and keyboard control, a one-card chat, and a phone with 240 additional cards, a fully readable named phone action, and a deep link whose last character turn is beyond the loaded window, and typing while a saved-choice request is held. `e2e/nextNoOne.spec.ts` covers No one: sends with no reply (a name in the box too), reload and a second tab, a pick's one reply and the return to No one, an empty Send, Auto again, a one-character chat, and the disabled plain chip of a chat with no character (`LAYOUT_AUDIT_NOONE_ONLY=1` audits its menu and pill); `test/replyPolicy.test.ts` its plan under every reply order. `test/composerChoice.test.ts` covers draft movement/copy, independent branch resets and conditional consumption, and No one through a pick, a send and a new branch; `test/isolation.test.ts` covers both choice RPCs. Deletion/restoration of earlier turns inside and outside the loaded window, the resulting Send/empty Send speaker, and remembered-tab pointer focus with keyboard tab navigation are covered at both widths. Client `test/session.test.ts` guards path invalidation without token or read-replay invalidation. Client `test/speaker.test.ts` covers writes crossing branch switches and concurrent tab events.
- **The Cast tab** (`CastTab.tsx`, DESIGN §2.1, §3.5, §4; ST's group and character panels): at the top, the persona row ("You play", the persona's portrait and name, which opens its tab, and **Switch**, the persona control `PersonaSwitch.tsx`, shared with This chat and the persona's tab) [owner question 9]: picking a card sets `played_by_me = [card]` from the leaf on, joining it first if it isn't in the chat, and a persona-folder card played until then leaves the chat (it isn't one of the characters): the persona's definitions swap, as in ST, and the history is untouched, its earlier messages keeping its name in the request (§15 "`roles.projection`", owner 2026-10-28). It's one `ChangeCast` `Persona` change: the server reads the cast at the leaf and writes the join, `played_by_me.set` and leaves with `AddStateEvents`, one transaction, so a failure leaves the persona as it was (`test/chatSetup.test.ts`). Then the characters: everyone in the chat at the leaf shown but the cards the user plays (which are in the persona row, and which the count "N characters" leaves out). Each is one row: the portrait (opening the portrait viewer, §14.5a), the name (opening their tab in the panel, where the card is edited), a version only when two characters share a name, the badges "writing…", "Muted" and "in the bin", and two icon buttons: **Mute** (`Presence`; labelled "Mute <name>" or, muted, "Unmute <name>", with a volume icon crossed out and the row dimmed) and **Speak now** (▶, the model writes their turn now: `Generate` for them without a direction). There are no usage counts in the Cast. **Muting** (DESIGN §3.5) is the existing `presence.set` event [owner question 8]: a muted character is never picked to reply automatically (Next's Auto, the default speaker the assembler picks when a version has none), but Speak now, Write as and an explicit Next pick still make it speak (Next lists muted characters as "Muted: replies only when picked", `replyFaces`, never as Auto's pick), and its card and notes stay in the context. The header counts "N muted". The UI says nothing of presence. Everything else is under the row's ⋯, a menu whose action components stay mounted so their dialogs stay open: **Write as** (the composer's speaker, and the cursor in the composer), **Edit the card here** (their tab), the `chatCardActions` contributions (**Full editor**, **Fork for this chat**, **Use another version**, a plugin's), **Use as my persona** (as the persona control) and **Remove from chat** (`Leave`). Under the cast, **One reply at a time** (`OneReplySection` in `ReplyOrder.tsx`, the `cast.one-reply` entry of `castSections`, beside Who replies when space permits, otherwise wrapped below; owner 2026-11-03) is a switch with its explanation beside it, off by default: on, each user action gets one reply instead of a round (`ChangeCast` `ReplySingle`, a `reply.single` event at the leaf shown; ST groups import without one, so off). **Who replies** (`ReplyOrder.tsx`, the `cast.reply-order` entry of `castSections`; importreport 2026-11-02): a `Select` of the reply policies that have a label (ST's four, and a plugin's), each explained beside it, the current one the chat's `reply.order` at the leaf shown, a choice written as `ChangeCast` `ReplyOrder` (one `reply.order` event, as other cast changes are). An ST group's chats bring its `activation_strategy` (`StGroup.replyOrder`; ST reads it as `Number(...)`, so a numeric string counts, and an unknown value is natural order) as a `reply.order` event at the chat's start when it isn't natural order, and a re-import writes one when it changed (`ChatState.replyOrder`). **Reply settings layout** (owner, 2026-11-03): `ReplyOrderSection` places the labelled select and the independently registered `cast.one-reply` section in a `flex-wrap` row with token gaps, centring the switch on the select via bottom alignment and a control-height wrapper; this row removes the switch’s usual top text-alignment margin. The select is capped to the available width. When both do not fit, the switch wraps left-aligned below. `CastTab` excludes `cast.one-reply` from its outer outlet because the reply-order section renders that registry entry in the row. `e2e/replyRounds.spec.ts` measures same-row alignment in a widened 1440px panel and wrapping at 390px in both themes; `LAYOUT_AUDIT_REPLY_SETTINGS_ONLY=1` audits Cast at 390/1024/1440. **Add characters** (`CastAdd.tsx`, owner 2026-11-01; ST's group "Add Members" list) is a section under the cast, the `cast.add-characters` entry of the `castSections` slot (`presentation.tsx`), so a plugin can replace or remove it or add a section beside it. Its title is a disclosure button with a tooltip; it's collapsed until opened, and open or closed is remembered per account in this browser (`castAddState.ts`, `rp.castAdd.open.<user>`); the grid is made only once it's open. Open, it's the left panel's character grid: the search ("Find a character to add", by name or version), the compact filter (All / With chats / Never used / Favourites / Personas, each with its count; no Groups) and sort with its direction (`CardBrowseBar`, `useCardBrowse("cast")`, its own sort remembered), kept in view at the top of the panel while the grid scrolls under them, and the tiles, adding columns as the panel widens (`auto-fill` columns of at least 7rem, 8.5rem from `@3xl`): the first 60, then "Show 60 more of N" (another search or filter starts again from 60). On the synthetic scale dataset (422 characters) at load 28–57, opening it took 0.6 s at 1440 and 1.0 s at 390 with pages, against 2.1 s and 3.7 s with every tile; two adds in a row 2.8–3.0 s against 7.4–24 s. A click on a tile opens its upstream ref in the existing center-column editor (`PresetWorkspace`), with Close returning to the viewed chat. A separate full-width "Add to chat" footer inside the tile’s shared border and background, below its details and separated by a divider, joins the character (`ChangeCast` `Join` at the leaf shown); adds clicked in a row go one after another, the button reading "Adding…" meanwhile. The section stays open. A line below the grid (`role="status"`) says who joined last, or why an add failed, without shifting its buttons. The grid shares the search field’s horizontal insets and 8 px row spacing; no blank feedback row is reserved above it. Add-character tiles omit the character-version subtitle. Cast members and the selected persona keep a disabled "In this chat" footer control with a hover/focus explanation saying why; their tile still opens the editor. The separate action uses the shared UI Button for mouse, touch and keyboard, without nesting buttons. Any card can join as a character (DESIGN §2.2): the persona folder's cards are under the filter's Personas (personalists), the one the user plays marked "You play", and Include personas at the end of the bar mixes them in among the characters, marked (personaswitch). The speaker switcher's **Add to chat** opens the Cast tab and asks for the section (`requestCastAdd`): it opens, scrolls into view and focuses its search; a request no section takes within 10 s is dropped (`e2e/castAdd.spec.ts` at 1440 and 390). One line at the bottom says changes apply from the latest message on, on this branch. `ListChatCards` reads, per card, at the leaf shown: its single library ref, "used by N chats" for it (§14.2; the Cast no longer shows it), whether the chat pins a `revision` or uses the `default` head, and the definition the next request reads, resolved by the assembler's rules (`cardInChat`: a pinned revision, else the upstream head). A card that isn't the user's live card (another user's, or binned) is `NotFound`, as a missing one; the tab asks only for live cards. It reads again at a new leaf and after any library change.
- **Card versions under names** (smallui1, 2026-11-14; audit item 016, CARD-FORKS surface 5, DESIGN §4's subtitle = `character_version`). Where a chat lists cards, a card's version (`CastCard.subtitle`, the version of the revision the chat uses) is a muted line under its name (`CardVersion.tsx`, `data-card-version`, full text on hover): the Cast tab's persona row, character rows and pending rows, and the composer's Speak as / Your persona rows and the persona picker's rows (`SpeakerSwitcher.tsx`). A card without a version shows no line. The cast tab strip and Next choices use the compact display name plus standard version; same-named cast tabs keep their text at phone widths, scrolling within the existing strip rather than collapsing to indistinguishable portraits; Next retains it for the chosen reply. Header portrait actions include the version in their accessible name and hover explanation. The informational header cast line keeps names only. Speaker/persona options describe the version to screen readers. Rename rules are unchanged: missing versions do not invent app-specific subtitles; imported cards with identical names and no versions retain their portraits as the existing distinction. `e2e/castVersions.spec.ts` checks two same-named cards and a persona with versions in the Cast tab and Speak as at 1440 and 390 in both themes with the layout audit.
  - **Card editing and forks** (DESIGN §4, `CardForkDialogs.tsx`): the Cast rows' ⋯ and each active character's own chat-panel tab share **Full editor**, **Fork for this chat** and **Use another version**. The persona's tab (a card the user plays) is its description alone, the one persona field (DESIGN §2.2), as a text box on the same store with the same sticky Save and Open large, a line that saving changes it in every chat where the user plays it, and **Switch persona**; its More menu has Full editor instead of New chat. The card tab reads its action metadata in the viewed fork at its leaf, as the Cast tab does. **Full editor** opens this card's library editor over the chat's column, in the chat's editor workspace (§14.6, preset overlays), where changes affect every chat using it; without the workspace (a plugin removed it) it navigates to the editor page as before. **Fork for this chat** opens a dialog with the display name, version (focused) and in-character name, plus a choice to move unsaved editor drafts (name drafts stay on the source). The display name and version must differ from every other live or archived card's pair; the client blocks a clash and the writer checks again atomically. The dialog captures its fork and position when opened. **Fork and edit** calls `ForkCardForChat` and opens the new card in the editor. The copy is an ordinary library card. **Use another version** shows the entire family as an indented tree with versions, usage counts and disabled binned/purged members; picking one calls the existing `ChangeCast` `Swap`. This also switches back to the parent. The old Only in this chat / Everywhere chooser, card override RPC and override metadata are removed.
- **Single-line field widths** (owner, 2026-11-02, fieldwidth). `ui/Field.tsx` caps `Input` at `max-w-controls` (40rem); numbers (`type="number"` or numeric/decimal input mode) at 8rem, with existing narrower sizes retained. `SecretInput` and `PasswordInput` render through `Input`, so keys, header values, proxy URLs and passwords follow the same cap. `fullWidth` explicitly opts a single-line input into the whole available width; no current feature needs it. The history panel's Find and Replace fields use the same primitive. Textareas and code editors keep using their container's whole width. `e2e/panelWidth.spec.ts` checks names, card metadata in both editors, preset and lorebook names, connection settings and numeric fields in both themes at 2560 (panel dragged wide), 1440 and 390 px, keeping the card description wide.
- **Interface naming** (owner, 2026-11-04). The registered Interface tab and Settings → Interface share `DisplaySettings`. Settings uses `/settings/interface`; `/settings/display` redirects with replacement and keeps search parameters. The panel uses `?panel=interface`; legacy `?panel=display` links and remembered choices open Interface and normalize the URL. Internal display preference and transform identifiers remain unchanged.

- **The side panel** (`ChatPanels.tsx`, as ST's panels sit beside its chat): two rows of navigation (`ui/PanelTabs.tsx`), each its own tab list over the same panels, so a character named "Model" is never one of the tools. **Tools** (`Chat panel`): icon over label, in the user's order (§5 "The chat panel's tool order"), by default the registry's (the most used first: **This chat** (`ThisChatTab.tsx`), Model, Prompt preset, **Notes**, **Lorebooks** (`LorebooksTab.tsx`), **Summaries**, Snippets, Interface, History edits; a portrait opens in its own column left of the messages instead, §14.5a), never wrapping: the row (`ui/ToolTabs.tsx`) measures each tab and shows the ones that fit, the rest under **More tools**, the tab open shown as a guest before More when its place is under it. **Characters**: **Cast** (`CastTab.tsx`: present, played by me, removed, added), then a chip per character with its portrait and name, in the chat's join order (the persona last, marked "you"). When the names don't all fit, the strip measures them and shows the other characters as portraits only (the name on hover and as the tab's accessible name), the open one keeping its name; past that it scrolls sideways with the open one in view. Each character's tab (`CharacterTab.tsx`) edits its card in place, below. The panel is on stock controls (`ui/PanelTabs.tsx`, `ui/Sheet.tsx`). From 1024 px wide it's a resizable column (416 px by default, at least 260 px, as wide as the messages' minimum allows; §14.5a) to the right of the messages, which stay readable, scrollable and sendable beside it; narrower, it's a full-height sheet over the chat with its title and a Close button. The open tab is the URL's `?panel=` (`cast`, `chat`, `lorebooks`, `notes`, `summaries`, `card:<entity id>`), so a reload or a copied link keeps it; the chat's own navigations (a branch switch, a summary's range) keep it too. This browser remembers, for each user, the tab open (`rp.chatPanel.<user id>`, removed on close) and reopens it on a wide screen when the URL names none, as after a link to a message, and writes it back into the URL; a phone opens the sheet only when asked, at the last tab used (`rp.chatPanelTab.<user id>`). Another account signing in on the same browser reads its own keys. The header's `PanelToggles` has one button per tab while the panel is closed and one "Hide panel" while it's open on a wide screen; a phone has a single "Chat panel" button. A tab's body takes the panel's whole width (owner, 2026-11-02: "Tabs should be able to fully utilize horizontal space"); a descriptor may ask for `width: "readable"`, at most 52rem from the left, and no built-in does. Three shared rules keep a wide body from spreading: **text** keeps a readable line, every `<p>` in a tab body at most 80ch (`[data-measure] p`, in the base layer of `styles.css`, so a paragraph's own width class wins); **multi-line text fields and editors** (textareas, code editors, descriptions, notes and prompts) take the whole width; single-line values, including Find and Replace, follow the shared input cap above; **a row of controls that belong together** stays within `max-w-controls` (40rem, a `--container-controls` theme size): every `Select` trigger and the panel pickers' dropdowns by default, and, by class, the "You play" rows of Cast and This chat, the model limits' rows with their pencil, search and filter fields with their bar (Cast's Add characters, the sidebar's, Snippets', a lorebook's entry filter), a card's new-tag row, the chat's lorebook list and the sidebar's chat rows; a lone button sits at the start (`self-start`), never stretched. A bordered box (a note, a prompt, a lorebook entry, the regex scripts) keeps its actions at its own corners, however wide. Grids add columns as the panel widens: Cast's Add characters tiles `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(7rem, 1fr))`, 8.5rem from 48rem; Cast's characters `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(22rem, 1fr))` from 48rem; Notes, the chat's and each card's notes side by side from 56rem, 26rem each at least; the Model tab's numbers `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(10rem, 1fr))` and its four capability choices two a row; Interface's colours as 6rem swatches side by side (12rem each). A tab mounts when first shown and stays mounted, hidden, while the panel is open, so switching tabs never ends what one holds (a summary's edit, a note's fields); This chat and Lorebooks read their lists to choose from again each time they're shown. Every tab's code is fetched once the panel opens, and if a tab's can't be fetched the tab says so with Try again instead of failing the chat. **A switch renders only the panel and the header:** the callbacks the chat passes down (`show`, the branch switch, the summary and message jumps) read the tab when called, not at render, so a switch leaves every message row as it was (it re-rendered each one), and the left panel's rows read only the search params they show (`useSearch` with `select`) or the URL at the click, so they don't re-render either. `perf/chat.perf.ts` ("switch the chat panel's tabs") holds this at zero message-row renders a switch and no code waits, and each first visit under 6 s, a loose bound since that time follows the host's load (master: 84 row renders over 14 switches; now 0). Every change in it is a state event at the leaf shown (`ChangeCast`), so from there on, on that branch; the context assembler (§15) reads it.
