- **Base UI under the CSP.** Base UI's Select adds an inline `<style>` to hide its scrollbar, which `style-src 'self'` refuses. `ui/CspProvider.tsx` turns those off (`disableStyleElements`) and `styles.css` carries the rule; `e2e/csp.spec.ts` opens a select to catch a regression.

**Waiting for a cache write.** Generations still run concurrently across chats, branches and swipes. The provider gate (§6) holds only followers sharing the same cold reusable endpoint and effective cache-routing identity. Different one-turn directions after a reusable block breakpoint share its gate; changing those directions does not make a fully warm history cold. Growing history coalesces until its new endpoint is covered; a warm earlier prefix alone does not release it. `WaitingCache` events and `Hello.live.waitingCache` keep that status visible through reconnects; the reply body says “Waiting for the cache…” and Stop works while held. This wait is separate from a message queued onto a generating parent: the cache follower already has its own version and context.

**The send queue** (owner, 2026-10-12, DESIGN §2.2; `queued_messages`, migration 0012). A message sent, or a reply asked for, onto a message whose selected version is still generating waits on the server, so it survives closing the tab, under that slot, not a version. It shows as pending under the streaming reply and can be edited or withdrawn until it posts, both with the row version the user saw, so a tab that missed another's edit gets `StaleWrite` and shows the conflict instead of overwriting or deleting it. Withdrawn text goes back to the composer, after anything already typed there, and is also kept as recovered text before the queue row is removed, so closing the caller cannot lose it.
- **Durable queue edits** (`QueuedMessages.tsx`, registered as `composer.queue`; backlog U03). Message text and queued generation directions use the message editor's durable store and browser copies (`MessageDraftTarget.Queue`, `queue_edit` draft keyed by chat and queue id). The draft records the queue row version it started from; another tab's update requires an explicit second Save. Save changes content or direction and commits only the named draft holding exactly that text and session in the same writer transaction. Earlier text reads/restores every retained state of the draft's server history (the shared controller uses `MessageDraftHistory` and `RestoreMessageDraft`; `QueueDraftHistory` and `RestoreQueueDraft` remain available), including the starting state before its at most 1,000 changes; cancelling sends it and destructive history to recovered texts. Refreshes and another tab reopen the editor. Posting or withdrawing never removes an unsent edit: its chat-owned draft remains visible as an unsent edit, including after reload, with Copy to composer and Cancel. Late saves still reach that draft after the queue row disappears. A chat purge removes its queue drafts. `test/chatSetup.test.ts`, the isolation matrix and `e2e/composerBacklog.spec.ts` cover messages, directions, history, commits, late saves and orphan recovery; `e2e/queue.spec.ts` covers the two-tab queue conflict. Queued image previews use the registered `chat.queued-previews` slot alongside this editor; withdrawing restores the message's images as well as its text through the composer contribution. `e2e/queue.spec.ts` checks edit, reload and withdrawal with image attachments at desktop and phone widths.
- **Stop belongs to a version** (backlog U07). No composer Stop contribution is registered. Every generating version retains its own Stop button, at the end of what's being written and sticky to the bottom of the message list's view while any of the reply shows (fcomposerr 2026-10-31), so a reply longer than the screen keeps it in reach on a phone, just above the composer's strip; `e2e/composerBacklog.spec.ts` checks it at 390 px with the reply's start scrolled away and with the view scrolled up. A version keeps its Stop when selected through its version picker too; changing the selected swipe never retargets a composer action.

- **Queue events leave in commit order:** each write that moves the queue publishes it before anything else it does waits, so a reply posted from a queue that ends at once can't have its newer queue overtaken by the older one.
- **Posting.** When a generation of the slot ends, or the user selects one of its finished versions (`SelectAndDrain`), and the version the queue's fork selects isn't generating, the first entry posts after the selected version, in that write's transaction: a message, then a reply to it by the speaker picked when it was sent (`reply_speaker_entity_id`, as the client picks one for an immediate send), or the reply asked for. It posts in the fork it was sent in (`queued_messages.fork_id`), which was chatted in when it was sent, so if the user has gone to another fork meanwhile, the chat stays where the user is: moving them back would hide what they sent there. Should that fork have gone on from the reply, or gone to the bin, the post makes a fork of its own there. Two forks can wait on one reply (a fork made at it while it was being written): each fork's entries post in that fork, each fork's first with a reply of its own (`QueueOutcome.more` beside `next`), in the order the forks queued first. The fork's composer stays its own throughout. The new reply starts generating, and the rest of the queue waits for it. A message sent with every character muted (`SendMessage` with `reply: false`, stored as `no_reply`, migration 0048) posts with no reply, as an immediate send does, and the entries after it post on from it under the same rule. So it posts after whichever version ends up selected: complete, stopped (right after the stopped version), or failed (which stays out of the context).
- **Generate onto a generating reply** is queued too, as an entry with no text, under the same rule: whatever is aimed at a reply still being written waits for it. Chosen over refusing it (the user would have to wait and retry) and over starting it at once (it would be generated without the reply it follows).
- **The reply goes to the bin** (or its chat does): the deletion stops its generation, and that generation's end recovers the queued message text and directions before removing the entries. Restoring or purging before the generation finishes runs the same recovery before clearing its queue. Subscribers get `Queue` with what's left.
- **A restart** with messages queued behind a reply that becomes `interrupted`: at startup they post in order after it, without replies, and queued replies are removed after their directions are saved as recovered text. The server doesn't start paid generations with nobody there; the user presses Reply. A reply interrupted by the server stopping leaves its queue to that startup.
- `test/queue.test.ts` covers each of these with a generator that ends only when the test says so; `e2e/chatSetup.spec.ts` covers posting after a finished reply, stop-then-post and withdrawing in the browser.

**The fake generator** (`dev/fakeGenerator.ts`, `dev/syntheticText.ts`) streams synthetic Markdown (prose, dialogue, lists, quotes, an occasional table), seeded by the version id, at `FAKE_GENERATOR_TPS` tokens a second, about `FAKE_GENERATOR_TOKENS` (400) per generation, in chunks of what's due every 10 ms or more. It's for tests, the development server and the performance harness, and only those can wire it: the production entry point `main.ts` never installs a fake generator whatever the environment says (`test/chats.test.ts`), and `src/dev/` isn't in the Docker image (`.dockerignore`). So production code reaches `src/dev/` only through a dynamic import behind its switch: `FAKE_CARD_SOURCE` loads `dev/fakeCardSource.ts`, and `FAKE_SAVED_MEDIA=on` loads `dev/fakeSavedMedia.ts` (in `runMain.ts`), failing with "FAKE_SAVED_MEDIA=on needs the development files (src/dev), which this build doesn't include." where they aren't shipped. `test/productionImports.test.ts` (in `npm run check`) reads the Docker CMD, worker entry map and Vite entry map, then walks static imports, runtime re-exports, literal dynamic imports at every depth and worker URLs, excluding type-only bindings. It checks `.dockerignore`, final-stage COPY locations, local assets, workspace resolution and production dependencies. Computed imports/globs, indirect worker entries and filesystem reads require exact, explained review entries; trusted registry module URLs and data-volume reads are recorded there. The two conditional development imports must retain their switch and failure handler. Both fail plainly without reflecting the switch's value or the loader's error. `test/startup.test.ts` runs each switch against a synthetic source projection without `src/dev`, requiring a nonzero exit before listening and the plain error. The import test also checks every worker-stamped source against the COPY set, every vendored tokenizer and licence against the generated worker output, and external bundle imports against production dependencies. This is a source/build guard; the deploy gate must still start the actual pruned image and exercise runtime assets. Before this check, a static import of `dev/fakeSavedMedia.ts` in `runMain.ts` made the image fail at start with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The development entry point, `src/dev/main.ts`, reads `FAKE_GENERATOR_TPS` and refuses to start with `NODE_ENV=production` (`test/config.test.ts`). The browser tests start it only for files that ask for the fake generator.

The generator service has an optional, non-sensitive `kind` identity. The context/provider generator reports `provider`, the development fake reports `fake`, an unlabelled plugin generator reports `custom`, and an absent generator reports `none`. `/healthz` returns this as `x-generator-kind`, allowing the final-image smoke check (§1) to prove that development environment flags did not install a fake generator without making a provider call. The body remains `ok`; the header contains no model, connection or user information.

**The client** (`packages/client/src/features/chat/`), on stock components (CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §8):
- **URLs:** `/chats` lists chats, newest first, with delete, and makes a chat without characters. `/chats/$chatId` opens a chat at the bottom of its current fork; `?fork=` shows another fork, `?slot=` opens at a message and flashes it (**Message jumps**, below). The URL names a fork only while it isn't the current one: once a send there makes it current, the URL drops it. Each message's menu has "Copy link" (that URL, with `fork` on a fork other than the current one) and "Branch from here" (`CreateFork` at it, named automatically "From #n" by the message's number, a name like any other the user can change; `ForkNotesDialog.tsx`, `forks.ts` `automaticBranchName`): the chat opens on the new fork, which is current, at that message, which the URL keeps (`?slot=`, with the panel), and Back returns to the fork it came from, even when that was the current one (the entry left behind is rewritten in place to name it, so it isn't opened first). The automatic name is stored (`name_user` 0): a message inserted before it later doesn't renumber it.
- **Message jumps** (DESIGN §10.1 [D] 2026-11-06; `features/chat/jumpFlash.ts`). Every way of opening a chat at a message ends as the URL's `slot`: a character's tile or row (the line it last spoke, `lastLine` in `features/characters/shellData.tsx`, behind the one switch `OPEN_AT_LAST_LINE`), Copy link's URL, History edits' matches, a summary's range, the branch menu's "Go to where this branch starts", the activity panel, the bin's branch links, a card revision's "used in" link, the context view's sources and a branch switch. Each time the window opens there (`view.opened` moves) `MessageList` flashes that message's `article` with `flashItem` from `ui/reveal.ts`, the same flash as an added item (the accent ring three times; with reduced motion one steady highlight that fades), once it has mounted and can be seen (`flashWhenShown`: a page loading or a summary expanding to it, at most 8 s; a summary's layer replacing the original it first rendered as gets the flash too; while a modal covers the chat, as a phone's card panel does when a character's chat opens, or its workbench tab isn't shown, it waits), then nothing marks it. A message the user inserts flashes the same way (`view.highlight`). The flash marks its history entry (`HistoryState.chatFlashed`, `<chat>/<slot>`), which the workbench mirrors to the browser's, so a reload, back/forward or a tab shown again opens at the message without flashing it; a reading position restored from the entry never flashes; the same jump chosen again on the same entry (`Flashes.again`) does. An explicit repeat jump discards the restored reading position and its history markers; a fresh history entry linking to the same `slot` reopens the existing window, while scroll/flash-state replacements and consumed Back/Forward entries do not replay the jump. Sidebar scope and Chats/Characters switches preserve the message entry's flash and reading state. A timeline-mode switch remounting the list doesn't flash again (`Flashes.opened`, kept by `ChatSurface`). Messages have no selection state of their own; focus rings on their controls are unchanged. `e2e/messageFlash.spec.ts` (support `e2e/support/flashes.ts` records each `data-flashing`) covers the character tile (on a phone, no flash until the card's panel closes), reload, back and forward, a message link, a History edits match and the branch-start link twice, at 1440 and 390 in both themes, and reduced motion; `chat.spec.ts`, `chatTimelineReview.spec.ts`, `lcm.spec.ts`, `summariesUx.spec.ts` and `binBranches.spec.ts` check their links flash and then leave the message unmarked.
- **Closing the chat panel** (panelclose, owner, 2026-11-02; built 2026-11-03). At widths of 1024 px and above, the header’s panel toggle is the close control; the panel’s tool-tab row has no trailing × and uses the recovered space for tabs. The compact header toggle exposes expanded and pressed state and uses the raised surface while open. Below 1024 px, the full-screen `Sheet` retains its top-right `WindowClose` (and Escape), matching the left navigation drawer’s corner control. Saved and pending chats share this behavior.
- **The header** (`ChatHeader.tsx`), one row: the faces of the characters the user doesn't play (up to four, each opening its card in the panel; hidden when narrow, below), the chat's readable name (`chatTitle.ts`: the card or group name and the day ST started it, never ST's file name; it's also the tab's title), which a click renames in place (Enter renames, Escape keeps it; in a group of several chats a dialog asks whether to rename the chat or the group), and under it the other characters' names, no versions ("with Zara"), else the day ST started it. Then the branch control (`chatBranchControls`) and the header's buttons, contributions to `chatHeaderActions` (`headerContributions.tsx`, rendering `headerParts.tsx` lazily): ☆ (the shown fork's pin; hidden when narrow), the side panel's toggle icon (`PanelToggles compact`) and ⋯ (`ChatCommandMenu`). **Narrow is the header's own width** (a `@container/header`), not the screen's: below 40rem, on a phone or with the chat at its 440 px minimum beside a widened panel, the faces, the pin and the name's rename pencil are left out (the side panel has the cast, the chat lists have the pin, ⋯ has Rename). The name's column keeps at least 6rem; the buttons don't shrink (`*:shrink-0`) and the branch control is the one part that gives up room, truncating its label (`e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts`, the `-wide-drag` panel surfaces). While the chat loads it shows placeholders, not a name it doesn't know, and the messages' place shows skeleton messages (`SkeletonMessages.tsx`, with the slow-load retry); while the chat view's own code loads, the route's fallback is the same shape (`ChatSkeleton`: a header placeholder above the skeleton messages), not a spinner (`e2e/chatView.spec.ts`). Between `sm` and `lg` it starts with ← to `/chats`. On a phone (below `sm`) it replaces the app's top bar on a chat route (`shell.tsx` hides it there), so the first message starts about 52 px down; its ← ("Chats and menu") opens that bar's menu (`openAppMenu`), the left panel with the chats and the chat's crumbs. Under it, a chat that has outgrown its context with summaries off has a one-line status bar with **Enable summaries**; a phone shows only "Summaries are off.", the reason in the button's title and description (`ChatPage.tsx`).

  Narrow-header allocation (suitegreen3, 2026-11-04): below 40rem, the title keeps its intrinsic width up to the header width minus 9rem for navigation and actions. The action row takes the remaining width; the phone branch trigger can shrink to its icon and padding (1.75rem), retaining its complete accessible name. The actions remain right-aligned when a short title leaves spare width (`headerAlignment.spec.ts`). `qaAttribution.spec.ts` measures the full synthetic group title after the branch state has loaded in both phone themes.
- **⋯, the chat's commands** (`commands.tsx`, registry `chatCommands`): Rename, Branches…, New chat with this cast (one character: `/cards/$id/chat`; several: `/groups/$chatId/new`), Export… (the branch shown or every branch, written by the server as SillyTavern `.jsonl` with every version, or plain text, §13b; `chatExport.tsx`, the formats a kind offers from `chatExportText.ts`, `client/test/chatExport.test.ts`), Search and replace, History edits, Keyboard shortcuts (a dialog listing every registered command with a key: its short label, its `description` under it saying what it does and where the keys work, and its keys beside a label that doesn't name them, `shortcutText`), and Delete chat (to the bin, with Undo, no confirmation). A command with a `shortcut` is listed under Keyboard shortcuts rather than in the menu unless it sets `menu: true` (Search and replace does); one with a `dialog` opens it from the menu; `tone: "danger"` puts it after a separator. The context gives commands `onRename`, `navigate` and `deleted` (the bin toast).
- **The branch control** (`BranchControl.tsx`, registered as `chat.branches` in `chatBranchControls`; the UI says "branch" for a fork everywhere). The header keeps its branch control disabled while the branch list is loading or there is only one live fork, with a reason. With more than one it shows "Branch: Split 12 Jan 2025, 21:40 at #14 ▾" (with "· not where it opens" when the fork shown isn't the chat's current one); it opens a popover on a wide screen (`Popover` `tall`: as tall as the room below the trigger allows, less 8 px, never flipping beside it) and a sheet on a phone, and ⋯ Branches… opens the same list (a dialog while there's one branch). The list is `ListForks` (`forks.ts` `useChatForks`, read when the chat opens and again when the fork shown, the chat's record, a branch name or a write made here changes; a branch made here is listed from `CreateFork`'s answer until a read has it): every live fork, pinned first, then named, then the rest, each by its last message, newest first (`orderBranches`, the left panel's order; headed "Pinned branches" / "Named branches" / "Branches" when more than one group is present, and the trigger's "2 of 3" counts in the same order). Each row is the left panel's branch row (branchmenu, 2026-11-05): a bordered rounded box, a one-line title (label, then a small pencil, then the "opens here" chip at the line's end), the last message's preview in a fixed two-line slot and "Last message <time>"; the shown one has the accent border and raised background and is scrolled into view when the list opens. **Every list names a branch one way** (`forkLabel` in `forks.ts`: this list, the left panel, the bin's affected branches): the name the user gave it; else "Original" for the chat's first fork; else where it splits off, its time first, "Split 12 Jan 2025, 21:40 at #14" (owner, 2026-11-01): the time of its first own message (else its making) and the number of the last message it shares (`ForkSplit`, from the fork summaries); a branch made here is unnamed too (Branch from here sends no automatic name). A row's open area is a link to the branch (`/chats/<id>?fork=`, none for the current one, the panel kept): a plain click switches to it in place, a middle or modified click opens it in a new browser tab; its pencil renames it in place with the shared compact `InlineRename` (`NameFork`; empty takes the name off; the row's height doesn't change), the pin in its upper corner pins it within the chat (`PinFork`, the left panel's pin and explanations) and the bin in its lower corner deletes it to the bin with Undo (disabled, with "The only branch: delete the chat instead", for the last one; deleting the one shown follows the current fork and drops `fork` from the URL). Its footer is a column of ghost buttons, icon first, always present and greyed with a reason when unavailable: "Back to the branch the chat opens on", "Back to “…”" (the fork it was made from, `parentForkId`, while live: ST's "Back to parent chat"), "Go to where this branch starts" (its start slot) and "Show in the left panel" (the sidebar's list of the chat's forks), then the hint for starting another. Browser coverage of the open menu's layout at 1440, 1024 in a half-width frame and 390, light and dark: `e2e/branchMenu.spec.ts`. Each message's own alternates stay on the message (`SwitchBranch`). Features extend the control through `branchControlParts` (`branchParts.ts`): the trigger's name, which forks the Branches list leaves out and sections above it; parallel threads use all three (§3.8 "Threads in the client").
- **One `ChatSession` per open chat** (`session.ts`) holds the loaded window of the path, kept current by the subscription. It subscribes first and opens the window on the first `Hello`; another `Hello` (a reconnect) or a `Reload` reads the loaded range again. Writes apply the server's reply at once (the event that follows changes nothing); selecting a version shows it before the reply and puts the slot back if refused, and a `StaleWrite` reads the slot again. The server may answer a read from before an event that reached the client while it was in flight; so `Slot`, `Version` and `Chat` events received while reads are in flight are applied again once each lands, and applying one twice, or after a newer state, changes nothing (row versions, and a finished version never goes back to generating). Each in-flight read owns its own event buffer, removed before replay (review-splitrefresh, 2026-11-12). Replayed events may read another fork’s slot as this fork shows it, or reload an unknown insertion without a position, but the new read never inherits the event that started it. This ends the replay/read loop without leaving a stale slot when an older window lands after its refresh or first loads that slot. The earlier fix-split-refresh suppression of other-fork reads on replay prevented the reported crash but missed those races and the insertion path. Slot refreshes reject answers after disposal or a fork switch (including away and back), and a fallback snapshot shown by another fork cannot trigger another refresh. `test/session.test.ts` bounds reads across reordered windows, multiple slots, repeated server events, failures, reconnects, unknown insertions and navigation. `e2e/splitRefresh.spec.ts` covers workshop first-message splits and story tabs on different branches at 1440, bounds ReadPath requests with a WebSocket fuse outside the renderer, and samples post-GC heap and DOM nodes over three seconds; run it under a browser memory cap. A change to the chat (`Chat`, `Slot`, `Version`, `State`, `Reload`, `Deleted`, a reconnect's `Hello`) refreshes legacy chat/group lists and split-chat links through `chat-lists` one second after the first change, once for a burst; the opening `Hello` does not. The shell uses its own incremental streams (section 12) and updates without that delay. The casts the messages on screen display with (`castAfter`, for their macros and display scripts) are asked together: what the rows ask for as they render goes in one `GetCasts` a page of 200 positions, which reads the state at each and the cards once for the positions that bind them alike. A position-cache generation rejects batches queued or in flight before a state change, fork switch or disposal, so an older response cannot restore old macro names or erase a newer cast. A fork switch publishes the new fork before notifying position subscribers, whose synchronous snapshot checks must request that fork (`test/session.test.ts`). The batched RPC is covered by `test/getCasts.test.ts` (a chat opened with one `GetCast` per message, each reading the cards and role projections again, 12 to 22 on a page). Readers of the account's defaults and preset list that follow the chat's context share one read a change (`useRefreshOnContext`, `pickers/defaults.ts`; the composer's chips, the Model and Prompt preset tabs and the preset fallback each read on their own), and the model choices (`useModelChoiceList`) show the last read at once and read again behind it, one read for every picker mounted. The library's lorebook list stays five minutes after its last reader and is read again behind what it shows (`useAtomRevalidated`, `actions.tsx`). The Cast tab's Import a new version reads the card's family only where the ref isn't known (it was one `CardFamily` per cast member). Measured on the 151-fork synthetic chat: see night/tabperf.md.
- **Chat-switch handover** (chatflash, 2026-11-05). `ChatPage.tsx` starts the incoming `ChatSession` while retaining the outgoing surface and its destination, inert until the first window or a read error is ready. Only then does the keyed surface change; `MessageList` retains its existing bottom, summary-boundary, deep-link and reading-position landing rules. Superseded pending sessions are disposed; the outgoing session is disposed when replaced. `LazyChatPage` chooses its loaded or lazy component once per mount, so completing the first import does not change the tree shape on navigation. Initial page loads retain the retryable skeleton. `OpenChatBranches` and `SplitChatSection` retain their previous resolved rows and split metadata while a new chat's uncached reads finish, reserving the section heights; retained sections are inert. These data waits occur in both Vite and built clients and grow with chat size. `e2e/chatFlash.spec.ts` samples animation frames across first and repeat sidebar switches at 1440/390 in both themes, rejecting centre loading/empty frames and missing branch/split sections, with video and CDP screenshots. A held-subscription regression covers superseded picks, returning to the outgoing chat, and retention of its composer draft.
- **The chat view loads with the first chat opened** (a lazy route): it carries the Markdown renderer, 170 KB gzipped of the client's 415.
- **The list** (`ChatPage.tsx`) is TanStack Virtual in chat mode (`anchorTo: "end"`), keyed by slot id with measured heights: prepending older history and growing rows below keep what's on screen in place.
- **Following the bottom:** at the end of a window that reaches the leaf, the list holds there while the last messages grow or arrive. The user scrolling up (wheel, touch, keys, grabbing the scrollbar, a middle-button autoscroll, or any scroll away from the last 48 px) lets go at once, and TanStack Virtual's own following goes off with it: when it wrote the scroll position as a smooth scroll began, the scroll stopped in its first pixels and the list never let go. Reaching the end again holds on once the user has stopped for 300 ms. Known gap: a scroll up with none of these signs, like find in page, is pulled back until it's 48 px from the end; telling it from content shrinking by the scroll position alone wasn't reliable.
- **Paging:** it pages older and newer from the server's cursors when the first or last rendered message nears the loaded edge, keeps at most 500 slots, and drops the far end, read again when needed. Rows have `contain: layout paint style` and are placed with `top`, not a transform, so sticky content inside a row (a streaming reply's Stop) holds to the view's edge.
- **A token updates views of its version.** Each generating version's text is an atom of its own (`liveText`), read by its message's body and any open picker preview or comparison of it, and kept alive while it streams whether shown or not. Deltas are collected and applied once per animation frame; any other event first applies the deltas before it. Message rows are memoized and re-render only when their slot changes.
- **Message rendering** (`ui/Markdown.tsx`, `ui/StMarkdown.tsx`) dispatches through the subscribed `messageRenderers` registry. `registerDisplay` registers the lazy ST formatter as `markdown`; plugins can replace or disable it, wrap its effective component to extend formatting, or add a higher-priority renderer. Disabling all renderers shows plain text. This applies to messages, reasoning, greetings, summary text and version previews. Each `Markdown` body has an error boundary around the effective registered renderer, including its lazy load and effects (review-htmlboundary, 2026-11-12): a failure shows the existing plain-text rendering, preserving source-copy metadata where the source is unchanged, without parsing markup or removing adjacent bodies. A text, source or renderer replacement retries it. `test/markdownBoundary.test.ts` checks render/effect failures, inert fallback, adjacent bodies and recovery; `e2e/htmlRendererBoundary.spec.ts` checks the fallback and layout at 1440/390 in light/dark. The formatter uses Streamdown 2.7's memoized blocks and renders React elements through the unchanged rehype-sanitize and rehype-harden pipeline. Raw HTML renders as formatting by default (next item); with the viewer's switch off it stays literal text. Markdown images use the external-media consent below; links open in a new tab without a referrer. A fenced code block is one frame (`styles.css`, `[data-streamdown="code-block"]`): the raised surface with a border, so it shows on the user's raised messages too, its language as a small muted label above the code; Streamdown's inner body and the `pre` draw no box of their own (before, an outer box held the label and a second framed box held the code). `e2e/messageFormatting.spec.ts` checks one painted or bordered element per block, at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark.
- **HTML in messages, inline** (`ui/html/`, `features/chat/htmlDisplay.tsx`; htmlbuild step 1, 2026-11-07; spec/HTML-MESSAGES.md §3.2, all [P]). A block of a message that contains `<` goes through its own rehype pipeline (`StMarkdown` `PositionedBlock`; blocks without a tag keep the plain one): `htmlMark` gives every Markdown element a random per-load trusted property, rehype-raw parses the raw HTML (stFormatting keeps mdast `html` nodes as HTML only on this path; `htmlRaw` runs it, and a document its parse5-to-hast conversion throws on, as on an SVG or MathML `<template>`, which parse5 gives no template contents, keeps its raw markup as text, as with the switch off, instead of failing the render; before, one such message replaced the whole chat view with the router's error page, wherever it was opened: htmlboundary. Streamdown keeps raw HTML only when the list holds rehype-raw itself, so the list carries it switched off, `[rehypeRaw, false]`, which unified skips), `htmlPrepare` drops `<style>` elements, turns `form` into `div` (fix 2) and, for tags the schema doesn't know, turns line breaks into `<br>` before the tag goes and its text stays, as ST shows `<Status>` lines. `htmlSanitize` runs hast-util-sanitize with the effective registered schema. `htmlFinish` then works on the unmarked (parsed) elements only, so Markdown's own footnote ids and links are untouched: DOMPurify's attribute value checks (`_isValidAttribute`: URI-safe names, its allowed-URI pattern, `data:` only on media tags); classes get `custom-` except `fa-*`, `note-*` and `monospace` (fix 5); ids and names get `user-content-` with `#` links (`href`, `xlink:href`, `usemap`, read as the browser's URL parser reads them, `urlAddress`: without the spaces and controls at their ends or the tabs and line breaks inside, so `" #root"` is a fragment too), `for`/`list`/`headers`/aria references rewritten (fix 3); the `form` attribute goes; a style attribute goes through the stylesheet's value policy (`css.ts` `cleanStyle`, Styles below) and becomes React's style object, not text, so React sets each kept property on its own and nothing reads the style's text again (`!important` can't be set that way and is left off); the SVG presentation attributes the browser reads as CSS values that can name a resource (`fill`, `stroke`, `filter`, `clip-path`, `mask`, `marker-*`, `cursor`) go through the same policy with `url()` only to the message's own `#id`, renamed (`cleanPresentation`), and go when refused (before, `fill="url(/x.svg#g)"` kept its address); without consent, remote `img`/`srcset`/SVG `image` hrefs/`input` images/`background` go, and audio, video, source and track go entirely (with consent, image/audio proxying below applies). Anything from another site that was taken out leaves a marker element, and the body shows one note under it, "Images from other sites are blocked." (`HtmlParts.tsx` `BlockedMediaNote`; its scoped Allow buttons and `/media/external` are described below). The image hardener then runs with `data:` images allowed; an anchor without an address stays an anchor rather than a blocked-link caption. Links are http, https and mailto only (schema protocols), open in a new tab with `noopener noreferrer` (an SVG link with only `xlink:href` too: `StMarkdown` `Link` reads whichever the browser follows), and `#` links stay on the page (fix 4).
  - **The schema** (`ui/html/schema.ts`) is DOMPurify 3.4.2's default lists (the version ST pins), generated into `purifyLists.ts` by `scripts/htmlSchema.ts` from the installed `dompurify` (a dev dependency) and mapped to the parser's tag names (SVG camelCase) and hast property names; `aria-*` and `data-*` are allowed as DOMPurify allows them. It leaves out `style` (it becomes the stylesheet), `form` (made a `div`), `title` (React hoists it), `template`, `html`, `head` and `body`, and the form submission, `popover` and `nonce` attributes. DOMPurify's FORBID_CONTENTS (and `script`, `title`) go with their content; other unknown elements leave their text. Comments and doctypes go; `clobber` is off because ids are prefixed afterwards.
  - **Rendering** (`HtmlParts.tsx` `htmlComponents`): the sanitized tree reaches the DOM as React elements, created with DOM calls; no markup text derived from a message is ever handed to an HTML parser again (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `DOMParser`, `document.write`, `srcdoc`, `createContextualFragment`), so there is no serialize-and-reparse step for mutation XSS to exploit (`test/htmlTree.test.ts` renders hostile messages into a DOM with every such sink watched). Parsed elements render as plain elements, not Streamdown's Markdown components (a card's `<table>` gets no table chrome); inputs, textareas and selects are uncontrolled (`defaultChecked`/`defaultValue`), so CSS-only games that toggle checkboxes work.
  - **Styles** (`ui/html/css.ts`, `messageHtml.ts`; rebuilt by htmlboundary, 2026-11-12): each of a message's `<style>` elements outside code is scoped on its own (kept in the formatter's lazy chunk; `setStyleScoper` injects it). Safe by construction rather than by pattern: the text is read by `@csstools/css-tokenizer` and `@csstools/css-parser-algorithms` (4.0.2, exact; CSS Syntax Level 3, the algorithm browsers run, so escapes, comments, strings, bad strings and brackets split where the browser splits them), and any tokenizer or parser error refuses the whole style, as does more than 200,000 characters or 64 nested blocks and functions, checked on the flat token list before anything recursive walks it. Rules, at-rules and declarations come from the component values (CSS Syntax's "consume a stylesheet's/block's contents"), and the output is written token by token from that tree: only allowlisted token kinds, identifiers and strings re-escaped (CSSOM's serialization), comments dropped, `/**/` between two tokens only where the pair would otherwise read as one; then the written text is tokenized again and must give exactly the tokens meant, or nothing is used. So a string, comment or escape can't end a rule early in the browser's reading (postcss had read a string across a line break that the browser ends there, so the rest of a selector became a global rule: found by this audit, present since step 1). Top-level selectors are scoped twice where the browser has `CSSScopeRule` (Chromium, current Firefox and Safari): wrapped in `@scope (.message-html)` with `:scope ` in front (same specificity as `.message-html `), so the browser itself keeps every rule's subject inside a message body; elsewhere they get `.message-html ` in front. Classes and ids are renamed as the markup's (`.` and an ident token, id hash tokens; an unrestricted hash like `#1a` refuses its selector); nested rules are renamed only, with explicit `&` allowed only once at the start of a nested selector; top-level selectors starting with `+`, `~` or `||` go; functions in selectors only after a colon (pseudo-classes); attribute selectors as written. At-rules: `@media`/`@supports`/`@container`/`@starting-style` recurse (their conditions pass the value policy, no `url()`), `@layer` blocks are unwrapped, top-level `@keyframes` and `@font-face` are written outside the scope with their names renamed along with their uses in `animation`/`animation-name`/`font`/`font-family` (keyframes use `custom-`; fonts use the per-message namespace below; a family must be exactly one plain name, quoted or not, read after escapes; a face whose descriptor names are escaped or with no `src` left goes; `unicode-range` is left out), and everything else (`@import`, `@namespace`, `@page`, `@property`, `@scope`, `@font-feature-values`, keyframes or fonts inside a grouping rule, …) goes. Values (every declaration, custom properties included): idents, numbers written plainly, strings, hashes, commas, a few delimiters, `()`/`[]` blocks and an allowlist of functions that name no resource (colors, math, gradients, transforms, filters, easing, shapes, `var`, `env`, `counter(s)`, `local`, `format`, `tech`, `repeat`, `minmax`, `fit-content`); `url()` (or a url token, escaped or not, as the browser reads it) only as `data:`, an in-document `#id` (renamed), or with media consent the proxy address `media.ts` builds; `image()`, `image-set()`, `cross-fade()`, `element()`, `paint()`, `src()`, `expression()` and any other function are refused; `attr()` has only the direct generated-text exception below, so message-defined custom property values pass the same policy. Inherited app variables are still readable; the built-in ones carry colors, dimensions and font names, not resource addresses. A refused declaration goes; `behavior` and `-moz-binding` always. Property names must be plain (no escapes) and well formed; no fixed list of names, since a name alone loads nothing. The `<style>` texts are found as ST finds them (`extractStyles`: `<style\b[^>]*>` to `</style>` or the end, outside code fences) with forward searches only; the regex it replaces rescanned to the end from every `<style` without a `>`, ten seconds of main thread on 40,000 of them, and the same held for `panelHasScripts` and the block's `![`…`]` check (`hasImageSyntax`), now single passes with the same answers. Fence extraction first finds an opener and a following newline before trying the original matching pattern, avoiding quadratic backtracking on a line of backticks while preserving its exact multiline behavior. Nested-rule parsing stops at each curly block rather than rescanning every remaining sibling for a semicolon (review-htmlboundary). Both timing regressions are tagged slow. The chat surface provider `display.html` (order 16, `HtmlProvider`) holds one `MessageStyles` per chat view: one constructed stylesheet adopted on the document, holding the styles of every message in the loaded window in order (a rendered body reports its display text's; one not rendered yet contributes its stored text's), so a greeting's style keeps applying after it scrolls out of the virtualized timeline. A new chat's greetings use `HtmlPreview`, the same with one entry. Every body that renders HTML carries `markdown-html message-html`; `.markdown-html` has `contain: layout paint; isolation: isolate` (`styles.css`), so a card's `position: fixed` stays inside its message (fix 1), and its images are at most the body's width.
  - **Consent and CSS conditions** (review-htmlboundary): `MessageStyles` eagerly retains every accepted stylesheet media address; `useQueuedMediaProps` does the same for inline values. The browser sees pending data images or fetched blob URLs. Ancestor/attribute selectors can still read DOM state, but do not control which addresses reach the media proxy. `e2e/externalMedia.spec.ts` checks that both branches of an ancestor-attribute condition and a never-matching media rule fetch before any condition is enabled, and changing the ancestor adds no address.
  - **Plain generated text and embedded fonts** (htmlfonts, 2026-11-12; owner approved allowing both, implementation choices remain **Proposed**). `attr()` is not in the general value-function allow-list. Its only exception is `content` in a style rule where **every selector branch ends directly in `::before` or `::after`** (including nested rules and grouping rules). The value must contain only strings and direct `attr(one-ident)` calls, with whitespace/comments and optional declaration-level `!important`. The decoded, case-sensitive attribute name must be exactly `title`, `alt`, `data-label`, `data-value`, `data-text` or `data-tooltip`: descriptive attributes on the sanitized markup, never `value`, `nonce`, arbitrary `data-*`, source-copy metadata or app ids. No typed/fallback form, substitution (`var`/`env`), nested function, URL, image function, other property, inline style attribute, SVG presentation attribute, condition or keyframe may carry `attr()`. These values cannot reach a fetch: there are no resource tokens or substitutions in this text-only grammar, and the result is never stored in a custom property or reparsed. The existing selector prefix/native scope admits only message-body descendants; `attr()` reads only the originating element's attribute, never an ancestor or sibling outside that message. The attribute list is deliberately narrow; for example `attr(data-description)` remains refused.
    - Embedded font sources accept only base64 `data:font/woff2`, `data:font/woff`, `data:font/ttf` and `data:font/otf`. Decoded bytes must start with the corresponding `wOF2`, `wOFF`, `00 01 00 00` or `OTTO` signature. WOFF/WOFF2 require their full container header, an exact byte-length field and a bounded declared SFNT size. Collections, SVG fonts, MIME/signature mismatches, non-base64 payloads and all other media types in font `src` are refused. The `src` descriptor accepts direct URLs, `local`, `format` and `tech`, with no `var`/`env` or other indirect source. This adds no other data type to another resource policy; existing image/SVG presentation restrictions remain unchanged. Without a message identity, embedded fonts are refused.
    - **Proposed limits:** 96 KiB decoded per source, 192 KiB decoded across all sources in all of one message's style tags; declared expanded SFNT sizes at most 2 MiB per source and 4 MiB per message (TTF/OTF count their decoded size). Repeated sources count again. Existing 200,000-character per-style and 64-level nesting limits remain. Synthetic valid rectangle fonts padded to 32,516 / 65,284 / 98,052 bytes measured base64 decode medians 0 / 0.1 / 0.1 ms (maximum 0.5 ms), and complete CSS scoping medians 7.3 / 10.0 / 20.2 ms (maximum 30.9 ms). Chromium font loading, layout and one animation frame had warmed medians about 16.6 ms; the initial cold sample reached 166 ms. Thus 96 KiB leaves room for CSS within the existing per-style limit, and 192 KiB permits two such faces while bounding repeated decode/parser work. The expanded-size limits further constrain compressed-font envelopes; they are not a native-memory or execution-time guarantee. Measurements use synthetic simple glyphs, not a worst-case font, and do not establish costs on phones or other engines.
    - `scopeStyles` shares the font-name table and size budget across a message's styles. The renderer and the offscreen stylesheet scoper both supply the message slot key. Font family definitions and references use a reserved `rpfont-<hex-encoded-slot>-<lowercase-family>` namespace; the message root gets the corresponding reserved class (authored classes are renamed, so cannot impersonate it). User-written private font names in property values are refused. For a message defining fonts, `font`/`font-family` rules are emitted with an additional selector requiring that message's root in both prefix and native-scope modes; nested/grouped declarations follow it. Other declarations retain the shared greeting-style behavior. Font/font-family animation declarations are refused on the keyed path, preventing shared keyframes from carrying a private font to another body. A plain inline `font-family: Card` does not resolve a renamed embedded family: use a stylesheet rule. No consent state, download queue, frame permission, stored text, copy source or prompt changes.
    - The combined app CSP uses `font-src 'self' blob: data:`; blob permits the existing approved media queue's generated font URLs, while data permits bounded embedded fonts; scripts, styles, images, media, connections and frame policies are unchanged. In Chromium, embedded fonts produce **zero font requests**, and two messages defining the same original family render different synthetic glyph widths without overriding each other or registering the app's original family. Both native-scope and prefix fallback paths are tested. The combined rehost/htmlfonts gate verifies that a queued synthetic font loads under the normal CSP before glyph and selector changes, with no additional network requests. Authored blob URLs and direct remote font URLs remain refused by the sanitizer.
    - This signature/envelope check is not a full font validator. Chromium and Firefox use [OpenType Sanitizer](https://github.com/khaledhosny/ots/blob/main/docs/DesignDoc.md), which parses/validates font structures and reserializes accepted tables, rejecting malformed structures and dropping unsupported information; its documentation explicitly does not promise TrueType-bytecode validation. [Chromium also describes sandboxing and fuzzing](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/memory-safety-fonts). These reduce font-parser exposure, not eliminate browser/font-engine vulnerabilities or bound all rendering cost. OTS does not establish that glyphs mean the stored text: **a font can draw different glyphs from that text**. That visual deception is confined to the source card's own message body by private families, private font selectors and the existing paint containment; stored/copy/prompt text is unchanged. Firefox/WebKit execution remains unverified on this host.

A fenced code block the classifier calls a document becomes an `rp-frame` element in `htmlFinish` (its text after the display transforms, its place among the message's blocks), which the effective document renderer draws: the built-in one is registered as `html.frame` (disabling it leaves the block as its code block). The renderer gets only its block's text. Its scripts run only once its sources allowed them (step 3, below).
  - **The frame** is `<iframe src="/frame/panel" sandbox="allow-scripts">` without `allow-same-origin`, so its origin is opaque (`origin` is `"null"` inside); its requests carrying `Origin: null` are refused by `RequestGuard` like any other site's. `allow-scripts` is there for our bootstrap only: the page's CSP (§1) runs no script but `/frame/bootstrap.js`, so the block's `<script>`s and handlers don't run (the spec's `sandbox=""` would stop the bootstrap too, and with it delivery and height). The server's `/frame/panel` route answers a fixed page that loads the bootstrap as a classic script (a module script's request would carry `Origin: null`); the client build emits it unhashed at `frame/bootstrap.js` (a second Rolldown input, `vite.config.ts`); Vite's dev server proxies `/frame/panel` to the server and serves the bootstrap from source.
  - **Delivery** (bootstrap): it posts `rp:ready` to its parent; the parent, checking `event.source` is that frame's window and `event.origin` is `null`, posts `rp:render` only once per frame window (including across listener replacements and navigation) with the block's text, the chat column's height and the theme. The bootstrap parses the text with DOMParser, removes `script`, `base`, `meta[http-equiv]` and `noscript`, rewrites `vh` (and `dvh`/`svh`/`lvh`) in style elements and attributes to `calc(var(--rp-vh) * N)`, replaces its document element with the result, and stops primary and auxiliary link clicks (HTML, SVG including `xlink:href`, and image maps) from navigating the frame. The bootstrap accepts messages only from its parent at the app origin and targets that origin in its replies. `--rp-vh` is a hundredth of the chat column's height (`[data-testid=messages]`), resent on resize; `--rp-text`, `--rp-background` and `--rp-accent` are the theme's text, surface and accent colours with `color-scheme`, resent when the theme changes. It reports `rp:height` from a ResizeObserver; the parent sizes the frame to it, at most twice the viewport height (the frame scrolls beyond that). The text never goes in the URL; parent-to-frame messages use target `*`, as the frame has no origin to name; the HTML can contain private expanded message content, so it must never be redelivered to a navigated document.
  - **Virtualization** (`FrameSlots`, one per chat view in `HtmlChat`): a frame loads while its row is on screen or within half a screen of it (IntersectionObserver on the timeline's scroller); at most 8 are loaded per chat view, and when a ninth comes near, the frame that left the screen longest ago unloads (losing its script state, as a reloaded ST chat does). One that finds all eight on screen waits for one to leave. An unloaded or not yet loaded frame is a placeholder of its last reported height (150 px before the first).
  - **While its reply streams** the block shows "Panel loading" and loads when the reply finishes. **Panel depth:** "Run panels in" (Interface panel, `PanelDepthSelect`; the `panelDepth` display preference, `null` for all messages, the default, or 1 to 1000) counts from the viewed fork's tip (`useDisplayContext().leafDepth` less the message's position, as display regex depths): a document block in an older message shows "Older panel" with a **Run panel** button, which loads it for as long as the body stays mounted.
  - **Copy**: the block copies as its whole stored range through one hidden placeholder character; the rich-text flavour leaves frames out (`messageCopy.tsx`).
  - **Delivered once**: the parent answers a frame's first `rp:ready` only, so a frame that navigates itself (to a page with more permissions, say) gets nothing. A frame is a new element for new text or new permissions (`key` of its URL and text).

A script can still change the frame's location: another site and the app are refused by the app page's `frame-src` and the app's `frame-ancestors 'none'`, and a frame page with more permissions loads empty, as a frame window gets its block once (above). The parent acts only on a message with that token, from that frame's window, while the app has activation too (a click in the frame gives it to its ancestors, and so does a click anywhere else in the app, which is why activation alone isn't enough): it opens `http(s)` links only (`bridgeLink`) with `noopener,noreferrer` and writes text with `navigator.clipboard`. Nothing reads or writes the app's data. **Focus**: a panel's script can focus its own document at any time, which would take the keys typed in the composer (and, with them, the activation the bridge's actions need). So a frame keeps focus only once the user pressed in it, which its bootstrap reports as a signed `rp:focus` on a trusted `pointerdown` or `pointerup` (a touch activates the page only on release; the parent then gives the frame focus, if it took it back already), or tabbed to it from the app (a Tab key press in the app just before). The parent can see the focus move before the pointer's arrival over the frame (its pointer events wait for its next frame, so a busy host makes them late): it then takes focus back at once, which blurs the field the press focused, and the press's `rp:focus` gives the frame focus back without that field. So the bootstrap keeps the element a trusted press focused (a `focusin` within 2 s of it) and, when the frame's window gets focus back within those 2 s with nothing focused, focuses it again (masterfix1: the first key typed after such a press was lost, all of them in a panel that doesn't refocus itself; `htmlScripts.spec.ts` "a press the app sees before the pointer's arrival", which holds the pointer's arrival back to make the order certain). Sending focus back is late, since the frame runs in its own process (and `inert` on the frame doesn't stop its own script in Chromium), so a key typed in that moment can still reach the panel. The bridge doesn't count keys: its actions need a pointer press in the frame (below). A panel that removes the bootstrap's listeners (`document.open`) only loses focus. The frame page's own policy has `sandbox allow-scripts`, so it is opaque however it's loaded; `/frame/lib/` answers `Origin: null` only for a path that stays under it once decoded and normalized.

Otherwise it runs the prompt scripts on the templates the history stage left (as `lore-scan` does), then takes each message's text after its prompt scripts: from depth `n` on it becomes `htmlDepthForm(text, mode)`, and a message nearer than `n` whose form would differ is marked volatile, so the cache breakpoint goes before it as for a depth-bound script. Nothing stored changes. Assembler version 58 includes the depth stage and bounded linear code-delimiter scans. HTML is read by `parse5`'s tokenizer, the one the client's renderer (rehype-raw) uses, driven with the tree builder's raw-text switches (textarea/title, style/xmp/iframe/noembed/noframes/noscript, script, plaintext; not inside SVG or MathML), so tags, quoted and unquoted attributes, comments, character references and raw bodies split where the browser splits them, never by regex: a custom `<style-note>` or `<head-line>` stays with its text, and a textarea shows its `<b>` as text. A `<` that Markdown shows as text but the tokenizer would open a bogus comment with (`</3`, `</>`, `<?` with no `?>` after it, `<!` without a letter) stays text; bytes no token covers (a tag cut off at the end) stay as written. Complete non-text elements and comments go before Markdown code spans are protected; code examples stay literal; output is a pure function of the text. `htmlDepthForm`: text without HTML comes back unchanged (its cache stays); fenced code stays as written, but a document block (the client's classifier: `html>`, `<head>` or `<body`) is reduced to its text, or dropped whole for `panels`; inline code stays; elsewhere only the elements HTML defines lose their tags (a model's `<status>` or reply-section tags stay), their text kept, `script`/`style`/`head`/`template`/`noscript` and comments dropped, a block's end and `<br>` a line break, a cell's end a space, HTML character references decoded as the tokenizer decodes them (none in raw text), doctypes removed and unfinished non-text elements dropped through the end. The setting is "HTML in older messages sent to the model" in the chat's settings (`chatSettingSections` `settings.html-depth`, order 16): **Send** As written / Text only / Leave out panels, each explained beside it, and, unless as written, **Older than** 1 to 20 messages. Tests: `server/test/htmlDepth.test.ts` (the form), `server/test/assembler.test.ts` (each mode, script-before-trimming order, disabling the registered stage, the depth, the breakpoint before the first message still to change, and none once settled), `server/test/chatSetup.test.ts` (the cast change from a position, absent before it); `e2e/htmlDepth.spec.ts` (the setting's choices, kept through a reload, the layout audit, at 1440/390 in light/dark).
- **External message media** (`net/externalMedia.ts`, `api/externalMedia.ts`, `db/externalMedia.ts`, `features/chat/externalMedia.tsx`; htmlstep45 step 5, 2026-11-12; spec/HTML-MESSAGES.md §3.2/§3.5/§5, [P]). `GET /media/external?url=…&chat=…&card=…` requires the app’s authenticated account and at least one owned, live chat or card. Consent is checked in the reader worker before network I/O and again before returning bytes. After authentication, the route requires `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` or `none` before checking consent or fetching: cross-site/same-site embeds, opaque panels and missing metadata fail closed even for cookieless local accounts. Non-browser clients must supply this header explicitly. `media.external`, an account-owned registered settings row, holds a blocked-by-default account choice and independent card/chat overrides; the chat wins, then the card, then the default. `GetExternalMediaPrefs` and `SetExternalMedia` are authenticated RPCs; the writer merges one choice atomically and checks ownership, and `null` clears an override. Imported documents never supply these settings. No baseline change or stored message form.
  - **Transport**: the replaceable/disableable `media.external` fetcher in `ExternalMedia.fetchers` uses `Network.fetchFor` with an address validator on every hop, without card-source private-host bypasses. Only HTTP/HTTPS URLs without credentials, at most 8192 characters, are accepted. Hostnames resolve through c-ares (A and AAAA, a resolver per request, 2 s per try, cancelled when the request ends), never `dns.lookup`: getaddrinfo holds one of libuv's four shared threads (file reads, zlib, scrypt) for its whole timeout and cannot be cancelled, so names whose DNS never answers could stall the server (`server/test/externalMediaDns.test.ts`). Every DNS answer must be public: IPv4 private, loopback, unspecified, link-local/metadata, CGNAT, special/reserved/multicast/documentation ranges and Azure’s platform address are refused; IPv6 must be global unicast, excluding protocol assignments, documentation and 6to4, so mapped/local/NAT64 destinations cannot bypass IPv4 checks. Network connects to the checked literals, retaining the original Host and TLS identity, including through the configured instance proxy. Redirects are same-origin only, at most five, resolved and validated again. Requests carry only fixed Accept/Accept-Encoding headers, no browser cookies, authorization, referrer, range or cache validators. The total deadline (DNS, headers and body) is 15 seconds, and both declared and decompressed streamed bodies are capped at 16 MiB. Only PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/AVIF and a fixed audio MIME allowlist return after `file-type` sniffs at most 4100 bytes of a recognized media signature and the detected MIME matches the declared one (APNG/WAV/M4A aliases normalized). Archive signatures are refused before the general detector can allocate or decompress their metadata; ID3 tags are skipped with checked synchsafe sizes and at most eight tags; unrecognized or mismatched bodies fail closed, including audio containers the detector identifies only as video; SVG, HTML, scripts, videos and generic binary types are refused. Responses forward no upstream headers, use `nosniff`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and a dedicated `sandbox; default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` CSP, preserved by RequestGuard. There is no disk/shared/browser HTTP cache or 304 path that can outlive consent.
  - **Resource limits** (`net/mediaLimits.ts`): the ExternalMedia service owns per-user token buckets (60 initial requests, replenished at one per second), at most eight simultaneous downloads per user and 32 instance-wide. Excess work gets 429 with Retry-After before opening a connection; interruption and failures release slots. Idle buckets expire after one minute.
  - **Rendering and controls**: `display.external-media` is a registered chat provider. The existing blocked-media note offers explained **Allow for this card** / **Allow for this chat** actions (only the chat action when an explicit chat block wins). The Interface panel has the account default; This chat has its override; the card editor’s shared Panels section has its override in both compact and large editors. Account queries refresh after writes, cross-tab notices and focus. While display text belongs to earlier sources, media stays blocked. With consent, HTML and Markdown image sources, simple remote `srcset` candidates, SVG image references, input/background images, audio sources and simple CSS `url()` values become scoped proxy URLs. CSS `url()`s are proxied by the scoper as it writes them (Styles, above): a `url()` inside a string stays text, and proxy addresses percent-encode quotes and brackets. Other loading CSS constructs stay refused; `@import` stays removed. Audio has controls, no autoplay and no preload. Video and tracks stay out. Data images remain local, and the app’s `img-src` stays self/data/blob; `media-src` is also self/data/blob. The opaque frame’s separate script/internet approval is unchanged.
  - **CSS review hardening (review3-htmlstep45)**: superseded by the token-level scoper (Styles, above); its size, depth and loading-function refusals carry over.
  - **HTML reduction work bound (review3-htmlstep45)**: assembler version 58 uses linear scans for fenced blocks and paired backtick runs; the prior code-span backreference regex could stall a reader worker on unmatched delimiters. Code-span protection advances through sorted spans once. Inputs above 200,000 UTF-16 code units retain their as-written, inspectable form without truncation. Tokenization and emission remain iterative at arbitrary tag nesting. The hostile maximum-size regression corpus must finish two identical reductions within two seconds per case (`htmlDepth.test.ts`, slow tag). Historical request inspection always shows the exact sent form, including retained hidden-element text in the as-written fallback.
  - **DNS review hardening (review3-htmlstep45)**: c-ares questions use absolute names with a terminal dot, so resolver search domains cannot change the checked host. Already-aborted requests start no resolver. Synthetic DNS tests cover IPv6-only and dual answers, a CNAME response, hosts-file independence and explicit cancellation at the total deadline; the checked literals remain the only retry/redirect destinations.
  - **Media port bound (review3-htmlstep45)**: external media accepts destination ports 80 and 443 only, including explicit web ports. All other ports are refused before DNS or a connection. This is a built delta from the otherwise silent HTML-MESSAGES proposal.
  - **Local-address exclusion (review3-htmlstep45)**: every hop samples all local interfaces and rejects their addresses even when publicly numbered. Node BlockList compares IPv6 values canonically; alternate spellings and DNS answers cannot reach a local interface. Loopback/private exclusions still apply independently.
  - **Bounded transport pools (review3-htmlstep45)**: Network retains at most 128 route/IP/SNI/Host dispatchers. Before reuse or creation it evicts entries idle for a minute; at capacity it closes the oldest idle entry, refusing a new route when all entries have active responses. Response completion, error and upgrade release activity. Layer shutdown closes all retained and already-evicted dispatchers.
  - **Media body storage (review3-htmlstep45)**: downloads stream into private, per-request temporary files, with awaited writes of at most 64 KiB and a 16 MiB decompressed size cap. Native byte streams use 64 KiB BYOB reads; replaceable transports with default streams retain at most their current supplied chunk. Sniffing reads at most 4100 bytes at a time and seeks past bounded ID3 metadata. Only a fully validated file is streamed back, with 64 KiB file reads and downstream backpressure; the request scope holds its limiter slot and removes the file on success, failure, revocation or disconnect. This is transient storage, not a reusable cache. The former two body-sized buffers (about 32 MiB/request, 1 GiB at 32 slots) are gone: application read/write/sniff working buffers are below 132 KiB/request (about 4.2 MiB for 32 slots), plus bounded HTTP/TLS/decompression and filesystem-stream queues; transient disk content is at most 512 MiB across 32 slots. Kernel page cache and runtime/transport overhead are additional, not claimed as a process RSS ceiling.
  - **Media reload queue (review3-htmlstep45)**: the client shares a four-download queue across the live HTML renderer, including Markdown/HTML/srcset/SVG images, audio, style attributes and constructed CSS. A 429 releases its active queue slot, waits the Retry-After interval (seconds or HTTP date, at least one second), then retries while a view still needs it. Pending resources use an inert data image; success uses a live-view blob URL. Duplicate live views share a download; final unmount or consent revocation cancels queued/active work and revokes the blob. Nothing is persisted across reloads, and no HTTP media cache is added. Only actual media attributes and parsed CSS URL tokens enter the queue: scoped CSS supplies its collected URL list, while inert strings, selector text and embedded data-URI text never trigger prefetch. Existing consent surfaces and layout remain the same; the externalMedia browser spec exercises 429 recovery and reloads at 1440/390 in both themes.
  - **Verification**: `server/test/externalMediaNetwork.test.ts` tests address classes after resolution, numeric URL tricks, mixed answers, each redirect refusal, DNS rebinding, credentials/schemes, MIME/size/deadline caps and fixed headers. `server/test/externalMedia.test.ts` exercises authentication, ownership, consent precedence/reset/revocation, no-store, disabling the part, and literal pinning/Host preservation through the real Network proxy transport. The isolation matrix covers both RPCs, the worker check and the HTTP route. `client/test/htmlMessages.test.ts` covers media and CSS rewrites; `e2e/externalMedia.spec.ts` covers blocked/no-request behavior, consent, loaded images/CSS, persisted overrides and the existing settings/editor surfaces at 1440/390 in both themes with layout audits. `e2e/layoutAudit.spec.ts` has `LAYOUT_AUDIT_HTML_MESSAGES_ONLY=1` for the chat/Interface settings and both card editor sizes.
- **Saved card media** (`savedMedia/extract.ts`, `api/savedMedia.ts`, `db/savedMedia.ts`, `shared/savedMedia.ts`, `ui/html/savedMedia.ts`, `features/savedMedia/`; rehost1, 2026-11-12; spec/SAVED-MEDIA.md). Media a library entry names on other sites is downloaded once, when the entry is saved or imported, and shown from this server; the entry's document, its export and what the model sees never change (owner [D]).
  - **Finding**: an `AFTER INSERT` trigger on `entity_revisions` queues every revision whose document holds `//` in `saved_media_scans`. The `SavedMedia` service (registry `media.saved`, a scoped background loop) reads queued revisions in a reader worker (`ReadSavedMediaScans`) and lists their media with the renderer's own tokenizers (`extract.ts`): parse5's HTML tokenizer for `src`, `srcset`, `poster`, `background`, `<source>`, SVG `href`/`xlink:href` and `<style>`/`style` contents; `@csstools/css-tokenizer` for CSS `url()` (fonts inside `@font-face`); a Markdown image pattern. Links, bare addresses and the avatar field aren't media. Addresses with macros or regex captures, credentials, non-web schemes or over 8192 characters are skipped (`mediaKey` normalizes: `//` becomes https, the fragment goes); at most 200 a revision. `RecordSavedMediaScans` writes one `saved_media` row per account and address (state `approval`, `pending`, `saved`, `failed`, `declined`) and the `revision_media` links, in one transaction.
  - **Approved sites**: `media.saved.hosts`, an account setting (registered `MediaHosts`), starts as `cardex.zip` exact (the card archive's mirrored images, `https://cardex.zip/i/<hash>.<ext>`). An entry matches a host exactly or, with `subdomains`, the host and everything under it, lowercased without a trailing dot. A scanned address on an approved host is `pending`, otherwise `approval`. `ListMediaApproval` (these refs' current revisions, or the whole account) scans first, then lists waiting hosts with file counts per kind; `DecideMediaApproval` applies Approve (adds the host), Approve with subdomains, This time only (`once`: these rows only, same-host redirects only) or Don't download (`declined`) in one transaction. `ChangeMediaHosts` adds or removes a host; adding one moves its waiting rows to `pending`; removing one keeps what was saved and returns unstarted, no-longer-approved downloads to approval. The downloader reads the current list before DNS and again after DNS on every hop; queued work never relies on the list captured at admission.
  - **Downloading**: four at once on the server, two per account; per revision a process-local 128 MiB / 3-minute budget (up to 2,000 recent revision budgets). Every received decompressed chunk is charged, including refused files and concurrent downloads; a file deadline is also capped by the remaining revision time. A bounded in-flight transport chunk can arrive at the limit; no subsequent file starts once exhausted. The fetcher is `net/externalMedia.ts`'s (c-ares, public addresses only, local interfaces excluded, pinned connections, ports 80/443, fixed headers, 15 s, 16 MiB, fonts 4 MiB) with the saved types (`SAVED_MEDIA_TYPES`: images, audio, MP4/WebM video, WOFF/WOFF2/TTF/OTF; SVG refused), the type sniffed from the bytes, never the response header, and `allowHost` checked on every hop: a redirect to another host goes only to an approved one (`Network.fetchFor`'s `crossOriginRedirect`). No transaction is open while downloading. Bytes go to the content-addressed media store under a `MediaHolds` hold, then `RecordSavedMediaResult` records the file or the user-facing reason (`failureReason`). `RetrySavedMedia` re-queues an entry's failed rows on still-approved hosts. Tests disable the fetcher (`test/support/config.ts`); `FAKE_SAVED_MEDIA=on` (browser tests, `dev/fakeSavedMedia.ts`) answers with a synthetic PNG and never downloads.
  - **Serving**: `GET /media/saved/<media id>` for the owning account only (others get 404), with the stored type, `nosniff`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`, `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox; default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and `Vary: Cookie, <proxy identity header>` so a later login cannot reuse an earlier account’s response without authorization; validators still require ownership.
  - **Showing**: `LookupSavedMedia` maps up to 500 addresses to the account's saved files. The client's store (`ui/html/savedMedia.ts`) answers the renderer synchronously from what it knows and batches the rest; `proxyMediaUrl` (the one chokepoint for HTML attributes, Markdown images, `style` attributes and stylesheets) returns `/media/saved/<id>` for a saved address, a blank `data:` placeholder while the lookup is unanswered or the file downloads (asked again every 3 s), and otherwise follows consent unchanged (blocked, or `/media/external`). Lookup errors remain placeholders and retry; only a successful lookup can permit the proxy fallback. An install/forget generation discards stale replies and polling callbacks, including across accounts. Until the signed-in shell installs the lookup (`features/savedMedia` registers `savedMedia.expect()`), every remote address is a placeholder, so nothing reaches another site before it's asked about. Each answer that changes something bumps a revision that re-keys the Streamdown processors and the message stylesheet. Saved audio plays without consent; video stays out. The hardener allows `/media/saved/` images. Every accepted remote address in a sheet is fetched up front by the existing queue, whatever selectors match, so a stateful rule (`:checked ~ …`) reveals nothing when it applies, saved or proxied. `externalMedia.spec.ts` counts every request with no-store/no-cache responses across checkbox, hover, `:has()`, attribute, media/container and animation changes, and a font whose only mapped glyph is added later: no extra request. `image-set()` remains refused and `unicode-range` remains stripped by the existing CSS policy; there is no additional state-selector ban.
  - **UI**: the approval dialog (in `appBanners`, `SavedMediaHost.tsx`) opens after a batch on the Import page, after adding a card from a card source and when a finished ST folder import is first seen (every waiting file); it lists only undecided sites. The card, preset and lorebook editors get a **Saved media** section (counts, Review, failures with reasons, Try again); **Settings → Media sites** lists, adds and removes sites and opens the dialog for every waiting file.
  - **Lifetime**: purging an entry deletes its revisions and their `revision_media` rows; the hourly media sweep first runs `PruneSavedMedia` (rows no revision names, and files nothing else uses), then removes unreferenced bytes.
  - **Verification**: `server/test/savedMedia.test.ts` (extraction; a local HTTP server behind a forwarding transport: approval before any request, private and rebinding addresses, redirects, sniffed types, SVG/HTML refused, size limits, no identifying headers, one download per address, owner-only serving, unchanged export, retry, prune); `isolation.test.ts` covers the seven RPCs; `client/test/savedMediaLookup.test.ts`, `htmlMessages.test.ts`; `e2e/savedMedia.spec.ts` (dialog, saved display with no request to any other origin, editor section, settings page, layout audits at 1440 and 390, light and dark).
