Pruning defers an account’s unreferenced rows until its scan queue is empty, then still requires all other asset references to be gone. No network runs in writer transactions. The seven saved-media RPCs are explicitly excluded from agent operation exposure.

- **ST 1.19 formatting** (`ui/stFormatting.ts`; DESIGN §10.2, built 2026-10-29) uses ST's six double-quote pairs and nearest-closing-delimiter regex, with no match across a newline or inside code. AST quote nodes preserve their original glyphs; italics inside quotes inherit the quote colour. As with ST’s default `encode_tags=false`, straight quotes inside `<...>` tags are shielded from dialogue matching. Both asterisks and underscores give italics, double/triple underscores give underline, and double asterisks remain bold. The underline AST uses sanitizer-approved `ins`, then a React component renders `u`; no HTML permission was added. Soft line breaks become `br`; blank lines still separate paragraphs. ST's `fixMarkdown(text, true)` runs on every message, completed or streaming: it removes adjacent horizontal whitespace from paired marks, then closes odd asterisks and straight quotes per line. Its original behavior is retained, including not closing underscores/curly quotes, touching code whitespace, and the quote check winning when both checks match one line. This changes display only; stored, copied, edited and prompt text stays original. The former remend display pass and direct dependency are removed. Reference links still receive only their needed definitions across blocks (`ui/referenceDefinitions.ts`, at most 32 KB copied per message, never into an open code fence). `markdown.test.ts` covers the formatting, protections and effective renderer replacement/wrapping/addition/disable/restore; `messageColors.test.ts` covers visible settings controls. `e2e/messageFormatting.spec.ts` checks rendering, inherited quote colour, colour persistence/reset, unchanged stored text and production CSP at 1440/390 in both themes.

- **Copying a selection** (`ui/sourcePositions.ts`, `ui/messageCopy.tsx`; built 2026-10-30). Actual message and reasoning prose opts in through `MessageBody`; editors, composer, previews and other text keep native copy. The registered `message.source-copy` entry in `messageCopyHandlers` can be replaced, wrapped, disabled or superseded by a higher-order handler. The ST renderer preserves parser positions through quote/underline/soft-break wrapping, carries UTF-16 source ranges through `fixMarkdown` and CRLF normalization, and attaches trusted DOM metadata after sanitization. Per-block plugin options keep Streamdown's processor cache from sharing offsets between blocks/messages; unchanged blocks retain their memoized parser pipeline while streaming. Contiguous text uses a compact offset; escapes, entities and display repairs carry individual ranges. Display-only closings, list numbering, code-frame labels and blocked-image caption labels have no stored text. Image hardening keeps its existing policy/output and retains only the original image position and alt text for mapping. Code maps the body independently of its frame, retaining logical line breaks between the rendered line elements; empty-line filler glyphs contribute no extra break in either clipboard flavour. Selecting an element's first/last rendered character includes its stored opening/closing markup; partial selections copy exactly the stored slice between their endpoints, without balancing marks. Several selected bodies contribute slices in DOM order separated by a blank line. Selections starting or ending outside message bodies retain the browser’s selected outside text and layout breaks around the mapped slices; temporary native-text reads restore the selection and its direction. Keyboard Copy and native menu/phone Copy use the copy event; native selection drags use the same effective registered handler through dragstart, without cancelling the drag or overriding an unrelated link/image drag. The handler writes both `text/plain` (stored slices) and `text/html` (selected rendered fragments with their formatting, without provenance attributes). Rich fragments retain code-line newlines and suppress native quote pseudo-glyphs without relying on the app stylesheet. Streaming bodies use their current live text, and reasoning uses its own stored/live text. Whole-message menu Copy text still copies the complete stored content. Nothing in the app cancels `contextmenu` (owner, 2026-11-01: the browser's own menu wherever there's text), so the browser's Copy, and a phone's selection menu, reach this handler; `e2e/textActions.spec.ts` dispatches a `contextmenu` over message text, the composer and an open editor and checks it isn't prevented. `sourceText` lets the renderer align transformed display text to storage with a bounded diff: replacements refer to their original range and display-only insertions have no source. Replacement renderers supply the same `data-source-map` contract or replace the copy handler. `test/sourceCopy.test.ts` covers every built-in text formatting kind, partial edges, reference/repeated blocks, repairs, literal HTML, escapes/entities, CRLF, emoji and alt captions; `e2e/messageCopy.spec.ts` grants Chromium clipboard permissions and exercises whole/partial/across-message and mixed outside selections, keyboard and browser Copy commands, native drag transfers, rich HTML, repairs, code (including selected blank-line breaks), native editing, streaming and reasoning at desktop/phone widths.
- **Message colours** are semantic theme tokens in `styles.css`: main text, italics, underline and quote. Dark defaults are ST's `#dcdcd2`, `#919191`, `#bce7cf`, `#e18a24`; light defaults are `#303039`, `#666666`, `#286044`, `#925000`, chosen for AA contrast against the message background. The Interface panel exposes four labelled colour inputs and individual Reset buttons (`MessageColors.tsx`). Nullable hex-colour patches (`mainTextColor`, `italicsTextColor`, `underlineTextColor`, `quoteTextColor`) use the existing account-owned display preferences; null follows the current theme. The registered `app.tools` contribution `display.message-colors` applies these tokens throughout the authenticated app, including portal previews, and clears overrides when unmounted. Theme changes update default colour swatches.
- **A message** (`Message.tsx`): the speaker's avatar and name (the card's, the persona's for the user's turns; an edit or a written version keeps the message's speaker, and an older one without a speaker shows another version's, or the first version's, deleted or not), and its side as the context reads it (`sideOf`: a card the user plays is the user's, another of the cast the model's, else `PathEntry.side`), which decides its presentation, its time (short, the full date in a tooltip), its number on the path (`#n`, counted from 1 as the inspector and the summaries count), and its state: generating, stopped, interrupted, failed (with its cause in the body), refused, edited. The Stop of a generating version is in its header, always shown.
  - **Versions** are at the end of the message, as in ST, where a swipe that changes the text's length leaves them on the last message: `‹ 3/7 ›` on every message. A single version keeps `‹ 1/1 ›`, with the unavailable previous/next arrows and picker disabled and explained. Model-written turns on either side, whatever their depth, keep an available › to generate another (`VersionControls.tsx`); it stays visible too. The counter opens `VersionPicker.tsx`: a scrollable desktop popover or full-height phone sheet with numbered two-line previews, writer/model and time, star/hide buttons, a starred filter and a Hidden section. **Find and sort** (smallui1, 2026-11-14; audit item 007, ST-COMPARISON:224): under the filter row, a **Find in versions** field keeps the versions whose text has the typed words (any case; the starred filter and the Hidden section apply to what it finds) and their preview shows the text around the first match with it marked; "No version has “…”" when none does. A sort menu beside it, with the chat list's Menu pattern and an explanation per choice: Order written (default), Newest first, Longest first, Shortest first, Starred first, ties in the order written (`arrange`). Numbers stay each version's own (#4 stays #4 in any order). Both are the picker's own state while the message is on screen in this tab (reopening keeps them), never stored or in the URL; the list follows typing through `useDeferredValue`. `test/versionArrange.test.ts` covers matching, every sort and fifty 20,000-character versions; `e2e/versionSearch.spec.ts` filters, sorts, keeps the Hidden section and starred filter, compares and picks among fifty long versions at 1440 and 390 in both themes with the picker's layout audit. A version row's thin selection border is a declared inset exception (its pick button and star/hide fill the row, as before). Hidden versions stay selectable there but leave the arrows' cycle; hiding a version does not hide its message from context. Compare selects two versions for both texts (side by side on desktop, stacked on phones) or the editor's `ValueDiff`. Past the last visible version, › generates another when the slot has model-written text; a horizontal swipe on touch does the same. A swipe is a touch drag of more than 60 px, at least twice as wide as tall, that starts on the message (`swipeCanStart` in `Message.tsx`): never on a control (button, link, input, textarea, select, summary, menu item), in an editor (a contenteditable such as CodeMirror's, any `role=textbox`, a label), or while the message is being edited; a `pointercancel` (the browser took the drag to scroll) drops it, and a pointerup with a text selection is no swipe (parity finding 2). The version arrows and picker are unaffected. `e2e/messageGestures.spec.ts` covers each case at 390 px. Picker previews and both comparison views subscribe to each version’s live text. Comparisons retain version IDs and resolve current content, status and model from the updated list, so they follow streaming through completion. Session version listeners update open lists and comparisons even when an unselected version changes in another tab.
  - **Actions** (`messageActions.tsx`, above; owner, 2026-11-01). The message's **More actions** menu (`ui/Menu.tsx`) lists every action available on it, in the registry's order with a separator between groups (change it, put something beside it, what the model sees and where it came from, copy, delete). Each row is `MenuItemWithCheckbox`: a `menuitem` that runs the action and closes the menu, with the action's icon and short label (a disabled one, Duplicate while writing, says why under it), and beside it a separate `menuitemcheckbox` named "Show ⟨label⟩ on the message" that pins or unpins it as a button on the message without closing the menu or running anything. Arrow keys reach the item, then its checkbox; Space or Enter toggles the checkbox; typeahead goes to the actions only. Each has a tooltip at the side (the action's to the left of the menu, the checkbox's to the right, clear of the rows below), and the same text as its accessible description. On a touch screen (`pointer: coarse`) rows are 44 px high and the checkbox a 44 px square. The pinned ones are icon buttons with the same tooltip, shown on hover or focus on a wide screen (always on a touch screen without hover), and on a narrow one after a tap on the message, below its text, with why it isn't sent (when it isn't) just above them, so scrolling the actions into view keeps the reason's start in view. They follow the menu's order, and an action a message doesn't offer isn't on it, pinned or not. By default Edit (its tooltip names the double-click and the composer's ↑), Continue where it applies, Branch from here and Delete version (Delete message when it has only one, DESIGN §6.2) are pinned. **Which are pinned** is the account's (`DisplayPrefs.messageToolbar`, a map of action id to pinned, over each action's `pinned` default; an id no action has is ignored): `messageActionPins` holds it for every host, fed and saved by the `display.message-toolbar` app tool (`MessageToolbarPreferences.tsx`), which shows a change at once and asks the server to merge only that id, so two devices pinning different actions keep both. **Many pins:** the toolbar takes the header's remaining width (the footer's, before the versions, on a phone) and shows the pinned buttons that fit beside More actions, measured as rendered (`useFit`, a `ResizeObserver`); the rest stay in the menu, still ticked, the checkbox's tooltip saying the row is full. It never wraps the message or scrolls sideways. **Icons:** no two actions share one: New version with guidance… has the composer's Guidance switch icon, Insert above and below their own, Delete message (every version) a bin with contents, apart from Delete version's empty bin. **Labels** are short, the tooltip carrying the detail (Delete message's says how many versions go). There is no Regenerate (owner, 2026-11-01): every model-written turn, on either side (a reply, a refused reply, a persona's generated turn), has the version arrows' ›, which past its last version generates another, as Regenerate did. Before the last version › steps to the next one, so another version from there takes stepping to the last. To generate with another model, choose it below the composer and then swipe (owner, 2026-11-02; nomodelretry); each version keeps the model it was written with. There is no message model-picker action or refusal-specific model picker. Stored pins for removed or unknown action ids are ignored when the toolbar reads the registered actions, including the former `message.regenerate-with` pin. The shared model-choice reader remains for settings pickers: it reads connections four at a time with a 20 s limit per connection, keeping successful lists if another fails. Copy text copies the text shown (streamed so far while it generates); Request it was generated from opens the request inspector (§15). The composer has Send as and Generate (above; "Send" and "Reply" when the user plays no card); it has no regenerate of its own (owner, 2026-11-01: the latest reply's ›, shown without a hover, is the swipe); Stop belongs to each generating version (DESIGN §3.1). Typing re-renders nothing else. Nothing waits for a reply: a send during one is queued (below).
  - **Editing** (Edit, Write your own version) opens an editor in the message, in place and focused with the caret at the end of the text. **A double-click on the message** (`onDoubleClick` in `Message.tsx`) invokes the effective `message.edit` (its availability, override or disablement), with the caret where the double-click landed: the browser's caret at the point (`caretPositionFromPoint`, else `caretRangeFromPoint`) mapped to the stored text through the body's source map (`sourceOffsetAt` in `ui/messageCopy.tsx`), used only when the body's source text is the version's content, else the end. Not while it generates or is being edited, nor from a control, a link, the version arrows and picker, an image, a label or a text-action bar (`canEditFrom`). It waits 450 ms (owner, 2026-11-01: long enough for a relaxed triple-click): any press within it (a triple-click's third, selecting the paragraph, or another action begun) cancels it, and so does a double-click drag that selected several words, so both still select text to copy; a plain drag never makes a double-click. When the wait ends it opens only on the version double-clicked, still finished and not already being edited. The word a double-click selects is the trade (owner, 2026-11-01). `e2e/textActions.spec.ts` covers the caret, triple-click, drag and a control at 1440 and 390 px. When the editor's text first takes focus, the row of Save and Cancel under it scrolls into view (`Message.tsx`), so a long message's editor opens with its end and its buttons on screen (ST's in-place edit, audit §7). It reads as a plain text box: its change markers (`quietMarkers` in `ui/codeChanges.ts`, a `CodeEditor` option) show only while the text differs from the saved text, keeping the gutter's width so the text doesn't shift, and unchanged lines carry no mark. Save and Cancel sit directly under the text, with the `message.editor.tools` contributions at the end of that row: the attach button (`message.editor-images`; the version's images on a line of their own above the row) and one History menu (`message.edit-history`, `editorHistory.tsx`) holding “Earlier draft text…” and “Compare with saved text…” (a dialog with the full comparison, offered once the text differs). An edit of a generated version, saved as a new one (DESIGN §3.1 [D]), says “Saved as version N” beside the counter for six seconds. Its text is a server draft (`messageDraft.ts`, the drafts above), held by the chat's session rather than the row, so a message scrolled out of the virtualized list keeps it: saved 400 ms after typing and when the page is hidden or the chat closed, read back with `MessageDrafts` when the chat opens, so a reload opens each editor again, on its version or message, with its text. Save names the draft to commit with the version, and once the version is saved drops the browser copy of exactly the text it submitted: text typed while the version was being saved stays in the editor, which stays open, with its copy, its pending save and its base (the draft it was typed on, whose ended session the server reopens with it). An edit that made a new version leaves that editor on the version edited, reached by its arrows. Cancel discards it to the recovered texts, and while the server doesn't have the text yet it refuses and keeps the editor open. As for summaries, every change also leaves a copy in this browser (§3.10 invariant 4, `backup.ts` kind `message`, the `SaveMessageDraft` payload as typed, filed under `messages:<chat>` with the editor as its field), replacing only this editor's copy not on its way to the server; a save's success deletes the copy it sent and re-files what was typed since on the new draft, and a failure keeps it. Opening the chat replays its copies, oldest first, once the chat's drafts are read, opening each editor again with the text the server took, or with what it still doesn't have and the error. So text typed while the server is unreachable survives a closed tab. The editor keeps its base apart from the draft the server last answered with: text shown from a copy the server refused keeps that copy's draft id, row version and session through retries and more typing, and the base moves only when the server answers a save with exactly the text sent, so the retry goes on top of text saved elsewhere meanwhile instead of being typed over it. Replays and saves run one at a time, in order. A replay (or the first save of a refused replay's text) that goes over text saved elsewhere shows the composer's notice (`ReplayNotice`: both times and the other text) until acknowledged, through typing; “Use the other text” restores the displaced text explicitly, keeping the browser text in the draft history. “Earlier draft text” (the summary editor's button, the message editor's History menu) lists every retained state (up to the common 1,000-state cap), including after reload. Escape closes its dialog without cancelling the message edit, including while focus is still on the editor’s history trigger before modal focus moves; `e2e/messageHistory.spec.ts` exercises that focus interval explicitly. Restores run with saves in order; text typed during a restore stays in the box with its browser copy. The registered `message.edit-history` and `summary.draft-history` contributions use `message.editor.tools` and `summary.editor.tools` slots. The registered `message.amendments` action opens saved amendment history for human-written versions, with full earlier text and an optimistic restore in the fork captured when the dialog opened. `e2e/messageHistory.spec.ts` exercises both editors and saved amendment restores at 1440 and 390 pixels in light and dark, including Escape from the history dialog without cancelling the message edit. `e2e/chatViewDrafts.spec.ts` holds a Write and an Edit's commit while more is typed, fails a replay once before a retry over another device's text, and replays over another device's text.
- **The composition scratchpad** (DESIGN §3.1 [D]; scratchpad, 2026-11-06; `Composition.tsx`, `composition.ts`, `compositionActions.tsx`): the user's own version of a message is its "Write your own version" draft (`scratchpad`, keyed by the slot, above), so it persists, survives a reload and becomes a version with **Add as a new version** (`WriteVersion`, a `user_written` version, selected; "Saved as version N" beside the counter, as an edit's). While it's open the message keeps the version shown above the editor, in a bordered box (region "Version shown") whose bar sits over the text: the message's version controls (the `message.versions` contribution, moved there from the footer while composing, so stepping to a version of another length never moves them) and the registered `textActions` for that version's stored text (`EditorTextActions` with a `scope`: `ownVersion`, the target `{ name, add }`). The chat registers **Add selection to your version** (`version.add-selection`, `editor: "selection"`) and **Add to your version** (`version.add-text`, `editor: "text"`); the snippets feature's Send text and Send selection to snippet show in the same bar. The selection is the rendered text's selection inside the box, read as stored text body by body (`selectedSourceText` in `ui/messageCopy.tsx`, the copy mapping without its moment of moving the selection; a selection that starts or ends inside italics, bold or strikethrough gets the marks it cut through, `*`/`_`, `**`/`__` or `~~` as the text used, so a piece never leaves a mark open or loses its formatting); a press on the bar keeps it, since a tap can collapse it before the click lands. The bar's buttons keep their places (the selection's come and go at its end-aligned start); the browser's own menu stays over the text. Touch swipes on the message still step versions while composing (only an edit stops them). `MessageDraft.append` adds text to the end after a blank line once the saved text is read, saved as typing is, and marks it for 1.6 s (`added`, the `CodeEditor`'s `flash`), leaving focus where it was. A snippet's own editor (`source: "snippet"`) offers the same two actions, to the composition used last that still shows (`registerComposition`/`compositionTarget`: opened, clicked or focused, most recent first, connected and passing `checkVisibility`), with a notice "Added to your version of message #N"; with none, Add to your version keeps its place disabled, "Open “Write your own version” on a message to add text to it." Two views of one chat in this tab (the workbench's frames, each its own `ChatSession`) share it: every server answer to a composition's draft (`share`) reaches the chat's other sessions (`viewsOf`), which open it or adopt the text unless text typed there isn't saved yet (`MessageDraft.adopt`), and adding it as a version or cancelling closes it there too (`closeEditor` → `peerClosed`, only when nothing typed there waits). Edits of a version aren't shared this way. `test/composition.test.ts` covers the offers, targets, appending and adoption; `e2e/composition.spec.ts` picks a selection from version 2, the whole of version 3 and a snippet's text, arranges, reloads, adds the result as version 5 and steps back (1440 light, 390 dark), shares one composition between two frames, keeps the italics of a selection that starts inside them, composes from an agent reply, and runs the layout audit on the composition at 1440, 1024 and 390 in both themes.
- **The branch switcher:** a message with alternates shows `‹ ⑂ 2/3 ›` (named "Branches: 2 of 3"), in its header, apart from its versions; the chat's header has the same switch for every place the path branches (above). A switch opens the fork through the alternate (above) at the message switched to, which the URL then names (`?fork=` unless it's the current fork, and `?slot=`); where the chat opens doesn't change until something is sent there. A new alternate arriving from another tab raises the count on the messages shown; a message another fork appended at the same tip (`PathEntry.forkId`) doesn't join the window.
- **Composer mode and phone layout** (`Composer.tsx`, `speaker.ts`): Guidance is an optimistic composer choice, scoped to the draft (§3.10). Its writes run in click order; a read after the last write accepts newer choices from other tabs, and a refused write rolls back with the control’s error. Enter and the visible Guidance switch use the same local mode while its server write waits. At viewport widths below 640 px the composer is the same strip and bar: the strip one row that scrolls sideways (its chips at most 9 rem, their popovers full width), the bar one row with the speaker's portrait alone, the input, attach, Guidance, Generate as an icon and Send. `e2e/composerQa.spec.ts` holds mode writes across submissions in both directions and asserts at least 422 px of conversation at 390×844 with five characters, three-line guidance and a warm cache (after dismissing the first-use impersonation notice); both themes also exercise the exposed controls. The suite also checks a newer composer choice arriving before readback, refusal/rollback and saving again; `test/speaker.test.ts` covers read/write ordering without wall-clock assumptions.
- **The composer's text is a server draft** (DESIGN §6.2; `composerDraft.ts`, `@rp/shared/composerApi.ts`): one per fork, the fork shown. `OpenComposer` (by fork; checks the chat and fork are the caller's and live), `SaveComposer` (600 ms after the last key), `ComposerHistory` and `RestoreComposer` (by the draft's id) act on the draft store of §3.10. Server calls run one at a time, in order.
  - **The text belongs to the draft it was typed into** (§3.10), kept apart from the fork the view asks for. Every save names that draft. Going to another fork opens its composer first, with the box read-only while its text loads: if it's the same draft (the view named the current fork it had), the text stays; otherwise the text is saved on its own draft, and the new fork's shows. The fork's tip moving (a message appended, or one deleted or restored) reads its draft again with the box open, for another tab's text. Going through several forks quickly shows only the last; each step saves on its own draft.
  - **Another tab's newer text** reaching this tab (the draft read again after a move, a send's reply, a save the server had already made): text not changed here takes it; text changed here is saved on top, the other text one step back in the history. The box's base changes only with its text (§3.10).
  - **A send** takes the text and its draft at the click, and the box empties: what's typed from then on is the next message. The text is saved on its draft, then sent in that draft's fork, at its tip, naming the draft, its session and the text (`composer`), so the server commits it in the send's transaction only if it still holds that text. If the view went to another fork meanwhile, it isn't sent, and stays in its own fork's composer. Once answered: a committed draft takes the next message; a draft another tab typed on meanwhile shows that tab's text, unless something was typed here since, which then goes on top of it. A send that didn't go puts its text back in the box, ahead of anything typed since.
  - **Recovered text:** text typed in this browser while offline in a session ended elsewhere, or another tab's text a send's commit took out of the history, is in the bin's recovered texts, and the box says so, with a link, until the page goes.
  - **Starting a branch** ("Branch from here") copies the composer into the fork made (`ChatSession.branchFrom`, `OpenComposer` with `copyFrom`). `composerWorkspace.ts` keeps the draft, its serialized save/send queue, busy state and operation errors with the chat session, across fork-scoped surface remounts. A remount therefore retains the source draft needed by `copyFrom`, and a held send rejected after switching forks remains visible as an error while its text stays in its original composer. `e2e/composer.spec.ts` covers both races against the real server; neither test’s contract was weakened.
  - **Leaving** follows the editors (§14.6): a hidden tab saves at once; closing or reloading with text not on the server asks first, and `pagehide` sends it with `keepalive` as `composers` in `POST /library/drafts` (§14.5), which `SaveComposer` saves, so it never recreates a moved or sent draft. While a send is out, that's the send's text if the server hasn't confirmed it, and what's typed since as `next`.
  - **This browser's copy** uses the editors' pending-save records (`backup.ts`, under `composer:<chat>`): each has an independent id and its original draft id, row version, session, text and `next` flag. RPC and keepalive send that same payload and acknowledge that copy's id; typing during a save leaves the newer copy intact. Typing replaces only this tab's unsent copy of the same draft; going to another draft leaves a copy that couldn't be saved in the browser, where it comes back as that draft's composer opens. Opening a composer replays every pending composer save unchanged, ordered by time with the send's text before its next message, and keeps every copy that fails, whatever the reason; one of the opened draft's shows in the box on its own base. Another draft's copies wait until they're 30 s old. The writer's operation receipts prevent an acknowledged save whose browser copy survived from resurrecting sent text or creating recovery. A replay over text saved elsewhere shows a warning with this browser copy's time and the writer's displaced-text time, a preview, Keep this browser's text, and Use the other text. The choice is an explicit restore, which cannot coalesce with typing and is itself undoable. Restore RPCs accept a picked `content` as well as a history position, bounded by the draft text cap and guarded by the draft id and row version, so the choice still works after history retention. The editors' per-user expiry and logout rules apply.
  - **History** (the History button): the draft's states, newest first; picking one restores it, itself undoable. It's restored only over the text the box showed at the pick, with nothing unsaved: if the box changed before it could go (calls before it were still out), it isn't. Text typed while it's on its way stays, saved on top of the restored state.
- **Deleting** shows a toast (`ui/Toast.tsx`, Base UI) with Undo and "Open the bin" (DESIGN §6.2), on messages, versions and chats, naming the chat by its readable name ("Deleted: Version of a message in “The Lantern Inn, started Apr 3, 2026”"). It stays 10 seconds (other toasts 8), and Base UI holds every toast while the pointer is over them or focus is in them.
- **Context membership:** the server publishes the next request’s history start in `Cache`, even before a first generation or without a TTL. Messages before that start have muted text, a dashed border and an accessible “Not in the context” icon labelled "Out of context". Deliberately hidden messages have a ghost labelled “Hidden from context” ("Hidden"), dimmed, without the dropped-message style. Each mark says why in its tooltip, and on a phone below the header once the message is tapped: where the history sent starts and the preset's budget that put it there (its name, maximum and target, from `NextContext.budget`), or that the user hid it and how to send it again (`PathEntry.hiddenByUser`), or that it was hidden in ST (an imported version), or that an empty message has nothing to send.
- **Hiding a message** (ST's ghost toggle; `e2e/hideMessage.spec.ts`): its "More actions" menu has **Hide from the model**, or **Show to the model again** on a hidden one. `SetMessageHidden` writes `SetSlotHidden` (§3.8) and publishes the slot; like an edit it starts no generation (DESIGN §8). The slot's event has `CacheWarmth` estimate again, which names a hidden message before the last breakpoint ("Message N was hidden."); stepped history treats a hide as any reduction before its start, and summaries covering the message go stale and fresh again by visibility, as for an ST-hidden run (§16, Freshness). `test/hideMessage.test.ts` checks the next request without and with it through a mock provider. A row before the first message sent says the same at the cut ("Messages above this aren’t sent to the model: the preset … allows …"). Boundaries are scoped to the path leaf, so an old event cannot mark another branch. Inactive paths use `GetNextContext(chatId, leafSlotId, forkId)` when opened and when a `Cache` event invalidates their estimate. Cache estimates carry their fork id, and an event for another fork sharing the same tip triggers a read of the viewed fork. The client checks the displayed fork, leaf and read generation before applying a result, so two tabs can show different branches without borrowing each other’s boundary. If next assembly fails, the server falls back to the nearest recorded start on that path.
- **A generated version** links to its context ("Context it was generated from", in its menu: the request inspector, §15), and shows the notes its context recorded, collapsed ("2 notes on its context"). Routine history truncation is filtered from this list, including older rollouts; it remains in the request inspector. **The cache-warmth indicator** sits above the composer (§15).
- **Notifications** (DESIGN §10.1; `features/notices.tsx`): `SubscribeNotices` streams the caller's notices: `ReplyFinished` when a generation ends complete or failed (`chat/Notices.ts`, published by `Generations`, per user, a bounded backlog of 256; overflow replaces pending notices with `UserDraftSync` and the newest event), not when stopped or interrupted. A reply in a chat this tab isn't showing, or while the tab is hidden, counts as unseen until that chat is open and visible: a badge on the chat in the list, the count in front of the tab's title, and a favicon with a dot (two static SVGs). Counts belong to the tab and go with a reload. **Optional completion sound** (U14; `features/completionSound.ts`, `completionSoundFeature.tsx`) registers as `notifications.completion-sound` in `noticeChannels` (`noticeContributions.tsx`): settings, interaction activation and unseen-reply playback resolve the effective entry, so replacing or disabling it changes all three without affecting badges or system notifications. The settings host subscribes to registry snapshots. Sound is off by default and saved per browser in Settings › Notifications, independently of system notifications. Enabling it, or interacting after a reload, activates Web Audio; an unseen complete or failed reply plays one short tone only while audio is running. A suspended or unavailable device skips the tone without queuing playback. Notice identities (version and terminal status) are deduplicated for the tab lifetime before badges, sound and system notifications, including retries of the subscription. Unit tests cover activation, suspension, opt-out, replay, channel replacement and disablement; browser tests exercise sound through real unseen completions, reload and touch activation. System notifications are a per-browser choice in Settings › Notifications: the page calls `Notification.requestPermission` only when the user turns them on, and the switch shows on only once the browser allows it. The registered Settings child uses the relative path `notifications`, so its navigation link opens `/settings/notifications`. `e2e/chatExtras.spec.ts` clicks that Settings link at 1440 and 390 pixels before exercising permission choices.
- **An unfinished ST import** (§13) shows as a badge, from the title's marker (`importState` in `stImportApi.ts`), not as part of the title.
- Card portraits use the authenticated media route (§14.5); initials are the fallback. **New chat** opens a pending chat with that card and saves a new peer chat on first send, rather than another root of the current chat.
- `e2e/chat.spec.ts` covers streaming, versions, stopping, editing, links, branches, deleting, another user, and the screens at phone and desktop width in both themes; `e2e/composer.spec.ts` the composer's drafts (reload, another tab, send, history, closing, a copy brought back) and its races, each with a request held on its way while the user goes on (typing during a send, a branch switched during one, another tab typing on, quick branch changes, a restore, starting a branch); `e2e/chatExtras.spec.ts` the branch switcher, Undo, the bin, recovered text, notifications, and asking for permission only when told to; `e2e/chatNotes.spec.ts` a note made in a chat reaching the request a fake provider receives through real generation (the production server, no fake generator), and leaving it once turned off, and a card's note edited from the chat as the card's; `e2e/inspector.spec.ts` the request inspector and the cache indicator; `e2e/cast.spec.ts` the Cast tab (absent, speak now, show card, add, write as, remove) and Edit opening the card used everywhere. `e2e/cardForkForChat.spec.ts` covers the Cast and card-panel actions, the fork dialog and its clash check, the new editor, branching three messages back with the fork retained, an existing sibling retaining the parent, and switching back through the family tree, at 1440 and 390 pixels in light and dark. `test/cardForkForChat.test.ts` checks the pinned source revision, note switches and version attachments, fork-local queue and composer updates, original message attribution, forking after a swapped-in card is purged, and full transaction rollback after a forced failure; `test/isolation.test.ts` probes the new RPC across users.

**Source-copy mapping cost (perfred1).** The ST formatter represents consecutive UTF-16 source offsets as runs. Ordinary unchanged blocks, including a displayed prefix while a stream's transforms catch up, pass one start/length pair to the source-position plugin; synthetic closing marks, display replacements and normalized CRLF retain explicit mappings where needed. `fixMarkdownMapped` still materializes its existing array contract for callers that need it. Streaming no longer allocates and serializes two offsets for every character of the completed prefix on every update. `sourceCopy.test.ts` guards serialization work as well as the existing stored-slice semantics; the message-copy and formatting browser specs cover the resulting markup and clipboard bytes.

**The performance harness** (`packages/client/perf/`, `npm run test:perf`; CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §7). The built client and the real server with bundled workers and the fake generator at 300 tokens a second per stream, on Chromium through Playwright, one worker.
- **Fixtures** (`fixtures.ts`, `fixtureWorker.ts`, version 6): the 100,000-message main path has 199 additional branches with 3,100–4,900-message paths (a shared prefix followed by 100 own messages). Many messages have 20–50 versions; the four-version sentinels, occasional HTML and original short side paths remain. This produces 119,960 slots, 200 forks and 805,415 versions. The summarized fixture has a 20,000-message main path with its first 18,000 covered, the same branch family, 39,912 slots and 447,962 versions. Two 300-message pacing chats remain (1,329 versions each). The server initializes a fresh baseline and creates the chats; a worker seeds SQLite, pauses/rebuilds fork labels and checkpoints the file. No fixture SQLite runs on the test coordinator thread. The expensive synthetic seed is cached per fixture version outside the run directory and copied for each scenario server.
- **Scenarios:** open at the bottom and 70,000 messages up; scroll the full length to the root, prepending about 1,650 pages of older history; six streams of 20 seconds, measuring renders, following at the bottom, typing in the composer, drift while scrolled up and prepending while they still run; swiping through versions; switching chats mid-stream and back; one reply streaming on past 4,000 tokens; three versions streaming at once under one slot, one shown; a bursty stream (300 tokens at once every second) and a slow one (4 tokens a second), each on a server of its own with the generator paced that way (`FAKE_GENERATOR_BURST_MS`, the development entry point only).
- **Measured:** long animation frames, frame intervals, Event Timing input durations, where the first loaded message is after older history lands above it (a message gone from the screen counts as an unbounded error), the distance from the end while the last reply grows, the JS heap after garbage collection at the start, every 400 pages and the end of the full scroll, renders of streaming bodies on screen per update to one of them, other bodies and rows re-rendered, and list renders (`features/chat/perf.ts` counts them, built in only with `VITE_PERF=1`, as `npm run test:perf` builds; elsewhere the counters, `mountedBodies` and `window.__rpPerf` are dead code and left out), delta gaps, the round trip of a trivial RPC while the streams run (the server's event loop carries every stream), and main-thread script time (CDP's `ScriptDuration`) while the long reply streams.
- **Harness readiness**: version assertions use their accessible counter names, chat switches use the existing sidebar and Back, and editor readiness uses the Save cluster state plus the mounted CodeMirror editor. The 100 imported prompt identifiers are counted independently of additional registered landmarks. The long-reply measurement requires at least twenty live updates so a stalled or ended stream cannot pass by measuring an idle browser. Panel-switch counters start after the initial cast read settles and two animation frames commit it, separating initial row data from tab-induced renders. A missing action has a 30-second timeout; the full-scroll test retains its 30-minute timeout.
- **Budgets** (`budgets.ts`) fail the run. They're set from runs on this shared 48-core host at load averages of 30 to 90, with headroom for that load. One run at load 33 (2026-10-12):

| Full scroll, 1,666 older pages | anchoring error 0 px; heap 7.2 → 11.3, 12.1, 12.4, 12.8 → 12.9 MB; frame p95 33 ms; 4 frames over 100 ms | 2 px; growth 40 MB, total 150 MB; 70 ms; 40 |
| Six streams | frame p95 16.8 ms; 0 frames over 100 ms; input p95 32 ms (88 to 112 at load 40 to 70); 1 render of a streaming body on screen per update, 0 rows re-rendered; 0 px from the end while at the bottom; drift and prepend error 0 px; no gaps; RPC round trip p99 25 ms | p95 50 ms; 3; 250 ms; 1; 0; 120 px; 2 px; 0; 100 ms |

| A long reply, 4,065 → 5,429 words | script 147 ms a second (128 with the incremental split, so it went); 1 body render per update; 0 px from the end; frame p95 16.7 ms; 0 frames over 100 ms | 400 ms; 1; 120 px; 50 ms; 3 |

| Slow, 4 tokens a second | 23 deltas, 23 updates: none held back; 0 px from the end; no long frames | equal; 120 px; 0 |

- **2026-10-13 run:** all 11 scenarios passed at load 10–18. Open at the bottom/deep slot: 727/893 ms. Full scroll: 1,665 pages, 0 px anchoring error, heap 8.2 → 13.9 MB, frame p95 16.8 ms. Six streams: frame p95 16.8 ms, input p95 32 ms, RPC round trip p99 9.4 ms, one body render per update and no row renders while typing; no drift or gaps.
- **What it found:** a list that stopped following a growing reply, then (with a wider threshold) one that wouldn't let go when the user scrolled up mid-stream; paging that read older history on every open; and races in its own measurements, found by mutating the client in review.
- **Not covered yet:** WebKit, CPU throttling for phone-class devices, real phones (CLIENT-FRAMEWORK §7), and CI: the full run takes about four minutes plus the build.

**Open decisions this leaves open:** "start over" with a card (DESIGN §2.1, [O]) isn't built.

---

### Rewrites: regex scripts on text as it's written (fregex)

ST 1.19 runs a regex script with neither `prompt_only` nor `markdown_only` on text as it stores it (`getRegexedString` without `isPrompt` or `isMarkdown`): a reply when it's received (`cleanUpMessage`, impersonation as user input), the user's message when it's sent (`sendMessageAsUser`), an edit when the script has `run_on_edit` (`updateMessage`, `isEdit`), and reasoning (`reasoning.js`, placement 6). The common use is stripping a chain of thought a preset asks the model to write into its reply. Here (coordinator decisions, [P] in DESIGN §11):
- **The version's `content` is the rewritten text**, so the display, copying, editing, summaries and later requests see what ST would have stored. **The text as it was is kept on the version** (`version_texts.raw_content`, `raw_reasoning`, and `raw_sections`, the reply sections as JSON before their text was rewritten; null when unchanged) with the record of what ran (`rewrite_json`: the scripts that changed it and those skipped, each `ScriptRef` {scope, id, name}). `Version.rewrite` carries the record and whether raw text is kept, never the raw text; `RawVersionText` reads it for the owner. The raw text is never sent to a model. Copies that change the text (an amend's fork copy, a history edit's changeset copy) don't inherit it; a queued message keeps it in `queued_messages.raw_content`/`rewrite_json` and posts with it.
- **Where:** `Generations.finish` for a reply that completes or is stopped (a new reply, a swipe, a regenerate): its body once its reply sections are out (after the parser settles what it held back), its provider reasoning and each reply section's text, the last two as placement 6 (reasoning), as ST's reasoning handler runs placement 6 on parsed reasoning. And for a continuation on the whole text, as ST's non-streaming continue joins the text continued and the new text before `cleanUpMessage`; its raw text is the joined text before the scripts. `SendMessage` (through `sendOrQueue`) for a message. `EditVersion`, `WriteVersion` and `AmendVersion` as edits. The rewrite runs before the write, and the draft commit compares the typed (raw) text. **Not rewritten:** greetings (ST runs AI-output scripts on `first_mes` when a chat starts; here greetings are templates expanded on display), the first message `StartChat` sends, an edit of a queued message (`EditQueued` writes the text as typed and clears the record), and slash-command placement 3, which has no counterpart.
- **How:** `chat/rewrites.ts` sends the text (and reasoning) to the reader op `RewriteText` and stores what comes back; the main thread runs no regex. The op runs the assembler's registered stages through `scripts` for the position (the version, or the next message after a leaf for a send; `assembleThrough` in `pipeline.ts`), with `AssemblyRequest.rewrite` set, so the `scripts` stage compiles the scripts with neither flag from every registered list (§15), then each registered rewrite in `Assembler.rewrites` in turn (built-in `rewrite.regex`, `scriptSources.ts`; a plugin wraps, replaces or disables it by id). Placement follows the text's side: the speaker card's when it's in the cast, else its writer's (`rewriteSide`); reasoning is placement 6. ST passes no depth when it stores text, so min/max depth don't apply. On an edit only `run_on_edit` scripts run.
- **Bounds:** the same engine as prompt scripts (§15): linear-time patterns, the context's 200 ms VM deadline and 8 million produced characters. A script that throws (output) is skipped for that text and recorded as failed; one still running when the deadline fires leaves the whole text unchanged, recorded against that script. A rewrite op that fails outright (an unreadable document) logs a warning and the text is written as it is.
- **Restore** (`RestoreRawText`): the raw text, reasoning and reply sections (each where kept, else the version's own) back as a new selected version of the slot, an edit (`origin: edited`, `sourceVersionId` the rewritten version), which no script rewrites. The client's message action "Show the original text" opens it (§12, client).
- **Client** (`client/src/features/chat/rewrites.tsx`). A version with `rewrite` shows a "scripts changed this" header badge (`messageHeaderDetails`). Under it, plain-text notes (`messageDirections`) name the scripts that changed it and each skipped script with its reason. When `rewrite.raw`, `rawReasoning` or `rawSections` is set, the `message.original-text` message action offers "Show the original text". Its dialog reads `RawVersionText` and shows the text, reasoning and thinking in the reply as plain monospace text, never Markdown. "Restore it" calls `RestoreRawText` with the slot's row version, through the session's slot write, so the new selected version shows at once.
- Tests: `test/regexRewrite.test.ts` (placements, scope order and approval, the character rule, depth, run-on-edit, macros, output and time limits, world info, the inspector record, registry override/disable), `test/regexWritePath.test.ts` (through the server: a reply's chain of thought stripped and the next request sending the stored text, raw text and restore, approval gating, global scripts and their stale write, a send, an amend, a continuation with a card's scripts), `test/formats/cardExport.test.ts` and `test/editor.test.ts` (card scripts and their approval), and the ST gate's "Regex scripts on text as it's written" (§7).

### Live rewrites: the scripts while a reply streams (fregexs)

ST runs the scripts on a reply as it streams, not only when it ends: `StreamingProcessor.onProgressStreaming` passes the whole text so far through `cleanUpMessage` (AI-output scripts) at every update, its reasoning handler runs placement 6 on the reasoning so far, and `messageFormatting` runs the display scripts on every render. Here every frame a subscriber gets is the text so far through the scripts the finish runs, so a chain of thought a script strips never shows and the stored text is what the last frames showed. Only what a script matching across the whole text inherently changes moves at the end (a `<cot>` arriving in pieces shows until the pattern can match it, as in ST; a script that also matches an unfinished one, `(?:</cot>|$)`, hides it from its first character).
- **Server** (`chat/Generations.ts`, `chat/liveRewrites.ts`): `Running` keeps the texts as they came (body after the parser, reasoning, sections) and `shown`, what subscribers were last sent of the body, the reasoning and the section panel. After each chunk a pump rewrites the texts so far (`rewriteItems`: body, reasoning, each section's text) and sends what changed: `Delta`, `Reasoning` and `Section` add text at `offset`, or, with `replace: true`, give the text from `offset` on when the rewrite took text back. One rewrite runs at a time per reply, each on the newest text, so chunks arriving during one are taken together by the next; the cost follows the worker's speed, never the token rate. Only text that went through the scripts is ever sent: what arrives during a rewrite waits for the next one, so text a script strips never shows for a moment, and on a slow worker the text arrives at the worker's pace rather than with raw text after it. After a rewrite that took 5 ms or more (there and back, waiting for a reader included), the pump waits as long again, at most 100 ms, before the next one, so one streaming reply under heavy scripts takes about half a reader worker rather than all of one. The scripts are prepared when the generation starts, while the provider is on its first token; until the first rewrite answers nothing is sent; if it says no script applies, the reply streams as it is from then on (`direct`, the old path, no worker call per chunk). A rewrite that fails (its worker busy or restarting, say) sends nothing: what's shown stays, the failure is logged once, and the pump tries again after 100 ms, up to five times in a row, then with the next chunk; it never falls back to the texts as they came, which would show what a script takes out (fregexr: fregexs's pump treated a failure as "no script applies" and streamed the rest of the reply raw). Once the reply ends nothing more is sent: the finished version replaces the live text. The exception is a reply that ends before its first rewrite answers (a short reply, a busy host): nothing has shown, so its stored texts, which went through the finish's scripts, go out once before the version, and its deltas still add up to the stored text (streamdelta: such a reply sent no `Delta` at all, and `chats.test.ts`'s 50 ms fake reply failed on a loaded host). `Generations.live` (the `Hello` of a new subscriber) carries `shown`. The pump is the base; what rewrites is `ExecutionRegistry.liveRewrites` (built-in `live.regex`), taken in order: a plugin replaces, wraps or disables it (disabled: the reply streams as it is and is still rewritten at its end).
- **Worker** (`RewriteLive`, `db/assemblyReads.ts`): `live.regex` calls this reader op with the version. Each worker prepares the rewrite once per reply (`Assembler.prepareRewrite`: the stages through `scripts`, as `RewriteText` at the version, not an edit; ownership checked then; the `lcm` stage passes a rewrite by, which uses no summaries, so a reply's first streamed text doesn't wait on checking them again) and keeps it, least recently used first, at most 32 replies and 10 minutes unused. Every call runs the registered rewrites (`Assembler.rewrites`) with a fresh runner: the 200 ms VM deadline and output limit of one rewrite. A run in which a script ran out of time (`OUT_OF_TIME`; it leaves that text as it came, which may hold what the script takes out) counts as a failed rewrite: nothing is sent, and the pump tries again (fregexr; fregexs sent that frame as it came, and on a busy host the thinking panel showed a word its script hides). If the finish's own rewrite runs out of time, the version records it, as before. `active: false` (no compiled script and only the built-in rewrite) is what turns the reply `direct`. Measured on a 20,000-character reply with 10 scripts (`test/regexRewrite.test.ts`, `MEASURE=1`) at a host load average of about 125 to 135: a median of 40 ms per rewrite when the scripts rarely match and 45 ms with a match every 8 words (160 ms at most); the linear-time engine scans about 100 ns a character per script here. That is worker time: the main thread never waits on it, and while a long reply streams under heavy scripts its text arrives every rewrite (about every 40 ms here) rather than every token.
- **Continue** goes through the scripts on the whole text (the text continued and the new text), as its finish does; **stop** finishes with the rewrite as a completed reply does; a reply parser's held-back text isn't shown until it's released, then goes through the scripts with the rest.
- **Client** (`features/chat/session.ts`): a `replace` delta sets the text from its offset on, even when shorter; a plain one only adds past what's shown, as before. The display transforms (§10) run on the live body and on both reasoning panels while they stream (`useDisplayed.ts`).
- Tests: `test/liveRewrite.test.ts` (a mock provider streaming a `<thinking>` section and a `<cot>` chain of thought a few characters at a time, each piece of the thinking only once the one before it was shown, since on a busy host the first rewrite can outlast the whole short thinking and it would arrive in one frame, as designed: every frame of the body and of the section panel never shows what the scripts strip or hide, the stored text and sections are the last frames, raw sections shown and restored; without scripts the deltas are append-only; `live.regex` disabled), client `test/session.test.ts` (replace deltas), `e2e/liveRegex.spec.ts` (every render of the body, the provider's reasoning panel and the thinking panel while a slow provider streams, at 1440/390 in light/dark); `test/liveRewrite.test.ts` also has a slow plugin rewrite over a reply of more than 2,000 characters, whose frames never show text it hasn't been through, and one slower than the whole reply, whose stream is the stored text in one frame.

### Message images (U15, U16)

Message input has an ordered `images` list of `{mediaId, altText?}` (at most 32, alt text at most 2,000 characters). `POST /chat/image` accepts a bounded 16 MiB octet-stream upload, detects PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP from its bytes, and returns `{mediaId}`. It uses the import routes' authenticated guard, upload permits, body deadlines, content-addressed atomic file writes and sweep holds. `RecordMessageImage` records the asset and the acting user's reference in one writer transaction. `GET /library/media?id=…` is the existing owner-scoped original/thumbnail route; knowing another user's media id grants neither a read nor an attachment.

`SendMessage` and `StartChat.first.Send` attach the list to the created version. The writer validates each image against the chat owner's media references before inserting its ordered `version_attachments` rows. Image-only messages enter context. `ReadPath`, version lists, slot reads and version events include the references. An `EditVersion` without `images` copies its source's list; an explicit list replaces it, and `[]` clears it on the new version. `WriteVersion` and regeneration keep the selected version's images by default; Continue copies its source. An `AmendVersion` without `images` preserves attachments, including the copy made when another fork shows the version; with `images` it replaces the set (an amend even when the text is unchanged). `version_history.images_json` snapshots the complete earlier set on every amendment, including text-only changes, through the text trigger or an explicit entry for an image-only change; a fork's copy copies that history and gets the new set while the version other forks show keeps its own. `VersionAmendments` returns each entry's earlier `images`. Restoring an amendment restores both its text and its images, through the same fork-local amend path; restoring is itself undoable. Selection and forks retain version ownership; ordinary deletion/restore retains attachments, and permanent purges remove them with the version's content. Existing history edits and ST suffix copies also copy these rows.

Queued sends store their list in `queued_messages.images_json` (baseline and equivalence fixture updated), including image-only messages. Normal completion and restart recovery post the same list. Text edits of a queued message keep it.

The registered assembler stages read images from the selected versions, pin their references with history and carry them through the final messages' source pieces. The snapshot format's assembler version is **38** (image controls, token estimates and image-aware cache identity, §15). Image-only history renders `[Image]` in the prompt so text filters and post-processing retain its position. The registered `reply` execution strategy receives an owner-scoped `resolveImages` callback. It loads only the last `maxImages` occurrences (four when unknown) with asynchronous file I/O immediately before provider mapping; snapshots never contain base64 bytes. Missing images fail explicitly. A model without vision fails with `images_unsupported`, with no caption model or provider call. Preview issues also report unsupported images and the last-N limit.

**Taking an image out (fimg).** The history read marks each image the fork took out (`HistoryImage.excluded`, from the `image_exclude` override; pinned with history, so a rebuild replays it). `requestStage` leaves those out of the request messages through `messageImages` (`assembler/images.ts`), so the vision refusal, the `images_limited` issue, reply and summary hydration and the provider boundary's last-N cap count only what's sent. The registered `images` stage, after `request`, records the path's images the request leaves out with their rule in `assembly.imagesLeftOut` and the snapshot (`imagesLeftOut`); an image taken out has rule `user`, "Taken out of the context by you". The other built-in rules, checked in this order, are `hidden` (its message isn't sent), `history` (its message was read but isn't in the request: not summarized yet, or over the budget), `vision` ("<model key> can't see images"; the reply still refuses), and `limit` ("Only the last N images are sent to this model", from `newestImages`, the same helper reply and summary hydration use to choose what they load). Messages the assembly never read are given as depth ranges: `summary` ("Covered by a summary", up to the LCM cursor) and `history` (older than the history read). A plugin's stage registered after `images` can push its own `<plugin>/<rule>` entries, or replace the stage. `GetNextContext` (and the `Cache` event) returns the next request's `images`; the client keeps it with the view's next-context estimate, so the reasons are what the next assembly does, never a second copy of the rules. The inspector lists each such image under Not sent ("Image 3 of message 2: Taken out of the context by you"). In the client, `message.images` shows a corner toggle on each message image (`ToggleIconButton` in `ui/Tooltip.tsx`): on hover or keyboard focus, and always on touch screens; an image taken out keeps it visible and pressed and is dimmed (`opacity-40 grayscale`), with a tooltip saying it isn't sent. An image a rule leaves out is dimmed the same way and its toggle is always shown, pressed and disabled (still focusable and hoverable); the image's tooltip, the toggle's label and the view button's accessible name give the rule's message. While the editor is open its attachment controls replace these previews and toggles. `test/imageExclusion.test.ts` covers fork independence, the next context's reasons (user, limit, vision, hidden), the sent request's images and limit, the inspector and putting it back, plus the actual summary cursor’s covered range. Assembler tests cover budget omission and replacing/disabling the registered image policy.


Chat Completions receives inline data URLs; Anthropic, Responses and Gemini receive SDK image blocks. The input APIs support images on user turns, so an image-bearing assistant/system history turn is projected to a user turn with its existing speaker text; inspector mapping uses that same projection. The common provider boundary still enforces its final payload cap after transforms. Image loading and sending belong to the registered reply policy and assembler stages, so a plugin can replace or disable those policies. The registered image composer, draft uploads, message viewer and summary range transport are built (U16/U22). Image token estimates use provider counts, documented formulas or ledger calibration (§6, §15); provider spending admission detects images in the final payload and reserves conservatively (§6), saturating unknown-context reservations at the largest safe ledger integer instead of overflowing it.

**Direct input and viewing (U16).** `features/chat/images.tsx` registers the effective `chat.composer`, a `chat.images` surface provider, `message.images` preview and `queued.images` preview. Disposing the composer override restores the base text composer; each other contribution can be overridden or disabled through its registry. The composer has a visible paperclip button (Attach images, `AttachButton`) in its action row beside Send, one tap to the picker, whose tooltip says that pasting an image or dropping it anywhere in the chat works too; `AttachmentInput.action` places it and `AttachmentInput.editor` (below the composer) renders only when something is attached or an upload failed, so an empty composer adds no rows. It shows removable thumbnails (`AttachmentList`), accepts image-only sends, and keeps images apart from guidance. Message and queued thumbnails open the owner-scoped original in the image column (§5 "Message images in the column"); the composer's and the message editor's attachments peek in a modal with the same viewer. Draft, message and viewer images use `ui/ContentImage.tsx`, which inherits the root blur/hide rules and supplies a hidden-image placeholder. With attachments, the composer shows the effective model's vision capability and last-N limit before Send; `GetNextContext.model` exposes optional `vision` and `maxImages` for this purpose. Text-only refusal and request-preview issues remain U15's server behavior.

The image surface waits for `ReadPath` to resolve the viewed fork before opening or reconciling its attachment draft. It never mounts a temporary `current` image scope: that scope's startup could rewrite the same IndexedDB image rows before the real fork read their unacknowledged-send markers, losing the reload warning. `e2e/chatImages.spec.ts` holds the path read across reload and checks the recovered attachment and warning after releasing it.

**Editing a message's images (fimg).** The message editor (Edit of a generated version makes a new version, Edit of the user's own amends it, and Write your own version) shows the set the version will own: its source's, with removable thumbnails and the same `AttachButton` and `AttachmentList` as the composer; picker, paste and drop on the editor add there, never to the composer. `message.editor-images` contributes to the `message.editor.tools` slot, so it is replaceable/disableable independently. `MessageDraft.images` is persisted with the text by `SaveMessageDraft`, including an image-only edit or an explicit empty set: `drafts.images_json` and the draft history's before/after image snapshots share the text's session, row version and conflict handling. Reloading or opening the account on another device reopens the set; browser recovery copies and the HTTP backup carry it too. Draft-history restore restores the matching text and images. A matching version save or Cancel ends the draft on every device; a stale save with matching text but different images leaves the newer draft active. Image changes made during a save stay in the editor with their recovery copy; Save waits for uploads and is disabled while an upload is pending. The preview's thumbnails/toggles are hidden while its editor is open. Saved amendment history names each earlier image count and restores the full set. `test/editImages.test.ts`, client `test/editorHistory.test.ts` and `e2e/chatImages.spec.ts` cover persistence, history, ownership, fork copies, commit races, uploads and another browser finishing the edit; screenshots cover both widths/themes and 390 px uses real touch input for toggles.

**Attachment drafts (U16).** `composer_images` (baseline and equivalence fixture) stores uploaded references against the fork's composer draft, with an immutable row identity and active/sent/removed states. `GetComposerImages` reads active rows plus requested receipts; `SetComposerImage` adds a reference or records removal. Both enforce the draft's chat and owner, and an added image must be readable by that owner. Writes are single worker transactions, with a maximum of 32 active images. Tombstones make offline replay idempotent: neither a sent image nor a removed one can become active again. `SendMessage.imageDraftIds`, paired with `composer`, consumes exactly those active rows in the same transaction as the post or queued send. A stale send cannot consume them twice, and a refused send rolls the consumption back.

`imageDraft.ts` stores separate browser IndexedDB rows scoped by account, chat and fork. The whole selected batch is persisted before any upload; failure keeps every selected blob for replay on reload and shows an error. A local pending position preserves selection order before server positions exist, including across reloads; later additions retry pending uploads in that order. Local blob thumbnails are allowed by the image CSP while bytes await upload. Upload acknowledgement replaces the blob with the server reference, then saves that reference on the composer before Send becomes available. The server row position keeps attachment selection order independent of browser UUID keys. Opening the composer merges the server draft with the browser's rows and honors sent/removed receipts; uploaded drafts therefore follow the account across browsers/devices. Bytes awaiting upload remain in the selecting browser. Sending captures only that send's rows and marks them locally until acknowledgement; images attached meanwhile remain for the next message. A failed send restores its captured rows. Without a server receipt after reload, an unanswered send stays in the draft with a note to check the chat before sending again. Queued withdrawal restores both text and images under fresh draft identities, with a browser copy before the server write. `e2e/chatImages.spec.ts` covers picker, paste/drop, removal, refresh, failed-upload batch replay and pending thumbnails under CSP, image-only sending, an attachment added during an unanswered send, recovery after a lost send, separate-browser draft reads/removal, model capability warnings, full-size viewing and text-only sending when browser attachment storage is unavailable. It captures the draft and viewer at 1440 and 390 pixels in light/dark themes.


`test/messageImages.test.ts` uses synthetic PNGs and real HTTP/RPC/worker paths for uploads, deduplication, owner isolation and rollback, image-only sends, edits and fork amends, selections, history replacement/undo, deletion/restore, queued posting, snapshot replay after a later attachment edit, last-N selection, explicit text-only refusal, and actual bytes through all four provider APIs. The client preserves image-only context eligibility when applying live version events (`session.ts`); `test/session.test.ts` covers visible, hidden, failed and attachment-cleared versions, so an image-only turn is never labelled empty merely because its text is empty.

## 13. Importing an ST data folder

**Account default persona** (followups-ac, 2026-11-07). After importing the avatar named by `settings.json`'s `power_user.default_persona`, the registered persona handler adopts its card as the account default through `StImportDefaultPersona`. The writer checks the current import lease and card ownership and writes only when the account has no default, in one transaction. An existing choice and unrelated defaults survive re-import; missing avatars leave the default alone. `test/stDefaultPersona.test.ts` covers account adoption, re-import, absent defaults/avatars, and the actual dev seed's settings and avatar from `writeRealisticStFolder`. The running dev sync's `dev:seed` command imports that generator, which already names `sam.png` as its default; fresh dev seeds therefore acquire Sam through this same import path.

**Global regex scripts** (stgapfix1, 2026-11-16). ST 1.19 keeps its global regex scripts in `settings.json`'s `extension_settings.regex` (`public/scripts/extensions/regex/engine.js`, `getScriptsByType(SCRIPT_TYPES.GLOBAL)`); it has no regex files of its own, and its regex presets (`extension_settings.regex_presets`) only name which scripts are on. `parseStSettings` reads that list with the same `readRegex` presets and cards use (ids kept or made unique, unknown fields kept for export, ST's `disabled` flag kept), at most `MAX_GLOBAL_SCRIPTS` (100), with a warning for the rest. The settings handler hands them to `StImportGlobalRegex`, which checks the import lease and writes the account's `regex.global` only while that list is empty, in one transaction: a re-import never replaces or merges into scripts the user has. As in ST, global scripts need no approval and run in every chat (§15 "Where scripts come from"). The report counts them as "Global regex scripts", shown only when some came in (`regex` added, or skipped when the list already had scripts). Since the report keeps no file's own warnings or any infos, the settings handler adds the warnings the user needs itself: `st.global_regex_kept` when the list already had scripts (how many weren't taken, why, and that emptying the list and importing again takes them), and the parser's `st_settings.regex_dropped` past the limit (review-stgapfix1). Tests: `test/stGlobalRegex.test.ts` (import into an empty list, ST fields and unknown fields kept, a second import with other scripts leaves the list and warns, an emptied list takes them again, the 100-script limit and its warning).

**Import warning timing** (importwarn, 2026-11-03; DESIGN §1.4). While a job runs, both report RPCs expose errors and progress, with warnings, informational issues, unsupported-file notices and report decisions deferred until the job ends. The server projects the report through `importer/stReport.ts`'s `visibleReport`, so partial settings, missing or unattached global lorebooks, skipped files and unmatched chats never produce premature advisories. Internal checkpoints retain the full report for recovery after a server stop; finished, cancelled, failed and interrupted jobs expose it. Cancellation and idle expiry save the final live report before discarding the session, and a superseding upload saves the old report before replacing its session. `stImportWarnings.test.ts` pauses a synthetic folder upload before its selected preset, checks live and persisted reports while errors remain visible, then imports the preset late with no missing-preset warning at completion; truly missing presets appear after completion, cancellation and supersession. The upload test helper explicitly finishes the run before returning its final report.

**Persona selection.** Speaker mapping prefers the message’s persona avatar, then its unambiguous name, then the locked header persona as fallback. Every persona who spoke is the user's (personacast1, 2026-11-16; DESIGN §2.2): only the persona mapped from the last user-side message is selected and stays in the cast. Each other persona that spoke and isn't one of the chat's characters joins and then leaves at the chat's start, after the selection (`participant.join`, `played_by_me.set`, `participant.leave`), as a persona switched away from in the chat leaves it (the Cast tab's persona control). So it never gets a model turn and never counts for Next, rounds, decisions, the derived title, groups (`ListChatGroups`, a new chat's members) or the shell's fork cast, and its card isn't assembled as a character's; its messages keep their speaker, name and face (`GetCast.cards` keeps departed cards named by join/leave events, the assembler's `departed`), and the user can switch back to it with the persona control. The pinned cast of the file's imported versions (`cast_json`, `stImportedCast` in `db/stImportProgress.ts`) still lists those personas, so their chats count as used (DESIGN §2.2 personausage). A branch file's first import diffs against the state in effect where it leaves its parent ("Inherited state" under Chat state below); `chatStateChange`'s `inherited` also writes the selected persona's join and `played_by_me.set` and the other personas' join and leave whatever that state says, so every branch plays its own last persona, and a persona selected there that the branch neither selects nor has speak leaves (a branch leaving its parent before the parent switched to it). Before, a branch whose parent ended on the same persona inherited the persona at its branch point instead, and one whose parent switched later kept that later persona as a character. The record's `ChatState.otherPersonas` keeps them, so a re-import joins and leaves each only once; one that becomes the last speaker rejoins and is selected, and the one it replaces leaves. The model writes as a persona only when the user generates as it explicitly. The client's reply policies count a turn a person wrote as a card no longer in the chat as the user's turn (`userTurn` in `replyPolicy.ts`). No migration: earlier imports keep their casts. A last user-side message with no mapped speaker clears the selection, rather than reviving an earlier persona. Without a mapped persona the existing no-selection fallback remains (`{{user}}` = `User`). This also applies to group imports. Card/preset/lorebook exports contain no chat persona set and preserve literal macros. Synthetic import and assembly regressions cover two personas, repeated speakers, multipart files, group imports and pinned names (`personaImport.test.ts`, `assembler.test.ts`). `importedPersonas.test.ts` imports owner-shaped chats (a switch every 300 messages, one-to-one and group, branches of branches, swipe-heavy replies; `support/stPersonaSwitches.ts`) and checks every file's fork cast, `{{user}}`/`{{char}}`, message speakers, groups, the shell, persona usage, the next request's card blocks and the provider request (the other persona's description absent, its messages on the user side, one reply and no round), switching persona and an explicit generation as a persona; `importedPersonasScale.test.ts` (slow) runs the cast checks at 2,000 messages with 60 and 200 branch files. `client/test/importedPersonaReplies.test.ts` checks every reply policy, rounds and Next faces against that cast.

**Full-folder arrival dates** (sttimes follow-up, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §1.4). Added inherits arrival in ST only for the full-folder import. Manual single-card imports and cards written here retain Added = now. Created is independent: the format worker exposes positive CCv3 `data.creation_date` in Unix seconds as `StLibraryFile.card.authoredAt`; it dates the entity's creation. Without an independent author date, arrival is the earliest available evidence of making, so Created and Added share the same fallback. This supersedes the earlier implementation that stored ST arrival only as Created while Added still used import time.

| Arrival evidence, in priority order | Character | Persona | ST group |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Saved metadata (basis 0) | Top-level `create_date`: ISO, epoch milliseconds/digit strings, compact/space-separated ST or English month/AM-PM forms, read in UTC | 13-digit epoch-millisecond avatar filename prefix (`<time>.png` or `<time>-<name>.png`) | 13-digit millisecond `id`, else a saved `create_date` |
| Recorded presence (basis 1) | Earliest actual `send_date` attributed to this full-folder card | Earliest actual `send_date` attributed to this full-folder persona | Earliest imported group-chat `send_date` or its header's start date, across all chats of the group |
| File evidence (basis 2) | Older available positive birthtime/mtime of the card file | Same, for the original avatar; settings edits do not establish arrival | Same, for the group definition file |
| No source evidence (basis 3) | Import start | Import start | Import start |

Metadata takes precedence over earlier archived messages: importing a chat archive can bring messages written before the character entered this ST installation. `ctimeMs` changes on metadata edits/atomic replacement and is no longer used for arrival. Birth/mtime can also change on replacement or copying; they are explicitly weaker fallbacks. Chat filenames can retain a downloaded card maker's dates. Thumbnails are deleted/regenerated on demand and cannot establish arrival; the importer still never reads them. Only actual recorded message dates count as presence, not the synthetic date used to store an undated message. Greeting-only files remain skipped; message evidence comes from chats the importer retains.
