The reference ST release [`06bde939`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/tree/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127) does **not** persist an explicit fresh-card date in `/create`'s `charaFormatData`; [its listing endpoint](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L411-L418) supplies missing `create_date` from file ctime. [JSON/PNG/CHARX imports](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L765-L785) explicitly reset `create_date` to now ([JSON](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L883-L900), [PNG](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L968-L987)), even when `/import` is given a [preserved replacement filename](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L1560-L1592). [Ordinary edits](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L1113-L1117) preserve the supplied date. Thus the exact original arrival before an ST replacement import may be lost; we preserve the earliest arrival evidence seen across our imports, rather than claiming to reconstruct unavailable provenance. [Persona uploads](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/avatars.js#L41-L58) use timestamp filenames and retain names on avatar replacement; [blank personas](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/public/scripts/personas.js#L496-L498) use timestamp-name prefixes. [Group creation](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/groups.js#L160-L199) stamps an id with `Date.now()` and edits retain that id. [Thumbnails](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/thumbnails.js#L83-L128) are invalidated/regenerated cache files.

Implementation: `ImportFile.arrival` dates the upstream ref's `created_at`, with nullable `entity_refs.st_added_basis` recording the evidence strength. Cards with no author creation date use that same date in `entities.created_at`. `StImports` retains only the full-folder entities' ref ids; batch `arrivalRefs` map actual speakers to those refs, so a manual link does not change a separately imported card's Added date. The format worker includes an optional `arrivalAt` in each parsed message, before date fallback. Arrival aggregation happens before `StImportMessages`' writer transaction; `db/stArrival.ts` applies owner-scoped updates there. Re-importing unchanged cards still records source evidence without a new revision or Modified change. Stronger evidence replaces weaker; equal evidence keeps its earliest date. Baseline columns `chats.added_at`, `st_group_id`, `st_added_basis`, and the owner/group index keep a group's chats together without scanning other chats. Group fallback evidence discovered on another chat, or a later import, dates all its chats consistently. Shell rows expose `ShellFork.addedAt`; GroupGrid passes Added through to the reader's sort instead of mapping it to Created. `LibraryRef.addedAt` lets the library sort personas as well as characters; home and sidebar already use `ShellCard.addedAt`. Existing Added labels/tooltips now describe inherited arrival. No new UI surface.

Tests: `stImportAdded.test.ts` uses synthetic folder uploads and on-disk folders with set file times for saved metadata, distinct author/arrival dates, persona filenames, group ids, chat/file/import fallback, archived earlier messages, shared group dates, re-import stability and the manual-import exception. `shellNavigation.test.ts` covers the updated file fallback with bundled workers. `characterBrowse.spec.ts` checks home Added sorting and an exact inherited date at desktop/phone widths, plus the existing sort controls and labels.

**Source revision dates** (sttimes, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §1.4). Browser folder uploads send `File.lastModified` as `modifiedAt` on every file/part (`features/library/stUpload.ts`, mirrored by `test/support/stUpload.ts`); path imports pass the scanned `mtimeMs` after the file-handle stability check. `StImports.file` validates and truncates file times to nonnegative integer milliseconds within the JS Date range; missing or invalid times fall back to the session's import-start time. Folder ZIP upload is not supported. CHARX is the only ZIP intake, through the existing card format importer.

| Imported content | Source used for its revision time |
| --- | --- |
| Cards (JSON, PNG, CHARX) | Positive CCv3 `data.modification_date`, converted from Unix seconds; zero is unknown. Otherwise CHARX uses the latest valid time among `card.json` and consumed assets, then the outer file time, then import time. V1/V2 cards without that field use file/import time. `create_date`, CCv3 `creation_date` and card `date_last_chat` never date edits. |
| Presets | Only the preset file time, including when copying text switches or attaching ST's selected global books from settings. |
| Standalone lorebooks | Only the World Info file time, including when resolving author's-note placement from settings. |
| Personas and description notes | Later avatar/settings-file time when settings define the persona; avatar time alone otherwise. |
| Embedded lorebooks, regex lists, Character's Note and exported card notes | Containing card/preset revision time; the embedded data have no independent saved edit timestamp. |
| Character author's notes | `settings.json` time. |
| Single/group chat messages and swipes | ST `send_date`, with existing previous-message/header fallback, then chat file/import time if all are absent. Chat activity still comes from messages. |
| Chat author's notes | Chat file time, or settings time when the chat inherits ST's default note. |
| Imported summary history | The saved-on message's time for each revision (`StImportNote.sources`); file/import time when the source message is unavailable. |
| Group definitions | Read for chat name/cast/reply policy, with no standalone entity or revision. `date_last_chat` is activity, not a group-edit date. |
| Settings adoption / import jobs | Import-time operational bookkeeping; no source revision is manufactured. Global regex scripts (below) have no saved edit date of their own and keep their import time. |

**Preset/book date correction** (presetdates, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §1.4). ST rewrites `settings.json` during ordinary use, so its mtime never dates preset or standalone lorebook edits. Mapped settings still contribute content and re-import hashes. Only the entity file's time dates its revision, with import-start fallback if unavailable. Persona definitions live in settings, so their existing later-avatar/settings rule remains; unrelated settings writes can still overstate their edit dates, since no per-persona edit date is available. Settings-owned notes retain their existing dates too. No migration or repair of already-imported dates is performed. Preset Created (`entities.created_at`) and Added (the upstream ref's `created_at`, exposed as `LibraryRef.addedAt`) remain first-import time here, independent of the source edit date; later re-imports retain both. ST presets provide no independent creation/arrival evidence.

`ParsedFile.stModifiedAt` carries a card's parsed source date separately from its document. The ZIP reader reads central-directory DOS timestamps as UTC (no timezone is recorded) and prefers the extended UTC timestamp (`0x5455`). Unused entries cannot advance a card's date. `ImportFile.modifiedAt` and `StImportCharacterNote.modifiedAt` reach the writer's existing revision insertion helpers; `StImportNote.modifiedAt` dates chat notes, with summary source-message dates read in the same writer transaction. `entity_revisions.created_at` stores the source time; a new ref's `updated_at` and a ref fast-forwarded to an imported revision use that revision's time, supplying the preset picker's "edited", Modified sort and History. Revision lineage/order still uses parents and insertion sequence, so older source times on a later re-import cannot select an earlier import. An unchanged file creates no revision and leaves Modified alone. A metadata-only merge-base move preserves Modified; actual user edits and merge revisions use the time of that edit/merge. Entity Created stays independent: existing card-addition rules above, otherwise the new entity's import time; the full-folder arrival rules above refine cards/personas. Revision dates themselves need no extra schema columns.

Source audit: ST release commit [`06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/tree/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127). [`characters.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/characters.js#L1113-L1117) preserves `create_date` on edits and derives card activity from chats; [`presets.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/presets.js#L42-L57), [`worldinfo.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/worldinfo.js#L143-L155) and [`settings.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/settings.js#L204-L210) write the supplied data without maintaining edit-date fields. [`personas.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/public/scripts/personas.js) stores descriptions in settings; [`global.d.ts`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/public/global.d.ts#L65-L87) defines message/swipe dates. [`groups.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/src/endpoints/groups.js#L128-L145) computes `date_last_chat` from chat-file mtimes. [CCv3](https://github.com/kwaroran/character-card-spec-v3/blob/main/SPEC_V3.md#modification_date) defines `modification_date` in seconds and zero as unknown; ST does not maintain that field itself, so it is the exporting editor's recorded date when present. Files copied with reset mtimes and shared settings-file dates remain best-effort evidence.

Tests: `test/stImportTimes.test.ts` imports synthetic browser uploads (including multipart chats) and on-disk folders with set file times, checking old preset/book mtimes against recent settings (mapped switches, global books and author's-note placement), library Modified, revision History, preset Created/Added at import time, creation/activity independence, note/summary times, changed/unchanged re-import and invalid/missing dates. `test/formats/stModifiedAt.test.ts` covers CCv3 units/unknown dates, PNG transport and CHARX DOS/extended timestamps, including assets and unused entries. `e2e/stImportTimes.spec.ts` picks a real synthetic folder in Chromium and verifies preset-picker dates and Modified order at 1440 and 390 pixels.

A SillyTavern data folder into the library and chats (DESIGN §1.4, §8.1; DATA-MODEL §14). Read from ST's public source at commit `06bde939` (`public/global.d.ts`, `scripts/chats.js`, `bookmarks.js`, `personas.js`, `authors-note.js`, `world-info.js`, `utils.js`, `extensions/memory`). Shared: `@rp/shared/stFolder.ts` (which paths are read) and `stImportApi.ts` (the RPCs and the report). Server: `formats/stChat.ts` and `formats/stData.ts` (the parsers), `importer/stParse.ts` (their format-worker side), `importer/StImports.ts` (the import on the main thread: sessions, library files, and each chat through its record), `importer/stMapping.ts` (what a chat file means: its card, speakers and state), `importer/stReport.ts`, `db/stImportWrites.ts` and `db/stImportReads.ts`.

**How the folder gets in.** The app usually runs on the user's own computer, where the ST folder is, so the import page takes the folder's path (DESIGN §1.4) and the backend reads it (`importer/stFolderDisk.ts`, `api/stImport.ts`). A folder browser under the path field (`features/library/FolderBrowser.tsx`, `ListFolder`) starts at the folder last looked in (kept on the device, else the newest path import's folder; fimport, 2026-10-31), else in `IMPORT_START_DIR` (the home folder when unset; a Docker deployment sets it to where ST's data is mounted), which the path field also shows until the user types or opens a folder (a start folder that's gone offers the home folder), and lists subfolders (hidden ones left out, at most 1,000), marking those that look like ST's from the names in them: its install (`server.js` and `data`), its data folder (`default-user`), or a user's folder (`characters` and `chats`). Opening a folder fills the field; it never fills it on its own, so typing isn't overwritten. A browser on another machine can pick the folder instead (`webkitdirectory`), and its files are uploaded.
- **By path:** `ScanStFolder` lists the files under the path that the import reads or lists (the same `classifyStPath` tails `findStRoots` uses), each with its size and, for a chat, the parent it names (`main_chat`), read from its first 64 KiB. It walks at most 6 levels below the path (enough for `<install>/data/<handle>/chats/<card>/<chat>.jsonl`), at most 500,000 entries, skips `node_modules` and `.git`, and doesn't follow symbolic links inside. `StartStPathImport` (the folder and the chosen ST user's prefix) then runs the whole import **on the server** as a job (below): it plans and orders the files as the upload does (`@rp/shared/stPlan.ts`, shared with the client), reads each file, or a chat's part from byte `start` (at most 8 MiB, cut at a line end), and hands the bytes to the same `StImports.file` the upload uses. Each read checks the file's size and modification time against the scan, and a file that changed since is refused (ST may be writing to a chat during the import), so parts never mix two versions of a file. The root must be absolute, and the file's path relative to the user's folder must classify, so `..` and files the import doesn't read are refused. Uploads are still driven by the browser, file by file (`features/library/stUpload.ts`), in the same order.
- **Admin only:** the three RPCs refuse anyone but an admin (isolation matrix, §4). On an instance with several users, anyone else could read any user's files by naming them.
- **By upload:** the client sends each file, one HTTP request each (`POST /st-import/file`), through the library upload's limits (§11.4): the same body reader, stall and trickle rules, memory permits and one transfer per user.
- **What's sent.** `classifyStPath` names the files read: `settings.json`, `User Avatars/*` images, `characters/*.png|json|charx`, `worlds/*.json`, `OpenAI Settings/*.json`, `groups/*.json`, `chats/<folder>/*.jsonl` and `group chats/*.jsonl`. Nothing else (backups, thumbnails, `secrets.json`, extensions) is sent, and the server classifies every path again and refuses the rest with `400`, as it does any path with an empty, `.` or `..` segment, a backslash, a colon or a control character. Text-completion presets and instruct, context, system-prompt and reasoning templates are listed by path in `StartStImport` and counted in the report as unsupported (DESIGN §1.2), never uploaded.
- **ST's multi-user layout** (`data/<handle>/`): `findStRoots` finds each user folder in what was picked (the ST install, its `data/`, or one user's folder), and the user picks one handle, which goes into their own account. **Not built:** the admin-only option of one user per handle.
- **Order** (`ST_FILE_ORDER`): settings, personas, cards, lorebooks, presets, groups, chats, group chats, so a chat finds what it links to.
- **Chats come in parts** of at most 8 MiB (`ST_CHAT_PART_BYTES`), cut at line ends and sent in order (`part`, and `last` on the last one): a chat can be far larger than any card, and a part bounds what one request holds in memory. A line longer than a part can't be sent. A part out of order, or after the server lost the chat's earlier parts (a restart), is answered `restart`, and the client sends the chat again from its start, which the matching below makes safe.

**Summarize settings.** `settings.json` retains `extension_settings.memory.prompt` and `promptWords` alongside the injection position, depth, role, template and enabled state (ST 1.19.0’s public `extensions/memory/index.js`). `StImportSummarySettings` saves these mapped settings under the importing user’s `import.st.memory` and fills `generation.lcm.tail` only if no instruction is set. The import lease fences old runs; re-importing preserves an instruction the user changed. No provider request starts on import. A newly imported chat stores a copy of the account's summarization default with summaries off (§16 *Defaults*); importing into an existing chat leaves its settings alone.

**Selected chat-completion preset.** `settings.json` also reads `oai_settings.preset_settings_openai`. When that named file from `OpenAI Settings/` is successfully imported (including an unchanged file), `StImportDefaultPreset` adopts its ref as the user's `generation.preset` only if the stored setting is absent or JSON null. The writer checks the import lease and preset ownership and makes the conditional write in one transaction; an existing choice, even one whose ref is no longer live, is preserved. The report names the preset ST used and says whether it became the default or the existing default was kept. Until its file is imported, the report warns that the selected preset file has not been imported from the folder. Other presets in the folder never become the default automatically.

**ST's global World Info books** (`globalSelect`) are attached to the preset ST had selected, and nowhere else: when that preset's file is imported, `ImportFile` takes the refs of the global books already imported (`presetLorebooks`, in ST's order; lorebooks come before presets in `ST_FILE_ORDER`), keeps those that are the user's live library lorebooks, and stores them in the document as `lorebooks` entries, each on (§15 "Lorebook activation"). They're part of the import's revision line (§3.9), so importing the same file with the same books adds no revision and no duplicate, a book the user took off the preset since stays off it, and a changed `globalSelect` merges in as a change of the file would. So the selected preset goes to the writer even when its file is unchanged. The report says where the books went, measured on each read: `st.global_worlds_attached` (an info, kept: "Attached ST's global World Info books “Lore A”, “Lore B” to the preset “X”."), `st.global_worlds_unattached` (a warning: the books are in the library but attached to no preset, since ST had no preset selected, its selected preset wasn't imported, or they came after it) and `st.global_world_missing` (a book that wasn't in the folder). `test/stImport.test.ts` covers the mapping, a re-import and the unattached cases; `test/assemblyRealistic.test.ts` the realistic folder.

**Unchanged persona notes.** When a library file is unchanged, `GetCardImportNote` resolves its existing first imported card note in a reader worker, using the same identity lookup as `ImportFile`. The persona-to-note map is populated before chat mapping even on re-import, so newly added chats with ST author-note frequency zero switch the persona note off. This reads the existing note without importing it again or changing local edits. `test/stPersonaReimport.test.ts` permanently covers the two-import inventory reproduction with synthetic files.

**The import** (`StImports`): one per user at a time, held in memory on the main thread until an hour after its last request or the user's next `StartStImport`. It holds what links chats to cards (each card's name, the first 4 KB of its greetings and its world; personas; groups; lorebook names), what earlier imports recorded, and the report, never a file. What it holds about the folder, and the summaries of the chat being read, is capped at 16M characters (about 50 MB of heap); a file that would add more is refused, and the report says to import the rest in another run. Every file is parsed in a format worker (§11.3) and stored through the writer; the main thread never parses a file or a document. `GetStImportReport` reads the report. Another user's import is `NotFound`, and a file sent to it is `404` before its body is read. Its RPCs and the route are in the isolation matrix (§4): cross-user probes, and admin-only for the three that read the disk.

**Shared branch prefixes** (importspeed2, 2026-11-02). The format worker supplies an optional SHA-256 for each complete normalized message, including its swipes, selection, visibility, dates and recorded metadata. The main thread forwards these unread. The writer keeps a disposable prefix trie for newly created chats: each edge is keyed by the parent slot, message hash and resolved speaker entity. Matching a batch's longest known prefix takes bounded in-memory lookups, with no positional SQL or swipe comparisons for those messages. The remaining suffix is prepared before the transaction and, when its first position is new, written by the existing ordered bulk inserts. Existing prefix versions are left alone. Ownership, leases, arrivals, progress, leaf movement and finish operations still run normally.

The trie holds at most 100,000 messages across 1,000 eligible chats; older family indexes are evicted first. It is published only after successful writes, is lost on worker restart, and is discarded before every writer operation except the explicitly listed import/progress, readiness, shell-summary-cache storage and summary-queue polling operations (`db/stImportPrefix.ts`). Reimports and positional reconciliation use the original matching path; reconciliation that changes stored versions, selections or visibility removes that chat from eligibility for the rest of the run. An unchanged subset of known swipes can populate another exact hash. This preserves local edits, fork selections, deletions and changed swipe lists, and lets registered parsers omit hashes. A tip move records a path-reachability touch only if the fork has children: its own summary is already invalidated directly, and no childless fork needs the expensive descendant walk (`summaryValidity.ts`). Forks with children retain the original reachability rules. A writer refresh of at most two stale forks reads just their paths (and live parents), rather than loading every slot in their growing chat; larger refreshes and reader batches retain the shared-tree strategy (`forkSummaries.ts`).

`stImportBatch.test.ts` compares complete synthetic branch families with 20–50 swipes through hashed and positional imports, including an edit during the import, an added swipe and a subset of existing swipes. It checks storage rows, participation, FTS, import records, note documents and shell summaries, normalizing independent IDs (and their dependent digests), sequence offsets and operational clocks. `summaryValidity.test.ts` checks both childless and parent tip moves. `stBranchFamilyScale.test.ts` imports a 100-branch, 2,000-message family with 30% of model messages carrying 20–50 swipes, using `support/stFolder.ts`'s deterministic on-disk generator; it bounds wall time at six minutes and checks the early/late per-file curve. Environment-selected big and mixed-folder modes measure 300 branches of 3,000 messages, alone or in three families with 100 ordinary chats and 500 cards. These scale tests run with `npm run test:slow`.

**Parsing** (`formats/stChat.ts`, `formats/stData.ts`), pure and under the shared caps (§8):
- **A chat part** is read line by line, each line its own JSON document through `parseJson`, under the shared depth, container, value and prototype-key caps. A line that isn't a message is skipped and counted, as ST skips it. The first line is the header when it has `chat_metadata` (or `user_name`) and no `mes`; old group chats have none. Messages cross to the main thread as JSON text in batches of at most 100 messages or 1 MiB, each with the speakers it names, which the main thread passes to the writer unread with only those speakers' cards. A part has at most 1,000 speakers; messages past that have none, and the report says how many. Before the cap, a file naming a new speaker on every line made each batch carry and check every speaker so far, quadratic in the file (a review measured 17.6 s for 20,000 lines, and about two hours of writer time for one 8 MiB part).
- **Caps:** a part 8 MiB; 1,000 swipes per message; 1,000 variables, each value at most 1 MB (the macro engine's cap, §10); names 200 characters; greetings compared on their first 4 KB. `settings.json` 32 MiB (it holds every extension's settings), a group file 1 MiB, 10,000 personas, 1,000 members per group. Each cap has a crafted file in `test/formats/stChat.test.ts` or `test/stImport.test.ts`.
- **Dates** as ST reads them (`parseTimestamp`): epoch milliseconds, digits, ISO 8601, `June 19, 2023 2:20pm` (read as UTC: ST uses the browser's time zone, which the server can't know), and ST's humanized forms. A message without one, or with a number past what a date holds (a timestamp column takes only whole numbers it stores exactly), takes the time of the one before it, so a re-import gives it the same time.
- **Only what's mapped is read** from `settings.json`: personas, `world_info_settings.world_info` (`globalSelect`, whose books go with ST's selected preset, below; `charLore`), the default author's note, the characters' own author's notes (`note.chara`) and `note.allowWIScan`, the Summarize extension's settings and whether it's disabled, the selected chat-completion preset name above, and `power_user.default_persona` for chats without a user turn. The rest, connection settings included, is dropped unread.

**The mapping** (DATA-MODEL §14):
- **Messages:** one slot per message. `swipes[]` are its versions, `swipe_id` selected; `mes`, which ST shows and sends, is selected even when it isn't among the swipes (as an extra version). Each version's time is its `swipe_info` date or the message's `send_date`. `is_user` decides the writer (`human`, else `model`); every version is `origin: imported`, `macro_mode: verbatim`, `status: complete`. `extra.reasoning` (and each swipe's) is the version's `reasoning`, unless its `extra.reasoning_type` is `"parsed"` (ST took it out of the reply's text): then it's the version's reply section (§12 "Reply sections"), in ST's default `<think>` / `</think>` tags with a `\n` gap, since ST keeps only the text between them. Either way it's the message's own thinking, which its edit changes (§12 "Thinking in a message's edit"). Reasoning ST marks as the user's (`reasoning_type` `"edited"` or `"manual"`) keeps that type in the version's recorded generation (`RecordedGeneration.reasoningType`), for the export. `is_system`, ST's one hidden flag (`hideChatMessageRange` sets it), is `context_excluded`. Attachments aren't imported; the report counts them.
- **Who generated each version, and how long it took** (msgmeta, owner 2026-11-01). ST records on the message, for the swipe it shows, and in each `swipe_info[i]` (a copy, `syncMesToSwipe`): `extra.api` (the chat completion source or text completion type, `getGeneratingApi`) and `extra.model`, `gen_started` and `gen_finished`, `extra.token_count` (its own tokenizer's count of the text with its reasoning, only with its token counter on, and on user messages too), `extra.time_to_first_token` and `extra.reasoning_duration` (ms). A Continue rewrites the api and model to its own and moves `gen_started` back by the time the first part took, so the span covers both; swipes generated together in one request (n > 1) lose `token_count`; an edit keeps them all. `stGenerationOf` (`formats/stChat.ts`) reads them per version: the shown version from the message's own fields (its `swipe_info` only where the message has none, never a mix), every other swipe from its `swipe_info`. Strings are trimmed and capped (api 64, model 256), counts and durations must be positive and bounded, and the two dates are kept only together and in order; anything else is dropped, so nonsense never blocks the text. They're stored on the version in two columns (`db/rows.ts` `recordedColumns`): `recorded_model_json` (`api`, `model`) and `recorded_generation_json` (the times and counts). An imported model isn't one of the user's connections, so `Version.model` reads "API · model" (`@rp/shared/stApis.ts` names ST's APIs: "OpenRouter · anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet", "Anthropic · claude-3-opus"), `Version.modelRef` is `{ provider: api, model }` for the lab mark (§5), and `Version.recorded` carries the figures. A duplicate keeps `recorded_model_json`, as it keeps `model_id`; it and an amended fork copy leave `recorded_generation_json` behind, as they leave `usage_json` (`insertWrites.ts`, `writes.ts`). A re-import matches versions by writer, time and text as before and doesn't rewrite what an earlier import stored. Tested by `test/stImportModels.test.ts`: two swipes by different models (OpenRouter and Anthropic) with their own figures, a Continue's model and span, swipes made together without a count, a user's count, nonsense dropped, and a re-import that changes nothing.
- **Speakers:** a user message is the persona its `force_avatar` names (ST's `/thumbnail?type=persona&file=…`, or `User Avatars/…`), else the one persona with its name when unambiguous, else the chat's locked persona (`chat_metadata.persona`). A model message is the card its `original_avatar` or `force_avatar` names, else the chat's card in a single chat, or the one member with its name in a group. Narrator messages (`extra.type: narrator`) have none.
- **Chat state**, as state events with origin `import` at the chat's start: `participant.join` for the card (or the group's members) and the personas that spoke, `presence.set false` for muted members, `played_by_me.set` for only the persona mapped from the last user-side message (last occurrence, including a return to an earlier persona and across file parts), then `participant.leave` for the other personas that spoke ("Persona selection" above); with no user-side message, the chat's locked persona or then `power_user.default_persona` is selected and joined to the cast when its avatar was imported; with neither available, no persona is selected and `{{user}}` reads `User`. The remaining events are `lorebook.attach` for the chat's world, the card's (`extensions.world`) and ST's extra books for the character (`charLore`), `lorebook.binding` to identify each card's primary ref, `lorebook.embedded` off for each card whose own `character_book` ST never sent, and `var.set` for each variable. ST's global lorebooks (`globalSelect`) are imported but not attached. A lorebook not in the folder is reported once per import, not attached.
- **Inherited state** (review-personacast1, 2026-11-16). A branch file's state events go in its fork at its first message of its own, and are what changed from the state it inherits there. That is the state in effect where it leaves its parent, not the parent's at its own end: a parent can switch persona, lorebook, variables or note after the branch point, and a branch of a branch can leave in the part its parent shares with its own parent, where the parent's own events don't apply. Each record keeps `stateAt`, the depth of the slot its first import's events went to (0 for a chat's start; `StImportFinishChat` sets it once, from the finish's position), and its `parentRecordId`. A branch's first import (`inheritedState` in `importer/StImports.ts`) walks up from its parent while the record's `stateAt` is at or past the branch's first own message, and diffs against the first record whose state applies there (`ChatState`, so persona, lorebooks and bindings, embedded books, variables, reply order, character notes off and the note hashes). Its previous notes are those of every record on the way, the nearer ones winning, so a note the nearer file dropped is still the one switched off and the chat keeps one note per ST note. A record finished before `stateAt` was kept stops the walk, and its state is taken as before. A confirmed re-import's new branch file (`StImportCommitChat`, smallfix2, 2026-11-16) computes its state before its messages are placed, so its first own message comes from the reader's plan of its batches (`stageBatch`, the same count `writeBatch` takes once written), and it diffs against the same inherited state and notes; the commit's summary note is compared with that state's summary (`finish.baseSummary`), and the commit hands back the record's `stateAt`, so the run's later branch files walk up through files it re-imported. No migration: existing records lack `stateAt`. `stBranchInheritedState.test.ts` checks a hand-made family (a branch leaving its parent's own part before the parent's switch, and one leaving the shared part with its parent's state exactly) and a generated one (`support/stBranchStates.ts`: each file with its own variables, lorebook, note and persona); Both also import each family without its nested leaf branch files, then the whole folder as a confirmed re-import, and check every file again (`checkReimportedBranchStates` in `support/branchStates.ts`). `stBranchInheritedStateScale.test.ts` (slow) runs the generated checks at 2,000 messages with 60 and 240 branch files, about 30% of them branches of branches.
- **A card's own lorebook** (DESIGN §1.3). ST 1.19 never sends a card's embedded `character_book`: `getCharacterLore` loads only the lorebook file `extensions.world` names (`loadWorldInfo`), and "Import Card Lore" (the dialog `checkEmbeddedWorld` shows once per card) is what makes that file from the card's book and links it. So a chat with a card that has a book but whose `extensions.world` file isn't in the folder gets `lorebook.embedded` off, as ST had it; a re-import that finds the file turns it back on. That `extensions.world` name is the book's name in the ST of whoever exported the card (ST writes it on save), so it isn't reported missing. Applies like the rest of a chat's state: at a new chat's start, and for a chat imported earlier only with new messages.
- **The author's note** becomes an ordinary chat-owned note titled "Author's Note", with no kind and no mark (DESIGN §4.1, owner 2026-11-01), and `note.activate` only if ST sent it: its text isn't empty and its frequency isn't 0. No frequency is kept: a note goes every turn. ST's default note applies to a chat without one of its own, as in ST. Empty chat notes and default settings without text are kept too, off, with their settings. Only missing chat and default settings leave no imported note. In-chat it's placed at its depth and role; after or before the main prompt it's a `section` placement with its imported role [P]. With `allowWIScan` it gets `scan_lore`. The record keeps it under the key `author_note` (`StImportNote.kind`), which only a re-import reads.
- **One note per ST note in a chat, its text per fork** (owner, 2026-11-01: "ST can only possibly have one"). A branch or checkpoint file merged into its parent's chat (below) starts from its parent record's notes; a re-import from its own record's. When the file's author's note (or summary) differs from that, its text is a new revision of the chat's existing note, parented on its head, bound in the file's fork from the file's first new message (`note.binding`, as an edit there is, DESIGN §3.4), with `note.activate` or `note.deactivate` there; the library head and the other forks keep theirs. Before, it was a new note: an ST branch family whose author's note grew from file to file listed every file's note in every fork, its own on and the others off (the owner's "two author's notes"). (`test/stImportBranchNotes.test.ts`: a three-file family whose note grows, then a re-import of the main file with a changed note).
- **What ST placed at the author's note's top or bottom** (World Info positions 2 and 3, a persona at the note's top or bottom, a character's own author's note before, after or in place of it) goes, kept, where the folder's default author's note is (`authorNotePlace` in `importer/stMapping.ts`: `settings.json`'s `note.default*`, else ST's own default, in-chat at depth 4 as the system): a note at its depth and role, or in the section beside the main prompt it's in; a lorebook entry at its depth and role (`at_depth`; `placeAuthorNoteEntries`, which the World Info importer reads from `AuthorNoteLorePlace`, the folder import providing it; an upload, or a card's own book, takes ST's default). Personas, characters' notes and lorebooks are the library's, used in every chat, so each has one place. A chat gets a warning (`st.author_note_riders`), as its context differs from ST's there, only when something rode on its own note and that note was elsewhere (importreport, 2026-11-02; before, any such persona, character note or book anywhere in the folder warned every chat whose note differed from the default, and since ST copies the default note's place into each chat when it's first opened, a changed default made that nearly every chat). What counts is what ST's `setFloatingPrompt`, `addPersonaDescriptionExtensionPrompt` and `checkWorldInfo` add to that chat's note: nothing while its note is off (frequency 0); the persona played there, when its description is at the note's top or bottom; the card's own author's note in a one-to-one chat where ST applies it (`useChara`; ST never applies it in a group chat, nor one that's only written down); and the lorebooks the chat uses (its own, its cards', ST's global ones) with enabled, non-empty entries at the note. Disabled or empty entries still receive a concrete placement and contribute to placement-sensitive import hashes, but do not trigger the warning (`lorebook.author_note_riders` in the parser report; `test/stImportReport.test.ts` covers disabling, emptying and re-enabling a book). The warning's message is the same on every chat, and its `detail` names what rode there and both places ("Dax's own author's note; the lorebook “Signs”'s entries at the note. This chat's note: depth 2 as system; the default's: depth 4 as system."). A book whose entries moved hashes with that place, so a changed default re-imports it.
- **A character's own author's note** (`note.chara`, matched to a card by its avatar file name without the extension) becomes, when the card file is imported and the note has text, a private card note titled "Character author's note" (`kind: character_author_note`, `StImportCharacterNote`, one per card, merged on a re-import) with `on_by_default` as ST's `useChara`, where the folder's default author's note is for ST's "before", "after" and "replace" (owner, 2026-10-28: "replace" never replaces anything; the chat's author's note is still sent), and `scan_lore` with `allowWIScan`. ST applies it only in one-to-one chats, so an imported group chat switches it off (`note.deactivate` once; `ChatState.characterNotesOff` remembers it). A one-to-one chat whose non-empty author's note ST would have replaced gets an info line (`st.character_note_replaced`). The report counts them (`character_note`).
- **Personas** become cards in the persona folder (tagged `persona` when created; a re-import leaves tags alone) with their original avatar file, named and described from `settings.json`. A persona placed anywhere but the prompt's persona description (at depth with its role, at the top or bottom of the author's note, or not sent) gets an **ordinary** note on its card titled "Persona description", on in every chat, with the text at that placement (`depth`, where the default author's note is, `none`), and the card's description is left empty: one copy, nothing hidden (DESIGN §4.1, owner 2026-10-28). ST 1.19.0 (`setFloatingPrompt`, `addPersonaDescriptionExtensionPrompt`) still sends the persona with an author's note that's empty but due, and none of it with frequency 0, which the import keeps for each chat: a chat whose author's note had frequency 0 gets `note.deactivate` for the persona's note (`FolderContext.personaNotes`, from the persona's import in the same run) and for the card's Character Author's Note, which ST adds the same way (both in `characterNotesOff`, once). A re-import whose persona file is unchanged doesn't know the note, so a chat new to that run keeps it on. An avatar `settings.json` doesn't list is a persona named after its file, as ST shows it. A persona's hash covers its image and its settings, so a changed description updates it.
- **Cards, lorebooks, presets** go through `ImportFile` (§11.1) like uploads, with the path in the folder as `source_path`. A file must be what its folder holds: a preset in `worlds/` fails.
- **Groups:** a group chat belongs to the group whose `chats` (or `chat_id`) names it. For a stamp-only chat file, ST's default group name (`Group: ` plus its actual members' names) yields the characters and the chat's start date; a renamed group yields its name and that start date. A user-named chat file supplies its own title. One no group lists is imported with its speakers matched by avatar.

**Linking a chat to its card** (single chats): the card whose file the chat's folder is named after (ST's own link), else the one card with the folder's name (a renamed card file), else the one card whose avatar the messages name, else the one card named as the chat's character speaks (a card downloaded again under a new file name, `name (1)`, keeps its old chats' folder), else the one card whose greeting the chat's first message is, with `{{char}}` filled in and `{{user}}` matching any name. More than one candidate, or none, puts the chat in the report's `links` with its candidates and why (no card has the folder's file name or the speaker's name; ST's `undefined` folder, where it saves a chat made with no character selected), and it isn't imported until the user picks a card (or none); the client then sends it again with `card=<entity>`. The writer checks that card like any id it's given, so another user's is refused.

**Branches and checkpoints** (`chat_metadata.main_chat`, ST's `bookmarks.js`) merge into their parent's chat, with one durable fork per file record (fork independence unit 9). A new main file uses the chat's first fork; a merged file gets its own fork, inheriting its recorded parent's bounded lineage, even when both files end at the same message. Fork creation for import does not switch the chat's current fork while messages come in. **The fork the chat opens on** (owner, 2026-11-01: "ST opens in the last one you opened") is set as each file finishes (`openOnStCurrent` in `db/stImportWrites.ts`): the fork of the file ST last opened, which ST records as the group's `chat_id` (`groups/<id>.json`; `parseStGroup` keeps it as `StGroup.chatId`) or the card's top-level `chat` (read like `create_date`, `ParsedFile.stChat`; ST's `script.js` and `group-chats.js` write them when a chat is opened), the file's record keeping `stCurrent`; else, when that record is missing or names a file that wasn't imported, the fork whose tip has the latest message (the earlier fork on a tie), as ST picks a card's chat by its last message when the one it names is gone. Only while the user hasn't chatted or branched in the chat here: a fork with `last_chatted_at`, or one made at a message (`base_slot_id`, which an import never sets), means the current fork is the user's, and a re-import leaves it (`test/stImportBranchList.test.ts`). Matching shares slots and versions by text, time and writer; a different selected swipe writes a `select` override with origin `import` in the file's fork. Hidden-flag differences can still start independent slots. Messages without a match append under the last match. State and note events written at finish belong to that file's fork, so shared-tip checkpoints keep separate state. Re-import checks non-import events on that fork's path through its bounded lineage (including dormant positional choices, excluding suppressed events). A local choice blocks imported changes to the same setting or target, including opposite switches; unrelated settings and choices made only in another fork do not block updates. An imported note locally edited, switched, rebound or deleted retains its identity and binding when ST changes or removes it; an upstream note edited in the library is likewise retained. The file record still remembers the latest ST state, so replay is stable. Parents are sent before children; unresolved parents defer, then import as separate chats when explicitly orphaned.

**ST file names name no fork** (owner, 2026-11-01: a name means the user promoted a branch into its own identity, which an imported file isn't). An imported fork stays unnamed and is labelled as one made here is (`forkLabel`, §12); the file it came from stays only in its import record. **The chat's title** is never a branch file's name either (`stChatTitle` in `importer/stMapping.ts`): the family's root is the file, or, for a branch whose parent chat wasn't imported, the main chat its header names, without ST's `- Branch #<n>`/`- Checkpoint #<n>` suffix; a name ST made up for a branch (`Branch #<message> - <date>`, `Checkpoint #<n> - <date>`, `Bookmark #<n> - <date>`, [ST 1.12 `bookmarks.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/1.12.0/public/scripts/bookmarks.js#L149)) goes. For a stamp-only group root, `stChatTitle` recognizes ST's default `Group: <member names>` against the actual group's imported card names, independently of member order and retaining duplicate names. This follows [`createGroup` in ST's `group-chats.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/06bde939fb1e9c4c8d8641d810f0a916b5bce127/public/scripts/group-chats.js#L2086-L2102): ST joins the selected characters' names in character-list order. A default-named group stores only the stamp, so `chatName` uses its cast; a renamed group stores `<group>: <stamp>`, preserving even a group name equal to one member's name. Older group stamps without milliseconds are normalized with `000ms`, letting the existing date display show `created_at` in the same format as character chats. A user-named group root keeps its own name without a group prefix. If the automatic branch name was dropped, a renamed group's name remains, otherwise the cast supplies the name. A solo chat is its root's name, else empty, which shows its cast's names (`test/stChatTitle.test.ts`). These are fresh-import title rules; no migration or repair rewrites existing titles, including on re-import. `chatName` reads both of ST's stamps, `2026-05-11@07h51m55s691ms` and, from ST before late 2024, `2024-9-10 @13h 44m 41s 16ms` (unpadded, with spaces); a title that's only a stamp is named by the chat's cast, and so is ST's own `<card> - <stamp>` (owner, 2026-11-02: what ST names a new chat, `${name2} - ${humanizedDateTime()}` in [`script.js`](https://github.com/SillyTavern/SillyTavern/blob/release/public/script.js), and a dropped-in card's first; a group's chats are bare stamps, `group-chats.js`), when the part before the stamp is one of the cast's names, case aside. Any other name before a stamp is the user's: a group's name, or a rename here, which keeps the stamp (`renamedTitle`); a name the user gave the chat in ST has no stamp and is the title as it is. **The day a list shows is when the chat started**, `chats.created_at` (the header's `create_date`, else its first message's time; before importreport, 2026-11-02, the last message of its first part), wherever the caller has it (the chat list, the header, the character browser's fork rows, the override's chat link, the import report's latest chat); only title-only places (the bin's, a card revision's and rename history's chat names) fall back to the stamp's date. The stamp can be years older than the chat: ST names a card's first chat after the card's `chat` field (`getChat` opens `characters[chid].chat`, and `characters.js` keeps the field an imported card brings), so a card downloaded with its maker's chat name starts the user's chat under that name (owner's chat, 2026-11-02: named `2024-9-10 @13h 44m 41s 16ms`, first message April 2026). `test/stImportReport.test.ts`, `shared/test/chatName.test.ts`. `test/stImportTitles.test.ts` imports synthetic default-named, renamed and user-named group chats, checking the created-at date (header and first-message fallback), a renamed group matching one character, mismatched default-looking names, shell names, and existing-title preservation on re-import.

**Names belong to forks.** `StImportFinishChat` places a merged file's custom name on `forks.name`, including checkpoints with no messages of their own. Automatic filenames supply no label. The record's `forkId` keeps the name attached across shared-prefix swipe changes, writer changes, truncation, parent movement and reimports; no naming collision can force a suffix copy. `name_user` protects both a local rename and an explicit clear. A record already named by import keeps its label. A new source path is a separate file and fork, even when its bytes match another file; the old fork keeps its local name. Slot naming columns are frozen by `slots_branch_name_frozen` and serve only as legacy switch-point labels. Records lacking `forkId` resolve their recorded end to a fork when claimed, or create one if no fork ends there; `stImportFork.ts` remains solely to resume old interrupted suffix copies. There is no migration of deployed user data in this baseline-only build.

**Re-running is idempotent and resumable.**
- **Library files** are matched by `source_path`: the same hash is `unchanged`, another hash is a re-import into the same upstream ref (§3.9), merged with the user's edits. A file with the hash of an upstream ref the user already has, from a manual upload say, is that ref.
- **Chat files** are recorded in owned `jobs` rows (`kind: st-import-chat`): source, chat, fork, notes, mapped state and end. Re-import matches the recorded path, preserving local selections, amendments, hiding and deletions as that fork shows them. Only this file's fork advances to its new end, including from the nearest live ancestor after tail deletions; local continuations keep their tip and composer. If an unmatched ST message would replace a suffix carrying local selections, edits, hides, deletions or positional state, or a message the user inserted where the replaced suffix starts (below its parent, or above the first message when the first is replaced) or inside it, that fork likewise keeps its current path and tip (an insertion counts while it is placed in the fork, deleted or not, as a deletion counts); the record retains ST's replacement path for matching later imports. The check uses indexed lineage overrides, amendment history and visible event provenance rather than copying the old suffix. A message the user inserted is never a candidate for a file message (matching reads children with `inserted = 0`), so a re-import can neither move a fork onto one nor overwrite it; an append-only re-import goes below the file's last message, after any insertion there. Other forks at the same tip never follow an import's extension. Unchanged replay neither moves a tip nor changes its name. An unfinished import retains its fork, last matched position and prior path across batches and claims. A deleted fork makes the record binned, just as a deleted chat does; importing does not restore either. `forkVersionsReimport.test.ts` covers insertions before, at, inside and after a rewritten suffix, above a rewritten first message, and a deleted insertion restored in its original gap after re-import; a shortened file also retains live and deleted insertions in its removed tail.
- **Old ST messages:** the file's recorded slot at the same depth and with the same writer wins even when ST overwrote every swipe or an identical sibling exists. New text becomes an imported version on the existing slot. Its selection changes only in the recorded fork, through `writeSelect`, and shortening records a history reduction only there. Local effective selection, replacement, hide and deletion overrides in that fork, and amendment history, preserve the user's choice. Choices in other forks do not block import. Shared-prefix changes retain every suffix slot, version history, attachment and event without copying. Swipes remain available to every fork's picker (owner Q1); selection is independent. Purged placeholders match only by their recorded position, timestamp and writer, and never receive erased text. Changed versions or selections report updated; replay reports unchanged. Existing message drafts keep their original source, optimistic conflict handling and recovery (§3.10).
- **The import never removes chat content** [P] (a design change of 2026-10-12, after reviews kept finding what an undo had to protect). The record is written with the chat's first message, as `processing`. A new chat is visible from then on, titled `<title> (import unfinished)` until its import finishes (the client shows the marker as a badge, §12), with its leaf following its messages as they come in (from unset, or where the import last put it, so a leaf the user moved stays). An import that stops halfway leaves the chat as it was: a new import run reports it (`st.unfinished`) and finishes it from the record, or the user deletes it like any chat, into the recycle bin; the bin and its purge are the only place content is removed. A new chat is finished as new, and a branch from where the stopped run went its own way (`firstAdded`, kept in the record), with its parent's state as the state it changes. A chat that fails or whose request is interrupted gives back the budget its summaries held.
- **One run writes a file at a time** [P]. The record holds a lease, the import run's id: a run claims it (`StImportClaim`, which also returns the record as it is now, so a run never acts on a view of it another run or a finished import made stale), and every batch and the finish check it (`ImportLeaseLost` otherwise). Finishing clears it, so no earlier run writes a finished file. Starting an import makes it the user's current run (`StImportBegin`, a `jobs` row of kind `st-import-run`), and only the current run may claim a record, start a chat or write one: a run's request still on its way after the user started another writes nothing, and the leases of runs that are over count as expired.
- Anything in the recycle bin (a chat, a library entry) isn't imported again; a chat deleted for good is. Messages in the bin match, so a re-import doesn't bring back what was deleted here. A message deleted for good has empty versions: its placeholder matches only on this file's recorded prior path, at the same depth with the retained timestamp and writer. Its erased text and versions stay erased; new messages continue below it. Purged versions never match by their empty text. Whole deleted branches, including purged subtree roots, remain hidden.

**Re-import preview** (reimport1, 2026-11-14; the coordinator's ruling on audit question Q15, which the owner may overrule; MODEL-UX cases 58, 59, 62). Before a folder import starts, the form checks what it would do to chats already here. The import then does what the check showed, file by file, or refuses the file and says so (reimport2, 2026-11-14: the owner's rule, "the import must do exactly what the preview showed, or refuse and say so, never something else silently").
- **What the user sees.** Under the folder's kinds table, "Chats already here": a progress bar with Stop checking while it works, then one row per chat file that goes into a chat here (`StPlanTarget`: imported before; an earlier import's unfinished file; a new branch file of a file already here; its chat in the bin; only a greeting; unreadable), with the chat linked, its conditional counts (new messages, new branches, new swipes, shown swipes that change, messages kept as the user left them), whether the user went on locally (`keepsTip`: they stay on their messages, the new ones go on a branch beside them), an Include/Skip choice for each importable existing-chat file (including a quiet dependent file), Include all/Skip all enabled after checking finishes, and a lazily paged list of the changed messages (position, yours or a reply, what changes, the start of its text, rendered as text). Files with nothing new collapse into one line; files that become chats of their own are counted by the kinds table, not previewed. Import is disabled until the check is done. Nothing about it is in the URL, as the form isn't.
- **One matcher.** `placeStMessages` (`db/stImportPlace.ts`) is the matcher `StImportMessages` ran inline before: every read is a plain query and every change goes through `PlaceWrites`. The writer passes writes that store; the preview (`StImportPlanBatch`, `db/stImportPlanReads.ts`, a reader worker) passes writes that only count and return ids no stored row has, and an `observe` callback classifies each message. The file-to-chat mapping is `stChatTarget` (`importer/stChatTarget.ts`), used by `StImports.beginChat` and the preview alike; the record is read as `StImportClaim` would leave it (`claimedPayload`), and a branch file's first import as a new merged record on its parent's fork. Parsing is the import's own (`Formats.st.chatPart`, the same fallback dates).
- **Files that share a chat.** The import writes a folder's files one after another, so a branch file matches the messages its parent file adds in the same import. The preview keeps, per chat that more than one previewed file goes into, an overlay of what the files before would write (`PlaceOverlay`: new slots, versions added to stored slots, selections scoped to their predicted fork (a new branch inherits only its parent’s), texts as SHA-1), passed to each batch as JSON and merged into the matcher's candidate rows; a file read again from its start takes its additions back.
- **Where it runs.** `StImportPlans` (main thread) holds one preview per user in memory until an hour after it was last read or the user's next. A folder named by its path is read part by part (`readStFolderFile`, at most 8 MiB) in a fiber `CancelStImportPlan` interrupts; a picked folder's tab sends the chat files the preview lists in `wanted`, in the import's order, to `POST /st-import/plan-file` (the import's body limits, permits and one transfer per user; nothing stored). At most 500 changed messages per file and 20,000 in all are held for the detail list; counts cover every message. Virtual writes across shared chats are capped at 50,000 entries; exceeding the cap fails the check without authorizing import. Completed and cancelled checks release their overlays. Starts are serialized across their asynchronous mapping reads, so replacement cannot orphan a concurrent path plan. Plan fibers belong to the service scope, and a minute sweep interrupts and removes plans idle for an hour. Preview batches are background reader operations, preserving one foreground reader when the pool has at least two. The file list displays pages of 50 rows.
- **Admission checks** (review-reimport1). Before mapping, the preview captures SHA-256 stamps of the owned chats' counters and complete import-record rows. Taking these before mapping avoids blessing a stale mapping with a newer stamp; hashing complete records avoids count/latest-time collisions. `StImportBegin` fences earlier runs; the final per-file transaction below checks the chat stamp. Path confirmation requires the same canonical folder and full ordered chat manifest (including new chats). The import hashes the actual bytes parsed, in bounded parts, detecting same-size changes with restored mtimes without reopening files for a separate confirmation hash. A failed file makes the check fail. Upload and path plans cannot be interchanged.
- **Displayed uncertainty.** Counts assume card links can be resolved: linking still happens in the importer, and the preview says a file needing a choice may wait in the report or not be imported. It also explicitly calls new-chat counts estimates: new chat files are not checked and may be skipped or share a chat. Skipping an earlier file for the same chat hides later files' counts and message details and replaces the total with an explicit explanation; it does not claim the original dry run still describes that selection.
- **Held to the check, per chat** (reimport2). The check keeps, per chat it read, a stamp of that chat (`stImportChatStamp`, `db/stImportPlanStamp.ts`: its counters and its import records, SHA-256), and per file the SHA-256 of its bytes (`stBytesHash`, fed part by part, so a browser and the server cutting the file differently agree; the import record keeps its own hash of the parts, as before) and a digest of its per-message outcomes (`planCounter`, `db/stImportPlanCount.ts`: an XOR of SHA-256 over each message's file index and outcome, so it doesn't depend on where parts fall). Confirming builds `StPlanExpect` (`importer/stPlanExpect.ts`): every checked file but those in the bin, with its route (the chat and record it goes into, read as the check read it), hash, counts, digest and `keepsTip`, and the stamps; files the user skipped are not imported. Files `stPlanAffectedBySkip` marks uncertain have their counts hidden, and are held to their bytes, route and stamp rather than the original counts. A confirmed run (`StImports`, exact mode) checks at a file's first part that the check listed it, that its route is the same, and doesn't claim it on its own; each part's messages go to `st_import_stage` (`StImportStage`, a row per batch) instead of the chat, and its bytes are hashed as they come. At the last part, if the bytes are those checked, one writer transaction, `StImportCommitChat`, checks the chat's stamp, claims or starts the record, writes every staged batch from the reader's plans ("Preparing the write" below; an unplanned existing-chat file is refused), compares the counts, digest and `keepsTip`, finishes the record (summary slots, hidden runs, state hash), deletes the staged rows and returns the chat's new stamp, which later files of the same chat are checked against. Any difference (`StImportPlanChanged`, `ImportLeaseLost`, other bytes, another route) rolls the whole file back: the answer is skipped, "Changed since the check. Not imported.", and the report lists it (`st.changed_since_check`, a warning). A message sent, an edit, a hide, a swipe or a deletion here between the check and the file's write therefore refuses that file and leaves the chat as the user left it. `StImportBegin` drops the user's staged rows (a new run ends the old one), and so does startup (`StImportJobsInterrupted`). A new chat (a file the check routed to no chat here, its branches included) is held the same way until its last part, so a Stop or refusal before then writes nothing; its contents remain explicitly unpreviewed. Reimport3 then writes it as an unconfirmed import writes one, not in one transaction (`commitNewChat` in `StImports`): `StImportStartChat` with `once` claims the record and starts the chat (checking the run still holds the file), then `StImportCommitBatch` writes each staged batch in a transaction of its own (`placeBatch` without matching, cast computed beforehand from the file's events and written with the versions, the batch's stage row deleted), with `Effect.yieldNow` between batches so writes queued meanwhile go first (without it one concurrent write waited 5.7 s for a 2,000-message chat), then `StImportFinishChat` with `castWritten` finishes it and deletes its stages. Meanwhile the chat is listed as "(import unfinished)". Once started it goes on to the end, Stop or not; one that stops part way (`ImportLeaseLost` from a newer run, `NotFound` for a card deleted meanwhile, or a database failure) stays unfinished, the report says "This chat stopped part way and shows as unfinished. Import it again to finish it." (`st.chat_unfinished`), and the next import finishes it as it finishes any unfinished import. The check showed no contents for it, so nothing is held to the check between batches; a change made in the half-written chat meanwhile is met as during an unconfirmed import. Dropping or restarting a file, parse failure and request failure release its staged rows. Ending a job deletes its stages in the job-status transaction; cancellation, failure and idle expiry also revoke the current lease. Staging and final commit reject an ended job, fencing an in-flight part after Finish as well. A completed job's persisted, still-pending card-link decision authorizes only its named file to be sent after an explicit choice; the successful final transaction removes its stages before the saved report removes that decision. The existing minute sweep ends abandoned uploads after ten idle minutes. StImports also sweeps partial files by the time of their last actual part, covering card-link uploads begun after their job completed; report polling does not extend that deadline. It releases sessions idle for an hour. Neither case needs another import or restart for cleanup. Stage sequence advances before sending the worker request, so even a committed stage whose reply was lost is included in failed-request cleanup. One file is staged at a time, capped at 256 Mi characters of encoded batch text; exceeding it refuses the whole file and reports “This chat is too large to import. Not imported.”
- **What the report offers.** The finished import lists the refused files under "Not imported" with Check again, which opens the import form for the same source (`?job=&again=`) and checks it again, so the user sees what it would do now and imports from that.
- **Preparing the write** (review-reimport2). An early read-only stamp check refuses an already stale target before staging or matching its messages; it does not replace the final transaction's check. A post-fix repeat with eleven 2,000-message files (53 MiB) refused the stale folder in 1.09 s, versus 14.61 s for its confirmed import. The earlier 201-file stale run took 326.55 s before this check; that exact large stale run was not remeasured. For a file into a chat already here (its own record, or its parent's for a new branch), `StImportPlanBatch` with `plan` matches each batch on a background reader while staging and plans every write of it (reimport3; `StBatchPlan`, `db/stImportPlanOps.ts`): the versions it adds with the ids they take (uuidv7, made in the reader), the selections it changes, the run of new messages after the matched end with their slot ids (their version ids are allocated while preparing rows in the writer, before its transaction), the imported versions still lacking a cast, how the fork's tip and the record's progress move (`stepPlanTip`, simulating the per-batch tip moves of `placeBatch`), its counts and the file's digest so far, and the chat's stamp as it read it. The next batch is planned from where this one left (`ChatProgress.prepared`). It also returns the stored, unchanged prefix slots, and a wholly unchanged batch retains just its arrival metadata and those slots, rather than copying every swipe's text into staging. When every staged batch has a plan, `StImportCommitChat` applies them (`commitPlanned`): outside the transaction it checks every plan carries the check's stamp, sums their counts against the check's (counts, digest, `keepsTip`), and builds the rows; inside it confirms the run holds the file and the chat's stamp is still the check's (so the chat is as every plan read it), claims or starts the record, checks the speakers are live cards, then writes a statement per kind of row: one `version_records` insert from JSON, the selections, the new messages in bulk with their cast, one fork-tip update (moving `row_version` and the shell stamp as the per-batch moves would have), one record update, the finish (its cast an `UPDATE` by id list) and the stage deletion. The shell's fork summaries are no longer refreshed inside it: after the commit `StImportChatSummaries` computes them on a background reader and `StoreForkSummaries` stores them (a failure only logs; the shell recomputes them on its next read). A batch the reader cannot plan (a record resuming an old shared-selection copy, `forkPrior`) now refuses that confirmed file before staging or changing its chat (review-reimport3); the writer fences direct unplanned existing-chat commits too. The report says its interrupted import needs repair and that nothing from the file was imported. Current imports never create `forkPrior`; it is a retained marker from the old suffix-copy implementation, not a field from SillyTavern JSONL. Unconfirmed legacy imports retain their old matching path. Any concurrent message, swipe, hide, deletion, Undo, fork or chat rename invalidates it. An image-only human-message amendment explicitly moves the chat stamp too: its new amendment-history row changes the matcher’s local-edit flag even when the text is unchanged. Claiming an existing record only validates and records a supplied parent id; it does not change the matching fork, so existing branch records use the same certified preparation. Decoding staged batches and preparing row inserts happen before the write transaction in the writer worker. A current unfinished import without the old suffix-copy marker still prepares and resumes normally. A stamp covers the entire chat: a change on another independent fork of that chat conservatively refuses the file too, although that branch's isolated change need not affect matching. Changes to a different chat do not invalidate it.
- **Independent review of the prepared write** (review-reimport3, 2026-11-15). Every existing-chat file still commits once: staging and planning its early batches write no chat rows. All batch plans must carry the same expected chat stamp; the synchronous final transaction rechecks that stamp and the owned run/file lease before any claim or chat write. The stamp certifies the graph, versions and amendment history, effective fork selections/replacements/hides/deletions/insertions, lineage and tips, state events and complete import-record payloads; immutable version identity/writer/ordinal and slot constraints complete the matcher inputs. Speakers and note/state references are rechecked for ownership/liveness in the transaction. File bytes and mapped message inputs are held in owner/run/path-scoped staging, never accepted as caller-supplied plans. A new run removes the old run's stages and revokes its lease. Reader-allocated ids use UUIDv7 with cryptographic random bits, independently of each worker's millisecond counter; database unique constraints refuse a collision and roll back the file. Earlier batches of this file cannot invalidate later ones because none commits separately. A completed earlier *file* updates the session's expected stamp; a concurrent external change between files still refuses the later file.
- **After-commit reads and interrupted new chats** (review-reimport3). Fork summaries here are sidebar caches, separate from LCM summaries and imported-summary notes sent in requests. Finished-chat reads require current chat/user stamps and format, recomputing missing or stale rows in the reader, including after restart. Message search now follows those checks for the current cast used to name a chat and retains the unfinished-import marker in its results. Request assembly and import planning read the committed graph/state directly with their own causal bounds; they never consume sidebar summaries. A growing unfinished chat deliberately keeps its last sidebar summary or an empty placeholder, labelled unfinished, until finish; opening, search, exports and approved workshop reads can read its committed prefix. Exports retain the unfinished title. New-chat LCM starts off. A local continuation during batch writes retains its own tip; deleting the chat stops further writes and leaves it in the bin. A superseding import revokes the old run; its next import can finish the committed prefix without duplicates. Stop now refuses later files and waits for a new-chat write whose claim has already been dispatched, including its final report, before ending the job and cleaning staging. A database failure during those batches now returns and records “This chat stopped part way and shows as unfinished. Import it again to finish it.” rather than a generic file failure. The resumed checked import is compared with an uninterrupted import for all message/swipe text, selection, timestamps, generation metadata, cast/presence, hidden/deleted state, state events and fork tip; operational revision counters depend on how many writes were needed.
- **Limits.** A file needing a card link choice may be refused rather than linked. New chats are counted from the file list, explicitly as an estimate. Every confirmed file into a chat already here is one transaction. A planned one only applies rows, so it grows with the rows the file adds or changes, not with the chat; a file with many new swipes or a large rewrite still holds the writer for its writes, and an unplanned (`forkPrior`) existing-chat file is refused without writes in a confirmed run. A confirmed new chat is written batch by batch instead, so it can be seen, and can stop, half written. Unconfirmed imports retain their previous bounded-batch behavior.
- **Measured owner shape** (review-reimport2). One 225,850,629-byte synthetic file, 20,000 messages with 20–50 swipes on every message (699,935 versions), in a chat with 201 forks (the 200 added checkpoints inherit the first three messages), then three new messages: the builder’s final writer transaction took 73.33 s, with a concurrent write waiting 73.51 s. Reader preparation and compact unchanged batches reduced those to 4.65 s and 4.73 s. **This still exceeds 500 ms.** These are observed pauses for that fixture, not a maximum for new or heavily rewritten files. Peak staged text fell from 224.4 MB to 6.1 MB; process RSS growth during checking/import fell from 698 MB to 300 MB. These comparison runs preceded the image-only-amend stamp fix, which is not used by this fixture. A final-source variation with all 200 added forks inheriting the full 20,000-message path took 27.65–28.00 s in its final transaction; the longest concurrent write waited 28.16 s. The repeated fixture verifies the stored branch-base depth (19,999). Its check took 60.01 s and confirmed import 100.05 s, with 6.1 MB staged text and 202 MB process RSS growth. These are shared-host observations. Reimport3 remeasured the same fixture, both variants, with the first import also checked and confirmed, against the review-reimport2 code on the same host (a rename sent every 20 ms through the import is the "concurrent write"): re-import with forks at depth 2, longest writer transaction 2.88 s → 255 ms, longest concurrent write 2.99 s → 367 ms; forks at depth 19,999, 19.59 s → 180 ms and 19.69 s → 282 ms (the rest of the transaction is mostly the end-of-write summary settlement every write of a 201-fork chat pays, 164–236 ms); first import, one transaction of 65.3–76.7 s (a concurrent write waited 74.4–86.5 s) → transactions of at most 485 ms per batch, longest concurrent write 564–662 ms, p99 417–432 ms. The summaries computed after the commit took 13.5 s (depth 19,999) on a background reader, which leaves a reader free for other reads. Peak staged text for the first import stays the whole file (224.4 MB), as before.
- **Final independent measurements** (review-reimport3, 2026-11-15). On disk-backed scratch, five repeats each of first import and shallow/full-depth 201-fork re-imports (20,000 messages, 699,935 versions, then three added messages) measured worst transaction / concurrent-write wait: first import **393.9 / 507.2 ms**, shallow re-import **263.7 / 381.7 ms**, deep re-import **261.7 / 502.4 ms**. Five additional first imports starting the deep repeats reached **496.6 ms** for a transaction and no larger concurrent wait. The batch encoded-character limit is now 512×1024 rather than 1 Mi characters; the 100-message cap remains. Ten reduced-batch first imports had median wall time **85.54 s**, versus **85.61 s** in five original-size controls on the same shared host; no throughput cost near 15% was observed. Whole-run one-minute loads ranged from 13.89 to 47.99 at the recorded endpoints; the report preserves all 1/5/15-minute samples and per-case timings. These are observations, not a bound for arbitrary rewrites or indivisible long messages. A synthetic legacy `forkPrior` record still held the unplanned transaction for **84.79 s** and a concurrent write for **92.68 s** before the guard, even without copying a suffix. It is now refused before staging or changing its chat: **3.424 s** end to end, no staged rows, worst concurrent write **20.51 ms**. No current importer creates that marker. The report gives the explicit legacy-refusal limitation rather than claiming that old unconfirmed copies are bounded.
- **Review coverage.** `stReimportExact` covers cleanup, resource refusal, a late write after Finish, multipart ordering, BOM/CRLF/Unicode/trailing newline, and mutations before and after staging including multi-delete and Undo. Its slow abandoned-upload case advances idle time and waits for the real sweep. It also writes a confirmed new chat in many batches, and fails one part way (a test trigger): the chat stays "(import unfinished)" with the earlier batches, its stages are gone, and the next import finishes it. `stReimportCrashScale` runs the production final-write handler in a test-instrumented writer, on the planned path (plans made by the production reader op), stops it after the batches' writes inside the transaction, and terminates the thread: every message rolls back, integrity and foreign keys pass, and startup removes the remaining stages. An unplanned existing-chat commit is now a refusal/cleanup regression instead. A separate killed-writer case pauses after commit but before summary refresh, preserving the complete file and proving that restart recomputes current sidebar data. `stReimportOwnerScale` opts into 20,000 messages, 20–50 swipes each and 200 additional forks, recording RSS, database/staging growth and concurrent writer latency.
