- **Tests:** `stReimportPlan.test.ts` previews and then imports a synthetic folder (a new swipe and selection, appended messages, a local choice and hiding kept, a merged branch, a new branch file inside messages its parent file brings in the same import, a binned chat, a new chat) and checks that the slots and versions the import adds equal the preview's counts, that the preview wrote nothing, and the refusals, including files changed after the check; `stReimportExact.test.ts` refuses a file after a hide, edit, swipe, deletion or message sent here, or with other bytes, writing nothing of it, writes a file once when a second import of the same check starts part way, and races an import with a message sent here; `stReimportRoutes.test.ts` checks a branch of a new branch and seeded random trees of branches up to four deep (renamed, copied, orphaned) and requires every file imported and the added slots and versions to equal the counts; `stReimportParity.test.ts` with `ST_REIMPORT_PARITY_CONFIRMED=1` runs the master oracle through checked imports; `isolation.test.ts` covers the RPCs; `stReimportPlanScale.test.ts` (slow) measures a 101-file, 2,000-message, swipe-heavy family; `e2e/stReimportPreview.spec.ts` covers the form at 1440 and 390, light and dark, by path and picked.

**The report** (`StImportReport`): counts per kind (added, updated, unchanged, skipped, failed), messages, summaries, greeting-only chats skipped (a chat of exactly one message, not the user's: the chat ST makes by opening a card, DESIGN §1.4. The chat's first message is held back until a second one comes or the file ends, so the outcome doesn't depend on where the parts fall, and the rule is the same when an earlier import made the chat. A file of no messages is skipped too. A chat of two or more messages with none of the user's goes in [P]. Earlier versions held messages in `DATA_DIR/st-staging`; at startup that folder is removed once, unless it's a link, which is left alone), unsupported files, what the user must act on (at most 20,000), the link choices and hidden-run offers (at most 2,000 each), and how many didn't fit. Its messages quote files through `shownText`, and are rendered as text.

Report issues retain the full relative file path, both as the displayed path and as the key used to attach a chat link. Shortening that key to 40 characters made chats whose paths share a prefix link to the last one imported. Messages that quote names still use `shownText`. `test/stReport.test.ts` covers two long paths with the same prefix and distinct chat links.

The report holds only what a user must act on (DESIGN §1.2, owner 2026-10-28): `Report.issue` drops infos, and of a file's own report only its errors are kept (its warnings say what the import chose, which the entry shows). What's left: files that failed or weren't updated, the import's cap (`st.too_much`), an unfinished earlier import (`st.unfinished`), edits that conflict (`st.conflicts`), a file whose earlier import is in the recycle bin (`st.in_bin`, a warning saying to restore it or delete it for good), a lorebook a chat names that wasn't in the folder (`st.world_missing`), one ST applies to every chat that wasn't (`st.global_world_missing`, measured on each read from `globalSelect` and the books imported), ST's global books attached to no preset (`st.global_worlds_unattached`) and, though an info, the preset they were attached to (`st.global_worlds_attached`, measured on each read too), ST's selected preset missing (`st.preset_missing`) or not adopted because the user had chosen a default (`st.preset_kept`). The other notes the importer had made (the summary's placement and history, a character's note ST replaced, a chat without a user turn, a fork with no message of its own, messages shown differently, a chat no group lists, the preset adopted) are infos, so not listed: each is shown where it applies (the note, the chat, the lorebook's switch, the default preset) or changes nothing the user does. The counts, messages, summaries, greeting-only chats and unsupported files remain in `StImportReport`; the client shows compact imported counts, and Copy log includes the other report totals.

**Hidden runs** (DESIGN §1.4): a run of at least 10 hidden messages from message 0 [P: the threshold, since the decision says only "long"] is offered for un-hiding, once, for a chat the import made. `UnhideImportedRun` clears `context_excluded` on the path from the chat's first message to the run's last.

**Import jobs** (fux1, 2026-10-31; `importer/StImportJobs.ts`, `db/stImportJobWrites.ts`). The owner, after importing their real folder: "I clicked away while the import was going. Did it complete, or did it stop? … There's no section to see past import jobs." The browser used to drive every import, and its progress and report lived in the page: a reload or a closed tab stopped it, and leaving the page hid it. Every import is now a row of `st_import_jobs`: mode (`path` or `upload`), source (the folder's path, or the picked folder's name), status (`running`, `complete`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`), start, finish and update times, files and bytes done of their totals, the file it's on, the counts, the report (`StImportReport`, bounded as before) and the files that didn't go in. A path import runs in a fiber of the service's scope, never a request's, so closing the tab, navigating or reloading never stops it. Progress is written at most about once a second and the report so far every 15 s, each a small writer transaction; a `StImportChanged` notice (`@rp/shared/noticeApi.ts`) tells the user's tabs at most about once a second per job. An upload's job records its files as the browser sends them and ends as `interrupted` when none has arrived for 10 minutes (`UPLOAD_IDLE_MS`). At startup, jobs left `running` become `interrupted`, keeping what they had; running the folder again finishes them (re-running is idempotent and resumable, above). One import runs at a time per user (`StImportBusy`), since a new run fences the old one's writes. `CancelStImport` stops a path import after the file it's on; what is in stays. `ListStImports` and `GetStImport` read the caller's jobs only; `ClearStImports` forgets one finished job or every finished one, leaving what they imported; `SeenStImport` marks a finished job opened. A persisted report stays actionable: `LinkStImportChat` imports a path job's chat with the chosen card, reading the file again (refused while another import runs), and `UnhideImportedRun` names the job whose offer it settles. Tested in `test/stImportJobs.test.ts` and `test/stImportPath.test.ts`.

**The client** (`features/library/stImport.tsx`, `stJobs.tsx`, `stUpload.ts`), reached from the import page ("Import a SillyTavern folder", `/import/st`): the folder path with its browser, or a folder picked in the browser (`FileDrop` with `directory`, which takes no drops: a dropped folder has no paths), the ST user to import when the folder has several, what's in it by kind (cards, personas, chats, group chats, groups, lorebooks, presets, settings), each with how many files are new and how many are already here (`StImportPreview`: which of the plan's paths the caller's earlier imports hold, library files by their source path and chats whose import finished; for a folder named by its path, admin only, the server also reads what it can't tell from the records (`previewStFiles` in `importer/stFolderDisk.ts`): a card, lorebook or preset at a path no import recorded is hashed when earlier imports hold files of its kind, and is here if its bytes are, as the import matches it (not a persona's avatar: its import's hash takes in the persona's settings too; a file over 8 MiB is hashed 1 MiB at a time, so no file holds the main thread for long); a chat file of at most 64 KiB that holds no message, or one that isn't the user's, is listed as skipped, as every import skips greeting-only chats; `stPlanKinds` in `@rp/shared/stPlan.ts` counts them; settings and groups aren't kept as entries, so they're "read on every import"; read again on each look and when an import ends, under its own reactivity key).

**Import result page** (importpage, 2026-11-03; DESIGN §1.4). `/import/st` opens the newest import by default, including finished imports; `?job=` opens a history selection and scrolls to its result. The existing `stImportSections` registrations provide the result flow, history, then start form:
- **Result:** one status/date/duration line, with files and percentage while running, then compact Cards, Chats, Presets, Lorebooks, Personas, Warnings and Errors stats. Imported stats total added plus updated; Chats combines single and group chat outcomes. Zeroes stay visible. Running results retain their progress bar, current file, tab-lifetime guidance and Cancel import. The detail query shares the `st-imports` reactivity key, so progress, report snapshots and completed decisions refresh on import notices. Finished results mark the import seen.
- **Needs your action:** present only for unresolved card-link choices and hidden-run offers, counted in its header. Each row explains the problem beside its controls; phone rows wrap. Linking still offers candidates, any library card when there are none, and No card; path jobs use `LinkStImportChat`, browser uploads reuse this tab's retained files. Un-hide still shows whether the imported summary covers the messages. Successful actions remove their report decisions; decision writes wait until the import finishes.
- **Warnings and errors** (`stImportIssues.tsx`): group by severity, code and message; errors, warnings, info, then rarest first. Every group, including a singleton, is collapsible and starts folded, with its message and affected-file count visible. Expanded files retain details and affected-chat links. Failed transfers and job failures join the log without repeating an identical report error. Empty logs say No warnings or errors. Copy log copies the whole report as text, including collapsed issue groups, source paths, chat URLs, outcome counts, pending decisions, unsupported counts and the dropped-issue count. The report still retains its existing caps, with a visible count when entries were omitted. `Disclosure` supports an optional hover/focus explanation for these groups.
- **History:** one list with a date, status, aggregate counts and result link per import. Its header contains the sole Clear finished imports button; each finished row's ⋯ menu contains Remove from history. Removing a result changes no imported content.
- **Start another import:** the form comes last, expanded for an empty history and otherwise behind Import ST data again. The trigger stays above the panel and shows its pressed state; a corner close button closes the form. Starting a new job folds it again. The path/upload intake and preview remain as above. The remote-folder hint is one sentence. The former separate job-facts/report cards, next-step links and duplicate removal controls are gone.

`e2e/stImportResult.spec.ts` imports synthetic warnings, a broken preset and an unlinked chat at 1440 and 390 pixels: section order, card-link resolution, full clipboard log, history navigation/removal, the single clear control, form folding and stable trigger position, running/cancelled results, screenshots and measured layout checks. Existing folder-upload/path/report/date tests follow the new stats and collapsed form.

The file import page's back link goes back where the user came from, or to the library when there's no history. That page (`import.tsx`) shows two equal cards, "Import a SillyTavern folder" first (the main path, its link a primary button) and "Import files"; updating an entry from a file (`?into=`) shows only the second. Measured on the UI audit's synthetic folder (2,651 files, 446 MB) at load 45–60: the import took 5 min 50 s (23 min on the old build), and `/healthz` answered meanwhile with p50 10 ms, p99 88 ms, max 264 ms. The job list is one query (`ListStImports`, its own reactivity key) refreshed on `StImportChanged`; while a job runs, the library and chat lists are read again at most every 10 s and once when it ends, never per file (before, every file's request invalidated the library, so every open tab re-read `ShellLibrary` thousands of times). **The shell shows a running import wherever the user is**, and a finished or failed one until it's opened (`stJobs.tsx`, registered in the `appTools` slot, so a plugin can replace or disable it). `e2e/stImport.spec.ts` drives it with a synthetic folder in ST's multi-user layout, at phone and desktop width.

**Imported summaries** (DESIGN §8.1; [P] throughout, as the owner's details are open):
- **Where ST keeps one:** the Summarize extension (`extensions/memory`) saves each summary on a message (`extra.memory`); the current one is the latest on any message but the last (`getLatestMemoryFromChat` skips the last). ST sends it through `extension_settings.memory.template`, `{{summary}}` replaced, at its `position` (-1 none, 0 after the main prompt, 1 in-chat at `depth` with `role`, 2 before the main prompt), unless the extension is disabled. The `{{summary}}` macro reads it too. In ST 1.19.0 both depend on the extension being loaded: `setMemoryContext` sets the extension prompt at the configured position (`public/scripts/extensions/memory/index.js` l.964–965), the macro is registered only when the module loads (l.1111–1130), and a disabled extension's script is never loaded (`public/scripts/extensions.js` l.626–628), so with the extension disabled ST sends the summary nowhere, and with position None only through `{{summary}}`.
- **Where it goes:** a chat-owned note with `kind: imported_summary`, titled "Summary (from ST)" (notes imported before keep their title), holding the current summary, ST's template and its placement, with the earlier summaries as its earlier revisions. It is switched on exactly when ST was sending it: the extension enabled, and either its position not None or an enabled prompt of the ST preset selected at import (`oai_settings.preset_settings_openai`, read when that preset file is imported, before the chats) holding `{{summary}}` (`summaryMacroPrompts`). Its placement is ST's position while the extension was enabled, else none, so a summary sent only through the macro isn't also injected. From then on only its switch decides whether it is sent (DESIGN §8 [P]). Each revision records the message ST saved its text on (`source_slot_id`, the earliest of a run of the same text), so the assembler can send the one a path has (§15). The template, frequency and coverage are on the current revision only (each keeps its placement, which a note needs), and the history keeps the latest 200 summaries within 256K characters, so storing a chat's summary is one short write however long its template (a 128 KiB template with 1,000 summaries took 69 ms under load; when every revision carried the template, a review measured 13 MB written from a 141 KB upload, holding the writer 689 ms). Notes already have placement, state events and history, so no migration was needed; a field on the chat was the alternative. A summary kept in the author's note stays in the author's note. The assembler places it as ST did, and `{{summary}}` reads it (§15 "Imported summaries").
- **Covering the hidden run:** the summary covers the run when the message it's on is at or after the run's last message, since ST summarizes the chat up to the message it saves the summary on. The note then records `covers` (the run's first and last slot and its length), and the offer says so (`summaryCovers`). A summary from before the run's end is reported as not covering it. **Import writes no L1 summary row:** enabling LCM is when the user chooses between adopting the summary as that range's L1 and redoing LCM (DESIGN §8.1); the adoption is `EnableLcm` (§16, *Enabling and backfill*), which reads `covers`.
- A summary on the last message, which ST ignores, is left unused, as ST leaves it.

**Bulk message writes and regression coverage** (importspeed, 2026-11-02). `db/stMessageBatch.ts` allocates IDs and encodes new message batches before the writer transaction. When a batch starts with matching off, two ordered `INSERT … SELECT` statements over JSON write its versions and slots, with the same constraints, indexes and triggers as the positional writer. Existing-message matching, edits and branch reconciliation retain the positional path. The format worker bounds batches by 100 messages / 512×1024 encoded message characters (a single longer message remains indivisible). Confirmed existing-chat files use the whole-file transaction described above; confirmed new chats and unconfirmed imports write one transaction per batch. Arrival ownership checks use an indexed entity lookup instead of constructing the owner's whole card list for each message batch. Cast pins retain slot-local summary invalidation, so finishing a new branch does not recompute older forks.

`test/stImportBatch.test.ts` compares all columns of the stored chat, forks, slots, versions, participation, state and import record, plus FTS contents and foreign-key checks, against the positional writer for the same synthetic multi-batch fixture (normalizing IDs, version sequence offsets and operational clocks). `test/stImportSummaryValidity.test.ts` verifies that importing another branch retains older cached summary rows and that their contents match a full recomputation. `test/stFolderTimingScale.test.ts`, included automatically in `npm run test:slow`, imports 2,000 synthetic files through the full path-import job and workers into a fresh database: 1,599 cards and 400 long chats, 120,000 messages / 160,000 versions. It reports end-to-end wall time, process CPU time and approximate scan/library/chat phases from persisted job progress, and enforces a generous three-minute budget. `ST_FOLDER_TIMING_OUT` saves its JSON measurement. Fixture generation precedes the timer; server startup is included. On the 48-core development host, the 201.7 MiB folder took 34.4–36.3 seconds in isolated repeats; the existing 650-branch test took 48.1 seconds in the full slow suite.

**Measured** (2026-10-12, `test/stImportScale.test.ts`, opt-in with `ST_IMPORT_SCALE=1`; source workers, load average 15 to 20): a synthetic 50,000-message chat (80.7 MiB; a third of the model's messages with three swipes; about 1 KB each) imports in 20.8 s, and again, unchanged, in 3.3 s. The writer took it in 500 transactions of 100 messages: 448 over 25 ms, median 29 ms, 95th percentile 68 ms, longest 192 ms (with 250 per batch: median 69 ms, longest 389 ms). The test process (the server, its workers and the test's own copy of the file) peaked at 1.06 GB RSS and 218 MB of main-thread heap, and the main thread's event loop was never more than 17 ms late (25 ms in an earlier run).

**Tested:** `test/stImport.test.ts` imports a synthetic folder (`test/support/stFolder.ts`) through the real server as the client does (`test/support/stUpload.ts`): cards, personas, a lorebook, a preset, a group, a main chat with a branch, a greeting-only chat, a renamed card, a chat linked by its greeting, (`test/stImportLinks.test.ts`) a card downloaded again under a new file name linked by its speaker's name, ST's `undefined` folder, and a card's own lorebook not reported missing, an ambiguous link resolved by a choice, a hidden run with several summaries (one on the last message), a summary without a hidden run, a summary kept in the author's note, and unsupported files. It checks the graph, speakers, state, notes and report. A second run of the whole folder in 600-byte parts changes nothing; a chat sent in parts matches one sent whole, and takes ST's later messages on a re-import; hostile paths are refused before the body is read. `test/stImportReimport.test.ts` imports ten synthetic messages, then reproduces ST 1.19’s `public/script.js` writes: a new selected swipe on old message 4 (zero-based), an in-place edit overwriting its selected swipe, both changes plus two appended messages, and an edit after a local continuation. It asserts the same slot ids and parents, preserved and selected versions, version metadata, no duplicate suffix, leaf and composer, updated reports and unchanged replay. Further cases preserve local selections, edits, hides and deletions (including purge), and prefer the recorded path over an identical sibling’s text. Its exhaustive graph snapshots use the existing fixture worker with a read-only connection, closing it and waiting for worker exit before the helper completes; a main-thread SQLite guard rejects application-database connections while allowing the startup instance lock. `test/stImportForkNames.test.ts` and `test/stImportForkNamesReview.test.ts` check automatic filename recognition and user names resembling it. `test/stImportNamePlacement.test.ts` checks fork-owned names and clears across Unicode and nested files, shared-prefix swipe and writer changes, replay and identical-byte files under distinct source paths; shared-tip checkpoints get separate named forks. `test/stImportSharedSelection.test.ts` checks fork selection overrides, unchanged shared slot IDs and suffix size, local amendment history and events, parent isolation and replay, including an interrupted 205-message import. The bin tests verify re-import creates no copies and preserves purge and restore. `test/forkVersionsReimport.test.ts` checks that re-import addresses the recorded fork even while a checkpoint is current, retaining each fork's amendment and attached events on the shared suffix; and that a re-import stops at an insertion right above the rewritten message, inside the rewritten suffix and above a rewritten first message, goes on as before with an insertion before the change (which stays in place), and never matches an appended ST message to an inserted one with the same text, writer and time. `test/stImportLocalState.test.ts` covers local variable choices, unrelated and other-fork updates, edited/switched/deleted notes, a writer change retaining a locally edited suffix, and shared-tip note editor routing with cross-chat fork refusal. `e2e/stReimportDrafts.spec.ts` covers saved and in-flight message drafts at desktop and phone widths, reload, a second re-import while version reads are held, Save’s original source and Cancel’s recovered text.

**Known limits:**
- A line of a chat file can't be longer than a part (8 MiB).
- A re-import changes a chat's state only from new messages on; without any, nothing moves.
- Speakers and links are matched only against the cards in the folder imported.
- The writer decodes each batch before its transaction, but still in the writer thread.

**Registered parts of the ST import** (PLUGINS §8). The folder import has two registries of §6's kind, apart from the library importers (§11.2), whose result cannot express chat parts. **Folder handlers** (`StImports.handlers`, `importer/StImports.ts`) dispatch a file by its kind (`settings`, `persona_avatar`, `card`, `world`, `preset`, `group`, `chat`, `group_chat`). The built-ins register at layer start through the same API plugins use. A disabled handler fails with a specific message and a `st.handler_disabled` report issue. The chat handlers retain the part, lease and recycle-bin handling. A handler reads through typed format operations (`Formats.st`) and stores through the writer's typed operations. The path classification, sessions, holds and ownership checks stay fixed.

**ST parser sources** (`StParserRegistry`, `importer/stParserRegistry.ts`) are exposed alongside `Formats` on the server. Entries name a parser id (`chat-part`, `settings`, `group`, `library-file`, `persona`), a trusted module URL and an export with the corresponding `StParsers` signature (`importer/stParse.ts`). The built-ins register the same source descriptors, using the bundled `rp:st-parsers` module. A plugin uses an absolute module URL; it may wrap the exported `builtinParsers`. These references come only from trusted server registrations, never uploaded contents. Each `Formats.st` job captures the effective source when its Effect executes and transfers it with its bytes through the typed RPC; the module is loaded only in the format worker. This works in source and bundle mode, across the pool and after a crash. `disable` sends an explicit absent source and returns a `st.parser_disabled` report. Closing a registration scope restores the previous source for new jobs; already admitted jobs retain their selection. ESM modules remain cached: changed code needs a new module URL. This is worker execution plumbing; plugin installation and consent UI are not built. `test/stFolderSeam.test.ts` covers the real workers and HTTP upload path.

### 13b. Exporting chats and the library (importexport1; reviewed 2026-11-14)

⋯ Export… is the registered `chat.export` command (`features/chat/chatExport.tsx`). It offers SillyTavern JSONL or plain text and this branch or every branch. The chat kind's registered profile controls its formats (`chatKinds.exportFormats`); workshops offer text only. Format and scope controls have hover explanations, progress and Stop. The existing tab URL is unchanged.

Neither format has a place for a chat's own picture (§12), so an export leaves it out; the dialog's list of what is left out names it (families1, 2026-11-15).

`POST /library/chat-export` accepts `{chatId, forkId, scope: "branch" | "all", format: "jsonl" | "txt"}`. `POST /library/archive` exports the account's library. Both require JSON and the ordinary authenticated session/cross-site guard. Ownership is checked before the response begins; foreign or binned chat/fork ids return 404. A shared per-account reservation covers preparation and transfer, so a second chat or library export returns 503 even while the first is preparing. Other accounts retain their own independent reservation.

**Bounded reads** (`importer/chatExport.ts`). Reader workers alone execute SQLite. A backwards pass through `ReadPath` windows of at most 1,000 keeps only page cursors, then re-reads each page root first. It retains one page of selected messages, not a branch's entire text. Swiped messages use the classified reader operation `ExportVersions` (ListVersions' fork-local replacement/deletion rules), in batches of 20 messages. The graph/display-path reader includes insertions, merge paths and branch-local choices while omitting binned messages/versions. Each read transaction has its own snapshot; the archive does **not** promise a snapshot across pages or files. Edits during export may appear, and deleting a referenced object may stop it. Both export surfaces explain changes made during export.

**ST lines** (`formats/stChatExport.ts`). The header carries `user_name`, `character_name`, `create_date` and `chat_metadata.main_chat` for a branch. Messages carry `name`, `is_user`, `is_system` (context excluded), ISO send/generation timestamps, `mes` and `extra`. Multiple versions have `swipes`, `swipe_id` and `swipe_info`, with dates and generation metadata for each swipe. Failed and in-progress versions retain their partial text; ST has no matching status field. `extra` carries reasoning via `stReasoningExtra`, with ST's `reasoning_type` (`stReasoningType`: an import's recorded `edited`/`manual`; thinking an edit changed is `edited`, thinking added where there was none `manual`, thinking an edit kept its source's type; else `model`, or `parsed` for sections), API/model, tokens, first-token and reasoning milliseconds. Native versions obtain token counts and generation times from the existing owner-scoped `VersionMetrics` reader, at most 200 version ids per request, within the 20-message export batch. Output counts follow the inspector's continuation ancestry; unknown counts stay absent. Start/finish and first-token delay are the last request's actual timestamps; native reasoning duration is not recorded in this ledger and is not invented. Imported figures remain unchanged. Template greetings fill `{{char}}` and `{{user}}`. Speaker identity comes from the selected version/first speaker, CastCards and the branch-tip persona/played-by-me state; ST has one speaker identity per message, so speaker changes between swipes and changing player roles cannot be represented. Plain text carries only shown text, as `Name: text`.

**Branches.** Every-branch scope always produces a ZIP, including a one-branch chat. Files come parents first and contain full paths. Names include the user's branch name, sanitised and de-duplicated case-insensitively; unnamed secondary branches use `Branch #n`. The unnamed root uses the chat title. `main_chat` names the immediate parent file; the parent's split message has ST's `extra.branches` link. Imported forks without an explicit base use their inferred shared-prefix count for that link. A split before the first message has no message on which to attach a child link. Names normalise Unicode, replace path/control/reserved characters, avoid Windows device names and trailing dots/spaces, and limit component lengths by UTF-8 bytes.

**ZIP writing** (`formats/zipStream.ts`). Entries deflate as they arrive, with bounded deflater input slices, ZIP64 local headers and 64-bit data descriptors. Central records use ZIP64 sizes/offsets when necessary; ZIP64 end/locator records cover files or offsets above 4 GiB and 65,535 or more entries. Only the central directory grows with the file count. Closing the generator destroys the deflater and closes its input iterator.

**Browser downloads** (`features/library/files.ts`). The page asks either POST route for a native download using `x-export-download: native`. The JSON response contains a random, account-bound, single-use ticket. An ordinary browser download from authenticated `GET /library/download?key=…` streams directly to the download manager; the page never reads archive bytes into a Blob. It polls authenticated `GET /library/download-status?key=…` for bytes produced/completion/failure. `POST /library/download-stop?key=…` requires JSON and interrupts an active stream, even under network backpressure, or releases an unstarted ticket. Stop/navigation aborts the page's work and warns to discard any unfinished file. Unstarted tickets expire after 60 seconds; completed status is consumed once or expires shortly after transfer. Foreign/guessed tickets return 404 on every route, unauthenticated requests 401. The legacy direct POST body remains available for API clients. All responses have `Cache-Control: no-store`. Progress measures bytes produced at the server, not disk-write acknowledgement at the device.

**Whole library** (`importer/libraryArchive.ts`, the `library.export-archive` card in the `library.import.cards` slot). The ZIP follows ST's folder layout: character PNGs in `characters/`, persona PNGs in `User Avatars/` with names/descriptions in `settings.json`'s `power_user`, lorebooks in `worlds/`, and prompt presets in `OpenAI Settings/` (ST's folder for all chat-completion API types). Existing registered format exporters write each document. World filenames are planned before cards; archive-only filename mappings update card `extensions.world` in the format worker, including sanitisation and collisions. Exact imported source names (including distinct NFC/NFD identities) take precedence over labels; ambiguous legacy names retain their original reference. Stored documents and individual-document exports are unchanged. Cards include the existing exportable card notes and public extension data; notes marked private are excluded. PNGs include V2/V3 chunks and embedded lorebooks, the avatar but no saved embedded assets. Personas use ST's default position/depth/role. Archived library entries are included; binned entries/chats/branches/messages/versions are excluded. Chats whose kind offers JSONL include every live branch under `chats/<character>/` or `group chats/`, with group definitions in `groups/`. Group messages carry `original_avatar` and `force_avatar` referencing the archive's de-duplicated filenames, so equal display names remain distinct. Persona messages carry their persona avatar. Chats without an exported character use an empty-member group, so ST can list and open their transcripts rather than leaving orphan files in a character folder. Avatar URLs use the actual captured character/persona folder even when the user plays an ordinary character card. The group definition selects the current branch, rather than always its root. An entry refused by a format exporter is listed in `Not exported.txt`.

**Format losses, shown before download.** Chat exports omit images, notes (including own-turn notes), shared/per-character summaries, edit history, binned items, version marks, per-version authorship and statuses. Separate contexts, away/presence periods, threads and joins flatten to their visible transcript; importing into ST does not preserve who knew what. Every branch remains a separate full path, without thread/join rules. Library archives also omit workshops, saved card assets, standalone/chat notes, application plugin state, connections, credentials and other account settings; public card/preset extension payloads remain ordinary document content. Exportable own-turn card notes remain in the card's extension, but ST ignores their own-turn rules. This is an interoperability archive, not a complete harness backup.

**Verification.** `test/chatExportNative.test.ts` checks ledger figures for a locally generated unswiped reply and an unselected model swipe using only a loopback synthetic responder. `test/chatExport.test.ts` retains the synthetic folder/chat/library round trips with every message/version, hidden flags, reasoning and recorded generation. Independent `test/chatExportReview.test.ts` covers named group branches, duplicate-name speakers, current branch, parent links, clean-account reimport, binned items, away-period flattening, preparation races, native transfers, cancellation and account isolation on all five routes. Client `test/downloads.test.ts` verifies a 12 GiB progress report without fetching file bytes, late preparation cancellation and streamed failures. `test/formats/stChatExport.test.ts` covers lines, partial versions, portable names and small ZIPs; slow `test/chatExportMemoryScale.test.ts` bounds RSS for a 1.5 GiB selected-text transcript; `test/zipExportScale.test.ts` writes an actual >4 GiB entry followed by >65,535 entries and verifies offsets and the large entry's entire CRC with Python's independent ZIP reader. `e2e/chatExport.spec.ts` downloads both scopes and the library with layout audits at 1440/390, light/dark. `test/chatExportScale.test.ts` measures a swipe-heavy synthetic family, one/every branch and the whole library, concurrent reads/writes, a second export and cancellation; `CHAT_EXPORT_BRANCHES`/`CHAT_EXPORT_MESSAGES` set the scale. The review report records actual runs and measurements.

## 14. Editing the library

**Copy over HTTP** (followups-ac, 2026-11-07; DESIGN §10.2). Message, reasoning and snippet copy actions and the bin's recovered-text Copy use `src/copyText.ts`. It tries Clipboard API first, then a temporary invisible textarea and `document.execCommand('copy')` when the API is absent or refuses. The fallback stays inside an active dialog, removes its field and restores focus and selection. Both paths receive the original source string, preserving Markdown and whitespace. `e2e/copyHttp.spec.ts` exercises the copy actions without `navigator.clipboard` and checks the actual clipboard text.

**Creation (newflows, 2026-11-06).** The Library's registered New actions follow its selected kind. Cards offer New persona under Personas; Lorebooks and Notes have their own actions. Notes lists use `ListSharedNotes` (global shared notes, excluding chat/card-owned slots). `NewDocumentDialog` names an empty lorebook (`CreateLorebook`, `CreateEntity` in the writer) or a library note (the existing `CreateSharedNote`); library/header actions open its large editor. Lorebook attachment pickers for chats and presets use the same dialog: a chat attaches and opens the book in its Lorebooks panel (revealed and flashed); a preset holds its attachment behind Save, as before, and opens the book. Cards currently author their own embedded book and have no separate attachment picker. Attachment retries keep the created ref.

**New persona is New card (personaform, 2026-11-07; DESIGN §2.2).** `NewCardDialog` with `persona` is the same form and flow: display name, in-chat nickname and version, the same name check and Create; only the title ("New persona") and its own server draft (`persona:new`) differ, and `CreateCard` gets `persona: true` (`CreateEntity` writes the persona tag in the same transaction, so the card is a persona from creation). The picture and every definition are then set in the card editor: the portrait with the cutout chooser (§14.5c), the description and the rest in the code editor. Persona lists on Home, the left panel, Add characters and Library open the full editor, as New card does; the persona editor's switcher opens it in that editor. The chat's persona picker (`SpeakerSwitcher` with `persona`) also makes the new card the chat's persona (its `onPick`, after reading the cards again; `PendingChat.listCards` refreshes its available cards and cast so a newly created persona can be selected before the first send; the pending page and selector pass their subscribed snapshot into `PendingChat.view(state)` so the production compiler refreshes the cast on persona changes; speaker/persona pickers reread their card choices on each opening, including personas made from another selector) and, once the chat's cast plays it, shows its card tab in the side panel (`useShowPanel`, `card:<entity>`). `CreateCard` still accepts an optional `description`, which no form sends. Browser flows and the focused layout audit share `e2e/support/newflows.ts` (1440/390, light/dark); server creation, ownership, editing and account-settings tests are `test/newflows.test.ts`. `e2e/pendingPersonaCreation.spec.ts` covers creation from the pending composer with no personas, selection, the side-panel editor and the first send at both widths in both themes.

The card and preset editors (DESIGN §4, §6.2): every field edits through a draft on the server, saving commits a revision, and nothing is ever lost. Contract in `@rp/shared/editorApi.ts` (merged into `AppApi`), the shared logic in `@rp/shared/editing.ts`, handlers in `packages/server/src/api/editor.ts`, storage in `db/editorWrites.ts` and `db/editorReads.ts`.

**Main is permanent** (owner, 2026-10-28). A preset always has a `main` prompt and an order entry for it. The editor permits switching it off and moving it, but never deleting it, including an imported Main marked as a custom prompt. `withMain` and `presetOrder` in `@rp/shared/presetOrder.ts` put a missing Main first, switched off, keeping any existing prompt text; if the prompt itself is absent they supply an empty Main. ST imports, our document import validation, editor reads of old revisions, order writes, and revision storage/restores apply this rule. Old revisions remain unchanged in history. Reordering and resetting retain the slot. Notes before and after a switched-off Main still occupy its empty slot, including when Main is placed in-chat. The assembler no longer skips those notes for an absent Main; no fidelity-gate matcher existed specifically for that case. Regression tests cover import/reimport, document validation, editor order writes, restore storage, note placement, and the custom Main's browser controls.

**Card fork surfaces** (card forks unit 5; `features/cardForks/`). The card page and editor offer, as buttons, and a library item's menu offers Fork, Forks, Compare with parent (or Compare with family for a root), Mark as a fork of… and Unlink. Fork starts with the parent's saved display name, version and in-character name; version is focused and the display name/version collision check blocks creation until one differs. It copies the card and its notes through the existing `ForkCard`, optionally moving the card's drafts after they reach the server, always moving its notes' unsaved text to the copies (§3.10), and opens the independent card's editor. Non-card variants retain their previous dialog and following semantics.

The editor and card page have a Forks section; the Forks action and the home grid's fork-count/fork badges open the same family list as an indented tree. Each member shows its display name, version, last use and chat count. Usage comes from the shared shell query, counting visible fork views as chats and dating a card by its own latest speaking activity, consistently with the card page and home; family metadata supplies lineage and deleted states. Live and archived members link to their editor, the current card is marked, and binned/purged members remain visible with state badges. Provenance says “Forked from” with the parent's name and state, and “Made for” with a link to the named chat when applicable. Comparisons are read-only field diffs of the two saved heads (drafts excluded), using the existing revision diff UI, with a selector for any other family member. A binned member offers a restore explanation, and a purged member says its content is unavailable, instead of attempting to open its editor. Taking text over is ordinary editing. The parent picker searches live and archived cards by display name, version and in-character name (`LibraryRef.modelName`, read from the saved head in the database worker), ranks matching display names first and surfaces writer refusals (including a cycle). Mark and Unlink only call `SetCardParent`; they write no content revisions. `LibraryRef.hasImport` reports whether an upstream has an import line; the library's Update from file action is shown on cards only when that is true, never on a newly made fork.

**Card contribution seam** (`features/cardForks/surfaces.tsx`). `cardContributions` uses the same reversible, reactive registry as chat contributions. `CardSurface` derives its rendered entries from the captured registry snapshot, so React Compiler observes replacements, additions, disablement and disposal after mounting; removing an action also unmounts its dialog. Hosts supply the entity and optionally an editor store, and request actions, provenance, family or badge placement through `CardSurface`. An `actions` contribution may also have a `menu` entry and a `dialog` (`CardMenuProps`: `openDialog`, `closeDialog`), which overflow-menu hosts list (`cardMenuEntries`; the library's item menu) and mount outside the menu; one with only a `component` shows only where actions are inline, and one with only a `menu` only in menus. The fork commands register all three; from a menu, Fork loads the card's editor store in its dialog ("Loading the card…") and Unlink reports a refusal as a toast. The library shows only the `badge` placement on its items; provenance and the family section are on the card page and in the editor. The fork feature registers each command separately (`card-forks.fork`, `.family`, `.compare`, `.parent`, `.unlink`) and each non-action surface separately (`.family-surface`, `.provenance-surface`, `.badge-surface`), with lazy bodies. Plugins can override, disable or add one contribution; hosts contain no fork-specific actions. An action may set `overflow`: a host with a More menu (the editor) renders those there and the rest in its bar (`CardSurface`'s `overflow` filter), other hosts render all inline; the fork feature marks every command but Fork. This is the new minimal seam for card actions and panels where the chat registries did not apply. Browser tests (`e2e/cardForkSurfaces.spec.ts`) import the realistic synthetic ST folder, make forks through the UI and cover the dialogs, multi-generation tree, arbitrary family comparison, linking/unlinking, cycle refusal, provenance, deleted members and badges at 1440/390 in both themes. The registry test covers replacement, disabling and restoration. The mounted Vite/React Compiler regression in `e2e/chatContributions.spec.ts` checks all four card placements across the card page, editor, library and home grid, including open-dialog removal. Card-fork browser regressions also check archived-parent search by in-character name, family counts against shell fork views and saved-head comparisons excluding drafts.

**Creating a prompt preset** (U11; `CreatePreset`, `features/editor/NewPreset.tsx`): the editor registers New card and New prompt preset in the `library.actions` slot. A named preset is created as an owned library upstream through the existing writer operation, with the built-in ordered prompt document, Main and Post-History Instructions forbidding card overrides, and regex unapproved. It opens immediately at its own address (`/library/$refId`), with the same drafts, history, save and export paths as an imported preset. It contains no model settings. Server and browser regressions cover creation, safe defaults, editing and reload.

**Revisioned text comparisons** (U17, 2026-10-28; DESIGN §6.2, UX-REWORK “Editing and saving”). Message and summary editors use the existing lazy `CodeEditor`, with change gutters and the existing server drafts and browser recovery. The registered `message.text-editor` and `summary.text-editor` contributions supply the editor; `message.editor.tools` and `summary.editor.tools` add a live, full-text “Compare with saved text” view (for a message, in its editor's History menu, as a dialog). An edit compares against its source message version (even when a different swipe is selected); a new written version compares against empty text. Summary drafts fix their comparison and save base on the first keystroke, before autosave, and retain their named revision when another tab selects a different one. The editor reads that revision's immutable text; a failed comparison read offers Retry saved text without closing or discarding the draft. Saving and discarding still use the existing draft lifecycle.

Library history now uses the paginated revision browser for notes as well as cards and presets: selected revision against its first parent (empty for the first revision), or against the current working document. Restoring makes a new revision; card name checks apply only to cards. All library Save comparisons use each changed field's draft revision base and the full-text merge view. The message version picker's Changes view, saved amendment history (earlier text → current saved version), and expandable summary revision comparisons (selected earlier revision → saved summary) also use full-text merge views. Expandable comparisons, including each library-history field, mount their merge editors only while open. These reuse `RevisionDiff`: side by side at desktop widths, unified removed/added text below 640 px, read only, with complete documents available through scrolling. `e2e/revisionText.spec.ts` covers note/preset Save, history and restore with long text at 1440/390 in light/dark; `e2e/messageHistory.spec.ts` covers restored message/summary drafts, change gutters, current comparisons, saved amendments and summary revision comparisons at the same sizes and themes. Existing draft safety tests use the code editor's full-document assertion helper. Review regressions in those browser suites check comparison-read retry with subsequent editing and Save, and allocation only for open library fields; `test/editorHistory.test.ts` covers a revision arriving before the first summary autosave.

Preset-attachment creation tests hold `CommitEditorDrafts` while checking that the previous revision has no attachment, then release it and wait for the save cluster to finish before reading the revision and reloading. The plain creation suite and focused layout audit share this regression (`e2e/support/newflows.ts`); an immediate read after clicking Save can still see the previous revision.

### 14.1 Drafts per field

**Every field the user edits is a draft** (§3.10), keyed by the ref and the field's path in the document (`entity_field`). A text field's draft holds its text; any other field's (a number, a switch, the prompt order, a new prompt, a list of tags) holds its JSON, with the path prefixed `=`; the literal `undefined` explicitly omits an optional field. So each field has its own undo history on the server, the order of 100 prompts included, and a reload or another device finds every unsaved change.
- **Paths name list elements by identity** where they have one (`["prompts", "identifier=main", "content"]`, as merge conflicts do, §3.9), so reordering never moves a draft to another prompt. Lists without identities (`alternate_greetings`) use indexes; an index into a list with ids (`modules`, `prompts`, `order`, `regex`, a lorebook's entries, or any list whose elements all have one) is refused, since after a reorder it would name another element.
- **Only the canonical spelling of a path is a field** (`parseField`): at most 8 segments, indexes whole and not negative, no `__proto__`, `constructor` or `prototype`. `SaveEditorDraft` refuses anything else (`EditRefused`). A value with such a key at any depth is refused when the drafts are applied.
- **The working document** (`applyDrafts`) is the head with the drafts applied: values first, shallowest first, then texts, so a text in a prompt a value draft added lands in it. In a list, `null` at an element removes it, and an identity no element has adds one at the end. The client builds it for the diff and the search; the writer builds it again to commit.
- **Protected fields** never change through a draft, each having its own action or none: `schema_version`; a card's `avatar_media_id`, `avatar_crop` (§14.5c) and `asset_media_ids`; a preset's `regex_approved`; a note's `owner`.
- A draft records the revision it started from (`baseRevisionId` when a session starts). Saving the same text against a new base now moves the base (`drafts.ts`), which is how the client keeps a draft after a conflict.

### 14.2 Saving

**`CommitEditorDrafts`** takes the ref's row version and the drafts to save, each with its row version, and in one writer transaction:
1. checks the ref and every draft are as the client saw them (`StaleWrite` otherwise: another tab typed on);
2. sets aside the drafts in something that's gone (a prompt or module deleted since, here or in what it follows): they end as discarded, their text going to the recovered texts, and the reply names them (`setAside`) so the client can say so. This comes first, so such a draft is never a conflict;
3. checks the others for conflicts: a draft whose base isn't the head conflicts where the saved version changed that field since its base, unless both now say the same. A base is read from the ref's entity, or from the card it was forked from for a draft moved with a fork (§3.9). Nothing is saved, and `EditConflict` names each field with the saved value and the draft's;
4. applies the other drafts and validates the result against the kind's schema (`validateDoc`), which would also drop keys the schema doesn't know. `InvalidDocument` lists the problems with their paths, at most 20. A draft the schema would drop (text at a key it doesn't know) is refused the same way, and stays: a save never ends a draft whose text it didn't keep (`droppedDrafts`);
5. writes the revision (origin `user`, with the user's message), unless nothing changed, and passes the change on to the refs that follow (§3.9);
6. ends the drafts' sessions on the new revision, each keeping its text and edit history (§3.10). The held structural changes (`HELD_FIELD`, §14.6) are never among them: a field list naming one leaves it out.

**Every revision is valid for its kind** (card, preset, note, lorebook; a preset overlay has no schema yet). Each write path checks what it was given and says why it refuses: commits, resolved updates and merges here, imports in the format worker (§11.2). `insertRevision` checks every revision but an import's again before storing it, and a document that fails is a defect, never a stored revision. Tests build their documents from `test/support/docs.ts` for that reason. A note is checked on every path, an import's too: the card importer's note (in `parsedFile`, as the writer will complete it), the writer's own (`insertRevision`), and the folder import's chat notes (`stImportWrites.ts`). A note's depth is at most ST's limit, 10,000 (`MAX_NOTE_DEPTH`): a card's Character's Note deeper than that is placed at the limit, and one that isn't a whole number from 0 at ST's default 4, each with a warning in the report (`noteDepth`).

Building and validating the document happens in the writer, because the drafts it applies are read in that same transaction; it's JSON and schema work, no I/O, as `EditRef`'s hashing already was. A 50 KB description and a 100-prompt preset save through it in the tests.

**Other writes,** each a revision on the head and passed on to followers:
- `RestoreRevision`: an earlier revision on the ref's line (its own entity's, or one a fork inherited: `RefHistory`, §3.9) as a new revision of the ref, `Restored the revision of <time> UTC`, `origin_ref` naming it; the inherited revision's own entry never changes. Restoring an inherited revision keeps the head's value of each top-level field a fork step crossed on the way set differently from the revision it copied (`lineRevision` in `db/editorWrites.ts`: a card fork's `name`, `nickname`, `character_version`; a copied note's `owner` and `condition`). Nothing in between is lost (DATA-MODEL §15, invariant 1). Another schema version is refused. Since live text is what's sent, the ref's fields changed since their last revision take the restored text too, each as a `revision` state of its edit history ending its session on the new revision (`drafts.settleOn`), so the editor shows, and replies use, what was restored, and what was typed before stays one state back. Restoring the head itself makes no revision and only does that.
- `RevertEditorDrafts`: every field changed since the ref's last revision (a chat's note: the revision bound where it's edited, as `OpenEditor` resolves it) back to that revision's value, each by `settleOn` as a `revision` state of its edit history, the text there before one state back; no revision is written, and the held changes aren't touched (the client clears those itself).
- `SetRevisionMessage`: a revision's message, a label and never content (owner, 2026-11-01), added, changed or (empty) removed at any time, automatic revisions' too; only revisions of the ref's own entity: an inherited one is its original's to label (`NotFound` from the fork). The `entity_revisions_immutable` trigger leaves `message` alone and refuses every other column.
- `SetRegexApproval`: below.
- `/library/avatar`: below.
- `ForkVariant` (the writer's `ForkWithDrafts`): a non-card variant following the ref, in one action, optionally moving the ref's unsaved drafts to it, so "make this a variant" works after the edits.
- `ForkCard` and `SetCardParent`: card forks, cards of their own (§3.9). The card editor’s Fork dialog calls `ForkCard` with display name, in-character name, version and the draft choice. `SetCardParent` remains API-only.
- `RenameRef`: the library label and subtitle (DESIGN §4: the in-chat name is the document's `name`, a field like any other). Labels are trimmed, 1 to 200 characters with no control characters.
- `CreateCard`: a card from scratch (`newCardDoc`), an upstream with every field empty but its name.
- Notes: `CreateCardNote` makes a note entity owned by the card (`newCardNote`: at the end of the tail as `system`, off in chats), `ListCardNotes` lists a card's notes by their upstream refs, and `DeleteNote` sends a card's or a chat's note, or a shared one, to the bin. A chat's own notes are made from the chat (§12). A note is edited like any ref. Both creates take an optional `link`, which must be a live shared note of the user's; the slot then takes its title.
- **Shared named notes** (DESIGN §4.1; `db/sharedNotes.ts`): note entities with `owner: { shared: "global" }` (snippets for all chats) or `{ shared: <chat> }` (a chat's snippets) (`newSharedNote`), so they have revisions, drafts, the bin and the editor like any note, with no new kind or table. A slot (a card's or a chat's note) with `link` shows the shared note's library head, in every chat and branch (a chat's snippet too); its own `content` is ignored while linked, and it keeps its own position, role, condition, scan switch and on/off state. `link` is protected from drafts (`PROTECTED` in `editing.ts`): it changes only by `CreateSharedNote { title, content, fromNoteRefId?, chatNote? }` (with `fromNoteRefId`, a new shared note from that slot's saved title and text, and the slot linked to it, in one transaction; a linked slot or a shared note is refused) and `UnlinkNote { noteRefId, chatNote? }` (the shared note's last revision, in the bin or not, as the slot's content, and no link). A chat's note at `chatNote` is written as `CommitEditorDrafts` writes it: a fork-local revision and its `note.binding` (`chatNoteEdit`). `ChatNotePosition` carries an optional `forkId` through editor reads, commits, History (`ListRevisions`, `RestoreRevision`) and shared-note actions; the Notes tab supplies its viewed fork and remounts its editor when that fork changes. **A chat's own note's drafts are its branch's** (DESIGN §4.1, 2026-11-01): their target is `<ref>/<fork>` (`entityDraftTarget` in `@rp/shared/drafts.ts`; `noteHere` returns the fork, its tip and that `scope`). `OpenEditor` returns it as `EditorSnapshot.chatNote.scope`, and the editor store sends it back as every draft call's `scope` (and keeps this browser's copies under that target); `draftTargets.entity_field` refuses a scope that isn't a live fork of the note's own chat, and the `drafts_gc_ref` trigger removes a ref's scoped drafts with it. `CommitEditorDrafts`, `RevertEditorDrafts` and `RestoreRevision` read the branch's drafts; `CheckpointLiveText` the reply's fork's. `EditorSnapshot.chatNote` also says whether another live fork has its own version (`otherBranches`: unsaved text there, or a change bound there that makes it differ, by content, at its tip; a fork that never changed it isn't counted). `chatNoteEdit` binds it at the branch's latest message (owner, 2026-11-02: an edit is at the current state). History of a chat's note (`ListRevisions` with `chatNote`) follows the line bound at the branch's latest message, each revision with `changedAt`: the messages its bindings are at, and whether each applies on the branch shown (`noteChangedAt`). `test/chatNoteBranches.test.ts` covers drafts per branch, `otherBranches`, `changedAt`, and an editor naming an earlier message editing at the latest. `ListChatNotes` passes the same fork to `ChatNoteEntries` and `noteAt`, so two forks sharing a tip resolve separate note revisions even while another fork is current. `ListSharedNotes { query?, refId?, entityId? }` lists the live shared notes, filtered by title (case-folded in JavaScript, since SQLite's `LIKE` folds ASCII only), each with an excerpt and how many slots link to it (a slot counts once: its library head links, or a chat bound a revision of it that does).
- **Snippets** (DESIGN §3.1, §4.1; owner, 2026-11-01; `@rp/shared/snippetsApi.ts`, `db/snippets.ts`, `db/snippetWrites.ts`, `features/snippets/`): the same shared note entities, refs, revisions and bin, with no second text store. A snippet is for **All chats** (`owner.shared` `"global"`) or **This chat**, every branch of it (the chat's id): it's the library head everywhere, not inherited by forks. Its text edits as every library field's does (§14.2a, §14.6): drafts typed live with their edit history, a revision only on Save or when a reply uses changed text (a note linked to it; `usedEntries` reads the shared notes slots show). `ListSnippets { chatId, query? }` lists the chat's and the global ones with their live title and text (an active draft's, else the head's), searched by both; existing shared notes are already snippets. `CreateSnippet { chatId, title, content }` makes one for the chat, or for all chats outside one. `SetSnippetScope { chatId, refId, global }` moves one between the two with a revision ("Now in all chats", "Now only in its chat"); narrowing needs a chat and is refused while a card's note, another chat's note or another chat's binding shows it (`shownOutside`). Writes and reads check ownership (`chatFork`); `test/snippets.test.ts` covers the scopes, live typing without revisions, Save, linked assembly in every branch and the bin.
- The **Snippets panel** is a registered `chatPanels` contribution (a registered app tool's sheet outside chats; a registered chat surface provider gives it the chat shown and opens its tab): a plain explanation at the top (text kept beside your chats, never sent by itself; a note can show one; Copy; Send text to snippet), search and New snippet, Expand all and Collapse all, then each snippet as a block (`ui/Block.tsx`, as notes and prompts): its header always shown, its name (renamed in place) with "This chat" or "All chats" and its first line under it, and **Copy** (one click, the live text to the clipboard); opened, its text (the code-editor box with its edit-history control, `source: "snippet"` so it offers no sending to itself), an **All chats** switch, Save (`SaveRevision`), and the registered `snippets.tools` slot (`features/snippets/slots.ts`): **History** (`snippets.history`, the revisions dialog) and **Delete** (`snippets.delete`: what's typed is saved first and goes with it; asks first only when notes show it, saying how many, then `DeleteNote` and the usual deleted toast). Each block's open state is remembered per user in this browser (`ui/openBlocks.ts`; open by default while there are fewer than 5). `SnippetWorkspace` (`workspace.ts`) outlives the panel: the list for the chat shown, an editor store per snippet, the snippets opened, clicked or typed into, most recent first (`used`), and the snippet editors on screen. Any surface showing a snippet's editor spreads `useSnippetEditorSurface(refId, shown)` (`features/snippets/index.tsx`) on the element around it: while shown it registers the element (`registerEditor`), and a click or focus in it moves it to the front of `used`. `target()` is the first of `used` whose registered element is connected and passes `checkVisibility` (a hidden tab or a closed sheet fails; scrolled away within the panel passes), else the first listed snippet that does; none otherwise. The target's header carries an accent dot ("Text sent to a snippet goes here.") in a room the header always keeps.
- **Text transfers** use the generic `textActions` registry (`textActions.tsx`); plugins can override, disable or add to Send and Open in Snippets. **Editors offer them in their own chrome, never in a context menu** (owner, 2026-11-01): an entry with `editor: "text"` is offered on the editor's whole text, one with `editor: "selection"` on its selection and only while it has one. `EditorTextActions` is the group of them in the strip inside the box (`ui/FieldFrame.tsx`, below) of the shared editors, `CodeEditor` (messages, summaries, card fields, notes, the chat's instruction) and `Textarea` in `ui/Field.tsx`. Only prose editors have it (owner, 2026-11-01: "It's of questionable utility to begin with"): every `CodeEditor` but one in monospace (`textActions={!mono}`: a pattern, a template's markers), and a `Textarea` only with `textActions` (a queued message, the default summarization instruction, a lorebook entry's text and the editor's other non-monospace text fields, recovered text in the bin); JSON settings, lorebook keys, tags, names, regex fields, numbers and URLs have none. Whole-text actions stay rendered, disabled with a reason when unavailable; the frame hides its idle strip by opacity, so neither the text nor anything around the box moves. Focus leaving by a press (the editor's own Save or Cancel) keeps it until the press ends and its click has landed (`useEditorFocus`) (`e2e/textActions.spec.ts`). A selection counts only while focus is in the editor or its bar (`useEditorFocus`): a box left for elsewhere keeps its selection unseen, so its selection's buttons go until it's back. Its buttons keep the editor's focus and selection. An entry with an icon shows only the icon, its label its accessible name and in its explanation with its description (Send text to snippet `snippet`, Send selection to snippet `snippetSelection`); one without shows its label (`shortLabel` on a phone). On a phone the strip is at the box's bottom, away from the OS's selection menu at the selection. An entry's `shortcut` (Ctrl/Command+Shift+key) works only inside an editor that offers that action, judged on the editor's selection at the key press (not on the last render, which fast typing can outrun), and its tooltip names it (`runEditorShortcut`). The selection's entries come first: the strip is end-aligned, so a button that comes and goes with the selection moves nothing else. An entry's `description` can be a function, read each time its tooltip shows. An entry with `choices` (a component of `ui/Menu` items) gets a menu at its button (`ActionButton`): a right-click on the button opens it, as does `run` returning `"choose"`, and its shortcut then opens it at the button (a `rp-text-action-choose` event); the menu keeps the editor counted as focused (`data-menu="text-action"`) and gives focus back to the editor's own element when it closes. The snippets feature registers **Send text to snippet** (`snippets.send-text`) and **Send selection to snippet** (`snippets.send`, Ctrl/Command+Shift+S); a snippet's own editor (`source: "snippet"`) offers neither. **Where it goes** (owner, 2026-11-02): with a `target()` and not on a phone or touch screen (`(max-width: 639.98px), (pointer: coarse)`), one click appends there (`append(refId, text, "target")`): no notice, and the snippet's code-editor box marks the added text for 1.6 s and scrolls to it without taking focus (`CodeEditor`'s `flash`, a CodeMirror mark decoration). Otherwise the menu lists the snippets, those picked from it last first (`recent`, kept per user in this browser), then New snippet; a pick appends (`"chosen"`) or makes one (`appendNew`, without selecting it), leaving the panel as it is, and shows the notice. Its explanation says which: "Adds this text to “<title>”. Right-click to choose a different snippet." or "Choose a snippet to add this text to." Rendered message text has no bar: a double-click opens it for editing, whose bar has both. The composer and the insert-message box (`AutoGrowTextarea`) have no bar. There's no Insert (owner, 2026-11-01: copy and paste does it); a snippet has Copy. Note pickers in a chat include that chat's snippets; linked text and assembly read their head, and another chat's snippet isn't offered. Linked chat notes open the corresponding snippet through an action contribution. Send adds to the end of the snippet (through its editor store, saved at once). **Sending never navigates** (owner, 2026-11-02): the source editor retains focus, its text and its edited marker, with no source revision cut. The existing `ui/Toast.tsx` notice says `Added to snippet “<title or first words>”` and offers **Open**, which selects that particular snippet and opens its panel (or the floating sheet outside a chat). `snippets.open` still opens it directly. Availability checks registration of the Snippets panel, independent of whether a chat is open; sending from the library creates an all-chats snippet without showing its sheet. `e2e/snippetStay.spec.ts` covers unsaved card text through Send, the notice's Open, returning and remounting, and checks source revisions at desktop and phone sizes; the notice is sampled by the layout audit on both surfaces. `test/snippetContributions.test.ts` checks which actions an editor offers; `e2e/snippetPick.spec.ts` covers one click to the target (expand A, B, C, close C and B: A), the marker following a click into another, the selection button not moving the whole text's (bounding boxes), the shortcut, right-click with a target, the menu with Snippets hidden (the panel unchanged), New snippet, and the menu at 390 px, with the layout audit on the strip and the menu at 1440 and 390; `e2e/snippets.spec.ts` sends from a note's and a message's editor by both buttons and the shortcut, and `e2e/textActions.spec.ts` checks the selection button appearing and going with the selection and the editor's focus, in a message's editor and a plain text box, at 1440 and 390 px.
- **A text box's own controls sit inside its border** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1; `ui/FieldFrame.tsx`). `FieldFrame` draws the box's border and focus ring around the control (which loses its own) and a strip inside it along one border: under a multi-line box's text (`side="bottom"`, 28 px, 36 px on a phone) or at a one-line box's end (`side="end"`, 5.5rem). The strip's start holds the box's status (`status`: "edited" while the field has changes, its token count) and its end the controls (`tools`): the text actions, the field's edit history, Open large. **Open large** (owner, 2026-11-02) is on every editable prose `CodeEditor` (`CodeEditorView`; `expand={false}` turns it off, as the large box itself does): card, preset, note and snippet text, summaries, the chat's instruction. A message being edited has none (`expand: false` in `Message.tsx`): it's edited in place in the chat, as wide as the message. It opens a dialog with a second `CodeEditor` bound to the same value, changes, base, tools and status, so it's the same draft with the same history and saving; Done or Escape closes it and focus goes back to the box in place. A `TextField` in a `Textarea` (a lorebook entry's text, the lorebook editor's other prose) has the same button opening `LargeField`, the same draft in a code editor. The strip always takes its room, whether its contents are there or not, so focusing, typing, a change, a new edit history or leaving the box changes neither the box's size nor anything around it, and text never runs under a control. The "edited" marker compares the displayed value with the current saved revision and stays fully visible while they differ. Typing back to that value, selecting it from history, or saving a revision clears the marker; draft persistence and history remain independent of that comparison. The token count and controls show only while the pointer is over the box or focus is in it, at 60% opacity, fully opaque while the pointer or focus is on the strip itself, by opacity alone (`[data-field-frame]` rules in `styles.css`); on a touch screen (`hover: none`) it takes taps only while the box has focus. Its controls follow the box in the focus order, keep their explanations, and are icon buttons (`chromeButton`). A `TextField`'s edit-history control stays disabled in the strip before there is any history (`FieldEditHistory`), with "No edit history yet." as its explanation. The strip carries a layout-audit inset exemption: its compact buttons sit 2 px from the box's own border by design (left and right keep the 8 px padding). `CodeEditor` (`tools`, `status`; a box without text actions or either keeps only the border), `Textarea` (with `textActions`, `tools` or `status`) and `Input` (with `tools` or `status`; `frameClassName` sizes the frame) use it, and the editor's `TextField` (`features/editor/controls.tsx`) fills it for every text field, the large field's dialog too; a setting's label keeps its "edited". Below the box stays only the rare notice of a copy that went over another tab's text (`FieldTools`). Revert beside Save (`ui/SaveControls.tsx`) stays visible and disabled while nothing changed, so the first key typed doesn't move the page under it. `e2e/fieldChrome.spec.ts` measures every element on the page before and after focusing, typing in and leaving a card's description, a one-line field and a lorebook entry's text at 1440 and 390 px (nothing outside the box moves, the box keeps its size), the strip's opacity idle, with the pointer over the box and over the strip, and Tab from the box reaching its edit history; and Open large on a card's description, a note's text, a preset prompt and a lorebook entry's text, typing in the large box and finding the text and the focus back in the box.

- **Dismissible explanations** (snippetsui, owner 2026-11-03). `ui/DismissibleInfo.tsx` shows explanation text in a subtle bordered box with a corner "Hide this explanation" X. Dismissal is account-owned in `DisplayPrefs.dismissedInfo`, a map keyed by box id, merged by id in the existing `SetDisplayPrefs` writer transaction and read through `GetDisplayPrefs` (old rows default to an empty map). The component passes the same text to its caller after dismissal; Snippets (`snippets.intro`) uses it for the standard `Field` help beside Search snippets, absent while the box is shown. The text says "marked with a dot in its corner". Viewer preference writes broadcast invalidation only to other same-origin tabs; mounted consumers also refresh on window focus. Failed writes restore the explanation and show the error. `e2e/snippetsUi.spec.ts` covers reload, a second mounted tab, identical help, passive corner geometry, exact target wording and stable header controls when the target changes.
