The card's `aria-description` and the dot's hover tooltip say exactly: `This snippet is currently the default destination for "Send text to snippet" actions.` Header controls never move with the marker (owner, 2026-11-03). Its intentional border overlap has a badge-only layout audit exception; snippet footer controls and the explanation close button keep at least 8 px from their enclosing border.
- **Text transfers** use the generic `textActions` registry (`textActions.tsx`); plugins can override, disable or add to Send and Open in Snippets. **Editors offer them in their own chrome, never in a context menu** (owner, 2026-11-01): an entry with `editor: "text"` is offered on the editor's whole text, one with `editor: "selection"` on its selection and only while it has one. `EditorTextActions` is the group of them in the strip inside the box (`ui/FieldFrame.tsx`, below) of the shared editors, `CodeEditor` (messages, summaries, card fields, notes, the chat's instruction) and `Textarea` in `ui/Field.tsx`. Only prose editors have it (owner, 2026-11-01: "It's of questionable utility to begin with"): every `CodeEditor` but one in monospace (`textActions={!mono}`: a pattern, a template's markers), and a `Textarea` only with `textActions` (a queued message, the default summarization instruction, a lorebook entry's text and the editor's other non-monospace text fields, recovered text in the bin); JSON settings, lorebook keys, tags, names, regex fields, numbers and URLs have none. It shows only while the editor has focus or a selection, and otherwise isn't rendered; the strip keeps its room either way, so neither the text nor anything around the box moves. Focus leaving by a press (the editor's own Save or Cancel) keeps it until the press ends and its click has landed (`useEditorFocus`) (`e2e/textActions.spec.ts`). A selection counts only while focus is in the editor or its bar (`useEditorFocus`): a box left for elsewhere keeps its selection unseen, so its selection's buttons go until it's back. Its buttons keep the editor's focus and selection. An entry with an icon shows only the icon, its label its accessible name and in its explanation with its description (Send text to snippet `snippet`, Send selection to snippet `snippetSelection`); one without shows its label (`shortLabel` on a phone). On a phone the strip is at the box's bottom, away from the OS's selection menu at the selection. An entry's `shortcut` (Ctrl/Command+Shift+key) works only inside an editor that offers that action, judged on the editor's selection at the key press (not on the last render, which fast typing can outrun), and its tooltip names it (`runEditorShortcut`). The selection's entries come first: the strip is end-aligned, so a button that comes and goes with the selection moves nothing else. An entry's `description` can be a function, read each time its tooltip shows. An entry with `choices` (a component of `ui/Menu` items) gets a menu at its button (`ActionButton`): a right-click on the button opens it, as does `run` returning `"choose"`, and its shortcut then opens it at the button (a `rp-text-action-choose` event); the menu keeps the editor counted as focused (`data-menu="text-action"`) and gives focus back to the editor's own element when it closes. The snippets feature registers **Send text to snippet** (`snippets.send-text`) and **Send selection to snippet** (`snippets.send`, Ctrl/Command+Shift+S); a snippet's own editor (`source: "snippet"`) offers neither. **Where it goes** (owner, 2026-11-02): with a `target()` and not on a phone or touch screen (`(max-width: 639.98px), (pointer: coarse)`), one click appends there (`append(refId, text, "target")`): no notice, and the snippet's code-editor box marks the added text for 1.6 s and scrolls to it without taking focus (`CodeEditor`'s `flash`, a CodeMirror mark decoration). Otherwise the menu lists the snippets, those picked from it last first (`recent`, kept per user in this browser), then New snippet; a pick appends (`"chosen"`) or makes one (`appendNew`, without selecting it), leaving the panel as it is, and shows the notice. Its explanation says which: "Adds this text to “<title>”. Right-click to choose a different snippet." or "Choose a snippet to add this text to." Rendered message text has no bar: a double-click opens it for editing, whose bar has both. The composer and the insert-message box (`AutoGrowTextarea`) have no bar. There's no Insert (owner, 2026-11-01: copy and paste does it); a snippet has Copy. Note pickers in a chat include that chat's snippets; linked text and assembly read their head, and another chat's snippet isn't offered. Linked chat notes open the corresponding snippet through an action contribution. Send adds to the end of the snippet (through its editor store, saved at once). **Sending never navigates** (owner, 2026-11-02): the source editor retains focus, its text and its edited marker, with no source revision cut. The existing `ui/Toast.tsx` notice says `Added to snippet “<title or first words>”` and offers **Open**, which selects that particular snippet and opens its panel (or the floating sheet outside a chat). `snippets.open` still opens it directly. Availability checks registration of the Snippets panel, independent of whether a chat is open; sending from the library creates an all-chats snippet without showing its sheet. `e2e/snippetStay.spec.ts` covers unsaved card text through Send, the notice's Open, returning and remounting, and checks source revisions at desktop and phone sizes; the notice is sampled by the layout audit on both surfaces. `test/snippetContributions.test.ts` checks which actions an editor offers; `e2e/snippetPick.spec.ts` covers one click to the target (expand A, B, C, close C and B: A), the marker following a click into another, the selection button not moving the whole text's (bounding boxes), the shortcut, right-click with a target, the menu with Snippets hidden (the panel unchanged), New snippet, and the menu at 390 px, with the layout audit on the strip and the menu at 1440 and 390; `e2e/snippets.spec.ts` sends from a note's and a message's editor by both buttons and the shortcut, and `e2e/textActions.spec.ts` checks the selection button appearing and going with the selection and the editor's focus, in a message's editor and a plain text box, at 1440 and 390 px.
- **A text box's own controls sit inside its border** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §10.1; `ui/FieldFrame.tsx`). `FieldFrame` draws the box's border and focus ring around the control (which loses its own) and a strip inside it along one border: under a multi-line box's text (`side="bottom"`, 28 px, 36 px on a phone) or at a one-line box's end (`side="end"`, 5.5rem). The strip's start holds the box's status (`status`: "edited" while the field has changes, its token count) and its end the controls (`tools`): the text actions, the field's edit history, Open large. **Open large** (owner, 2026-11-02) is on every editable prose `CodeEditor` (`CodeEditorView`; `expand={false}` turns it off, as the large box itself does): card, preset, note and snippet text, summaries, the chat's instruction. A message being edited has none (`expand: false` in `Message.tsx`): it's edited in place in the chat, as wide as the message. It opens a dialog with a second `CodeEditor` bound to the same value, changes, base, tools and status, so it's the same draft with the same history and saving; Done or Escape closes it and focus goes back to the box in place. A `TextField` in a `Textarea` (a lorebook entry's text, the lorebook editor's other prose) has the same button opening `LargeField`, the same draft in a code editor. The strip always takes its room, whether its contents are there or not, so focusing, typing, a change, a new edit history or leaving the box changes neither the box's size nor anything around it, and text never runs under a control. The "edited" marker compares the displayed value with the current saved revision and stays fully visible while they differ. Typing back to that value, selecting it from history, or saving a revision clears the marker; draft persistence and history remain independent of that comparison. The token count and controls show only while the pointer is over the box or focus is in it, at 60% opacity, fully opaque while the pointer or focus is on the strip itself, by opacity alone (`[data-field-frame]` rules in `styles.css`); on a touch screen (`hover: none`) it takes taps only while the box has focus. Its controls follow the box in the focus order, keep their explanations, and are icon buttons (`chromeButton`). A `TextField`'s edit-history control keeps its room in the strip before there is any history (`FieldEditHistory` `reserve`), so its appearing moves nothing beside it. The strip carries a layout-audit inset exemption: its compact buttons sit 2 px from the box's own border by design (left and right keep the 8 px padding). `CodeEditor` (`tools`, `status`; a box without text actions or either keeps only the border), `Textarea` (with `textActions`, `tools` or `status`) and `Input` (with `tools` or `status`; `frameClassName` sizes the frame) use it, and the editor's `TextField` (`features/editor/controls.tsx`) fills it for every text field, the large field's dialog too; a setting's label keeps its "edited". Below the box stays only the rare notice of a copy that went over another tab's text (`FieldTools`). Revert beside Save (`ui/SaveControls.tsx`) keeps its room while nothing changed (hidden, out of the accessibility tree), so the first key typed doesn't move the page under it. `e2e/fieldChrome.spec.ts` measures every element on the page before and after focusing, typing in and leaving a card's description, a one-line field and a lorebook entry's text at 1440 and 390 px (nothing outside the box moves, the box keeps its size), the strip's opacity idle, with the pointer over the box and over the strip, and Tab from the box reaching its edit history; and Open large on a card's description, a note's text, a preset prompt and a lorebook entry's text, typing in the large box and finding the text and the focus back in the box.

- Updates from what a ref follows (§3.9): `PreviewUpdate`, `ApplyUpdate` (when no help is needed) and `ResolveUpdate`. A resolved document comes from the client, so the writer (`ResolveMerge`) takes it only while an update is pending, checks it against the kind's schema, refuses media and cards that aren't the user's as `NotFound` (`avatar_media_id`, `asset_media_ids`, a note's `owner.card`), takes each protected field from one side or the other (`protectedChanges`), and grants nothing (§14.3).
- **An automatic merge never makes an invalid document** (`planMerge` in `db/library.ts`). Two valid edits can merge into an invalid one: a variant deletes a prompt the upstream then adds to its order. The fields the schema refuses become conflicts, the ref stays as it was with "update available", and the resolver shows them. This costs a schema check of the merged document per merge, in the writer.

**Reads:** `OpenEditor` returns, in one snapshot, the ref, its head document, how many chats use it, every draft of its fields (ended ones too: their row versions are what the next save starts from) and, for non-cards, the entity's upstream and variants (empty for cards). `ListRevisions` and `GetRevision` (of the ref's own entity, and for a fork the revisions of the card it was forked from, which a moved draft may have started from) are the history. `CardFamily` is a card's family tree (§3.9). `EditorDraftHistory`, `RestoreEditorDraft` and `DiscardEditorDraft` are §3.10's operations, for `entity_field` drafts only.

**"Used by N chats"** (DESIGN §4): for cards, the user's live chats with recorded version participation through `card_chat_membership`, including after departure; a temporary cast change or dormant card binding alone does not count. Other entities count chats from `preset.binding` and `lorebook.attach`. One query (`usedByChats` in `db/library.ts`) serves the editor and the Cast tab, and card-replacement previews use the same membership when counting pinned versus following chats.

### 14.2a Live text and checkpoints

**Live text is what's sent** (owner, 2026-11-01; DESIGN §6.2). A reply uses every library field as it's typed, never a saved revision behind it, and a revision is cut only when a reply uses text changed since the last one, or the user saves. It's built as a checkpoint before the reply's assembly, so the assembler itself still reads heads and pins revisions (§15), and a context built again reads exactly what was sent:
1. The client flushes every open editor's pending typing before it asks for a reply (§14.6, `replyHooks`).
2. `ContextGenerator` assembles the reply (`AssembleContext`, in a reader). The reader also returns what the assembly read (`usedEntries` in `assemblyReads.ts`: the preset's ref, the cards, the lorebooks, the notes and the shared notes they show, each with the revision read) and the reply's number in its chat (`message`, the target's display depth + 1).
3. `CheckpointLiveText` (writer, one transaction, `editorWrites.ts`) takes those, and for each entry whose ref has fields changed since its last revision (`status = 'active'` drafts but the held changes, and but a preset's prompts added behind its unsaved bar, definition and text: `heldPromptPaths` of its `HELD_FIELD` draft, §14.6) and whose revision read is that ref's head (one a chat pinned to an earlier revision isn't following the live text), applies the drafts to the head and writes a revision of origin `generation`, with no message and `origin_ref` `{"usedBy":{chatId, forkId, slotId, versionId, message}}`, passed on to followers as any edit; a chat's own note gets a fork-local revision and its binding at the reply's history leaf (`chatNoteEdit`), as its editor's Save does. The drafts' sessions end on it, keeping their text and history (§3.10). Drafts in something gone (a deleted prompt's text) wait for the editor's Save to set them aside; an entry whose drafts wouldn't make a valid document is left as saved (the head is sent) and its Save says why. Nothing changed: nothing is written.
4. If anything was cut, the chat's subscribers hear `State` (open editors read their state again, §14.6) and the reply is assembled again from the new heads; a new revision can bring another entry in (a note's new link), so up to three rounds, each only when something was cut. Then the rollout starts as before.

**A summary request checkpoints the same way** (owner, 2026-11-01): `AssembleSummary` returns what it read and the messages its job covers (`from`, `to`, by number), and `Summarizer` runs the same rounds before its rollout starts, the revision's `usedBy` naming the job's last message as `slotId`, `versionId` null and `summary: {from, to}` (History: "Used by a summary · <chat> · messages 1–4"). The library entries an assembly read are `usedEntries` (`db/usedEntries.ts`), shared by both.

Another reply with nothing changed cuts nothing. Switching presets (or chats) loses nothing: a preset's live text waits, uncommitted, in its drafts, and goes out, with its revision, the next time a reply uses that preset.

**Revision numbers and labels.** A revision's number is its place along the ref's line from 1 (`revisionNumber` in `db/revisionNumbers.ts`): the first-parent line, run on through what a fork was forked from (§3.9 `RefHistory`). `OpenEditor` returns the head's (`EditorSnapshot.revisionNumber`, which History shows; the save cluster doesn't); `ListRevisions` returns each revision's `number`, and for a `generation` revision its `usedBy` (`RevisionUse`: the chat and its title as it is now, the fork, slot and version, and the message number), read by `revisionUse`; a chat that's gone or not the user's reads as a chat without a title.

`test/liveText.test.ts` covers a reply sending card and preset text that was never saved, one labelled and numbered revision per changed entry and none for an unchanged reply, typing on after a checkpoint saving without a conflict, revision messages added and removed, a preset switch keeping the other preset's typing uncommitted until it's used again, the held changes never sent or saved by a reply, an append-only edit-history restore past a Save, and settings never reaching the bin.

### 14.3 What changes never grant

A preset's or card's scripts run only once its `regex_approved` is true (§8, §9), and only `SetRegexApproval` changes it (a protected field for both kinds), with its own revision ("Allowed the regex scripts to run"). The user's own edits in the editor keep it, a script's included. Anything else keeps it only for the scripts it was given for (`keepsRegexApproval`, comparing them as canonical JSON): a merged import or variant change that brings different scripts (`applyMerge`, `ResolveMerge`), and a restored revision, come out not approved. Without that, a re-import of a file with a new script merged into an approved preset arrived approved, since a merge keeps the side that changed the flag. A fast-forward is no exception: a ref without edits of its own would move to exactly the revision it follows, approval included, so where that revision has an approval or permission the ref doesn't, the ref gets a merge revision with it kept off instead (`applyMerge`).

The agent's permission to edit a note (`agent_editable`) works the same way (`withoutGrantedAgentEdits`): the user turns it on in the editor, and a merge, a resolved update or a restored revision keeps it off wherever the head has it off.

**A preset's lorebook ids grant nothing.** `PresetDoc.lorebooks` may name any id; it isn't checked on write, since every read of it is owner-scoped: the assembler reads each through the chat owner's live lorebooks (§15 "Lorebook activation"), and `LorebookPresets` lists only the caller's presets.

**What a note names is the user's own** (`checkReferences` in `libraryWrites.ts`), checked on every write path that takes a note document (`CreateCardNote`, `CreateChatNote`, `CommitEditorDrafts`, `ResolveMerge`): its owner card and each of its condition's cards must be cards of the user's, and its `link` a shared note of the user's (a shared note itself links to nothing); anything else is `NotFound`. The isolation matrix probes each.

### 14.4 Documents

- **Notes** (`@rp/shared/docs/note.ts`, schema version 1; every key below is optional, so older revisions decode) have a placement: in-chat at a depth with a role; at the tail with a role; in a section with an optional role (system when absent), the start of the context, the start or end of the tail, before or after the main prompt, or the card's own (`card`, with its definition); or none, read only by a macro. Nothing is placed relative to another note (owner, 2026-11-01); a lorebook entry has no position at ST's author's note either. An owner: a card, a chat or `{ shared: "global" }` or `{ shared: chatId }` (a global or chat-scoped shared named note/snippet). `condition`: `{ when: "always" }`, `{ when: "turn", cards }` or `{ when: "not_muted", cards }` (one to 100 card ids, each once), absent meaning always. The single-card shape written before (`{ when, card }`, still in stored revisions and drafts) decodes as `cards: [card]` (`SingleCardCondition`), and every save goes through the schema, so it writes the list; the editor reads an undecoded document's with `readNoteCondition`, and `droppedDrafts` takes a draft holding the older shape as kept, not dropped (`OLDER_SHAPES` in `@rp/shared/editing.ts`). No migration: old revisions stay as they are. `scan_lore` (absent off, ST's default), `on_by_default` (a card's note on in every chat with the card unless switched off there), `link` (the shared note a slot shows), `module_id` (the card module or exported note it came from). `interval`, ST's frequency, is still decoded for older imports, never written and ignored (DESIGN §4.1: no insertion frequency). Export writes ST's Character's Note from a depth note, and from a tail note at depth 0, never from the others, which ST's note has no place for. The fields the editor doesn't edit (a chat note's `kind`, `template`, `covers`) stay as they are: a draft changes only its own path, and the schema keeps them.
- **`agent_editable`** on notes (DESIGN §4.1a, proposed) is only stored: nothing reads it until agents exist. Import never reads it and export never writes it, as with `regex_approved`: a file never grants anything (DESIGN §11). Card fields don't have the flag yet.

### 14.5 Avatars and images

- **`POST /library/avatar?ref=<card ref>&rowVersion=<n>[&crop=<cutout>]`** (`importer/routes.ts`): the image as the body, `application/octet-stream`, at most 16 MiB, with the import's limits on slow bodies, its permits and one transfer per user (§11.4). The ref is checked before the body is read. The type comes from the bytes (`importer/images.ts`, the same classifier the importers use, a PNG needing its whole signature): PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, else `415`. The file goes to media storage as an import's do (§11.1), held from the sweep until `SetCardAvatar` records it, and the card gets a revision, "Changed the avatar". A stale row version is `409`. `crop` is the cutout chosen for the new image (§14.5c), as a thumbnail URL names it; without it the image has the default, never the old image's cutout. One that isn't inside the image is `400`, before the body is read.
- **`POST /library/drafts`**: editor drafts a closing page sends with `fetch(…, { keepalive: true })`, JSON, at most 500 and 4 MiB; each saved as `SaveEditorDraft` would, naming the draft it was typed into, the writer deciding a conflict with another tab's save (§3.10). Another user's ref is `404`. A chat's composer goes in `composers`, saved as `SaveComposer` would (§12); a summary's edit in `summaries` (`SummaryDraftSave`), saved as `SaveSummaryDraft` would, and a message editor's text in `messages` (`MessageDraftSave`), saved as `SaveMessageDraft` would, both of which Browser recovery's Retry sends.
- **`GET /library/media?id=<media id>`**: a stored file the user holds a reference to (`GetMediaFile`), only if it's one of those four image types, with `nosniff`. Anything else, another user's file included, is `404`. The same bytes uploaded by two users are one file both reference, so both can read it. Originals and thumbnails now use `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` and a strong ETag; `If-None-Match` (including weak validators and lists) returns an empty `304` after authentication, ownership and file-existence checks. **Privacy change:** the old `private, no-store` was a privacy default. The browser's own disk cache now holds image bytes, including across logout; shared caches still may not store them. Image concealment still applies to cached images. Media bytes are immutable: `recordMedia` inserts by SHA-256 without updating an existing asset, and `SetCardAvatar` records changed bytes as a new media id before revising the card.

### 14.5a Portrait display and images in public

**Top viewer header alignment** (viewertop, approved by the owner 2026-11-04 after the ui/next trial). The registered portrait column passes `alignToChatHeader` only to its first viewer. That toolbar uses the same `h-shell-header` token as the chat header, aligning their bottom borders. Controls stay vertically centred; when the viewer is narrow, its zoom row uses 32 px so both rows fit within the shared height. Lower viewers and full-screen viewers retain their existing compact toolbar. Reordering or closing the top viewer transfers the aligned height to the new first viewer.

`ui/Avatar.tsx` shows the card's cutout (§14.5c): every stock avatar requests a thumbnail of the cutout (`crop` in its URL) at its measured CSS width × `devicePixelRatio`, rounded up to 96, 192, 384 or 768 pixels (`ui/mediaImage.ts`, shared snapping in `@rp/shared/media.ts`). ResizeObserver covers tiles, group collage cells, header faces, composer, message portraits, Cast, card pages and editor previews, including resized panels; window resize also rechecks display density. No guessed initial URL downloads an unnecessary smaller image. Avatar images use `loading="lazy"` and `decoding="async"`. All stock avatars use one rectangular renderer (`ui/Avatar.tsx`), with 2:3 proportions at each fixed size; all cropped portraits share `ui/Portrait.tsx`'s 2:3 frame through `Avatar`, including home tiles, chat rows, individual header cast faces, speaker pickers, cast chips, group faces and reply-from. Chat messages default to ST 1.19's rectangular size: 60 × 90 px, 10 px corners (50 px base, width factor 1.2, height factor 1.8, corner factor 5). The chat panel's Interface tab (also Settings → Interface, the same registered component) offers message portrait sizes 48 × 72, 60 × 90, 72 × 108 and 84 × 126, saved per account through display preferences. The old browser avatar-style choice (`rp.avatarStyle`) is no longer read. Full-image viewing retains the image's natural aspect ratio. Header faces, cast, composer and library tiles keep their own compact sizes. A portrait's initials use the same box when it has no image or images are hidden.

**Avatar initials** (groupinitials, 2026-11-04). The shared `ui/Avatar.tsx` frame is an inline-size query container. Its initials use `40cqi` with unit line height, so text scales with the actual portrait width, including small group-collage cells and resizable chat portraits. Initials take the first letters of up to two words, uppercase them, then cap the result at two Unicode code points (uppercase expansion included); empty names show `?`. The relative font size overrides the size variants’ inherited font sizes. The focused avatar-stack layout audit also visits the group page and seeds two-letter and expanding-uppercase names. Chat-list start dates can wrap within narrow group-page rows instead of overflowing beside their portraits.

**Portrait grid spacing** (groupgrid, 2026-11-02). Fill-sized `ui/Avatar.tsx` portraits use block-level flex boxes, so collage cells do not reserve inline baseline space below the picture. `GroupFaces` keeps its existing single `gap-1` CSS grid gap in both directions, including the centred third member and the four-cell overflow collage. This applies to Groups tiles on home and in the sidebar, the group page and the new group-chat header. Home, sidebar, library and Cast Add characters tile grids retain their single CSS gap. `e2e/portraitGrid.spec.ts` measures rendered neighbouring tile/portrait edges within 1 px at desktop, phone and widened-panel sizes in both themes, with two, three, four and seven-member groups.

The chat header's portrait buttons use `inline-flex` and the avatar's `rounded-sm` corners, with a ring only on keyboard focus. Their bounds match the image, with no inline baseline space or permanent circular ring below it; the loading placeholder has the same 32 × 48 px rectangle. `e2e/portraitFix.spec.ts` checks the header bounds and focus ring, message portraits, Cast and chat-list avatars in light and dark at 1440 and 390 px, and verifies that a card with no chats opens the same original in the same viewer from its pending greeting and saved first message (a side column on desktop, a dialog on a phone). The pending greeting's alternate controls keep the article's bottom inset (no negative footer margin), matching saved messages. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_HEADER_ONLY=1` limits the layout audit's navigation to pending and saved chat pages.

**Cast overflow tiles** (overflowchip, 2026-11-03). The header's +N tile is the same 32 × 48 px, `rounded-sm` rectangle as its adjacent portraits, with no permanent ring; the stack centres its children. The count uses `bg-surface-raised` / `text-muted`, and its hover/focus tooltip names the omitted characters. Group collages on home and in the sidebar use the same muted tokens and portrait corner radius for their full-cell count overlay, retaining 70% background opacity so the fourth portrait stays visible, with hidden names in its title. Chat-list `AvatarStack` uses rectangular portraits (three shown, followed by the shared overflow tile when needed), as do library and Cast rows. The route-loading header placeholder also uses the compact rectangular portrait shape. `e2e/overflowChip.spec.ts` covers the six-character header's count dimensions, corners, centring, containment and tooltip, plus home groups, chat lists, library rows and Cast at 390/1440 in both themes. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_AVATAR_STACKS_ONLY=1` audits those surfaces with a six-character synthetic cast.

**The portrait viewer** (owner, 2026-11-01: the full image beside the chat, as ST's zoomed avatar, not over it). A click on a message's portrait, a Cast row's (any stock avatar with `preview`, `ui/Avatar.tsx`), or any editable card header portrait (§14.5c) shows that card's whole original image (`/library/media` without `w`). `ui/Portrait.tsx`'s `PortraitProvider`, installed as the `chat.portraits` surface provider, holds which portraits are open, per open chat, so they stay open across replies: a stack, top first (`ui/portraitStack.ts`, pure, `test/portraitStack.test.ts`; owner, 2026-11-02, DESIGN §10.1). A click on a portrait that isn't open opens it on top of the others, splitting the column; a click on one that's open closes that one (as ST's). A character's chip in the panel's cast strip only switches the tab; it never opens, switches or closes a viewer image, whether a viewer is open or closed (owner, 2026-11-04). Every editable portrait uses the same `useOpenPortrait` click toggle as message and greeting avatars (owner follow-up, 2026-11-02). `ViewablePortrait` previously called the provider's non-closing `show`, which made repeated header clicks stay open; it now uses the same provider `open` → `portraitStack.toggle` path as `Avatar.preview`. Every page with editable portraits has a viewer: the chat's, the pending chat's (`StartChatPage` installs `ChatPortraitProvider` too), and on the full editor's own page `EnsurePortraitViewer`'s full-screen one (it adds a `PortraitProvider` only where no host gave one). **Only keep one image open at a time** (`DisplayPrefs.singlePortrait`, default off, the account's, written with `SetDisplayPrefs` so it follows the user across tabs and devices) is a checkable item in every side viewer’s ⋯ menu (explained on hover): turning it on closes the others and keeps that one, and from then on a click replaces the image, as before stacking; turning it off returns to stacking. Personas use the same mechanism. There is no Portrait tab. In the workbench the column sits left of the frames, never inside one (§5 "The workbench", "Portrait column").
- **Wide screens (from 1024 px): the portrait column** (`features/chat/PortraitColumn.tsx`, registered as `chat.portrait-column` in the `chat.columns` slot, which the chat page renders left of the messages). It's a column of its own between the chat list and the messages, where ST's zoomed avatar sits in the gap left of its chat, so the messages stay readable, scrollable and sendable beside it and the side panel keeps its place and width on the right; nothing covers the chat and focus stays where it was. Its viewers stack top to bottom, each an `aside` named "<name>'s portrait" (`data-portrait-viewer`) with its own header (name, the zoom toolbar, ⋯ options, **Close the portrait**) and image. A new one takes an equal share of the height (1 / (n + 1); the others give up theirs in proportion); the boundary between two is a `ResizeHandle` with `axis="y"` ("Resize <upper>'s and <lower>'s portraits": pointer, up and down arrows, Home, End, a double-click evening the two, explained on hover as sharing the height between the two images) that changes only those two (`split`, `even`), with a preferred minimum of 180 px when space permits (`MIN_VIEWER_HEIGHT`); additional viewers share the fixed column without scrolling. Its width follows the images: the widest need among them, each image whole at its own box's height (a 2:3 portrait alone at 900 px high is about 560 px wide; a wide one under a tall one sets the width and the tall one shows narrower), a small one enlarged at most twice (`MAX_UPSCALE`), unless the user dragged its edge (`ResizeHandle`, as the other columns: arrows, Home, End; a double-click returns to the image's own width; `rp.panelWidth.<user id>.portrait`). In a short window it gives way first, before the sidebar and the side panel, so the messages keep 440 px (`MIDDLE_MIN`), never narrower than 200 px: at 1440 px with the chat list and the side panel open it's about 260 px. Dragging the sidebar or the side panel wider narrows it, down to its 200 px. A viewer's header (`PortraitView`, `data-portrait-toolbar`; owner, 2026-11-02, DESIGN §10.1) is one aligned row: the card's name, a small logarithmic zoom slider (`ui/Slider.tsx` `ToolbarSlider`, "Zoom", from the fit, or 100% when the fit enlarges, to 800%), the percentage shown beside it (fixed width, tabular numbers; its tooltip: "Shown at N% of its own size, W × H pixels"), then **Fit | 100%** in the shared `ui/Segmented` control ("Zoom presets", `aria-pressed` on the current preset, neither at another zoom), each explained on hover and focus, then ⋯ options ("Keep one image open", a checkable menu item; explanation when off: "Click to keep only one image open at a time.", and when on: "Click to allow multiple images open at a time.") and **Close the portrait**. The slider and percentage are one group with a 4 px gap; groups have 12 px gaps, with 20 px before Close (viewerbar, owner, 2026-11-02). Preset labels keep a constant weight so choosing a preset cannot move controls. `Segmented` retains its `multiple` mode for independent choices, accepts a null single-choice value for no selection, and `inlineDescription={false}` for toolbar explanations that stay on hover/focus and in accessible descriptions without adding another line on phones; other consumers retain the inline description. In a viewer under 22rem the zoom controls take one aligned row of their own under the name and the slider shrinks to fit. Before 2026-11-02 the header showed the scale as a small loose percentage and one button reading **100%** or **Fit** for the other state, which read as two unexplained numbers; Escape closes the top one too, from anywhere on the chat page, after whatever has focus has had the key, and not while typing in a field or while a dialog, menu or list popup is open (`ui/openPopups.ts`: a popup kept mounted while closed, as a Cast row's menu, doesn't count; the chat's command shortcuts and the message editor's Escape use the same check). Panning is clamped so the image's edges never come inside the box's on an axis it overflows, and an axis it doesn't fill stays centred; the cursor is grab, grabbing while dragging, only when the image is larger than the box. ### 14.5b Thumbnail workers and measured image loading

`GET /library/media?id=<media id>&w=<positive pixel width>` rounds up to **96, 192, 384, 768**, capped at 768; invalid widths return `400`. A request's `Thumbnail` runs in a **thumbnail pool of its own** (`THUMBNAIL_WORKERS`, default 1): the same worker code as the format pool (§11.3), one job per worker, with a 30-second execution deadline. It used to share the format pool, so during an ST folder import every thumbnail the grid asked for waited behind the import's files, each parse in turn (the owner, 2026-10-31: "Even THUMBNAILS load SLOWLY"). **Avatars get their thumbnails when they're stored:** a card upload, a new avatar and the ST import (`prepareAvatarThumbnails`, `importer/prepareThumbnails.ts`) run `PrepareThumbnails` on the format pool, the lane that parsed the file, which decodes the image once and writes the widths the grid and lists show at 1× and 2× (96, 192, 384; `PREPARED_WIDTHS`) that aren't on disk yet. 768, a 3× phone's tile, is made on its first request: measured on a 2.4 MB synthetic portrait it took about 450 ms of a card's 600 ms, which tripled the ST import's time per card. So a freshly imported library's grid is served from disk; a failure there only leaves a width to be made on its first request. On-request and ahead-of-time derivatives are the same files. Native sharp 0.35.5 uses one libvips thread per worker and no process image cache; decoding is limited to 40 million pixels. The main thread performs only authentication, owner-scoped reader RPCs and asynchronous disk I/O. A map of pending cached Effects coalesces simultaneous requests for each immutable file/width. Already admitted native work continues if an HTTP caller disconnects, so its replacement waits for the same job.

`importer/thumbnail.ts` auto-orients, keeps aspect ratio, never upscales, and encodes WebP quality 80 into `media/<prefix>/<sha256>.thumb-v1-<width>.webp`, next to the original. A private temporary file is atomically renamed into place; later jobs and server restarts reuse it. The derivative version is part of the path and ETag and must change if encoding rules change. Header-only metadata inspection has no pixel limit; actual decoding retains the 40-million-pixel limit. Images above that bound, or whose resize exceeds sharp's 20-second timeout, serve their original bytes, MIME type and ETag even on sized URLs. A private `.original-v1` marker remembers this fallback across widths and restarts, avoiding repeated doomed work. The media sweep keeps derivatives and fallback markers while their original is recorded, and sweeps unreferenced derivatives and interrupted temporary files. Corrupt or missing files return `404` without taking down the worker.

**Animation policy:** animated GIF/WebP and APNG requests serve the original bytes and original MIME type, preserving animation rather than flattening it. GIF/WebP detection uses page metadata; PNG chunk boundaries are checked for APNG's `acTL`. The `.original-v1` fallback marker avoids repeating metadata work; existing `.animated-v1` markers are also honored. Animation therefore retains its original download cost.

**Native deployment:** sharp stays external to the formats bundle. Its pinned npm optional dependencies include linux-x64 glibc and darwin-arm64 sharp/libvips packages in the lockfile. Docker's production `npm ci --omit=dev` and final `node_modules` copy include the native binaries; building needs only npm packages, with no system libvips or separate download. The production image was built and an offline container generated a 192×96 WebP through the actual bundled format worker. Tests that put bundles outside the repository link their external sharp dependency into the temporary bundle directory.

**Measurement (2026-10-15):** Chromium/Playwright, 1440×900 and 390×844 at DPR 1, built client, real HTTP server and worker storage on port 5995. `test/support/stLargeImages.ts` adds 150 deterministic uncompressed RGB PNG cards (100 at about 3 MiB, 50 at about 6 MiB) to `writeRealisticStFolder`'s 12 cards, 3 personas and long group chats. Pixels are generated; no private or downloaded images are used. There are 151 distinct original image files after deduplication. Browser caches start empty for each cold run; the first post-change desktop run also has no disk thumbnails. Warm means a literal `page.reload` in the same browser context, with the scroll position reset before timing. The measurement scrolls every viewport and waits until every image has loaded, so totals include the entire library, not just images near the fold. Scroll pacing (100 ms per step, 13 desktop / 33 phone steps), UI loading, waits and the final 200 ms settle are included in elapsed time. CDP `encodedDataLength` counts transferred image bytes including HTTP headers; zero-byte disk/memory cache reads are excluded from network request counts.

| Viewport / run | Before image bytes | After image bytes | Before / after network requests | Before / after all-images time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1440×900 cold, unthrottled | 629,525,221 | 659,538 | 151 / 153 | 4.273 s / 5.546 s |
| 1440×900 warm, unthrottled | 629,525,221 | 0 | 151 / 0 | 3.642 s / 2.662 s |
| 390×844 cold, unthrottled | 629,525,221 | 657,535 | 151 / 152 | 5.322 s / 4.944 s |
| 390×844 warm, unthrottled | 629,525,221 | 0 | 151 / 0 | 5.558 s / 4.839 s |

The first visible viewport finished in 1.372 / 1.243 s before/after on desktop, and 1.166 / 0.905 s on phone. At that point the browser had initiated 46 / 48 desktop image requests and 12 / 13 phone image requests; only nearby tiles were requested. The extra cold derivative requests are shared originals at different rendered sizes (including the desktop sidebar), not duplicate generation. Entire-library cold bytes fall about **99.9%**. Unthrottled loopback can transfer hundreds of MB very quickly, so cold native generation is slower than that baseline on desktop; a literal warm reload transfers no image bytes. Browser image events still exist on warm reload (153 desktop / 152 phone) but cause no HTTP image transfers.

The Fast 4G-like CDP run uses 150 ms latency, 9 Mibit/s download and 1.5 Mibit/s upload. Browser caches are empty for cold loads; existing disk thumbnails are reused. Literal warm reloads stay in the same context. This includes throttled application JavaScript and the same library traversal, not only image transfer.

| Viewport / run | Image bytes | HTTP image requests | All images loaded | First visible viewport |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1440×900 cold | 659,538 | 153 | 6.550 s | 2.490 s |
| 1440×900 warm | 0 | 0 | 3.143 s | 1.306 s |
| 390×844 cold | 657,535 | 152 | 7.091 s | 2.480 s |
| 390×844 warm | 0 | 0 | 5.303 s | 1.254 s |

An additional original-build throttled whole-library traversal was stopped after more than 12 minutes without completing; it is not used as a completed timing or byte measurement, and its cause was not diagnosed. The completed unthrottled before/after runs and completed changed-build throttled runs are the reported comparisons.

Server tests cover snapping, WebP, ratio, no upscale, originals, ETags/304, ownership/authentication, corrupt pixels, animated GIF/WebP/APNG, concurrent cold requests and disk reuse (`test/thumbnails.test.ts`), alongside media sweep and format worker tests. `e2e/images.spec.ts` imports the large fixture and checks lazy thumbnail requests and rendered-width × DPR 2 at both sizes, then opens the original 1024×2048 portrait in the portrait viewer. Existing portrait and privacy/layout browser tests also pass with the thumbnail preview.

### 14.5c Portrait cutouts

**Picture and Portrait cuts (picturecrop, owner 2026-11-02).** The registered Picture dialog starts on **Picture**, with **Free / 2:3 / 1:1** presets, the shared box/handles, keyboard controls and size slider, and Large view / Export previews. **Portrait** uses the same editor constrained to the Picture rectangle, with Message / Cast / Tile previews. Replacing an image starts on Picture again. **Reset to the original** restores the whole original and the default portrait. Personas use the same card path.

Both cuts are settings bound to the unchanged original: optional `avatar_crop.picture` is a free rectangle, while `avatar_crop`'s existing coordinates describe the 2:3 portrait in original-image fractions. Missing `picture` means the whole image. Both save together through the existing `SetCardAvatar` / `SetCardAvatarCrop` writer transactions and protected document field, and flow through existing summary projections; no migration or baseline change. The shared schema verifies portrait containment. Changing the Picture bounds retains an enclosed portrait or resets to its default inside the new bounds.

The large portrait column and full-screen viewer carry the Picture rectangle from the existing avatar read model. `/library/media?picture=<rectangle>` renders a cached PNG on the format worker; originals remain available to the editor. PNG export renders and re-encodes the cut with sharp in the registered exporter on a format worker, embeds the card data and rebases exported portrait coordinates to the rendered image, avoiding a second Picture cut on import. ST imports retain their existing behavior. CHARX retains the original and settings. Tests: `portraitCutout.spec.ts`, `avatarCrop.test.ts`, existing portrait surface specs, and `LAYOUT_AUDIT_PICTURECROP_ONLY=1` for both tabs at 390/1024/1440 in both themes.

The earlier full-original viewer/export descriptions below are superseded by Picture cuts above.


The owner, 2026-11-01: "ST lets you select the cutout for the avatar. We should do the same, but keep the entire image." ST's crop popup (Cropper at 2:3, then `/api/characters/edit-avatar` resizing to 512 × 768) bakes the crop into the file and discards the rest. Here the original is stored whole and never altered; the **cutout** is a 2:3 rectangle stored beside it, and every small portrait is a thumbnail of that rectangle.

- **Where it lives: the card document's `avatar_crop`** (`@rp/shared/docs/card.ts`, `StoredCrop` in `@rp/shared/media.ts`): `{ media_id, x, y, width, height }`, the rectangle as fractions of the original's width and height (stored on a grid of 1/10000, `snapCrop`), with the media id of the image it was chosen on. Personas are cards, so they have it too. Because it's a field of the document, each revision, a chat's own version of a card (`ForkCardForChat` copies the document) and a variant carries the cutout of its own image. **It applies only to the image it names** (`avatarCropOf`): a merge that took one side's image and the other side's cutout, or any other path that changes the image without it, shows the default rather than a cutout chosen for another picture. Absent, or for another image: the default. **No migration**: documents are JSON and the field is optional, so existing cards read as the default and the database is kept as it is.
- **The default** (`defaultCrop`): the full width, from the top, of an image taller than 2:3 (where a portrait's face is); the full height, centred, of a wider or square one; all of a 2:3 image. It's computed, never stored: the thumbnail worker works it out from the decoded (auto-oriented) image, and the chooser from the loaded one. Imported cards and personas, ST's included, and every card made before cutouts existed have it.
- **Protected, with actions of its own** (§14.1): no draft changes it. `SetCardAvatar` (the avatar upload, above) takes the cutout chosen for the new image, or none; `SetCardAvatarCrop` (`EditorApi`, writer `db/editorWrites.ts`; refused on a card without an avatar, `StaleWrite` on a stale row version, `NotFound` for another user's ref) chooses again for the image the card has, or with `null` goes back to the default. Each is one writer transaction and a revision of its own ("Changed the avatar's cutout", "Reset the avatar's cutout"), flowing to followers as any edit.
- **The read models carry it**: `CastCard`, `CardUsage` and `ChatGroup` members have `avatarCrop` beside `avatarMediaId`, present only when one was chosen (`avatarCropField`), from `db/cards.ts`, `db/chatSetupReads.ts` and `db/shellReads.ts` (the SQL reads extract `$.avatar_crop` with the avatar).
- **Thumbnails of the cutout** (§14.5b): `GET /library/media?id=…&w=…&crop=<auto | x_y_w_h>` (`cropKey`: `auto` for the default, else the four values in 1/10000) makes the cutout's derivative, `media/<prefix>/<sha256>.thumb-v1-<width>-c<key>.webp`. The cutout is in the path and so in the ETag, like the width, so a changed cutout is another URL and another file and a browser never shows a stale one. The worker cuts exactly 2:3 pixels (`cropPixels`: trimmed about the rectangle's centre and kept inside the image, whatever the stored values), then resizes to the snapped width, never enlarging past the cutout's own pixels (a 300 px wide cutout asked for at 768 is 300 × 450). It runs in the thumbnail pool, coalesced per path, width and cutout. An image served whole (animated, or over the pixel limit, §14.5b) is served whole for a cutout too. `crop` without `w`, or naming a rectangle outside the image, is `400`. Without `crop` the URL is the whole image's thumbnail, as before (the portrait viewer's stand-in while the original loads, message images). Upload and import prepare the cutout's 96, 192 and 384 widths (`prepareAvatarThumbnails` with the cutout: the chosen one on upload, the default on import), since those are what the lists and grid ask for. The media sweep keeps a cutout's derivatives while their original is recorded.
- **ST round trip** (`importer/exporters.ts` `withCrop`, `importer/importers.ts` `exportedCrop`): a PNG or CHARX export holds the full original and the cutout in our namespace, `extensions.rp_harness.avatar_crop` (the four fractions and the image's `image_width` and `image_height`), which ST ignores and keeps. Our import moves it onto the card when the file's image has the same size, and the writer (`ImportFile`, `db/libraryWrites.ts`) binds it to the stored file; an image of another size (ST cropped it since) gets the default. A JSON export has no image, so no cutout. A new version of a card from a file without an image keeps the card's avatar and its cutout; one with an image takes that file's cutout or the default. An ST card has no such field: the default.
- **Choosing it** (`ui/CutoutChooser.tsx`, the registered Picture dialog; picturedialog, 2026-11-02): the whole image fitted in the dialog, the rest dimmed around a 2:3 box. A mouse or one finger drags the box; its four corners resize it about the opposite corner, staying 2:3 inside the image, at least a twentieth of the largest box (or 8 source pixels). The focusable box retains arrow-key movement (Shift: ten times as far) and +/− resizing. One centred control row under the image has **Cutout size** (`ui/Slider.tsx` `ToolbarSlider`, shared with the image viewer), a reset icon (“Reset the cutout”) and `AboutHint`’s small ?. The slider linearly sets the source-pixel box width between its minimum and the largest fitting box, resizing about its centre with edge clamping; corner and keyboard resizing update it. Reset restores the image’s default box. Gesture/key help is in the ? hover/focus/tap, with no standing title explanation or caption. **Previews** contains only the live **Message**, **Cast** and **Tile** cutouts: message and chip sizes come from `Avatar.tsx`’s shared `AVATAR_SIZES` (message uses the account’s `chat-portrait` size; chip 18.667 × 28 px), tile uses the responsive library/home grid’s 134 × 201 px image area inside the minimum 136 px bordered tile. Previews stack in a right column on desktop and form one row below the image at 390 px; the phone’s image is capped at 36dvh (desktop 60dvh). **Replace picture…** is left, secondary like **Cancel**, with Cancel and **Save cutout** (or **Save picture** for a new image) grouped right; the footer wraps when needed while keeping that pair together. During saving the spinner visually replaces the label in its reserved space, retaining the accessible name and keeping the button and dialog bounds fixed. The shared dialog retains its corner X, outside-click dismissal and Escape; cancellation changes nothing. Images blurred or hidden (§14.5a) stay so in every preview; while hidden a line explains the image setting. Every control has hover/focus help.
- **Where a picture is set** (`features/editor/PortraitControls.tsx`; owner, 2026-11-02, DESIGN §4: one set of picture controls). Every editable portrait (a character's and the persona's tab, `TabPortrait`; the full editor's header, `StorePortrait`; Metadata's **Picture**, `EditorPortrait`) is the same: a click on the portrait opens its whole image (`ViewablePortrait`, "View <name>'s picture", explained "View the whole picture"; a plain portrait while there's no image), and exactly one overlay button, **Picture** (an image icon, `PictureButton`, `data-picture-button`), over its lower-right corner, opaque on a touch screen. It opens the Picture dialog: the cutout chooser on the card's original, titled "<name>'s picture", with **Replace picture…** (`CutoutChooserProps.onReplace`, its own file input) beside Cancel and **Save cutout**; a new image chosen there, or dropped on the portrait, reopens it as "<name>'s new picture" with **Save picture**. With no picture the button picks a file straight away (Metadata keeps its dashed **Add a picture** box instead). Before this, the enlarge button showed only where a `PortraitProvider` was mounted (inside an open chat, not a pending chat or the full editor's own page) and only on the tab and header portraits, not Metadata's; and a click replaced the picture, with a camera in a dark circle centred over a hovered portrait (the "black dot"). The Picture dialog uses `ui/Dialog`’s shared corner X and closes on an outside click; focus starts on the image stage so a tooltip does not cover the footer on a phone. Below, the older detail of the two paths: picking or dropping a new image opens the chooser before anything is saved (a picked file is shown from an object URL, revoked when the chooser closes), and its Save uploads the image with the cutout (`POST /library/avatar?crop=`); **Adjust cutout** opens it on the card's original (`/library/media` without `w`) at the cutout it has, and saves through `SetCardAvatarCrop`. Both invalidate `library`, so the cast, lists and grids read the new cutout. A card that's in the bin or still loading shows the plain portrait, which opens the viewer. Message portraits, Cast rows and the cast strip keep opening the viewer. After a change from the tab the chat reads its cast again (`ChatSession.rereadCast`), so its portraits follow at once; a change made in the full editor (over the chat or on its own page) reaches an open chat's cast when that's next read (a reload, another branch, a change of cast), as other card edits do.
- **Every small portrait shows it**: messages, the cast and cast strip, the header's faces, the chat list, the left panel and home grid, library rows and tiles, group collages, speaker pickers and the composer's recent speakers all pass the read model's `avatarCrop` to `Avatar`. The full-image views (the portrait column and phone viewer) show the original. A portrait the server serves whole (animated or very large) is placed by `object-position` at the cutout's centre, an approximation.

A plugin replaces or wraps either by registering the same id, and undoes it with the returned function; with the chooser disabled, a new picture is saved with the default cutout and Adjust cutout isn't offered.

### 14.5d Card galleries and embedded image assets (gallery, 2026-11-03)

The registered `card.gallery` contribution to `cardEditorSections` (`features/gallery/`) appears in Extra on the side panel and full editor. It groups stored CCv3 assets by kind: `icon` and `user_icon` under Portraits, `emotion` under Expressions, `background` under Backgrounds, and every other kind under Other. The main icon keeps its separate portrait control. Asset names remain as imported. Thumbnails toggle the same viewer as portraits, with a title `<card display name> · <image name>` (an unnamed image uses `N of M`). The section header's Add images (+) chooses multiple files; dropping files on the section adds them too. Added boxes use `revealAdded`. Thumbnails use the shared `ContentImage` frame, including the browser’s concealment mode and hidden-image placeholder. Thumbnail menus rename, change Kind, remove, or (alternative icons) Use as portrait. No expression or background activation behavior is implemented.

Storage reuses `CardDoc.assets` (ordered membership, CCv3 type/name/ext/URI) and `asset_media_ids` (content-addressed media IDs keyed by URI); no second image store. `POST /library/gallery` shares the avatar upload's authenticated, bounded binary pipeline, content sniffing, upload permits and media holds, then calls `AddCardAsset`. The writer records the media and appends an Other asset under a unique embedded URI in one new revision. `ChangeCardAsset` checks ownership and the expected ref row version before renaming, changing kind, swapping the portrait, or removing membership. A swap replaces the main icon with the chosen image, retains the old main as an alternative with the chosen alternative's name and position, and clears the old portrait's cutout. Each operation creates a normal user revision. The character panel observes changes to the saved avatar and rereads its cast, so choosing an alternative portrait updates the visible header immediately. Main is reserved for the current icon; asset lists and mappings are protected from field drafts.

Removal creates a `card_asset` bin item whose origin keeps the owning entity/ref, asset descriptor, media ID and array index. The bin's registered asset restorer writes a new revision of the current card, inserting the image at its saved position while preserving other edits. Ownership is checked again on restore. Purging the card clears its gallery bin items too. Purging a gallery bin entry removes its restore record; earlier immutable card revisions retain their images, as they do after other picture changes.

`GalleryApi` has a separate authenticated handler layer to bound TypeScript's RPC inference. `GetCardGallery` reads only the card name and gallery image descriptors in a reader worker. Chat viewer IDs encode the ref and asset URI; the provider resolves them through that read after reload and library/cast refreshes. The same provider handles open/close, stack order, height shares and single-image preference for portraits and gallery images.

Fresh ST folder imports classify `user/images/<folder>/<image>` and process them after cards, through the registered gallery folder handler. ST's public `getGalleryFolder` uses `extension_settings.gallery.folders[avatar]` or the card display name, and its server sanitizes that folder with `sanitize-filename`; the import mirrors both. Only cards created by this import receive folder images; existing cards and unmatched folders are skipped. Synthetic import coverage includes an avatar filename differing from the display name, a sanitized folder override, a mismatched folder and a repeat import. Embedded CHARX assets continue through the existing asset import/export pipeline, retaining all supported image kinds, names, bytes and order. PNG/JSON export behavior is unchanged.

`test/gallery.test.ts` covers the real upload/RPC/worker paths, CHARX export/import, kind/name preservation, stale writes, portrait swaps, removal/restore, and fresh-only ST galleries. Isolation probes cover both gallery RPCs, the add worker operation and upload route. `e2e/gallery.spec.ts` covers the shared Extra grid at 1440/390, viewer toggling and saved order, pointer/keyboard/menu stack moves and the ⋯ keep-one preference. The layout audit populates the card gallery before auditing Extra in both editor surfaces.

### 14.6 The editors in the client

**Prompt rendering work (perfred1).** The editor retains equal plain-object and array nodes in its displayed working snapshot, preserving key order, property descriptors and serialized values. Outgoing draft/commit documents still use the freshly applied working document. Changing one order entry therefore preserves the other entries and prompt definitions (`editorSnapshot.test.ts`). Prompt controls dispatch through committed callback refs so a reorder uses the latest index without changing every unrelated control. The prompt block resolves optional defaults inside its body: parameter default patterns made React Compiler skip the entire block, recreating hundreds of controls per toggle. `presetRender.spec.ts` checks unchanged control renders and callback identities in the production build at 1440/390 in both themes. The merge with own-turn notes retains its optional insert action in the same committed callback wrapper, including its availability when the marker is added or removed (`ownTurnNotes.spec.ts`).

**Lorebook prompt editors** (lorebookmacros, 2026-11-07; DESIGN §5.6). Standalone lorebook entry content now uses the same `CardTextEditor` binding as card-owned entries, presets and notes, in both the library and chat panel. It reuses the registered macro-highlighting extension and the revision-base change gutter, retaining server drafts, native undo, field history and field-only revert. Snippets already use this binding through their note stores, in the panel and large editor. `e2e/lorebookMacros.spec.ts` checks parser colours, unknown macros, change marks, Save and draft reload at 1440/390 in light/dark, with scoped layout audits.

**Merging into forks** (forkmergeui, 2026-11-05; `features/forkMerge/`, DESIGN §4). A registered feature over the §3.9 RPCs; the old `UpdateDialog` (PreviewUpdate/ApplyUpdate/ResolveUpdate) is gone from the client, those RPCs stay for compatibility. Three editor slots in `editor/editorSlots.ts` carry it, so a plugin can replace or drop each part: `editorNotices` (rendered by `EditorPage` where the update alert was, and by `PresetTab`, `CharacterTab` and the library `LorebookPanelEditor` under their tools), `editorActions` (beside History/Fork in the full editor; the side panels use `panelEditorActions`) and `revisionActions` (beside each revision's Restore in `CardRevisionBrowser`).
- `MergeNotice` reads `ForkMergeStatus` through the client's query family (one read per ref, shared with History's Undo), again on window focus and when the editor's head moves; a failure shows with Retry; a hand-marked card parent (parent, no base) explains instead of offering the review.
- `MergeDialog` (lazy): the editor's store (given, `openEditorStore`, or one of its own), then the status and the parent's name/link from `LibraryGenealogy`. While the store has unsaved fields it shows the editor's own `SaveRevision` controls and asks no preview; the server refuses drafts from another tab too, shown with Retry. Each `PreviewForkMerge` answer names the comparison it answers (revision, attempt, head), so a stale answer is never shown. `MergeReview` lists units with `theirsChanged` (conflicts first; local-only units are counted, not listed), a `Switch` per unit for `selection.excluded`, the parent's change through History's `FieldComparison`/`ValueDiff`/`ReadableDiff` (orders as numbered names, `elementNames`), and the shared `ConflictPicker` (now with no initial pick, a `show` reading and a pick-only mode for orders) per included conflict. A conflict is included unless an excluded unit path is its prefix, as on the server. The result is `libraryMergePolicies.get("library.merge") ?? defaultLibraryMergePolicy` `.resolve(...)` then `validateDoc`, shown as `changedFields(ours, result)`; Merge is disabled with the reason until every included conflict is picked and the result validates. Picks (`excluded` unit keys and per-conflict `Choice`s, JSON) are a user draft `merge:<ref>:<base>:<ours>:<theirs>` / "Merge choices" (`useUserDraft`), committed around `CommitForkMerge` so the draft ends only after a successful merge; a `StaleWrite`/`EditRefused` keeps them and Compare again seeds the next comparison's draft with them. Success refreshes the store and open editors.
- `UndoMerge` shows only on `merge` revisions with a `library_merges` record; enabled at the head with no unsaved fields and not yet undone, else disabled with why. The server’s merge guard ignores only the empty preset structural draft retained after Save/Revert; empty ordinary text drafts still refuse. Both review and Undo include held preset additions, deletions, reorders and lorebook attachments in their unsaved check. The review waits for its private choices draft before showing editable picks or enabling Merge; Compare again saves carried picks into the new comparison’s draft even without further typing. A refused choices-draft save keeps the review open and never announces a successful merge (review-forkmergeui, 2026-11-05).
- `GenealogyDialog`/`FamilyButton` (presets and lorebooks): the `LibraryGenealogy` tree by node and parent node ids from its root, each live/archived non-override member a router `Link` (in a chat panel `PanelVariantNavigation` opens it in place; modified clicks keep their new-tab behaviour), state badges, fork and last-merge dates, "Marked as a fork by hand" without a fork revision, foldable members.
- "Make a variant" keeps its label; its explanations say later changes can be merged instead of promising automatic updates.
- `e2e/forkMerge.spec.ts` (synthetic presets, lorebooks, cards): preset fork review/conflict/merge/undo at 1440 and 390, light and dark; drafts refusal and an older parent revision; a stale comparison keeping an edited pick; lorebook fork from the chat panel with exclusion and the family tree; card file Merge vs the card's own edit; a card fork's notice in the character tab and a hand-marked fork. `FORK_MERGE_ARTIFACTS=<dir>` saves the surfaces; `LAYOUT_AUDIT=1` audits each. Review regressions also cover reload after Compare again, a delayed choices-draft read preserving excluded entries, refused draft saves, and held preset changes in the review and Undo.

**Document selection (centerheader, 2026-11-04).** Full preset, lorebook (including a card's embedded lorebook), card, persona, note and snippet editors contribute their title, rename pencil, kind badge and save/close controls to the shared center header. The card identity/version/save row moves there; its portrait, nickname, provenance and token rows remain in the body. `DocumentSwitcher` opens the kind's complete picker (switchers, 2026-11-06; below, **Header switchers**). Snippets use their workspace's choices, and expanded chat notes use the chat's notes. Selection navigates to another library ref or changes the overlay's `editor` search parameter, retaining note/snippet focus where appropriate. Existing `useLeaveGuard` cleanup flushes outgoing drafts; switching does not cut a revision or change the existing draft/recovery policy. Chat retains its branch switcher. The editor routes and registered workspace views retain replacement ownership.

**Card header readability (cardheader1, 2026-11-16).** The full card editor caps the version at the remaining 40% of the identity text area beside the name's existing 60% cap, releasing that limit while renaming. An empty version's add prompt or a long version could previously shrink the name switcher's text to zero on a phone, leaving only its chevron and pencil. The shared identity row keeps its existing controls. `e2e/cardHeader.spec.ts` checks the actual name-text width against its font's first two characters plus an ellipsis, with no version, a short version and a long version, at 1440 and 390 in both themes. The focused card-header layout audit includes the portalled center identity as well as the portrait rows and side-panel widths.

Browser expectations use the standard name/version pair in character tabs, header portrait actions and Next choices, and retain version subtitles in Cast rows. The width screenshot sweep opens the owner-named History edits tab and bounds individual actions separately from its whole-sweep budget. The scale import fixture uses link tiles and filters older cards into the mounted grid. Composition setup waits for a distinct, completed provider version before adding swipes; duplicate-view text comparisons read rendered text on both sides, including tables.

**Header switchers (switchers, 2026-11-06; DESIGN §10, owner decision).** The header's trigger (`HeaderSwitcher`, `pickers/DocumentPickers.tsx`) shows the document's name with a chevron, stays pressed while its popover is open and explains "Switches to another <kind> in this editor."; the popover is the pickers' `PickerPopover` below the header. Presets open the registered `preset.picker` body, the side panel's own picker, through `useEditedPresetSelection` (`usage: "edit"`): the same lists, Name/Modified/Used/Archived views, edit and use lines, archive/unarchive with Undo and **New preset…**, with Default (built-in) left out because it can't be edited. Choosing opens that preset in the editor and doesn't change the preset the next reply uses; a new preset opens in the editor. Cards and personas open `card.picker` (`CardPicker`): the card lists' filter with counts, sort with direction and Include personas (`CardBrowseBar`; the sort, its direction and Include personas are the account's `cardSwitcher` display choice), filtered by name or version, each row with the card's portrait (`Avatar` `md`, as the speaker switcher's rows), the version and the sort's date or chat count under each name, a Persona badge where personas are mixed in. Its rows are the card lists' own (`GetShellCards` through `browseCards`), so whatever those lists leave out it leaves out too. It opens on Personas when the edited card is one, and ends with **New persona…** under Personas or **New card…** under the other filters, using the shared `NewCardDialog` and opening the created card in the editor. Lorebooks (with a card's own book offered under its name), notes and snippets open `document.picker` (`DocumentPicker`): a filter, **Name** or **Modified** (the account's `lorebookSort`, `noteSort` and `snippetSort` display choices, stored in `settings` as `presetSort` is) and "edited 3 days ago" under each name; a list without edit times sorts by name only. A host can end the list with a New row (`create`): the large snippet's **New snippet** (the workspace's `create`) and the large chat note's **New note** (the Notes tab's add, for this chat, on from the latest message) each open what they made in the editor; lorebooks and library notes end with **New lorebook…** and **New note…**, using `NewDocumentDialog` (§14). Archive stays the presets' alone. Choosing navigates as before. `e2e/switchers.spec.ts` seeds 300 presets, 300 lorebooks and 2,000 cards and, at 1440 and 390 in light and dark, opens each kind's switcher (preset, lorebook, card, persona, note, snippet) with bounded rows and its filter focused, filters to one row, chooses it with Down and Enter, and chooses another with the mouse; it also walks a long list by arrow keys past the first rows mounted, archives and unarchives from the header, and checks that the chat's Prompt preset tab opens the same views. With `LAYOUT_AUDIT=1` it audits each open picker and its header.

Snippet History reads its button label and dialog title from the live editor title, including a rename before saving a revision. Note History also uses the live title; card, persona, lorebook and preset revision dialogs use the fixed title “History”.

**Responsive prompt rows** (promptrows, 2026-11-04): below a 36rem list container, `PromptDocument` headers use a grid that keeps the handle and switch beside a wrapping title and puts secondary items on a following line. Placeholder descriptions and prompt previews use the full content width; descriptions wrap only between words. The same rule covers built-in, custom, marker and definitions rows in the panel and large editor; wide layouts retain their existing flex arrangement. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_PROMPTROWS_ONLY=1` audits both lists, including the panel minimum, and captures list crops.

Side-panel History access (cardhistory, 2026-11-04): card and persona panels, compact lorebooks (including a card's embedded book), and the Prompt preset panel render `editor.panel.actions` beside Search and replace. The registered `editor.panel.history` action opens the existing `RevisionsDialog` with the same editor store and caller, preserving unsaved edits and the revision restore flow. Notes retain History in their action menu; snippets retain their registered History control. The buttons open the shared redesigned dialog described below.

**Revision history layout (historyui, 2026-11-04).** `RevisionsDialog` and `CardRevisionBrowser` remain the shared history for cards, notes (including chat and card notes), lorebooks, presets and snippets, reached through the registered editor/snippet features. `ui/RevisionEntry` gives each revision a bordered entry with number/latest and a separate timestamp, origin badges and branch context, a message-row pencil plus labeled Restore to revision N and Compare actions in that order, and an optional message below the name/badges, above the action row (owner follow-up, 2026-11-04). The dialog opts into the shared Dialog’s top placement and inset-scroll mode: a container-sized content frame keeps 20 px padding on all four sides (21 px measured from the outside border), with the stable scrollbar gutter inside the right padding, keeping action positions fixed during expansion. A selected entry opens its comparison underneath, with no close X (superseding its former placement beside the tabs; owner follow-up, 2026-11-04), equal 8 px gaps above the tabs row and below it before the first field, a diff view with shared tabs “Changes from previous revision” and “Changes from current state” and expandable field changes, and an accent border. The no-difference state shares the field accordion’s 1 px border, 8 px padding, 16 px disclosure slot and 4 px gap, aligning its text at 29 px from the panel’s left edge; field disclosure icons have an explicit size. Compare toggles the comparison, retaining its pressed state while open and an explanation of what clicking does. Restore is before Compare in every entry and reads “Restore to revision N” (owner follow-up, 2026-11-04); the latest entry keeps a disabled action with an explanation. Restoration loads the revision on demand, rechecks card-name conflicts before writing, retains chat-note context and row-version checks, refreshes the editor on success and reports failures. User/Saved has no origin label; Imported, Updated (merge), Agent edit and Changed (changeset) are header badges. Generation usage keeps its reply/summary link as a line; changed-at-message branch context remains below the header. `ui/RevisionMessage` puts the icon-only Edit pencil after the message text with the shared title-pencil 2 px gap, or shows the original ghost-style pencil-and-text Add message button when empty and reuses `InlineRename` for the inline input, Enter/Escape, confirm/cancel and the 500-character limit (owner follow-up, 2026-11-04). The shared inline editor caps the input wrapper at the same control width as the input, so confirm/cancel follow it with 4 px gaps instead of drifting to the row’s far edge (owner correction, 2026-11-04). Empty, short, truncated, expanded and editing states keep the message control row at 32 px. Overflow is a single truncated line with a full-text hover popup; an explicit ellipsis toggles a multi-line region below that row, keeping its trigger stationary. Native text context menus remain available. The tabs replace the former radios and caption (owner follow-up, 2026-11-04); their hover/focus explanations name each comparison, including the first revision’s empty document. Diff headings use the list’s revision names (owner follow-up, 2026-11-04): parent → selected revision, or selected revision → Current state; a first revision’s parent is Empty. Full-text comparisons pass those names to the column headings and accessible textbox names; the phone’s unified header names both states with removal/addition markers. Parent/current comparison, linked generation origins, revision-message saves, restoration, URL selection and earlier-revision pagination retain the existing mechanisms. The opt-in `revision dialogs` cases in `layoutAudit.spec.ts` audit list, comparison and message-editor states at 1440/390 in both themes against fresh synthetic notes and cards.

**Sidebar navigation, prompt badges and note links (smallfixes5, 2026-11-04).** The card panel renders the replaceable `card.edit` contribution after Save in the identity row as the shared expand IconButton, excluding it from the panel action list; cast menus retain their existing presentation. Prompt kind badges identify only the editable Main, Post-history, Auxiliary and Enhance definitions slots, whose titles can change. Tinted placeholders (World Info before/after, Definitions, Description, Personality, Scenario, Persona, Examples, Chat history, Newest message and Summaries), custom prompts and unknown kinds have no kind badge. The positive-depth note marker reads “Notes in the chat history”; depth-zero placement and all depth/due annotations stay unchanged. Each listed title links to the existing note editor, opening over the chat when a workspace is present. The reader's existing preset-context projection includes each note's owned upstream ref; no database operations run on the main thread. Targeted coverage lives in `presetMarkers.spec.ts` and `cardHeader.spec.ts`; `LAYOUT_AUDIT_SMALLFIXES5_ONLY=1` audits the card header and both preset surfaces.

**Depth-zero note placement** (smallfixes4, 2026-11-04). `PromptDocument` lists depth 0 only under Notes after the newest message; Notes inside the chat accepts positive depths. `e2e/presetMarkers.spec.ts` checks both destinations in the panel and large editor.
