`packages/client/src/features/editor/`, at `/library/$refId` (loaded with the first entry opened), on stock components. The library lists **Edit** on cards and presets and has **New card**.
- **The page says which state you're in** (DESIGN §6.2), in a header without boxes: the name, once (a kind badge and variant/chat badge for kinds other than cards; a preset over the chat has it in the sticky bar instead of a heading; a preset, lorebook or note is renamed in place, `RefName` in `RefDialogs.tsx` on `ui/InlineRename.tsx`: a pencil beside the name turns it into a field with Save and Cancel, Enter and Escape, writing `RenameRef` with the subtitle kept), the card's provenance, its version, and one muted line on what an edit reaches ("Used by 3 chats: what you change here is used in all of them as you type. To change it in some only, fork it.", "make a variant" for other kinds; a chat's own version names its chat with a link back and says the original's later changes still reach it). The header holds the save cluster described below. Under it a sticky bar: Search, History, Make a variant for presets and lorebooks, and for cards their `actions` contributions (Fork) and **More** (a popover kept mounted so the dialogs its actions open stay open: the `actions` contributions marked `overflow`, which surfaces without a More menu still show inline: Forks, Compare, Mark as a fork of…, Unlink). Every action carries a tooltip saying what it does (`ui/Tooltip.tsx`; menu items take a `hint`, shown beside the menu on pointer or keyboard focus), and for a preset the held changes (`HeldChangesBar`, below) on a line under it. The card family section shows only for a card with forks (`whenForked`; the card page shows it always). An update from what the entry follows shows as a banner. A preset's Search is a toggle at the end of the toolbar (keeping the sticky bar with the search open under 400 px on a phone). An address whose entry was deleted or never existed says "This item was deleted or never existed · Library", the last word a link to the library (`NotFound` for a ref reads that way in any error too).
- **The store** (`store.ts`) holds the snapshot and a draft per field: typing changes the field at once and saves it 600 ms after the last key, one save per field at a time, naming the draft's id, row version and session as last seen; if another tab saved the field meanwhile, or another draft is at the field now (the one named moved to a variant), the server puts this on top and keeps theirs (§3.10). A field's base changes only with its text: reading the drafts again (after a commit, say) leaves a field with unsaved text on the base it was typed on. Every store on the page guards itself (`useLeaveGuard`), the card's notes included: leaving the editor saves what's left, closing or reloading the tab with a change not yet on the server asks first (`beforeunload`), and the page sends those changes as it goes (`pagehide`, to `/library/drafts`, with `keepalive`). A send counts only once the server answers, so a failed one goes again the next time. Browsers cap such a request at 64 KB, and a larger one isn't sent. Every change also leaves a pending-save record in this browser (`backup.ts`, IndexedDB), shared with composers: an independent id, target and field, original draft id, row version, session, revision base and request payload. A tab may replace only its own copy of the field that has not been sent; requests already out keep separate copies, and one that fails goes only if a newer copy typed from it replaces it. Acknowledgement deletes exactly that id. Opening the entry, a note included, replays all its copies with their original bases, so the writer preserves displaced text, and shows a notice. A displaced copy also leaves a conflict in that field's client state, shown beside its controls with both times, a preview, and an undoable switch through the same explicit restore as the composer. An entry that can't be opened (in the bin, say) keeps its copies until it can. A stale active field keeps its revision base across a commit; committing it goes through the conflict picker.
  - **Browser retention.** Copies are plain text in the browser profile, partitioned by user, and only that account's copies are exposed. Unacknowledged copies have no automatic age or capacity expiry. Retry and logout flushes accumulate `x-drafts-recovered`; recovery retries retain the explanation and recovered-text link through further retries and reopening the dialog. Logout retains this notice if it fails, and carries it in the login URL when it succeeds, including after a retry or reload. The login notice directs the user back to the same account; it contains no recovered text or account identity. Logout flushes each exact pending save before ending the session; failed saves keep the session open and offer Browser recovery (inspect/copy out, retry saving, or confirmed deletion of a selected copy). Another account's login leaves earlier copies untouched. Browser recovery (the sidebar's **Unsaved text**) remains accessible for expired sessions, missing targets and other failed saves. Every record requires the complete original payload; intermediate plaintext editor and JSON-in-content composer formats are not supported. Removing a module, prompt or script discards its descendant drafts, and Revert or the conflict picker's take-theirs response carries recovery metadata so the editor keeps its source link to recovered texts.
- **Components read the store only through hooks over `useSyncExternalStore`** (`useText`, `useValue`, `useDirty`, `useEditorState`), each subscribed to its own field's channel. Typing in a 50 KB description re-renders that field, and the page only when a field starts or stops having changes. A component that read the store directly showed stale values: the React Compiler memoizes what a stable object's methods return. For the same reason no closure in render uses `x!.y` on state that can be null: the compiler reads a closure's dependencies while rendering.
- **Each text field** has an **Edit history** control in the strip inside its box (`FieldEditHistory` in `controls.tsx` on the shared `ui/EditHistory.tsx`; owner, 2026-11-01) always present and disabled until the field has history, clearly apart from revision History: a ⟲ icon button whose dialog lists every state the field had, newest first, from any device or session, past every revision (§3.10), pages of 50 with **Earlier states**; picking one shows its whole text (`EditorDraftState`), swapped in place: the text shown last stays until the picked one's is read (texts read once are kept while the dialog is open), so picking never blanks or remounts the pane (owner, 2026-11-02: it showed "Loading its text…" for a frame on every pick, collapsing the pane and growing it back; `e2e/fieldChrome.spec.ts` counts removed and missing panes frame by frame while picking), and **Put this text in the box** makes it the newest state (`RestoreEditorDraft`, append-only: the text there before stays listed). It's for recovery; the box's own Ctrl+Z is the everyday undo. The field-only Revert described below restores the last revision through that same edit history. Settings (numbers, switches, selects, a list such as tags) have no control of their own: they apply as changed and History shows them. A copy from this browser that went over another tab's text still shows its notice beside the field (`ReplayNotice`). Numbers keep what's typed until it's a number. Alternate greetings and tags are each one value draft. `EditorStore.undo` remains for the protocol model test's history steps; no control calls it.
- **Saving** (`SaveRevision.tsx`, binding `ui/SaveControls.tsx`; saveflow, owner 2026-11-02 option B) cuts a checkpoint of live text (§14.2a) and applies any held preset changes. Every editor has one cluster in the top-right of its header: cards at the right end of the shared header’s first row beside the display name/version, presets and lorebooks at the right end of their title row, notes and snippets in their per-item header. The same three icon buttons (32px by default, with the note header’s existing 24px compact size) stay in order and keep their size in every state: **Save**, **Save with message…**, **Revert**. All are greyed while clean; Revert stays visible. Exact explanations are “Save a revision: a version of this you can go back to from History.”, “Save a revision with a note saying what changed.” and “Revert to the last revision.”; clean buttons say “No changes since the last revision.” The group exposes `data-save-state` (`clean`, `unsaved`, `blocked`, `saving`, `saved`, `failed`); saving shows a spinner; blocked card names are explained by the editor’s name check, and save failures show their reason below the buttons. Success shows “Revision saved.” below the buttons for 1.8 seconds without changing layout; the confirmation wraps within a compact cluster’s width. Save with message opens its one-line field below the buttons, with a pressed trigger and corner ×; Enter saves, Escape cancels. Revert puts all fields back to the last revision through `RevertEditorDrafts` and drops held preset changes, with no confirmation; edit history retains replaced text. The held-change bar only describes the pending preset changes. Save flushes pending drafts and preserves the existing per-field conflict picker when the revision changed meanwhile.
- **Unsaved tab indicators** (`ui/UnsavedChanges.tsx`, `Tabs.tsx`, `PanelTabs.tsx`): a small accent dot at each changed tab's top-right, with “Unsaved changes” on hover and in the tab's accessible description. Registered card tabs use their `holds` predicates for document drafts; nested tab scopes aggregate stable editor-store subscriptions and propagate note and embedded-editor changes to the parent tab, including the chat's tools and character strip. Visited editor sources remain observed while their navigation scope lives, so changing tabs does not clear a dot; a checkpoint or Revert does. Hidden dirty tools also mark More. Workspace editor sources also feed registered panel descriptors’ `holdsEditor` predicates, so edits made in a large card, preset or lorebook editor mark their panel tabs before the panel is first visited. Indicators take no layout space. Preset marker names and kind tags wrap within the available title width; tags can shrink and use an ellipsis, while closed-name controls reserve their chevron’s width and open-name controls reserve the chevron and pencil.
- **Field reverts** (`FieldRevert.tsx`, `ui/FieldRevertButton.tsx`): every multiline revision field has a small “Revert to last revision” button in its existing bottom chrome, disabled when equal. It flushes the field and restores only that field through the existing explicit `RestoreEditorDraft` operation, retaining replaced text as a separate history state even when nearby typing would otherwise coalesce. Fields inside one enclosing value draft preserve its other values. Code-editor fields also record the revert as an isolated CodeMirror edit, so Ctrl+Z restores the replaced text. Revision comparisons continue using the draft's immutable typing base; the field revert uses the current head revision. Greetings, line-list settings, primary/secondary lorebook keys and reply-section tags use their existing enclosing value-draft mechanism. Escape in the primary-keys editor ends that field edit without dismissing a phone’s panel sheet.

Total adds the first message, the example messages and the card's two prompts; alternate greetings and creator's notes aren't counted. As ST does (`substituteParams`), each text's macros are expanded before it's counted (`countMacros.ts`, `useCountMacros`, through the display's expansion, `chat/macros.ts`): `{{char}}` is the card's name for chats, `{{user}}` who the user plays in the open chat (the chat's `CastContext`), else "User" as in ST, and `{{description}}` and the like read the card's own fields; the tooltip says so. **Counting** (`tokenCounts.ts`, `useTokenCounts`): a text is counted once it rests for 400 ms, the texts every counter on the page wants then go in one `CountTokens` (at most 64 texts of 500,000 characters; a longer one counts as its four-characters estimate), and each text is counted once per chat model (the cache's key is `GetGenerationDefaults`' model), the last counts staying shown meanwhile; the tooltip says which tokenizer counted ("Counted with gpt-4o's own tokenizer (o200k_base, …), the model chats use.", or "Approximate: counted with o200k_base, …, as an approximation." and why, §6 "Text tokens"). The full editor's header is the same card header (`StorePortrait`: a click views it, the Picture button or a drop changes it); its actions include **Export…** (`features/cardExport/`, registered in `cardContributions` `actions` and in `chatCardActions`: a menu of the card formats `ListExportFormats` lists, the formats named in its tooltip; the file is always a saved revision, and unsaved changes are asked about first, §11.4 "Export with unsaved changes"). The book-only view (`?focus=lorebook`, the large editor) shows the embedded section alone; **Show the whole card** opens the card on its Lorebook tab. The note editor (`notes.tsx`, which a note's own page and a chat's notes use too): name; content in the code-editor box, or for a linked slot a banner naming the shared note and how many places an edit changes, with "Open shared note" (its own page, which says how many notes show it) and "Unlink" (or, while it's in the bin, "Restore" and "Unlink"); position, offering the five decided places (start of context, with the definitions, at a depth, start of the tail, end of the tail) with depth and role, and an older or imported place only on a note already there; when it applies (Always, On a chosen character's turn, While a chosen character isn't muted, each explained under its label in the list), and for the last two **Characters**: a multiple choice (`ui/MultiSelect.tsx`, Base UI's combobox) of the chat's cast, or in the card editor the card itself, the chosen ones as chips with a remove button (none on the last: a condition names at least one, and Always drops it), an Add button opening the list, a search above it past eight, and each character's explanation ("Sent when Mira writes the message.") at the list's foot while it's highlighted, or under its name on a phone or touch screen; a card the condition names that isn't offered is a dashed chip, "A card not in this chat", removable like the others; a new condition names the note's own card when it's offered, else the first; a one-line warning when a conditioned note sits above the history; "Lorebook entries can trigger on this note"; for a card's note "On in every chat" and "Private (not exported)"; the agent switch; and in its menu "Save as shared note" and "Delete the note". Saving as or unlinking from a shared note asks for unsaved changes to be saved first, then reopens the editor.
- **Embedded card lorebooks** (U19; `EmbeddedLorebook.tsx`) are a registered `card.editor.sections` contribution (`card.embedded-lorebook`), rendered through `SlotOutlet` in the book-only view (the card's Lorebook tab renders the same `LorebookForm` in the full editor and `LorebookPanelEditor` in the side panel, and the Extra tab leaves this section out with `SlotOutlet`'s `except`). A plugin can replace, disable or add sections with the same store. Cards with no book offer Add lorebook entry, creating a valid embedded document. Entries are collapsible rows; only open rows mount their forms, with the first entry and a newly added entry open initially. Book name, description, scan depth, budget and recursive scanning, and entry title, enabled/constant flags, primary and secondary keys, selective logic, case/whole-word matching, content, insertion order, position, depth, role, outlet, probability, entry scan depth, group selection, sticky/cooldown/delay message counts, recursion exclusions and budget bypass use the existing card field drafts and revision save. Keys are one per line, so regex keys containing commas survive. Entries use `uid=N` paths; additions have fresh random integer identities and removal uses `EditorStore.removeItem`, recovering drafts inside the deleted entry. Imported extension data and fields outside these controls stay untouched. Undo, revert and rebase of a structural draft recover descendant drafts whose parent disappears, keeping those that still fit; the first Undo restores the field from its own base revision through draft history, including an absent value, so it remains undoable. `test/protocol/draft-regressions.test.ts` and the browser tests cover this recovery and later card saves. Draft reload, field revert, revision restore and card export use the existing mechanisms; no separate lorebook write API or storage path was added. `e2e/embeddedLorebook.spec.ts` covers imported metadata preservation, drafts after reload, revert, deleting an entry with a text draft, adding entries and authoring an absent book, saving an empty book, earlier revision restore and V2 export, at desktop and phone widths in both themes.
- **Lorebook editor** (DESIGN §1.3, standalone authoring; `LorebookForm.tsx`, shared by standalone books, rooted at the document, and the card's embedded section, rooted at `character_book`). The book's name is renamed in place with the pencil beside it (`BookName` in `LorebookPanelEditor.tsx`: a library lorebook's `RefName`, whose rename also sets the document's `name` as a change of the book; a card's own book's `character_book.name`); its description, scan depth, token budget and recursion fold under **Book settings**, a card's book keeping its name field there too. The entries are a table (`LorebookTable.tsx`): a toolbar with **Add entry** (the new entry leads the table, open, its title focused; the view scrolls only when its header or title field isn't wholly in view, and then brings the whole header in under the sticky toolbar: `revealIfHidden` in `ui/reveal.ts`, shared with a prompt added in the preset editor; owner, 2026-11-02), a filter over titles, keys and content (drafts included), **Show** All / Enabled / Disabled, a sort and, while filtering, the count ("12 of 400 entries"; a card's book and the side panel show it always, a standalone page has it in its header); under it the **All entries** row: **Expand all** (every entry shown) and **Collapse all**, **Enable all** and **Disable all** (every entry's own switch, never the book's) and **Select**. Below it, one row per entry: an open/close button, the enabled switch, the title edited in place (owner, 2026-11-01: "This is fine. Leave it.") with the keys at a glance (closed, a click opens the entry at its keys; open, they're edited there), then the registered columns and a ⋯ menu (beside it, while the entry is open, its settings button). **Compact headers** (the side panel, `panel`, and any container narrower than 760 px: a phone, the chat's overlay) leave the columns out: under the title, the keys line and a few badges (`EntryBadges`, each explained on hover: Constant or Vector, never Normal; the position's short name, "@D 4" with its role unless system; a trigger % under 100 while it's used; the secondary key logic with its keys while they're used), the columns moving into the entry's Settings. Which entries are open is remembered per book and view in this browser (`lorebookOpen.ts`, `localStorage` `rp.lorebookOpen:<ref>:<root>` for the large editor, with `:panel` appended for the side panel). Each view restores its own expanded set on reload; opening or closing an entry in one leaves the other alone (owner decision via coordinator, 2026-11-02: "expansion is per view"). The URL entry target is also scoped per view (`entries:<ref>:<root>:entry` for the large editor, `entries:<ref>:<root>:panel:entry` for the side panel), so restoring a target never opens or focuses the other view; Collapse all clears that view's target. Title and keys IDs carry a unique per-table prefix, so opening at the keys, adding an entry or following a search visit focuses the field in the invoking editor even with both views mounted. `e2e/lorebookEntryClicks.spec.ts` covers keys-line editing and independent title, switch, menu and checkbox clicks, plus independent expansion/collapse across reloads with both views open. Its repeated held-press tests use 174-entry books in both views, at normal speed and 6× CPU throttling, checking the hit target before release and keys focus after release for text, inter-key space and trailing padding, with the clicked entry both closed and open. The spec resolves each view's title IDs once for repeated row lookup. Its forty-press loops keep tracing, with a ten-minute total budget at 6× CPU throttling (five minutes at normal speed), a fifteen-second action limit and the existing ten-second focus assertions, so the repeated workload's budget does not hide a missing target or lost click. Rows are virtualized (`@tanstack/react-virtual`, in a `"use no memo"` `Rows` component; the scroll parent is found by walking up, so the page and the chat overlay both work). The table itself stays eligible for React Compiler memoization: optional defaults are resolved in its body, and search/URL restoration uses effect events to read current state while reacting only to a new target. Registry lists stay memoized, equal root paths share an identity across URL navigation, and `Rows` forwards actions through stable callbacks whose current table handlers are refreshed in a layout effect (URL setters change with the target). Opening or focusing one entry therefore does not repeatedly render every mounted row in a large book. Strategy and Position use the shared `ui/Select.tsx` Select, including standard trigger styling and highlighted-option explanations. Plain icon buttons and a ⋯ that mounts its `Menu` only when first used (`Menu`'s `defaultOpen`) keep the remaining collapsed-row controls light. The order is computed when the entry list, search, filter or sort changes, never on an edit. Added and duplicated entries lead the table, newest first, open, with the newest's title focused, until the search, filter or sort changes (`arrangeEntries`' `pinned`), so a duplicate doesn't push the entry it copies away. A row's keys line says when there are none what that means (always included, by similarity, or never matched). A search visit (`SearchNavigation`) to an entry clears the filter, opens the entry and scrolls to it. A row opens to `EntryDetails` (`LorebookEntryDetails.tsx`; owner, 2026-11-01: "only entry content and primary keys should generally be expanded right away"; 2026-11-02: open entries are for scrolling and skimming): with its settings closed, an open entry is its title, its keys and its text, with no labels or hint lines. The keys stay on the header's line under the title (`KeysLine`: comma-separated and wrapping; a click or focus shows the box, one key per line, in place; the box is always mounted for the keyboard and assistive technology and visually hidden until focused; Escape or leaving it turns it back; a pointer press that leaves it keeps the box in place through the resulting click (`useEditorFocus`, shared with editor action strips), so collapsing an earlier keys box cannot move a later row between pointerdown and pointerup; the "/pattern/flags" rule is in the standard “?” beside its first line, never a tooltip on the field itself). The content has a hidden label and is as tall as its text, full width (`TextField fit`: from two lines to 60% of the screen; a card book's code editor grows the same way), opening large. A sliders button in the header beside ⋯ (`BlockOptionsToggle`, as a preset prompt's options; **Settings of** the title, shown only while the entry is open) opens **Entry settings** above the text, a second level each entry opens on its own (held per page by the table; a search visit to anything but the title, keys or content opens it): in a compact header's entry the columns first, labelled, then the secondary keys and logic, outlet name (outlet position), **Matching** (case, whole words, scan depth, the six "also look for keys in" sources, generation types from `TRIGGERS`), **Inclusion group**, **Recursion and budget** (non-recursable, prevent recursion, delay until recursion with an optional level, ignore budget, use trigger %) and a folded **Timing, filters and automation** (sticky, cooldown, delay, character filter, automation id, add memo, and for card books name, priority and `use_regex`), which says chats don't use those yet. `placement_override` and `decision_hint` have no control: the assembler doesn't support the first (`loreStages.ts`), and decision models aren't built. While a row's own fields have changes, the opened entry lists them with their Undo, History and Revert (the whole entry's too, named by its title); edited cells get an accent ring. Deleted entries are listed above the table ("Deleted, until you save") with **Restore**, which discards the removal draft. **Registries** (`lorebookTable.ts`, defaults in `lorebookColumns.tsx`): `lorebookColumns` (header, grid width, cell), `lorebookSorts` (label, compare with the entry's index, typed title and whether it has changes) and `lorebookEntryActions` (label, icon, tone, and `run` or a `dialog`), so a plugin can add, replace or disable columns, sorts and row actions. The defaults are strategy, position, depth (disabled unless at a depth), order and trigger %; order (ST's Priority, highest first), title, depth, trigger % and recently changed; Duplicate, Copy to another lorebook…, Move to another lorebook… and Delete. Copy and move load the other book in a separate `EditorStore`, add the entry under a fresh uid, and commit only that field (`EditorStore.commit(message, only)`), so that book's own drafts stay drafts. The standalone editor renders through the registered `lorebook.editor.sections` slot (`cardSections.ts`): `lorebook.use` (the entry count and the prompt presets that send it, each a link, from `LorebookPresets`; the chats it was added to are the editor header's line, `EditorPage.tsx` `addedTo`: "Not added to any chat yet." / "Added to N chats: saving changes it in all of them…") and `lorebook.entries`.
  - **The header** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §1.3): the side panel's title row is the name and its pencil, Close, the save cluster and **Large editor** as its rightmost icon button. The table's toolbar (`[data-lorebook-toolbar]`, a size container) has an **editing row** (role toolbar "Editing": **Add entry** and the host's `tools`, the panel's **Search and replace** toggle, whose label hides below 22rem of width), the host's `toolPanel` under it (the Search and replace panel), and a **filter row** (group "Filter entries": All/Enabled/Disabled and the sort picker kept together on one line, the sort narrowing first; then the filter field, `flex-1` up to `max-w-sm`, which takes the next line when there's less room than its 11rem minimum, with the count inside its end: "3 entries", "2 of 3 entries"). Without an editing row (the large editor and the card page, whose title row has the save cluster and whose sticky bar has Search and replace) Add entry leads the filter row. The **list header**, inside the list's border, is one row at every width: the select-all checkbox over the rows' checkboxes (checked, unchecked or indeterminate, for the entries shown), then "N selected" with **Edit N entries** while something is selected (in place of "Title · keys" in the wide table's column header, so ticking never moves the list), and at its end the expand/collapse toggle (Expand all while every shown entry is closed, else Collapse all) and ⋯ with **Enable all** and **Disable all**. Every row has its checkbox; there is no Select mode. **The whole entry header toggles the entry** (`headerClick`): a click on its own space opens or closes it, while a click inside a button, input, textarea, label, switch, checkbox or a `[data-own-click]` element (the open keys line) is that control's, and a click that ends a text selection does nothing; the arrow stays the keyboard's toggle. Add entry and Duplicate reveal the new entry with `revealAdded` (`ui/reveal.ts`): scrolled wholly into view, header included, as far as needed, then its box flashes three times (one fading highlight with reduced motion).
  - **Header gaps and field help** (lorebookfix2; owner, 2026-11-03): one `gap-2` (8 px) separates adjacent header controls, including the switch and title and the settings/⋯ buttons; the checkbox has no extra horizontal wrapper padding and uses a top margin in compact headers so its wrapper is not treated as a padded control container. Primary keys and the filter text field never show an explanation on hover, focus or click. Their help is in the shared `AboutHint` beside the field; labelled entry fields use `Field.about`. Strategy and Position use the shared Select and its item explanations, with the placement descriptions derived from assembler markers, example placement and depth roles. `e2e/lorebookEditorRework.spec.ts` measures every adjacent header gap within 1 px in both editors at 390/1024/1440, checks keys help without field popovers, visible placement controls and help, shared Select triggers and every option's displayed explanation. The shared MultiSelect documents its compact chip/Add padding as the interior of one bordered field, an inset-only audit exception; other controls and geometry rules remain audited. The layout audit has a focused `LAYOUT_AUDIT_LOREBOOKS_ONLY=1` mode for both editors, closed/open settings and focused keys, with scroll-end sampling at all six width/theme profiles.
  - **Changes to many entries** (owner, 2026-11-01, 2026-11-02; `lorebookMass.ts`): **Enable all** / **Disable all** under the list header's ⋯, and **Edit N entries** (`LorebookMassEdit.tsx`): the entry settings form (below) for the selected entries, every section open in two columns on a wide screen. Each setting has a checkbox ("Change <setting>"); unticked it's greyed and disabled and shows the value the entries share or Mixed, never as a value: a switch with its thumb in the middle and a dashed track, a select with an italic "Mixed" placeholder (no such option), a text or number field empty with an italic "Mixed" placeholder; a small dashed ≠ marker beside the setting gives the breakdown on hover and focus ("2 off, 1 on", `commonValue`). Ticking starts it at the shared value, or for a mixed one empty (text and numbers, which clears it) or unchosen (choices and switches, which changes nothing until chosen). The ticked settings' patches merge in form order (`manyPatch`; an empty number clears to null where it can, else to a new entry's value via the setting's `patch`), only the fields that differ change (`patchEdits`), and **Apply to N entries** counts the entries that will change (none: disabled). Each is **an ordinary unsaved change** (owner, 2026-11-02; `applyMassChange`): the edits are value drafts, as any setting's change, so **Revert to the last save** beside Save undoes them and Save keeps them; no revision is cut for it, and its toast ("Disabled all 40 entries", "Changed Order, Sticky on 2 entries") has no Undo of its own.
  - **The entry settings form** (owner, 2026-11-02; `lorebookSettings.ts`, defaults in `lorebookSettingsDefaults.tsx`): two registries a plugin can add to, replace or disable, `lorebookEntrySections` (id, title, hint, column, `visible`, an optional `lead`, `plain` for an always-visible unboxed group, and `headerStatus: false` to suppress the marker and summary) and `lorebookEntrySettings` (section, label, description, an input kind: switch, choice, number, text or inherit (unset/on/off); `current`, `patch`, the entry `field` a single-entry control binds to, or a `single` renderer; `visible`, `group` for a shared heading, `many: false` for those not offered for several entries, `card` for a card book's own, `summary`). The sections: Strategy and position (where the row hides its columns, the side panel and narrow screens, its `lead` is the row's columns; else only an outlet's name), Secondary keys, Matching (the six "also look for keys in" sources under one heading, generation types), Inclusion group, Recursion and budget, Timing and filters (sticky, cooldown, delay, the character filter), and **Card export only** (automation ID, add memo; in a card's own book also export name, priority and the regex flag), with no per-field "kept for export" text. Card export only has `headerStatus: false` (owner, 2026-11-03): a collapsed header is only its title and arrow, without a dot or summary even for non-default export values; its wide heading also has no dot. An opened entry is its title, keys line and text; its header's settings button opens the settings **below the text** (`EntryDetails`). Strategy and position is a plain group ahead of the other sections, always shown while entry settings are open in the side panel; the large editor keeps these controls visible as row columns when wide, or below the content even with options closed when narrow. Every column label has a “?” help button, including the wide table header (`LorebookColumn.description`). In the side panel and on a narrow screen the remaining sections are accordions (`SettingsLayout`, `ui/Block.tsx` `BlockSection`), closed until opened, its header saying what differs from a new entry's values (`sectionSummary`: "Sticky 3", "Default settings") with a quiet accent dot (`changed`) that the accessible name reads as "changed from the defaults". This compares the currently displayed settings’ `current` values with a new entry’s defaults (`emptyEntry`), not the saved revision or draft state; saved/imported values and explicit choices equivalent to inherited defaults can therefore show a dot. Only differing values enter the closed summary, otherwise it says "Default settings". The wide large editor shows the boxed sections open in two columns, with the same dot except on Card export only. Accordion summaries are computed only while their section is closed; section bodies are built only while open. One entry's settings bind to its fields (`SingleSetting`: `SwitchField`, `InheritedSwitch`, `SelectField`, `NumberField`, `TextField`, or the setting's `single`); Edit N entries renders the same sections and settings with its own controls. `client/test/lorebookMass.test.ts` covers the patches, Mixed breakdowns, merging several settings, clearing and the summaries.
  - **The side panel's book** (`LorebookPanelEditor`, owner 2026-11-01): one book (a store and the book's place in its document, so the card editor can embed a card's own book the same way), with its name renamed in place, **Large editor**, a close button ("Closes this lorebook."), the shared Save controls (`SaveRevision`) beside Add entry, a **Search and replace** toggle (pressed while open; its panel inline under the editing row, its own ids, scoped to the book) and the table in its `panel` form. Search and replace reaches every entry's title, text, outlet, group and keys through the `editorTextFields` contribution `lorebook.entries`. The save dialog names entries by title (`fields.ts`: an element's `comment` names it, `entries` elements are called "Entry", and a removed element is named from the saved document), and an entry's fields as the table does (Title, Strategy (constant), Position (role), Trigger %…); a card's embedded book is labelled the same way under "Lorebook:". Opened over the chat, the overlay is named "Lorebook editor" (`PresetWorkspace.tsx`) and its way out is **Back to the chat**. The entry's content opens large (`TextField expandable`, the card fields' dialog). Discarding a value draft of `null` (a removal) puts nothing in the bin's recovered texts (`db/bin.ts` `recover`). `test/lorebookTable.test.ts` covers arranging (pinned entries included), ST names and diff labels (removed entries, card books); `e2e/standaloneLorebook.spec.ts` covers opening from the chat over it, the table's search, filter and sort, inline and opened edits after reload, save with titled diff, delete and restore, duplicate, add, copy to another book, search and replace, export and revision restore at 1440 and 390 px, and on a 400-entry book that rows are virtualized, the five cells save, an added entry and its duplicate both lead, Move saves in the other book, the entry text opens large, and the diff names entries and fields; `e2e/embeddedLorebook.spec.ts` covers the same table in the card editor.
- **Preset warnings** render above the prompt document through `preset.editor.warnings` (`presetSections.ts`), with built-in contribution `preset.warnings` registered by the editor feature. Plugins can replace, disable or add warnings with the same draft store and a callback that opens and scrolls to a prompt. The mounted editor host is covered by `endOfRequest.test.ts`.
- **Placeholder sources** (placeholdersource, owner follow-up 2026-11-03): promptKinds.tsx supplies source noun phrases for known markers, history and the synthetic summaries row. PlaceholderSource pairs italic text-muted copy with the standard ui/AboutHint question-mark button, shared by the panel, large editor and occupied notes placements. The narrow column keeps the title and end cluster on one line, reserving the expand control’s width while the kind tag can truncate; block-name captions remain bounded by their control. The source line has no hover or tab stop of its own; its text wraps even within a word when a narrow panel leaves less than a word’s width. placeholderHelp supplies 2–3 sentences naming what each request inserts, why the text cannot be edited in the preset, where to edit the original and any notes, Definitions routing, formatting, examples or lore-placement settings. Unknown markers say “No content source” and explain that nothing is inserted. Text, edit destinations, sentence limits and standard help-button interaction are covered by promptKinds.test.ts and presetMarkers.spec.ts; the preset-only layout audit includes a saved Definitions block.
- **The preset editor** (`PromptDocument.tsx`, owner P1–P7, 2026-11-02; preseteditor, 2026-11-03) is one scrolling document with every prompt, including off prompts, and no separate pool. Both views share the document and store. The panel keeps picker + New, name + pencil with the expand icon, editing actions, then view controls. The large editor has name + pencil + preset badge and `WindowClose`, editing actions followed by History and Make a variant, then the same view row. The document portals its controls into the large editor’s sticky toolbar; no second add toolbar appears in the list. Editing actions are Add prompt, Add definitions block, the unchanged SaveRevision cluster, Search and replace; search is pressed while its panel is open below the actions, and the panel has a corner close. Whole labels disappear, with their hover/accessibility names retained, at container widths 52/44/25rem in the large editor (search/definitions/prompt), and 38/30/20rem in the panel; history/variant labels disappear under 35rem. Internal group gaps are 4px, between groups 8px. The view row has a single expand/collapse-all button and the Auto-expand options checkbox, explained by “Opening a prompt also opens its options.” Its default is per account in this browser (`rp.presetOptionsOpen:<user id>`). Turning on opens the options of already open prompts; opening a prompt then also opens its options. Turning off closes all options; individual options toggles still work, including opening a collapsed prompt with its options.

  Each editable row is a bordered block: drag handle, live switch, expand arrow and title with its rename pencil. In the large editor the slot tag, options and menu follow the title, while read-only info is right-aligned: warnings/summary/condition/generation types, placement, role, tokens last, with 8px gaps. Its first text line is below the title, muted and truncated; below a 36rem list width the info has a right-aligned line of its own. The panel keeps compact headers, with the same order for expanded badges. Placement says “in place” or “depth N”; roles, placement, tokens and less common badges all explain themselves on hover/focus. Names and content retain text drafts and CodeMirror. Options retain role, position, depth/order, condition, generation types and card overrides. Titles remain renamed in place; handles and outline names reorder by pointer, touch or arrow keys with edge scrolling. The outline remains resizable and remembers its width per user.

  `promptKinds.tsx` distinguishes custom cards, built-in editable slots (Main, Post-history, Auxiliary, Enhance definitions, with named slot tags) and placeholders (kind icon/tag, tinted card, muted filled-from line, no text box or preview). `styles.css` defines a distinct semantic tint for each known slot/kind in both themes. Unknown built-ins use the accent fallback. Chat history is a stronger full-width band with its chat icon and larger label. The fixed Summaries placeholder sits immediately before that band, matching `stages.ts`/`st.ts` summary-layer insertion, even when the layer is empty, and has no drag handle. Card override explanations live in slot tag hovers; an actual replacement or refusal in the open chat still appears below the header with the card link.

  A new prompt goes at the end (card overrides forbidden by default). Definitions goes before the first per-field definition marker, else just before history, else at the end; its hover names the real place. With Definitions present its button is disabled and explains why. Both actions open the added block, wait one animation frame for the sticky unsaved bar’s measured height, keep the header visible and flash the box three times through the shared `ui/reveal.ts` helper, with its reduced-motion highlight also used by lorebook additions. Editable additions focus their text. Insert above/below stays in each row’s menu. All additions retain the existing held Save/Revert behavior. Marker rows show the current chat's estimated content and definition names ("Definitions: Aria, Rook"), or “no chat open” in the library; with the Definitions marker on, the per-field markers say "Filled by Definitions". The Main and Post-history tags explain card overrides; an actual replacement or refusal still appears with the card’s link, from `PresetContext.overrides`. The card editor's System prompt and Post-history instructions fields say whether their text is used (`PromptUseNote.tsx`, `GetCardPromptUse`): "Used in place of ⟨preset⟩'s Main Prompt", "Not used: ⟨preset⟩'s Main Prompt can't be replaced", "… is off", or "⟨preset⟩ has no Main Prompt". The same component in its `column` layout is the side panel's Prompt preset tab (below, **Preset overlays**). After the prompts, **Lorebooks sent with this preset** (`PresetLorebooks.tsx`; owner, 2026-11-01) lists the preset's `lorebooks` as blocks, each with its switch (a value draft of its `enabled`, live like a prompt's; `EditorStore.switchLorebook`), its name from the library (or "A lorebook no longer in the library", switched off and not sent), **Open** (over the chat through the workspace, else its page) and a ✕ that takes it off the preset; **Attach a lorebook** picks one of the library's books (`LorebookPicker`). Attaching and taking off wait behind the unsaved bar (below). **Held preset changes** (owner, 2026-11-01 for moves; 2026-11-02 for every preset-level change without a confirmation of its own, a prompt's on/off switch excepted; `@rp/shared/presetHeld.ts`, `EditorStore` `addPrompt`, `deletePrompt`, `attachLorebook`, `detachLorebook`, `revertHeld`): moving, deleting and adding a prompt (the Card definitions block too) and attaching or taking off a lorebook are the editor's `HELD_FIELD` draft (`{order, deleted, added, attached, detached}`, only the parts in use; one from before 2026-11-02 still reads), shown in place (`withHeld`) and applied only by the bar's Save (`applyHeld`, then the commit). An added prompt's definition is a live value draft, so its text has a place to be typed into, but its order entry, switch included, waits in `added`: the live order lacks it, so `presetOrder` lists it as an off prompt and nothing sends it, and a reply's checkpoint leaves its drafts alone (`heldPromptPaths`, in `CheckpointLiveText`), so Revert (the bar's, or Revert to the last save) takes it away entirely. Deleting a prompt only added behind the bar removes its definition at once. A preset book's switch on a book attached behind the bar switches it there. The bar (`HeldChangesBar` in `SaveRevert.tsx`, floating in the Prompt preset tab, a line in the large editor's toolbar) says what waits ("new order · 1 prompt added · 1 lorebook taken off", `describePresetChanges` of the live preset without the added definitions, `beforeHeld`, against the shown one). Text, a prompt's name and options, and the preset's other settings stay live (DESIGN §6.2). The chat's Lorebooks tab shows the preset's books as the editor does, and switches them through `switchLorebook`. The large editor scrolls there for the focus `PRESET_LOREBOOKS_FOCUS`, which the chat's Lorebooks tab links to. Between rows, `placeReuseLines` retains every entry from `PresetContext.cacheAfter`, including multiple points projected onto one row, without reducing them to two. `CacheBreakpointLine` uses thin dividers labelled “Cache breakpoint · prefix/summaries/history”; pinned points use prefix. The exact owner-supplied cache explanation is in the (i) popover. The reader projection supplies none unless the model’s caching is explicit; summary pieces project to their own Summaries row. Breakpoint assembly is unchanged. An enabled prompt at or above the first displayed breakpoint gets “Changes every reply” for parsed macros marked volatile in the shared display macro registry, with their actual names in the hover. `pick` is deterministic and gets no warning. Random and clock macros in preset text are fresh on each request (unlike stored message draws); the assembler currently does not mark those preset pieces volatile solely for these macros, so the warning identifies a cache limitation without changing placement. Notes retain their occupied-place rows, now tinted with a kind tag; in-chat notes follow the history band. The after-chat divider remains. `e2e/presetMarkers.spec.ts` covers the headers, reveal/flash, options, row order, kinds, summary landmark, cache labels/counts and warnings at 390/1440/1920 in both views; its optional layout audit uses the shared geometry detector. Then prefill (the start of the reply, of a reply written as you, and what goes after a continued message; ST's continue prefill has no switch, owner 2026-11-02: `prefill.continue` is kept as imported and exported back, and nothing reads it), utility prompts and regex approval retain their controls; samplers and formatting are model settings (**Model settings**, `@rp/shared/modelSettings.ts`).
- **Preset editors from a chat** (`PresetWorkspace.tsx`; the overlay over the chat's column is replaced by the workbench's editor tabs, 2026-11-05, §5 "The workbench": where this paragraph says overlay, read the editor's tab beside the chat) open beside the chat, leaving the mounted chat, its scroll and composer intact. The sticky toolbar keeps the preset’s name, Close preset editor and save status visible after scrolling or jumping to a prompt; closing uses the existing workspace close path and leaves drafts protected. `e2e/presetOverlay.spec.ts` checks the scrolled close control and identity at 1440 and 390 in both themes. The nonmodal Base UI dialog portals into its own column; other panels remain usable. On phones opening it closes the panel sheet. The registered chat workspace also reconciles an open editor when the layout crosses below 1024 px: the panel closes instead of becoming a modal sheet over the existing editor and making it inert. This applies to lorebook, preset and card overlays; `e2e/editorResize.spec.ts` covers 1024 → 390 px with forty lorebook entries expanded, a fifteen-second resize-and-edit bound, and returning to an interactive chat for all three kinds. The library's Edit opens the preset's editor as a page at `/library/$refId` instead, without the overlay's Close preset editor. A card opens in the same workspace from its chat tab (Full editor), with "Card editor" as the overlay's name and **Back to the chat** in its sticky bar: the chat, its fork and scroll stay mounted under it, and the chat path stays the same; `editor` and `focus` identify the overlay in its query. A workspace shares its `EditorStore` between the overlay and the right panel's **Prompt preset tab** (`PresetTab.tsx`; owner, 2026-11-01), so an edit in either shows in the other. The tab opens the preset the next reply's context estimate names, or, in a chat without one yet (a chat with no messages has none), the account's selected preset (`GetGenerationDefaults`). It edits the whole preset in the column: its name (renamed in place), **Large editor** (the overlay, for the whole preset), the warnings slot, then `PromptDocument` in its `column` layout: every block starts closed to one row (handle, switch, name, the first line of its text, tokens, ⋯), so a collapsed prompt mounts no editor; a row's name opens it to the same header as the large editor's (rename, chips, options toggle) above its text in the code editor, growing with it. The ⋯ menu adds **Open in the large editor** (the overlay, scrolled to that prompt and expanded). Note places show only when they hold a note, here as in the large editor (owner, 2026-11-02: quiet when empty); the chat and reuse lines show as there. The rest of the preset (end of request, reply sections, text switches, prefill, utility prompts, regex scripts: `PresetSettings` in `PresetEditor.tsx`, the large editor's own sections) folds under one lazily mounted disclosure (`Disclosure lazy`). What's typed and switched is live (§14.2a): the next reply uses it, and the tab's own **Save** and **Save with a message…** (above the warnings) cut a revision. Moving a prompt and deleting one are held behind a bar stuck to the bottom of the panel's scroll (owner, 2026-11-01: easy to do by accident), and the same bar is a line in the large editor's toolbar (`HeldChangesBar` in `SaveRevert.tsx`). They're the editor's `HELD_FIELD` draft (`["~held"]`, JSON `{ order, deleted }`, `heldOrder.ts`), on the server like any typing but never a field of the document: `applyDrafts`, Save's field list and a reply's checkpoint leave it out. The store shows the order as arranged (`arrange`: the live entries in the held sequence, deleted prompts out) while the live order keeps the saved positions; an order the user makes is split (`splitOrder`, against the order as stored, so a prompt just added, which the shown order lists last until it has a place, counts as new): each kept entry's own change (its switch) and an added prompt, after its nearest neighbour above, go live, the arrangement is held. The bar says what's held (`describePresetChanges` of the live and the arranged document: "new order · 1 prompt deleted"); the header’s **Revert** restores the last revision, including text and settings, and drops held changes without asking; the header’s **Save** applies the arrangement and the deletions (`removeItem`, their text drafts to the recovered texts as a deletion's are) and saves a revision of the whole preset, as the header's Save does too. `client/test/heldOrder.test.ts` covers the split and the arrangement. `e2e/presetTab.spec.ts` covers, on a synthetic 30-prompt preset with unnamed prompts and emoji names, at 1440 and 390 in both themes: closed rows and labels, expanding, options, the bar staying in view while the column scrolls, keyboard and pointer reorders, a touch drag at 390 (CDP touch events), opening the large editor at a prompt with the tab's drafts and the tab showing the overlay's, adding (renamed in its header) and deleting; and the large editor's blocks, folded options, Show all options and rename at 2560, 1440 and 390.
- **Snippets and notes large** (notesnippetlarge, owner 2026-11-02; DESIGN §4.1; since workbench, 2026-11-05, in an editor tab bound to the chat rather than an overlay, and `editor=` links open that tab): a snippet or a note opens in the same workspace, so it stays open while the side panel changes tab or character, and its place is `editor=<ref>&focus=snippet|note` (reload, links, Back/Forward; on phones opening it closes the panel sheet, as for the other large editors). A feature supplies such a view through the `workspaceViews` registry (`features/editor/workspaceViews.ts`: `{ id: <focus>, label, page?, component }`); `ChatBoundEditor` shows a registered view for the tab's `focus` (its `label` the region's name) instead of the library editor, passing the chat's `session` and `view`, and `EditorPage` shows a view marked `page` for `/library/$refId?focus=<id>`. The workspace's `store(ref, chatNote?)` keys a chat's own note's store by its position (chat, fork, message shown), and `NoteBlock` (`NoteList.tsx`) takes its store from the workspace when there is one, so the Notes tab, a card's Notes in the character tab and the large view edit through one `EditorStore` (same live text, "edited" marker and save cluster); a shared store is loaded once and re-read on a relink. **Note** (`ChatNoteLarge` in `ChatNotes.tsx`, registered lazily in `registerPanels.tsx`, "Note editor"): the Notes tab's block with `large`, always open, its name a heading, the text box at least 12 rows, the switch, rename, save cluster, ⋯ and settings as in the tab, and the shared close control (`ui/WindowClose.tsx`); it reads the chat's notes as the tab does (`useChatNotes`, shared by both) and finds the note there (a card's note too); deleted there, it closes. Its **Large editor** is in each note's ⋯ menu wherever a workspace exists (the library's card page has none). A slot showing a shared note offers **Large editor** on its banner, which opens the shared note as a snippet. **Snippet** (`features/snippets/SnippetLarge.tsx`, "Snippet editor", `page`): its name renamed in place, its scope, Copy, close, the **All chats** switch, Save and the `snippets.tools` slot, then its text (`source: "snippet"`, at least 16 rows, with the added-text flash) through `SnippetWorkspace.store`, the panel block's store; its editor registers with `useSnippetEditorSurface` while loaded, so it counts as an expanded snippet for one-click Send (and opening it uses it); once listed and gone (deleted) it closes. Its block in Snippets has a **Large editor** icon beside Copy; in the floating sheet outside a chat that opens `/library/$refId?focus=snippet` instead. `e2e/largeNoteSnippet.spec.ts`: a note and a snippet open large while the panel edits two characters' Descriptions, both copies keeping their text and marker, Save in the large one clearing the panel's, reload restoring it, Back/Forward, 1920 and 390 px, the library page, and Send text to snippet from a card's Description in the side panel landing in the snippet open large; with `LAYOUT_AUDIT=1` it audits the overlay at 1440, 1920 and 390.
- **Current-chat annotations** travel in `NextContext.presetContext`, including the Cache event and the client's session projection. The reader transaction projects sent root pieces, their descendant card names, active notes (including empty ones, marking an interval-skipped note as not due) and the request's existing breakpoints (`db/presetContext.ts`); it sends no prompt text. Counts are estimates of expanded piece text, excluding provider framing. Failed assembly yields unavailable context, not a fabricated fill. Draft edits show their own text estimates; marker annotations describe the saved preset's current assembly until a revision is saved.
- **Search and replace** (`SearchDialog.tsx`, shared controlled fields/options in `ui/SearchReplace.tsx`, `searchCore.ts`) covers every text field of the working document, with case, Unicode whole-word, regex captures and preserve case (upper, lower or title case) options and before → after previews. Patterns run in Unicode mode when they can; one that only a plain regular expression accepts (`\'`, `\-`) runs without it, with ASCII word boundaries for whole words. It's called **Search and replace** everywhere, with the search-and-replace icon (`replace`), never a lone magnifier (owner, 2026-11-02). Presets and lorebooks keep it in the sticky toolbar, folded away until the shared **Search and replace** toggle in the editing toolbar (`aria-pressed`, `pressedButtonClass`) opens it below, in the overlay and on the page; the side panel's book has the same toggle in its editing row. Inline, it's an `InlinePanel` (`ui/InlinePanel.tsx`; here `titleHidden`: its heading for assistive technology only and its × (`WindowClose`) in the corner beside the first row; Escape inside it closes it, focus going back to the toggle) bounded to `max-w-5xl`: Find with its **Find** button and Replace with with its **Replace all** button (the fields named by their placeholders, their labels for assistive technology), each pair one line, side by side when the panel is at least 42rem wide (a size container) and stacked below that, then the four compact matching toggles and Look in; on a phone those fold behind **Options**, beside Replace all. Go to keeps the inline panel open. The large card editor and side-panel card editor use the same inline search, shared `SearchReplaceButton`, `SearchDialog` and `ui/SearchReplace` controls as presets and lorebooks (searchreplace, 2026-11-04); on a phone its options fold behind an Options button, the match list is shorter and the editor actions use compact spacing, so the bar leaves most of the screen to the document (`e2e/unitGPreset.spec.ts` retains the 400 px toolbar limit at 390 px). Editor searches expand below the pressed trigger and close with their corner X or Escape. Every match has a clickable field label and a Go to action. The shared dialog calls its host’s reveal callback with the field path and match range; the editor supplies navigation through `searchNavigation.ts`. Prompt and regex sections expand the matched field, and card text, alternate greetings and embedded lorebook fields use the same range selection. A marker-name match focuses and reveals its marker row with the matching text highlighted, since markers have no name input; any other prompt's name match opens its rename field (`InlineRename` `goTo`, also when the field mounts with the match, as a closed prompt in the column does) with the match selected and scrolled into view, and a lorebook title match focuses the entry's title with the match selected (`e2e/lorebookEditorRework.spec.ts` covers both). Lorebook key selection applies once per visit so subsequent typing keeps its new caret position. Field controls focus without editing, reveal closed details, and scroll the match below the measured sticky toolbar in the overlay or page. CodeMirror focuses on the next animation frame so a host can open a closed details section first. Repeated visits reselect the range. `e2e/presetOverlay.spec.ts` covers collapsed-prompt and marker-name navigation at 1440 and 390 in both themes, plus closed utility and regex fields and offscreen ranges in long prompts; `e2e/editor.spec.ts` covers card code-editor and single-line matches. Each search runs in a worker terminated after 2 s, so a catastrophic pattern cannot hang the page; empty matches advance correctly, and at most 500 previews are listed while Replace all still covers all matches. Matches also stay highlighted in the actual expanded text boxes: `searchHighlights.ts` publishes current preview ranges per editor store, including joined list offsets for keys; `CardTextEditor` passes them to CodeMirror's search decoration field, while `ui/SearchHighlights` mirrors native text controls with non-interactive semantic warning marks, tracking wrapping, size and scroll. Rename fields use the same mirror when open. Highlights clear when the preview becomes stale or the search closes, and mount with newly expanded fields. All matches are returned by the time-limited worker for highlighting; the result list remains capped at 500. `e2e/searchReplace.spec.ts` covers card/preset/lorebook large and panel surfaces at 1440/390, and `LAYOUT_AUDIT_SEARCHREPLACE_ONLY=1` audits the six surfaces. Replacements write through field drafts. If fields change while the worker is running, replacement stops and asks for a fresh search. Feature sections contribute text through the `editorTextFields` registry (`fields.ts`), with override and disable by id; registration changes invalidate open previews. `card.embedded-lorebook` contributes book name and description, entry title, content, outlet, group and primary/secondary keys (`lorebookFields.ts`), including closed entries. **Look in** (owner, 2026-11-01; `searchScopes.ts`): a preset's and a lorebook's search (now in the sticky toolbar like a preset's, and a card's own book's) chooses what it goes through, by field path: Content, Keys (primary and secondary), Both or Everything for a book (`lorebookScopes(root)`, which also keeps a card's own book's search inside the book), Prompt text, Prompt names, Both or Everything for a preset (`presetScopes`); Everything is the default and the choice is remembered per kind in this browser (`rp.searchScope.<kind>`); on a phone it folds behind Options with the other options, which counts a scope other than Everything, so the 400 px toolbar limit holds. Every option, button and the scope explains itself on hover and focus. Key replacements write their list draft under the entry’s uid, preserving comma-containing regex keys. `test/lorebookFields.test.ts` and `e2e/embeddedLorebook.spec.ts` cover replacements, closed-entry navigation, key range selection, continued typing after navigation and registry overrides.
- **Across the library** (search, 2026-11-12; DESIGN §6.2 "Search, and search and replace, everywhere", ST-GRIPES F13). The library's **Search and replace** button (`SearchReplaceButton`, registered in the library's `library.actions` slot) opens an inline panel under the library's actions (`LibraryReplacePanel`, in the new `library.panels` slot; both in `features/editor/LibraryReplace.tsx`, so a plugin can replace or drop either). The panel has the editors' shared fields and options (`ui/SearchReplace.tsx`), a tick per kind (cards, lorebooks, presets, notes) with its matches and entries once found, and the preview: every entry with a match (name, kind, matches, "Unsaved changes" when it has some, its first change as struck text and its replacement), each ticked, its fields listed one by one with their own ticks on demand. **Replace N** changes what's left ticked and reports what it skipped, with **Undo**; **Recent replaces** lists the last ten with Undo each. The URL keeps the panel open (`replace=open`) and the text found (`find`). An open editor of a changed entry reads it again (`refreshOpenEditors`).
  - **What's searched** (`@rp/shared/libraryText.ts`, which the editors' own Search and replace now reads too: `features/editor/fields.ts` and `lorebookFields.ts` re-export it). Every live, unarchived card, lorebook, preset and note of the user's, each as its editor shows it: its head with its unsaved changes on it (active `entity_field` drafts through `applyDrafts`), through the fields the editors search (a card's built-in fields, regex scripts and embedded lorebook; a lorebook's name, description and entries; a preset's prompts, prefill, utility prompts and regex scripts; a note's title and content). A chat's own note (its text is per branch, §14.2a) and a note an agent reply wrote are left out. Fields a feature registers in the client's `editorTextFields` only are not searched here. The matcher is the chat's (`db/historyScan.ts`, the VM deadline now a parameter): plain or regular expression, match case, whole word, preserve case.
  - **The reads** (`db/libraryReplace.ts`, reader worker). `PreviewLibraryReplace`: for a plain search, SQL keeps the entries whose saved search text (`entity_revisions.search_text`) could match (`instr` with Match case, ASCII `LIKE` without; a non-ASCII search without Match case reads all), always with entries that have drafts and presets (whose editor adds prompts the head stores elsewhere); the documents are read 100 a statement and scanned a few megabytes at a time, each scan with a 2 s deadline (past it, "The search took too long"). Each entry has a `stamp`, its head, row version and drafts with their row versions. An entry whose drafts can't be saved as they are (a held preset change, a draft with no place, an invalid document) is listed `blocked` with why, and can't be ticked. `PlanLibraryReplace` reads the chosen entries again, skips one whose stamp moved ("It changed since the search"), and works out the documents: the replacements in the ticked fields only, validated, with a regex approval dropped where the replace changed approved scripts (`keepsRegexApproval`).
  - **The write** (`db/libraryReplaceWrites.ts`, writer worker, one synchronous transaction; `api/textSearch.ts` plans in the reader then writes). It rechecks each entry’s head, row version and active drafts. Unsaved entries are skipped, with a reason and an editor link; no drafts are checkpointed or ended. The client also flags pending editor copies from this browser profile (including other tabs, scoped by user) and local open-editor changes before Find and Replace, covering text still waiting for a draft timer or a failed save. The writer still checks server drafts independently. A chosen clean entry gets one `changeset` revision and a `library_edit_items` row naming its before/after revisions and match count, under one changeset group. Identity replacements write nothing. `UndoLibraryEdit` restores the earlier document only while the saved head is the exact replace revision and no active draft exists; changed entries are kept and reported. It restores the prior regex approval exactly, retains current HTML permissions and never grants agent editing. The user’s own library-wide replace preserves existing regex approval even for a material pattern/flag change, and returns each changed script whose approval was retained in `approvedScripts`; the outcome lists those script names and editor links. Unapproved scripts stay unapproved. Workshop replace/rewrite tools, imports, source updates and ordinary revision restoration retain their existing approval checks; this exception lives only in the user replace and its guarded Undo. Both refresh the user’s cache estimates. Baseline: existing `library_edit_items` metadata only.
  - **Time budget** (`test/libraryReplaceScale.test.ts`, server-slow): 2,000 cards of about 8 KB, 40 lorebooks of 300 entries and 50 presets. A word in four cards previews in under 0.5 s; `{{char}}` in every card, entry and preset previews in under 3 s, and replacing it in 2,040 entries takes under 10 s (measured 0.07 s, 0.85 s and 3.2 s, of which the writer's transaction 2.0 s; undo 2.2 s).
  - **Tests.** `test/libraryReplace.test.ts`: counts per kind and a kind left out, the excerpt, only the ticked entries and fields replaced, the revisions and the list of replaces, undo with an entry changed since kept, unsaved changes searched and saved first, an entry changed since its preview left alone, regular expression groups and a bad pattern refused; the isolation suite's probes (another user's entries are never found, replaced or undone, and their replaces never listed); `e2e/libraryReplace.spec.ts` at 1440 and 390 in light and dark: the panel from the button, counts per kind, an entry unticked and kept, Replace, the URL through a reload, Undo from Recent replaces, closing, and the layout audit of the panel with the preview.
- **Regex script editing** (`RegexScripts.tsx`). **Add a script** on a document without scripts (a card has no `regex` until its first) writes the list itself, since a draft naming an element of a list that isn't there has no place and was refused, so the add did nothing (`regexAdd.ts`, `test/regexAdd.test.ts`, and the Extra tab in `e2e/cardEditorTabs.spec.ts`). One form serves every script list: `ScriptFields` takes a binding, either the editor store (a preset's or a card's `regex`, paths `["regex", "id=…", field]`) or a local list. Each script's row has its on/off switch (`disabled`, "Run ⟨name⟩") and a badge saying what it changes (rewrites messages, display only, prompt only, display and prompt, or off); Edit opens the form. It edits the name, the pattern, how macros in the pattern are handled (`substitute_regex`), the replacement, the strings removed from each match (`trim_strings`, one per line), where it applies, ST's two ephemerality flags as "Leave the saved message as it is, and change only: What's shown / The prompt sent" (`markdown_only`, `prompt_only`) with a sentence saying what the combination does, run on edits and the depth range. **Try it** (ST's test mode) runs the script alone on a sample text, whatever its placement, flags and depths, through the display-regex worker queue (`runRegexJob`, §10), never on the page's thread. `DocumentRegexScripts` adds approval: `regex_approved` changes only through `SetRegexApproval`, after a confirmation that lists each saved script's name and pattern. The preset editor renders it directly. Cards get it as the `card.regex` entry of `cardEditorSections` (the slot receives `call`), and their script text is registered in `editorTextFields` for search. The account's global scripts have their own settings page (`features/regex/`, route `settings.regex`), which needs no approval. Its unsaved list is a server user draft. Save sends `SetGlobalRegex` with the revision read from `GetGlobalRegex` (reactivity key `globalRegex`, also signalled to other tabs). A stale revision shows a notice offering to keep the local list on top of the saved one, or to use the saved one. Global scripts are stored in user-scoped `settings` (`regex.global`: the list and a revision; `GlobalScripts` refuses repeated ids and more than 100).
- **Card long-text fields use CodeMirror 6** (`ui/CodeEditor.tsx`, dynamically imported `CodeEditorView.tsx`), including alternate greetings and module content. Single-line fields remain inputs; presets use the same editor with full-height prompt bodies; notes (including snippets), lorebook entry content and message/summary editors also use it; composers retain their existing controls. The reusable editor soft-wraps prose (or a caller-selected monospace font), grows to a bounded height, then scrolls. Its left gutter uses `@codemirror/merge`'s incremental chunks to mark added (+), modified (bar), deleted-here (−), and unchanged (dot) lines against the draft's base revision, including empty final lines created by appended newlines. A change ending at an empty line includes that boundary line only when its base endpoint was inside a line; a base endpoint already at a line start leaves the unchanged suffix unmarked. Every user transaction calls the same `EditorStore` mutation as the textarea did, retaining its immediate browser copy, server drafts and recovery. Controlled echoes leave selection and native field undo intact; external replacements change only the differing span without echoing a new draft, and composition defers replacements until it ends. Every controlled update supersedes the deferred value, including an update matching the current document; only the latest pending replacement is applied, without firing `onChange`. CodeMirror lives in open shadow roots and mounts constructed stylesheets, preserving the strict CSP without inline style elements or a policy exception. Semantic CSS tokens supply fonts, colors, markers and diff highlights in both themes. The editor and diff libraries are lazy chunks, absent from the chat's initial dependency graph.
- **Shared editor highlighting** (`ui/macroHighlight.ts`): the editor feature registers the lazy `editor.macro-highlighting` contribution in `editorExtensions`. Active views reconfigure when a contribution is replaced/disabled; a failed optional import leaves the text editable. CodeMirror caches completed top-level macro nodes before an edit and reparses the suffix in absolute coordinates; a malformed opener prevents reuse past that point. Scoped pairing is recomputed so an edited closer can change an earlier opener. Only visible text receives decorations, and scrolling reuses the parsed document. The semantic `--macro-comment`, `--macro-value` and `--macro-directive` tokens provide muted, low-chroma colors in light/dark themes. All callers of the shared field editor receive highlighting, including its large dialog, without changing draft or undo transactions. A 5,000-line unit fixture verifies prefix reuse and token equivalence.
- **Textarea baseline measured before CodeMirror** (`perf/editor.perf.ts`, part of `npm run test:perf`, load average about 22): a card with a 50 KB description opens in 1.1 s, and typing in it has an input p95 of 48 ms with no frame over 100 ms; a preset with 100 prompts opens in 1.1 s, and toggling, moving and typing have an input p95 of 72 to 104 ms over two runs (a toggle re-renders the 100 rows) with no frame over 100 ms. The budgets are the chat's: 250 ms input p95, 3 frames over 100 ms, 8 s to open.
- `test/codeEditor.test.ts` covers line markers with full and incremental comparisons, including appended empty lines and insertions before existing interior or final blank lines. `e2e/codeEditorComposition.spec.ts` mounts the real editor through an isolated Vite harness and covers successive controlled updates during composition, including a return to the composing document, with no external-change echo.
- `e2e/editor.spec.ts` covers edit and save with the diff, undo, history restore, a card fork with unsaved changes, reordering by drag and keyboard, the regex approval, search and replace with a stopped pattern, and the update resolver; `layout.spec.ts` checks the card editor's layout and `csp.spec.ts` the avatar and the search worker under the CSP.
- **Sources**: `features/cardSources/` lists where a card came from, read-only (CCv3 `source` is only appended to). `cardSources(doc)` is pure: it runs every enabled recognizer in `sourceRecognizers` (a client registry; a plugin adds, overrides or disables one by id), keeps the http(s) links they return, de-duplicated by URL (any other scheme never links), then lists the `source` entries no recognizer claimed (a recognizer claims one by naming it as a link's `from`): URLs as plain links named by their host, anything else as an id shown as text. A recognizer that throws drops only its own links. The built-ins: Chub (`extensions.chub.full_path` → `https://chub.ai/characters/<full_path>` and the creator's `https://chub.ai/users/<creator>`; `chub.ai` and `characterhub.org` character and lorebook URLs in `source` normalized to `chub.ai`), RisuRealm (`realm.risuai.net` URLs, with RisuAI's `extensions.risuai.source` entries read as sources too), and JanitorAI, JannyAI, Pygmalion, AI Character Cards and Perchance by host. `CardSources({ doc })` renders the list: each link opens in a new tab, with a tooltip saying where it goes; "No sources recorded" when empty. `test/cardSources.test.ts` covers each recognizer, de-duplication, plain links and ids, a plugin recognizer, a disabled one and a throwing one.

**Remaining editor limits:** there is no per-card-field agent-edit permission control or avatar-removal control. Per-chat prompt-preset overrides were rejected (DESIGN §6.1); cards use fork and swap, and lorebook selections/switches are chat state (§12), with no separate chat-local lorebook document editor. Card-family comparison is built: its picker compares this card’s saved content with another available member of its family (`features/cardForks/surfacesImpl.tsx`); it does not compare unsaved drafts or arbitrary unrelated cards.

---

## 15. Context assembly

`packages/server/src/assembler/` (DESIGN §5, DATA-MODEL §7.1). It turns a version being generated into a provider-neutral request (Chat Completions' messages, with names, plus ST's sampler values) and a record of where every piece of it came from, for the run inspector (DESIGN §7.4).

**The pipeline** (`pipeline.ts`, PLUGINS §8). Stages are registered by id in a stage registry (§6's generic registry) and run in registration order over one `Assembly`; a plugin overrides a stage by its id, wraps one by `get`ting it first, or disables one. The built-ins (`stages.ts`) register the same way:
- `path`: the version being generated, its slot and the slot before it
- `state`: the events on the path to that slot, folded (§3.8)
- `cast`: participants and the "played by me" set, each card through its layers; the speaker (the version's, else the first character not muted, else none); the generation type ST's presets name (`normal`, `swipe` for a new version of a reply, `impersonate` for a character the user plays)
- `model`: the account's current connection/model pair; summary retry/fallback jobs can explicitly override their request's model
- `preset`: the account's current prompt preset, else the built-in preset named Default
- `notes`: the chat's own notes and the cast cards' that are on, a linked slot with its shared note's head
- `mode`: the chat's role projection, its "only below the history" lorebook setting and its "HTML in older messages sent to the model" (`htmlDepth`, below); a `layout.cards` event on the path is ignored, with one `layout_ignored` issue
- `lorebooks`: attached refs through their current heads, the preset's enabled books the chat hasn't attached, and participant cards’ embedded books; the scan depth history must supply
- `knowledge`: the chat's context view (`context.per_speaker`, resolved against `assembler.contextViews`) and the card whose knowledge filters the history (§3.8 "Separate contexts")
- `lcm`: the selected summary layer and cursor, when enabled (§16); with a `knowledge` viewer, that viewer's own layer (§3.8 "Summaries kept per view"); a source without views withholds it, with `summaries_withheld`, where it covers a message the viewer wasn't present for
- `macros`: the expander for preset and card text
- `scripts`: the prompt regex scripts of every registered list (global, preset, character), compiled (below); for a rewrite (§12, "Rewrites"), the scripts with neither flag
- `text-tokens`: prepares the selected model's local tokenizer, with bounded reuse of fragment counts
- `history`: the previous recorded start, pinned, and windows of the path, newest first, until the text read, as the regex scripts leave it, would fill the budget on its own; in a separate context each window's messages the viewer doesn't know are marked `unknown` and out of the context first, so they never count
- `resolve`: the path's messages resolved, and given to the macros that read the chat
- `image-tokens`: each resolved image's token estimate for the model (`assembler/imageTokens.ts`; "Image tokens" below)
- `roles`: role projection (DESIGN §5.4). It dispatches to the projection the chat names, from the assembler's own projection registry (`assembler.projections`, `RoleProjection` in `pipeline.ts`: `id`, `label`, `role(message)`); `by_writer`, `alternate` and `perspective` are registered by `registerBuiltinProjections`. `roles.projection` stores an open string (the legacy ids stay valid) and is resolved at use: an id nothing registers (a plugin off or removed) assembles by writer and records a `role_projection_missing` issue, and the chat's settings show the id as "not installed" instead of dropping it.
