The Roles picker reads the worker registry's current labels and descriptions through `GetCast.roleProjections`; plugin projections are selectable and disabled built-ins disappear. A plugin registers, overrides or disables a projection in a scope like any registry entry.
- `merge-layout`: where a merged chat's section and join marker are sent (§12 "Merging another chat into this one"): the chat's `merge.layout`, resolved against `assembler.mergeLayouts`; a chat without a merge in its history passes through unchanged. Agent replies (`request.agent`) go through it like any reply, and `RebuildContext` replays it from the pinned state, so a rebuild keeps the layout the context was built with.
- `gap-lines`: in a separate context, a system line without a name where the speaker missed a stretch between messages it was present for, and the optional join line at a merge it was never in (§3.8 "Gap lines"); without a viewer it passes through unchanged
- `note-gate`: condition gating (on the turn of any of its cards, while any of them isn't muted), before any injections
- `lore-scan`: prompt regex scripts on resolved templates, reused during composition
- `lore-activation`: resolved scan inputs, keyword matching, issues and activation/skip source tags
- `context.htmlDepth`: older messages' HTML as the chat chose (§12 "HTML in older messages sent to the model"); as written, it changes nothing
- `end-of-request`: prepares the end-of-request renderer (below, "Who writes, and the direction"); `compose` expands it after other text and before prefill, budgets it, and `messages` sends it last
- `compose`: ST's prompt manager and budget, with the tail content and the prefill
- `messages`: squashing and post-processing, with the end-of-request message last, and the one fallback
- `breakpoints` (below), `request`, `images` (the request’s omitted images and rule reasons, §12)

**Image tokens** (DESIGN §10.2a; formulas, counts and calibration in §6). The `image-tokens` stage, after `resolve`, writes an `estimate` on every image of the history read (`RequestImage.estimate`: tokens or null, basis, detail, note, a bound, and `sent: false` for one left out). Images also carry their media's `sha256`, `width` and `height`, read with the history (`media_assets` columns; `describeImage` now reads PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP and AVIF headers at upload, so new images have their size). It reads `AssemblySources.imageTokenFacts` (the stored counts for the model and its calibration samples; pinned in `SourcePins.imageTokenFacts`, so `RebuildContext` estimates as the snapshot did, and an older snapshot by formula alone) and the rules in the assembler's `imageTokens` registry (`Assembler.imageTokens`, passed to stages on `AssemblyRequest.imageTokens` like the macros and projections). Rules are tried newest registration first: a plugin or assembly module adds, overrides or disables one; the stage itself can be replaced like any stage. Initially newest first, images past the model's `maxImages` (four when unknown) and images carrying the fork's `excluded` flag are marked unsent: history is cut from its oldest end, so the newest N read are the newest N sent, as dispatch selects them. Composition re-evaluates the cap in the actual request order with the same `newestImages` helper as dispatch, including when a preset moves Newest message before History. The budget uses those final-order figures and the outer cut admits the complete candidate; an inner chronological cut cannot silently remove a turn whose image the final cap leaves out. A moved-Newest image layout uses an ordered suffix scan because its image costs need not decrease monotonically. Post-processing preserves image estimates when it merges messages.
- `tokensOf` counts a message's sent images: the figure, else the rule's bound, else a reserve of 1,024 for an unknown image (never zero). History chat lines carry their entry's images, so the history cut, the fixed-part check, the target and maximum, `fitSummaryOutput` for summary requests, the LCM prefix sizes, the cache-effect estimate (`prefixChange`, which takes a captured wire message's images from its inputs) and the inspector all count them.
- `GetNextContext` and the published cache estimate carry `imageTokens` (count, tokens as budgeted, how many are unknown, the bases). The client shows it above the composer through the `chat.composer-notes` slot (`composer.image-tokens`, `features/chat/imageTokens.tsx`), and each message's images in the context view.

**First run** (`features/firstRun/`, registered from `features/index.ts`). The home screen has a `home.intro` slot (`features/characters/homeSlots.ts`, above the pinned chats); `first-run.steps` (`FirstRunSteps.tsx`) shows three steps, each ticked when done: **Connect a model** (done once the account has a default model; with connections but none chosen it reads **Choose a model** and links to Settings → Chats), **Import from SillyTavern** (done with any character) and **Start a chat** (done with any chat). It shows while any step is undone and disappears when all are. While the library is empty and an intro entry is registered, the intro stands in for the grid: the filters, search and sort, with nothing to work on, aren't shown, nor the grid's "No characters here" empty state. A composer with no model says so instead of letting a send fail: `first-run.no-model` in `chat.composer-notes` shows "No model chosen · Choose" over an open chat whose `NextContext.model` is null (no model named by the chat or the account), and the same note is a `notes`-placement entry of `pendingComposerControls` in a chat not started yet (the account's default only; `notes` is a row of its own above that composer, so the note never narrows the speaker or the message box). **Choose** opens a list of the user's models; picking one sets the account default. `e2e/firstRun.spec.ts` covers the steps, a new connection's fetch and default, a second connection leaving the default alone, and both composers.
- A reply fails with a `budget` error if its newest eligible message would be cut entirely; the error names its images, their budgeted token count and the history limit. A summary request likewise fails if any of its declared chunk would be cut, preventing an image from disappearing before summary admission. Images missing an estimate use the unknown reserve rather than zero.
- LCM leaf planning reads owner-scoped attachment hashes/dimensions with the path and estimates them for the summarizer through the same registered rules and stored facts, excluding images taken out in that fork. Its chunk sizes and recent-window trigger count image tokens; planning conservatively counts every image in a candidate chunk, while dispatch and request admission apply the model's last-N cap.
- Draft uploads use the same worker-installed registered formula rules, stored counts and calibration in the reader's preview, respecting the combined history/draft last-N limit. Drafts do not enter the generation snapshot until sent.
- Tests: `test/imageTokenCounts.test.ts` (shared serialization, cross-connection deduplication, persistent cache recheck and timeout/backoff), `e2e/imageTokens.spec.ts` (draft add/remove and inspector at 1440/390, light/dark), `test/imageTokens.test.ts` (each formula against the providers' documented examples, header sizes, the counting endpoints with a fake fetch, calibration), `test/imageTokenBudget.test.ts` (an expensive image moves the history's start; last-N; unknown at the reserve; summary output), `test/imageTokenEstimates.test.ts` (through the server with a mock provider: formula in the snapshot, context view and next context; ledger calibration of an unknown model; one background count with Anthropic's endpoint, used afterwards, never published).

Stages reach data only through `AssemblySources`, so the same pipeline runs over the database (`db/assemblySources.ts`) and over in-memory fixtures (`test/support/assemblySources.ts`, used by the tests and the ST harness). A stage that runs before what it needs throws (`need`): only a misregistered stage can cause it. `AssemblyFailed` (`no_model`, `budget`, `invalid_document`) is the one way a context fails as a whole.

**Final transforms** (`pipeline.ts`, `assembler.ts`). After the stages produce the snapshot, assembly runs the `transforms` registry in registration order. An `AssemblyTransform` receives the source-indexed snapshot and the original `AssemblyRequest`, and returns an effectful snapshot. It uses the same scoped register/override/wrap/disable contract as stages. Job metadata is present on the request before stages execute and on the snapshot before transforms execute. `summary-request` (`lcm/request.ts`) is the registered default for instruction rendering, direct/tool suffixes, output allowance, pinned-prefix application and raw/full request shaping. It does nothing for ordinary reply assembly. Replacing it controls the actual summary request; disabling it leaves the ordinary quiet assembly without those additions. `merge-sections` follows it: a summary request whose material holds a merged chat's join asks for one section per line (§12 "Merging another chat into this one"). Additional transforms can follow it. There is no summary-specific request-shaping pass after registered assembly; worker checks still enforce owned jobs, declared rendered inputs and the model’s output budget.

**Where it runs.** In a reader worker: `AssembleContext` (`db/assemblyReads.ts`) reads and assembles in one read transaction, so the context sees one snapshot of the database. It reads the path in one fork (`forkId`, else the fork through the slot, §3.8): the versions that fork shows, the events attached to them, and its summaries' freshness. The main thread gets two JSON strings: the snapshot, which it only passes on to be stored, and what generating needs of it (`Generation`: the request, the model, the variable writes, the values template messages drew, and the inspector's display metadata), which it parses. Each reader constructs one scoped `WorkerAssembler` service and shares it across context/rebuild, summary planning/execution and backfill-estimate handlers. Its stages, macros, projections and final transforms share the same registry objects for the reader’s life; trusted request modules (§15, Assembly modules in readers) install scoped registrations into those objects. Handlers do not construct private assemblers. Measured on a synthetic 100,000-message chat (source workers, load 13 to 15):
- with ST's default budget (4,095 tokens): 13 ms
- with one state event in the chat: 220 to 380 ms, all of it the walk to the root every state read made before chains (§3.8). `test/historyPerf.test.ts`'s 100,000-message assembly took 152 ms before chains and 46 ms after, on the same host (load about 1)
- with a 200,000-token preset: 1,662 messages, 250 to 340 ms, and a 2 MB result parsed on the main thread in 5 to 12 ms

The pipeline itself took 5 to 13 ms of that, measured alone on 2,000 messages.

**The sources over the database**, each the acting user's (another user's chat or version is `NotFound`, `test/assemblyStorage.test.ts`):
- **Cards** (DESIGN §4): a `card.binding` revision, else the card’s single upstream head. A card in the bin is left out; one whose document no longer decodes as a card fails the context (`invalid_document`), never silently replaced.
- **Notes:** the notes whose upstream head names the chat, or a participant card or a persona of the cast, as owner, at the revision `note.binding` pins. A card's note with `on_by_default` (an imported Character's Note, which ST always sends, or one the user marked "On in every chat") is on unless the chat turns it off (`note.deactivate`); any other note, the chat's own included, is off until `note.activate` (DESIGN §4.1: not activated in other chats automatically). A linked slot reads its shared note's resolved revision (`sharedHead`: the upstream head for globals, the fork binding for scoped snippets), pinned with the slot for a rebuild; a shared note in the bin pins as none, and the slot sends nothing.
- **The current prompt preset:** a chat's `preset.binding` when locked, otherwise the account's `generation.preset`, else the built-in preset named Default. `preset.unbind` returns to the account selection. A connection lock changes the account selection when switching connections, rather than imposing a persistent assembly override.
- **The model:** what assembly needs (kind, wire API, key, prefill and breakpoint capabilities, a context size some source reported, its model-specific settings), merged by `resolveModel` (§3.12).

**Macros by source** (`macros.ts`, §10's caller contract). Every piece is expanded on its own through `expand()`:
- preset and card text always, card fields as ST's baseChatReplace does (trimmed, without card-field macros); notes count as card text
- a message of the path only when its mode is `template`, against the state before its own events (the cast, `{{user}}` and `{{char}}`, the card fields and the variables as they were there, so a later join, leave or pinned binding doesn't rewrite it) and the resolved text of the messages before it. Until a template's variable writes are recorded (no rollout `var.set` event of its version yet; `frozen_macros` can't tell, since a chat freezes its greetings when it's made), they're kept: they count for the pieces after it, as if at its position, and the generation records them there (below); after that they're state events, and expanding it again writes nothing
- each piece's random and time draws are kept by piece id (`preset:main`, `card:<entity>:description`, `message:<version>`), over a message's stored `frozen_macros`; passing them back builds the same context
- variable writes from preset and card text come back in order as the snapshot's `effects`, and each piece sees the variables the pieces before it left
- a piece that reaches a macro limit is left out and reported, not the whole turn
- messages the history didn't read still count for the macros that number messages (`{{lastMessageId}}`), as placeholders

**The one assembly path** (`st.ts`, `stages.ts`; DESIGN §1.2, §5.0). Every chat is assembled the same way, whatever its number of characters: the preset's order says where the cards go (below), and what ST 1.19 would send for one character, persona, preset and chat, with the join wrapper empty and lorebook entries by position, is what's sent here, with the deliberate differences below. There's no hidden mode. ST behaviour that depends on what the chat observably holds stays: with more than one character, names are prefixed by ST's group rule, `new_group_chat_prompt` replaces `new_chat_prompt`, and the user-played speaker's card has no prompt overrides; every persona of the cast is read. The group nudge and impersonation prompt are end-of-request texts of the preset (§9 "Conditioned prompts"; "Who writes, and the direction" below), whatever the cast size. History uses the same stepped cuts everywhere. `st.ts` follows ST's functions one by one (named in its comments):
- the prompt collection: the order's enabled prompts whose condition holds and whose triggers allow the generation type (§9 "Conditioned prompts"), with a disabled `main` kept empty; the end-of-request texts are never among them. A missing `newestMessage` marker in an older revision is resolved immediately after history. Composition budgets the complete history with its injections before moving the newest admitted history message and following depth-zero injections into that marker's slot. Adjacent history/newest slots preserve imported ST ordering; moving newest after the tail deliberately changes it
- markers filled where the order has them, and appended where it hasn't
- the speaker's card prompt override and post-history instructions in place of `main` and `jailbreak`, unless the prompt forbids it or is off (below)
- in-chat prompts and notes injected by depth, then order, then role
- the budget: all consumers count toward the thresholds below. With `pin_examples` on, whole example blocks are admitted before history; off, history takes priority and examples use the remaining room. Admitted examples are retained until a history cut or configuration change, so a held start does not re-admit examples and rewrite the prefix. With `strip_examples` on, neither card nor lorebook example dialogues are sent, even with pinning on; direct uses of example-text macros remain text. `collapse_newlines` follows ST’s `baseChatReplace`: repeated newlines in expanded character fields and lorebook examples become one, then carriage returns are removed. Preset prompts and saved history keep their blank lines; persona descriptions are card fields and follow the switch too. Lore entries forced below history remain ordinary lore text, rather than example dialogues. The source pieces record the transformed text for the inspector.
- squashing, post-processing, names behavior, impersonation and swipes

The request maps to Chat Completions per provider kind as ST maps its sources (`wire.ts`): ST's custom source for OpenAI-compatible connections, OpenRouter's extra samplers, DeepSeek's non-zero `top_p`, a seed only when set, and ST's rules for models that refuse some samplers (OpenAI's o-series, GPT-5 and GPT-6 Astra take `max_completion_tokens`; Claude's newest take no samplers, and its limited ones temperature or `top_p`).

**The fidelity gate** (`npm run test:st`, §7). Since 2026-11-01 the gate gives ST the lorebook as ST's own World Info file, its author's-note entries at positions 2 and 3 (`stWorldFile`), and our side places them, the persona and the character's note as our import does (`authorNotePlace`, `placeAuthorNoteEntries`); the lines that differ for it are a documented difference ("what ST puts at the author's note's top or bottom goes where ST's default author's note is"). A synthetic lorebook adds four captures across both cards and the default/full presets: keyword, AND ALL, NOT ANY, constant, two depth roles, author-note top/bottom and example top/bottom entries. ST must actually send the keyword entry, so equal empty results cannot pass. Two synthetic cards: one with a prompt override, post-history instructions, two example blocks and a Character's Note in the user's role; one with none of these and no personality. Each has its chat and the fixture persona, and is captured under ST's fresh settings, the three fixture presets, the poison preset, the `full` preset with each of ST's four post-processing modes, ST's impersonate and swipe on two presets, a Summarize extension summary after the main prompt, before it, and in-chat at the Character's Note's depth and role (saved on the chat's second message, with the extension's settings, and read as ST reads it when a chat opens; the harness checks ST sent it), and an author's note (set in the chat's metadata, read the same way): in-chat at the Character's Note's depth and role, after the main prompt, before it with the summary there too, and in-chat every second message of the user's, which one chat reaches with the message sent and the other doesn't (the harness checks ST sent it in one and not the other); an empty send with the full preset counts its filler toward interval 2, and notes after main as user and before main as assistant retain those roles on both cards. The gate also covers a summary template writing a variable read by the author's note, interval-2 impersonation, and skipped section and depth-zero notes under squashing and impersonation. Our side imports the card through our importer, and the settings ST had in force through our preset importer, with the card join wrapper set empty (ST's single-character output) and lorebook entries by position (`lorebook.below_history` off). The persona's placement is imported as ST folders import it (`buildPersona`), and ST's page is set to the same position, depth and role. The gate's persona cases: the description at the top and at the bottom of the author's note, in-chat, after the main prompt as the user and before it as the assistant, with ST's default note when the chat has none, with the lore at the note's top and bottom, with the note switched off or not due (nothing sent), and the persona at depth and not sent. The author's note is parsed and mapped through the real chat/default-settings importer. Empty chat and default notes cover depth 0 as user, after main as user, before main as assistant, frequency 0 and frequency 99, with personas at both sides and lore. An active nonempty note edited to frequency 0 also suppresses both attachments. The harness checks that ST sent the description (or not) as each case says. The first chat has a reply that the `full` preset's prompt-only regex script strips, and the harness approves the presets' scripts on both sides. Results (2026-10-13): 142 of 142 requests equal, apart from the documented differences (62 before the persona cases, which add 36; empty-note and active-zero regressions add 44); checked against breakage, squashing with a blank line instead of ST's newline made 14 of the 26 differ, and putting the author's note after the Character's Note and sending a note on every turn whatever its interval each made one of the author's note's requests differ. Since notes dropped insertion frequency (DESIGN §4.1), the interval and frequency-0 cases are documented differences, and an `allowWIScan` case keys a lorebook entry only on the author's note's text, which ST must trigger. Results (2026-10-27, unit P1-2): 140 of 144 requests equal apart from the documented differences; the other 4 (an impersonation's last-turn filler and its prompt order, and the legacy preset's `[Stay in character.]` after the group nudge) come from unit P1-1 and appear on the merge before P1-2 too; that run predates the one assembly path too. Results (2026-10-28, fb-gate, master plus fb-rp, fb-notes, fb-sum): 144 of 144 requests equal apart from the documented differences. Before the structural matchers, 6 differed: the closing user turn on impersonation, the nudge shifting later messages (legacy preset), and the speaking card's override and post-history instruction on an impersonation (owner: the persona has none). The other sections (fixtures, macros, preset round trips, preview overlap) were equal apart from the macro deviations. Results (2026-10-30, w1, the end-of-request instruction): 168 of 168 requests equal apart from the documented differences, the other sections the same; before the gate took the end-of-request texts off a message ST's "single" post-processing had named (`Tobin: […]`), and before the impersonation-override matcher covered the preset's own post-history prompt left at the end once ST's replacement is taken out, 3 differed.

Reference captures disable only PromptManager’s automatic `tryGenerate()` preview call before page initialization. In ST 1.19.0, previews and real sends mutate the same author-note buffer while awaiting lore activation; overlap can append lore twice. The real generation path and strict request comparator are unchanged. A deterministic regression runs the actual ST reset/await/append sequence: its unprotected control must duplicate both adjacent lore entries, and the protected capture must send each once. A unit scheduling test covers the same interleaving; a changed pinned preview call site fails capture rather than silently weakening isolation.

**Deliberate differences from ST.** The gate lists each documented difference it sees apart, without failing:
- "Stream": we always stream; ST sends the preset's `stream_openai`. A person watches the reply (PROVIDERS §7.2).
- "End-of-request instruction" (DESIGN §2.2, owner 2026-10-29): we send one user message last, the speaker's turn text (the group nudge whenever the model writes as a character, one or many; the impersonation prompt when it writes as the persona) and the direction; ST sends the nudge only in groups, at its prompt position, and the impersonation prompt at its marker, last. The gate takes our texts off the end of our request (a message of its own, or the end of the user message a merging post-processing mode joined it to) and the same impersonation text off the end of ST's, before diffing, so later messages aren't reported as shifted (`dropEndOfRequest` in `test/st/assembly.ts`).
- "Impersonation override": on an impersonation turn the speaking card's prompt override and post-history instructions apply (owner, §2: impersonating the persona, none); ST applies the chat character's. The gate documents the line where the character's override text is missing from our system prompt, and takes the character's post-history instruction out of ST's request when we send none, or, where ST's replaces the preset's own post-history prompt, documents the line.
- "`{{char}}` in groups" (DESIGN §5.3): in preset text `{{char}}` is every character in the chat but the persona, comma-joined, whoever speaks; ST uses the current speaker in a group. The gate's chats have one character, where both are its name, so it's listed and not compared.
- "Name wrappers" and "one-character mode": ST sends a lone character's fields bare and wraps them only when it joins a group's. Here there is never only one character (`{{user}}` is a cast card, DESIGN §5.0), so that mode is removed: every cast card's definitions, the persona's included, are wrapped `<Name>…</Name>`, in the per-field markers and at the Definitions marker. The gate sets our join wrapper empty (ST's single-character output), so the wrappers are documented here and not compared.
- "Summaries as blocks": summaries are separate blocks placed like the history, usually just before it, so a new summary never invalidates the earlier ones (PHASE1-DECISIONS §2); ST sends one monolithic summary at its position. The gate's summary cases import ST's summary as one note at ST's position and compare equal; summaries made here aren't compared.
- "n": no multi-swipe requests; ST sends a preset's `n` above 1. DESIGN §3.1: "There's no dedicated 'generate ×N' action".
- "send_if_empty": expanded like all preset text when it fills the user's turn; ST sends it as written before an impersonation. After a reply with an empty composer, ST sends it as a new user message that it stores in the chat; here it's in the context only.
- "Macros expand once": ST expands a card field, then the marker prompt holding it again (`preparePrompt`), and extension prompts again when it joins them (`getExtensionPrompt`), so text a macro produced, or an escaped `\{\{`, expands the second time. Here a macro's output is never expanded again (§10).
- "Chat messages verbatim": ST runs every message through its macros when it builds the prompt and when the user sends one; here typed and generated text stays as written unless the message is a template (DESIGN §5.6: "Text the user types is not macro-expanded by default", "Model output is not macro-substituted by default").
- "History cuts": once the maximum is crossed, history drops to the target instead of ST’s moving maximum cut. The assembly gate adds two synthetic overflow captures and requires fewer retained history turns than ST; existing below-maximum cases still compare equal.
- "Token counts" (tokencut, 2026-11-07): history window reads, composition (fixed prompts, notes, examples, summaries and raw history), continuation and schema-input reserves and cache-prefix/suffix estimates use the selected model's local tokenizer. The registered `text-tokens` stage prepares `TextTokenCounter.prepare` after scripts and before reading history; newest local registrations win. `prepareTokenizer` shares the encoders used by batch/display counting. Unknown models use local `o200k_base`; a tokenizer that fails falls back to the character estimate. No fitting or cache estimate contacts a provider. Each preparation memoizes repeated fragments within 4,000,000 characters and 20,000 entries, so binary fitting probes reuse counts without retaining an unbounded chat. Three-token message framing and image estimates remain approximate. Schema-prefill output reserves retain the wire adapter's existing allocation, so the sent response limit matches its budget. The historical inspector and `NextContext.budget.countedInput` still use `db/textDisplay.ts` and its per-model calibration; historical display counts only use samples completed by the snapshot's build time. Preset marker counts, lore activation allowances and stored LCM planning sizes retain their existing estimates. Cache estimates prepare the previous and next models separately, use the next model for changed wire suffixes, and retain existing image costs, TTLs and provider cache rules. Assembler version 54. `test/tokenCut.test.ts` covers model-family fitting, dense Unicode versus repeated text, multi-window reads, prefix/suffix counts, schema reserves, registry replacement, memoization and local failure/fallback. The budget remains the preset's context size clamped to the model, less its response length; tokenizer counts do not make provider framing exact.
- "Fixed prompts over budget": ST shows an error and sends what it had built before the overflow; here the generation fails, saying the preset's prompts don't fit (`budget`).
- "Prefill": sent to any model whose prefill capability is `assistant`, and otherwise dropped and reported (DESIGN §1.2); ST sends it only for its Claude source and ignores it elsewhere. A prefill that's sent comes out of the budget; ST doesn't count it, so it can send more than the preset's context size.
- "Post-processing": the preset's `postprocess` always applies; in ST it's a connection setting, which a preset changes only when it's bound to the connection.
- "Reasoning and stops": ST's `reasoning_effort` and `verbosity` for the OpenAI models it lists aren't sent, nor its custom stop strings and logit-bias presets.
- "Card overrides": the speaker's card's, in every chat (ST's group generation takes the speaker's too). ST expands a card's prompt override twice, the second time with `{{original}}`; here it's expanded once, in ST's order (before the preset's prompts), and its first `{{original}}` then becomes the prompt it replaces.
- "Regex scripts": a script's replacement is expanded before the match is put into it, so text it captures from a message isn't expanded (ST expands after, per match: a random macro in it draws once here). Their pattern, replacement and trim strings are expanded before the path is read, since the scripts decide how far back it's read: macros in them that read the chat (`{{lastMessage}}`) find it empty. A case-insensitive pattern matches both cases of ASCII letters only, and `u` is dropped where nothing in the pattern needs it. Scripts whose pattern expands macros escaped (`substituteRegex` 2), or that need backtracking, are left out and reported (below).
- "Several notes at one depth": joined in the order above, by note id within each group; ST joins its extension prompts in key order. The summary comes first, as ST's `1_memory`, and the chat's notes (an imported author's note among them) before the cards', as `2_floating_prompt` sorts before `DEPTH_PROMPT`.
- "Author's note": a note goes every turn (DESIGN §4.1: no insertion frequency), so ST's author's note at frequency 2 or more, which ST skips on some turns, differs on those turns; a frequency-0 note imports off. Nothing rides on a note (owner, 2026-11-01): what ST joins around its author's note's text (a persona at its top or bottom, a character's own author's note, World Info before or after it) is at the default author's note's depth and role (§13), joined there in the order above, after the chat's notes and before lore, and in a chat whose author's note is elsewhere it's not at that note; with an empty or switched-off author's note, ST's blank line between what's above and below it isn't there. ST's per-character author's note is a card note there, never replacing or prefixing ST's floating prompt text.
- "Summaries": the summary's template is expanded once, with the summary in place of `{{summary}}`; ST expands it, then the whole prompt again, which only shows when a macro in it draws or writes. An in-prompt summary keeps its imported role (system when absent), as other section notes do (§13). `{{summary}}` is explicit (DESIGN §8 [D], owner 2026-10-28): it reads the chat's switched-on summary notes (kind `imported_summary`) on the path that are due by their condition (a summary note's condition is checked here as the note gate checks it later), in note order, joined with blank lines, and is empty when none is on; it never reads the LCM layer, whose summaries are separate messages before history (§16). A switched-off note sends nothing anywhere. ST leaves the macro as written when the extension is off. What it fills in is recorded on the snapshot (`summaryFill`: the preset prompts holding it, notes or none, their count and tokens) and projected into `PresetContext.summary`, which the preset editor's badge and the Notes tab read.
- U20 text/context switches are compared against ST 1.19 in all eight combinations, with multiline card fields/examples, plus pinned and unpinned cases over the context maximum and card fields read through preset macros with collapse on and off. The registered field macros receive the preset's newline switch through the macro context, so `{{persona}}`, `{{mesExamples}}`, greetings and other field macros follow the same expand/collapse/remove-carriage-returns order as field markers; surrounding prompt text and the unexpanded character version retain their newlines. `ST_DIFF_ONLY=assembly ST_DIFF_TEXT_SWITCHES=1 npm run test:st` runs that subset. The overflow cases compare the fixed prefix and independently assert example presence on both sides; different history cuts remain the documented stepped-history difference. Unit regressions live in `presetTextSwitches.test.ts` and the shared macro tests; `e2e/presetTextSwitches.spec.ts` covers draft/revision persistence and 1440/390 light/dark views.
- Regex scripts that rewrite stored text (neither flag) are compared on their own, against ST's `getRegexedString` (§7, "Regex scripts on text as it's written"); the assembly gate's chats are stored ST chats, already rewritten. Continue and notes/card modules are implemented separately; their current behavior is documented above.

**Card definitions** (DESIGN §5.0, §5.2; `stages.ts` `composeStage`, `layouts.ts`), filled the way the preset says, never per chat:
- **Per-field markers** (`charDescription`, `charPersonality`, `scenario`, and `{{description}}`, `{{personality}}`, `{{scenario}}` in preset text) are filled as ST's group join fills them (`getGroupCharacterCardsLazy`): each character's trimmed field, expanded with `{{char}}` bound to that character, is wrapped in the preset's `utility_prompts.card_join_prefix` and `card_join_suffix` (absent: `<{{char}}>\n` and `\n</{{char}}>`; `{{char}}` that character, `<FIELDNAME>` `Description`, `Personality` or `Scenario`), empty fields are skipped, and the parts are joined with newlines in cast order, muted members included (DESIGN §3.5). `personality_format` and `scenario_format` apply to the joined text, as the macros read it. A card's notes placed with the definitions (`after_main_prompt`, and older notes' `section: card`) go at the top of their card's description part, inside its wrapper. The macros read the joined fields without notes, already expanded, so their macros never expand again (`CardFields.joined`). Template messages read the first character's fields, as before. ST imports get the default wrapper; the fidelity gate sets it empty, which is ST's single-character output.
- **`personaDescription`:** each persona's description, with its notes placed with the definitions at the top, wrapped like the characters' parts (`<Tobin>…</Tobin>` by default) for the one selected persona (DESIGN §5.0: there is never only one character, `{{user}}` is a cast card; ST sends one persona bare, a documented difference the gate's empty wrapper hides).
- **The Definitions marker** (`charDefinitions`, `@rp/shared/presetOrder.ts`, `layouts.ts`): each character whole (its notes placed with the definitions, description, personality, scenario, joined with blank lines), then each persona (its notes so placed, its description), each wrapped in the preset's join prefix and suffix like the per-field parts (`<Mira>…</Mira>` by default, `<FIELDNAME>` `Definitions`), joined with blank lines; a card with nothing to send is left out. It's never added to an existing order; the preset editor inserts it. When the order sends it, the per-field markers and `personaDescription` stay empty.
- **Examples** keep their handling: each character's parsed into example chats, names prefixed with more than one character.
- **Card prompt overrides** (DESIGN §5.0): the speaker's card's `system_prompt` and `post_history_instructions` replace `main` and `jailbreak`, as ST's group generation takes them, on impersonation turns too (owner 2026-10-28; ST passes the character's prompts for every generation type): a card the user plays applies its own, and a persona without them has none. An empty override does nothing, a prompt that forbids overrides or is off is kept, and the first `{{original}}` becomes the replaced text. Each decision is recorded in the snapshot's `cardOverrides` (replaced, forbidden, disabled, missing), which the preset editor shows at the prompt through `PresetContext.overrides` ("Replaced in this chat by Aria's system prompt", "Aria has a system prompt; this prompt forbids it", "A card can't replace it"). The card editor's prompt fields say whether their text is used in the preset chats use now (`GetCardPromptUse`, a reader op reading the preset's `main`/`jailbreak` flags, no assembly). The built-in Default preset forbids overrides on `main` and `jailbreak` (`forbidCardOverrides`), and prompts the preset editor inserts forbid them; imported ST presets keep their file's value, and the import report lists the prompts a card can replace (`preset.overrides_allowed`).
- **Card layout is never per chat:** `layout.cards` events still parse (old events), but assembly ignores them and says so once per context. The card-filling code stays split by card (`cardBlock`, the per-card parts), so the card-swap reply mode sends only the speaker's part (§16, "Agent rollouts").
- **Prompt-name controls** (DESIGN §5.3; backlog U09): This chat → **Advanced: names in prompts** (collapsed) is the registered `settings.macro-bindings` contribution to `chatSettingSections`. It shows the next prompt’s `{{user}}` and `{{char}}` names ("Your name in prompts", "The character's name in prompts"), using in-chat model names, and whether each follows the persona or cast or is kept as set. **Keep this name** pins the current value or an explicit override (including empty text); **Follow the persona again** / **Follow the cast again** unpins, resuming the live cast/persona set. `GetCast` returns `macroBindings` and resolved `macroNames`; `ChangeCast(MacroBinding)` records `macro.binding` or `macro.unbind` through the existing ownership-checked writer operation, at the viewed fork and leaf, publishing `State`. Unbind removes just that map entry. Pins are independent of the turn’s speaker; card-local expansion rules remain the same. The control explains, in plain words, the scope and that the next reply re-reads the whole prompt. After a successful save, the session rereads the current cast while its fork and leaf are still displayed, rather than applying the save’s potentially older snapshot. Cast reads reject superseded results and results for a moved or disposed view; a failed save leaves in-flight reads valid. `client/test/session.test.ts` covers navigation, overlapping pin responses and failed saves. Tests cover the reducer, assembly with three speakers, nickname resolution, fork isolation and the browser controls across reload/persona changes (`shared/test/state.test.ts`, `server/test/assembler.test.ts`, `server/test/chatSetup.test.ts`, `client/e2e/backlogBindingsCutoff.spec.ts`).
- **Stable bindings** (DESIGN §5.3): in preset text `{{char}}` is every character of the cast except the single selected persona (muted ones included) and `{{user}}` the single selected persona, unless `macro.binding` pins them; for one character and one persona these are ST's. A card's own text binds `{{char}}` to that card, a persona's `{{user}}` to that persona.
- **No tail directive:** the group nudge and the impersonation prompt are end-of-request texts, with `{{speaker}}` naming who writes (below, "Who writes, and the direction"); nothing fills the `impersonate` marker.
- **Disabling the `notes` stage (M2):** raw `stages.disable("notes")` is safe: the stages after it read a missing `notes` as none (no notes, no author's-note placement, no off-note), so the context is that of a chat without notes (`test/assembler.test.ts`). Other stages stay required; only optional features have this baseline.
- **`roles.projection`:** `by_writer` (ST's: messages on the user's side are `user`, the side taken from the speaker when it's a card, else from the slot's first version); `alternate` (by depth: even depths, the greeting's, are `assistant`, so roles never change as the chat grows; the end-of-request message still ends the request on a user turn, below); `perspective` (the speaker's own messages are `assistant`). A message is named by its recorded speaker, also one who has since left the cast (an earlier persona, say: `resolveStage` reads those cards into `departed`), else by its side's first card.
- **The LCM layer** (§16) is one system message per summary before the history in every chat.

**Notes** (DESIGN §4.1, §5.2; §13 for the imported ones). Every note that's on, and due this turn, goes where its placement says (the start of the context and the start and end of the tail are placed relative to the preset's sections in `composeStage`, §15 "Newest message"):
- **In the chat** at its depth and role, as ST's extension prompts go; a `tail` note at depth 0, DESIGN §4.1's "tail/D0" [P].
- **Beside the main prompt,** before or after it, one after another as ST's `injectToMain` puts its summary and then its author's note: each "before" goes in at the start in turn, so the later one ends up first. An in-chat main takes them as injections beside it, the same way. Section notes keep their role, defaulting to system for documents without one.
- **With the definitions**, for a card's note (`after_main_prompt`, or older notes' `section: card`; owner, 2026-10-28): at the top of its card's part of the `charDescription` marker (or the `personaDescription` one for a persona), inside the card's wrapper, or at the top of its card's part at the Definitions marker. A chat's note "with the definitions" goes after the main prompt (above); a chat's `section: card` note has no card to go with and is left out. A conditioned card note there is allowed (the editor warns): due or skipped, its piece is volatile (`markVolatile`), so the card's part, and the message holding it, is never in the cached prefix; skipped, it sends nothing. The preset editor lists these notes in the "With definitions" slot (`presetContext.ts`).
- **No author's note** (DESIGN §4.1, owner 2026-11-01): no note is placed relative to another, and none carries others. Before (assembler version 42 and earlier), a chat's author's note (`author_note.set`, else a note of kind `author_note`) took what was placed at its top or bottom into its text, wherever it went.
- **Nowhere** for `none`.

Their order is ST's for its extension prompts (`1_memory`, `2_floating_prompt`, `DEPTH_PROMPT`, `PERSONA_DESCRIPTION`): the chat's summary, its other notes [P] (an imported author's note among them, ST's `2_floating_prompt`), then the characters' notes, then the personas', each group by id, then lore at that depth. Notes at one depth and role are joined with newlines in that order. A card's note expands with `{{char}}` bound to its card, the chat's notes and a persona's with the chat's bindings.

**Replacements** (`replacements.ts`, DESIGN §4.2, spec/NOTE-OVERRIDES.md §3; assembler version 49). A note's `replaces` (`@rp/shared/docs/note.ts`: `{ kind: "preset_prompt", identifier }` or `{ kind: "card_field", field, card? }`, a card's own note leaving `card` out for its card) names what it's sent in place of; `own_position: true` sends it at its own placement and leaves the target out instead. The `replacements` stage, registered after `note-gate`, reads the notes that are on (`assembly.notes`, and `skippedNotes` for those not due), resolves each target (a card field's place through the path's `card.swap` events with `swappedCard`, so the card forked for this chat or another version takes the note) and records an outcome per note in `assembly.noteReplacements` (snapshot `noteReplacements`): `replaced`, `own_position`, `not_due`, `forbidden` (a card's note on a prompt with `forbid_overrides`), `missing` (no such prompt, or the card isn't in the cast), `disabled` (the prompt is off in the order), `conflict`. One note per target: the chat's notes before cards', each by entity id, the first winning, with a `note_replacement` issue for the rest. A note that goes in its target's place is taken out of the notes to be placed. Composition asks `withReplacement(assembly, key, own, options, finish)` (`stages.ts`) wherever a prompt's or field's text is made: preset prompts in `collectionOf` (key `preset:<identifier>`), card fields in `cardText` (`cardFieldKey`, the card's own text now `ownCardText`), and the persona's inline description. Every card field goes through `cardText`, so a card-swap agent reply's tail card (`tailCard`) and the speaker's card prompt overrides take the note too; agent replies and `RebuildContext` run the same stages. It returns the note's text as a piece whose source is the note, expanded with the target's options (a card field's names and bindings; a card's note on a preset prompt binds `{{char}}` to its card), `{{original}}` the target's own text (computed only when the note uses it), finished as the target is (`cardNewlines`); an empty piece for `own_position`; the target's own text for `not_due` and `disabled`; a conditioned note marks the place volatile (`markVolatile`, and `potentialVariableWrite` for the gate's reads). Card prompt overrides check first: a note replacing `main` or `jailbreak` wins over the speaker's `system_prompt` or `post_history_instructions`, and a note on the card's `system_prompt` field is the override's text. `PresetContext` (`db/presetContext.ts`) lists them as `replacements` (`NoteReplacementView`: note, title, card, resolved target, own position, status) and counts a replacing note's piece as its target's block (a card field's as its marker, `FIELD_BLOCKS`), so the prompt keeps its tokens and **Cache breakpoint** dividers; the note isn't listed again in a slot. **For Phase 4 (agent tools):** a change to a card or prompt in one chat is a note with `replaces` (and `placement` with `own_position` for text going elsewhere), made with `CreateChatNote`'s optional `replaces` and `content` and turned on at the version that produced it; nothing else in assembly needs to know, and disabling the stage sends such notes at their own placements. `test/noteReplacements.test.ts` covers a field with `{{original}}` and off, empty and own position, a preset prompt over a card's system prompt, a swap, the conflict, missing and forbidden outcomes, and a note not due. Version 49 expands `{{original}}` at a replacing note's own position too (ordinary notes and imported-summary templates share `noteText`), and retains conditional replacement barriers on their target slots even for empty text or a card override on a skipped turn (examples included). `CreateChatNote`, editor saves, revision restores and live-text checkpoints check target claims inside the writer transaction (`db/noteReplacementWrites.ts`), including off notes, branch-bound revisions and swapped card identities; a conflicting save preserves its drafts. A new note's initial head applies across forks, so its claim is checked in every affected fork. Card-note library edits check their own card and affected live forks. The field's immediate preview lasts only until the next context estimate, so switching the note off restores the original field while the editor stays open. Preset prompt rows use the assembled block count whenever a replacing note is shown (including empty and own-position replacements), in both collapsed and expanded rows; ordinary prompts retain their model-tokenizer counts. `test/noteReplacementWrites.test.ts` covers concurrent creates and saves, unlinking, swaps and branch-local claims; `test/assemblyStorage.test.ts` covers replacement token attribution and pinned plain/agent/card-swap replays.

**A persona's notes** are ordinary card notes (DESIGN §4.1: no hidden note kinds). The notes of every persona of the cast are read with the characters'. The persona's description is always sent where the persona goes (`personaDescription`, the Definitions marker); a note's kind or title never takes it away (`persona_description`, still decoded in old revisions, is ignored; migration 0050, §14.4). An ST import with the persona placed elsewhere leaves the card's description empty and puts the text in a note at that place (§13), so it is sent once. The gate compares the positions against ST (§15).

**ST's Character's Note** for macros and lorebook matching (`{{charDepthPrompt}}`, an entry's "Character's note" match) is `characterNoteText` (`types.ts`): the first character's notes that are on (for the lorebook, due) and placed in the chat, at a depth or after the newest message, as ST's note is, joined with newlines in id order. Only those visible settings decide it; before, it was the card's oldest note not made from a module and not of kind `character_author_note`.

**A condition** (DESIGN §4.1) makes a note due only on the turn of any of its cards (the speaker of the message being generated is one of them, a swipe's or continuation's included, and the user's own card when they write as it, owner question 8) or while any of its cards isn't muted (P1-1's mute, `presence.set`, at the leaf, `isMuted`): one unmuted card is enough, and it stops only once all of them are muted. A card that isn't in the cast at the leaf counts for neither. A note whose condition doesn't hold isn't due: no text and no macro effects. The inspector's note activation carries the condition in words ("on Aria's turn", "on Aria's or Bram's turn", "while Aria or Bram isn't muted", naming the cast's cards only, or "a card not in the chat" when none is) with whether it was due. **Cache:** a conditioned note is volatile at its placement: one at or below the history never touches the cached prefix, and one placed above it (allowed, owner question 7; the editor warns) keeps its potential boundary there on every turn, due or not, so the cached prefix ends before it. Conservatively, each conditioned note is a potential variable writer: any note or prompt expanded after it that reads variables is volatile at its actual placement, including on skipped turns and when the reader expands to empty; this tracks a single expansion-order flag and variable reads, not a dependency graph. Empty cache markers do not decide the last message's role for `send_if_empty`; their volatility propagates before they are removed ahead of squashing and post-processing. An older note's `interval` is ignored: it goes every turn. Tested in `test/notes.test.ts` (several cards, either condition) and `test/assembler.test.ts`, the two shapes in `shared/test/noteCondition.test.ts`, the fork's copy in `test/cardForks.test.ts`, the editor's choice at 1440 and 390 in `e2e/noteConditionCards.spec.ts`, over the database (the single-card shape too) and on branches in `test/assemblyStorage.test.ts`, and the cache in `test/steppedHistory.test.ts` and `test/warmthSources.test.ts`.

**The lorebook scan switch** (DESIGN §4.1). Each due note with `scan_lore` (not an imported summary) has its expanded text added to the lorebook scan as ST's `addInject` adds its extension prompts: whole, whatever its placement and the scan depth (`loreActivationStage`, `injections`). A card's note is expanded as it's sent (`{{char}}` its card, without card fields). An entry whose primary key is in a scanned note's own text names the note in its reason (`why.notes`), which the request inspector shows.

**Imported summaries** (DESIGN §8.1, §13). A chat's `imported_summary` note, while the chat has it on (`note.activate`, as the import sets it when ST sent it), goes where ST's Summarize extension put it. Its text is the newest of its revisions saved on a message of the context's path, up to the leaf (DATA-MODEL §15, invariant 5): a branch from before the latest summary sends the one saved by then, and one from before the first sends none (a revision with no source message applies wherever its binding does; the template and placement are the bound revision's). The chat note list and editor use the same path selection, showing empty content before the first summary while retaining the bound settings. Saving a correction creates a revision without the imported `source_slot_id`; its branch-local binding supplies applicability, even before the first imported summary (`test/importedSummaryEdit.test.ts`). It reads the revisions back along their first parents, at most 1,000, and which of their messages are on the path, both of which never change, so a rebuild reads the same. It goes out as its template with the summary in place of `{{summary}}` (or `Summary: ` and the summary, without one), expanded with the chat's macros, in-chat at its depth and role, or beside the main prompt (before or after it, in its message group, so squashing merges them as ST's does; an in-chat main takes it as an injection beside it). Expansion follows dependency order independently of placement: main, then the summary template, then the author's note, the other chat notes and card notes. Each sees preceding variable writes. The hidden messages it covers stay out of the context, like every hidden message. `{{summary}}` reads it anywhere while it is on. With summarization on it is placed by its own switch too, beside the summaries; enabling summarization switches it off in the same write (§16 *Enabling and backfill*), and nothing suppresses it out of sight. Tested in `test/assembler.test.ts`, over the database in `test/assemblyStorage.test.ts`, on an imported chat's branches in `test/stImport.test.ts`, and against ST by the gate.

**Who writes, and the direction** (DESIGN §2.2, owner 2026-10-27; the end-of-request instruction, owner 2026-10-29, provisional), in every chat:
- **Conditions** are evaluated in `collectionOf`, for in-chat prompts too, beside the prompt's ST triggers (§9): `as_user` when the speaker is in the played-by-me set, `as_character` when it's any other card, `with_direction` when the version's direction isn't blank. A summary request sends only `always` prompts [owner question 11]. The inspector's piece source names the condition that admitted a conditioned prompt ("Preset prompt “No impersonation” (sent when writing as a character)"). Conditions stay for the order's prompts, such as anti-impersonation lines.
- **The end-of-request message** (`end-of-request` stage, `@rp/shared/endOfRequest.ts`) is one user message, always the request's last, after everything else: post-history instructions, other prompts after the history, the notes at the end of the tail, the lorebook's block below the history. It holds the speaker's turn text, `continueNudge` ("when you continue a reply") on a Continue without a prefill (§15 "Continue"), else `impersonationPrompt` ("when your card speaks") when the speaker is in the played-by-me set, else `groupNudge` ("when a character speaks"), then, when the version's direction isn't blank, a newline and `directionPrompt` ("when you give a direction"). Neither conditions nor ST's triggers apply to the four; their stored role is ignored. Each is its own piece, with its preset source, so the inspector names each ("End of request: when a character speaks", `sourceDescriptors.ts`). A text that's empty, or expands to nothing, is left out. The registered stage installs `renderEndOfRequest`; `compose` expands it after ordinary prompts and notes and before prefill, so variable reads see earlier writes, end writes cannot affect the prefix, and prefill can read end writes. `compose` reserves its tokens in the budget; `messages` appends it after squashing and post-processing, so it remains one separate, verbatim user message in every mode, including merge and single.
- **With a prefill** (Continue, or the preset's prefill on a model that takes one), the message is the last of `messages`, so it goes right before the partial assistant message the wire appends (`withPrefill` in `wire.ts`), which stays last. **A summary request** sends none: the summary instruction takes its place as the final user message (§16 "Summary requests"), with no direction.
- **The one fallback:** when there's no end-of-request message (its texts empty, or the stage disabled), no prefill and no summary, and the final request's last message is the assistant's, a user message `[Write {{speaker}}'s next message.]` (source `assembler`, "end of request fallback: who writes next", volatile) goes last; on a Continue without a prefill it's the default continue nudge ("end of request fallback: continue the reply"). It's decided on the final request, after post-processing, so an assistant prompt or note at the tail is caught too. The budget reserves it whenever there's no end-of-request message. It's no issue on the reply: only the request inspector shows it (contexts before assembler version 30 recorded a `last_turn_filled` issue, which `toVersion` never shows). The closing user turn after the last chat message and the default direction prompt with its `direction_prompt_missing` issue are gone (assembler version 34).
- **`{{speaker}}`** is the speaker's in-chat name and **`{{direction}}`** the direction, verbatim: a macro's output is never expanded again (§10), so a `{{random}}` typed in a direction stays literal. Outside a generation, and in a template message of the chat, both stay as written. A piece whose text names either is volatile (`macros.ts`), a conditioned prompt after the history is volatile, and the end-of-request message is volatile, so none of them ever sits inside the cached prefix.
- **The reference-harness delta** (its "Satellite block and final user turn" and "Cache control"): reference-harness always ends on one user turn carrying its volatile satellite, so everything that changes per turn follows its cache-stable timeline. Here the layout is the preset's (DESIGN §5.0), and the end-of-request message plays reference-harness's final user turn: per-turn text is volatile, after the history breakpoint, and the request ends on it. A conditioned prompt above the history (an anti-impersonation line in Main marked `as_character`) does change the prefix on impersonation turns: the owner's decided trade, which the inspector shows.
- **The preset editor** (`PromptDocument.tsx`) has a **Condition** select and the **Generation types** checkboxes on each prompt of the order (each shown as a badge when it limits the prompt). The four texts are in a fixed **End of request** section below the order (`EndOfRequest.tsx`, registered as `preset.end-of-request` in the `preset.editor.sections` slot, `presetSections.ts`): "When a character speaks", "When your card speaks", "When you continue a reply" and "When you give a direction" (its line says it's added after the turn text), so the continue nudge is no longer among the utility prompts, each with a line saying when it's sent, and nothing to drag, delete, switch off or condition. The warnings at the top (`PresetWarnings`, computed by `presetWarnings` in `shared/presetConditions.ts`) are a direction text without `{{direction}}`, which would lose the direction, with a link to the text; and each switched-on prompt of the order whose condition and generation types never meet (§9, `gatesNeverMeet`), named, with both gates in words, that it's off in an ST export, and **Go to the prompt**, which expands and scrolls to it (`PresetEditor` hands `PromptDocument` a `goTo` request). Tests: `shared/test/presetWarnings.test.ts`, client `test/endOfRequest.test.ts`, `server/test/presetFormat.test.ts` (export and reimport), `e2e/rpLoop.spec.ts` (setting a condition the prompt's types never meet, the warning, the link, clearing it). It subscribes to that field’s current text draft, so removing or restoring the macro updates the warning before a revision save. The fixed sections use the toolbar’s measured scroll margin, so the warning’s link reveals the field below the sticky toolbar. The impersonation notice (DESIGN §2.2) counts only prompts of the order marked for writing as `{{user}}` (an `as_user` condition, or ST triggers of only `impersonate`); the end-of-request text "when your card speaks" doesn't, so a preset without such a prompt shows the notice once.

**Cache breakpoints** (assembler version 45; `breakpoints.ts`, DESIGN §5.5), placed structurally, as deltas from reference-harness's scheme (its `src/agent/cache-breakpoints.ts`, ARCHITECTURE "Cache control"):
- **Every message knows what it's made of** (`Stability` in `st.ts`): the preset's and cards' prompts ahead of the chat (`prefix`), lorebook entries pinned above the history and whatever follows the first place one can go, until the history (`pinned`: stable until the history's start moves, below), the chat's own messages (`history`), and what moves or changes every turn (`volatile`): in-chat prompts and notes, which keep their depth as the chat grows, the tail, the user turn ST fills in, a message a depth-bounded regex script will change as it gets deeper (one that applies now and has a maximum depth, or one that matches and hasn't reached its minimum yet), and one a script was skipped for. Squashing and post-processing merge it with the text. reference-harness finds its boundaries by searching the wire text for `<system>` and `<conversation_summary`, and flags that as a weakness itself.
- **reference-harness's (a), the leading system item:** here `prefix`, the last message of the leading run of prefix messages, which ends at the first pinned lore, the summary layer or the history. It's what survives a move of the history's start: the preset's prompts, the card definitions and card overrides wherever the preset's order puts them before `chatHistory`, and notes placed there. With "only below the history" on, no lore is above the history, so it reaches the summary layer or the history. When the provider takes them as its system parameter, its own marker there covers them; with pinned lore, Anthropic's system parameter ends with the (a) message (`wire.ts`), so pinned lore stays in messages without spending a dedicated checkpoint.
- **reference-harness's (b), the conversation summary:** the last summary message (§16), after stable history. Prefix and layer keep separate message boundaries through squashing and post-processing.
- **Pinned lore** (a delta: reference-harness has no lorebooks): a marker after the last pinned message before the history, when a slot is free.
- **reference-harness's (c), the last timeline item the next session reproduces verbatim:** here `history`, the last message before the first volatile one. The deepest in-chat prompt or note is where the next request starts to differ, since it moves down as messages are added; with none, it's the chat's last message. **Priority** (most important first, as a provider with fewer free markers keeps the first): while the history's start holds, (c), then (a), then (b), then the pinned marker, so with two markers (a) beats (b); after the start moved (a cut, a restore, LCM's cursor), (a) comes first, since the history after it is new anyway. With an `explicit` model a fifth boundary can't be marked (Anthropic's four, one taken by pi-ai's own): the snapshot records a `cache_breakpoints` issue naming what isn't marked, rather than dropping it silently.
- **reference-harness's (d) and (e), every request's end and the previous request's:** pi-ai already marks the last message, and Anthropic reads back about 20 blocks before a marker. With `auto` breakpoints that marker moves to (c), before the end-of-request instruction (§6 "Default cache markers").
- **No token floor:** reference-harness's 1,024-token minimum is Bedrock's; Anthropic ignores a marker on a shorter prefix.
- **Editor display** (owner P7, 2026-11-02; preseteditor, 2026-11-03): the preset editor shows all supplied points as thin “Cache breakpoint” dividers with kind qualifiers and the owner’s exact cache explanation, only for explicit-cache models (§14.6). The inspector retains its earlier two-line reuse display.
- **Pinned lore has no dedicated marker** (owner, 2026-11-02). Its placement and activation pins are unchanged. The prefix boundary still ends before pinned lore; Messages system extraction uses the separate `request.pinnedStart` structural boundary without depending on the removed marker; ordinary leading system prompts keep their prior role. Historical requests retain the old pinned-reason fallback. The old `pinned` reason remains readable in historical snapshots.
- **reference-harness's (c), the last timeline item the next session reproduces verbatim:** here `history`, the last history message before the first volatile one. Responses explicit layouts choose the last user/system message at or before it because checkpoints require `input_text`. The deepest in-chat prompt or note bounds reuse because it moves down as history grows.
- **Model capabilities:** `cacheLayout` is an optional capability record merged and persisted alongside `cacheBreakpoints`, pinned in `ModelInput`. `lookback: false` enables an exact-position repeat; absent/true keeps the lookback layout. `summarySplit: true` adds a checkpoint after the leading highest summary tier, before a lower tier can be rewritten. `marker: "prompt_cache_breakpoint"` selects the OpenAI-compatible extension; `maxMarkers` is a positive declared budget (Messages/Responses still clamp at four); `minTokens` supplies the OpenAI-compatible cumulative floor. TTL remains the existing separately resolved `cacheTtlS`. The stage and provider transforms remain registered replaceable parts.
- **Exact-position repeats:** each explicitly enabled exact-position context saves the SHA-256 digest at its current history checkpoint in `historyStart.state.cacheHistory`. The next context reads the existing path-scoped, replay-pinned history state and finds that complete prefix among the new message-prefix digests. Role, name, text and image metadata participate. Only an identical history endpoint before volatility qualifies; an edit, changed summary, cut or sibling divergence drops the repeat naturally. This is conservative assembly evidence, not a claim that a provider cached the previous request. No new query, main-thread database work or prompt text is stored.
- **Priority:** with lookback, history → prefix → older-tier split (if enabled) → whole summary layer. Without lookback, history → matching previous history → older-tier split → prefix → whole layer. After a history-start move, prefix → split → history → previous history → whole layer. Coincident endpoints collapse. Existing SDK markers do not consume an extra slot when a candidate already has one. The snapshot retains candidate boundaries and reports excess candidates; the wire injector subtracts actual SDK/tool markers. Every context's final checkpoint stays with the SDK on Messages/Responses and is injected explicitly for Chat.
- **Volatile macros:** the macro engine's optional observer reports evaluated random/clock handlers, including nested card fields and plugin macros. Assembly records those dynamic dependencies separately and emits a `cache_breakpoints` issue for changing prefix prompts. Detection is advisory: it preserves structural checkpoints so coincident clock/random values can still read the cache; full prefix digests and the provider’s actual matching decide reuse. A seeded `pick` declares `changesPerReply: false`, retaining its frozen replay semantics without falsely classifying it as random per reply. Clock macros are conservatively volatile even if their formatted output changes only once a day. Verbatim history and frozen template messages retain their existing semantics. The editor can consume the same issue; no new editor UI is added here.
- **Frozen LCM prefixes:** `lcm/prefix.ts` carries the frozen prefix’s structural lore boundary and restores a continuity checkpoint when pinning makes a structurally volatile prefix (such as a speaker-dependent prompt) reusable. Condensation material and raw messages are excluded from that restored endpoint. Requests without a pin keep their original volatility boundaries; raw summary requests discard the lore boundary with the preset.
- **Simulation:** `test/support/cacheSimulator.ts` models exact, 20-position lookback, automatic and absent caching, cumulative floors, budgets, TTL refresh, and separate read/write prices. `test/support/cacheStudy.ts` captures actual composition metadata through a scoped registered stage, assembles 2,400-message synthetic branch paths with repeated swipes and depth notes, appends summary leaves, and uses the real maintenance planner for same-level condensations. `npm run measure:cache-study` (or the direct Node command for pure JSON output) prints the layout comparisons and macro/depth sensitivity as JSON. Counts use a four-characters estimate plus framing; these are controlled synthetic input-cost comparisons, not provider measurements. Tests exercise digest invalidation/replay, floors/expiry/budget, layout cost regressions and wire placement. The study and evidence qualifications are recorded outside the checkout in `<work>/artifacts/cachestudy/cachestudy.md`.
- **Shown in the user's terms** (owner, 2026-11-02; DESIGN §5.5): the preset editor and the inspector draw them as "Above this line: reused by every reply" (`prefix`) and "Above this line: reused until old messages drop out" (the last of the others), with an explanation behind an (i) (`promptLines.tsx`; §14 "The preset editor").
- **Off unless the model's breakpoints are `explicit`,** as reference-harness's are off unless configured: the snapshot always records them, and the provider request sends them only then (§6 "Explicit cache breakpoints").

**Stepped history** (`stages.ts`, DESIGN §5.5, owner 2026-10-13). The maximum is the current model’s context size, capped by its reported window. Its optional `settings.context_target` is a total token count; absent, it defaults to 80% of the maximum [P]. Context and response length are edited on the model, and folder-imported prompt presets never change them. Response reserve, prefill, fixed prompts, admitted examples, notes and summaries in every placement, and the stable lorebook tail allowance all count toward the same total. Hidden messages spend nothing. Budget checks use the larger estimate before and after squashing/post-processing, counting names and placeholders those transforms introduce while retaining ST’s conservative pre-transform accounting [P].

The start is a slot and its path depth, recorded as `historyStart` in every new context. Below the maximum, it stays at the previous start. Crossing the maximum removes whole oldest messages until the total fits the target. A first context that fits the maximum retains the full history; with no prior start, an overflow cuts to the target. If fixed content alone exceeds the target, that content is the minimum achievable total [P]; exceeding the maximum fails assembly. The admitted example count is part of the cut state and source pins; it is reconsidered only at a cut or a configuration change (preset, model, cast, notes, the lorebooks read and the chat's lorebook setting: `cutState.ts` `configurationOf`). Admission and cuts use a composition with all note reservations present, including skipped intervals, then send only the actual due text. Re-admission recomputes the target floor before cutting.

With LCM on, recent messages kept as written have their own pair (DESIGN §8; §16 *Defaults*): the maximum and target above become the fixed part plus the recent maximum and target, in tokens. Both pairs are first scaled down by one factor when their maxima don't fit the model's context beside the fixed part and the reply, keeping their proportions, and the recent pair is then fitted to the history allowance left after the layer reserve and admitted examples (`fitPair`); the total limit always wins and no reply fails because of them. A summary request (`summarizing`) is bounded only by the window, since it must render its whole chunk. The recent pair cuts only messages that can still be summarized: when its cut would turn fresh failed leaf ranges into markers, the start moves back to the earliest such range's first message whose history fits the allowance before the pair capped it, so those ranges stay raw while the window fits (§16). The fitted pairs are recorded as `lcm.recentBudget` and `lcm.layerBudget`, with the figures the settings panel shows (`lcm.measure`: the context, the fixed part, the reply reserve, the current recent and layer tokens, and whether a pair was scaled). With LCM off nothing here changes and the ST differential gate is byte-identical. Assembler version 25 pins this, the explicit `{{summary}}`, the summary note placed by its own switch, and the summary request without the preset.

The provider cache identity hashes the retained history in the final reusable prefix: a cut changes that prefix, while unchanged retained turns preserve its earlier checkpoints between cuts. A newly appended endpoint can still be cold and stagger even when its shorter prefix is warm.

The start never moves back on ordinary sends. Restoration requires a raised maximum or target, a different preset/model identity, or a durable reduction before the recorded start; the entire earlier suffix must then fit the target. Changes confined to retained messages do not unlock restoration. This prevents a skipped interval note from restoring dropped history only for the next due note to cut it again. The same slot-based boundary can later be supplied by LCM coverage: its proposed cursor is the slot immediately before verbatim history (`spec/LCM.md` §2.1).

Notes and formatted summaries are never shortened to fit a context budget. Stable expansions count at their actual size. The cut state pins each note’s largest observed size and one shared allowance for unused capacity: at most 25% of the available input window or 1,024 tokens, further limited by the space left after full fixed content [P]. There is no per-note quarter-window charge. Notes allocate unused capacity in placement order; every candidate counts at least the full actual composition and at most that cost plus the shared allowance, including role framing, merging and post-processing. Optional capacity cannot make a fixed context fail. Skipped notes never expand or execute macro writes; literal skipped text can seed its size observation, while a first unseen macro expansion is measured when due.

When an expansion exceeds its pinned size observation, its full text updates that observation, example admission and the target floor are recalculated, and history is cut again to the target. This is an explicit note-budget change, recorded as `historyMove: budget` when the maximum itself was not reached; the cache estimate explains it. A smaller or skipped expansion retains the observation, so the next occurrence of the same large note does not manufacture another budget change. Ordinary sends still cannot move the start backward. Observations reset on configuration changes; pinned source inputs reproduce them exactly on replay. Only full actual fixed content exceeding the maximum fails assembly, with an error naming full notes, fixed context and the response reserve. The lore tail allowance remains independent of activation.

`StartRollout` extracts the start and generation depth into three rollout columns (migration 0021). `rollouts_history(chat_id, history_depth DESC, id DESC)` supplies candidates; a single materialized parent walk finds the nearest ancestor generation whose start remains on the path. An empty candidate set exits without walking. Sibling generations and abandoned swipes never restart the walk: the 10,001-slot worker regression reads exactly 10,000 ancestry edges with 0, 100 or 500 unrelated candidates, about 26–31 ms in isolated samples (formerly over five million reads at 500). The test checks the index plan and measured work, independently of host timing. At 100,000 messages, assembly measured 71.3 ms without a prior start and 62.6 ms with the indexed start (five-run medians). `test/assemblyScale.test.ts` (opt-in, `ASSEMBLY_SCALE=1`) assembles the next request over 1,000 and then 5,000 synthetic messages that all fit, with summarization off, and fails when the time grows more than tenfold (linear work grows about fivefold). The history images' lookup by version is built once per request (`messageImagesOf` in `images.ts`); built once per request message, it made assembly quadratic: 1.9 s at 1,000 messages and 54.7 s at 5,000, against 0.4 s and 1.5 s now.

**Inserted messages** (spec/MESSAGE-INSERT.md §3.2, unit 4). In a fork that places insertions, the sources read its display path (`display` in `sqlSources`, `displayThrough` in `db/displayPath.ts`), and everything the assembler calls a depth is a display position: a history entry's (`HistoryEntry.depth`; an inserted one also has `inserted`), an event's, the target's (`Target.depth`), the history start's and the LCM cursor's. Without insertions a position is the depth and every read is the structural one, so chats without insertions assemble as before, and the ST differential gate is unchanged. The target is placed on the path by the sources (`placeTarget`): a version at its position, a next reply after the leaf, or after the display end when the leaf is the fork's tip (an inserted message after the tip comes before an appended reply). When the message right before the target isn't its parent (an inserted message sits between them), `Target.historyLeaf` names it, and the stages read the history, its events, the history start and revision, the message count and the summary layer from it (`historyLeafOf`); `parentSlotId` and the snapshot's `leafSlotId` stay structural. `history(leaf, limit, after)` reads the last `limit` positions up to the leaf, after `after`'s, through `displaySlots` (the window's pieces driving one range of `slots_chain` each), with the same columns as the structural read: an inserted message's images, their per-fork exclusion (`image_exclude` on its original version) and their estimates are read like any message's. `older` is the slot at the position before the window.
