A fork that moves messages reads LCM over its display path as one with insertions does (`insertionPieces` is non-null for it; a moved slot counts as an inserted one for `insertedAt`, `onlyInsertedBetween` and `insertedThrough`). `readSummary` marks a summary stale there when its first and last are out of order on the display path, or its inputs, in the order it read them, aren't in increasing display order. A summary whose range lost a slot to a move (its range is shorter than its slot count) is left out of the layer, as before, and planning writes the range again; one whose range gained or reordered slots stays in the layer, stale.
- *Lineage.* `lineageValidator` with the fork's view checks a summary's inputs, or its parts' ranges, in display order with only inserted slots between them and its ends where it says; an input the fork doesn't show makes it inconsistent there, so a summary that includes an inserted message is ignored in a fork without it.
- *Inside a range.* `readSummary` makes a summary stale in the fork when its display range holds more slots than it covers: an insertion anchored at one of its slots other than its last, for a condensation anywhere its parts cover or between them. That is the edit rule: it stays in use until replaced, the next reply's pass writes it again over the display range (`lcmPath`), the inserted message included, and other forks are untouched.
- *At a seam* (`seamStale`). A summary followed only by inserted slots that no summary starts at, up to one that starts right after them, covers those slots for the layer walk and the planner, stale, with its last slot moved to the gap's end. So the walk keeps the later summaries, and the planner writes it again over its first slot to the end of the gap; for a condensation, its last part is written again first and the condensation over the new part after, by the existing cascade. The same holds for a summary preceded only by inserted slots (an insertion above the first message): it reaches back to the first one. An insertion directly after the layer's cursor isn't a seam: it is raw history.
- *Paths and planning.* `lcmPath` reads the display stretch from `first` to the leaf in one statement driven by the pieces (`windowPieces`), with `position`, `previous` (the slot before it there; its parent without insertions) and `inserted`; `children` counts only children that weren't inserted, so an anchor isn't a branch point. Summary requests take the slot before the job's first as `summaryBefore`. Candidates of the layer, failures, maintenance and the UI reads are summaries ending on the structural walk from the leaf or at an inserted slot shown up to it. `EnqueueSummaries` and `EnqueueCondensations` compare live jobs' display ranges with the chunk's or parts' positions (`nearInDisplay`), check coverage by the chunk's slots, and require parts next to each other there. `AssembleSummary` lets a condensation's parts have inserted slots between them.
- *UI membership.* Coverage and failed-summary reads require the whole lineage on the viewed display path, rather than only a shared last endpoint. In a fork without inserted pieces, the structural span/count check excludes summaries that include another fork's inserted inputs without adding lineage walks to ordinary coverage reads. In a fork with pieces, the display lineage validator rejects absent inputs even when an unrelated insertion happens to keep the range's length equal to its input count.
- *Client data.* `GetLcmState` adds `cursorSlotId` and `cursorPosition` beside `cursorDepth` (the cursor slot's depth); `GetLcmCoverage` takes `fromPosition` and `toPosition` (else reads `fromDepth` and `toDepth` as positions; the numbers agree without insertions), and the client's coverage reads send positions. The message list's summarized and dropped marks and its summary divider compare positions (`placeOf` in `features/chat/summaryBoundary.ts`: an entry's `position`, else its depth) with the cursor's position and the history start (`test/summaryBoundary.test.ts`); the coverage rail still compares depths, and numbering by position is the client unit's.
- *Claims.* `ClaimSummaryJob` resolves live level-1 job starts to display positions in forks with inserted pieces and keeps the existing depth ordering elsewhere. Earlier ranges finish before later ones in that fork, retaining continuity context even when an insertion is structurally deeper than the later range. The two-worker account cap and per-fork serial guard are unchanged.
- *Known limits.* Imported-summary adoption (`lcmImported.ts`, the enable copy) and the backfill estimate read the structural path; an imported summary over a range that later gets an insertion is stale by the rule above.
- *Tests.* `test/lcmInsert.test.ts`: inside a range (stale in F, fresh in a fork made before, the plan's rewrite including X, enqueue and overlap by position, the result ignored in the other fork); at a seam (the later summary kept, the earlier rewritten over the gap; inside a condensation, the part then the condensation; before the first summary); directly after the cursor (raw, no work); jobs, L1 and condensation, completing across an insertion; a refused completion that skips a message that wasn't inserted; the relaxed triggers on their own; a summary including X ignored in a fork without X and used in forks made after; raw-SQL rejection of reversed inserted siblings, ordinary-branch returns, reversed condensation children and reversed endpoints; display-ordered claims; deletion, restore and edits in a fork made at an insertion, with repeated plans proving repairs settle; and a random oracle (four seeds of 28 insert, fork, append, summarize and condense steps) comparing validity, positions and freshness of every summary in every fork, and the layer's continuity and seams, with first principles.

**Context membership.** `NextContext` and cache events carry the selected layer’s last covered depth alongside the raw history start, scoped to the viewed leaf. The client labels those covered messages “Summarized”; only uncovered messages before the raw start have the faded dropped marker. Hidden messages retain their separate hidden marker.

**Budget and cache.** With LCM enabled the summary cursor first removes covered messages. Assembly retains the recorded stepped raw start strictly after the cursor. It holds between sends and summary landings until that suffix exceeds the maximum, at which point it cuts toward the target. A cursor landing past the start advances it to the first remaining raw slot; a landing before it leaves it in place. The existing on-path restoration check fences branch state. Its runway is measured against the maximum allowance, not the smaller target used by that cut. With LCM disabled the recorded stepped start and restoration rules in §15 apply unchanged. Both modes pin their resulting raw start and example admission for replay.

In LCM mode examples are budgeted before the changing verbatim window. The summary block's target allowance (the chat's `layerTarget`, fitted as in §15 *Stepped history*) counts each summary message's rendered text, wrapper and message overhead; unused allowance is reserved from history, bounded by the remaining budget. Fixed prompts and the actual layer must fit. This keeps the example prefix stable while a growing layer stays inside the allowance. Its maximum (`layerMax`) is the budget condensation measures against (below); send waits are described below. Fresh failed leaf ranges beyond the selected cursor remain raw while the window fits. When a cut would remove part of such a range, it removes the whole failed range and sends `[Messages A–B could not be summarized.]` before the retained history. Overlapping failures share one marker; adjacent ranges stay separate so a later range can remain raw when it fits; its tokens and provider post-processing are included in admission, so trimming cannot silently drop it. It is an assembler source and a `summary_failed` assembly issue. Failed inputs that changed no longer produce a marker; selected successful coverage replaces it. Other omitted raw ranges are recorded by immutable path depths and reported in the inspector as “Messages A–B left out: not summarized yet”; LCM omits the repetitive history-truncation warning from reply events. Stable history, the layer and the prefix receive breakpoints in that priority. Provider system extraction ends before the layer, preserving independent Anthropic prefix/layer markers and source attribution. The provider’s reusable cache identity includes the summary layer, so a summary replacement invalidates the prefix from that layer onward and cold followers stagger at the new boundary. Idle summary claims use the same historical expiry calculation as the chat estimate, including fixed cache write origins; a model TTL edit cannot extend an existing cache. The cache-warmth estimate identifies summary replacements and cursor changes as “Summary of messages A–B replaced.”

**Pins and inspection.** A version-19 snapshot also pins the on-path failed summary ids/revisions and their immutable depth ranges, separately from the selected layer; the snapshot records the ranges whose markers were actually sent. Rebuilds use those ranges without querying live failure state, even after an edit, retry or successful replacement. A snapshot pins each selected summary id and immutable revision, freshness/status and cursor, plus selected, omitted and logical verbatim ranges. `RebuildContext` uses those pins without selecting again, even after summary edits, revision changes, staleness or a cursor move. Purging covered originals does not prevent replay. The inspector labels summary sources with level, depth range and revision number, and derives whether they have since become stale or been replaced from the current layer on the recorded path. Historical stale flags remain in the original capture.

**Defaults.** The typed `lcm.settings` state event is fork-scoped and accepted only at the initial position, without version or role scope. It applies throughout that fork and is inherited by later forks through their bounded lineage (owner Q5). Its fields (`@rp/shared/lcmSettings.ts`, DESIGN §8): `enabled`; `withPreset` (`current`, `specific`, or `raw`) and optional `preset` (the specific preset ref; absent until chosen); `withNotes` (send the chat's notes with a summary request); `tail` (the instruction); `recentTarget`/`recentMax` (recent messages kept as written) and `layerTarget`/`layerMax` (the summary block), positive tokens, a target below its maximum when both are stored; `when` (`after-reply` while the cache is warm, or `next-reply`); `leafInput` (chunk size) and `leafTarget` (summary length); `style`, `fanout` and `condenseTarget` are not shown. The account default (`generation.lcm`, `LcmDefaults`) has the same fields, `enabled` included as the default for new chats; its old `spendAhead` is read as `when` (false is `next-reply`) while `when` is absent, and writing `when` removes it. `resolveLcm` (shared by server and client) takes each field from the chat, else the account default, else the built-in: on, with the preset, without notes, recent 12,000/20,000 and summary block 14,000/18,000 tokens (owner, 2026-10-28: summaries cover unbounded history and recent chat grows faster, so it gets the wider band), after the reply, length 600, and the chunk min(4,000, half the recent band once fitted) (`chunkSize`). `CreateChat` and `StartChat` store a full copy of the account default as it resolves then (`newChatLcm`; the instruction and chunk size only when the account sets them), so a later change of the default leaves them as they were (Q2); newly imported chats store the same copy with `enabled: false`; importing into an existing chat preserves its settings. Chats from before store only `enabled` and follow the account default field by field. Existing chats without the key remain off. Migration `0051_lcm_new_defaults` (`lcmDefaultsMigration.ts`) moved chats to the new built-in sizes when they held a copy of the old ones (16,000/24,000 and 8,000/12,000): a size moves when every `lcm.settings` event of the chat has it at the old value and the account default doesn't set it, and a pair moves back whole if its target would reach its maximum; it appends one new event per chat it changes. A size the user set, in the chat or in the account default it was copied from, stays.

`ChangeLcmSettings { chatId, forkId, change }` writes one partial change (null removes a field, so it follows the account default) as a new fork-scoped event in one writer transaction that reads the current one; a stored target at or above its stored maximum is refused (`LcmSettingsInvalid`), and other misfits are shown, not refused. It publishes `State` and `Lcm`. `SetLcmEnabled` is the same write with the switch alone. `ChangeGenerationDefaults` takes the account default's fields as `change.lcm`, one at a time, with the same check. `GetLcmSettings { chatId, leafSlotId, forkId }` (reader `LcmSettingsAt`) returns `{ stored, resolved, account, fitted, room, now, fit }` from one assembly of the next context with LCM forced on, as `EstimateBackfill` does: the pairs as fitted, the model's context, fixed part and reply reserve, the current recent and layer figures, and one sentence per misfit (`lcmMisfits`): both maxima beside the fixed part and the reply against the context ("Recent messages (24,000) and summaries (12,000) need 36,000 tokens; this model's context leaves 22,400 after the preset and reply.", under the pair with the larger maximum), the chunk twice inside the fitted recent band, and each target below its maximum. While the chunk doesn't fit twice, `PlanSummaries` plans nothing and returns as it does with summarization off: the misfit is the user's setting, shown under the chunk size, not a failure to log. Both RPCs and both operations have isolation probes in both directions. Enabling an imported chat, adopting its summary and the backfill are described under *Enabling and backfill* below. Edits and reads never start summarization.

**Tests.** `lcmAssembly.test.ts` exercises real OpenAI and Anthropic captures, both assembly modes, literal macros, freshness preference, coverage gaps, failures while raw fits, inspector/cache invalidation and replay after purging covered originals. `lcmPlacement.test.ts` covers depth and absolute placements, late main ordering for default and imported before/after-main summaries, card overrides, provider provenance and stable example budgeting across both zero-to-one and one-to-two layer transitions. `lcmFailureMarker.test.ts` checks originals while they fit, markers and maximum-budget admission in both layouts, stale failures disappearing, successful repair and exact replay of both decisions. Schema tests exercise publication, closure and lower-level lineage; real-worker corruption probes verify raw fallback for off-path endpoints, wrong input chains and self-links. The independent graph model (`test/protocol/lcm.model.test.ts`) runs four seeds of 150 steps with real workers, server and sockets and synthetic fixture summaries, checking path, exact partition, freshness, immutable retention and historical replay after every graph/summary step. Its independent in-memory graph oracle and shrinking traces extend the drafts model's pattern. Job and batch oracles are described below; refusal judging remains slice 4.

**Maintenance input reads (perfred1).** `lcmMaintain` asks `lcmPath` for input metadata without prose: selected version identities, amendment counts, image identities, generating flags and positions remain unchanged, including fork visibility and audience projection. The path query omits the `version_texts` join and repeated content-eligibility expressions. Chunk planning and request assembly retain their content reads. `lcmPathInputs.test.ts` probes the reader in a worker, compares the complete input metadata with the content-bearing path and checks that it does not query the prose table. Maintenance signatures and queued inputs retain their previous bytes.

**Planner and durable queue** (`db/lcmPlanning.ts`, `db/lcmQueue.ts`, `lcm/Summarizer.ts`; slice 3). The planner uses the recent pair as the assembly fitted it (`lcm.recentBudget`). It keeps the target, plans once the uncovered recent tokens pass the midpoint of target and maximum (built in, Q6: summaries are usually ready before the maximum, where a send waits), and batches whole-message chunks from before the kept part; `over` is the maximum. The default chunk is min(4,000, half the band), so the runway fits two chunks; a chunk size breaking `maximum − target ≥ 2 × chunk` fails planning before a provider request, and the settings panel says so. Branch points end chunks above a quarter of their target; generating or merged slots stop planning. Chunks also stop after 128 slots, independently of tokens. The writer rejects oversized chunks before reading their chains, and its coverage query uses a bounded chain CTE rather than a parameter per slot. All-null chunks and condensations of empty summaries seal zero-token lineage without a provider call; the next pass continues from that coverage without a gap. An enqueue race rolls back and the scheduler retries from the frozen episode. The default output target is 600. Condensation and re-summarizing are described below; an edit never schedules work.

`EnqueueSummaries` rechecks chains and effective version/amendment pins in one transaction and rejects overlapping live L1 ranges and ranges already covered by complete or truncated L1 summaries with identical effective input pins. Planning splits around that completed coverage independently of the selectable prefix cursor, so a failed earlier chunk cannot cause repeated paid summaries of later chunks. Claims order interactive, idle, then background by age, admit two processing jobs per user, and serialize a chat's L1 jobs in path order. Attempts count at claim. Migration `0024_summary_attempts` adds a monotonically increasing claim epoch, rollout binding and clipping cap. Release and startup reset refund attempts without refunding epochs, fencing late callbacks. The scheduler records each acknowledged claim in a live-attempt registry before forking its task and removes it only after task cleanup. Before claiming again, owner-scoped `ReconcileSummaryJobs` refunds processing rows absent from that registry and closes their rollouts. Claiming and reconciliation run serially in the single instance-locked scheduler; a lost worker acknowledgement is recovered after respawn without resetting still-running tasks. Job-specific operations require the acting owner; reset is internal and has no RPC. Failure and release can clean up an owning binned chat, so deletion during a request cannot strand a processing job. Completion compares inputs with the frozen request before the atomic summary write. Concurrent edits may make the result stale but cannot change its pins. Failures close rollouts, retry twice, then leave a failed job; original messages remain available. Terminal failures become failed summary rows (below). Each provider call has a ledger row, rolled up into its summary rollout.

Job reads use the range's last slot when storage has no planning leaf. Planning, reconciliation and claim failures, including RPC schema defects, are isolated to that operation and logged; they do not stop the scheduler. Failed reconciliation skips that user's claims until the next poll. A committed claim whose acknowledgement cannot be decoded is recovered by the existing reconciliation fence. Interruptions still stop work normally. `lcmPool.test.ts` exercises the nullable leaf, each scheduler boundary, lost acknowledgement recovery and a job defect followed by a successful retry.

**Summary requests.** Registered assembler stages run in `quiet` mode, with the path cut at the chunk end. The model is the **summary model** (audit item 067; DESIGN §8 left its configuration open, the coordinator's Q17 ruling chose this): `summaryModelBinding` (`shared/lcmSettings.ts`) takes the chat's own (a `model.binding` scoped `summarizer`, written by `ChangeCast { _tag: "SummaryModel", model }`, null writing a scoped `model.unbind`; `Cast.summaryModel` reports it), else the account's (`generation.lcm.summarizer`, set by `ChangeGenerationDefaults { summarizer }`, checked as the user's like the fallback, an unavailable choice retained for replacement or clearing), else the narrator's, else the chat's binding, else the user's default model; the model stage applies it only when `request.summarizing`, so a reply is never written with it. `resolveSummaryModel` tries these destinations through the owned source reads, skipping only missing-model failures and recording a plain context note when a summary falls through. Other storage or assembly failures propagate. `EstimateBackfill`, planning and the workshop summary context use that same resolver. Hidden models remain usable when explicitly selected (hiding is a picker filter, not disabling). Settings → Chats → Summaries has "Summary model" ("Same as the chat's model" until one is chosen); a chat's Summary settings (Summaries tab) has "This chat's summary model", which follows the account ("Account default: …" or "Same as the chat's model") until the chat picks one, from the shown position on. Each takes its choice off with a row under the picker's list (`ModelSelect`'s `clear`, shown while a model is chosen). A summary's details name the model that wrote it. In-run workshop summaries retain the actual model key in their transcript metadata; the Summaries panel and run inspector display it, or “Model not recorded” for older entries. This metadata is excluded from the summary text sent to the model. The tool operation policy refuses scoped state events, since its undo restores only chat-wide bindings. Planning checks the resolved summary model. Recent retention and condensation thresholds keep the reply model's window; when no reply model is available, planning can measure with the summary model. A different summary model gets a local summary-frame measurement without material, bounding chunk clipping plus reserved output to its own window. Workshop frames omit the reply's tools and preset. Backfill estimates use the same helpers (`db/lcmModelBudget.ts`). The same-model path retains its single assembly. No provider call is made for these measurements or by opening settings. The kept planning facts (§16 "Kept planning facts") hold no model, binding, setting, fitted chunk or blocked result, so every plan resolves the summary model afresh: an account, chat or branch summary choice, its removal, a model's revision or its connection's deletion changes the next plan without moving the LCM stamp (`planCacheSeams.test.ts`, combine1115). Tests: `summaryModel.test.ts` (the order of choice, and a reply keeps the chat's model), `summaryModelApi.test.ts`, `isolation.test.ts` (another user's model refused), `e2e/summaryModel.spec.ts` (1440 and 390, light and dark, layout audit). Preset bindings: the summarizer's fall back to the narrator's. Earlier coverage supplies continuity; exactly the chunk's effective inputs supply material. Assembly rejects trimmed chunks. Individual oversized messages are clipped at 1.5 times the planned chunk size with a marker. Direct output is the default. The instruction resolves the chat's `tail`, the account default's, then the built-in (`BUILTIN_SUMMARY_INSTRUCTION`, the owner's Sum2 request made neutral: pause the roleplay, summarize the story so far, start where an existing summary stopped, keep language, voice, names, events, relationships and unresolved threads, at most `{{words}}` words). `{{words}}`, and a condensation's "at most N words", are the summary length in tokens as words, about 0.75 a token (`summaryWords`: 600 tokens ask for 450 words), since models follow word counts better. The chat's notes are sent only when `withNotes` resolves on (off by default): the notes stage then gates none, otherwise it passes no notes at all, since the current notes may tell of events after the chunk. Only reply text becomes the summary. Prefill, the end-of-request message (§15 "Who writes, and the direction") and the one-turn direction are suppressed: the instruction takes the end-of-request place, the request's last message, and no fallback turn is added. Output is capped at target times 2.5 and reduced when needed to fit the preserved prefix and whole chunk; clean length stops are clipped at sentence boundaries and saved as truncated. After retries, a nonempty partial response from the final transport-failed attempt can also be saved as truncated, after output checks. Refused or aborted responses are never salvaged, and drafts from earlier attempts are not reused across changed input pins.

The instruction is always one final user-role message (DESIGN §2.2), for both preset modes and both direct/tool styles; `midChatSystem` does not change that role. Its inspector piece is `lcm:instruction`. Requests retain prefix and layer cache markers and remove the history marker. Migration `0025_summary_prefix` pins the triggering reply’s assembled prefix at enqueue, by its explicit version id even if a selection changes before coalesced planning runs; startup and overflow planning fall back to the closest selected reply on the path. Summary requests reuse its frozen macro values, selected example messages, source pieces and mapping decisions when model and preset identities agree. The output allowance is applied after prefix selection. Different model or preset bindings assemble independently and are treated as cold when the actual prefix differs. Current snapshots retain that prefix alongside quiet mode, frozen tail, style, clipping cap and version pins for exact replay. LCM-off ST assembly remains under the unchanged differential oracle.

*Without the preset* (`withPreset: false`, ST's Raw; `rawSummary` in `lcm/request.ts`). The request is built from the same assembly, so the chunk is exactly the one the full-preset path renders and clips: the earlier coverage as continuity, one user message per summary (`<summary level from to>`); then a level-1 job's messages in their roles, or a condensation's parts as one block; then one final user message carrying the instruction (its instruction names "the last N summaries" without "above"). Nothing of the preset, cards or notes is sent; prefill is dropped. It shares no prefix with the chat: one breakpoint after the continuity (`summary`), or no breakpoint when there is none, lets consecutive requests read the summaries back: the next chunk's request repeats those messages byte for byte and adds the new summary after them (a single continuity message would change with every summary, and provider caches match whole messages). Its inspector pieces keep their indices: the summaries and messages point at their new messages, the rest at none, and `lcm:instruction` names the instruction. The job snapshot records `withPreset: false`, and `RebuildContext` replays either mode through the same registered `summary-request` transform. Fresh jobs supply resolved instruction settings, target and condensation range before assembly; snapshots freeze the original transform inputs in `summaryAssembly` (job, instruction parameters and input samplers). Rebuilds replay those inputs before transforms and apply the same fixed context-budget cap afterward, so plugins can derive instructions and samplers without applying their own changes twice. Earlier snapshots without that envelope retain their frozen tail and sampler replay and their original shape. The backfill estimate counts the instruction as uncached input on every request. Output checks, refusal judging, truncation and `OpenLlmRequest`'s reservation are unchanged.

`summaryAssembly.test.ts` runs real generation and rebuild handlers in a reader worker with a synthetic scoped replacement of `summary-request`, for both preset modes. It checks job metadata in stages before transforms and pinned-prefix control, derives its output from the original instruction and samplers, and checks the outgoing generation request, exact snapshot rebuild (including source indexes and breakpoints), disablement and restoration. A scoped observer also exercises every assembler consumer: ordinary context, cache warmth, summary planning and assembly, backfill estimates, settings measurements and rebuilds. Existing summary settings, prefix, condensation and fork tests retain their behavioral assertions.

**Execution registries** (`execution.ts`, `chat/replyOutput.ts`, `lcm/strategies.ts`). `serverWith` provides and exposes a scoped `ExecutionRegistry` with five registries: reply orchestration (`reply`), reply output strategies (`reply`), reply parsers (`continue-join`, §15 "Continue"; `reply-sections`, §12 "Reply sections"), summary execution strategies (`direct`, `tool`), and summary tool factories (`summary_tool`). Each built-in registers through the same scoped mechanism as plugins: replacing an ID changes execution, disabling it fails the generation/job with an unavailable error before a provider request, and scope exit restores the previous entry. The generator and summarizer capture the registry instance, then resolve entries for each generation/job attempt. Standalone service construction without this service builds the same defaults in its enclosing scope.

- A reply output factory creates a decoder per generation and optionally names its forced reply tool. The built-in emits text/reasoning and preserves tool-schema prefill validation and incremental prefix stripping. Rollout acquisition/finalization, provider attribution and version persistence remain in the generator and generation services.
- A summary strategy creates per-attempt state from the owned job and frozen snapshot, including chat/user and leaf position, chooses tool definitions, reads streaming text and interprets completed assistant turns. It returns candidate text and tool feedback; the summarizer retains provider execution, the eight-call bound, output checks, empty-output rejection, clipping, retry/salvage and fenced completion/failure writes. `direct` keeps streamed partial text for salvage and accepts final text. `tool` resolves `summary_tool` from the tool factory registry, using that factory's definition, draft reader and executor together. Draft state belongs to an attempt, never a registry entry.
- Strategies can supply an output-instruction function; tool factories can supply usage instructions. The built-in tool strategy uses its selected factory's instructions, or generic guidance to follow the offered tool's definition. A replacement tool is never told to call the old built-in name or schema. The summarizer captures strategies and a read-only view of tool factories together before assembly, and passes their instruction strings to `AssembleSummary`. Only data crosses the worker boundary. The registered summary transform applies them before budgeting and freezing the request; frozen transform inputs also drive exact rebuilds after the plugin scope closes. Built-in instruction bytes are unchanged. Direct worker callers omitting this optional catalog retain the built-in suffixes from `lcm/instructions.ts`.
- Reply orchestration (`chat/replyStrategy.ts`) owns the existing single provider turn, streaming preference, waiting-cache notification and output decoding. It receives the generation request (including fork), assembled generation, rollout, providers and per-generation decoder. Replacing `replyStrategies` changes the actual generated stream; rollout opening/closing, storage and admission stay in `ContextGenerator`.
- Worker policies are registries on `Assembler`: `leafPlanners` (`leaf`) groups raw messages into chunks, `maintenancePlanners` (`maintenance`) chooses repairs/condensations, `summaryInstructions` (`leaf`, `condensation`) renders base instructions, and `summaryStyles` (`settings`) selects the output strategy. Defaults preserve the existing midpoint/target, chunk/fork boundaries, maintenance algorithm and instruction text. Reader queries gather owned inputs and keep fixed limits; the writer still validates/enqueues/commits. Policy code never runs in a writer transaction. Missing policies fail with `AssemblyFailed` before provider execution.
- Trusted `AssemblyModules` install these worker policies using the same per-request scoped snapshot as stages, projections and transforms, in source and bundled workers. Planning and summary assembly install modules around the whole reader operation; nested assembly recognizes the same assembler and avoids installing a wrapper twice. Scope exit restores defaults, and subsequent requests/respawns receive the current module snapshot.
- Summary style is an open nonempty string (bounded to 200 characters); absent still selects `direct`. A plugin can persist another ID in `lcm.settings` and register its execution strategy, or replace the worker selector. The summarizer pins its strategy/tool view before assembly and supplies available output instructions; a missing selected strategy fails clearly before calling a provider. Rendered base instructions are frozen in `summaryAssembly.instruction.base`, so exact request rebuild remains possible after the instruction plugin unloads. Older snapshots without this field retain their previous rendering path.
- `Commands` (`commands.ts`) exposes scoped command descriptors (ID, description, input/output schemas and executor). The built-ins `history.search`, `history.rename` and `message.insert` (§3.8 `InsertMessage`) register the existing preview, rename and insertion workflows, and those RPC handlers dispatch through the registry. Commands resolve `CurrentUser` at execution and use the existing owned worker operations, atomic application, limits and invalidation. `makeCommand` validates input/output; typed RPC dispatch also validates the expected output and reports a disabled command as unavailable. Additional commands can register without changing these RPCs. This is a trusted command seam for a future agent runtime; no generic remote command endpoint, tool-offer UI or plugin loader is added.
- The client `features/chat/replyPolicy.ts` registry registers `natural`, `list`, `pooled`, `manual` and the plugin-selectable `round-robin`; `planReply` dispatches through the chat's `reply.order` (default `natural`) for both the composer's preview and submitted reply speaker/flag. With no available chosen or default policy, posts use `reply: false`, including queued sends; an unavailable per-chat policy falls back to the default when that is available. An explicit one-turn reply choice still works. The built-in registers the existing unnamed-reply fallback for chats without characters; plugins may supply their own or decline an automatic reply. Muting and guidance retain their existing behavior. As with other client registries, plugins register before rendering; registration changes do not themselves trigger React renders. Client registrations use undo disposers, which can be tied to a plugin scope.
  Reply policies receive the submitted text and whether images are attached. An image-only Send is a posted user turn: Manual waits for an explicit pick, List starts at the first character, and Pooled starts a fresh pool. Preview uses the current attachments and submission uses its captured attachments (`client/test/replyPolicy.test.ts`, `e2e/composerSpeaker.spec.ts`).
- `planningRegistry.test.ts` exercises planning overrides in source/bundled readers, maintenance suppression/restoration, registered leaf/condensation instructions and replay after unload, selected and persisted additional styles, reply orchestration and history command RPC dispatch. `executionRegistry.test.ts` exercises scoped replacements through persisted generations and durable summary jobs, unavailable failures and restoration, both summary request modes, actual replacement tool calls and exact request rebuilds. `summaryStrategies.test.ts` covers replaced tool definitions/executors, unknown tool rejection, disable/restore and isolated drafts; `client/test/replyPolicy.test.ts` and `session.test.ts` cover scoped choice replacement, disable/restore and immediate/queued sends without an unwanted unnamed generation.

**Agent rollouts** (spec/AGENTIC.md U1–U9; `agent/`, client `features/chat/agent/`). `orchestrationModes` (`agent/modes.ts`) is an internal registry with one built-in `default` planner, replaceable or wrappable by plugins. `ContextGenerator` folds state at the generating slot's parent in its fork and plans from independent settings: `agent.enabled` (absent/off: the single `reply` strategy; on: `agent` with its instructions and tools), `agent.tools` (absent: the existing default tool list), and `cards.rotation` (independent of tools). Tools on keeps the former narrator request; tools plus rotation keeps the former card-swap request; everything off keeps the plain request byte for byte. Context remains shared; turn picking uses the existing composer and decision connections. `orchestration.mode` is removed from the state schema/fold, Cast and ChangeCast, with no migration or compatibility reader. SQL baseline unchanged. A disabled default planner fails as `unavailable` before any request. The plan still names the strategy, tools, output contract, turn cap and assembly inputs; rollout snapshots retain the planner id for provenance and resume. `rolloutTools` (`agent/tools.ts`) classifies each tool as `read`, `chat_state`, `library`, `setup` or `outside` (`external` remains accepted for existing registrations).
- **Settings plan** (DESIGN §7.1). With `agent.enabled` on, the default planner runs the `agent` strategy with the contract from `output.contract` (`both` when unset), a request cap from `agent.request_cap` (below), and the chat's `agent.tools` list (state key `{ tools }`) in place of the default list when set. The tools a plan lists but nobody registered are left out. An agent plan carries its assembly (`AgentAssembly`): `AssembleContext` takes it as `agent`, the snapshot keeps it (`agentAssembly`), and `RebuildContext` passes it back. Its `instructions` are worked out from the tools actually offered and the contract. The `end-of-request` stage appends them to the end of the request as an `Agent instructions` piece, making that message when the preset has none, so the prefix is the plain reply's, unless the preset places or edits its Agent instructions prompt (§9 "Agent instructions"). Card swap (DESIGN §5.2 [D] 2026-11-06, as ST's "Swap character cards") is a card layout, with or without tools: the chat's `cards.rotation { on }` state key (`ChatState.cardsRotation`, `Mode.cardsRotation`, `ChangeCast`'s `CardsRotation`, This chat's "Card swap" switch, `CardLayoutSetting.tsx`, `chatSettingSections` entry `settings.card-layout`, order 30). An agent assembly also records `speakerCardOnly` for replay. Rotation makes the compose stage's characters the speaking character alone: the Definitions marker, the per-field markers and `{{description}}`-style macros hold only its card, examples are only its own, and notes placed with the definitions follow their card. Notes at other positions (`placedNotes`) keep their own conditions for every cast card, including with rotation on: a deliberate difference from ST's speaker-only depth prompt (CHARACTER-CONTEXT §4.1). The persona and everything else go where the preset says; nothing moves to the end of the request. With several characters, markers and preset field macros holding the card are volatile (they change with the speaker). Each left-out character goes into `skippedPrompts` as a `card` source with `field: "definitions"` and `swapped: true`, which the inspector's "Not sent this turn" list labels "(card swap: sent only on its character's turn)". A persona speaking keeps every card, as before. Assembler version 53 (chatsettings: include macro-only rotating definitions in cache warnings); `assembler.test.ts` covers both rotation paths and both marker layouts with always and own-turn notes. Continue and Write for use the plain reply strategy with the plan’s assembly; Continue retains its source prefill. Other agent turns drop preset prefills during assembly, with a `prefill_dropped` issue, so the snapshot, parser and output decoder agree with the request. A plain plan has no assembly, so its requests are unchanged.
- **Read tools** (`agent/tools/history.ts`; DESIGN §7.3, AGENTIC §4.5), registered as built-ins: `search_chat` (every word, case aside; newest first; `speaker`, `before_message`; excerpts of about 240 characters), `read_messages` (verbatim, from a message number, at most 20), `expand_summary` (named by the range it covers, as each summary in the context shows it: a first-level summary gives its messages, a higher one the summaries it condenses, up to `max_tokens`, saying how many were left out) and `search_summaries` (the most detailed first). They are causal: they read the path to the generating slot's parent in the generation's fork (`ReadPath` windows of 500 from the bottom, each message as the fork shows it), never the reply being written nor any later version of its message, and leave out hidden, generating and failed messages; stopped and interrupted messages with text remain readable. Condensation expansion follows its actual ordered child IDs, including mixed-level children. Messages are numbered as the path shows them (position from 1), with the speaker's card name, and the user's own messages with the persona's they play there. A template message (a greeting) gets its `{{char}}` and `{{user}}` filled in, and no other macros [P]. Summaries are the LCM layer at that leaf (`GetLcmState`) and what it condenses (`GetSummary` in the fork), at most 300. The path and the summaries are read once per rollout (`ToolContext.cache`). A failed read is a tool error the model sees, and a logged warning. `search_chat` reads through full-text search (reader `SearchChat`, `db/agentReads.ts`): the versions on the path to the parent, as the fork shows them (selection and replacement), whose text has a word starting with each query word, newest first, at most 200, then matched in memory as before. With at most 2,000 full-text matches in the database (a rare word) it starts from them, checking each against the path and the fork; with more (a common word) it walks the path newest first until the limit [P]; template messages are always read, to be matched with their names filled in. A fork that places inserted messages, whose numbering is the display path's, is read through the path instead [P], and so is a chat with a merge (§3.8 "The agent's read tools across threads"); a character view with no readable joined rows keeps indexed ordinary-only search so an unseen join cannot change matching behavior. Whole-path workshop/user-agent, narrator and persona searches retain their existing fallback. In a separate context they read as the reply's speaker (§3.8 "Tools in separate contexts"). `lookup_lore` (`agent/tools/lore.ts`) reads the enabled entries of the lorebooks the reply's context was assembled with: an agent snapshot freezes them as `agentLore` (the attached, the preset's and the cards' embedded books, by revision), and reader `LookupLore` matches an entry by title or uid, or every query word in its keys, title or text, key matches first. It never changes what the context admits. The synthetic `agentHistoryScale.test.ts` covers the in-memory path read (5,000 messages, 300 forks, 50 swipes): first access loads the whole path in windows and later reads reuse it.
- **Chat-state effects** (`db/rolloutEffects.ts`; AGENTIC §4.3). A `chat_state` tool writes through `ApplyRolloutEffect`, in one transaction: the notes it writes (`create`: a chat note, `origin: generation` with the effect's ref, turned on by a `note.activate`; `revise`: a revision of a note on the revision the position shows, bound by a `note.binding`), its state events, all at the rollout's slot and attached to its version (`origin: rollout`, `origin_ref` `<rollout>:<tool call>`), so they hold only while that version is shown and a swipe takes them back, and the call's receipt in `rollout_receipts`. A call already receipted writes nothing and answers with its first result, so re-running it on a resume is harmless. A rollout no longer running takes no new effects. Successful chat-state calls publish `State` to refresh the live notes and cast. The note tools read the chat where the reply is being written (`StateEventsAt` and `ChatNoteEntries` at the generating slot), so they see the reply's own effects so far; the context doesn't change mid-reply. A note the agent writes exists chat-wide as a library entity, off wherever its version isn't shown [P].
- **Chat-state tools.** `set_presence` (`agent/tools/presence.ts`): a character of the chat's cast at the position, by name, present or away from the next message on, as the user's away mark writes it (`away.set`, apart from Mute; contexts C8); a narrator is refused, never in or out of the scene. `list_notes` (`agent/tools/notes.ts`, a read tool) lists the notes the assembler reads at the position, as the chat's notes list does: title, whose, on or off, and whether the agent may change it, with an off note's text. `switch_note` turns one on or off by title. `write_note` writes a new chat note (title unique among the notes, at most 8,000 characters, at the tail as a system message or at a `depth`, `for` a character: on their turns only), marked `agent_editable` so the agent may change it again [P]. `edit_note` replaces one exact passage (`find`, `replace`) or the whole `content`; a linked note (a shared note's text) is refused.
- **The request cap** (sendmsg1, 2026-11-17; DESIGN §7.2 [D]). One agent reply is one rollout of model requests; `AgentPlan.turnCap` is the most it makes, the last without tools ("Write the reply now."), nudges counting as requests. A story's comes from the branch-owned state key `agent.request_cap { cap: 1–100 | null }` (`ChatState.requestCap`, absent: `DEFAULT_REQUEST_CAP`, 12; `Cast.requestCap`; `ChangeCast`'s `RequestCap`, null back to the default); This chat → Tools shows it as "Model requests per reply" (`RequestCapField` in `ToolsSection.tsx`: a number field saved on leaving it or Enter, "At most N model requests per reply", with a hover explanation), and the chat's settings marks list it. The cap is frozen in the snapshot's `agent.turnCap`, which Resume reads, so a resumed run keeps its own cap whatever the chat's is now. **A workshop run has no cap**: the workshop planner sets none, its snapshot has no `turnCap`, and `session.ts` treats an absent cap as none (`Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`); nothing else bounds a run (pi-agent-core has no turn limit), so it goes on until the model ends it or the user stops it, the workshop's compaction and elision keeping its context in bounds. User-facing text calls them model requests or steps, never turns. Tests: `agentInstructionsPrompt.test.ts` (a cap of 3 makes three requests, the last without tools, frozen as 3; the default is 12; Resume after the chat's cap changed to 10 keeps the run's 3), `workshop.test.ts` (fifteen tool rounds, then the answer, every request with tools; the snapshot has no cap).
- **`send_message` says who is present** (orchestr1, 2026-11-14; DESIGN §3.5 [D], §7.2; spec/AGENTIC.md §4.5). `agent.send_presence { mode: off | optional | required }` is a branch-owned state key (`ChatState.sendPresence`, absent when off; `Cast.sendPresence`; `ChangeCast`'s `SendPresence`). Off, the send tool and every request are byte for byte what they were. On, the planner's `AgentPlan.sendPresence` makes the contract tool `sendMessageWithPresence(mode)` (`agent/tools.ts`): `present`, an array of names, with no list of names in the schema, so the definition is the same for every cast and position and stays cached. `required` also makes the contract `send_message` (text alone is nudged once, as that contract does; at the turn cap the text is taken and presence stays as it was). A chat whose contract is final text only has no tool to say it with, so the setting does nothing there. The session reads the mode back from the tool the snapshot froze (`sendPresenceOf`), so a resume behaves as its first run. On a send, `declarePresence` (`agent/tools/sendPresence.ts`) resolves the names against the cast at the reply's parent (card name or model name, case and outer spaces ignored); a name nobody has is a tool error listing the cast, and the model sends again. Then `DeclareRolloutPresence` (writer, `db/rolloutEffects.ts`), one transaction keyed by the tool call like `ApplyRolloutEffect`: of the cast the version recorded, every character that isn't a narrator, isn't played by the user and isn't the speaker is away exactly when not named; the speaker is present; the user's cards and narrators stay as recorded. It rewrites the generating version's own `presence_json` (so in separate contexts a character left out doesn't read this message), and attaches an `away.set` to the version for each character whose standing changes (origin `rollout`, ref `<rollout>:<tool call>`), counting what the run's earlier `set_presence` calls already did, so the next message starts from it, a swipe takes it back, and the Cast tab's away marks list it as the speaker's. A call already receipted writes nothing (`replayed`); a rollout no longer running is refused. It is one branch's state: other branches and threads don't change. The setting is in This chat under Tools (`ToolsSection`: Replies don't say / may say / must say). Tests: `test/sendPresence.test.ts` (off and never-set requests identical; required: the record, the marks, each character's later request; wrong and missing names refused and corrected, one write, replay; optional with a narrator, a swipe and the user's own change; after a thread join, this branch only), `isolation.test.ts`.
- **Permissions** (DESIGN §4.1a; AGENTIC §4.3). The agent may change a note marked `agent_editable` (its own notes are), and a card field the card lists in `agent_editable_fields` (card doc; import and export leave it alone, and `withoutGrantedAgentEdits` keeps a restore, merge or replace from adding a field the head doesn't list). A chat's `agent.permission { note } | { card, field }, on` overrides either way (`ChatState.agentPermissions`, keyed by `permissionKey`), written by `ChangeCast`'s `AgentPermission { target, on }` at the leaf shown; `on: null` drops the chat's choice from there on, so the note's or card's own setting holds again (cardswap, DESIGN §7.3). Off by default; a refusal is a tool error naming what isn't editable. `GetAgentPermissions { chatId, slotId, forkId? }` (AgentApi, `api/agent.ts`) reads what holds at a position by the same rule: each note `notesAt` lists (title, card, linked) and each cast card's six replaceable fields, with `on` (the effective value), `own` (the note's or card's own setting) and `chosen` (the chat overrides it).
- **Agent-written notes exist only where their reply is** (phase4perm; DESIGN §7.3 [D], owner 2026-11-06). `db/agentNotes.ts`: a chat note whose first revision's origin is `generation` (`agentWrittenNotes`) exists at a position only where a `note.activate` of it is on the path (`notesNamed`), which its reply's own is exactly where that reply is shown (a later reply's `note.binding` revising it doesn't count, so it doesn't come back where its reply was swiped away; a user's later `note.deactivate` leaves it listed, since the activation is still on the path). The reader's `ChatNoteEntries` leaves it out elsewhere, so every listing built on it agrees: `ListChatNotes` (the Notes panel, its large view, note targets), the note tools' `notesAt` (`list_notes`, `write_note`'s title check, `edit_card`'s tail note) and `GetAgentPermissions`; and `replacementConflict` (one note per target) ignores it on forks that don't name it, so the user or the model can claim that target there. The assembler and inspector only see notes that are on, which it never is elsewhere. The library's note list (`ListLibrary` for `note`, which the note editor's switcher reads) leaves out every such note, on any branch (cardswap, owner 2026-11-06). Selecting another version publishes only a `Slot` event, so the client session (`selectsAnother`) also reads `chat-notes:<chat>` again when a slot event selects another version of a message shown: a swipe adds or removes the reply's note in the Notes panel and in Model may change.
- **Card edits as notes** (`agent/tools/cardEdit.ts`, `agent/noteTargets.ts`; AGENTIC §4.6, DESIGN §4.2 [D]). `edit_card { character, field, find, replace, wrap? }` never edits the card. It reads the card as the chat uses it (reader `AgentCards`: the bound revision, else the chat's override, else the library entry, with the replaceable fields and `agent_editable_fields`). `find` must be once in the field's current text: an on note replacing the field there (`replacing`, a note whose `replaces` names that field of that character's place), else the card's. The field without the passage goes in a chat note replacing it in place (`replaceEffects`: a new note with `replaces { card_field, field, card }`, or a revision of the existing one, turned on if off), so the top of the context changes once per field; the passage as it now is goes in one tail note per field and character ("Mira's current description", wrapped by `wrap`, default `[{{char}}'s current {{field}}: {{text}}]`, `{{char}}` and `{{field}}` filled in when written [P]), and a later edit naming a passage already moved there revises that note only, at the tail. A second passage moved out of the field is added to the same tail note [P]. A note replacing the field that the agent may not change refuses the edit.
- **The `agent` strategy** (`agent/strategy.ts`, `agent/session.ts`) runs one pi-agent-core 1.0.3 `Agent` per reply. Its transcript starts with an `rpRequest` custom message, which stands for the frozen assembled request. The loop starts with `continue()`, so the model is sent no user turn of the app's own.
- **Requests.** The `streamFn` builds each request as the frozen prefix plus the live suffix (`agent/wire.ts` `rolloutRequest`). The prefix is `providerRequest` of the assembled request; agent assembly has already dropped the preset prefill, since a turn that may call tools can't be prefilled. The suffix is the transcript after `rpRequest`. pi-converted APIs get the suffix as pi messages. Chat Completions gets it in the exact `payload.messages`, as assistant `tool_calls` (with `reasoning_content` on tool-call turns) and `role: "tool"` results. The summarizer's tool loop uses the same function. On explicit-breakpoint models, the last suffix message gets a tail breakpoint after the prefix's breakpoints, so the provider's marker budget drops it first. Every request goes through `Providers.stream`, attributed to the chat, rollout and version, so the ledger, the retries before the first token, transforms and the sent-context capture apply. A provider error becomes an `error` assistant message, as pi's `StreamFn` contract requires, and its typed failure fails the version with its class.
- **Output.** Text and thinking stream through the registered reply output decoder into the body. When a turn's first tool call arrives after it streamed text, the strategy emits `{ restart: true }`. `Generations` then resets the text, reasoning and sections to where the generation began, and subscribers get a `replace` delta. `throughParse` starts each reply parser afresh. Only the final turn's text is the message, and it goes through the same parsers, live rewrites and persistence as a plain reply. The last request (`turnCap`) follows an `rpHarness` message, "Write the reply now.", is sent without tools (pi-ai sends an empty list once the history holds tool calls) and ends the loop, whatever it returns. The tool hook also blocks execution at the cap, and after a reply has been sent. The cap instruction takes precedence over the send nudge, including a cap of one. Tools execute sequentially with the agent’s abort signal, so Stop interrupts a running tool before closing the rollout; their results are capped at 16,000 characters with a marker.
- **Persistence.** The snapshot written by `StartRollout` gains `agent: { mode, contract, turnCap, tools }`, the frozen tool definitions with their effect classes and labels, including `send_message` when offered. The row records `rollouts.mode`. `SaveRolloutTranscript` writes the agent's whole `state.messages` to `rollout_payloads.transcript_json` and its tool calls to `rollouts.step_count`. It runs after each `turn_end` and `agent_end`, and in the release, chained in order. Before each allowed tool executes, the hook awaits a transcript flush, preserving the pending call and its ID before any effect can commit; a failed flush blocks that call and is logged. Aborted and failed assistant turns retain their streamed text and reasoning. A process kill during a provider request can still lose that incomplete turn; completed turns and pending executed calls remain durable. The baseline adds `rollouts.step_count` and `mode`, and the `rollout_receipts` table for chat-state tool receipts (AGENTIC §4.3), and the version origin `resumed`.
- **Output contracts** (DESIGN §7.2). The snapshot's contract decides how the message is given. `final_text`: the last turn without tool calls. `send_message` and `both` add the `send_message` tool, with one `message` argument. Its complete message goes to the body only when the validated, offered tool executes, after a restart if the turn streamed text first. Partial arguments, unoffered calls and calls refused at the cap cannot publish a reply. Thinking before it stays as the message's reasoning. The tool ends the loop (`finishTurn`), and a second call in the run gets an error result. Under `send_message` alone, a turn ending in plain text is asked once to be sent (`rpHarness` "Send your reply with send_message."), and the body restarts. If the next turn is plain text again, it's taken as the message. `both` takes either.
- **Resume** (`agent/resume.ts`, DESIGN §7.5; reference-harness `recovery.ts` with the interruption policies added). `ResumeVersion` (`AgentApi`) carries on a version whose agent rollout stopped, failed or was interrupted. `planResume` strips the failed tail (assistant turns that ended `error` or `aborted`, and results a stop cut short, which carry `details: { interrupted: true }`) and picks a policy: a call without its result is run again (`rerun`; a chat-state call's receipt answers it if it was written); a turn cut off with a tool call in it is dropped and resampled; a turn cut off in its text, on a model whose prefill is `assistant`, is carried on (`continuation`): the first request ends with that text as a trailing assistant message, has no tools, and its output is appended to it, in the body and in the transcript; anything else unusable starts over from the frozen request (`fresh`). A failed turn keeps what it streamed (text, thinking, calls) for this, and the tool hook saves a call before it runs, so a crash mid-call leaves the call to run again. `StartResumedVersion` (writer, one transaction) adds a new generating version of the slot, selected, with origin `resumed` and the stopped one as its source, and its rollout, a child of the stopped one, with the same snapshot, model, mode, issues, lore activations and cast and the kept transcript; it copies the stopped version's state events, of its tool effects only those of the calls kept (effects are told apart by `origin_ref` `<rollout>:<tool call>`), with their receipts, and writes the cut tail as a `rollout_branches` row (reason `resume`, or `edit`). A second resume while one is being written is refused (`NotResumable`). `ContextGenerator` then generates without assembling: `generationOf` the frozen snapshot, the snapshot's frozen tool definitions offered as they were, the agent seeded with the kept transcript, its turn count, and its nudge. Dangling calls run first (receipts answer a chat-state call already written), their results are saved, then `continue()`, so no turn of the app's own is added and every request is the one the stopped run would have sent. **The model now** (resume1, 2026-11-12; AGENTIC §12): the resumer reads the chat's model binding at the reply as the composer shows it (`chat/shownModel.ts`: `StateEventsAt` with `displayEnd`, since an assembly reads the state before the reply), or the one "Retry with…" names, and assembles at the slot with it (no model refuses "No model is chosen for this chat."). An `AssemblyFailed` refuses as `NotResumable { savedRequest: true }` ("Its request can't be built from the chat as it is now: …"); `ResumeVersion { saved: true }` then sends the stored snapshot, model and tools unchanged, skipping the assembly (AGENTIC §12.5). **The tools now** (`toolsNow` in `api/agent.ts`, AGENTIC §12.4): the registered planner (`planTurn`) runs on the state before the reply (`StateEventsAt` at the parent slot, as the run's assembly read it) and on the state at the reply; tools it drops between the two leave the frozen list, tools it adds join it (`toolForKind`, then `offeredByGrants`), so a planner or tool replaced in code since the run changes nothing (`workshop.test.ts`). A kept tool keeps its frozen definition, the output contract's tool stays, and a list equal to the frozen one leaves the snapshot alone. The snapshot goes to `StartResumedVersion` whenever it changed, the model only when it did. The plan gets that model (its prefill decides a continuation). When it equals the frozen `inputs.model`, the frozen snapshot is sent unchanged; otherwise `forModel` (`api/agent.ts`) swaps in the new model, its samplers and context budget, empties `continuity.breakpoints`, and `StartResumedVersion` gets the new `model` and `snapshot`. `agent/wire.ts` `forTarget` drops thinking and tool-call `thoughtSignature`s from suffix turns another API or model wrote, and the Chat Completions suffix replays `reasoning_details` only to the model that wrote them; to a target of kind `deepseek`, an assistant turn with tool calls and no reasoning carries `reasoning_content: ""`, which DeepSeek's thinking mode requires; text, calls and results convert through pi-ai as before. `Regenerate` without a named model and `ContinueVersion` use `shownModel` too, so a model chosen while a stopped reply is last applies to its swipe or Continue. **Partial turns** (resume1): `session.ts` saves the turn being streamed with the transcript (`SaveRolloutTranscript`, the turn marked `aborted`, "The app stopped while this turn was written.") at most every 2 s and once 2 s after its last delta, so a kill leaves the cut text for Resume's continuation; the final flush overwrites it. A connection error ("Connection error.") is classed `network`.
- **Recovery review (2026-11-06).** Before executing a chat-state tool, the session reads its owner-scoped `RolloutReceipt`; a saved result returns before tool validation, so an already-created note or already-replaced passage cannot change the result on resume. A successful `send_message` result in the kept transcript restores that call's text through the normal output pipeline and finishes without another model request. `edit_card` checks both the replacing note and any tail note it changes: each must permit agent edits, including the per-chat override, and neither may link to shared text. All refusals happen before writing either note. `agentNotes.test.ts` covers protected and linked notes; `agentResume.test.ts` reproduces crashes after each note effect commits and after a terminal send is saved.
- **Step edits** (`planStepResume`, AGENTIC §4.4). `ResumeFromStep { versionId, step, edit? }` carries on from a step of any finished agent version (its index in the version's steps, `placedSteps`): new text for a thinking or text step keeps that turn's results and cuts what followed; new arguments for a call run it again under a new id, so its old receipt and effects stay behind, and drop the turn's later calls; a new result replaces it and cuts after it, so the turn's later calls run again; no edit cuts after the step. The new version is made as a resume's, the cut tail recorded with reason `edit`.
- **Steps** (`agent/steps.ts`, `@rp/shared/agent.ts`). `stepsOf` projects a transcript into the steps a version shows: thinking and text from turns that went on to call tools, and each tool call with its label, a one-line title from its first argument, status (`running`, `done`, `error`; a call without a result at the end failed) and result. The message's own turn and `send_message` are never steps. A plain turn that was then sent with `send_message` is. As the loop runs, the strategy emits `{ steps }` after each message, tool result and turn when they changed. `Generations` publishes them as the `Steps` chat event (the whole list each time, so a late subscriber catches up with the next one). Afterwards `GetRolloutSteps` (`AgentApi`; reader `RolloutSteps`, `db/agentReads.ts`) projects the stored transcript with the snapshot's frozen tools. A version's `steps` (`{ count, ms }`) is read with it when its rollout made tool calls: `rollouts.step_count` and the run's duration. In the same subquery (`versionExtras`), `agent: true` marks a version whose rollout ran with tools (`rollouts.mode` set), with or without steps, so the client knows which stopped replies can be resumed (resumeui). `GetRunTranscript` gives each thinking, text and tool-call part, and each tool result, the `step` index `ResumeFromStep` takes (`placedSteps` over the stored transcript; none for the message's own turn or `send_message`), and `cut`: the rollout's `rollout_branches` rows (reason `resume` or `edit`) as entries, each placed at the entry index where the kept transcript ends (`fork_index`), without step indices.
- **In the client** (phase4ui, 2026-11-05, and resumeui, 2026-11-12; AGENTIC U7 and U8; `features/chat/agent/`, registered by `registerAgent()`). `Generations` keeps the steps last sent on the running entry, and `Hello`'s `live` entries carry them (`steps`), so a tab that joins mid-run sees them. `session.ts` keeps them in `liveSteps(versionId)` (each `Steps` event replaces the list), cleared with the live text when the version stops generating. **The steps element** (`Steps.tsx`, `reasoningPanels` entry `agent.steps`, order 5: above the reasoning, as the steps came before the final turn's reasoning and text). While generating, once there are steps, a toggle reads "Working…" (pulsing) with the tool count, and the list streams: a tool row (icon by effect class, label, title, a spinner, check or cross) whose result opens under it; a thinking or text step as its first line, opening to the whole. It's open while streaming by the user's `steps` display preference (`DisplayPrefs.steps`, `expanded` by default, as `reasoning`), folded once the reply is done; folding or opening during the run writes the preference. Done, it reads "N steps · T s" from `Version.steps` (N tool calls), only for a version whose run made tool calls, and opening it reads `GetRolloutSteps` once (showing the last live steps meanwhile), with "Open the run" (the inspector at `#run-steps`). **The header badge** (`messageHeaderDetails` entry `message.steps-badge`) is the same "N steps · T s" (live count while running) as a pressed-state toggle that opens the element and scrolls it into view; the element and badge share the choice through `stepsChoice(versionId)`, and both save the streaming preference when toggled during a run. Pure parts (`steps.ts`: count, labels, `stepsView`, `isOpen`, `turnsOf`) are tested in `test/agentSteps.test.ts`. **Run inspector** (`RunSteps.tsx`, the new `runInspectorSections` slot in `ContextPage.tsx`, after the context and Not sent): `GetRunTranscript` (reader `RolloutTranscript`, `db/agentReads.ts` `transcriptEntries`) returns the frozen tool definitions and the transcript after `rpRequest` as `assistant` (thinking, text and tool-call parts verbatim, stop reason, error, and whether tools were offered on that request, from the frozen turn cap), `toolResult` and `app` (the app's `rpHarness` messages) entries. "Tools offered" shows each definition (name, label, description, parameters as JSON under a disclosure); "Steps" groups the entries into requests (`turnsOf`): what each added to the context ("Added by the app", "Result of …") and the model's answer, with each request's ledger row under it when the rows line up one for one (a retry breaks that, and the Usage table still lists every attempt); results after the last answer show as "Not sent". **Activity** (`ActivityPanel.tsx`, `chatPanels` entry `activity`, order 95): `ListActivity { chatId, before?, limit? }` (reader op, owner-scoped) groups the chat's ledger rows with purpose other than `generation`/`test` by rollout and purpose (a request without a rollout alone), newest first, 50 a page by first start, rollout/request id and purpose (`before` carries all three sort keys, preserving ties), from the `llm_requests_chat` index: kind, status (running if any request is, else the last one's), the last request's model and connection, start and duration, request count, input/cache read/cache write/output (null when any request's count is unknown), cost when every request has one in one currency, and links: a summary's request page (`summary_revisions.rollout_id`, else `summaries.rollout_id`); generated revisions carry `summaryRevisionId` in Activity and the link's `revision` parameter selects `GetSummaryRevisionRequest`, keeping the request tied to the work that row paid for or, for a judgment (`decision`), "Go to the reply". It reads again when shown and when the summaries change. Agent replies are reached from their message. **This chat settings** (chatsettings, 2026-11-06; CHARACTER-CONTEXT §1's built shared-context subset). Registered sections show Context (one shared context or separate contexts, §3.8 "The Context setting"), Tools (`ToolsSection.tsx`, `settings.tools`, order 20), Cards (`CardLayoutSetting.tsx`, order 30) and Who replies (`ReplyChoicesSetting.tsx`, order 40). Tools writes `agent.enabled` through `ChangeCast`'s `AgentEnabled`; when on, Allowed tools checkboxes write `agent.tools` in registry order. The list survives turning Tools off. `ListReplyTools` returns registered non-external tools and the default planner's offered ids with tools enabled, without exposing internal modes. Cards holds the independent Card swap switch; its help says the preset's positions and persona are preserved, with a cache-cost sentence only when on. Who replies opens the composer's existing Next picker (Auto / No one / a character), closing the settings panel first, and links to decision connections. Every control has hover/focus help. `Cast.agentEnabled` replaces `replyMode`. `e2e/chatSettings.spec.ts` covers combinations, persistence, retained tool choices, both destinations and layout at 1440/390 in both themes; `LAYOUT_AUDIT_CHAT_SETTINGS_ONLY=1` audits This chat at scale. **Model may change** (phase4perm; `AgentPermissionsSection.tsx`, `chatSettingSections` entry `settings.agent-permissions`, order 21, shown with Tools on): `GetAgentPermissions` at the leaf shown, read again on the `chat-notes:<chat>` and `library` keys; checkboxes in groups "Chat notes", "<Name>'s card" (the six fields, `CARD_FIELD_LABELS`, in equal columns) and "<Name>'s notes", each written as `AgentPermission`. A box the chat overrides (`chosen`) has a "Reset" button at the end of its row (or column), explained on hover, that writes `on: null` (cardswap). A note keeps that Reset after linking to shared text, while its checkbox stays disabled (review-cardswap): Reset clears only the chat permission, retaining the link, text and own setting; `switch_note` still uses that permission for the slot's activation. Note boxes are disabled with the reason while no note tool (`edit_note`, `switch_note`) is ticked under Tools, card boxes while `edit_card` isn't, and a linked note's always (only its shared note's editor changes it). The card's own list (`AgentEditableFields.tsx`, registered into the new `cardDefinitionSections` slot, `card.editor.definition-sections`, at the end of the Definition tab, so the side-panel and full editors both have it): six checkboxes writing `agent_editable_fields` in field order. `ToolsSection` and the section share `useReplyTools` (`replyTools.ts`). `e2e/agentPermissions.spec.ts` (a loopback provider whose replies each write a note) covers the card's list saved from the side panel and shown in the full editor, the chat's section starting from the card's and note's settings, overriding a field and resetting a note after linking it to shared text, the Notes panel listing each swipe's note only on that swipe, and the layout audit on each surface at 1440 and 390, light and dark; `test/agentNotes.test.ts` the same rule and overrides through the RPCs. `e2e/agentSteps.spec.ts` drives it with a scripted provider (`e2e/support/agentProvider.ts`: two `search_chat` calls, then the reply, held on request) at 1440 and 390, light and dark: a plain reply without steps or badge, the Tools switch and allowed tools, the running element and its sticky fold, the folded "2 steps · N s" and badge, the stored steps, the inspector's tools and requests, an Activity summary row with cost, and the layout audit on each surface. **Resume** (resumeui; DESIGN §7.5 [D]): the `messageActions` entry `message.resume` (order 25, beside Continue, pinned by default, group `change`), offered by `resumeOffer` (`agent/resume.ts`) on a version with `agent` whose status is stopped, failed or interrupted, written by the model, enabled even when it has no steps, text or reasoning (resume1: a failed first request resumes from the saved request). It calls `session.resumeVersion` (`ResumeVersion` through `slotWrite`, with the fork shown and the entry's row version; no `beforeReply`, since the run goes on from its frozen request), which applies the returned entry, so the new version is selected and streams as any reply. `NotResumable` reads "This reply can't be carried on: <the server's reason>" under the message ("…it's already being resumed."); with `savedRequest` (client reason `saved_request`) the alert adds **Send the saved request** (`resumeVersion(entry, { saved: true })`). **Beside the status** (resume1, AGENTIC §12.7; `ResumeButton` in `Message.tsx`, through `VersionBody`'s `onResume`): a model-written version that failed has Resume in its error box, and one interrupted gets a note, "The app stopped while this reply was being written.", with Resume; both call `session.resumeReply`: an agent version resumes, a plain one with text continues (`continueVersion`, no guidance), a plain one without text regenerates. The version picker names a resumed version "<model>, resumed from #N". **Step edits** (`RunSteps.tsx`): with the run finished, each box with a `step` (thinking or text before a call, a call's arguments, a call's result) has Edit and Resume from here in its header, explained on hover. Edit opens the step in the shared `CodeEditor` (arguments as JSON, mono); `stepEdit` (`agent/resume.ts`) turns the text into the `StepEdit`, or none when unchanged, and checks arguments are a JSON object fitting the tool's frozen `parameters` (type, required, properties, enum, const, items, anyOf), saying why otherwise, with Resume disabled. Resume reads the slot's row version in the viewed fork (`ReadPath` around it), calls `ResumeFromStep`, and opens the chat at the slot, where the new version is being written. Step edit text uses `useUserDraft`, keyed by the run version and transcript part/result, with the shared history and conflict notices. Closing the editor keeps its draft; a successful resume ends it. The open editor is named by `stepEdit` in the run URL, so reload restores it with its text. Each `cut` span shows before the entry it was cut at as a dashed, folded `Disclosure` ("Cut when this step was edited" / "Cut when this reply was resumed", `data-run-cut`) holding its entries verbatim, without actions. `test/agentResume.test.ts` (client) covers the offer and the edit checks; `e2e/agentResume.spec.ts` (the scripted provider, now with `hold(at)` and `fail(at)`) at 1440 and 390, light and dark: a reply stopped after its first call resumes as a new version that sends the same request; showing the stopped version again while that runs and resuming it is refused in words; a failed reply resumes; the inspector shows the resume's cut, a result is edited and resumed from, the model is sent the edited result, and the new run's inspector shows the edit's cut folded; layout audit on the message (stopped, refused, failed) and the inspector (editing, cut open). `agentResume.test.ts` (server) covers the step indices, `cut` and `agent`.
- `test/agentTools.test.ts`: a scripted narrator searches for its own reply's words and for the greeting's, reads the messages and opens a summary in a chat without any. Only messages 1 and 2 are found and read, for the reply and again for a second version of it.

Through generation: a stop mid-tool resumes as a new version that runs the call again, whose request is the first one's plus the call and its result, with the same tools; a second resume meanwhile is refused; the rollout is a child with the same snapshot. A reply interrupted mid-call (as a restart leaves it) resumes with a request identical to the one the run had sent. Text cut off by a dropped connection goes on through a prefill without tools. A new result for a lookup keeps an earlier `set_presence` effect; new arguments for that call run it under a new id and drop its old effect.

- **Resume review hardening** (review-resume1, 2026-11-13; AGENTIC §12.8). `shownModel` resolves the account default when the reply's binding was removed, before assembly reads the parent. Resume and provider-backed Continue/Regenerate refuse an absent choice before creating a version. `GeneratorShape.requiresModel` is true for `ContextGenerator`; local and plugin generators may omit it and keep working without a provider model. A changed model checks the frozen request, kept transcript, tool definitions and continuation with reader `CountRolloutContext` against its new context budget before any pending tool executes; an oversized run asks for more room without trimming it. Unchanged-model replay keeps its prior behavior (including the existing small-budget workshop default), preserving the frozen request. A dangling call reads its durable receipt before looking for its executable tool, so removing a tool cannot erase the result of a completed write. Receipt-read failure parks the run rather than guessing whether to execute. `VersionEffects` also accepts matching source/current receipts whose recovered text equals the resumed transcript result as proof of a carried effect when a crash prevented the original result from flushing; this retains Changes, Undo and the regeneration warning without attributing an unrelated call solely by its id. The agent obtains the target's pi provider identity from `ProviderRegistry` for thinking/signature conversion; kinds such as Bedrock and Vertex retain their own signed thinking, while a provider switch with the same API and model key drops foreign thinking. No persistent schema or baseline change; `CountRolloutContext` adds an optional continuation for sizing. `Message.tsx` reuses the status note and Resume button for stopped replies as well as interrupted/failed ones, including plain replies.
