Slow `resumeKill` additionally kills before any response byte, during reasoning, inside tool-call JSON and a UTF-8/SSE frame, while a workshop approval waits, and during a delegated reply after library creation, chat setup and an earlier posted message. It verifies no automatic request on restart, fresh consent, one copy of each committed effect and no duplicate delegated send. `resumeSaveScale` measures three simultaneous stalled replies at 5,000 messages, 300 forks and 50 versions per message (250,000 versions per chat), concurrent Stop from two tabs, a late save and deletion. `replyResume` exercises failed and stopped plain replies at 1440/390 in light/dark with layout assertions; the focused Resume layout audit also covers agent messages and the inspector.

Assembler version 47 fences snapshots made before these assembly corrections; no schema change.

A second `send_message` in the turn gets an error result, and the first is the reply. The cap's request has no tools and ends the loop. **Workshop chats, server** (workshop1, 2026-11-12; spec/WORKSHOP.md W1). The scoped `ExecutionRegistry.chatKinds` registry (`@rp/shared/chatKinds.ts`) maps a stored kind to its planner and `allowsOutside` policy. Built-ins: `rp` → `default`, outside effects refused; `workshop` → `workshop`, outside effects allowed. Planners receive both the kind and the causal folded state. A disabled kind or planner fails before a provider request; replacing a profile changes planning through the same registry as plugins. The RP plan, assembly inputs and provider bodies stay unchanged.

- `agent/workshop.ts` registers the workshop planner: the `agent` strategy, contract `both` unless `output.contract` overrides it, cap 40, and the fixed built-in workshop toolset `list_library`, `read_card`, `read_preset`, `read_lorebook`. Story `agent.tools` preferences cannot override workshop capabilities; plugins replace the registered workshop planner to change its toolset. W1 originally had one message per turn and fresh assembly each turn; W5 below extends this. The existing stopped-run Resume and Resume from a step work for workshop rollouts; carrying on the previous turn and several messages are separate work. The profile filters external tools both for fresh and resumed execution, and the loop also checks the policy before an external call. W1 adds no tools that change the library, settings or outside world.
- `WorkshopApi.CreateWorkshop { title? }` (`workshopApi.ts`, `api/workshop.ts`) creates a chat of kind `workshop`. `db/workshopWrites.ts`, installed beside the library writers so it can share their revision steps, performs one transaction: validate each saved default against the user and kind, create missing seeds, write the registered user setting `workshop.defaults { card, preset }` (card entity id and preset ref id), create the chat, join the Assistant and the account persona (not for a side chat beside a story, workfix1), set the persona as played by the user, bind the preset, write LCM settings with LCM off, and insert the Assistant's current saved greeting as an ordinary template version. (Since workctx1: the card and persona can be chosen, the persona is the workshop's own and LCM starts as a story's; see "Workshop context" below.) The model follows the account default. The default title is “Workshop”.
- The Assistant card and Workshop preset are ordinary editable library entries, created once per user and reused. Their first revisions have origin `import`, with `origin_ref` `builtin:workshop-assistant@1` and `builtin:workshop-preset@1`. Deleting either seed causes only that seed to be recreated at the next workshop; the other seed and its edits survive. A saved default naming another user's item is never reused.
- The seeded prompt order is Main, Definitions, chat history and newest message. Main describes an assistant working on the app; the Assistant's description asks for practical, brief, factual replies. The registered `workshop-instructions` assembly stage follows `end-of-request`, adding the last user instruction as a “Workshop instructions” inspector piece. It expands macros and uses a `workshopTurn` preset prompt when present, outside the normal order (even if an edited order contains it). `AgentAssembly.workshop` and the instruction text are frozen in the snapshot and replayed. RP's existing agent-instruction piece stays as it was. Assembler version 56 fences older replay implementations.
- Library tools (`agent/tools/library.ts`) use the existing owner-scoped `ListLibrary` and `OpenEditor` readers. `list_library { kind, query?, limit? }` filters names, subtitles and tags, returning names and ids, default 20 and at most 100. The three read tools resolve a name, ref id or entity id against the user's live and archived entries, returning an ambiguity error with candidates rather than choosing a duplicate name. They read the saved head, exclude unsaved drafts, and return its revision and document; `read_card` accepts field selection and retains alternate greetings, its embedded lorebook and agent-editable fields. Results use the existing rollout result budget. No new reader operations were necessary.
- Workshop replies write rollouts of kind `workshop` and ledger requests of purpose `workshop`, including Continue and Write for. They are interrupted on startup and resumed through the existing rollout machinery. Activity excludes workshop requests because they make timeline messages. Reply metrics and model last-use reads include them. No baseline tables or columns changed: this uses existing `chats`, library revisions/refs, `settings`, state events, slots/versions, rollouts and request ledger storage.
- `test/workshop.test.ts` covers seeded creation and edit/replacement, a scripted provider's library read and reply, causal piece order, frozen request/tool replay, instruction overrides, workshop purpose and Activity, the outside-tool distinction, library-head reads and ownership. Existing generation/agent tests retain their exact request assertions; `isolation.test.ts` classifies the new authenticated RPC as caller-only creation.

**Workshop kind review (review-workshop1, 2026-11-12).** Profiles now live in the shared scoped `chatKinds` registry, exposed by `ExecutionRegistry.chatKinds`. `ChatKind` and worker row DTOs accept registered strings; storage membership remains writer-validated. Profiles select rollout kind and request purpose as well as the planner and outside-tool policy, so a plugin kind can reuse workshop execution without core string comparisons. Trusted `StateModules` installers receive this registry as their fourth argument, applying the same registrations in the main thread and source/bundled workers. Client registrations use the shared registry. `workshopKinds.test.ts` round-trips a plugin kind through real RPC and both worker modes, replaces its planner, and checks stored rollout/request attribution.

**Workshop operation boundaries (review-workshop1, 2026-11-12).** Kind profiles declare summary, merge, ST import and export support. Workshops support plain-text export, ordinary listing/opening/search, branches and split-chat views; they refuse merges (as source or destination), ST history imports into the existing chat and ST JSONL export. The existing merge picker excludes unsupported kinds, and its preview/write workers both enforce the profile. Export format choices and the file serializer use the same profile. Summary settings cannot enable LCM through any state writer, explicit enabling/backfill and enqueue operations refuse unsupported kinds, and planning returns an empty disabled plan even if old settings say on. Generic chat creation also starts unsupported kinds with LCM off. `workshopPolicies.test.ts`, client `chatExport.test.ts` and `workshopBoundaries.spec.ts` cover these paths; `LAYOUT_AUDIT_WORKSHOP_ONLY=1` runs the same four viewport/theme cases and dialog measurements through `layoutAudit.spec.ts`.

**Outside-effect resume guard (review-workshop1, 2026-11-12).** Each tool executor checks the kind's outside-effect policy as well as the normal pre-call hook. A dangling call replayed directly during Resume or a step edit therefore cannot bypass that check. `workshop.test.ts` injects an outside executor after planning filters it, verifies that no effect runs, and verifies that editing its unoffered RP call is refused before a new version or request is created; the workshop still executes that tool once.

**Seed lifecycle verification (review-workshop1, 2026-11-12).** `workshopSeeds.test.ts` checks eight concurrent creations share one card/preset pair, archived seeds are reused, deleted seeds are replaced, and both older workshops and a new one can still generate replies after both original seeds are deleted. It also checks a large library read is capped at the rollout result budget and stored connection secrets are absent from the transcript. Existing workshops use the normal missing-library fallback rules; deletion does not rebind their old events to the new seeds.

**Workshop setup tools and undo** (workshop3, 2026-11-12; spec/WORKSHOP.md W3). This implements the proposed W3 subset, without promoting any proposal to Decided. The delta from reference-harness's `tools/side-effects.ts` is the spec's finer `library`, `setup` and `outside` classes, transactional receipts and explicit undo records, rather than a compensation/fork boundary.

**W3 integration with W2 and Resume (review-workshop3 follow-up, 2026-11-12).** The registered workshop planner offers all four library reads and all four setup tools, independently of story tool preferences. Frozen offers include their capability and plain step-title metadata, survive Resume and step editing with the original schemas, and retain the inspector metadata imported with W2. Setup steps use the existing row to say, for example, “Created the card Mara Quill”; W4 adds each change's Undo and Open under it (“Workshop approvals and undo” below). Kept calls carry their receipts to the resumed rollout. Chat-state effects follow the existing version-copy rules; library/setup effects remain canonical independent records on their originating rollout, visible in the workshop’s effects list and undoable after Resume. Editing an earlier step leaves discarded calls’ library changes and effect records intact: if the model then chooses a new create call, it makes a separate card and effect. No old change is silently repeated or undone. A dangling setup call without a receipt still refuses pending W4’s approval flow.

`WorkshopApi.ListWorkshopCapabilities` is an authenticated, owner-scoped read over the existing chat/state readers and the registered kind planner, tool metadata and `ExecutionRegistry.workshopCapabilities`. It returns only registered capabilities of tools offered for that kind. The chip reads this server result instead of maintaining a separate client catalog: library reads say “Always allowed”; W4 adds each row's choice and the grants behind it (below). Story chats return no workshop capabilities; other users cannot inspect the list. Registrations can replace labels or change the planner’s offered set. `workshopEffects.test.ts`, `workshopKinds.test.ts` and the isolation matrix cover the read; `workshopEffects.test.ts` exercises an actual stop after creation, receipt-preserving Resume, an earlier-step edit and undo. `workshop.spec.ts` and the workshop layout audit cover three capability rows, creation labels and effects retained after editing an earlier read result at 1440/390 in both themes. The W3 baseline changes remain; this follow-up adds no baseline table or column.

**Setup bounds (review-workshop3).** All four setup argument schemas reject unknown fields, including nested edit alternatives. Execution validates them again after receipt lookup. Names, lookups and titles allow 200 characters; text fields allow 65,536; tags, alternate greetings and edit lists allow 32 entries; chat casts allow 16 cards. The worker caps each persisted document at 262,144 UTF-8 bytes, each clone at 32 owned notes and 1,048,576 bytes including active drafts, and greeting setup at 33 options per card, 128 options overall and 1,048,576 bytes including frozen macros. A run permits 32 successful non-read calls and 128 effect rows; excess work rolls back with a correctable error. Receipted calls still replay after a limit is reached. These bounds apply to the built-in setup operations; trusted plugin tools retain responsibility for their own work limits. Regression coverage: `workshopEffects.test.ts`.

**Created-card undo review (review-workshop3).** Creation recipes also pin the owned-note set. Undo refuses if a note was added, removed or changed, including unsaved note drafts, before hiding its card. A clone’s untouched notes can be undone individually in either order with its card, and revisions restored by successful undos still count as unchanged. All checks and draft restorations share the writer transaction. `workshopEffects.test.ts` reproduces added and edited note cases.

**Registered workshop effects (review-workshop3).** Setup and undo resolve the chat-kind profile in the worker, requiring its outside-effect policy and workshop rollout kind. The baseline fences effects to workshop rollouts and owned targets without hard-coding the built-in chat kind, so registered workshop kinds can reuse the operations in source and bundled workers. Story profiles remain refused. `workshopKinds.test.ts` exercises both worker modes. **BASELINE CHANGED**.

**Dynamic tool loading** (toolload1, 2026-11-12; statuses in spec/TOOL-LOADING.md). Registries on `ExecutionRegistry`: `toolLoadingProfiles` (per chat kind, the immediate tools: `rp` → `*`, `workshop` → `list_library`), `toolLoadingWires` (per wire API, which models carry deferred tools: `anthropic-messages` for connection kind `anthropic` and the measured Sonnet/Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet/Opus/Haiku 5.5 versions, including dated aliases; `openai-completions` for connection kind `openrouter`, `anthropic/claude-` Sonnet/Haiku 4.5 or Sonnet/Opus/Haiku 5.5, when the model's routing pins one upstream (`pinnedRoute`) that is `anthropic` or `google-vertex`; no other native built-in wire enabled; dispatcher profiles below), `skills` (`agent/skills.ts`) and `toolLoaders` (`tool_search`, `load_skill`; `agent/tools/loading.ts`). `agent/loadingPlan.ts` splits a fresh run's offer: with no profile, no supporting wire or nothing left over, the offer and every request are exactly as before. Deferred tools are frozen with `deferred: true`; all offered skills, registered or card-carried (`extensions.rp_harness.skills`, persona cards left out), are frozen as `agent.cardSkills`. The session (`agent/session.ts`) derives the loaded set from successful loading results' `details.loaded`, refuses calls to unloaded deferred tools, checks a call-specific capability (`RolloutTool.capabilityFor`: a card's own skill needs `skills.card`, default Ask first), and passes `toolLoading` (deferred definitions and load points) to `Providers.stream`. The transforms in `providers/toolLoading.ts`, registered first: Anthropic declares every tool, marks deferred ones `defer_loading`, moves the tool cache marker to the last immediate tool and turns each loading `tool_result` into `tool_reference` blocks with its text after the message's tool results; OpenRouter (`openrouter-tool-loading`) marks deferred tools `function.defer_loading` on every request without ever changing the flags, moves pi-ai's tool cache marker off deferred tools to the last immediate one, and appends the loaded definitions as JSON lines to each loading call's tool message after "Loaded tool definitions (call them by name):"; the disabled candidate Responses transform sends immediate tools only and adds a client `tool_search_call`/`tool_search_output` pair after each loading call's output, with `namespace` on later calls of loaded tools. `RolloutTranscript.tools[]` has `deferred`, `loadedBy` and `tokens` (each definition counted with the run's model's text counter), and the run inspector (`RunSteps.tsx` `Tools`) groups them as sent from the start, loaded during the run (with the loader) and never loaded. The built-in skills are offered in every workshop whatever its card (Decided); a card's own skills come on top, and `{ "use": id }` only adds a registered `always: false` skill. `CreateWorkshop` writes no skills onto the seeded Assistant card. `CountRolloutContext` counts a deferred tool only once loaded. The workshop capability chip lists `skills.card` when the kind's plan defers a tool. Operation tools retain their original `parameters` for frozen offers and full argument validation. Only the registered `openrouter-openai-tool-schemas` compatibility shim (OpenAI models on OpenRouter Chat Completions) uses `portableParameters` (`providers/toolSchemas.ts`) on the wire: `pattern`s with Unicode property escapes are dropped and a non-object schema becomes an empty object schema. Other providers retain their original request bytes; the shim can be replaced or disabled. SQL baseline unchanged.

**Tool dispatcher** (calltool1, 2026-11-13; TOOL-LOADING §11.1(b) [D], other implementation details follow its proposals). `ExecutionRegistry.toolLoadingWires` also registers the replaceable `dispatcher` fallback. Automatic uses it only for direct `deepseek-flash` and OpenRouter `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` pinned to `deepseek` or `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` pinned to `amazon-bedrock`, the live profiles measured in TOOL-LOADING §11.1. Measured native profiles take precedence. Other targets send every tool unless Connection → Advanced → Tool loading explicitly selects “Try dispatcher (untested)”; “Every tool from the start” disables loading. `ProviderSettings.toolLoading` is stored in existing provider-settings JSON and frozen into `ModelInput`; an active run keeps its choice. Chat-kind profiles still bound whether any tools are deferred, preserving RP. No SQL baseline change.

The dispatcher declares only immediate tools, the loaders, the output-contract tool and one fixed `call_tool {name, arguments}`. Deferred definitions are JSON lines in successful load results, labelled as data, assembled at the same transcript-derived load points by `agent/dispatcher.ts`. The array stays fixed through loads, with the existing tool-free final/cut-text request exception. Completed inbound dispatcher calls resolve to the real tool before pi-agent receives them: transcript, steps, approval identities, receipts, Changes, Undo, Resume and step edits all use the real name/arguments and original call id. Providers captures the actual raw request before this canonicalization. Immediate tools and loaders must be called directly; recursion is refused. Names are exact and `call_tool` is reserved across ordinary tools, variants and operation exposures. Unknown, unoffered, unloaded and Off targets return the unknown-tool text. Targets must already be loaded before their assistant turn; parallel calls retain sequential execution.

`fitsTool` validates a copy against the full frozen JSON schema without coercion, before consent/execution, and the executor repeats this for dangling calls. Tool-specific full Effect validation and worker target/permission checks still run. Before cloning or recursive validation the walk bounds depth to 48, values to 32,768 and key/string characters to 262,144. Oversized arguments are refused and omitted. Refusal markers are app-owned transcript metadata: a crash cannot turn a rejected dispatcher call of an immediate tool into an allowed direct call. An argument edit creates a new id, clears the marker and validates again. Card skill text remains frozen and behind approval; loaded descriptions confer no permissions.

Only request construction wraps canonical deferred calls back into `call_tool` and pairs their result names on name-bearing wires, including refusals and repeated call ids. The transport definition is frozen/reused on ordinary Resume alongside the real tools. Provider defaults are resolved before freezing the mode. On a model-switch Resume, native/every-tool modes replay real direct calls with their declared definitions; dispatcher reconstructs wrappers and definition text. The original frozen offer, partition and skills remain in force (a run that already offered everything retains its immediate tools until a fresh turn). Inspector transport metadata follows the selected target. Connection help and existing continuity notices explain the one-time full input cost of a different tool list. DeepSeek's replayed reasoning uses `agent/wire.ts` field handling; dispatcher requests also supply an empty `reasoning_content` for a tool call without visible thinking, including a model-switch replay. Assembler version 68 fences the combined request shapes (the dispatcher originally used 64). Native provider transforms/serializers and their request bytes are unchanged.

Dispatcher review hardening (review-calltool1, 2026-11-13): completed dispatcher-mode calls also check the provider's original argument JSON, captured by `providers/toolArguments.ts` for Chat Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages. Streaming previews repaired by pi-ai cannot authorize a completed malformed call. The output-contract tool receives the same bounded, non-coercing validation. A validation refusal remains durable across a mode switch; changing its arguments under a new call id still validates the replacement. Dispatcher context recounts (carried turns and model-switch Resume) render the same wrappers and loaded text definitions, counting only the fixed declared array; native/every-tool recounts keep their original path. Current capability availability is checked before returning a schema error, so an Off tool has the same unknown-name response even with invalid arguments. This availability check never asks for approval; full validation still precedes descriptions, consent and execution. Native and every-tool validation/request paths retain their previous behavior.

The master merge retains Resume's explicit settings-change policy and completed-receipt recovery. Its model-switch path updates the dispatcher transport metadata beside the frozen real catalog and preserves the one-time full-input-cost notice. Assembler version **68** is above both merged branches. No SQL baseline change.

Regressions: `dispatcher.test.ts` (malformed/bounded inputs, full schema constraints/coercion, exact names/reserved/immediate targets, definition escaping/provenance, parallel canonical round trips, measured profile matrix); `dispatcherWorkshop.test.ts` (real loop, approvals, unknown/unloaded/Off refusals, canonical steps/transcript, kept receipts/effects and Undo, every/native/dispatcher Resume switches, parked approval across restart and DeepSeek reasoning); existing toolLoading/review/router/workshop, operationTools, providerShims and agentResume suites. Browser `toolLoading.spec.ts` covers native and dispatcher inspector groups after restart; connection tests and `LAYOUT_AUDIT_DISPATCHER_ONLY=1` audit the new Advanced choice at 1440/390 in light/dark. No provider calls were made by this job.
**Resume with tool loading, and the workshop's later tools** (merge-batch9, 2026-11-13). The resumer (`api/agent.ts`) treats a model as changed only when its connection, model or connection revision differs from the frozen one. Settings edited on the same model since the run (samplers, an OpenRouter route pin) leave the frozen request byte for byte, so a run's tool loading keeps the route it was planned for, as AGENTIC §12.3 says for the same model. On a changed model, the size check counts the tools as the session will send them: on a model whose registered wire defers tools (`loadingWireFor`), a deferred tool that the kept transcript hasn't loaded (`loadedSet`) takes no room, as `ContextGenerator` already counted for a carried turn, so a run is no longer refused on a smaller window that its actual request fits. A carried workshop turn's elision recounts with the same rule. The built-in skills cover the workshop tools added beside them: `presets-lorebooks` adds `edit_preset` and `edit_lorebook`; a `this-workshop` skill holds the conversation's own history tools and `read_run`; `stories` adds `read_chat`, `search_chats` and the three rewrite tools. A side chat's four story tools are immediate in the `workshop` profile, because its instructions send it to them; only a side chat is offered them. Tests: `resumeToolLoading.test.ts` (a smaller window that fits the request as sent; the run's frozen skills and loads after a card with its own skill joins) and `toolLoading.test.ts` ("beside a story…").

**Threads with the workshops** (merge-batch9, threads TH4–TH8 with batch 8's side chats and workshop history tools). Assembly now gives a whole-path reply with a character speaking a stretch view (`Generation.viewers` = the speaker and `STRETCH_VIEW`), so a workshop's own runs carry one too, where they used to carry none. `read_run`'s rule that a separate context's character reads only its own runs therefore leaves a stretch view out: it filters only a separate join's stretch, and the workshops `read_run` is offered in have no joins, as the history tools read a stretch view whole where no separate join is on the path. Without that, a workshop couldn't read its own earlier steps (`workshopContext.test.ts`, the elision and regenerated-middle-reply cases). A side chat's story tools still read with no viewers (`viewers: null`), so they read the user's whole thread, joined rows included, while a story character in a separate join's stretch gets TH8's uniform refusal. The queued send's `story_at_json` moved into the `sendOrQueue` helper that `SendToThreads` shares. Assembler version 67, above both sides' 66.

Side-chat review hardening (review-calltool1, 2026-11-13): `read_run` withholds both arguments and results for positioned or undeclared tools when the earlier run's story position/stamp no longer stands. Search queries and rewrite arguments can contain story text too; filtering results alone is insufficient. The catalog guard checks native and dispatcher loading partitions, including the loaders' explicit conversation-only declarations, and its negative control fails with an undeclared deferred `get_cast`. A real fake-provider dispatcher side chat verifies the selected branch's cast, setup approval, exact write, Changes entry and Undo against a sibling sentinel.

Positioned operation approval rows omit the internal chat/fork/slot coordinates; the existing structured branch/range scope supplies their user-facing identity. `features/workshop/StoryScope.tsx`, shared by approvals and Changes rows, reads owned `ListForks` to render the current branch-menu name after a rename. Saved display metadata remains the fallback for a deleted branch, with “(deleted)” when the live list confirms its absence. Changes' existing undo JSON also records the validated story position for presentation; Undo still reads its original worker-owned recipe and proofs. Branch-list changes refresh this presentation through the existing branch notification mechanism, and reopening/focusing reads it again. The side-panel Changes control, per-change Undo and Undo all retain their existing placement and behavior; default reversible rewrites still run without asking. Browser tests cover renamed approvals and saved/deleted Changes at 1440/390, light/dark. SQL baseline unchanged.

Tool-loading review (2026-11-13): native loading is limited to the measured direct Anthropic versions and pinned OpenRouter Claude profiles above; dispatcher defaults use only their separately measured exact profiles. Native Responses loading remains an offline-tested disabled candidate. `load_skill` reads the frozen offer only, so registry edits, disablement and restart cannot silently substitute skill instructions. Reserved registry names cannot be shadowed; ambiguous card-carried names are omitted. Imported descriptions and source-card names never enter the always-visible skill index: it contains a validated name and fixed approval notice. Model-facing `read_card` removes the skill extension before field projection; stored documents and export/import retain it. At most 16 entries, 300 description characters, 8,000 instruction characters and 64 tool patterns per entry are consumed. Only successful loader results paired with preceding matching calls contribute loads. A changed card, frozen skill or tool catalog rejects continuity and rebuilds the request, resetting loads; unchanged turns, Resume and step edits retain their transcript-derived loads. These guards apply when either offer defers tools, preserving RP and unprofiled requests. `toolLoadingReview`, `toolLoading`, `toolLoadingWorkshop` and card-export tests cover the boundaries; browser `toolLoading.spec.ts` verifies inspector groups after a process restart. The layout detector treats a zero-size flex-growing action toolbar as a spacer even when it retains hidden controls, avoiding a false unequal-gap report between message details and branch controls; a synthetic browser detector regression covers it. Baseline unchanged.

**Workshop skills in every mode** (wsb2, 2026-11-15; TOOL-LOADING §5, §6, §10; WORKSHOP-CONTEXT §4.2, §4.3). `planToolLoading` lists skills whenever the kind's profile leaves tools for loading (`loadableTools`), whatever the wire: with no supporting wire (Every tool from the start, or an unmeasured model) the offer is every tool plus `load_skill` after them, nothing deferred, its description the same frozen index, and the listed skills frozen in `agent.cardSkills`. Loading then returns instructions only; a card's own skill still needs `skills.card`. RP and kinds without a profile keep their exact offer. Continuity compares cards, skills and tools when either snapshot defers a tool or carries skills. An existing every-tool workshop rebuilds once on its next turn (its tool list gains `load_skill`). The preset markers are filled: `ContextGenerator` passes `AgentAssembly.skills { kind, registered, loadable }` (`skillMarkerInput`, admin-only tools filtered by `offerableTools`), and the compose stage lists the run's skills with the same `offeredSkills` from the cast's non-persona cards at the assembled revisions. `skillsIndex` sends the installed skills (`skillsIndexText`, load_skill's own index lines); `cardSkills` sends the card's skill names only (`cardSkillsText`) with the fixed approval notice, never their description, instructions or the card's name. Each is placed only where the preset has the marker and it is on (the seeded preset has both off), as an assembler piece `workshop:<id>`; summarizing requests skip them. `@rp/shared/cardSkills.ts` holds the card-skill format, limits and reading (`readCardSkill`, shared with the server) and `cardSkillProblems`/`duplicateSkillNames` for the editor. Client: `features/workshop/CardSkills.tsx`, registered as `card.skills` in `cardEditorSections` (the Extra tab, which now holds `extensions.rp_harness` for search's Go to), lists the entries in a `SortableList` with a row context menu, marks references to installed skills, shows why an entry is skipped or shortened, and adds or edits one in a dialog (name, what it's for, instructions, tools); it writes the value field `extensions.rp_harness`, other keys kept. Editing is not approval: the server asks before any card skill's text reaches the model. The workshop start card (`StartCard.tsx`) adds Assistant and You choices from the registered card picker (`CardPicker` gains `personasOnly` and `rowHint`), kept in the URL (`workshopCard`, `workshopPersona`, `none` for no persona) and sent as `CreateWorkshop { card?, persona? }`; the defaults never change. `GetWorkshopDefaults` adds `makesPersona` while the first workshop would still make the persona. Tests: server `workshopSkills.test.ts` (every, native and dispatcher modes: identical tools and system across a deny, an allow and a built-in load, each request extending the previous one's messages; the card's description never sent and its instructions only after the allow), browser `workshopSkills.spec.ts` (1440/390, light/dark, layout audits). Baseline unchanged.

**Workshop skills review** (review-wsb2, 2026-11-15). A card skill's approval is bound to its exact content. `RolloutTool.approvalTarget` (beside `capabilityFor`) gives `load_skill` a digest of a card skill (`cardSkillDigest`: the card's entity and name, the skill's name, description, instructions and tools, from the run's frozen offer). The permit puts it in the approval's digest and in `ApprovalPrompt.grantTarget`; "Allow in this workshop" on such a prompt writes `workshop_grants (chat, skills.card, target = digest, allow)` instead of the capability's standing (`AnswerToolApproval` reads the target from the stored prompt, never from the client), and a later load of the same digest in the same workshop runs without asking (`WorkshopGrants { target }`). Any change to the skill or its card's name, the same-named skill of another card, and another workshop or account ask again; a decline is never remembered. `skills.card` now offers only Off and Ask first (an earlier standing Allowed reads as Ask first), and choosing its standing in the chip forgets the remembered digests (`SetWorkshopGrant` deletes the capability's targeted rows). A card's instructions cannot close the `<skill>` element of their result. The skill markers are sent only where the compose stage filled a preset marker (`compose { filled }`): a story or workshop preset prompt that merely has the identifier `skillsIndex` or `cardSkills` is sent, or not, exactly as before wsb2, and a user prompt of that name is counted once. With every tool sent from the start `load_skill`'s description says only that it returns instructions (`loadSkillDescription(skills, false)`); its definition is about 260 tokens for the eight built-in skills (277 in the loading modes), the cost an every-tool workshop pays once per request, cached after the first, and why `workshopContext.test.ts` carries with a 37k window instead of 36k. `ASSEMBLER_VERSION` stays 81: a snapshot stored before wsb2 has no `agentAssembly.skills` and rebuilds to its own bytes, and a new one stores what the markers were filled from. `cardSkillProblems` follows `readCardSkill` step for step (a name or reference over 48 characters is cut, not skipped; unusable tool names are reported), `isSkillReference` decides what the editor shows as a reference, and a reference row says it offers the installed skill of that name "if there is one" (the client has no list of installed skills). The start card drops a `workshopCard` or `workshopPersona` id the library doesn't have (deleted, another account's, or not a persona) from the URL instead of sending it. Tests: `workshopSkillsReview.test.ts` (every, native and dispatcher modes: allowed once in a workshop, loaded again without asking, asked again in another workshop and after an edit, the changed words never sent when declined; digest, element, marker and story-preset parity cases), `cardSkillsReview.test.ts` (hostile names, editor reasons against the reader), browser `workshopSkillsReview.spec.ts` (keyboard and drag reorder, 17 maximal skills, Back, a second tab, unknown ids). Baseline unchanged.


**Extensible undo results (review-workshop3).** `rollout_effects.undo_json` is immutable for every kind. A separate object, `undo_result_json` (returned as `undoResult`), records the successful undoer’s result, atomically with its one-way undo timestamp. This supports later setting revisions, changeset outcomes and plugin revert commits without adding kind-specific columns or making recipes mutable. Revision-chain undo reads its new head from that result. A database CHECK couples the result and timestamp; neither can be written a second time. A synthetic registered plugin undoer tests non-revision results and repeat undo in source and bundled workers in `workshopEffectSchema.test.ts`. **BASELINE CHANGED**.

**Effect-recipe constraints (review-workshop3).** The baseline checks a revision recipe’s ref as well as both revisions against the target entity, requires integer current/previous row versions, and requires a chat-creation state stamp. Revision undo results must name a revision of that target and an integer row version. Invalid effect writes roll back their receipts. `workshopEffectSchema.test.ts` rejects wrong refs, missing row versions and missing chat recipes. **BASELINE CHANGED**.

**Story persistence parity (review-workshop3).** The new fallback receipt recorder runs only for profiles that permit outside effects; RP chat-state tools retain their existing atomic success receipts and their former refusal rows. Kind resolution also omits workshop capability metadata from story tool definitions, preserving frozen story snapshots even when library reads are explicitly selected. `workshopEffects.test.ts` reproduces both persistence changes, checks forged setup calls and cross-owner card/preset/model IDs, and proves create-card receipt replay through Resume, effects retained across regeneration/version purge, source-chat cascades, and serialized repeated/concurrent undo. No story provider definitions or request pieces change.

- **Registered tools and policy.** The workshop planner now defaults to the four library reads plus `create_card`, `edit_card`, `clone_card` and `start_chat`. `agent/tools/setup.ts` registers the setup tools with `library.write` or `chats.setup` capability metadata, retained in frozen tools and the transcript inspector. The existing step DTO keeps its three display classes; refined classes appear as optional `effectClass` metadata, so library/setup/outside steps use the existing external-effect icon without client changes. `rolloutEffectClasses` classifies effects; the registered `capabilityDefaults` table follows WORKSHOP §10 question 1's provisional recommendation, with W4 grants and approval waits (below). Both fresh and resumed story turns filter/block every effect outside `read` and `chat_state`. `ExecutionRegistry.kindTools` permits a kind-specific replacement of a public tool name: workshop `edit_card` edits saved library text, while story `edit_card` keeps its existing note-based behavior. Disabling the workshop variant removes it rather than falling back to story semantics.
- **The normal user operations.** `AgentCreateEntity` composes `CreateEntity`, using validated documents, owned references, tags/persona folders and an `agent` revision whose origin ref is `<rollout>:<call>`. `AgentReviseEntity` composes `EditRef` on the row version read, preserving unsaved drafts, validating documents/references and retaining the head's permissions through `withoutGrantedAgentEdits`, HTML approvals and regex-approval rules. A moved head is a correctable tool error. Whole text or an exact unique find/replace can be applied, all changes together. `AgentCloneCard` composes `ForkCard`, including its lineage, notes and draft carry; it records each created entity, retaining ForkCard's normal revision provenance. The setup tools resolve names or ids using the same owner-scoped library readers as the read tools, with ambiguity errors.
- **Greeting-only chat setup.** `StartGreetingChat` shares the complete greeting/cast initialization with `StartChat`, omitting only the first human/generating turn and creating the normal fork. `start_chat` reads `GetCardForChat`, uses the registered greeting sources and the existing macro freezer, and accepts a persona, greeting, title, preset and model. `AgentStartChat` composes this operation and the normal `AddStateEvents` preset/model bindings in the same transaction. It creates an ordinary `rp` chat and never requests generation there. Existing user `StartChat` behavior is unchanged.
- **Atomic effects and receipts.** `db/workshopEffects.ts` composes the typed operations inside one outer synchronous writer transaction. It writes the result receipt and every `rollout_effects` row before committing, so an effect-insert failure rolls back the operation too. The new STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID baseline table has key `(rollout_id, tool_call_id, seq)`, registered `rollout_effects.kind` values, target/title, JSON undo recipe, creation time and undo time. It references both its rollout and its receipt. Baseline checks/triggers enforce nonnegative sequence, valid recipes, owned workshop targets, target/revision relationships, immutable identity and one-way undo. The target index supports undo history; the call index covers the receipt foreign key from its call-id side. `rollout_receipts.is_error` preserves error results too. The loop replays all non-read calls from receipts before argument/state validation and records successful or refused non-read results through `RecordRolloutEffects` when the operation has not already recorded them. `RolloutToolReceipt` returns text and error status; the existing string reader remains compatible. Resume copies receipts and their error status, without copying or undoing the original library effects. A dangling library/setup/outside call without a receipt fails with “may already have happened”; W4 will add asking first.
- **Owner-scoped undo.** `WorkshopApi.ListRolloutEffects` reads a workshop's changes newest first, with a stable four-part cursor and a bounded page. `UndoRolloutEffect` reads the owned effect and runs its registered worker undoer, marking it undone in the same transaction; a repeated undo is a no-op. `rolloutUndoers` is passed as the fifth `StateModules` installer argument, so plugins can replace/disable an undo policy in source and bundled workers. A new card/note is binned only when its head, metadata and drafts still match. A clone's moved source drafts are restored through the normal draft store, preserving history; changed source/copy drafts refuse undo. An edit uses `RestoreRevision`, creating a new revision and retaining normal draft/history behavior. Only revisions restored by earlier successful effect undos advance an older effect's expected head, so reverse-order undo works while intervening user edits refuse with a plain reason. Chat creation undo checks its recorded state before binning. Undo uses the ordinary bin deletion steps without capacity eviction, so it never purges history.
- **Versions do not undo library changes.** Selecting another version, regenerating or resuming retains these independent library/chat effects. W3 exposed the reads and undo RPCs; W4 adds the client (Undo and Open, the Changes tab and the regenerate warning: “Workshop approvals and undo”). The original W3 lighthouse fixture uses one final workshop message; the combined setup/continuity suite also covers several messages. `workshopEffects.test.ts` covers that example through the mock provider, atomic rollback, provenance, dangling-call recovery with/without receipts, reverse undo, stale heads, drafts/permissions, clone notes/drafts, greeting setup and two-user isolation. The isolation matrix also covers the new RPCs and reader operations. **BASELINE CHANGED**; the recorded schema fixture is updated, with no migration.
**Workshop messages and continuity** (workshop5, 2026-11-12; spec/WORKSHOP.md W5, §2.3–§2.4). The registered workshop planner defaults to `several` and `resume_previous`; the ordinary story planner retains its one-message contracts. `send_message` posts without ending a several-message run. A plain answer ends it and supplies the final message. The tool's description matches this contract; story definitions and instructions retain their earlier bytes.

- **One commit pipeline.** A posted message passes through the registered output decoder, reply parsers (flushed and reset at the boundary) and final rewrites. `Generations` waits for outstanding live rewriting before the boundary. Worker `PostRolloutMessage` completes the current version, appends a generating slot/version of the same rollout, moves its fork tip and waiting send queue, and stores the send receipt in one synchronous transaction. The session waits for that commit before returning `details.versionId` in its tool result. Live output, Stop, provider attribution and subsequent chat-state effects follow the new working version. The existing finish transaction removes a pristine empty working slot without a bin item; tail rollout events are copied onto the preceding posted version before the empty slot and its original events are removed. A stopped or failed working version stays resumable; earlier posted versions remain complete.
- **Steps and versions.** `stepsOf`/`placedSteps` cut at successful sends' `details.versionId`, assigning calls by their result position, including calls after a send in the same assistant turn. Headers, live steps and stored `GetRolloutSteps` use that segment; a tail with no final text belongs to the last posted message. The inspector reads the whole run from any message. Regenerate and swipes on a several-message version resume before that message's send (or before its final answer), retain earlier messages/calls and branch at that slot when a tail exists; the original branch remains available. Resume-from-step indexes the selected message's segment. Each slot keeps its ordinary versions and version picker: selecting an existing version swaps that slot in place and keeps the viewed branch's tail; it does not restore a different run's entire tail. A new generation uses the selected version as its source. Retry with another model retains the transcript with that model pinned; a changed direction is appended as an explicit replacement instruction. Kept receipts are copied. Library/setup effects retain one canonical record on their originating rollout, including kept and discarded calls. Regeneration, Resume and step editing copy receipts without duplicating undo targets or undoing any outside change. W4 owns the effect warning.
- **Carrying a turn on.** `agent/continuity.ts` checks the causal path before the generating slot, using version identities, amend counts, text, hidden state and image selections. A child rollout reuses the previous frozen request, its whole transcript and new rendered user messages; images stay as references in the transcript and hydrate only for dispatch, with a text placeholder for a model without image input. New tool definitions replace the previous ones. The request and inherited explicit cache markers are retained, including Anthropic's previous tool-result marker; only carried runs prioritize them over the SDK's new automatic tail marker. Turn caps count this turn's requests. Snapshot continuity metadata retains the path proof, original prefix pins for exact rebuilding, source inspection and parent link; `parent_rollout_id` records the parent run. Edits, insertions, hidden or changeset-replaced messages, unavailable transcripts, fenced assembler versions, unfinished parents and model changes rebuild fresh with a stored inspector reason. Missing parents never make a generation fail.
- **Configuration invalidation (review-workshop5).** Carrying a request compares the frozen model and connection configuration and preset identity/revision with the new assembly, as well as model IDs. A changed preset, model settings or connection revision rebuilds fresh with its inspector reason; the newly sent user message remains in the request. The worker also reports whether any version in the run originated from Resume or a step edit, so the next independent turn rebuilds even when its message IDs still fit the original path; frozen snapshots remain byte-identical. `workshopContinuity.test.ts` exercises actual preset edits and model/connection updates.
- **Provider replay review (review-workshop5).** Several-message and continuous workshop requests preserve Chat Completions reasoning replay metadata, including OpenRouter's opaque `reasoning_details` stored by pi-ai in thinking signatures. Opaque replay data is retained only for its original provider/API/model; choosing another model for regeneration drops it. Story request conversion keeps its previous behavior. Continuity token counting includes this metadata. `workshopWire.test.ts` exercises complete serialized prefixes through OpenRouter, Responses (including encrypted reasoning), and Google (including thought signatures and tool results); `workshopContinuity.test.ts` also checks Anthropic signed and redacted thinking.
- **Message-local inspector actions (review-workshop5).** The run inspector still displays the complete transcript, but only steps belonging to the viewed message receive Edit/Resume indices. Other messages' steps can be edited from their own inspector. Result indices are paired with their assistant turn, so reused call IDs cannot attach an earlier result to a later call. The workshop browser matrix edits the second posted message's card-read result and verifies the replayed result. The existing joined branch selector declares its intentional shared-border inset to the layout audit, matching other joined controls; its appearance is unchanged.
- **Automatic cache endpoints (review-workshop5).** Carried snapshots preserve the automatic layout's stable endpoint and the previous request's transcript tail as well as explicit checkpoints. Anthropic replay therefore retains its prior marker positions instead of moving the previous tail marker to the new user turn. Automatic and explicit wire-prefix regressions both include signed/redacted thinking.
- **Image-limit continuity (review-workshop5).** A new image that would evict an image from the carried prefix triggers a fresh build, with an image-limit reason in the inspector. Provider-wide image limits therefore cannot silently rewrite a cached prefix. A later text-only turn can carry the new request normally. `workshopImageContinuity.test.ts` checks successive screenshots under a one-image limit, the exact admitted bytes, and text-only continuation.
- **Overflow.** The reader measures the prefix, transcript, tool definitions and admitted image estimates with the selected model's local tokenizer, against the current context maximum less reply reserve. On overflow it assembles fresh from the timeline; the registered `workshop-step-summaries` assembly stage adds one line listing each included message's tool steps before fitting. The single constant `WORKSHOP_OVERFLOW_STEP_SUMMARIES` enables this brief-authorized initial policy; workshop LCM remains proposed. The request inspector shows a parent link or the fresh-assembly reason using existing text/link surfaces.
- **Verification.** `workshopContinuity.test.ts` covers multiple sends, message steps, a middle-message swipe and retained W3 effects, empty-slot removal, stop/failure with Resume, exact serialized Chat Completions and Anthropic prefix bodies, rebuilding and every listed fallback. `workshopStoryParity.test.ts` runs unchanged on the pre-W5 branch to compare serialized story requests and complete slot/version/payload/rollout/state rows, normalizing generated identities, their derived identity hashes and clocks only. The existing story agent suites and isolation matrix remain gates. Client `agentSteps.test.ts` and the workshop browser fixture cover per-message steps and the complete run; workshop e2e and its focused layout audit cover 1440/390 in both themes, including continuity links. No database baseline tables or columns change.

**W3/W5 integration (merge-workshop35, 2026-11-12).** The merged planner combines all eight workshop tools with `several` and `resume_previous`. Assembler version 57 is one higher than both parents' highest version (56). The multi-message setup regression checks each effect's originating run/call, message-local step and inspector indices, earlier-message undo/refusal, middle-message regeneration, step-result editing, and Stop/Resume after a posted message. All library effects before and after a regenerated message remain recorded and independently undoable on the original run; none are automatically undone or copied. Earlier messages and the original branch survive. The former W5 synthetic effect-table fixture is replaced by these real W3 operations.

Before carrying a previous turn, `RolloutMaterial` validates effects from that run and its parent chain in the reader worker. Any undone effect causes a fresh build with an undo reason; a moved/missing saved library head or changed created chat does the same with a changed-library/chat reason. Library proofs follow recorded agent revision edges, so the run's own later edits are accepted without consulting clock order. The existing `rolloutUndoers` registry exposes optional read-only `unchanged` proofs; an unsupported effect kind rebuilds conservatively until its registration supplies one. This keeps the rule replaceable for plugins. The reason is a worker projection, never added to frozen story snapshots. The newly sent user message survives every fallback.

`workshopSetupContinuity.test.ts` covers direct and ancestor undo/user-save invalidation, unchanged and agent-edited library continuity, canonical effects through regeneration/Resume, and the existing per-rollout bounds across carried turns. Historical successes are context, not this turn's receipts: a new carried turn starts a separate 32-call/128-effect budget and still validates its new arguments. Repeated call IDs in different turns make distinct effects rather than replaying a parent receipt. `workshopStoryParity.test.ts` matches W3 requests and complete persisted rows with only assembler version 55 → 57 after generated-identity/clock normalization. No baseline table or column changes relative to W3.

**Workshop Resume integration (review-workshop2 follow-up, 2026-11-12).** Workshop and story runs freeze their actual filtered tools, including the output-contract tool, through the same `ContextGenerator` snapshot path. Resume and step argument validation read that frozen offer, not the current planner or story `agent.tools` preferences. The offered-tools check remains mandatory: an injected call absent from the original offer cannot become editable merely because a later kind planner offers it. `workshop.test.ts` stops an actual library read mid-tool, resumes it, then edits its arguments and resumes again; snapshots and outgoing definitions stay identical after planner/description changes. It also checks the unoffered-workshop-call refusal without creating a version or request. The workshop browser matrix stops after a library result, uses the existing Resume action, edits a library result through the existing inspector, and checks the replayed tools and edited result, with layout audits at both widths and themes. The merge failure was an outdated test expecting an unoffered RP call to be editable; the offered-tools guard is unchanged. Browser coverage also found that `generationOf(snapshot)` lost the inspection metadata on Resume, so later wire captures had messages but no display labels or model. Agent snapshots now optionally freeze the existing `Generation.inspection` metadata beside the tools; Resume supplies it to the existing provider capture path. This preserves historical labels, model and Workshop instructions for both kinds without reassembling or changing provider requests. Older snapshots without this optional metadata keep their existing unavailable display. Server Resume tests cover the story inspector too. No baseline or assembler-version change.

**Workshop chats, client** (workshop2, 2026-11-12; spec/WORKSHOP.md W2). A kind's behaviour stays the shared profile (`@rp/shared/chatKinds.ts`); its look is a client registry, `chatKindLooks` (`features/chat/kindLooks.ts`): `{ id, badge?: { label, hint }, accent?: <token name>, hides: ids, shows?: ids }`. A kind without a look looks like a story chat, so `rp` registers none; the workshop feature (`features/workshop/`, registered after `chat`) registers the `workshop` look, its start card and its chip; capability data comes from the server registry. Nothing in the chat feature compares a kind with `"workshop"`; a plugin's kind brings its own profile and look, and disabling the workshop's look gives its chats the story look.
- **Start cards.** The Chats page renders the new slot `chatStartSections` (`chats.start-sections`, `ChatsPage.tsx`) under the list. The chat feature registers "A chat without characters" (`chats.start-empty`, order 10); the workshop registers **Workshop** (`workshop.start`, order 20): "Ask an assistant about your cards, presets and lorebooks, outside any story.", an optional title and **New workshop**, which calls `CreateWorkshop` and opens the chat at `/chats/<id>`. Both use one `StartChatForm` (title kept as a user draft, `chat:new` and `workshop:new`). Apart from a story's side chat (“Workshop side chat” below), no other place creates a workshop; the chat's URL alone identifies it, and a reload opens it as one because the kind is the chat record's.
- **Badge.** `KindBadge` (`features/chat/KindBadge.tsx`) shows the look's badge, neutral, with its hover explanation ("A workshop: the assistant works on your app, not in a story."). `ChatBadges` (the chat header's title) shows it before "import unfinished"; the Chats page's rows (`ChatList.tsx`) show it after the name, and the left panel's and home's chat rows (`ForkRow`, `ShellBrowser.tsx`) after the title, where it's also appended to the row link's accessible name. In rows it isn't a separate tab stop. Filters and search treat a workshop as any chat (its cast is the Assistant).
- **Accent.** `styles.css` defines `--accent-workshop` and `--accent-workshop-contrast` for light and both dark blocks (teal, hue 185). `kindRootProps(look)` gives the chat page's root (`ChatPage.tsx`) `data-chat-kind`, `data-chat-accent` and the custom properties `--chat-accent: var(<token>)` and `--chat-accent-contrast: var(<token>-contrast)`; one rule, `[data-chat-accent]`, sets `--accent`, `--accent-contrast`, `--focus` and their `--color-*` theme variables from them (Tailwind's theme variables resolve at `:root`, so both are set). The side panel, which is portalled beside the frames or into a phone's sheet, applies the same props itself. Popovers and dialogs portalled to the page keep the app's accent.
- **Hidden controls.** `availableComposerControls`/`invokeComposerControl` and `panelTabs` leave out ids the look `hides`; This chat's sections pass them to `SlotOutlet`'s `except`. The workshop hides `composer.next` (the assistant always replies), and This chat's `settings.tools`, `settings.agent-permissions` and `settings.who-replies` (the workshop's tools are its capabilities; story tool settings do not change its planner). Cards stays visible: the cast is editable and Card swap affects assembly here too. Behaviour the profile refuses is gated by the profile, through `summarizes(chat)` and `mergesInto(chat)`: the Summaries tab, This chat's Summaries switch and the "Enable summaries" line under the header are left out where `allowsSummaries` is false, and ⋯ "Merge another chat…" and a message's "Merge a chat here…" where `allowsMerge` is false (W1 already filtered merge sources and export formats). Everything else is the story chat's: speaker switcher, swipes and versions, Continue and Write for, branches and the branch control, notes, lorebooks, model and preset, cast, History edits, Activity, pin, rename, delete, plain-text export, split, "New chat with this cast" (which starts a story chat with the Assistant).
- **Capability chip.** `workshop.capabilities` (`composerControls`, placement `strip`, order 35, offered only where the look `shows` it) reads `ListWorkshopCapabilities` through `features/workshop/capabilities.ts`; the server registry returns `{ id, order, label, explanation, mode: allow|ask|off, always? }` for the owned chat's offered tools. Built-ins: `library.read` "Read your library", `library.write` "Create and edit library items", and `chats.setup` "Set up chats", each with the choices W4 adds (below). The chip says "Can: N" (with "· Asks: M" and "· Off: K" when any), named "What the assistant may do: N allowed[, M asking first][, K off]", hover "What the assistant may do in this workshop. Click to see or change it."; it opens a strip popover titled "What the assistant may do" with one full-width row per capability and "These hold for this workshop only." The server read was added with W3 integration.
- **Other names.** The phone sheet, browser and workbench tab titles and system notification body prefix the title with the registered kind badge label. This chat's identity heading also shows the badge. Bin entries retain `origin.chatKind` (captured inside the deletion transaction) and render the existing `KindBadge`; restoring keeps the original kind. Story titles stay unchanged.
- **Inspector.** The workshop's instruction piece is labelled "Workshop instructions" by the server (W1); the inspector shows it as any assembler piece, and the run's steps through the existing run inspector.
- Tests: `test/workshopKinds.test.ts` (the strip with and without the look, the Summaries tab, merge and summary gates, the accent's props, a synthetic plugin kind's look and profile, disabling the look, the chip's text). `e2e/workshop.spec.ts` (`e2e/support/workshopChat.ts`, scripted provider `e2e/support/workshopProvider.ts`: `list_library`, then `read_card` of the Assistant, then the answer) at 1440 and 390, light and dark: the Chats page's two cards, New workshop, the header badge and accent, the chip and its popover, a sent message answered with two library steps, the run inspector's "Workshop instructions", This chat without the story's sections, a reload from the URL, the badge in the Chats page's and the left panel's rows, and a story chat with no kind, the story accent, Next, Tools and Summaries. `LAYOUT_AUDIT=1 LAYOUT_AUDIT_WORKSHOP_ONLY=1` runs the same cases through `layoutAudit.spec.ts`, auditing the Chats page (both start cards with long translated-length headings and entered titles), the popover, the reply, This chat, the reloaded chat, the list and a workshop in the bin. Review coverage also checks accent text and focus contrast against the themed surfaces (explicit light/dark and automatic dark), kind-labelled notifications and tab/sheet titles, bin restore, and a story Send answered by the scripted provider.

**Workshop approvals and undo** (workshop4, 2026-11-12; spec/WORKSHOP.md W4: §3.4, §3.6, §2.5's chip choices and Changes tab). This implements the proposed W4 subset without promoting any proposal to Decided. The delta from reference-harness is the same as W3's: no compensation/fork boundary; approvals wait inside the run and are bound to one call.

- **Capabilities and defaults.** `agent/capabilities.ts` registers ten capabilities in `ExecutionRegistry.workshopCapabilities` (`{ id, order, label, explanation, example?, modes }`): `library.read` (modes `allow` only), `chats.read`, `library.write`, `chats.setup`, `chats.rewrite`, `settings`, `generate`, `network`, `plugins.write` and `plugins.apply` (modes `off`/`ask`). Defaults come from one registered table, `capabilityDefaults`, following §10 question 1's recommendation (allow: library reads and writes, chat setup and rewrite, settings, plugin writes; ask: chat reads, generation, network, applying plugins); that question stays Open. `ListWorkshopCapabilities` returns, per offered capability, `mode` (the workshop's grant, else the default), `defaultMode`, `modes` and `chosen`.
- **Grants.** A new baseline table `workshop_grants (owner_user_id, chat_id, capability, target, mode, expires_at, …)` keyed by chat, capability and `target` ('' for the whole capability), with `workshop_grants_owner`. `target` and `expires_at` are unused until per-plugin and session trust. `SetWorkshopGrant { chatId, capability, mode | null }` (null deletes the row, back to the default) refuses with `GrantRefused` a story chat, a capability its kind doesn't offer, or a mode outside `modes`. The read `WorkshopGrants { userId, chatId, now }` skips expired rows. Delta from the spec's branch-owned `workshop.grants` state key through `ChangeCast`: a grant is the workshop's, not a branch's, so swipes and forks don't revert it, and keeping it out of chat state keeps it unreachable from any operation a tool can call.
- **Off.** `offeredByGrants` (`agent/approvals.ts`) drops an Off capability's tools from a turn's definitions in `ContextGenerator` (the cache breaks once), and the workshop instructions say "Turned off in this workshop: <labels>." A call to an Off tool anyway (a crafted Resume from a step, or the grant turned off mid-run) gets “<label>” is turned off in this workshop, so this wasn't done. Don't try it again unless the user turns it on." Ask first and Allowed send byte-identical definitions.
- **Asking first.** A tool may define `describe(ctx, args)`, the server's own account of the call from its real arguments and the items they name: `create_card` "Create the card “X”" with the fields it sets; `edit_card` the card's real name and each changed field before and after; `clone_card` and `start_chat` with the real source and card names. `AgentRun.permit` runs in the tool's execute path after the receipt check, so it covers calls carried over by Resume too. For an Ask call it writes a `tool_approvals` row (`rollout_id, tool_call_id` key, the arguments' `digest`, capability, prompt JSON, status `pending|allowed|denied|cancelled|used`, answer, note, times; a trigger keeps the identity fixed and finished rows final), shows the step as `status: "waiting"` with `approval: ApprovalPrompt` (on live Steps events and to a later subscriber's Hello), and waits in memory with no provider request open. `AnswerToolApproval { rolloutId, toolCallId, digest, answer: allow|allow_chat|deny, note? }` is refused (`ApprovalRefused`) unless the row is pending, its run is running, the capability is still on and the digest matches; `allow_chat` also writes the grant in the same transaction. Deny returns "The user declined this." (with "Their note: …"). Stop cancels the row. Tools receive `toolWriter(writer)`, which hides the four user-only writes (`SetWorkshopGrant`, `AnswerToolApproval`, `RequestToolApproval`, `SettleToolApproval`).
- **Restarts.** A run waiting when the server stops is parked as interrupted, and the existing Resume carries it on. The earlier row only tells the re-run call whether it may have started: pending or cancelled never ran; allowed, denied or used, or a call without an earlier row/receipt, conservatively asks with `uncertain: true` ("The app stopped while this was running. It may already have happened: check before allowing it again."), even where the capability is allowed. Resumed versions find earlier status through `source_version_id` (origin `resumed`), not `parent_rollout_id`. Answers never transfer to another run. An interrupted/parked run cannot accept an old prompt; Resume describes the current targets and asks under its own run id. Committed receipts still take precedence and never execute twice.
- **Review hardening (review-workshop4, 2026-11-12).** Approval digests include the registered tool name and capability as well as the real arguments. Repeated approval identities in one run fail closed; consumption reports whether an allowed row actually changed to used. Turning Off cancels pending rows/live waits and spends unconsumed allowed rows (used, conservatively uncertain on Resume), so switching back on cannot resurrect an earlier answer and old prompts cannot reinstate a grant. Setup tools retain the resolved target ids/row versions from their server descriptions, and edits retain the described document; the effect transaction checks those saved heads, the run's current status and the current grant. Ask-first writes also require the consumed approval digest for that run/call/capability. Thus a later Off/Ask choice or target edit cannot race the permit into an unauthorized change. Missing or ambiguous targets fail before asking, instead of resolving a different target after consent. Outside-effect tool and kind-variant registrations require a registered capability; unknown or newly registered capabilities without an explicit default are Off. Reply-local story tools retain their existing capability-free frozen shape. `capabilityDefaults` is the only default-policy table; effect classes classify effects only. Approval rows carry complete argument text: the existing panel folds values beyond 4,000 characters with an explicit cut-short notice and a hover-explained disclosure of all characters, rendered as plain text. A failed effects or steps read keeps regeneration blocked in the existing warning dialog, with an error and Cancel, rather than treating the failure as an empty change list. No baseline changes are added by the review.
- **The client.** `features/chat/agent/stepActions.ts` is a registry of what a tool step's row shows under it (`{ step, version, session }`). The agent feature registers `ApprovalPanel` (title, "Asks first: <capability>", the rows, a text diff per changed field, the uncertain warning, and Allow "Lets the assistant do this once.", Allow in this workshop, Decline, Add a note). A waiting call keeps the steps open, shows a waiting icon, and the header badge says "Waiting for you". The chip's rows (`CapabilityChip.tsx`) offer the capability's modes as `Segmented` Off / Ask first / Allowed with hover explanations (the default marked), and "Use the default" once chosen.
- **Undo, Open and Changes.** The workshop registers `StepEffects` (step action, for a done library/setup/outside call in a kind that `shows` `workshop.changes`): its changes from `ListVersionEffects { versionId }` (the version's run and the calls it kept from runs it was resumed from), each an `EffectRow` with Undo (hover per kind: bin a made item or chat, or restore the previous revision) and Open (`/chats/<id>`, else `/library/<refId>` from the recipe, else `/cards/<entityId>`; none for an undone made item). A refused undo shows its reason ("Changed since; open its history before undoing this change.") beside Open. The **Changes** tab (`workshop.changes`, `chatPanels` order 92, only where the look shows it) lists `ListRolloutEffects` newest first, 50 a page with Show older, with time, Undo and Open; it reads again on any undo (reactivity key `rollout-effects`) and when the newest reply settles. Since workfix1 the rows are grouped by the reply that made them (`groupByReply` in `effects.ts`: by `rolloutId`, in the order the newest-first list meets them, so an older page joins its reply's group), each group headed "Reply of <time>" with its count and **Undo all of this reply** (hover: "Takes back everything this reply changed, newest first. It stops at a change that can’t be undone."), offered while any of its changes can be undone; each change keeps its own Undo and Open. Undo all calls `UndoRolloutEffects { chatId, rolloutId }` (WorkshopApi; writer op in `db/workshopEffects.ts`, user-only in `exposures/exclusions.ts`): in one writer transaction it takes the run's standing changes newest first (`created_at`, tool call id, `seq`, all descending), runs each registered undoer in its own savepoint, and stops at the first refusal; it returns `{ undone, refused: { effect, reason } | null, left }`, which the group shows under its header ("Undid 2 changes.", "Not undone: <title>. <reason>", "Left as they are, since a newer change couldn’t be undone: …"). Owner checks are those of `UndoRolloutEffect`, plus the run must be in the named workshop. Tests: server `workshopUndoAll.test.ts` (order, stop and savepoint, report, owners), the isolation matrix, client `workshopApprovals.test.ts` (grouping across pages); e2e `workshopChanges.spec.ts` at 1440 and 390, light and dark, also in the layout audit's workshop group.
- **Regenerate warning.** `features/chat/replyGuards.ts` is a registry of guards that may cancel a new version before it's asked for (`guardReply`), beside `replyHooks`; `ChatSession.regenerate` (Regenerate, the › past the last version, guidance revisions) and step Resume in the inspector call it. The workshop's guard (`askBeforeReply`) passes replies without steps and kinds without changes; otherwise the `appTools` host reads the version's changes and, when any still stand, asks: "This reply changed things outside the chat", "A new version won’t undo them, and the assistant may make them again.", with Undo them, then make a new version (newest first; the first refusal stops it), Keep them and make a new version, and Cancel. Plain Resume of a stopped reply isn't warned: its kept calls keep their receipts and aren't run again.
- **Runs of several messages** (merged with W3/W5's job/merge-workshop35 at a81ec64d). A call waits inside the message it belongs to; the waiting overlay is applied per version when steps are shown, so a later subscriber's Hello shows it on the right message. `steps.ts` `callsFrom(messages, versionId)` lists the calls a run made from a message on (its own steps and every later message's), with their result text. `ListVersionEffects` uses it: the version's own run's effects by call id, and a resumed lineage's effects only where the earlier transcript's result equals the one the version kept, so a call re-made under the same id isn't credited to the old effect. Regenerating a message keeps that message's own steps and changes, so the warning lists only the changes the run made in later messages (none for its last message), with “Made by the replies its run wrote after this one. A new version keeps this reply’s own steps and changes and undoes none of these, but the assistant may make them again.”; carrying on from a step lists those from the step on (`keptCalls` in `regenerateWarning.ts`; `guardReply`'s `fromStep`). A carried run (`continuity.ts` `previousRun`) is rebuilt instead of carried when the workshop instructions changed (an Off or Use the default change: “What the assistant may do here changed, so this request was put together again.”); Ask first and Allowed leave the instructions identical, so they carry. A call carried into a new turn, after a restart or an undo asks again under its own id, never replaying an earlier answer. `test/workshopApprovalsContinuity.test.ts` covers these, and `e2e/workshopApprovals.spec.ts` uses a two-message run (the warning on the first message lists the second message's card).


**Workshop chat rewrites (workshop8, 2026-11-12).** Registered `rewrite_chat`, `rewrite_messages`, `rewrite_instructions`, `read_chat` and `search_chats` extend the workshop planner. Story assembly and its tools remain unchanged. Reads use `chats.read` (Ask first by default), independently of `chats.rewrite` (the existing registered Allowed default). Worker reads and writes recheck current grants and a consumed, call-bound approval; they never trust permissions supplied by a model. Read prompts name the saved chat and explicitly explain that the workshop reads the whole chat as its user sees it, including separate character contexts. Results label chat text as untrusted input, page on displayed message positions, omit other branches and unshown swipes, and cap each response's text at 12,000 characters. Searches scan at most 100 positions per call; a cursor advances even without matches. Long messages page through `nextOffset`; searches return an excerpt around a match, with its offset for a full read.

`ApplyAgentChangeset` applies a server-prepared rewrite through the existing `ApplyHistoryEdits` handler in one outer writer transaction, with the workshop receipt and one `changeset.apply` undo recipe. It refuses a generating target chat, a changed path/state proof, inaccessible targets and unrequested swipes. The proof reads only the selected path's version identities, amendment counts and state/summary metadata, bounded at two million characters; it does not materialize every swipe or branch. Each new changeset group uses its in-memory copy map instead of searching stored copies, messages-only previews probe the selected version directly, and fork overrides save their text-replacement provenance and summary flag in the same write. Calls change at most 10,000 texts in total (instruction calls keep their separate 32-binding limit) and write at most 262,144 UTF-8 bytes of resulting text. Larger searches refuse before writing, rather than splitting an approved changeset. A run writes at most 1,048,576 bytes; rewrites share the existing 32-change receipt quota with library/setup operations, and undone writes still count. Message text is supplied explicitly for up to 10,000 messages and summaries combined per call. Search pairs use the panel's original-text, first-overlap semantics, with an explicit messages/swipes/summaries scope per pair, at most 200,000 match candidates and 8 MiB of retained original text per call. The older registered history-rename name uses this same path, restricted to the shown branch; the history-search name uses reading consent and bounded excerpts.

Instruction rewrites revise existing chat-owned notes without moving their library head or drafts and bind the revision at the current message. Preset and lorebook bindings are new state items in the same changeset. Only instruction keys are admitted; permission/approval keys cannot be replaced or suppressed. Existing state-event undo suppresses these items and restores the previous bindings, so one Undo restores the entire instruction rewrite. Summary and version copies retain the existing changeset provenance, fork-local selection, freshness and undo mechanisms (§3.13).

`StartEditRollout` writes a completed `edit` rollout in the target chat, with a frozen snapshot identifying the workshop chat, originating rollout, tool call and workshop message. Application creates that rollout inside the same transaction as the changeset, satisfying the same-chat rollout constraint. It performs no model call and creates no usage-ledger row. Activity includes these edits with zero model requests; a real generation still uses the chat's own connection and the existing `generate` approval path. History edits adds “Made in the workshop” and a link to the originating message through its existing slot URL. Approvals use server-computed target names, branch identity, message/swipe/summary counts and every complete before/after text in the existing diff control. Each text names its exact target and revision, including unshown swipes; a separate row identifies unchanged dependent summaries that need updating. The prompt states the 10,000-text limit and byte/run limits. Above 32 diffs, the existing comparison disclosure mounts each full diff only when opened; every target and complete before/after document remains available. The existing sticky Stop row declares its intentional overlay to the layout audit, as it can float above long approval content; its positioning and interaction are unchanged. The audit also recognizes transparent flex-growing hover toolbars as reserved space when comparing sibling gaps; `layoutAuditRules.spec.ts` checks both that case and a real uneven-gap failure with a display-none toolbar. The assistant's title is not used to describe consent. Chat Reload/Lcm events refresh open views after application.

Tests: `workshopRewrite.test.ts` covers coordinated message/summary rename and one-step undo, ten explicit message texts and individual undo, sibling/unshown-swipe isolation, live-generation and stale-preview refusal, read permission and paging, untrusted text, instruction bindings, ownership and byte/run limits. `workshopRewriteScale.test.ts` exercises 5,000 messages, 200 branches and 20–50 swipes: complete explicit rewrites, a rename across those messages and 100 summaries, sibling/swipe isolation, Off during preparation and one-step undo.
