A disappearing focused control returns focus to the composer without clearing its draft; unavailable panels use the existing panel close/fallback behavior.

`pluginLifecycle.ts` exports `syncClientPlugins()` through the host for P3 after a successful local enable/disable/update. It revokes removed/replaced scopes and loads new commits immediately; route changes additionally offer reload. Other tabs compare the descriptor fingerprint on `PluginsChanged`, reconnect and focus, and show “Plugins changed. Reload to apply.” They never reload automatically. Instance changes notify every account, not just admins. Reload and Open without plugins flush open editor drafts, with browser backups retained. `plugins=off` is a URL parameter preserved by router search and browser-tab shell keys across workbench tabs, links, panel choices and reload; it has no device/account setting.

An already-open other tab retains its previous evaluated code and contributions until the user reloads or a local sync revokes them; its banner does not claim otherwise. Browser ESM namespace objects and already-admitted imports cannot be unloaded or revoked by HTTP headers. Subsequent network requests still require the current enabled pin and unchanged approved build/tree; there is no service worker or plugin preload/import map installed by the app. Existing trusted code can retain arbitrary page state under the full-trust model.

`server/src/plugins/serve.ts` authenticates facade, descriptor and module requests. A user asset is available only to its owner; instance assets are available to authenticated users. The only plugin asset path accepted is the canonical `/plugins/<instance|user>/<id>/<40-hex-commit>/client.mjs`, with no decoding or arbitrary file suffixes. The host admits at most four parallel asset checks and checks authorization under the lifecycle lock before and after file verification. It verifies the current unsuspended active pin of the requested plugin only (the same membership test as `clients()`, without reading every other plugin), the process-attested check report, a bounded-child verification of the approved Git objects and checked-build source against that commit, and the generated file's checksum/type/link count/size. The child verification runs once per build per process (plugcache1, 2026-11-17): `check.ts` caches it under a fingerprint of the attested `check.json` text and the lstat identity (inode, mode, links, size, mtime/ctime in ns) of every entry under the plugin's `.git` and build folders, taken before the verify. Any write, rename, link, commit or recheck changes that fingerprint and verifies again; the pin and artifact checksums are still checked on every request, so a revoked or repinned approval is refused on the next request. `pluginBuildCache.test.ts` covers verify counts, invalidation and revocation. Working-tree edits and a newer HEAD do not affect these checks. Altered approved trees or generated files fail closed and suspend the still-current pin under the lifecycle lock. All facade/descriptors/module responses and errors use **`Cache-Control: no-store, private`**, `nosniff` and same-origin resource policy. This deliberately replaces the proposed immutable module cache so disable/rollback always require current authorization. No third-party script/connect origin, inline script or eval permission was added to the CSP.

Service-worker entry-script requests are refused in every authentication mode, including passwordless local sessions: a persistent registration must not answer future module navigations without current pin/account checks. Ordinary same-origin dedicated workers keep the existing CSP rules. HEAD follows GET authorization and sends no body. Range and conditional headers do not bypass the gate or yield cached/partial responses: an authorized bounded module is returned as 200, and an unavailable module as 404. Generated entries above 16 MiB are refused before reading their bytes. Stylesheets, images, fonts, maps, extra chunks and directory listings are not plugin asset surfaces. In development Vite proxies `/plugins` to this gate and shares the source API facade; its sensitive-file denylist additionally rejects every plugin data tree, including `/@fs/` and raw/URL imports even when DATA_DIR is inside the workspace. The development facade contains framework exports and no plugin selection. The RPC adapter returns only the published pending/error-message/run result shape, without internal error descriptors or action methods.

Tests: `client/test/pluginHost.test.ts`, `pluginUi.test.ts`, the browser-build regression in server `pluginHost.test.ts`, `e2e/plugins.spec.ts`, `pluginFailures.spec.ts`, `pluginDevelopment.spec.ts`, `pluginStartup.spec.ts`, plus existing CSP/composer/chatPanelTabs gates. Browser cases use synthetic plugins and cover each failure phase (including early errors, uncaught rejections and React update loops), route URL/layout collisions, live enable/disable during streaming, focused controls/open panels, safe-start deep links/navigation, content never importing modules, private/disabled/changed/encoded/traversal/out-of-build asset requests, HEAD/range/conditional/oversized responses, rollback caching, and layout audits at 1440/390 in light/dark. `LAYOUT_AUDIT_PLUGIN=1` adds a checked fixture to the general sidebar/composer audits. Startup measurements compare a separately built client when `PLUGIN_BASELINE_DIST` is supplied and sample ten fixtures in five cold contexts. The image smoke opens an actual Chromium page with a checked working client plugin and a broken import, while verifying production checking has all required declarations.

### Settings → Plugins and consent (P3, 2026-11-13)

`features/plugins/index.tsx` registers the Plugins settings group, `/settings/plugins` and `/settings/plugins/<instance|user>~<id>`. The scope prefix distinguishes an instance plugin from a private plugin with the same id; the separator avoids the static server's file-extension routing. Parsing requires exactly one separator and the supported plugin-id alphabet; encoded invalid ids never alias a valid detail. These use the existing Settings navigation, Card/CardHeader, divided list rows, dialogs and responsive back link. The URL holds the selected exact version in `enable`, the reviewed settings revision in `enableRevision`, and data confirmation in `deleteData=1`; neither selection is restored from device storage. The list includes pinned plugins whose repository folders are missing, so suspension and retained data remain reachable. Repository metadata reads use at most four concurrent bounded children, keeping lists of 50 plugins usable. The list's empty state explains installation through the server's plugins folder. There is no install/fetch UI or workshop management exposure.

Check results display a plain sentence per failed stage instead of compiler/API/dependency jargon; the server's fixed diagnostic report remains available to future authoring workflows. Details show status, declared additions, saved versions (the enabled or last enabled version marked), check stages/report and private saved keys with their encoded UTF-8 JSON sizes and aggregate size. Values are not sent to this screen. Instance private-data metadata is admin-only; other authenticated accounts can read the plugin's version/check metadata. `PluginDataInfo`, declared in `db/ops.ts` with `OpsOf`-typed handlers, reads sizes entirely in the reader worker. There is no baseline change or migration in P3.

`repoVersions` reads version information and manifests from verified Git objects in the existing bounded repository child. Consent never uses an uncommitted working manifest. List/detail names and declared additions also come from verified committed objects, selecting the active version while it is on and the latest saved version while off. The bounded repository child's `info` operation reads just that version's metadata; no working manifest is an authority source. Shared `pluginConsent.ts` supplies the plain-language descriptions for every currently supported surface, client authority, replacements, instance-wide application, and server/worker authority. All server/worker code warns of full server access including stored keys/every account's chats and the ability to send data to other sites, even with `network: false`. Browser code is described as able to act as the user. No containment category is claimed. Internal service overrides remain unsupported by the checker.

The detail's Turn on opens consent for that exact version and applies through `PinPluginCommit`. Every enable/update requires consent; session trust is **not implemented**, because PLUGINS §10 question 1 and WORKSHOP §10 question 3 remain Open. Existing dormant session-trust fields confer no authority. A failed check returns its report and leaves the plugin off. Checks run again under the lifecycle lock, so displaying version metadata/check success does not authorize a changed source tree. Optional `expectedRevision` on the existing enable/pin RPCs protects Settings actions against another tab changing enabled settings. Duplicate enables without that guard are idempotent once the same version is active.

The existing `plugins.instance`/`plugins.user` settings pins additionally retain `previousCommit` and at most 50 distinct successfully enabled commits. Ordinary disable retains this history and data. `GoBackPlugin` chooses only the previous enabled version, checks the settings revision and exact committed access declarations, then uses the same serialized durable-suspension/checkout/check/enable path. Going back to the same or fewer declared capabilities is immediate; an earlier version that adds declared access opens exact-version consent instead. The server refuses bypassing that review through GoBackPlugin. A failed rollback stays suspended. An already suspended version keeps its suspension identity during a failed retry, so the notice/error does not disappear and repeat. P1's arbitrary-target `PinPluginCommit` still requires explicit consent. Prior installations without history acquire it on subsequent successful enables; no earlier enable history is invented.

Admins alone enable, check, change versions and manage instance/server plugins. A regular account has no such controls and can turn off/delete private data for its own browser plugin. Ownership derives only from CurrentUser; no owner is accepted in RPC payloads. Non-admin disable/delete inspect the pinned version's committed server/worker/override declarations (the latest saved version when unpinned), and refuse unavailable authority metadata. Editing or deleting the working manifest cannot grant server-plugin controls. Delete its data confirms the entry count and account scope, that only private saved entries are permanently lost, that chats/library items/plugin files/versions remain, and whether the running plugin can save new data. It uses the existing atomic writer deletion and keeps enabled code on. The confirmation says all private entries are deleted and labels its displayed count as a snapshot, since running code can save more entries. Long names wrap within the shared confirmation. `ConfirmDialog` accepts an optional `confirmHint`, used here to explain the permanent loss on hover instead of repeating the button label. Successful deletion publishes the existing account-scoped PluginsChanged notice, so other open details refresh data metadata; unchanged code descriptors do not require a reload.

The protected `plugins.host.suspended` banner uses durable list/detail state and existing PluginsChanged notices, including startup replay. It offers Go back, Open plugins and Dismiss. Dismissal is tab-local, keyed by scope/id/suspension timestamp, and survives subscription retries/remounts; details retain the problem. New suspension identities can notify again. Successful local management calls `syncClientPlugins()`; failed actions refresh details for safe retries. Changed route contributions keep P2's explicit reload banner, including after another successful local action syncs the same descriptors; the route-dirty flag clears only with a page reload. Open without plugins reuses the host's draft-flushing recovery navigation; `plugins=off` continues to reach every management screen. Composer/editor drafts use their existing saving/backup paths.

Tests: shared `pluginConsent.test.ts`; server `pluginSettings.test.ts`, `pluginData.test.ts`, the GoBackPlugin classification in `isolation.test.ts`, and inherited plugin/operation gates; browser `pluginSettings.spec.ts` covers consent, updates adding server code, rollback, disable, data confirmation, startup suspension/recovery, refused dirty-tree recovery, bad checks, double click/stale tabs, regular-account controls, 50 long-name fixtures, long version text, route reload and draft retention. Its screenshots and geometry audits cover list/detail/dialogs/notices at 1440/390 in both themes. Session-trust expiry is inapplicable until the owner closes the Open question. Independent P3 review adds regressions for dirty/missing working manifests, committed display metadata, rollback that grows server/network declarations, a disk change between dialog and confirmation, malformed/encoded detail URLs, other-tab data deletion, and long consent/deletion dialogs in all four width/theme combinations.


### Workshop plugin authoring (P4, 2026-11-13)

`agent/tools/plugins.ts` registers fifteen replaceable tools through the existing execution registry, installed by `PluginHost` after its service is constructed. The workshop planner offers them only in a standalone workshop; side chats and RP do not offer them. The reader-worker `AuthorizePluginTool` independently checks the owner, live standalone workshop, current account role/grants and, where needed, a consumed exact-call approval. `app_source`, `plugin_enable` and `plugin_rollback` are removed from a regular account’s offer as well as refused at execution. With the plugin host disabled, none of the authoring tools are registered or offered. Generic PluginApi exposures and the pin settings remain excluded. No model parameter, source text, check report, tool result or dormant session-trust field grants authority.

| Tools | Effect / capability | Approval and Undo |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `plugin_list`, `plugin_api`, `plugin_read`, `plugin_search`, `plugin_diff`, `plugin_log`, `plugin_check`, `app_source` | read / plugins.write | Normally allowed; the workshop's Off/Ask choice still holds. No Undo. |
| `plugin_create` | library / plugins.write | Normally allowed. Undo turns off and keeps the repository, history and data. |
| `plugin_write`, `plugin_edit` | library / plugins.write | Normally allowed. Undo restores the recorded previous file text without enabling code. |
| `plugin_commit` | library / plugins.write | Normally allowed. Undo creates a revert commit restoring the preceding saved tree, without applying it. |
| `plugin_enable` | outside / plugins.apply | Always asks, even if a registry default says allow. Undo turns it off, retaining files/history/data. |
| `plugin_rollback` | outside / plugins.apply | Immediate only for the exact previous approved version with no increase in declarations. Off still refuses. Undo turns it off. Arbitrary versions use enable/consent. |
| `plugin_disable` | setup / plugins.apply | Ask first; keeps files/history/data. Turning back on requires consent. |

The model uses repository ids, with `instance:<id>` identifying an instance repository. Browser templates belong to the acting account; server templates are instance-scoped and admin-only. Authoring does not widen the Settings rule: admins alone enable/apply versions, including browser versions. A regular account can author/check its own browser repository; code probes and tests are skipped with an explicit message. Server declarations fail before any probe for a regular account. `plugin_copy_builtin`, source/base rewriting and editable copies are implemented in P5 below.

Authoring file/Git work runs in the existing bounded repository child under the same lifecycle lock as Settings. `authorRepo.ts` validates the complete existing and proposed tree before a write: relative NFC paths, case-folded/file-directory collisions, parent directories, symlinks/hard links, special files, Git metadata, reserved names, UTF-8 text, 512 KiB/file, 8 MiB/256 files and depth 24. Model text fields have a tighter 64,000-character bound. Edits require exactly one occurrence per replacement and are prepared all-or-nothing. Literal searches return at most 30 excerpts; reads page by line, at most 200 lines. Results cap at 15,000 characters. No shell, executable Git, package manager, hooks or repository configuration runs. A rejected file edit leaves the existing pin untouched; validation precedes any repository mutation. Successful authoring edits/commits leave the approved pin and its checked build running; none load or enable the new work. Undo of repository work also leaves that pin running. Explicit disable and Undo of enable/create still turn it off.

Creation records its intent before Git initialization and can resume from an empty metadata directory or an intent without HEAD/config. Git initialization is idempotent before finishing the original deterministic commit. Before creation or mutation, a private Git-metadata intent records the operation's before/after trees and stable commit parent/time. The tool snapshot keeps a server-generated authoring identity across Resume/model switches; that identity, call id and argument digest locate the same journal after a stop. Each file publishes through an atomic rename. Commits create a deterministic immutable object before moving the branch ref, then finish the journal. The receipt/effect transaction follows the file/Git work. A missing SQLite receipt therefore recovers a completed file/commit journal rather than repeating it. Preflight remains read-only even for a pending journal. Recovered operations and refused stale file Undo leave the enabled pin running. SQLite only reads/writes its own tables: `AuthorizePluginTool`, `RolloutEffectFor`, `RolloutEffectsForRun` are classified reader operations; `CompletePluginUndo` is one owner-scoped synchronous writer transaction. External undo runs under the lifecycle lock before marking the effect undone. Existing non-plugin single-effect Undo retains its original writer path. Mixed reply Undo proceeds newest first and stops at a refusal; reverting a commit can supersede earlier unsaved-file changes, so those older individual Undos can refuse rather than overwrite the reverted tree. Creation Undo retains the inert repository rather than deleting history. Journal/Git metadata has the existing separate size/count bounds. Process-crash recovery is covered; this is not a cross-filesystem/SQLite atomic transaction or a power-loss/fsync guarantee.

A working-tree check creates an immutable Git snapshot without moving HEAD or adding a visible commit. The ordinary bounded compiler checks that snapshot against the exact working files; a successful check is held only in process memory and matched to the same tree after committing. Explicit saved-version authoring checks read verified Git objects into an isolated build without moving HEAD or the working files; this read-only historical mode does not relax the ordinary host/activation snapshot check. Enable preparation refuses an absent passing check, resolves the full commit and consent manifest/message from verified Git objects, verifies a clean current tree, and freezes both the current HEAD and settings revision in the call's server cache. The existing approval row displays P3's `pluginConsent` sentences, plugin name, short version and saved message (the consent binding retains the full commit), with **Turn on** / **Not now**; session trust has no control or authority. Prepared consent itself binds the entire argument digest and both repository scope and id, so duplicate call ids cannot substitute an identical instance commit for a private version. The approval must be consumed for this run/call/argument digest, and enable rechecks the frozen HEAD, clean files, current account/grants, selected tree/check and reviewed revision under the lifecycle lock. Settings' checked checkout/activation/pin path applies the selected commit after consent, including an older never-enabled version; its ordinary snapshot still requires exact HEAD and files. A changed commit/tree fails closed. A restarted process has no attested authoring check: check again, then ask for fresh consent. Stops/Resume never transfer an earlier approval.

Check output exposes stage names and, for type failures, at most eight plugin-relative file/line/TypeScript codes, with guidance to consult the API. It never interpolates diagnostics or exceptions that could contain source literals, environment values or host paths. Plugin source, Git messages/diffs, reports and reference source are explicitly labelled untrusted data through ordinary tool results. They do not change dispatcher, loading or approval boundaries.

`packages/plugin-api/src/docs.ts` contains the supported recipe index/examples. `plugin_api` reads type declarations and their comments from the installed API package: composer controls/draft, panels, extension routes, app banners, server data-only tools, worker state keys/value macros and private storage. Recipes are checked by `pluginApiDocs.test.ts`; existing typed host/browser tests exercise their adapters. Structural descriptors, full credential-bearing providers/reply transports and internal overrides are not advertised as authoring contracts. Index/topic results cap at 12,000 characters.

Admin-only `app_source` is a read-only allowlist over shipped `packages/server/src/agent`, `packages/server/src/plugins`, `packages/plugin-api/src`, plus shared `registry.ts`, `pluginClient.ts`, `pluginConsent.ts`. P5 below adds the finite copyable client-source allowlist. It exposes no data directories, runtime configuration, environment or secrets. Only `.ts`/`.tsx` files pass, names containing config/secret/credential/environment are excluded, the configured data volume is excluded even beneath a source root, links are refused, and limits are 256 files, depth 8, 128 KiB/file, 200 lines or 30 literal matches and 12,000 characters/result. Every output states this scope/limits.

The registered `plugins` skill feeds the existing tool-loading pipeline and frozen catalog, with no new wire defaults. Native/dispatcher loading adds one skill-index line to an untouched workshop: measured **16 o200k tokens**. No source/docs are injected until requested. The deliberate Every-tool fallback declares only tools admitted by the account role and the workshop’s current capabilities. With both plugin capabilities on, the fifteen admin definitions measure **1,527 o200k tokens / 6,979 characters** before provider framing; a regular account’s twelve definitions measure **1,220 tokens / 5,558 characters**. Off capabilities remove their definitions in every transport; both Off, a disabled host, a side chat or an RP turn add zero plugin definitions/listing. The coordinator explicitly accepts the Every-tool cost only for available, enabled capabilities; no unmeasured loading profile was enabled. Mid-run and retained historical offers still refuse revoked calls through live authorization; fresh turns apply the filtered offer.

Steps, receipts, Changes and per-effect Undo use the real tool names/call ids under direct and dispatcher transport. Completed plugin changes and Undo use the existing local client synchronizer; the exact locally approved enable is also followed after its approval reply, so folding its Steps does not prevent the button appearing. Existing descriptor notices, safe-start URLs, draft-saving reload, route reload notice and host recovery registrations remain. Workshop summaries explicitly retain plugin ids/paths/full checked/saved/enabled versions and pending approvals, while continuing to treat source/results as untrusted data. Tests cover the failed-check/fix/commit/one-consent dice flow, forged/direct/unloaded enable refusals, stale source/commit, decline, Stop/Resume with a model switch, regular-account refusal/probe skipping, rollback growth, confined text/journal recovery and recipe checks. New browser dice/consent/Undo cases audit the existing surfaces at 1440/390 in light/dark; the established plugin/workshop/loading gates remain required.


**Live-test fixes (fixes1114, 2026-11-14).** The enabled plugin is the checked build of its approved commit. Runtime asset verification and startup rechecks validate that commit's Git objects and checked source/artifact files independently of repository HEAD and working files. Startup refuses altered approved build sources or outputs before recompiling against the current app; ordinary approval checks still require the reviewed clean working tree. Changes in authoring work do not show a suspended banner. The fault banner says the approved version failed a check or stopped working; explicit Turn off is not a fault. Plugin approval/Steps use the committed name with the short version on a secondary line. Generic `presentation` metadata is kept in approval/transcript data, outside model-facing tool results. Local management also broadcasts descriptor changes to other tabs through `BroadcastChannel`, covering a gap before their server-notice subscription; the other tab retains evaluated code and offers the existing reload banner. Server notices remain the cross-device path. Refused write Undo explains that newer edits must be undone or versions reviewed.

Tool loading now selects native Responses loading only for provider `openai`, API kind `openai-responses`, exact `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini` and `gpt-5.4-pro`; nano, dated snapshots and prefixed/suffixed look-alikes are excluded. Direct OpenAI Chat Completions selects the dispatcher only for exact `gpt-5.4-nano` and `gpt-5.4-mini`. The assembly snapshot records the connection provider and a non-secret direct-OpenAI flag separately from API kind. The flag is derived from provider `openai` and its canonical API address (or its default); the transport address is never copied into a context snapshot. These defaults require that flag, so named OpenAI connections with proxy/custom addresses do not inherit them. Older snapshots lacking that classification conservatively retain the old mode until a fresh assembly. Anthropic and all other defaults are unchanged. The existing GPT-5.4 Chat tool/effort shim remains; a replaceable refusal-specific shim handles an unfamiliar model's explicit 400 saying function tools require effort `none`, with at most one corrected attempt before any output. Each attempt has its own ledger row and captured payload. A compatibility note in the existing sent-context inspector states the selected and sent reasoning effort whenever a shim changes it, including the inherited known-model shim; saved settings are unchanged. Workshop rebuild explanations for older snapshots and changed tool catalogs also state the possible one-time full input cost. Other 400s, APIs, providers and post-output errors do not take that path. **Assembler version 74** fences the changed selected-model request shapes. Offline selection-matrix, wire, refusal/retry and request-parity tests cover this; live measurement numbers are in TOOL-LOADING §16, not new provider calls by this job.

For workshop summaries, the recent pair explains when a summary is pending for the next reply: older messages/tool steps become summaries, followed by recent text, with the existing single-message/unread-result exception. This is a display correction and adds no summary requests; the existing batching and before-reply planning remain. The workshop instruction explicitly confines action/status claims to its input range and says “no result in this excerpt” for missing results. Compaction deliberately excludes the newest unread group, so a mid-run summary may end before later completed work; it must not claim that work never happened. Synthetic compactor tests capture this exact boundary. This retains reference-harness's input-addressed summary principle (§16 reference delta), without changing the scheduling policy.

Side-chat rewrite Changes take their story-title segment from the owned chat record in the applying writer transaction, independently of the model's change title. Existing branch-menu naming, live rename, saved deleted-branch naming and message ranges remain. Moving card text to an own-turn note normalizes only contiguous whitespace immediately on either side of the cut (one horizontal separator, or at most one empty paragraph; no leading/trailing cut whitespace). All text outside that boundary is byte-preserved, and library Undo restores the original document bytes, including prior replacement text. No database baseline or operation shape changes.


**Independent review (review-fixes1114, 2026-11-14).** Server activation and worker module snapshots now use data URLs containing the approved, process-attested artifact bytes, after bounded source verification and generated-file type/link/size/hash checks. The worker bridge is constructed by the host around that captured worker module; new or respawned workers cannot reopen a replaced `worker.mjs` or bridge path. Mutable build-file imports previously escaped validation on fresh workers. Browser assets use the same all-artifact verifier before serving and still suspend only the current pin on verification failure. Manifest and report reads check regular-file type, link count and size before reading. Startup still rejects altered recorded source/output and recompiles from verified Git objects; forged disk reports cannot attest code in a live process or skip the full startup check. Already evaluated full-trust code and in-flight snapshots remain outside revocation, and an operator controlling pins/files or racing filesystem checks remains trusted as described above. List-line cuts preserve the retained line's indentation, including CRLF; Undo still restores the exact original bytes. No planner optimization or baseline change was made.
### Editable built-in copies (P5, 2026-11-14)

Settings → Plugins adds Built-in parts using the same Cards, divided rows, Buttons and semantic tokens. `ListBuiltinParts` returns the copy catalog and tools whose adapters are not yet available, with plain explanations. Make an editable copy creates a private browser plugin or an admin-only instance server/worker plugin, checks its first commit, and opens its existing detail URL. Copying does not enable anything. The badge names the enabled replacement; application still uses the existing exact-version consent. The comparison dialog is selected by `compare` in the URL, including after reload. It shows saved/current original text side by side on desktop and stacked on phones; initial focus stays on the heading so a long comparison opens at its first source, including after reload. It never modifies the editable files.

Independent P5 review restricts stable-handle replacement and disable to the finite adapter catalog on both browser and server/worker hosts. The checker refuses unknown replacement declarations or a missing runtime entry before probing. New contributions remain available on the existing supported surfaces. A declared id alone cannot authorize replacing a different built-in, an unsupported registry, or another plugin's entry.

Consent names each committed replacement: “Replaces Completion sound.”, “Replaces Who's present (set_presence).” or “Replaces Reverse text macro (reverse).” Tool/macro replacements also say “Changes what the model sees.” Unknown declarations get one fixed unsupported-part warning and cannot pass checks. The full server/browser authority warnings and exact-version approval remain unchanged. Presence replacements retain `chat_state`, reject added authorization/snapshot hooks and require declared presence access; the stable type fixes the effect too. The app adds the approved plugin name with “(plugin)” to the tool's frozen label, so both persisted Steps and Tools offered identify it. No provider description or parameter bytes change when the plugin is off. The built-in's existing `chat_state` permission behavior is retained: the workshop permit exempts capability-free in-reply state tools from per-call approval; this review adds no new ask-first policy.

P5 initially shipped three typed, credential-free adapters (the registry expansion below supersedes the macro and tool coverage limits):

| Registry | Editable part | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `noticeChannels` | `notifications.completion-sound` | Browser settings component plus no-argument activation/completion callbacks. `Switch` and `Alert` use the same UI/React facade. Existing sound preference and activation rules are preserved. |
| `rolloutTools` | `set_presence` | `PresenceTool`/`PresenceContext`: causal cast data and a validated presence write, using the existing worker operations, narrator rule, owner/run/call identity and reversible receipt. Requires `server:presence` and `server:rolloutTools`. No database client, provider, key, arbitrary state write or ambient service is supplied. Retained cast readers/setters check their supplying plugin scope before and after reads and before admitting a write; turning off revokes them. |
| `macros` | `reverse` | `DataMacroSpec`: text arguments and plain call metadata. No resolver, variables, randomness, work callback or assembler services. Runs through the existing worker macro handle. |

The completion sound and presence policy are small source modules used by both the built-in and copied plugin. The built-in presence tool's parameters retain TypeBox's previous JSON property order, description and labels, so unchanged model-visible request bytes are preserved. All built-in entries in the three copyable registries declare `source: import.meta.url`; tests enumerate the tools (including generated/authoring tools), macros and notice channel. Only the finite catalog in `plugins/builtins.ts` authorizes copying; a registration's source field or a plugin's base metadata never authorizes opening an arbitrary file. The registry-adapter expansion below supersedes this initial macro/tool catalog; other registries remain unavailable for copying until their own complete adapters and dependency rewrites exist. Existing composer/panel/page/banner adapters support new contributions but cannot reproduce their built-ins' session/editor contracts. Display/message actions need those contracts too. Provider/reply/assembler transports retain P1's explicit limitations.

`plugins/copy.ts` runs only in the bounded repository child. It reads the catalog's exact source/dependency closure (128 KiB/file), checks every parent, refuses links/multiply linked/non-text files and excludes the configured data volume. It copies only exclusive allowlisted helpers, never an entire directory or Git metadata. The TypeScript parser rewrites exact known imports/re-exports/type imports to the side's stable API and confined copied helpers; strings/comments are untouched. Dynamic/computed imports, require-style imports, other plugins, system modules and unsupported dependencies fail closed. The ordinary checker uses the same syntax policy, returning fixed plain categories such as “file or system access” or “the chat session”, never arbitrary source/module literals. This constrains ordinary imports; it does not change the approved full-trust runtime model or claim to prevent dynamic-code escapes.

The first committed tree contains `replaces`, `base: { app, path, sha256 }`, inert `builtin-base.json` with the exact original texts and closure digest, and `NOTICE.md`. `base.app` is the installed source/API/lockfile/worker build stamp; it now includes client sources and excludes the configured data directory. `sha256` hashes the original entry file; the separate closure digest detects helper changes too. There is no project redistribution licence declared and no third-party implementation is copied; the notice records this and leaves React/Effect as API dependencies. The image ships `packages/client/src` for copying, but static HTTP serves only the built client directory. Source is never a browser executable module or an unauthenticated source endpoint. Admin `app_source` additionally includes only the two allowlisted copyable client files, retaining its previous limits and data exclusion.

Details compare only verified committed objects. `base.path` must equal a catalog path and is never used to resolve a file. Saved text/digests are validated before comparison. A changed entry/helper shows “The original changed in this update”; an unavailable or invalid original warns and offers a fresh copy. Other app changes do not silently merge or alter the copy. Original text remains untrusted display data, never instructions, authority or code to execute.

`plugin_copy_builtin` is a dedicated `library`/`plugins.write` tool: no arguments lists the available parts; registry/id plus optional pluginId creates, commits and checks. It shares P4's live standalone-workshop/role/grant authorization, owner confinement, server-generated argument-bound journal identity, lifecycle lock, receipts and creation Undo (turn off and retain history/data). A regular workshop may copy the browser part; probes/tests remain skipped and server/worker copies are refused. An admin's successful copy check supplies only the same in-process attestation used by `plugin_enable`; application still needs consumed exact-call consent, unchanged HEAD/tree/settings revision and the committed access declarations. Source/check results remain labelled untrusted. Generic copy/pin RPCs remain excluded from assistant operation exposure. Dormant session trust grants nothing.

Creation writes its private intent before files/Git, publishes immutable commit objects before refs, then records the ordinary synchronous SQLite receipt/effects transaction. New creation intents retain path ordering so recovery can verify/reuse the original committed file payload across an app update without regenerating it from changed shipped sources. Only the same server-generated creation key in the same owner/repository can recover it; copying imports no other repository's journals. Before all original files have been saved, an intervening source update can make an incomplete copy refuse safely rather than invent the former source. As in P4, this is process-crash recovery, not cross-filesystem/SQLite atomicity or power-loss/fsync durability. No new database operation or baseline object is needed.

Enabled manifests reserve explicit replacement ids across overlapping account/instance scopes. Startup considers pins by enabled time, then owner/id for ties, and durably suspends a later conflicting pin with the same explanation. The already enabled replacement wins; a second enable is refused with “Another enabled plugin already replaces this part. Turn it off first.” No silent stacking override is allowed. Scope disposal restores the original object and behavior. Registration/startup failures dispose partial registrations. Server tool call failures suspend the plugin durably and restore the built-in for subsequent calls. Worker macro call failures propagate a host `PluginFault` through the macro evaluator, which otherwise preserves ordinary failed macros as text; the request fails and the main host suspends the plugin, restoring the original on the next request. Browser callback/render failures close the replacement's whole tab scope and restore the built-in for subsequent events, with the existing recovery notice. Notice callbacks also observe returned Promises/thenables locally, including rejections without an Error stack, rather than relying on global error attribution. In-flight approved full-trust effects and ESM unloading retain P1/P2's limits.

Tests: fast `pluginCopy`, `pluginHost` client, recipes/consent/import-audit/operation-isolation suites; one-worker slow `pluginCopies` and `pluginHost`; `pluginReplacement` checks effect/authorization/provenance and unsupported replacement refusals; `pluginCopies.spec.ts` exercises a changed sound frequency, exact original restoration, committed-access consent, original-change comparison and source URL refusal. Sound, committed-presence consent, copied-tool Steps and the run inspector have screenshots and geometry audits at 1440/390, light/dark. Source-update comparisons cover every copyable registry; copied presence effects follow the selected swipe independently across forks, and the complete first provider request is byte-identical before enabling and after turning off. Assistant creation Undo retains the inert repository. The image smoke creates/checks all three inert copies from shipped sources and verifies source URLs disclose no modules, in addition to the established real-browser/import/startup smoke. No real provider requests are part of these tests.


### Registry adapters (adapters1, 2026-11-14)

The stable worker API v1 exports `MacroContractV1`, `MacroCall`, `MacroContext`, the variable overlay methods and the built-in formatting/hash helpers. Every built-in macro uses that contract and declares shipped source. The finite copy catalog includes every primary name; a copy reserves and replaces its aliases together. Copies include only their family module and its exclusive macro dependencies, with parsed imports rewritten to the worker API. Metadata-only `lookup` cannot recover another handler. Resolver/template expansion, delayed arguments, `macrosIn`, `once`, `charge` and variable methods use the same evaluator, budgets and causal expansion. Arguments/context are detached and frozen, projected by explicit field lists. Names, card fields and message rows are projected before traversal, so undeclared nested fields are never read. Each adapted entry memoizes detached message rows, comparing all allowed field values and own-property presence before reuse; host edits, additions and deletions refresh the projection without changing a retained earlier context. The weak cache is local to that registration and does not retain source rows. There are no settings, credential, branch, arbitrary-note or database methods. Card templates still clear nested card/original fields. Variable writes stay overlays/effects; no new persistence path is added.

Random uses the evaluator's injected source; `pick` keeps chat seed, content hash and offset hashing. `volatile: true` freezes values, `clock` freezes observed time, and `accepts`/`work` still validate and charge frozen draws. Full-trust closures can use ambient randomness, so **every plugin macro conservatively marks its segment as changing**, even when volatility is undeclared or its draw is frozen. This does not freeze directives or skip variable writes. The picker, consent and API docs explain the cost to prompt cache reuse. Original macros retain their previous cache behavior. Calls to handler/accepts/work run through Node VM execution with a 100 ms synchronous deadline; a throw, non-string or over-262,144-character text result (including a frozen value), invalid work/charge (nonfinite or negative), non-boolean acceptance result or timeout propagates PluginFault, fails that assembly and suspends the plugin, restoring the original on later assemblies. If a preflight or LCM-planning assembly fails first, generation may proceed using the restored original; no invalid expansion reaches the provider. Evaluator budget failures retain their ordinary limit result. Retained callbacks refuse after scope closure. VM execution supplies a deadline, not a security sandbox for approved full-trust code. The explicit fields and guarded methods are the supported contract for honest plugins. Ordinary object/function prototypes and approved plugin closures retain ambient process, filesystem and network authority; neither projection nor a VM deadline enforces isolation against malicious code. Consent retains the full-server-access warning.

`StoryToolV1` exposes only filtered history reads: causal messages, private address projections, summaries and bounded indexed searches. The four built-in policies (`search_chat`, `read_messages`, `expand_summary`, `search_summaries`) use this same contract, with original TypeBox definition order/bytes. The host keeps the existing snapshot prepare/freeze hooks and private-address commitments across Resume. The contract's messages method itself uses private coordinates in a restricted join; summaries return nothing there and indexed search cannot bypass the private guard with `ordinaryOnly`. No raw source identities, ranks, private seed, database handles or caller-selected branch/viewer are supplied. The projection is detached/frozen; reads check scope before and after execution.

`NoteReadToolV1` (`list_notes`) receives only a notes read; `NoteSwitchToolV1` (`switch_note`) additionally receives a validated switch. Both use the original `notesAt` projection, including shared history's active speaker and own-turn-note restrictions. Only the fields needed by their policies cross the boundary, without documents/revisions. The switch rechecks visibility/edit permission, fixes branch/run/call identity in the host and writes through the existing `ApplyRolloutEffect` receipt transaction. Selecting another version reverses only that branch's state. Presence retains its P5 cast/set contract. These seven story-tool copies cannot change effect class, capability, per-call approval, describe or snapshot hooks through the stable handle; unknown fields are refused. Read-only note copies cannot obtain a switch. Results are restricted to text/isError and cannot invent receipt/effect/loading records. Server full-trust consent remains explicit. Tools needing library/setup/outside effects, approvals, runs, loading or other domain operations remain unavailable for copying until their adapters exist; listing them grants no handle.

Tool provenance is frozen in Steps and Tools offered as before. Macro replacements add a `plugin_replacement` context issue identifying the macro and approved plugin, shown by the existing inspector/context-notes surfaces without changing sent text. Turning off restores the original registry objects. `ASSEMBLER_VERSION` is 74, inherited from master’s prompt changes; this adapter merge does not change no-plugin behavior, wire definition ordering or request bytes. No database operation or baseline object changes.

Settings → Plugins groups parts into Sounds and alerts, Story tools and Prompt macros using existing cards, rows, fields and buttons. Unavailable parts explain their missing copy support in plain language, without internal adapter/receipt terminology. Groups longer than eight have a labelled search. Each group’s search is stored in `builtinSearch` in the tab URL, retained through copy/detail navigation and restored on reload. The assistant's existing list/copy tools use the enlarged catalog; API docs describe both contracts and give examples. The requested assistant catalog groups copyable and unavailable ids by registry, omitting repeated prose so every installed part fits the existing result limit. No tool definition, loading profile, default skill listing or unsolicited docs are added to workshops. Published recipes are checked against the installed API. The private-address regression suite and separate-context tool helper also register the shipped editable policies through declared replacement handles, covering frozen Resume maps, unseen joins, branch corrections, card swaps and narrator/persona own-turn notes. Coverage includes source/provenance for every macro family, synthetic macro corpus equality (text, effects, frozen draws), VM timeout and lifecycle attacks, permission/receipt attacks, real copy/edit/replace/off restoration for the tools, thread/own-turn regressions, and four width/theme browser/layout checks.
**Merge seam verification (merge-fixes1114, 2026-11-14).** P5 replacement reservations and deterministic startup conflict ordering coexist with fixes1114's captured approved executable bytes. Startup rechecks the approved copy independently of newer commits and working files before registering replacements. Ask-before-copy approvals use the catalog's editable plugin name, state that the copy starts off and retain live capability/role checks without creating files. Copy Steps now use the name from the exact created commit and its short version as display-only presentation, including journal replay; model-facing results remain unchanged. Regression coverage exercises copied sound/presence/reverse WIP and newer commits, fresh browser loading, pending exact-version replacement consent, repository/enable Undo, restart and approved-output tampering. Turning off in another tab offers the existing reload notice before the original sound returns there. The deferred 200-ms planner profile remains an external artifact test, outside normal fast/slow and browser discovery; it is not weakened or moved into a gate by this merge. No database baseline change.


**Adapter merge verification (merge-adapters1, 2026-11-14).** All macro and story-tool copies retain master's approved-build semantics while working files and newer commits change. Runtime workers import captured approved bytes; tampered output suspends the pin at verification/restart and restores the original. The grouped picker's URL searches coexist with the local second-tab reload broadcast. Unchanged copied tool definitions retain the original model-facing bytes through every-tool, native and dispatcher loading, including direct OpenAI Automatic defaults; frozen labels identify the copy in Steps and the inspector. Summary assembly uses copied macros with the same audience/own-turn/thread boundaries and master's workshop excerpt instructions. Cuts beside macros retain the adjacent-whitespace normalization and whole-macro selection guard.

The macro adapter reuses its private VM execution context per registration, restoring the enclosing invocation after nested calls or errors. Projection, result/acceptance/work validation and every callback remain inside the same 100 ms deadline; disabling still revokes retained methods. No result is memoized: even a macro declaring `volatile: false` can consume `once`, write variables or resolve another context. Reusing the empty execution context avoids repeated realm creation without trusting those callbacks to be pure or retaining text across assembly/audience boundaries. The controlled review benchmark retains its 3,000 selected messages, 31 callbacks, three warm-up pairs and twelve measured pairs. Its enabled-copy acceptance allows at most 50 ms additional median assembly time, a small absolute request cost with shared-host timing margin; the separate no-plugin comparison against master retains the no-slower assertion. Remaining measured cost is below the approximately 50 ms detail-page disclosure threshold. Full measurements and commands are in the merge report. No database baseline change.


**Small UI review (review-smallui1, 2026-11-14).** The version picker's search and length ordering subscribe to live version text, including versions currently filtered out; rows continue selecting by immutable version identity. Newest ordering keeps written order on timestamp ties. Preview flattening excludes reopening Markdown delimiters and collapses whitespace before table-ruler matching, so malformed bracket/link sequences and whitespace-only 20,000-character swipes avoid repeated regex backtracking. Unit and browser fixtures include this text. Search highlights remain React text nodes. The 50-swipe browser fixture uses roughly 20,000 characters per swipe, records input-to-paint latency, and checks pointer/keyboard picks after filtering and ordering, hidden/starred grouping, comparison and reload reset at 1440/390 in both themes. Card choices use the standard name/version mapping without changing names sent to models or rename rules. Summary-model regression coverage includes branch inheritance and clearing, account ownership, unavailable choices, account-only planning, fitting with different windows, actual loopback summary execution and writer labels, failure fallback and explicit retry overrides. ### Browser display-rule adapters (adapters2, 2026-11-14)

`packages/plugin-api/src/display.ts` defines API v1 `DisplayTransformV1`, `DisplayScriptListV1` and `TimelineTransformV1`. All nine built-in entries declare shipped source and have finite editable-copy closures. Their `DisplayRegistryV1` handle offers activation-time registration only; page-registry lookup, disable and per-registration disposers are not advertised through this worker contract. Plugin closure owns restoration. The two text policies, three script-list policies and four timeline policies are the same typed policies used by the built-ins. Settings → Plugins groups them as Display rules, Display script lists and Timeline rules, with searches stored in the existing `builtinSearch` URL state. Exact-version consent names the replaced part and browser-only execution. Interface's existing Display transformations section lists active replacements with hover explanations. Existing replacement reservations refuse a second plugin for the same part; disposal restores the original registry objects.

Text input projects only text, stored macro mode/writer/frozen draws, positional display names and card fields, the two display switches, approved scripts, placement, relative depth and streaming state. Neither a complete Version, settings object, chat session, RPC client nor request assembler crosses this contract. Script-list inputs contain only the user's global and approved preset/character scripts. Ordering remains global → preset → character, then macros → regex, unless the user explicitly enables a copy changing it. The existing regex runner retains placement, enabled/display-only flags, depth, capture/macro and size rules. Stored, edited, copied and model-facing text stays separate from display output.

Timeline policies receive row metadata, message positions/origins, summary ranges, thread split identities and divider state as data. Existing message/merge/history-budget/summary/thread bodies remain host-owned, with their existing slots, controls and permissions. The five non-message bodies are separate `timelineBodies` registrations, including the thread feature’s own renderer; the worker bridge resolves those registrations rather than hard-wiring feature bodies. They declare source and are listed as not yet copyable because changing their controls needs a further presentation contract. Returned rows can retain/reorder those bodies or add literal Markdown text. Unknown identities/body kinds, duplicate keys, invalid heights/ranges and oversized results fail. No plugin React renderer or markup enters the page through this adapter. The host keeps virtualization, measurements, scroll anchoring and link positioning. Built-in policies run synchronously on their existing owned rows, without projecting the full path; only copies cross the detached worker boundary. A timeline copy accepts at most 2,000 input/output rows; a larger loaded window falls back and turns the copy off here.

Display copies run in a dedicated, terminable browser worker, including import/activation and callback code. They cannot mix page-control or server surfaces in one plugin. The checked client module still uses the existing authenticated, exact-pin, no-store asset gate. The pure `@rp/plugin-api/display` helper facade has a separate Vite build graph and authenticated `/plugin-display.mjs` route, so workers never import the combined page/UI/RPC chunks. The app CSP is unchanged; no eval, blob/data module or worker permission was added. This worker is a liveness boundary for these callbacks, not a new trust category or protection against all effects of approved full-trust code.

Worker import/activation has the existing 3,000 ms client deadline. One call is with the worker at a time per display plugin, and each has a **50 ms** deadline from the moment it is sent, including output serialization. Throws, malformed/oversized output, a worker error or timeout terminate its worker, reject queued work and close the whole tab-local plugin scope.

**The page trusts nothing the worker posts (review-adapters2, 2026-11-14).** The plugin shares the worker's global scope, so every check inside `displayPlugin.worker.ts` can be bypassed by it and none is relied on. `displayPlugin.ts` installs one message handler for the worker's life. Each exchange (activation or a call) carries a number; an answer must be a plain object of the expected kind carrying the number of the one exchange in flight. Anything else terminates the worker and turns the copy off in this tab: an unknown shape, a repeated or early answer, an answer for another exchange, and any message while nothing was asked (a flooding worker is stopped at its first surplus message; with no call waiting to fail, the bridge's `onFault` reports it, so the copy still shows as failed and off). A deadline that comes due while the page itself was busy waits one more turn, so an answer that already arrived is read first. What activation announces is validated on the page: at most 100 rules, each a declared display registry of this plugin, `api: 1`, a string id of the registry pattern, a finite order, no duplicates; a failure registers nothing. Answers are rebuilt from the contract's own fields before use (`displayAdapter.ts`): text results as `{ text, issues }`, scripts through the `RegexScript` schema, timeline rows field by field, so extra properties or a forged prototype key never reach page objects. One answer carries at most 1,000,000 characters of text, 2,000,000 characters of scripts or of timeline keys and literal text in all, 1,000 scripts and 2,000 rows. Structured cloning has already copied an oversized answer into the page when it is refused; the refusal terminates the worker, so that cost is paid once per load.

**Queueing (review-adapters2).** A caller passes an `AbortSignal` with each call (`transform(input, abandoned)`, `asyncTransform(rows, context, abandoned)`). `useDisplayed` aborts when a finished message's input changes or the message leaves the screen, and `useTransformedRows` when the timeline changes; a call not yet sent is then removed from the queue and never reaches the worker, and the adapter treats it as superseded, never as a fault. A script-list copy is asked once per distinct input: the adapter keeps its last 32 answers by the identity of the three script lists, the character and the placement, so a screen of messages makes one call, not one per message. The queue therefore holds live work only: at most one call per mounted text per copied text rule, one timeline, and the distinct script-list inputs. Its limit is 512 waiting calls; past it the call fails and the copy is turned off. Before this, every re-render queued another call and the 129th turned a working copy off. The time a screen takes to settle is at most 50 ms times the calls waiting, and the page never waits: until a copy answers, a message shows its previous answer or its text with macros expanded (invisible where a display script applies), and the timeline shows the original rows. `perf/displayCopies.perf.ts` measures opening, two streams with typing, and scrolling on the 100,000-message chat with no copy, one and all nine unchanged copies, in alternating rounds, and fails if a copy is turned off or the shared input and open budgets are crossed; `window.__rpPerf` gains `displayCalls`, `displayCallMaxMs`, `displayQueueMax` and `displayCallMs` in the perf build only. Measured 2026-11-14 on a shared host under load (load average 30–52), two rounds: opening took 1.1–1.3 s with no copy, 1.5–1.9 s with one and 2.9–3.1 s with nine; input p95 was 24–56 ms in every case; the queue never held more than 6 calls; a call took 1–3 ms at the median and 25–57 ms at p99 as the page sees it.

**What the worker can reach (measured by `e2e/displayWorkerBoundary.spec.ts`).** The worker script is served with the app's Content-Security-Policy, as every response is, so in it requests, WebSockets and EventSource to any other origin are refused, as are `eval`, `new Function` and `blob:` workers; it has no document, window, storage object or parent. A dynamic `import()` never gets that far: the plugin check refuses the source. It is the app's own origin with the user's session: a request to the app's own routes succeeds, with everything that implies (the consent text says "It can do anything you can do in the app"). The worker is a liveness boundary, not confinement; PLUGINS §5's sandboxed type is still later. The same spec holds what a copy returns to the built-in's sanitising: a hostile payload returned for a message, and as a timeline row's literal text, renders to the same DOM as the same text stored in a message, runs nothing, and requests nothing from another origin (the sanitiser keeps a bare password field in both; no `action` or `formaction` survives). `e2e/displayRequestIdentity.spec.ts` compares provider request bytes for a story reply and a workshop reply with one plugin changing all three registries off and on, under the every-request, native deferred and dispatcher tool-loading transports. A copy of Display regex runs the scripts inside the copy's worker under the 50 ms deadline, where the built-in allows its own worker 500 ms and reports a slow script on the message instead of turning anything off: scripts that take between the two turn the copy off. The failing call uses its captured original text/list/timeline policy; subsequent calls use the restored original. Normal closure gives cooperative worker cleanup at most 50 ms, then terminates remaining timers and callbacks; a hung worker is terminated immediately at its call deadline. Other tabs keep the existing explicit reload behavior. Original timeline rows remain visible while a copy answers. Script-list answers are awaited before showing a copied display, streaming work keeps only the latest input, and late/stale answers cannot replace newer rendering or revive a disabled scope. Built-in regex retains its existing independent 500 ms worker deadline and queue.

All text output still enters the existing Markdown sanitizer, HTML classifier, panel permission checks and sandboxed frame/CSP. The adapter never accepts executable markup into the app document. It adds no storage operation, baseline object, provider definition or model-facing source. API recipes and installed declarations cover the three contracts. No Proposed/Open decision is promoted; this implements PLUGINS §§3–5/8 and WORKSHOP §§5.3/5.7's registered, explicit-consent copy direction.
